description:
Kingdom of Ash is the seventh and final book in Sarah J. Maas's Throne of Glass series, the epic fantasy that follows assassin-turned-queen Aelin Galathynius. Locked in an iron coffin by Maeve, Queen of the Fae, Aelin endures months of torment while refusing to break, knowing that surrender would doom everyone she loves.

With Aelin captive, her companions are separated and sent across the continent, each facing their own battles as the war for Erilea reaches its climax. Bonds deepen, alliances are forged and some ties are lost for good. Long, emotional and full of action, it draws years of storylines together and is the essential finale for readers who have followed the series from the start.

description:
Queen of Shadows is the fourth book in Sarah J. Maas's Throne of Glass fantasy series. Celaena Sardothien has finally embraced her true identity as Aelin Galathynius, heir to the throne of Terrasen, but before she can claim her crown she has to fight for the people she loves.

Aelin sets out to stand by her loyal cousin, rescue a friend trapped by dark forces and confront the brutal king who has enslaved her kingdom, all while deciding who can still be trusted. A turning point in the series, it raises the stakes with darker magic, shifting loyalties and a heroine set on vengeance. A strong pick for readers who love romantic, action-filled fantasy.

title: White Bird A Wonder Story (A Graphic Novel)
sheet_title: White Bird A Wonder Story (A Graphic Novel)
author: R.J. Palacio
description:
White Bird is R.J. Palacio's first graphic novel and a companion to her much-loved novel Wonder. It tells the wartime story of Grandmère, grandmother of Julian from Wonder, who as a young Jewish girl was taken in and hidden from the Nazis by a local family in occupied France during the Second World War.

Told in expressive illustrated panels, the story explores courage, compassion and the risks ordinary people took to protect others, including a boy she and her classmates had once shunned. It handles difficult history with honesty and care, making it a thoughtful read for middle-grade and teenage readers and for families who want to talk about kindness and the Holocaust together.

  • Author: R.J. Palacio
  • Publisher: Knopf Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Wonder
  • ISBN: 9780593487785

title: The Nine Lives of Rose Napolitano
sheet_title: The Nine Lives of Rose Napolitano
author: Donna Freitas
description:
The Nine Lives of Rose Napolitano is a novel by Donna Freitas built around a single turning point. Rose has never wanted to be a mother, but her husband now wants a baby, and the argument that follows sends her life down nine different paths. In some versions her marriage ends; in others it survives as she rethinks her future.

Tracing how one decision ripples outward, the novel explores marriage, motherhood, identity and the expectations placed on women, asking how much of a life is shaped by choice and how much by chance. It is a thoughtful pick for book clubs and for readers who enjoy literary fiction with a what-if structure.

  • Author: Donna Freitas
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008370640

title: Great Circle
author: Maggie Shipstead
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Great Circle is a sweeping historical novel by Maggie Shipstead about a daring female aviator. Saved as babies when an ocean liner went down in 1914, twins Marian and Jamie Graves are raised by their uncle in Missoula, Montana, where a chance meeting with barnstorming pilots sparks Marian's lifelong passion for flight and her dream of circling the globe over both poles.

Her story is woven together with that of Hadley Baxter, a troubled Hollywood actress cast to play Marian in a film decades later. Moving from Prohibition-era Montana to Alaska, wartime London and modern Los Angeles, the novel explores freedom, ambition and the price of living on your own terms. Ideal for readers who enjoy long, immersive literary fiction.

  • Author: Maggie Shipstead
  • Language: English

title: The Conversation
author: Robert Livingston
description:
The Conversation: How Talking Honestly About Racism Can Transform Individuals and Organizations is a practical book by social psychologist Robert Livingston. Drawing on years of research and hands-on practice, he shows how difficult discussions about race at work can lead to real, measurable change rather than defensiveness.

Livingston draws on behavioural economics, management, psychology and sociology to build a clear, solution-focused framework for tackling bias in hiring, leadership and workplace culture. Written with wit and clarity, it suits managers, HR professionals and anyone who wants to help create a fairer, more inclusive organisation.

  • Author: Robert Livingston
  • Publisher: Penguin Business
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241502860

title: Milk Blood Heat
author: Dantiel W. Moniz
description:
Milk Blood Heat is a collection of short stories by Dantiel W. Moniz. Set in Florida's cities and suburbs, the stories follow girls, women and men whose everyday lives are suddenly shaken by intense moments of grief, desire, violence and personal reckoning.

Among them, a thirteen-year-old grapples with sadness and her friendship with a white classmate after an unexpected tragedy, a woman struggles to move on after a miscarriage, and a teenager rebels against her family's church. Moniz writes about family, faith, forgiveness and what people owe one another in intimate, unflinching stories that will suit readers of contemporary literary fiction.

  • Author: Dantiel W. Moniz
  • Publisher: Atlantic Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781838950583

title: Harlem Shuffle from the author of The Underground Railroad
sheet_title: Harlem Shuffle from the author of The Underground Railroad
author: Colson Whitehead
description:
Harlem Shuffle is a crime novel by Colson Whitehead set in 1960s Harlem. Ray Carney sells furniture on 125th Street and is working hard to build a respectable life for his wife and growing family, but he comes from a line of small-time crooks, and his cousin Freddie keeps bringing him goods of doubtful origin.

When Freddie gets caught up in a hotel robbery, Carney is pulled deeper into the city's world of heists, shakedowns and double-crosses. Part family saga and part caper, the novel is a lively portrait of a changing neighbourhood and of a man caught between two lives. It is the first book in Whitehead's Harlem trilogy.

  • Publisher: Fleet
  • Format: Hardcover, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Harlem Trilogy, Book 1

title: Ready Player Two A Novel
author: Ernest Cline
description:
Ready Player Two is Ernest Cline's sequel to Ready Player One, the near-future adventure that was adapted into Steven Spielberg's film. It returns readers to the world of the OASIS, the vast virtual universe at the heart of the first book, for a new quest packed with puzzles, games and pop-culture references.

Fans of the original will find the same blend of high-stakes adventure, gaming culture and 1980s nostalgia, along with fresh questions about technology and how people live online. It is best enjoyed after reading Ready Player One, and suits readers who love fast-paced science fiction with a playful, geeky streak.

  • Author: Ernest Cline
  • Publisher: Diversified Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 609 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Ready Player One, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780593400388

The series introduces young readers to Arab role models whose achievements come from knowledge and service rather than celebrity, offering a positive alternative to the usual idea of being famous. As the clues build, readers follow Dania's detective work and share her curiosity to learn more about the person behind the puzzle. Illustrated by Rasha Al-Kilani, it combines a mystery-style story with an introduction to inspiring Arab figures, making it well suited to young readers in Arabic.

description:
The Call of the Wild is Jack London's classic adventure novel, first published in 1903 and presented here as a Collins Classic. It follows Buck, a powerful dog stolen from a comfortable home in California and sold to work as a sled dog in the frozen north during the Klondike gold rush.

Drawing on London's own time as a gold prospector, the story is a vivid tale of endurance, loyalty and the pull of nature, as Buck learns the harsh rules of the wild. Short and gripping, it suits younger readers meeting the classics for the first time as well as adults returning to an old favourite.

I Am Brave is an early reader by Suzy Capozzi, illustrated by Eren Unten, from the Positive Power series in the Step into Reading programme. A little girl sets off on a big family holiday full of firsts, from her first plane ride to a giant hotel water slide and a dark cave full of bats.

With help from her brother, her parents and even a magician, she finds the courage to try new things, and young readers take on the affirmation I am brave. Pitched at Step 2, the text keeps to simple words and brief sentences for children who recognise common words and are beginning to decode new ones with support.

  • Author: Suzy Capozzi
  • Illustrator: Eren Unten

Any child who has just lost a tooth, or who has ever imagined being tiny enough to fly, will enjoy exploring the details of her little world. Step 1 readers combine big type, easy words, rhyme and picture clues for children who already know their letters and are ready to take their first steps in reading.

Map Skills for Today: Grade 1: Finding Your Way is an activity workbook from Scholastic Teaching Resources that introduces young children to maps. A friendly bear named Buddy guides learners through the simple idea that a map is a picture showing where things can be found.

Colourful activities cover map symbols, the cardinal directions and the link between a globe and a map, using hand-drawn maps of rooms, neighbourhoods and hidden treasure before moving on to maps of states and countries. Designed for Grade 1, it works well in the classroom and for learning at home.

Hippo & Rabbit in Three Short Tales is a Level 1 Scholastic Reader by Jeff Mack. Hippo and Rabbit could hardly be more different, but they are the best of friends, and these three short stories follow them through a full day and night together.

Rabbit helps turn Hippo's breakfast into a feast, the pair take turns giving each other wild rides on the swings, and at bedtime they discover that thunder and lightning are far less scary with a friend close by. Simple words and funny pictures make it a good fit for children just starting to read on their own.

title: Tess of the D'Urbervilles
author: Thomas Hardy
description:
Tess of the D'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's classic novel of rural Victorian England, presented in the Collins Classics series. Tess Durbeyfield, a young woman from a poor family, is sent to claim kinship with the wealthy D'Urbervilles in the hope of improving her family's fortunes, a step that shapes the rest of her life.

Following Tess as two contrasting men shape her fate, Hardy lays bare the hypocrisy and double standards of the society around her, writing about his heroine with great sympathy. Moving and ultimately tragic, it remains one of the great novels in English and is essential reading for students and lovers of the classics.

  • Author: Thomas Hardy
  • Publisher: Harper Press (Collins Classics)
  • Format: Paperback, 500 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007350919

Indestructibles: Baby Peekaboo is a playful peekaboo book for babies, created by Amy Pixton and illustrated by Kate Merritt. Little ones discover who is hiding behind the curtains, behind the toys and under the covers, with a happy surprise on every page.

The pages are rip-proof, waterproof and washable, the book is light enough to tuck into a nappy bag, and bright pictures with very few words invite parents and babies to talk about what they see.

The Bad Guys Movie Novelization by Kate Howard retells the DreamWorks animated film based on Aaron Blabey's illustrated series. Mr Wolf and his crew have a fearsome reputation, but these unlikely heroes are determined to prove they can do good, whether anyone wants them to or not.

Written as a brand-new novel adapted from the film, it follows the gang's big-screen adventure in an easy, fast-paced read. It is a great pick for young fans of the books and the movie who want to relive the story at their own pace.

Indestructibles: Hello, Farm introduces babies to the farmyard in a book created by Amy Pixton and illustrated by Maddie Frost. Hungry cows munch on grass, playful pigs roll in the mud and roosters crow to welcome the morning.

Like all Indestructibles books, it is designed for the way babies explore, with hands and mouths. The pages are rip-proof, waterproof and washable, it is light enough to go anywhere, and its bold illustrations with hardly any text encourage parents and babies to chat about each page.

  • Illustrator: Maddie Frost

Pippi Longstocking is Astrid Lindgren's much-loved classic about the strongest, most surprising girl in the world. When Pippi moves into Villa Villekulla next door, siblings Tommy and Annika discover a neighbour with bright red pigtails, no grown-ups to boss her around and a horse living on her veranda.

From then on, every day brings a new adventure, as Pippi's outrageous ideas turn ordinary life upside down. Funny, warm and full of mischief, this first book in the series, translated by Florence Lamborn, is a wonderful read-aloud and a great choice for independent readers who love spirited heroines.

Restart is a middle-grade novel by Gordon Korman about a boy given a second chance. After falling from a roof and hitting his head, Chase wakes up in hospital with no memory at all and has to relearn his whole life, beginning with his own name.

Back at school, Chase finds that classmates react to him in very different ways: some treat him as a hero, some are clearly scared of him, and one girl is furious with him. As he pieces together who he used to be, he must decide who he wants to become. Funny and thought-provoking, it explores bullying, friendship and redemption.

Who Was Martin Luther King, Jr.? by Bonnie Bader is an accessible biography for young readers from the Who Was? series. It tells how King, at just 25, helped organise the Montgomery Bus Boycott and went on to rally people across the United States for voting rights, desegregation and equal civil rights.

The book explains his commitment to nonviolence, even when his life was in danger, and his campaigns against racial and economic injustice up to his assassination in 1968. Clear writing and around 80 black-and-white illustrations by Elizabeth Wolf make this turbulent period of history easy for young readers to follow.

  • Illustrator: Elizabeth Wolf
  • Publisher: Penguin Workshop
  • Format: Paperback, 112 pages
  • Language: English

My Side of the Mountain is Jean Craighead George's classic survival story. Young Sam Gribley leaves city life behind and heads for the Catskills in upstate New York, where he makes his home inside an enormous hollow tree.

With a pet falcon and a wild weasel as his companions and only his wits to rely on, Sam learns to survive on what the forest provides, weathering blizzards and loneliness and dodging hunters. Funny, touching and rich in detail about the natural world, it is the first book in a series and a timeless read for young adventurers.

description:
How to Trick a Twit is a prank-packed activity book by Kay Woodward, inspired by Roald Dahl's The Twits. Mr and Mrs Twit love nothing more than playing nasty tricks on each other, and this book challenges young readers to become such skilled pranksters that they could outwit a Twit themselves.

Alongside a host of fiendish pranks, it is stuffed with quizzes, recipes, jokes, fun facts and games, plus extracts from the original story and bonus material. It is a great pick for young Roald Dahl fans with a taste for mischief.

  • Author: Kay Woodward, inspired by Roald Dahl
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241520987

title: One For The Murphys
sheet_title: One For The Murphys Lynda Mullaly Hunt
author: Lynda Mullaly Hunt
description:
One for the Murphys is a moving middle-grade novel by Lynda Mullaly Hunt. Twelve-year-old Carley Connors has learned to be tough during a Las Vegas childhood with her mother, but after a painful betrayal she finds herself in foster care, placed with the Murphys, a warm, noisy household with three sons.

Unsure that happy families even exist, Carley keeps her guard up, especially around Daniel, the brother closest to her age, who resents her arrival. But Mrs Murphy truly listens to her and the younger boys slowly win her over, until news from her mother turns everything upside down. It is a heartfelt story about belonging, trust and what makes a family.

  • Author: Lynda Mullaly Hunt
  • Publisher: Puffin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780142426524

title: Willy Wonka's Everlasting Book of Fun
sheet_title: Willy Wonka's Everlasting Book of Fun
author: Roald Dahl
description:
Willy Wonka's Everlasting Book of Fun is a bumper activity book hosted by Roald Dahl's extraordinary chocolate maker, Willy Wonka. Favourite characters from Dahl's stories join in across 365 activities and puzzles, so there is something new for each day of the year.

Ideal for summer holidays and rainy afternoons, it is designed to chase away boredom and keep young readers busy and entertained. A treat for Dahl fans who want to step inside the world of Wonka's factory.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241428139

title: The Water Horse
sheet_title: The Water Horse Dick King Smith
author: Dick King-Smith
description:
The Water Horse is a magical story by Dick King-Smith, set on the Scottish coast. The morning after a fierce storm, Kirstie and Angus discover a strange egg lying on the beach and take it home. Overnight it hatches into a tiny sea creature with the head of a horse, four flippers and the tail of a crocodile.

This baby monster soon becomes the family pet, but there is one big problem: it simply will not stop growing. Warm, funny and gently adventurous, it is a lovely read for confident young readers and anyone fascinated by legends of sea monsters.

  • Author: Dick King-Smith
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 96 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141302232

title: National Geographic Kids Quiz Whiz: 1,000 Super Fun, Mind-Bending, Totally Awesome Trivia Questions
sheet_title: Quiz Whiz: 1000 Super Fun Mind Bending National Geographic
author: National Geographic Kids
description:
National Geographic Kids Quiz Whiz is a bumper book of 1,000 trivia questions designed to feel like fun rather than a school test. The questions range from how hot lightning gets to the proper name for a gathering of cats, with plenty of surprising facts in between.

Based on a quiz feature from the National Geographic Kids website, it is full of colourful photos and a lively design. Children can test themselves, challenge their friends or put the whole family on the spot to see who scores highest.

  • Author: National Geographic Kids
  • Publisher: National Geographic Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Quiz Whiz, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781426310188

title: Sidney Sheldon's Angel of the Dark
sheet_title: Sidney Sheldon S Angel Of The Dark Sidney Sheldon
author: Sidney Sheldon, Tilly Bagshawe
description:
Sidney Sheldon's Angel of the Dark is a thriller by Tilly Bagshawe, who continues the work of the late Sidney Sheldon using material from his private archives. When an elderly multimillionaire art dealer is found murdered in his Hollywood home and the investigation turns up no solid leads, the case is closed without answers.

From there, the hunt for the truth spans the globe, as a son seeks answers about the violent death of his rich father and a pattern of killings among wealthy men begins to emerge. Written in Sheldon's signature style, full of glamour, twists and suspense, it will appeal to his fans and to anyone who enjoys a stylish international thriller.

  • Author: Sidney Sheldon and Tilly Bagshawe
  • Publisher: Harper
  • Format: Mass Market Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780062073457

title: Hello Baby Animals Black And White Board Book
sheet_title: Hello Baby Animals Black And White Board Book
author: duopress labs
description:
Hello, Baby Animals is a high-contrast board book from duopress labs, with art by Julissa Mora. It introduces ten baby animals using bold black-and-white patterns and a friendly text, designed to catch the attention of very young, developing eyes.

Linking pictures on the page with things in the real world is an early step in a baby's communication skills, and this sturdy book gives little ones plenty to look at and parents plenty to talk about. It follows on from Hello, Ocean Friends by the same team.

  • Author: duopress labs
  • Illustrator: Julissa Mora
  • Publisher: duopress
  • Format: Board Book, 20 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781938093685

title: Rules
author: Cynthia Lord
description:
Rules is Cynthia Lord's warm and funny debut novel, named a Newbery Honor Book in 2007. Twelve-year-old Catherine longs for an ordinary life, but her family revolves around her brother David, who has autism, and she has spent years teaching him rules to stop him embarrassing her in public.

Then one summer she meets Jason, an unexpected new friend, and Kristi, the girl next door she has always hoped to get to know, and her own behaviour starts to surprise her. Thoughtful and touching, it explores difference, acceptance and what being normal really means.

  • Author: Cynthia Lord
  • Publisher: Scholastic
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780439443838

title: Who Was J. R. R. Tolkien?
sheet_title: Who Was J. R. R. Tolkien? Pam Pollack
author: Pam Pollack, Meg Belviso
description:
Who Was J.R.R. Tolkien? by Pam Pollack and Meg Belviso is a biography for young readers from the Who Was? series. It tells the life story of the author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, from his birth in South Africa and his childhood in the English countryside to the creation of his famous fantasy worlds.

Readers discover how a boy who was reading and writing by the age of four grew into a gifted linguist who invented whole languages and imaginary realms for his stories, proving that fantasy is not just for children. With illustrations by Jonathan Moore, it is an engaging introduction for young fans of Middle-earth.

  • Author: Pam Pollack and Meg Belviso
  • Illustrator: Jonathan Moore
  • Publisher: Penguin Workshop
  • Format: Paperback, 112 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Who Was?
  • ISBN: 9780448483023

title: Secret Seven 01: Adventure On The Way Home
sheet_title: Secret Seven 01: Adventure On The Way Home Enid Blyton
author: Enid Blyton
description:
Adventure on the Way Home is the first book in Enid Blyton's Secret Seven Colour Short Stories series. Peter, Janet, Jack, Barbara, Pam, Colin and George make up the Secret Seven, a club of friends always ready to solve a mystery, and in this short story the journey home turns into an unexpected adventure.

Alongside her fifteen Secret Seven novels, Blyton wrote six short stories about the club, and this edition presents one of them in short chapters with full-colour illustrations by Tony Ross. It is ideal for newly confident readers and a great first step towards the full-length Secret Seven and Famous Five books.

  • Author: Enid Blyton
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: Hodder Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 80 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Secret Seven Colour Short Stories, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781444927641

title: Secret Seven 2: The Humbug Adventure
sheet_title: Secret Seven 2: The Humbug Adventure Enid Blyton
author: Enid Blyton
description:
The Humbug Adventure is the second book in Enid Blyton's Secret Seven Colour Short Stories series. When the Seven go out star-gazing, they soon grow bored and turn their attention to the town instead, only to spot someone setting fire to a haystack. Can they move quickly enough to save the barn?

Presented in short chapters with bright full-colour illustrations by Tony Ross, this classic mystery is just right for newly confident readers. It is a great way to meet Peter, Janet and the rest of the club before moving on to the full-length Secret Seven novels.

  • Author: Enid Blyton
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: Hodder Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 80 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Secret Seven Colour Short Stories, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781444927665

title: Secret Seven 5: Hurry Secret Seven Hurry
sheet_title: Secret Seven 5: Hurry Secret Seven Hurry Enid Blyton
author: Enid Blyton
description:
Hurry, Secret Seven, Hurry is the fifth book in Enid Blyton's Secret Seven Colour Short Stories series. After an accident, an injured man tries to pass an urgent message to the people helping him, and the Secret Seven are the only ones who can work out what it means.

Racing against time, the club must use the clue to stop anyone else from coming to harm. Told in short chapters with full-colour illustrations by Tony Ross, it is a quick, exciting mystery for children who are growing in confidence as readers.

  • Author: Enid Blyton
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: Hodder Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 80 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Secret Seven Colour Short Stories, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9781444927696

title: The Richest Man In Babylon Charles Conrad
sheet_title: The Richest Man In Babylon Charles Conrad
author: George S. Clason
description:
The Richest Man in Babylon is George S. Clason's classic guide to building wealth, presented here in its complete original 1926 text and edited by Charles Conrad. Through parables set in ancient Babylon, Clason shares simple, lasting principles for earning, saving and growing money.

Its stories of Babylonian traders, craftsmen and herders show how to hold on to more of your income, clear your debts, make your money work for you and guard your savings for the future. Short and easy to read, it suits anyone who wants to take control of their personal finances.

  • Author: George S. Clason
  • Editor: Charles Conrad
  • Publisher: CreateSpace Independent Publishing Platform
  • Format: Paperback, 100 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781508524359

title: THE FOUR AGREEMENTS
author: Don Miguel Ruiz
description:
The Four Agreements: A Practical Guide to Personal Freedom is a short, insightful book by don Miguel Ruiz. Drawing on ancient Toltec wisdom, Ruiz explains where self-limiting beliefs come from and how they drain our happiness and cause unnecessary pain.

At the heart of the book are four simple agreements to live by: be impeccable with your word, don't take anything personally, don't make assumptions and always do your best. Clear and easy to return to, it suits anyone looking for a grounded approach to happiness, relationships and inner freedom.

  • Author: Don Miguel Ruiz
  • Publisher: Amber-Allen Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 140 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Toltec Wisdom
  • ISBN: 9781878424310

title: THE DINOSAUR THAT POOPED CHRISTMAS
author: Tom Fletcher, Dougie Poynter
description:
The Dinosaur That Pooped Christmas is a gloriously silly picture book by Tom Fletcher and Dougie Poynter. All Danny asks for this Christmas is everything, yet he ends up with a ravenous dinosaur that swallows the festivities whole.

Of course, everything a dinosaur eats has to come out again, and the result is a festive romp full of presents, poop and prehistoric chaos. Told in bouncy rhyme with bright pictures, it is a laugh-out-loud Christmas read-aloud for families who enjoy a bit of toilet humour.

  • Author: Tom Fletcher and Dougie Poynter
  • Publisher: Red Fox
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Dinosaur That Pooped
  • ISBN: 9781849417792

title: The Puffin Book of Stories for Five-Year-Olds
sheet_title: THE PUFFIN BOOK OF STORIES FOR FIVEYEAROLDS (YOUNG PUFFIN RE
author: Wendy Cooling
description:
The Puffin Book of Stories for Five-Year-Olds is an anthology of short stories chosen by Wendy Cooling, with illustrations by Steve Cox. It gathers tales of adventure and magic from writers such as Malorie Blackman, Margaret Mahy and Ted Hughes.

Inside, children meet Eric and his elephant, a hedgehog with a sudden craving for hamburgers, a king who will not wash and a girl desperate for a particular pair of trainers. Just the right length for bedtime, the stories are ideal for sharing aloud with five-year-olds or for early readers to enjoy on their own.

  • Editor: Wendy Cooling
  • Illustrator: Steve Cox
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780140374582

title: James And The Giant Peach: The Play
sheet_title: James And The Giant Peach: The Play Roald Dahl
author: Roald Dahl
description:
James and the Giant Peach: The Play is a stage adaptation of Roald Dahl's classic story, dramatised by Richard R. George. James gets away from his cruel aunts and sets off inside an enormous peach with a band of giant insect friends on a wonderful, fantastical journey.

The script is written to be staged in a classroom, performed at home or just read through with friends, with tips on props, lighting and how to stage it. George first adapted the story as a play while working as a primary school teacher in the United States, and Dahl liked it so much that he wrote an introduction.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Adapted by: Richard R. George
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 96 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141374291

title: Room 13
author: Robert Swindells
description:
Room 13 is a spooky mystery for young readers by Robert Swindells. On a school trip, Fliss and her friends stay at the eerie Crow's Nest Hotel, where there is supposedly no room thirteen. Yet when the clock strikes twelve, something strange happens to the linen cupboard door beside room 12.

Meanwhile, their classmate Ellie-May Sunderland is changing too, in a way that grows more sinister with every night. Tense and atmospheric, it is a chilling story that keeps the pages turning, perfect for confident readers who enjoy a good scare.

  • Author: Robert Swindells
  • Publisher: Corgi Yearling Books
  • Format: Paperback, 158 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780440864653

title: Twelfth Night
author: William Shakespeare
description:
Twelfth Night is William Shakespeare's romantic comedy of love, disguise and mistaken identity, presented in the Folger Shakespeare Library edition edited by Barbara A. Mowat and Paul Werstine. Shipwrecked on the coast of Illyria, Viola disguises herself as a young man and enters the service of Duke Orsino, believing her twin brother Sebastian has drowned.

Orsino sends her to woo the Countess Olivia on his behalf, only for Olivia to fall for the messenger, while Malvolio, her self-important steward, and Sir Andrew Aguecheek pursue their own hopes. Alongside the text, this edition provides background on Shakespeare, the Elizabethan theatre and the play itself, making it ideal for students and general readers alike.

  • Author: William Shakespeare
  • Editors: Barbara A. Mowat and Paul Werstine
  • Publisher: Washington Square Press (Simon and Schuster)
  • Format: Mass Market Paperback, 222 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Folger Shakespeare Library
  • ISBN: 9780743482776

title: Stuart Little
author: E.B. White
description:
Stuart Little is E.B. White's classic tale of a very small hero, illustrated by Garth Williams. Stuart is a mouse born into a human family in New York City, sharing a home with Mr and Mrs Little, big brother George and a cat named Snowball.

When his dear friend Margalo, a little bird, vanishes from her nest, brave and adventurous Stuart leaves home for the first time to find her, meeting new friends and facing one escapade after another along the way. Gentle, funny and full of charm, it is a timeless read-aloud and a lovely book for young independent readers.

  • Author: E.B. White
  • Illustrator: Garth Williams
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 162 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141354835

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar And Father Christmas
sheet_title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar And Father Christmas Eric Carle
author: Eric Carle
description:
The Very Hungry Caterpillar and Father Christmas is a festive board book starring Eric Carle's famous caterpillar. The Very Hungry Caterpillar travels to the North Pole to help Father Christmas prepare for Christmas Eve, from wrapping up warm and feeding the reindeer to loading the sleigh with presents.

With simple rhyming text, bright artwork in Carle's style and a fold-out surprise at the end, it captures the excitement of Christmas for the very youngest readers. The sturdy pages are ideal for little hands.

  • Author: Eric Carle
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Board Book, 12 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241527634

title: There's an Elf in Your Book
sheet_title: There S An Elf In Your Book Tom Fletcher
author: Tom Fletcher
description:
There's an Elf in Your Book is an interactive Christmas picture book by Tom Fletcher, illustrated by Greg Abbott. A little elf has crept into the pages to find out whether the reader belongs on the naughty list or the nice list, and asks a few simple questions to decide.

But this elf is rather tricksy, and young readers will need to keep their wits about them to avoid being tempted into mischief and stay on Santa's Nice List. From the team behind There's a Monster in Your Book, it is a playful read-aloud that invites children to join in on every page and makes a fun festive tradition.

  • Author: Tom Fletcher
  • Illustrator: Greg Abbott
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Who's in Your Book?
  • ISBN: 9780241357347

title: Leonora Bolt: Secret Inventor
sheet_title: Leonora Bolt: Secret Inventor Lucy Brandt
author: Lucy Brandt
description:
Leonora Bolt: Secret Inventor is the first adventure in Lucy Brandt's lively series, illustrated by Gladys Jose. Leonora spends her days creating brilliant inventions in a top-secret laboratory on Crabby Island, watched closely by her frightening Uncle Luther.

Then a boy arrives on the shore riding an inflatable lobster, bringing news that Uncle Luther has been taking her creations and selling them across the water. Leaving the island for the very first time, Leonora sets out on a daring journey with a talented otter, a cook of questionable skill and a sea captain who sings, determined to outwit her villainous uncle.

  • Author: Lucy Brandt
  • Illustrator: Gladys Jose
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Leonora Bolt, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780241436769

title: The Christmas Pine
author: Julia Donaldson
description:
The Christmas Pine is a festive picture book by Julia Donaldson, illustrated by Victoria Sandøy. In the heart of a wintry forest, a small pine tree is growing towards a remarkable future: one day it will become a famous Christmas tree.

Told in Donaldson's gentle rhyme, the story traces how the tree travels out of the icy woods to stand in a glittering city square, with atmospheric illustrations that capture the magic of the season. It is a warm, heartfelt choice for sharing at Christmas.

  • Author: Julia Donaldson
  • Illustrator: Victoria Sandøy
  • Publisher: Scholastic
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780702318009

title: The Colour Monster
author: Anna Llenas
description:
The Colour Monster by Anna Llenas is a picture book about understanding feelings. The Colour Monster wakes up in a muddle, with all his emotions jumbled together, and a little girl helps him sort them out, giving each feeling its own colour.

Simple and playful, the story gives young children words for happiness, sadness, anger, fear and calm, and offers parents and teachers a gentle way to start conversations about emotions. This sturdy board book edition is ideal for small hands.

  • Author: Anna Llenas
  • Publisher: Templar Publishing
  • Format: Board Book, 20 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781787412736

title: Start-up Nation: The Story of Israel's Economic Miracle
sheet_title: Start Up Nation Miracle Dan Senor
author: Dan Senor, Saul Singer
description:
Start-up Nation: The Story of Israel's Economic Miracle by Dan Senor and Saul Singer examines why Israel, a small and young country with few natural resources, produces so many new companies. The authors set out to explain how it came to generate more start-ups than far larger economies.

Drawing on their background in foreign policy, they look at a culture that flattens hierarchy and values informality, alongside government policies aimed at innovation, and ask what other economies can learn from it. It will interest readers of business, economics and entrepreneurship, as well as anyone curious about how innovation ecosystems develop.

  • Author: Dan Senor and Saul Singer
  • Publisher: Twelve
  • Format: Paperback, 378 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781455502394

title: How The Grinch Stole Christmas Pocket Edition
sheet_title: How The Grinch Stole Christmas Pocket Edition Dr. Seuss
author: Dr. Seuss
description:
How the Grinch Stole Christmas is Dr. Seuss's timeless festive story, presented here in a handy pocket-sized edition. The grumpy Grinch cannot bear the joy and noise of Christmas in Who-ville, so on Christmas Eve he creeps down from his mountain to steal every present, decoration and festive treat.

But when Christmas morning comes, the Grinch discovers that the spirit of the season cannot be taken away so easily, and his small heart begins to grow. Told in Seuss's famous rhyming verse with his distinctive illustrations, it is a classic to share every December.

  • Author: Dr. Seuss
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Hardcover (pocket edition), 64 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008183493

title: Roald Dahl: On The First Day Of Christmas
sheet_title: Roald Dahl: On The First Day Of Christmas Roald Dahl
author: Roald Dahl
description:
Roald Dahl: On the First Day of Christmas is a festive counting board book featuring Quentin Blake's illustrations of Roald Dahl's characters. It puts a playful twist on the traditional rhyme, beginning with a chiddler giving away a simply enormous crocodile.

Working through the festive countdown with golden tickets, fantastic friends and more, it helps little learners practise their first numbers in a gloriumptious seasonal way. The sturdy pages make it ideal for toddlers.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Board Book, 16 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241492888

title: White Fang
author: Jack London
description:
White Fang is Jack London's classic adventure story, set in the freezing wilderness of the Yukon. Born half dog and half wolf, White Fang is the only pup in his litter to survive, and he quickly learns that life in the wild is governed by harsh laws.

Passed between cruel and kind owners, he must discover whether he can ever trust people again, and his story becomes a powerful portrait of survival, loyalty and the pull between wildness and love. A companion to The Call of the Wild, it is a gripping read for young readers and adults alike.

  • Author: Jack London
  • Publisher: Puffin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 307 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141321110

title: THE CREAKERS
author: Tom Fletcher
description:
The Creakers is a spooky, funny adventure by Tom Fletcher, illustrated by Shane DeVries. What is behind the creaks you hear after dark? Lucy Dungston has always wanted to know, and one morning she discovers that all the adults in her town have disappeared without a trace.

While the other children run riot and enjoy the chaos, Lucy, still missing her late father, is determined to get her mum back and uncover the truth. Nothing will stop her, except perhaps the mysterious Creakers that lurk beneath the bed. Full of humour and heart, it is ideal for confident young readers.

  • Author: Tom Fletcher
  • Illustrator: Shane DeVries
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 342 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141388847

title: Somebody Swallowed Stanley
author: Sarah Roberts
description:
Somebody Swallowed Stanley is a picture book by environmental expert Sarah Roberts with an important message about plastic pollution. Stanley looks a little like a jellyfish, and every sea creature seems to want a taste of him, but he is not quite the jellyfish he seems.

Instead of dangly tentacles he has two handles, and instead of a magical glow he has stripes, because Stanley is really a plastic bag. Through his journey, young children see why plastic bags do not belong in the sea and how waste can harm ocean animals. It is a gentle, eye-opening way to start conversations about caring for the planet.

  • Author: Sarah Roberts
  • Publisher: Scholastic
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781407195100

title: TABBY MCTAT
author: Julia Donaldson
description:
Tabby McTat is a rhyming picture book by Julia Donaldson, illustrated by Axel Scheffler, the team behind The Gruffalo. Tabby McTat is a cat who loves to sing along with his friend Fred, a busker, as he plays his guitar in the street.

When the two friends are separated, Tabby finds himself in a whole new life, but he never forgets Fred. Warm, musical and full of heart, it is a lovely story about friendship and belonging to read aloud together.

  • Author: Julia Donaldson
  • Illustrator: Axel Scheffler
  • Publisher: Alison Green Books
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781407170701

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar's Easter Picnic
sheet_title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar S Easter Picnic Eric Carle
author: Eric Carle
description:
The Very Hungry Caterpillar's Easter Picnic is a springtime board book starring Eric Carle's famous caterpillar. In this Easter adventure, the Very Hungry Caterpillar heads outdoors and meets lots of friendly creatures as they gather for a delicious picnic.

Bright illustrations, easy-to-read sentences and a glittering fold-out finale make it a cheerful seasonal treat for babies and toddlers. The sturdy pages are made for small hands.

  • Author: Eric Carle
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Board Book, 12 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241553527

title: The Red Pony
author: John Steinbeck
description:
The Red Pony is John Steinbeck's short, moving novel of boyhood on a California ranch. Ten-year-old Jody Tiflin is given a small red colt by his father, on the condition that he learns to feed, groom and care for it himself.

Through the colt and other experiences on the ranch, Jody discovers that responsibility can bring sacrifice and pain, that happiness can quickly turn to sorrow, and that the simplicity of childhood must give way to the complications of growing up. Told in linked episodes, it is a powerful coming-of-age classic for teenage and adult readers.

  • Author: John Steinbeck
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 112 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241980378

title: Stone Cold
author: Robert Swindells
description:
Stone Cold is Robert Swindells' gripping novel about life on the streets. At sixteen, Link finds himself homeless, frightened and alone in London, cut off from his family and getting by with help from Ginger, a friend who knows how the streets work.

Then Ginger disappears, and as other homeless young people start vanishing one by one, Link begins to sense that something terrible is happening. Told partly from the point of view of a chilling killer, it is a tense, thought-provoking thriller that is widely read in schools and suits teenage readers.

  • Author: Robert Swindells
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141368993

title: Secret Seven: Three Cheers Secret Seven: Book 8
sheet_title: Secret Seven: Three Cheers Secret Seven: Book 8 Enid Blyton
author: Enid Blyton
description:
Three Cheers, Secret Seven is the eighth book in Enid Blyton's classic Secret Seven mystery series. While searching for their lost model aeroplane, Peter and Jack stumble on a deserted old house where a fire is burning in one of the rooms. Someone must be staying there, but who, and for what reason?

First published in 1956, the story appears here with its classic text, illustrated throughout by Tony Ross, and a bonus section of quizzes and puzzles at the back. It is a great pick for young readers who love mysteries and detective clubs.

  • Author: Enid Blyton
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: Hodder Children's Books
  • Format: Mass Market Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Secret Seven, Book 8
  • ISBN: 9781444913507

title: Percy Jackson And The Sea Of Monsters
sheet_title: Percy Jackson And The Sea Of Monsters
author: Rick Riordan
description:
Percy Jackson and the Sea of Monsters is the second book in Rick Riordan's Percy Jackson and the Olympians series. Percy, the son of Poseidon, is finding that life as a half-blood never gets easier, when even a game of dodgeball turns into a fight against a gang of cannibal giants.

Meanwhile, the protective magic around Camp Half-Blood is failing, and only the Golden Fleece can save it from a monster invasion. Packed with Greek mythology, humour and nonstop action, it is a must for young fantasy fans following Percy's adventures.

  • Author: Rick Riordan
  • Publisher: Puffin

When twelve-year-old Tammy disappears, her remote Northumberland village is turned upside down, but Tammy's twin, Ethan, is sure she is safe and knows the astonishing truth about where she has gone. If he reveals it, he may lose her for good.

Refusing to give up, Ethan joins forces with his friend Iggy, Hellyann, a hairy and mysterious stranger, a trained chicken named Suzy and a spaceship called Philip for a breathless race to bring his sister home. Over one long night, Clay listens to every tape, following Hannah's directions around their small town and piecing together what happened to her. Told in two intertwining voices, the novel deals honestly with bullying, isolation and suicide, and is a powerful, thought-provoking read for teenagers and adults, best approached with care given its subject matter.

Gladwell profiles inventors, entrepreneurs and pitchmen, including the people behind the contraceptive pill and the salesman Ron Popeil, and explores how we hire, predict and judge. Curious, lively and full of surprising connections, it is a great introduction to his work for readers who enjoy psychology, business and ideas that change how you see the everyday.

sheet_title: The Bridgertons: Happily Ever After Julia Quinn
author: Julia Quinn
description:
The Bridgertons: Happily Ever After is a collection by Julia Quinn that revisits the family at the heart of her Regency-era Bridgerton novels, the series behind the Netflix drama. It gathers her second epilogues, short follow-up stories set after each of the eight original books ends, showing what became of the couples readers came to love.

The volume also includes a novella about Violet Bridgerton, mother of the eight siblings, alongside epilogues to novels including Romancing Mister Bridgerton and The Duke and I. Warm, witty and romantic, it is a treat for fans of the series who want more time with the family.

  • Author: Julia Quinn
  • Publisher: Avon
  • Format: Mass Market Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Bridgertons (companion collection)
  • ISBN: 9780063141278

title: The Mark Of Athena Heroes Of Olympus Book 3
sheet_title: The Mark Of Athena Heroes Of Olympus Book 3
author: Rick Riordan
description:
The Mark of Athena is the third book in Rick Riordan's Heroes of Olympus series, which continues the world of Percy Jackson. Annabeth is on the verge of seeing Percy again after six months apart, but as she, Jason, Piper and Leo arrive at Camp Jupiter aboard the warship Argo II, the Roman demigods seem ready for war.

Annabeth also carries a troubling message from her mother, Athena, that sends her on a dangerous personal quest, while the prophecy of the seven demigods pushes the group towards closing the Doors of Death. Packed with Greek and Roman mythology, humour and friendship, it suits readers who loved the Percy Jackson books.

  • Author: Rick Riordan
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 602 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Heroes of Olympus, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780141335766

title: THE SILMARILLION
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description:
The Silmarillion is J.R.R. Tolkien's history of the Elder Days, the First Age of Middle-earth, edited and published after his death by his son Christopher Tolkien. It tells of the creation of the world, the coming of the Elves and the long war waged against Morgoth, the first Dark Lord, over the Silmarils, three jewels holding the light of Valinor.

Written in a grand, mythic style, it provides the ancient backdrop to The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, including the earlier deeds of figures like Elrond and Galadriel. It is essential reading for devoted Tolkien fans and anyone drawn to epic, legend-rich fantasy.

  • Author: J.R.R. Tolkien
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Middle-earth
  • ISBN: 9780007523221

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
description:
Man's Search for Meaning is psychiatrist Viktor E. Frankl's account of surviving Auschwitz and several other Nazi camps during the Second World War. Drawing on his own experience and on what he observed in fellow prisoners, he reflects on how people endure unimaginable suffering and why some find the strength to carry on.

The book goes on to introduce logotherapy, Frankl's approach to psychology, which holds that our main drive in life is the search for meaning. Brief, profound and deeply humane, it is regarded as a classic of Holocaust literature and offers lasting insight to anyone seeking purpose in their own life.

  • Author: Viktor E. Frankl
  • Publisher: Rider
  • Format: Paperback, 156 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781844132393

title: Imagine Me
author: Tahereh Mafi
description:
Imagine Me is the sixth book in Tahereh Mafi's Shatter Me series, a young adult dystopian romance. Now that Ella understands who Juliette is and the purpose she was created for, her world has only grown more complicated, and the line between the two identities is starting to blur.

Haunted by her past and facing an uncertain future, she must decide which side she will fight on as old enemies close in and a final reckoning with the Reestablishment draws near. Intense and emotional, it suits readers who have followed Juliette's journey from the start.

  • Author: Tahereh Mafi
  • Publisher: Electric Monkey
  • Format: Paperback, 450 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Shatter Me, Book 6
  • ISBN: 9781405297042

title: The Paper Palace
author: Miranda Cowley Heller
description:
The Paper Palace is a novel by Miranda Cowley Heller set at a family holiday home in the woods of Cape Cod. One August morning, Elle Bishop slips into the pond for a swim and thinks back to the night before, when she gave in to a passionate encounter with someone other than her husband, just outside the house that holds all her secrets.

Unfolding across a single day and five decades, the story moves between Elle's present and her past, revealing the loves, losses and family secrets that led her here and the life-changing choice she now faces. Absorbing and emotionally charged, it suits book clubs and lovers of literary fiction.

  • Author: Miranda Cowley Heller
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241990452

title: Losing Hope
author: Colleen Hoover
description:
Losing Hope is the companion novel to Colleen Hoover's Hopeless, retelling the story from the perspective of Dean Holder. For thirteen years Holder has been unable to move past the day his childhood best friend, Hope, was taken, and he has never stopped blaming himself for losing her.

Then he meets Sky, who looks just like the little girl he lost but has no idea who he is. As he falls for her, Holder must face his guilt and the truth about the past. Emotional and intense, it deepens the story of Hopeless and is best read after it. It deals with themes of abuse and trauma.

  • Author: Colleen Hoover
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster UK
  • Format: Paperback, 353 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Hopeless, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781471132810

title: PURPLE COW TRANSFORM YOUR BUSINESS BY BEING REMARKABLE
sheet_title: PURPLE COW TRANSFORM YOUR BUSINESS BY BEING REMARKABLE
author: Seth Godin
description:
Purple Cow: Transform Your Business by Being Remarkable is Seth Godin's short, punchy argument that the old rules of marketing no longer work. In a world crowded with choice, he says, playing it safe makes a product invisible, and the only way to stand out is to create something genuinely remarkable from the start.

Using examples of companies that grew by doing something unexpected, Godin shows why remarkability must be built into the product itself rather than added later through advertising. Quick to read and full of ideas, it suits entrepreneurs, marketers and business leaders looking for a fresh way to think about growth.

  • Author: Seth Godin
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141016405

title: The Hating Game
author: Sally Thorne
description:
The Hating Game is Sally Thorne's office romantic comedy about two executive assistants who cannot stand each other. Lucy Hutton is cheerful, cake-baking and liked by almost everyone at work, except Joshua Templeman, her cold, unsmiling rival, who sits opposite her every single day.

Their days are filled with petty games of one-upmanship, and when both go for the same promotion, the stakes rise. But as the rivalry heats up, Lucy begins to wonder whether hate is really what she feels. Witty, sharp and full of chemistry, it is a must for fans of enemies-to-lovers romance.

  • Author: Sally Thorne
  • Publisher: Hachette
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780349414263

title: The Rooster Bar Number One Bestseller
sheet_title: The Rooster Bar Number One Bestseller John Grisham
author: John Grisham
description:
The Rooster Bar is a legal thriller by John Grisham about three third-year law students, Mark, Todd and Zola, who enrolled hoping to make a difference in the world. Instead, they find themselves buried under huge loans at a second-rate for-profit law school whose graduates seldom pass the bar exam.

When they discover the school belongs to a shady hedge-fund operator who also owns a bank that profits from student loans, the friends begin to plot a daring escape from their debt and a way to expose the scam. Sharp, fast-paced and timely, it suits fans of Grisham's courtroom and con-artist stories.

  • Author: John Grisham
  • Publisher: Hachette UK
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781473616981

title: The Basic Laws of Human Stupidity The International Bestsel
sheet_title: The Basic Laws of Human Stupidity The International Bestsel
author: Carlo M. Cipolla
description:
The Basic Laws of Human Stupidity is a short, witty essay by Carlo M. Cipolla, the late Italian economic historian who taught for many years at Berkeley in California. Tongue firmly in cheek, he sets out five laws explaining how stupid people, who harm others without gaining anything for themselves, shape human affairs far more than we care to admit.

Using a simple economic model, Cipolla shows how to recognise this force at work, whether in boardrooms, politics or everyday life. Compact, clever and very funny, this hardback makes a thoughtful gift and an entertaining read for anyone who has ever despaired at the foolishness around them.

  • Author: Carlo M. Cipolla
  • Publisher: WH Allen
  • Format: Hardcover, 96 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780753554838

title: Spoon Fed
author: Tim Spector
description:
Spoon-Fed: Why Almost Everything We've Been Told About Food Is Wrong is a myth-busting book by Tim Spector, a leading scientist in food and nutrition research. Despite constant headlines and endless dietary advice, he argues, many of our firmest beliefs about healthy eating rest on surprisingly weak evidence.

In short, accessible chapters, Spector takes on popular food rules one by one, explaining what the science actually says and why each of us responds differently to what we eat. Practical and eye-opening, it suits anyone who wants to make better-informed choices about their diet and health.

  • Author: Tim Spector
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 286 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529112733

title: The Communication Book: 44 Ideas for Better Conversations Every Day
sheet_title: The Communication Book 44 Ideas For Better Conversations Eve
author: Mikael Krogerus and Roman Tschäppeler
description:
The Communication Book: 44 Ideas for Better Conversations Every Day is a compact guide by Mikael Krogerus and Roman Tschäppeler, the authors of The Decision Book. It gathers short, practical models and ideas for talking, listening and getting your point across more effectively.

Presented in the authors' trademark bite-sized format, it is designed to be dipped into and applied straight away, at work or at home. It suits professionals, managers and anyone who wants to communicate with more clarity and confidence.

  • Author: Mikael Krogerus and Roman Tschäppeler
  • Publisher: Portfolio Penguin
  • Format: Hardcover, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241982280

title: How Do You Live
author: Genzaburo Yoshino
description:
How Do You Live? is Genzaburo Yoshino's classic Japanese coming-of-age novel, first published in 1937 and available here in English translation. Fifteen-year-old Copper looks down on the crowded streets of Tokyo and, struck by how many lives are unfolding around his own, begins to ask himself the question of the title.

Guided by the thoughtful notes and gentle wisdom of his uncle, Copper wrestles with friendship, courage, poverty and what it means to live well. Hayao Miyazaki has named it a favourite book from his childhood, and it lent its Japanese title to his Studio Ghibli film. Reflective and warm, it suits teenagers and adults alike.

  • Author: Genzaburo Yoshino
  • Publisher: Rider
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846046469

title: Revolting Rhymes (Colour Edition)
author: Roald Dahl
description:
Revolting Rhymes is Roald Dahl's gleefully wicked collection of six well-known fairy tales retold in verse, presented here in a full-colour edition with Quentin Blake's illustrations. Forget the usual happily-ever-afters: Cinderella's prince turns out to have a taste for chopping off heads, and Little Red Riding Hood deals with the wolf in a most unexpected way.

Snow White, Goldilocks, Jack and the Beanstalk and the Three Little Pigs also get the Dahl treatment, with plenty of twists and dark humour. Funny, rhythmic and perfect for reading aloud, it suits children who like their stories a little bit revolting, and the grown-ups who share them.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 46 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141369327

title: The Greatness Guide
author: Robin Sharma
description:
The Greatness Guide is a motivational handbook by Robin Sharma, the leadership coach and author of The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari. It offers a series of short, punchy lessons designed to help readers raise their standards and perform at their best in both their personal and working lives.

Each brief chapter delivers a single idea or practical prompt on themes such as habits, leadership, productivity and living with purpose, so the book can be read straight through or dipped into for a daily boost. It suits professionals, entrepreneurs and anyone looking for fresh motivation to reach their potential.

  • Author: Robin Sharma
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007242870

title: I'm OK, You're OK
sheet_title: I Am Ok You Are Ok Thomas A. Harris
author: Thomas A. Harris
description:
I'm OK, You're OK is psychiatrist Thomas A. Harris's classic of popular psychology, built on the Transactional Analysis theory developed by Eric Berne. Harris explains how each of us moves between three ego states, which he calls Parent, Adult and Child, and how these shape the way we think, feel and communicate with others.

He argues that many people carry the 'not OK' feelings of childhood into adult life, and shows how understanding these patterns can free us to change, make better choices and build healthier relationships. Clear and practical, it suits readers interested in psychology, personal growth and improving how they relate to others.

  • Author: Thomas A. Harris
  • Publisher: Arrow
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099557555

title: The Female Brain Louann Brizendine Md
sheet_title: The Female Brain Louann Brizendine Md
author: Louann Brizendine
description:
The Female Brain is a popular-science book by neuropsychiatrist Dr Louann Brizendine that explores how hormones and brain structure shape women's lives. She describes the female brain as unusually flexible and constantly changing, and examines how this affects the way women think, communicate, form relationships and decide what matters to them.

Following the brain through each stage of life, from girlhood and adolescence to pregnancy, motherhood and menopause, Brizendine explains the biology behind everyday differences between women and men. Accessible and engaging, it suits general readers curious about neuroscience, psychology and women's health.

  • Author: Louann Brizendine
  • Publisher: Bantam (Transworld Publishers)
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780553818499

title: WITHOUT MERIT
author: Colleen Hoover
description:
Without Merit is a novel by Colleen Hoover about the far-from-ordinary Voss family, who live in a converted church. The household includes a mother who has moved into the basement after her battle with cancer, a father now married to her former nurse, a sheltered younger half-brother and two older siblings who seem annoyingly perfect.

Then there is Merit, who collects trophies she has never earned and keeps far too many secrets. When she decides the truth must finally come out, the fallout forces the whole family to face what they have been hiding. Funny and moving, it explores family, honesty and mental health, and suits readers of emotional contemporary fiction.

  • Author: Colleen Hoover
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781471174018

title: Switch: How To Change Things When Change Is Hard Dan Heath
sheet_title: Switch: How To Change Things When Change Is Hard Dan Heath
author: Chip Heath and Dan Heath
description:
Switch: How to Change Things When Change Is Hard is a book by brothers Chip Heath and Dan Heath, the authors of Made to Stick. It asks why lasting change is so difficult, whether in companies, communities or our own lives, and traces the answer to a tug-of-war between our rational and emotional sides.

Using the memorable image of a rider steering an elephant along a path, the Heaths offer a practical framework for making change stick, illustrated with real stories of people who achieved dramatic results with limited resources. Clear and engaging, it suits managers, leaders and anyone trying to change habits at work or at home.

  • Author: Chip Heath and Dan Heath
  • Publisher: Random House Business
  • Format: Paperback, 305 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847940322

title: WHO MOVED MY CHEESE?
author: Spencer Johnson
description:
Who Moved My Cheese? is Dr Spencer Johnson's short parable about dealing with change, with a foreword by Kenneth Blanchard. It follows four characters, two mice and two little people, who inhabit a maze and search for the cheese that keeps them nourished and happy, until one day it disappears.

The cheese stands for whatever we want from life, from a job or relationship to health or peace of mind, while the maze represents the places we look for it. Quick to read yet thought-provoking, the story shows how different attitudes to change lead to very different outcomes, making it useful for teams, managers and individuals facing change.

  • Author: Spencer Johnson
  • Foreword: Kenneth Blanchard
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 95 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780091816971

title: Scrum: The Art of Doing Twice the Work in Half the Time
sheet_title: Scrum: Art Of Doing Twice Work In Half Time Jeff Sutherland
author: Jeff Sutherland
description:
Scrum: The Art of Doing Twice the Work in Half the Time is Jeff Sutherland's account of the Scrum method, written by one of its co-creators. Scrum is an approach to project management and teamwork that began in software development and has since been adopted in sectors from healthcare to the military.

Sutherland explains how Scrum works in practice, using short cycles, constant feedback and small, focused teams to deliver results faster, and shows how its principles can be applied to almost any kind of work or project. Practical and full of real examples, it suits managers, team leaders and anyone looking to boost productivity.

  • Author: Jeff Sutherland
  • Publisher: Random House Business
  • Format: Paperback, 248 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847941107

title: Slammed
author: Colleen Hoover
description:
Slammed is the first book in Colleen Hoover's Slammed series, a young adult romance. After the sudden death of her father, Layken finds herself holding her family together, and when her mother takes a new job they move across the country to Michigan.

There she meets her new neighbour, Will Cooper, whose love of slam poetry is matched only by his zest for life. The pair share an instant connection, until a shocking revelation threatens to end their romance before it has begun. Heartfelt and poetic, it suits readers who enjoy emotional love stories.

  • Author: Colleen Hoover
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster UK
  • Format: Paperback, 317 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Slammed, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781471125676

title: Steve Jobs: Volume 48 Maria Isabel Sanchez Vegara
sheet_title: Steve Jobs: Volume 48 Maria Isabel Sanchez Vegara
author: Maria Isabel Sánchez Vegara
description:
Steve Jobs is a picture-book biography from the Little People, BIG DREAMS series, written by Maria Isabel Sánchez Vegara and illustrated by Aura Lewis. It tells how Steve Jobs grew up among inventors in California's Silicon Valley and, with his friend Steve Wozniak, turned a passion for computers into a company started in a garage.

Young readers discover how his belief that computers were the future helped change the way people use technology. With stylish illustrations, plus a short timeline and further facts at the end, it is an inspiring introduction to a visionary inventor for children who love to build and create.

  • Author: Maria Isabel Sánchez Vegara
  • Illustrator: Aura Lewis
  • Publisher: Frances Lincoln
  • Format: Hardcover, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Little People, BIG DREAMS, Volume 48
  • ISBN: 9780711245761

title: The Next Person You Meet in Heaven The sequel to The Five P
sheet_title: The Next Person You Meet in Heaven The sequel to The Five P
author: Mitch Albom
description:
The Next Person You Meet in Heaven is Mitch Albom's sequel to The Five People You Meet in Heaven. In the first book, Eddie, an amusement-park maintenance man and former soldier, died saving a little girl named Annie. This novel tells Annie's story, following the girl he rescued as she grows up marked by that accident.

When a tragic event sends Annie to heaven, she meets five people of her own, each revealing how her life connected with others and leading to a reunion with Eddie. Gentle and moving, it explores loss, love and the idea that every life matters, and suits readers who were touched by the first book.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Hachette
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Five People You Meet in Heaven, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780751571912

title: We Are Not Like Them
sheet_title: We Are Not Like Them Christine Pride
author: Christine Pride and Jo Piazza
description:
We Are Not Like Them is a novel by Christine Pride and Jo Piazza about a lifelong friendship tested by tragedy. Jen, who is white, and Riley, who is Black, have been inseparable since kindergarten in Philadelphia and are still as close as sisters, even as their lives have taken different paths.

Jen is finally pregnant after years of trying, and Riley is about to become among the first Black women to anchor the news on a leading local channel. Their bond is pushed to breaking point when Jen's police-officer husband shoots an unarmed Black teenager. Told in alternating chapters, it is a powerful book club read about race, loyalty and friendship.

  • Author: Christine Pride and Jo Piazza
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008335977

title: With Fire In Their Blood: Tiktok
sheet_title: With Fire In Their Blood: Tiktok Kat Delacorte
author: Kat Delacorte
description:
With Fire in Their Blood is the first book in Kat Delacorte's Skeleton Keepers series, a young adult supernatural romance. Sixteen-year-old Lilly Deluca is far from thrilled when she moves to Castello, an isolated, crumbling mountain town in Italy, to finish her final years of high school.

Castello is split in two by a long and brutal war between mafia-style clans, held in check only by a mysterious leader known as the General, while dark magic runs through its streets. As Lilly is drawn into its secrets and dangers, she discovers that the past is far from buried. Atmospheric and romantic, it suits fans of dark fantasy.

  • Author: Kat Delacorte
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Skeleton Keepers, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780241487624

title: King Of Fools
author: Amanda Foody
description:
King of Fools is the second instalment of Amanda Foody's Shadow Game series, the sequel to Ace of Shades. Winning the Shadow Game has not brought the victory Enne Salta and con man Levi Glaiyser hoped for: they are now wanted for murder, and Enne must hide in plain sight as the mysterious underworld figure Séance.

In the City of Sin, Levi makes a risky bargain with Vianca Augustine's estranged son in pursuit of freedom and power, while Enne is still held by a binding promise to Vianca. As a street war brews and new players appear, both face an impossible choice between survival and legend. Rich and twisty, it suits readers of YA crime fantasy.

  • Author: Amanda Foody
  • Publisher: Inkyard Press
  • Format: Paperback, 608 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Shadow Game, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781335040015

title: THE FAULT IN OUR STARS
author: John Green
description:
The Fault in Our Stars is John Green's moving young adult novel about Hazel Grace Lancaster, a sixteen-year-old living with terminal cancer. A medical breakthrough has bought her extra time, but she has always known her story will be cut short, until she meets Augustus Waters at a cancer support group.

Witty, charming and fearless, Augustus turns Hazel's world upside down, and together they set off on an unforgettable journey that leads them to Amsterdam. Funny, heartbreaking and full of big questions about life, love and mortality, it suits teenagers and adults alike and was later adapted for the screen.

  • Author: John Green
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 313 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141345659

title: He Said/She Said: Must Read Bestselling
sheet_title: He Said/She Said: Must Read Bestselling Erin Kelly
author: Erin Kelly
description:
He Said/She Said is a psychological thriller by Erin Kelly. In 1999, young couple Kit and Laura head to a Cornish festival to see a total solar eclipse. In the hush after the shadow passes, Laura stumbles upon a man and a woman and is certain she has witnessed a terrible crime, but he denies it.

Laura's testimony sets her word against his, and the grateful victim soon becomes an unsettling presence in the couple's lives. Fifteen years on, Kit and Laura are still living with the consequences of that day. Twisty and tense, it explores truth, trust and consent, and suits fans of slow-burn suspense.

  • Author: Erin Kelly
  • Publisher: Hachette
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781444797145

title: It'S Not Summer Without You
author: Jenny Han
description:
It's Not Summer Without You is the second book in Jenny Han's Summer trilogy, which began with The Summer I Turned Pretty. A year ago, everything Belly had dreamed of finally came true, and she could never have imagined missing a summer at Cousins Beach. Now the season she once lived for is one she dreads.

When Jeremiah calls to say that Conrad has vanished, Belly has to decide how to spend this summer: pursuing the boy she loves or letting go for good. Tender and bittersweet, it explores grief, first love and growing up, and suits readers who enjoyed the TV adaptation.

  • Author: Jenny Han
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Summer, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780141330556

title: The Spanish Love Deception TikTok made me buy it!
sheet_title: The Spanish Love Deception TikTok made me buy it!
author: Elena Armas
description:
The Spanish Love Deception is Elena Armas's fake-dating romantic comedy. Catalina Martín urgently needs a date for her sister's wedding in Spain, after a small fib about an American boyfriend gets completely out of hand. Her ex and his new fiancée are among the guests, and everyone is dying to meet him.

With only a month to find a willing partner, she is stunned when Aaron Blackford, her tall, infuriating and condescending colleague, volunteers for the job. What follows is a slow-burn, enemies-to-lovers story full of banter, family chaos and growing tension. Warm and funny, it suits readers who love workplace rivals and big romantic payoffs.

  • Author: Elena Armas
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster UK
  • Format: Paperback, 468 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Spanish Love Deception, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781398515628

title: The Stranger: Now A Major Netflix Show
sheet_title: The Stranger: Now A Major Netflix Show Harlan Coben
author: Harlan Coben
description:
The Stranger is a thriller by Harlan Coben, later adapted as a Netflix series. A stranger appears out of nowhere, whispers a devastating secret, and vanishes, leaving lives in pieces. Adam Price seems to have it all: a loving marriage, two sons, a comfortable home and a good job.

Then a stranger tells him something about his wife, Corinne, that shatters everything he believed. When he confronts her, the perfect picture falls apart, and Adam is drawn into a conspiracy far bigger and more dangerous than he could have imagined. Gripping and twisty, it suits fans of suburban suspense and domestic thrillers.

  • Author: Harlan Coben
  • Publisher: Orion
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781409197959

title: The First Phone Call From Heaven
sheet_title: The First Phone Call From Heaven Mitch Albom
author: Mitch Albom
description:
The First Phone Call from Heaven is a novel by Mitch Albom set in Coldwater, a little lakeside town in Michigan. When several residents begin receiving phone calls they believe come from loved ones who have died, the town suddenly finds itself the focus of worldwide attention.

Is it a miracle or an elaborate hoax? Sully Harding, a grieving single father, sets out to discover the truth. Combining a gripping mystery with reflections on faith, grief and hope, it is a thought-provoking read for fans of Albom's uplifting storytelling and anyone who has lost someone they love.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751541205

title: Men Are From Mars Women Are From Venus
sheet_title: Men Are From Mars Women Are From Venus John Gray
author: John Gray
description:
Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus is Dr John Gray's classic relationship guide. Using the memorable idea that men and women seem to come from different planets, he explores how the sexes often differ in their needs, emotional responses and ways of communicating, and how misunderstandings can grow from those differences.

Gray offers practical advice for listening, expressing feelings, handling conflict and offering support in ways a partner can truly hear and appreciate. Easy to read and full of everyday examples, it suits couples and anyone hoping to build stronger, more understanding relationships.

  • Author: John Gray
  • Publisher: Thorsons
  • Format: Paperback, 286 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780722538449

title: Never Never
author: Colleen Hoover and Tarryn Fisher
description:
Never Never brings together the complete Never Never trilogy by Colleen Hoover and Tarryn Fisher in a single volume, a romantic mystery with a twist. Charlie Wynwood and Silas Nash grew up as best friends and fell in love at fourteen, but one morning they wake up as total strangers.

Every memory they shared, from their first kiss to the day they fell for each other, has disappeared. Working together to piece together the cause, they begin to uncover truths they may have been better off forgetting. Gripping and twisty, it suits fans of both authors and readers who like romance with suspense.

  • Author: Colleen Hoover and Tarryn Fisher
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 358 pages
  • Language: English

In her twenties, Emma Blair weds Jesse, her sweetheart since high school, and the pair travel the world together, far from their Massachusetts hometown. Then, a year into their marriage, Jesse's helicopter vanishes over the Pacific.

Queen of Air and Darkness is the third and final book in Cassandra Clare's Dark Artifices trilogy, part of her wider Shadowhunter Chronicles. After Livia Blackthorn is killed at the Council Hall, the Clave stands on the edge of civil war and the Shadowhunter world is thrown into turmoil.
