Little Fires Everywhere is a novel by Celeste Ng set in Shaker Heights, an orderly, carefully planned suburb of Cleveland where everyone is expected to follow the rules. Georgia Stanton's grandmother, the celebrated romance novelist Scarlett Stanton, died before finishing her final book, and Georgia is set on seeing the story completed. When a mysterious woman arrives at the inn and begins telling stories, the villagers slowly change, and Rendi comes to see that his own story may hold the answers he is looking for. Inspired by Chinese folklore, it is a gentle, beautifully woven tale for middle-grade readers and families.

  • Publisher: Little, Brown Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780316125970

The Bromance Book Club is the first book in Lyssa Kay Adams's romantic comedy series of the same name. Nashville baseball star Gavin Scott's marriage is in serious trouble, and when his wife Thea asks for a divorce, he realises his pride may have cost him everything.

Help comes from an unlikely place: a secret book club of tough, successful men who read romance novels for relationship advice. With a Regency romance as their guide, they coach Gavin on winning Thea back. Funny, heartfelt and a little steamy, it suits readers who enjoy rom-coms about second chances in love.

  • Publisher: Headline Eternal
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages

author: Anna Todd

The Burning is the second novel in the Brightest Stars series by Anna Todd, author of the After books. It continues the passionate, emotional love story of Karina that began in the first instalment, set against a military backdrop.

Intense and romantic, it suits new adult readers who enjoy dramatic contemporary love stories and want to follow the series onward.

  • Publisher: Little, Brown Book Group
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Brightest Stars, Book 2

author: Mohsin Hamid
description:
The Last White Man is a short novel by Mohsin Hamid. One morning Anders wakes to find that his skin has turned dark and the face in the mirror no longer feels like his own. At first he confides only in his old friend Oona, but soon similar changes are being reported across the town and beyond.

Told in Hamid's flowing, hypnotic prose, the story becomes a fable about race, identity, fear and love as a society faces sweeping transformation. Brief but powerful, it suits readers of thought-provoking literary fiction and fans of Hamid's earlier novel Exit West.

  • Author: Mohsin Hamid
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241995556

title: Tower Of Dawn
sheet_title: Tower Of Dawn Sarah J. Maas
author: Sarah J. Maas
description:
Tower of Dawn is the sixth book in Sarah J. Maas's Throne of Glass series, moving the story to the Southern Continent. Chaol Westfall and Nesryn Faliq travel to the city of Antica, hoping to win the Khagan's vast armies to Erilea's cause and to find healing for Chaol at the Torre Cesme.

There Chaol meets Yrene Towers, a gifted healer with every reason to hate anyone from Adarlan, and both must face their own wounds as ancient secrets come to light. Running alongside the events of Empire of Storms, it suits fans of the series and readers of sweeping romantic fantasy.

  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 660 pages
  • Language: English

  • ISBN: 9781526635280

title: Unwind
author: Neal Shusterman
vendor: Simon & Schuster Books for Young Readers
description:
Unwind is the first book in Neal Shusterman's Unwind Dystology. After a second American civil war fought over reproductive rights, a settlement allows parents to have teenagers between thirteen and eighteen unwound, with every part of their bodies transplanted into other people so that, technically, their lives never end.

The novel follows three teens marked for unwinding, Connor, Risa and Lev, as they run for their lives and push back against the system. Gripping and provocative, it raises hard questions about the value of life and who gets to decide it, making it a powerful read for teen and adult fans of dystopian fiction.

  • Author: Neal Shusterman
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Unwind Dystology, Book 1

title: One Day I Shall Astonish The World
sheet_title: One Day I Shall Astonish The World Nina Stibbe
author: Nina Stibbe
description:
One Day I Shall Astonish the World is a novel by Nina Stibbe about a friendship that spans three decades. Susan and Norma are first brought together by a job at The Pin Cushion, a haberdashery in 1990s Leicestershire, and stay close largely because neither is very keen on making other friends.

Thirty years on, with Susan's husband chasing immortality and Norma increasingly out of reach, their bond is put to the test. Funny, tender and full of sharp observation, it explores the ebbs and flows of female friendship and suits readers who enjoy warm, witty British fiction.

  • Author: Nina Stibbe
  • Publisher: Viking
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241451175

title: Talking to My Daughter A Brief History of Capitalism
sheet_title: Talking to My Daughter A Brief History of Capitalism
author: Yanis Varoufakis
description:
Talking to My Daughter: A Brief History of Capitalism is an introduction to economics by Yanis Varoufakis, the economist and former Greek finance minister. Written as a series of letters prompted by his daughter Xenia's questions, beginning with why there is so much inequality, it explains how markets, money, debt and capitalism came to shape the world.

Varoufakis draws on familiar stories, from Greek myths such as Oedipus to Faust, Frankenstein and The Matrix, to make complex ideas easy to grasp. Engaging and approachable, it suits curious teenagers and adults who want to understand the economy without the jargon.

  • Author: Yanis Varoufakis
  • Publisher: Random House UK
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784705756

title: The Last Lecture
author: Randy Pausch, Jeffrey Zaslow
description:
The Last Lecture: Lessons in Living is the memoir of Randy Pausch, a computer science professor at Carnegie Mellon University, written with journalist Jeffrey Zaslow. After learning that he had terminal pancreatic cancer, Pausch gave a final lecture on achieving childhood dreams, and the talk was widely shared around the world.

The book expands on that lecture with stories and advice about living fully, overcoming obstacles, helping others and making the most of the time we have. Funny, moving and full of practical wisdom, it was written as a lasting gift for his young children and is an inspiring read for anyone.

  • Author: Randy Pausch with Jeffrey Zaslow
  • Publisher: Hodder
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English

title: The Wrath & The Dawn Renee Ahdieh
sheet_title: The Wrath & The Dawn Renee Ahdieh
author: Renée Ahdieh
vendor: G.P. Putnam's Sons Books for Young Readers
description:
The Wrath and the Dawn is the first book in Renée Ahdieh's young adult fantasy duology, inspired by One Thousand and One Nights. Khalid, the teenage Caliph of Khorasan, marries a new bride every night and has her executed at sunrise. When Shahrzad, just sixteen, offers herself as his next wife, she has a plan to survive and to avenge her best friend.

Shahrzad's wit carries her past the first dawn, but she finds herself falling for the very ruler she meant to destroy, and learns that he is not what he seems. Lush, romantic and full of intrigue, it suits readers who enjoy retellings and slow-burn fantasy romance.

  • Author: Renée Ahdieh

  • Format: Paperback, 422 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Wrath and the Dawn, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780147513854

title: Protecting What's Mine
author: Lucy Score
description:
Protecting What's Mine is the third book in Lucy Score's Benevolence series of small-town romances. Fire chief Lincoln Reed enjoys an easy, carefree life, until Mackenzie O'Neil, a flight trauma surgeon, turns up at one of his accident scenes and then becomes his new neighbour.

Close to burnout, Mackenzie has taken a temporary post as a small-town family doctor and has no intention of falling for a flirtatious firefighter. But Linc is persistent, and a casual fling between neighbours soon turns into something more. Steamy and funny, it suits fans of small-town romance.

  • Author: Lucy Score
  • Publisher: Hodder
  • Format: Paperback, 464 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Benevolence, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781399726863

title: Shift: The Thrilling Dystopian
sheet_title: Shift: The Thrilling Dystopian Hugh Howey
author: Hugh Howey
description:
Shift is the second book in Hugh Howey's Silo series and a prequel to Wool. It goes back to the beginning, revealing how the underground silos came to exist and how humanity reached the brink of its own destruction, from advances in nanotechnology to a drug able to erase traumatic memories.

Moving between the near future and life inside the silos, the novel uncovers the secrets behind the world readers first met in Wool. Tense and thought-provoking, it suits fans of dystopian and post-apocalyptic science fiction who want to know how it all began.

  • Author: Hugh Howey
  • Publisher: Penguin Cornerstone
  • Format: Paperback, 592 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Silo, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781804940839

title: Loathe To Love You
sheet_title: Loathe To Love You Ali Hazelwood
author: Ali Hazelwood
description:
Loathe to Love You brings together Ali Hazelwood's three STEMinist novellas in one paperback, plus an exclusive extra chapter. Three friends, Mara, Sadie and Hannah, are dedicated scientists whose love lives turn out to be every bit as complicated as their research.

In Under One Roof, an environmental engineer ends up sharing a house with an infuriating oil-company lawyer; in Stuck with You, a civil engineer is trapped in a New York lift with her rival; and in Below Zero, an engineer in trouble in the Arctic is rescued by her long-time nemesis. Witty and romantic, it suits fans of enemies-to-lovers stories.

  • Author: Ali Hazelwood
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 370 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The STEMinist Novellas, Books 1-3
  • ISBN: 9781408726778

title: The Worst Best Man
sheet_title: The Worst Best Man Lucy Score
author: Lucy Score
description:
The Worst Best Man is an enemies-to-lovers romantic comedy by Lucy Score. Franchesca takes her role as maid of honour very seriously, which is just as well, because her best friend's wedding party is full of rich, entitled guests, led by Aiden Kilbourn, an arrogant best man.

Aiden is too occupied with his business empire to want anything long-term, while Franchesca is determined he will not spoil the big day. As the wedding drama unfolds, the sparks between them become impossible to ignore. Funny and steamy, it suits readers who love sharp banter.

  • Author: Lucy Score
  • Publisher: Hodder
  • Format: Paperback, 436 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781399726900

author: Haruki Murakami
description:
Men Without Women is a collection of seven short stories by Haruki Murakami. Each one follows a man who, in his own way, has ended up alone, in a world of lonely hearts and disappearing cats, smoky bars and enigmatic women, with baseball and the Beatles never far away.

Written with Murakami's characteristic wry humour and dreamlike atmosphere, the stories explore loss, love and isolation in quietly unsettling ways. It is an accessible introduction to his work and a rewarding read for existing fans of Japanese literary fiction.

  • Author: Haruki Murakami
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 228 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784705374

title: Gamora & Nebula: Sisters in Arms
sheet_title: Marvel Guardians Of Galaxy Mackenzi Lee
author: Mackenzi Lee

Gamora & Nebula: Sisters in Arms is a Marvel Guardians of the Galaxy novel by Mackenzi Lee, part of the Marvel Rebels & Renegades series. It centres on Gamora and Nebula, the adopted daughters of Thanos, raised as rivals and trained to fight for him.

When Gamora is sent to a once-thriving planet that has been stripped of its resources and left a toxic, dying desert, the sisters' tangled loyalties are put to the test. Full of action, rivalry and questions of trust, it suits young adult readers and fans of the Guardians of the Galaxy films and comics.

  • Author: Mackenzi Lee
  • Publisher: Autumn Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 393 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Marvel Rebels & Renegades
  • ISBN: 9781800222076

title: Mythos A Retelling of the Myths of Ancient Greece
sheet_title: Mythos A Retelling of the Myths of Ancient Greece
author: Stephen Fry
description:
Mythos is Stephen Fry's retelling of the myths of ancient Greece and the first book in his Great Mythology series. Beginning with the creation of the cosmos, it brings to life the gods, goddesses and mortals of Greek legend, from Athena bursting from the head of Zeus to Persephone's descent into the Underworld.

Fry also recounts Pandora opening her jar of torments and the love story of Eros and Psyche, telling each tale with wit, warmth and an eye for human drama. Lively and accessible, it is a perfect introduction to Greek mythology for adults and older teens.

  • Author: Stephen Fry
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 459 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Stephen Fry's Great Mythology, Book 1

description:
This is the York Notes Advanced study guide to William Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, written by N.H. Keeble. Part of a long-running series of literature guides, it is designed for A-level and undergraduate students studying the play.

The guide introduces more sophisticated analysis of Shakespeare's tragedy of young love and family feud, together with differing critical viewpoints and the play's historical and literary background. It is a useful companion for students preparing essays and exams, to be read alongside the text of the play itself.

  • Format: Paperback, 152 pages

author: Sarah J. Maas

Queen of Shadows is the fourth book in Sarah J. Maas's Throne of Glass series. Celaena Sardothien has accepted who she truly is, Aelin Galathynius, heir to the throne of Terrasen, and returns to Rifthold ready to fight for her kingdom.

Those dearest to Aelin have been taken from her, and she must battle for her warrior cousin, for a friend trapped in a terrible prison and for her people, enslaved under a brutal king. Driven by vengeance, she confronts old enemies and forges new alliances. Packed with action, magic and romance, it is a turning point in the series for fans of epic young adult fantasy.

  • Format: Paperback, 656 pages

title: Waverider

Waverider is the ninth and final volume of Kazu Kibuishi's Amulet graphic novel series. Following her showdown with Ikol, Emily finally grasps her stone's true power and her role in protecting Alledia from the encroaching darkness.

As Emily heads to Typhon to help her mother and her brother Navin, Prince Trellis goes home to the Elf kingdom to confront the fraud who has seized power in his absence. With striking full-colour artwork and high-stakes adventure, it brings the saga to a close for middle-grade readers and longtime fans.

sheet_title: King Lear: No Fear Shakespeare Deluxe Edition Sparknotes
author: William Shakespeare

This deluxe student edition of William Shakespeare's King Lear comes from the SparkNotes No Fear Shakespeare series. In the tragedy, an ageing king divides his kingdom between the daughters who flatter him, rejects the one who truly loves him, and is driven to madness as the consequences unfold.

Each page of the original text sits beside a plain modern English version, making the language easy to follow without losing Shakespeare's own words. It is an ideal companion for students studying the play and for anyone reading King Lear for the first time.

  • Publisher: SparkNotes

sheet_title: Harry Potter And The Goblet Of Fire Book 4 J K Rowling
author: J.K. Rowling
description:
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire is the fourth book in J.K. Rowling's Harry Potter series. Harry, now fourteen, is looking forward to the Quidditch World Cup with his friends and the Weasley family, and to a year at Hogwarts with nothing more than ordinary worries, but nothing in his life stays normal for long.

When Hogwarts hosts the Triwizard Tournament, a contest between three schools of magic not held for a century, Harry is unexpectedly entered and must face dangerous tasks while dark forces gather. Longer and darker than the earlier books, it marks a turning point in the series for readers of all ages.

  • Illustrator: Mary GrandPré
  • Publisher: Scholastic Inc.
  • Format: Paperback, 752 pages

author: Malcolm Gladwell
description:
Talking to Strangers: What We Should Know About the People We Don't Know is a nonfiction book by Malcolm Gladwell, author of The Tipping Point and Outliers. It examines why our encounters with strangers so often go wrong, and why we are so poor at reading the intentions of people we do not know.

Gladwell explores cases from history and the headlines, from the Cuban double agents who deceived the CIA and Neville Chamberlain's meetings with Hitler to the fraud of Bernie Madoff and Amanda Knox's trial. Provocative and highly readable, it suits anyone interested in psychology, communication and human behaviour.

  • Author: Malcolm Gladwell
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141988498

title: The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari Robin S. Sharma
sheet_title: The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari Robin S. Sharma
author: Robin Sharma
description:
The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari is a self-help fable by Robin Sharma. It tells the story of Julian Mantle, a high-flying lawyer whose out-of-balance life drives him to a personal crisis. Leaving his career and possessions behind, he travels to the Himalayas and returns with practical wisdom learned from an ancient culture.

Through Julian's lessons, Sharma offers a practical, staged method for living with more purpose, discipline and joy, including making the most of time, nurturing relationships and following your calling. Simple and inspiring, it suits readers looking for motivation and a calmer, more meaningful way to live.

  • Author: Robin Sharma
  • Publisher: HarperOne
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780062515674

author: Raina Telgemeier
description:
Sisters is a graphic memoir by Raina Telgemeier and the companion to her book Smile. Raina could not wait to become a big sister, but baby Amara turns out to be grumpy and happiest playing on her own, and the two never quite get along as they grow up.

Told through a family road trip from San Francisco to a reunion, with flashbacks woven in, the story shows the sisters learning to rely on each other as a baby brother arrives and tension builds between their parents. Funny and honest, it suits middle-grade readers and anyone who has a sibling.

  • Publisher: Graphix
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages

  • Series: Smile, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781338801880

title: Summer Brain Quest: Between Grades Pre-K & K
sheet_title: SUMMER BRAIN QUEST BETWEEN GRADES PREK and K
author: Bridget Heos
description:
Summer Brain Quest: Between Grades Pre-K & K is an activity workbook for children who have just finished pre-kindergarten and are getting ready for kindergarten. Designed to keep young learners sharp over the summer break, it follows Common Core standards and is packed with hundreds of activities, exercises and games.

A map leads children through the book, covering letters and phonics, early vocabulary, counting, shapes, patterns and the seasons, while stickers let them track their progress. Bonus challenges, outdoor activities, a summer reading list and a Brain Quest mini deck add extra fun for parents and children to share.

  • Author: Bridget Heos
  • Illustrators: Edison Yan and Maris Wicks
  • Publisher: Workman Kids
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781523502998

title: THE FIFTH AGREEMENT
author: Don Miguel Ruiz, Don Jose Ruiz
description:
The Fifth Agreement: A Practical Guide to Self-Mastery is the follow-up to The Four Agreements, written by don Miguel Ruiz with his son, don Jose Ruiz. It revisits the original four agreements from a fresh angle and adds a new one, drawn like the others from ancient Toltec wisdom.

The authors explore how the beliefs we absorb while growing up can distance us from who we really are, and how greater awareness can help us reclaim the genuine self we started life with. Clear and thoughtful, it suits readers of spiritual self-help and anyone who found the first book helpful.

  • Authors: Don Miguel Ruiz and Don Jose Ruiz
  • Publisher: Amber-Allen Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 252 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Toltec Wisdom
  • ISBN: 9781878424617

title: The World For Sale
author: Javier Blas, Jack Farchy
description:
The World for Sale: Money, Power and the Traders Who Barter the Earth's Resources is a work of investigative nonfiction by journalists Javier Blas and Jack Farchy. It takes readers inside the little-known world of commodity trading houses, the firms that buy, move and sell much of the oil, metals and food the global economy depends on.

The authors trace how these traders built vast fortunes and political influence, often doing business with governments and regimes that others avoided. Revealing and highly readable, it suits anyone interested in business, finance, geopolitics and how global markets really work.

  • Authors: Javier Blas and Jack Farchy
  • Publisher: Penguin Cornerstone
  • Format: Paperback, 410 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847942678

title: What They Don't Teach You at Harvard Business School
sheet_title: What They Dont Teach You At Harvard Business School
author: Mark H. McCormack
description:
What They Don't Teach You at Harvard Business School: Notes from a Street-Smart Executive is a practical business book by Mark H. McCormack, founder of the sports management firm International Management Group (IMG). Drawing on his experience of building a global company, he argues that many of the real skills of business are learned from people and practice rather than in the classroom.

McCormack offers advice on reading people, making a strong first impression, running meetings, negotiating, selling and moving up within an organisation. Direct and full of anecdotes, it suits managers, entrepreneurs and anyone starting out in a business career.

  • Author: Mark H. McCormack
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781781253397

title: WHEN BREATH BECOMES AIR
author: Paul Kalanithi
description:
When Breath Becomes Air is the memoir of Paul Kalanithi, a neurosurgeon who learned at the age of thirty-six, as he neared the end of a decade of training, that he had terminal lung cancer. Almost overnight, the doctor who cared for the dying became a patient fighting for his own life.

Kalanithi traces his path from a student fascinated by literature and the question of what makes life meaningful, to a surgeon working on the brain, to a husband and new father facing mortality. Written in the last months of his life, it is a profound and moving reflection for anyone who has faced illness or loss.

  • Author: Paul Kalanithi
  • Publisher: Random House UK
  • Format: Paperback, 229 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784701994

title: Invisible Women
author: Caroline Criado Pérez
description:
Invisible Women: Exposing Data Bias in a World Designed for Men is an investigation by Caroline Criado Pérez into the gender data gap. She shows how much of the information used to design products, plan cities, test medicines and shape policy has been based on men, leaving women overlooked.

Through striking examples, from phones too large for many women's hands to car safety and unpaid work, Criado Pérez reveals the real costs of this bias for women's health, safety and livelihoods. Eye-opening and rigorously researched, it suits readers interested in feminism, economics, design and social justice.

  • Author: Caroline Criado Pérez
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 411 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784706289

title: Just Because
author: Matthew McConaughey
description:
Just Because is the first picture book by actor and author Matthew McConaughey, illustrated by Renee Kurilla. Told in playful rhyming verse, it explores the contradictions we all carry, such as feeling nervous and excited at once, or being hurt but choosing to forgive.

With humour and warmth, McConaughey encourages young readers to see that there may be several right answers and that mixed feelings help make us who we are. It is a thoughtful read-aloud for families and classrooms that opens up conversations about emotions and possibility.

  • Author: Matthew McConaughey
  • Illustrator: Renee Kurilla
  • Publisher: Viking Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Hardcover, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593622032

title: Stillness Is the Key An Ancient Strategy for Modern Life
sheet_title: Stillness Is the Key An Ancient Strategy for Modern Life
author: Ryan Holiday
description:
Stillness Is the Key: An Ancient Strategy for Modern Life is a book by Ryan Holiday on the value of calm and focus. He argues that great leaders, artists and athletes throughout history have shared one quality, the ability to stay steady in a noisy world, which the Stoics called ataraxia and Zen Buddhists described as inner peace.

Drawing on figures from Winston Churchill to Oprah Winfrey, Holiday shows how stillness of mind, spirit and body can be practised day to day. The third book in his series after The Obstacle Is the Way and Ego Is the Enemy, it suits readers of practical philosophy.

  • Author: Ryan Holiday
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Way, The Enemy, and The Key, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781788162067

title: The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read
sheet_title: The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read
author: Philippa Perry
description:
The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read (and Your Children Will Be Glad That You Did) is a parenting guide by psychotherapist Philippa Perry. Rather than a rigid plan, she offers a broad look at what makes for strong, healthy relationships between parents and children.

Perry starts with parents themselves, showing how our own upbringing shapes the way we raise our children, and explains how to repair mistakes, handle feelings and build lasting connection. Warm, wise and free of judgement, it suits parents of children of any age, as well as parents-to-be.

  • Author: Philippa Perry
  • Publisher: Penguin Life
  • Format: Paperback, 266 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241251027

title: The Cloud Searchers Amulet Book Three
sheet_title: The Cloud Searchers Amulet Book Three Kazu Kibuishi
author: Kazu Kibuishi
description:
The Cloud Searchers is the third volume in Kazu Kibuishi's Amulet graphic novel series. Emily, her brother Navin and their band of resistance fighters hire an airship and set out to find Cielis, a lost city where they hope the powerful Stonekeepers of the Guardian Council can help them.

Alledia's survival depends on the mission, and Emily must reach Cielis before the Elf King catches up with her. With vivid full-colour artwork and plenty of danger and suspense, it suits middle-grade readers who enjoy fantasy adventure told in comic form.

  • Author: Kazu Kibuishi
  • Publisher: Graphix
  • Format: Paperback, 203 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Amulet, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780545208857

title: The Last Letter From Your Lover
sheet_title: The Last Letter From Your Lover Jojo Moyes
author: Jojo Moyes
description:
The Last Letter from Your Lover is a novel by Jojo Moyes that weaves together two love stories set decades apart. In 1960, Jennifer Stirling wakes in hospital after a car accident with no memory of her life or her husband, until she finds a passionate letter signed only with a B, urging her to leave him.

In 2003, a journalist named Ellie comes across the same letter in her newspaper's archive and becomes determined to discover what happened. Romantic and absorbing, it explores love, choice and regret, and suits readers who enjoy dual-timeline fiction. The novel was adapted as a Netflix film.

  • Author: Jojo Moyes
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780143136323

title: The Things You Can See Only When You Slow Down
sheet_title: The Things You Can Only See When You Slow Down
author: Haemin Sunim
description:
The Things You Can See Only When You Slow Down is a gentle guide to mindfulness by Haemin Sunim, a Korean-born Buddhist monk who studied in the United States, translated from the Korean. Built from short reflections that began as replies to questions on social media, it offers advice on setbacks, rest, relationships and the pressures of modern life.

Paired with calming full-colour illustrations, his simple teachings remind readers how much calm and happiness slowing our pace can bring. Easy to dip into, it suits anyone feeling overwhelmed and looking for quiet encouragement.

  • Author: Haemin Sunim
  • Publisher: Penguin Life
  • Format: Paperback, 267 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241340660

title: The Viscount Who Loved Me
sheet_title: The Viscount Who Loved Me Julia Quinn
author: Julia Quinn
description:
The Viscount Who Loved Me is the second novel in Julia Quinn's Regency-era Bridgerton series, and it belongs to Anthony, the eldest Bridgerton brother. Having decided it is finally time to marry, Anthony settles on a suitable bride, only to find her older sister, Kate Sheffield, standing firmly in his way.

What follows is a sparkling battle of wills between a confirmed rake and a woman convinced he will make a dreadful husband. Witty dialogue, ballroom intrigue and a slow-burning enemies-to-lovers romance make this a favourite with fans of the Netflix adaptation and of historical romance in general.

  • Author: Julia Quinn
  • Publisher: Avon
  • Format: Paperback, 480 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Bridgertons, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780063138629

title: Oprah Winfrey: Biography Of Oprah Winfrey
sheet_title: Oprah Winfrey: Biography Of Oprah Winfrey
author: University Press
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Oprah Winfrey Book: The Biography of Oprah Winfrey is a short, accessible biography of the American talk show host, television producer, actress and philanthropist, published by University Press.

It traces her journey from a childhood of poverty and hardship in Kosciusko, Mississippi, where she was born in 1954, through her early break as a television news anchor in Nashville to her later influence on American media. A quick, approachable read for anyone curious about her life.

  • Author: University Press
  • Publisher: University Press
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9798741310373

title: Shadow & Flame
author: Mindee Arnett
description:
Shadow & Flame is the concluding volume of Mindee Arnett's Rime Chronicles, a young adult fantasy of magic, monsters and rebellion. Kate Brighton, now hailed as the Wilder Queen, helped her people survive the war against the Rimish empire, but the cost was steep and the crown is one she never wanted.

With the illegitimate King Edwin still on the throne of Rime, peace remains fragile and a new conflict is gathering. Arnett delivers sweeping battles, political scheming and a romance tested by loyalty, bringing to a close the story that began in Onyx & Ivory.

  • Author: Mindee Arnett
  • Publisher: Balzer + Bray
  • Format: Paperback, 480 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Rime Chronicles, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780062652713

title: The Obstacle Is The Way
author: Ryan Holiday
description:
The Obstacle Is the Way by Ryan Holiday is a modern guide to Stoic philosophy, showing how the difficulties we face can become the very path to progress. Drawing on thinkers such as Marcus Aurelius, Seneca and Epictetus, Holiday turns ancient ideas into practical advice on perception, action and will.

Short chapters pair historical examples, from statesmen and soldiers to athletes and entrepreneurs, with clear lessons on staying calm under pressure and turning setbacks to advantage. It suits readers new to Stoicism as well as anyone seeking a steadier approach to work and life, and pairs naturally with his later Ego Is the Enemy and Stillness Is the Key.

  • Author: Ryan Holiday
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 201 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781781251492

title: The Stonekeeper's Curse
sheet_title: The Stonekeeper S Curse Amulet Book Two Kazu Kibuishi
author: Kazu Kibuishi
description:
The Stonekeeper's Curse is Book Two of Kazu Kibuishi's Amulet series, a full-colour graphic novel adventure for middle-grade readers. Emily and her brother Navin are desperate to save their mother, who lies in a coma after being poisoned, and their search for a cure leads them to Kanalis, a beautiful city of waterfalls.

Aboard their walking house with Miskit and a crew of robots, the siblings soon discover that the city hides as much danger as hope. Kibuishi's cinematic artwork and fast pacing make this a gripping continuation of the story begun in The Stonekeeper, ideal for young fans of fantasy comics.

  • Author: Kazu Kibuishi
  • Publisher: Scholastic (Graphix)
  • Format: Paperback, 220 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Amulet, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780439846837

title: Nudge
author: Richard H. Thaler, Cass R. Sunstein
description:
Nudge by Richard H. Thaler and Cass R. Sunstein explores how the way choices are presented shapes the decisions people make about health, money and happiness. Introducing the idea of choice architecture, the authors show that no option is ever offered in a truly neutral way, and that small design changes can steer people towards better outcomes without restricting their freedom.

This fully revised edition brings the ideas up to date with fresh material on subjects such as retirement saving, personal finance, diet, organ donation, climate change and the COVID-19 pandemic. Readable and often witty, it suits anyone interested in behavioural economics, public policy or simply understanding why we so often make poor choices.

  • Author: Richard H. Thaler, Cass R. Sunstein
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141999937

title: The Rose & The Dagger Renee Ahdieh
sheet_title: The Rose & The Dagger Renee Ahdieh
author: Renée Ahdieh
description:
The Rose & the Dagger is the second and final book in Renée Ahdieh's The Wrath and the Dawn duology, a lush young adult fantasy inspired by One Thousand and One Nights. Shahrzad has learned that Khalid, the king feared as a murderer, is in truth bound by a terrible curse, and now she is separated from him and sheltering among his enemies.

Torn between her family and the husband she loves, Shahrzad must awaken her own hidden powers to break the curse before war engulfs the kingdom. Rich in romance, magic and Middle Eastern-inspired settings, it brings the story to a sweeping close for readers of retellings and romantic fantasy.

  • Author: Renée Ahdieh
  • Publisher: Nancy Paulsen Books
  • Format: Paperback, 420 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Wrath and the Dawn, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780147513861

title: Harry Potter And The Order Of The Phoenix Book 5
sheet_title: Harry Potter And The Order Of The Phoenix Book 5 J K Rowling
author: J.K. Rowling
description:
Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix is the fifth book in J.K. Rowling's Harry Potter series. Harry returns to Hogwarts for his fifth year haunted by dreams of a long corridor ending in a mysterious door, while much of the wizarding world refuses to believe that Voldemort has returned.

Facing O.W.L. exams, a sinister new teacher sent by the Ministry of Magic and authorities who will not listen, Harry leans on his friends as never before. Longer and darker than the earlier books, it explores loyalty, grief and standing up to injustice, and it marks a key turning point in the series for readers young and old.

  • Author: J.K. Rowling
  • Illustrator: Mary GrandPré
  • Publisher: Scholastic
  • Format: Paperback, 896 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Harry Potter, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9781338878967

title: The Education Of Henry Adams: An Autobiography
sheet_title: The Education Of Henry Adams: An Autobiography Henry Adams
author: Henry Adams
description:
The Education of Henry Adams is the celebrated autobiography of the American historian Henry Adams, grandson of John Quincy Adams and great-grandson of John Adams. Written in the third person, it follows his life from a privileged Boston boyhood through the Civil War era and into the rapidly changing America of the Gilded Age.

Part memoir and part history, the book reflects on politics, science, art and the failure of a traditional education to prepare a man for the modern world. First circulated privately in 1907 and made widely available only after the author's death in 1918, it remains a classic of American nonfiction. This Modern Library edition includes an introduction by historian Edmund Morris.

  • Author: Henry Adams
  • Introduction: Edmund Morris
  • Publisher: Modern Library
  • Format: Paperback, 560 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780679640103

title: Harry Potter And The Half Blood Prince 6
sheet_title: Harry Potter And The Half Blood Prince 6 J K Rowling
author: J.K. Rowling
description:
Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince is the sixth book in J.K. Rowling's Harry Potter series, in a special paperback edition with a cover illustration by Brian Selznick. Voldemort's forces are gaining ground, even the Muggle world is feeling the effects, and Dumbledore is often away from Hogwarts on secretive business.

Yet school life carries on: sixth-years learn to Apparate, the Weasley twins expand their joke shop, and romance blossoms in the corridors. Harry, meanwhile, finds unexpected help in an old Potions textbook once owned by the enigmatic Half-Blood Prince, as Dumbledore prepares him for the battles ahead. A rich, poignant penultimate chapter in the saga.

  • Author: J.K. Rowling
  • Cover illustration: Brian Selznick
  • Illustrator: Mary GrandPré
  • Publisher: Arthur A. Levine Books
  • Format: Paperback, 688 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Harry Potter, Book 6
  • ISBN: 9781338299199

title: The 50th Law
author: 50 Cent, Robert Greene
description:
The 50th Law is a collaboration between rapper and entrepreneur 50 Cent and Robert Greene, author of The 48 Laws of Power. Built around 50 Cent's rise from the streets of Queens to business success, it sets out a philosophy of fearlessness for anyone trying to get ahead in an unpredictable world.

Each chapter blends stories of hustlers, historical figures and 50 Cent's own dealings with Greene's trademark strategic analysis, covering themes such as self-reliance, momentum, awareness and turning setbacks into opportunity. It will appeal to readers of Greene's other books and to anyone interested in power, ambition and entrepreneurship.

  • Author: 50 Cent, Robert Greene
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846680793

title: The 5 Levels Of Leadership
sheet_title: The 5 Levels Of Leadership John C. Maxwell
author: John C. Maxwell
description:
The 5 Levels of Leadership by John C. Maxwell argues that real leadership has little to do with a job title. Holding a position is only the starting point, and Maxwell maps out five stages through which leaders grow their influence: Position, Permission, Production, People Development and Pinnacle.

For each level he explains why people choose to follow, the benefits and pitfalls involved, and the practical steps needed to move upwards. Clear and structured, the book is a useful handbook for managers, team leaders and anyone seeking to build lasting influence in an organisation.

  • Author: John C. Maxwell
  • Publisher: Center Street
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781599953632

title: Leadership Wisdom Robin S. Sharma
author: Robin Sharma
description:
Leadership Wisdom from the Monk Who Sold His Ferrari is Robin Sharma's follow-up to The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari, applying the same parable style to the world of work. Julian Mantle, the former high-flying lawyer who found a new way of living after a heart attack, returns to share lessons on leading people well.

Through a series of conversations, Sharma sets out practical principles for building trust, commitment and morale within a team and for leading with vision. Easy to read and organised into short, practical lessons, it suits managers, entrepreneurs and anyone who enjoyed the original book.

  • Author: Robin Sharma
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari
  • ISBN: 9780006385622

title: The Choice: A True Story Of Hope
sheet_title: The Choice: A True Story Of Hope Edith Eger
author: Edith Eger
description:
The Choice is the memoir of Dr Edith Eva Eger, who in 1944, at the age of sixteen, was deported to Auschwitz with her family. A young ballet student, she was torn from her parents as soon as they arrived and endured the camp, including being forced to dance for Josef Mengele, before being rescued, barely alive, at the end of the war.

Decades later, after becoming a clinical psychologist, Eger drew on her own experience to help others heal from trauma. Weaving her story together with those of her patients, the book is a moving account of resilience and of the freedom we have to choose how we respond to suffering.

  • Author: Edith Eger
  • Publisher: Rider
  • Format: Paperback, 367 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846045127

title: Harry Potter And The Order Of The Phoenix 5
sheet_title: Harry Potter And The Order Of The Phoenix 5 J K Rowling
author: J.K. Rowling
description:
Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix is Book 5 of J.K. Rowling's much-loved series, presented here in the Scholastic paperback edition with cover art by Brian Selznick. Troubled by nightmares of a locked door and a Ministry of Magic that denies Voldemort's return, Harry begins his fifth year at Hogwarts feeling isolated and angry.

As exams loom and a cruel new professor tightens her grip on the school, Harry and his friends form their own secret resistance. The longest book in the series, it is a powerful story of friendship, courage and sacrifice that marks the point where the wizarding war truly begins.

  • Author: J.K. Rowling
  • Cover illustration: Brian Selznick
  • Illustrator: Mary GrandPré
  • Publisher: Scholastic
  • Format: Paperback, 912 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Harry Potter, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9781338299182

title: The Beautiful Renee Ahdieh
author: Renée Ahdieh
vendor: G.P. Putnam's Sons Books for Young Readers
description:
The Beautiful is the first book in Renée Ahdieh's young adult series of the same name, a dark historical fantasy set in New Orleans in 1872. Seventeen-year-old Celine Rousseau has fled Paris and her work as a dressmaker to find refuge with the Ursuline nuns, and she is soon drawn to the glamour and danger of the city.

Her path crosses with La Cour des Lions, a secretive underworld group led by the mysterious Sébastien Saint Germain, just as young women begin turning up dead. Blending vampires, murder mystery and slow-burning romance in a richly atmospheric setting, it suits readers who enjoy gothic fantasy with a historical flavour.

  • Author: Renée Ahdieh
  • Publisher: G.P. Putnam's Sons Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Hardcover, 448 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Beautiful, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781524738174

title: Your Baby Week By Week
sheet_title: Your Baby Week By Week Simone Cave
author: Simone Cave, Caroline Fertleman
description:
Your Baby Week by Week by Simone Cave and Caroline Fertleman is a practical guide to caring for a newborn through the first six months. Each chapter focuses on a single week of a baby's development, so tired parents can quickly find what is relevant to them right now.

Weeks are divided into clear sections covering sleep, feeding, crying, bathing, play and development, along with tips for checking that a baby is progressing well. Reassuring and straightforward, it is a handy companion for first-time parents who want sensible answers during those uncertain early months.

  • Author: Simone Cave, Caroline Fertleman
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780091910556

title: The New Contented Little Baby Book: The Secret to Calm and Confident Parenting
sheet_title: The New Contented Little Baby Book The Secret To Calm And Co
author: Gina Ford
description:
The New Contented Little Baby Book is Gina Ford's well-known guide to establishing feeding and sleeping routines for babies, based on her experience of caring for more than 300 infants. First published in 1999, it has been fully revised in this edition with updated advice shaped by feedback from readers.

Ford sets out detailed daily routines designed to fit a baby's natural rhythms, aiming to reduce hunger, overtiredness and excessive crying and to help babies settle and sleep well. Structured and thorough, it suits parents who prefer a clear plan and a predictable day for both baby and family.

  • Author: Gina Ford
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780091912697

title: Prayers Of The Pious
sheet_title: Prayers Of The Pious Omar Suleiman
author: Omar Suleiman
description:
Prayers of the Pious by Omar Suleiman is a short devotional collection of thirty prayers taken from the Prophet Muhammad's own teachings and from the earliest generations of Muslims. Each supplication is accompanied by a brief reflection that helps readers understand its meaning and carry it into daily life.

Gentle and uplifting, the book is designed to deepen the reader's connection with God, nurturing love for Him and His Messenger alongside gratitude and contentment. Its compact format makes it an ideal companion for quiet moments of reflection, or a thoughtful gift.

  • Author: Omar Suleiman
  • Publisher: Kube Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 128 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847741295

title: The Archer
author: Paulo Coelho
description:
The Archer is a short illustrated fable by Paulo Coelho, translated from the Portuguese by Margaret Jull Costa and illustrated by Christoph Niemann. It tells of Tetsuya, a once-legendary archer who has withdrawn from public life, and the boy who seeks him out with a head full of questions.

In answering him, Tetsuya explains the way of the bow, and through it Coelho offers reflections on courage, discipline, risk and living a meaningful life. Brief and beautifully presented, it suits fans of The Alchemist and readers looking for a contemplative book to read in one sitting or give as a gift.

  • Author: Paulo Coelho
  • Translator: Margaret Jull Costa
  • Illustrator: Christoph Niemann
  • Publisher: Knopf
  • Format: Hardcover, 131 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593318270

title: The Twice Lost
sheet_title: Twice Lost Lost Voices Part 3 Sarah Porter Health/Massage
author: Sarah Porter
description:
The Twice Lost is the third and final book in Sarah Porter's Lost Voices trilogy, a dark young adult fantasy about mermaids. With the authorities now set on wiping out the mermaids who have sunk ships for centuries, Luce, whose powers make her especially dangerous, becomes the government's prime target.

Fleeing south to San Francisco, she discovers hundreds of exiled mermaids hiding beneath the docks, girls cast out by their own tribes. When they choose Luce to lead them, she refuses to be a queen and instead prepares them for war. A haunting story of survival, loyalty and resistance that brings the trilogy to a dramatic close.

  • Author: Sarah Porter
  • Publisher: Clarion Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 471 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Lost Voices, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780547482521

title: The Jolly Christmas Postman
sheet_title: The Jolly Christmas Postman Allan Ahlberg
author: Allan Ahlberg, Janet Ahlberg
description:
The Jolly Christmas Postman by Janet and Allan Ahlberg is a festive picture book in which the much-loved Jolly Postman makes his rounds on Christmas Eve. Pedalling from one fairy-tale home to the next, he delivers seasonal post to familiar characters such as Baby Bear, Red Riding Hood and Humpty Dumpty.

Real envelopes are bound into the pages, holding letters, cards, a board game and a jigsaw for children to take out and explore. Told in gentle rhyme with richly detailed illustrations, it is a classic Christmas read-aloud and a follow-up to The Jolly Postman.

  • Author: Allan Ahlberg, Janet Ahlberg
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Hardcover, 52 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Jolly Postman
  • ISBN: 9780141340111

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description:
Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind by historian Yuval Noah Harari tells the story of our species from its earliest days to the present. Around 100,000 years ago several kinds of humans shared the planet; Harari asks why only Homo sapiens survived and how it came to dominate the Earth.

Moving through the Cognitive, Agricultural and Scientific Revolutions, he explores how shared myths, money, empires and religion allowed vast numbers of strangers to cooperate, and what that progress has meant for our happiness. Wide-ranging and provocative, it is an engaging introduction to big-picture history for curious general readers.

  • Author: Yuval Noah Harari
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 544 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784873646

title: Home Body
author: Rupi Kaur
description:
Home Body is the third poetry collection from Rupi Kaur, illustrated throughout by the author. It takes readers on an intimate journey through past, present and future, looking honestly at the self and the body we live in.

Written in Kaur's spare, direct style, the poems explore self-acceptance, love, family, community and the courage to change, moving between light and dark, nature and nurture. It will speak to fans of Milk and Honey and The Sun and Her Flowers, and to anyone drawn to reflective, accessible modern poetry.

  • Author: Rupi Kaur
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781471196720

title: One True Loves: A Novel
sheet_title: One True Loves: A Novel Taylor Jenkins Reid
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description:
One True Loves is a heartfelt contemporary novel by Taylor Jenkins Reid about a woman torn between two great loves. Emma Blair married her high school sweetheart, Jesse, and the pair built an adventurous life together far from home, until Jesse vanished when his helicopter went missing over the Pacific on their first anniversary.

Years later, having slowly rebuilt her life and agreed to marry another man, Emma learns that Jesse is alive and coming home. Reid handles the impossible choice with warmth, humour and emotional honesty, making this a moving read for fans of character-driven romance and book club fiction.

  • Author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
  • Publisher: Atria Books
  • Format: Paperback, 331 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781476776903

title: The World's Worst Parents
author: David Walliams
description:
The World's Worst Parents by David Walliams is a collection of ten funny stories about the most outrageous mums and dads imaginable, illustrated in full colour by Tony Ross. It follows the earlier World's Worst Children and World's Worst Teachers books in the same spirit of gleeful mischief.

Readers meet characters such as Peter Pong, whose feet are the smelliest anywhere, speed-obsessed Harriet Hurry, and Monty Monopolize, a dad who takes over his children's toys. Silly, exaggerated and full of slapstick humour, it is ideal for young readers who enjoy laugh-out-loud stories to read alone or share aloud.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 308 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008430306

title: Outliers: The Story Of Success
sheet_title: Outliers: The Story Of Success Malcolm Gladwell
author: Malcolm Gladwell
description:
Outliers: The Story of Success by Malcolm Gladwell investigates what really sets exceptionally successful people apart. Rather than focusing on personal talent alone, Gladwell argues that culture, family background, generation and the quirks of opportunity play a far bigger role than we tend to admit.

Through memorable case studies, from software pioneers and professional sportspeople to the Beatles, he explores ideas such as the 10,000-hour rule and the hidden advantages of timing and upbringing. Lively and thought-provoking, it suits readers interested in psychology, sociology and the real roots of achievement.

  • Author: Malcolm Gladwell
  • Publisher: Little, Brown Paperbacks
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780316017930

title: YOU CAN HEAL YOUR LIFE
author: Louise L. Hay
description:
You Can Heal Your Life by Louise L. Hay is a classic of the self-help genre, built on the idea that our thoughts and beliefs shape our health and wellbeing. Hay shares her own philosophy and experiences, encouraging readers to examine the limiting patterns that hold them back.

The book is arranged in four parts, moving from her core beliefs to a session with the author and then practical ways of applying the ideas, with exercises designed to be worked through in order. It is well suited to readers interested in affirmations, self-love and a spiritual approach to personal growth.

  • Author: Louise L. Hay
  • Publisher: Hay House
  • Format: Paperback, 253 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780937611012

title: When the Body Says No
sheet_title: When the Body Says No Exploring the Stress-Disease Connecti
author: Gabor Maté
description:
When the Body Says No by physician Gabor Maté examines the link between mind and body, and in particular the toll that stress and suppressed emotion can take on our health. Drawing on scientific research and his own clinical work, Maté asks whether the way we cope with feelings can influence the illnesses we develop.

He considers conditions such as multiple sclerosis, cancer, arthritis, diabetes and heart disease, illustrating his argument with many case studies, including those of well-known figures. Compassionate and thought-provoking, it suits readers interested in health, psychology and the hidden costs of stress, as well as anyone seeking to understand their own patterns.

  • Author: Gabor Maté
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 306 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781785042225

title: The Autistic Brain
author: Temple Grandin, Richard Panek
description:
The Autistic Brain by Temple Grandin, written with Richard Panek, combines Grandin's personal experience as an autistic adult with the latest scientific research into autism. She explores what brain imaging and genetic studies reveal about how autistic minds work.

Grandin draws attention to often-overlooked sensory difficulties and argues that autism should be tackled one symptom at a time instead of under a single broad label. Above all, she urges parents and educators to build on the distinctive strengths of autistic children rather than dwelling on their weaknesses. Accessible and hopeful, it is valuable for families, teachers and anyone curious about different ways of thinking.

  • Author: Temple Grandin, Richard Panek
  • Publisher: Rider
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846044496

title: How To Change Your Mind
sheet_title: How To Change Your Mind Michael Pollan
author: Michael Pollan
description:
How to Change Your Mind by Michael Pollan explores the history and new science of psychedelics such as LSD and psilocybin. Pollan traces how these substances went from promising research subjects to banned drugs, and how a new generation of scientists is now studying their potential to treat conditions like depression and addiction.

Combining reporting with his own first-hand experiences as a willing subject, he examines what psychedelics may reveal about consciousness, the brain and the experience of dying. Curious, balanced and highly readable, it suits readers interested in science, psychology, mental health and the workings of the mind.

  • Author: Michael Pollan
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 480 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141985138

title: Spark Joy: Illustrated Guide To The Japanese Art
sheet_title: Spark Joy: Illustrated Guide To The Japanese Art Marie Kondo
author: Marie Kondo
description:
Spark Joy is Marie Kondo's illustrated guide, organised room by room, to the KonMari method of tidying the home. Following on from The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying, it covers every space, including kitchens, bedrooms and bathrooms, and belongings ranging from clothes and books to papers, cosmetics and keepsakes.

Simple line drawings show how to arrange drawers, wardrobes and cupboards and demonstrate Kondo's distinctive folding technique for everything from shirts to socks. At its heart is her approach of keeping only what truly brings you joy, making this a practical companion for anyone wanting a calmer, clutter-free home.

  • Author: Marie Kondo
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781785043499

title: The Fourth Revolution Adrian Wooldridge
author: John Micklethwait, Adrian Wooldridge
description:
The Fourth Revolution by John Micklethwait and Adrian Wooldridge, both long-serving journalists at The Economist, asks what government is really for. The authors trace three great revolutions in the history of the state, which gave rise first to the nation-state, then to the liberal state and finally to the welfare state.

They argue that a fourth revolution is now under way, driven by disillusion with Western government and competition from alternative models in Asia and elsewhere, and they make the case for a leaner, more effective state. Sharp and wide-ranging, it suits readers interested in politics, economics and public policy.

  • Author: John Micklethwait, Adrian Wooldridge
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141975245

title: THINKING FAST AND SLOW
author: Daniel Kahneman
description:
Thinking, Fast and Slow by Nobel Prize-winning psychologist Daniel Kahneman is a landmark exploration of how we think and make decisions. Kahneman describes two systems at work in the mind: a quick, intuitive and emotional System 1, and a slower, more deliberate and logical System 2.

Drawing on decades of research, he shows how cognitive biases, overconfidence and loss aversion shape everything from business strategy to personal happiness, and helps readers recognise when intuition can and cannot be trusted. Rich and rewarding, it is essential reading for anyone interested in psychology, economics or better decision-making.

  • Author: Daniel Kahneman
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 499 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141033570

title: Hold On to Your Kids: Why Parents Need to Matter More Than Peers
sheet_title: Hold on to Your Kids Why Parents Need to Matter More Than
author: Gordon Neufeld, Gabor Maté
description:
Hold On to Your Kids by developmental psychologist Gordon Neufeld and physician Gabor Maté examines a growing trend in which children look to their peers, rather than to parents and other caring adults, for guidance and identity. The authors argue that this shift is far from natural and can undermine healthy development and family closeness.

They explain how peer orientation can leave children anxious, conformist and alienated, and offer practical advice on rebuilding a strong attachment with sons and daughters, restoring parents' natural authority and making the family home a secure base again. Thoughtful and reassuring, it suits parents and educators of children of all ages.

  • Author: Gordon Neufeld, Gabor Maté
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781785042195

title: Mad About You
author: Mhairi McFarlane
description:
Mad About You is a warm, witty romantic comedy by Mhairi McFarlane. Harriet Hatley is a sought-after wedding photographer who has little faith in romance, so when her long-term partner proposes, her panic ends the relationship and leaves her urgently searching for somewhere new to live.

She moves in with Cal Clarke, a hopeless romantic recovering from his own wedding disaster, and the mismatched pair go from strangers to housemates to friends. When a secret Harriet has long kept hidden comes to light, Cal proves an unexpected source of support. Funny yet emotionally honest, it suits readers who like romance with real depth.

  • Author: Mhairi McFarlane
  • Publisher: Avon
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063117945

title: The Wealth of Nations: Books IV-V
sheet_title: The Wealth Of Nations: Books Iv V Adam Smith
author: Adam Smith
description:
The Wealth of Nations, Books IV-V presents the closing parts of Adam Smith's foundational work of economics, edited by Andrew Skinner for Penguin Classics. In these books Smith responds to the French Physiocrats, examines the mercantile system and considers Britain's colonial relationship with America.

He also sets out his view of the proper role of the state: limited, but responsible for defence, justice, public works and education where markets fall short. Still widely studied today, this volume is essential for students of economics, politics and history, and for anyone wishing to read Smith's arguments in his own words.

  • Author: Adam Smith
  • Editor: Andrew Skinner
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 672 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780140436150

title: Maybe Now: A Novel (3) (Maybe Someday)
author: Colleen Hoover
description:
Maybe Now is Colleen Hoover's follow-up to Maybe Someday and the novella Maybe Not, returning to Ridge, Sydney, Warren, Bridgette and Maggie. Ridge and Sydney are at last free to be together, but their happiness is complicated by old ties and new jealousies.

As Maggie lives with her illness, she sets out to tick off a long-forgotten list of things she always meant to do someday, keeping Ridge updated along the way, while Sydney struggles with her suspicions about their bond. Romantic, emotional and full of Hoover's heartfelt drama, it asks what matters most between friendship, loyalty and love.

  • Author: Colleen Hoover
  • Publisher: Atria Books
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Maybe, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781668013342

title: Maybe In Another Life: A Novel
sheet_title: Maybe In Another Life: A Novel Taylor Jenkins Reid
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description:
Maybe in Another Life is a thoughtful novel by Taylor Jenkins Reid about how a single decision can change the course of a life. At twenty-nine, Hannah Martin has drifted between cities and jobs without direction, and she returns home to Los Angeles to stay with her best friend, Gabby.

On a night out, she runs into her high school boyfriend, Ethan, and must decide whether to leave with Gabby or stay with him. From that moment the story splits into two parallel timelines told in alternating chapters, each following a very different future. Romantic and reflective, it explores fate, friendship and love.

  • Author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
  • Publisher: Atria Books
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781476776880

title: Million Dollar Weekend
author: Noah Kagan
description:
Million Dollar Weekend by entrepreneur Noah Kagan is a practical guide to starting a business quickly, without waiting for the perfect idea or a big budget. Kagan argues that fear and perfectionism are the main barriers holding would-be founders back, and sets out a method for testing an idea and finding paying customers within 48 hours.

Step by step, he shows readers how to build confidence in asking for what they want, check demand early and turn a small experiment into a growing company. Energetic and direct, it suits aspiring entrepreneurs, side-hustlers and anyone who has been putting off launching an idea.

  • Author: Noah Kagan
  • Publisher: Ebury Publishing
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529146189

title: The Little Book of Lykke: Secrets of the World's Happiest People
sheet_title: Little Book Of Lykke: Secrets Of World Happiest Meik Wiking
author: Meik Wiking
description:
The Little Book of Lykke by Meik Wiking, who leads Copenhagen's Happiness Research Institute, sets out to discover what makes people happy around the world. Following his book on hygge, Wiking looks beyond Denmark to places as varied as Bhutan, Finland, South Korea and Brazil in search of the habits behind a contented life.

He organises the book around six key factors, among them trust, kindness, freedom and togetherness alongside health and money, and offers simple, practical suggestions for bringing more of each into everyday life. Charming and upbeat, it is a cheerful read for anyone interested in wellbeing and the science of happiness.

  • Author: Meik Wiking
  • Publisher: William Morrow
  • Format: Hardcover, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Happiness Institute Series, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780062820334

title: The Seat Of The Soul
author: Gary Zukav
description:
The Seat of the Soul by Gary Zukav is a spiritual classic about the evolution of human consciousness. Zukav argues that humanity is moving beyond an understanding of the world based only on the five senses, towards a deeper awareness of ourselves as souls with a purpose.

He explores ideas such as authentic power, intention, karma and reverence, encouraging readers to take responsibility for their choices and to build relationships rooted in harmony, cooperation and sharing. Reflective and inspiring, it suits readers drawn to spirituality, personal growth and questions of meaning.

  • Author: Gary Zukav
  • Publisher: Rider
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780712646741

title: What to Expect When You're Expecting
sheet_title: What to Expect When Youre Expecting
author: Heidi Murkoff
description:
What to Expect When You're Expecting by Heidi Murkoff is a comprehensive, month-by-month guide to pregnancy, answering the questions expectant parents most often ask. This fifth edition has been fully revised, covering everything from prenatal screening and medication safety to the latest birthing options.

Alongside the medical information, it gives plenty of attention to everyday life during pregnancy, including eating well, exercise, work and the many physical changes along the way, all delivered in a warm, practical tone. A thorough reference for first-time parents and anyone wanting clear answers in the months before birth.

  • Author: Heidi Murkoff
  • Publisher: Workman Publishing Company
  • Format: Paperback, 644 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: What to Expect
  • ISBN: 9780761187486

title: The Daily Laws
author: Robert Greene
description:
The Daily Laws by Robert Greene distils the ideas from his earlier books, including The 48 Laws of Power, into 366 short meditations, one for every day of the year. The entries range across power, seduction, mastery, strategy and human nature, as well as leadership, productivity and dealing with adversity.

It works both as an accessible introduction for newcomers to Greene's thinking and as a handy daily companion for existing readers who want to absorb his lessons gradually. Ideal for anyone interested in psychology, ambition and self-mastery.

  • Author: Robert Greene
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 464 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800816282

title: Power Of Positive Thinking Peale
author: Norman Vincent Peale
description:
The Power of Positive Thinking by Norman Vincent Peale is one of the best-known self-help books of the twentieth century, first published in 1952. Combining practical psychology with Christian faith, Peale shows how belief in yourself and a hopeful outlook can transform both personal and professional life.

Through simple techniques, prayers and real-life stories, he offers guidance on building confidence, breaking the worry habit, staying calm under pressure and improving relationships with others. Encouraging and accessible, it remains a source of motivation for readers seeking a more optimistic and purposeful approach to life.

  • Author: Norman Vincent Peale
  • Publisher: Touchstone
  • Format: Paperback, 218 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780743234801

title: The One Minute Manager Meets The Monkey
sheet_title: The One Minute Manager Meets The Monkey Kenneth H. Blanchard
author: Kenneth H. Blanchard, William Oncken Jr.
description:
The One Minute Manager Meets the Monkey by Kenneth Blanchard and William Oncken Jr. tackles a familiar problem: managers who end up overloaded because they take on their team's problems. In the authors' memorable metaphor, each problem is a 'monkey' that leaps from an employee's back onto the manager's.

Told as a short, lively story, the book shows how managers can hand problems back to their rightful owners applying the four rules for handling monkeys that Oncken devised, freeing time for their own priorities while helping staff become more self-reliant. A quick, practical read for supervisors and team leaders at any level.

  • Author: Kenneth H. Blanchard, William Oncken Jr.
  • Publisher: William Morrow Paperbacks
  • Format: Paperback, 137 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: One Minute Manager
  • ISBN: 9780688103804

title: The Second Brain Michael Gershon
author: Michael D. Gershon
description:
The Second Brain by Dr Michael D. Gershon explores a remarkable discovery: the gut contains its own network of nerve cells that can operate independently of the brain in our heads. Gershon, a researcher who has spent decades studying the bowel, explains how this enteric nervous system works and why it matters.

He shows how the two brains must work together, and how problems in their communication can lead to digestive troubles such as cramps and irritable bowel conditions. Combining science with accessible explanation, it suits readers with an interest in health, medicine and neuroscience, and anyone living with functional bowel disorders.

  • Author: Michael D. Gershon
  • Publisher: Harper Perennial
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780060930721

title: Harmony
author: Whitney Hanson
description:
Harmony is a poetry collection by Whitney Hanson exploring love, loss, grief and healing. Written in the wake of losing a loved one, the poems follow the journey through grief and recovery, using music as their guiding image.

Hanson compares a life to a song that begins with a single note and grows into a melody, suggesting that silences and pauses are also part of the music. Tender and accessible, it suits fans of contemporary poetry and readers looking for comfort and hope while coping with loss.

  • Author: Whitney Hanson
  • Publisher: Penguin Life
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780143138013

title: The Art Of Being A Brilliant Teenager
sheet_title: The Art Of Being A Brilliant Teenager Andy Cope
author: Andy Cope, Andy Whittaker, Darrell Woodman
description:
The Art of Being a Brilliant Teenager by Andy Cope and Andy Whittaker is a lively guide to wellbeing and positivity written especially for teens. This updated edition tackles modern pressures such as social media and screen time alongside timeless concerns like confidence, motivation and relationships.

Grounded in research on human flourishing but written in a fun, quirky and non-patronising style, with illustrations by Amy Bradley, it helps young people get ready for real life and make the most of their potential. A good choice for teenagers, and for parents and teachers looking to encourage them.

  • Author: Andy Cope, Andy Whittaker, Darrell Woodman
  • Illustrator: Amy Bradley
  • Publisher: Capstone
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780857089397

title: The Midnight Library: A Gma Book Club Pick A Novel
sheet_title: The Midnight Library: A Gma Book Club Pick A Novel Matt Haig
author: Matt Haig
description:
The Midnight Library by Matt Haig is a moving novel about regret, hope and the choices that shape a life. Between life and death stands a library filled with endless books, each holding a version of the life Nora Seed might have lived had she chosen differently.

Given the chance to step into these alternative lives, Nora explores paths she once abandoned, from rock star to glaciologist, searching for the one that will finally make her happy. Warm, thoughtful and quietly uplifting, it is a fine choice for book clubs and readers who enjoy fiction with a touch of magic.

  • Author: Matt Haig
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780525559498

title: Where The Crawdads Sing: Reeses Book Club
sheet_title: Where The Crawdads Sing: Reeses Book Club Delia Owens
author: Delia Owens
description:
Where the Crawdads Sing is Delia Owens's debut novel, blending a coming-of-age tale, a murder mystery and a deep love of the natural world. For years the people of Barkley Cove on the North Carolina coast have whispered about the 'Marsh Girl', so when a local man, Chase Andrews, is found dead in 1969, suspicion falls on Kya Clark.

Abandoned as a child, Kya has survived alone in the marshland, learning from the gulls, the tides and the wildlife around her. When she longs for connection, two young men from town enter her life, with consequences that change everything. Atmospheric and absorbing, it suits book clubs and readers who love lyrical, nature-rich storytelling.

  • Author: Delia Owens
  • Publisher: G.P. Putnam's Sons
  • Format: Paperback, 391 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780735219106

title: Why We Sleep: Unlocking the Power of Sleep and Dreams
sheet_title: Why We Sleep: Unlocking Power Of Sleep 7 Dreams Matthew Walk
author: Matthew Walker
description:
Why We Sleep by neuroscientist Matthew Walker is an eye-opening look at one of the most essential yet least understood parts of human life. Drawing on decades of research, Walker explains what sleep does for the brain and body, and why we suffer so much when we do not get enough of it.

He explores how sleep affects learning, memory, mood, creativity and physical health, examines the role of dreaming, and offers practical advice for better rest. Engaging and persuasive, it suits anyone curious about the science of sleep or looking to improve their own sleeping habits.

  • Author: Matthew Walker
  • Publisher: Scribner
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781501144325

title: Welcome Home: A Guide to Building a Home for Your Soul
sheet_title: Welcome Home Guide To Building Home For Ur Soul Najwa Zebian
author: Najwa Zebian
description:
Welcome Home: A Guide to Building a Home for Your Soul is the first book of inspirational prose by poet and educator Najwa Zebian. It introduces her idea of home as an inner sanctuary in which you can accept your vulnerability and recognise your own worth.

Too often, Zebian suggests, we build our sense of home in other people and feel empty when they leave. Opening up about her own life in depth for the first time, and weaving memoir with poetry and practical guidance, she shows readers how to create that home within themselves. A comforting read for anyone healing from loss or rejection.

  • Author: Najwa Zebian
  • Publisher: Harmony
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593231753

title: Maybe Not
author: Colleen Hoover
description:
Maybe Not is a novella by Colleen Hoover set in the world of Maybe Someday, this time telling the story of Ridge's funny, charismatic friend Warren. When Warren gets the chance to share an apartment with a female roommate, he jumps at it, but the roommate turns out to be the cool and seemingly ruthless Bridgette.

Sparks fly as the two can barely tolerate each other, yet Warren suspects that anyone capable of such fierce dislike might also be capable of fierce love. Light, funny and romantic, it is a quick read for fans of the Maybe series and of Hoover's playful side.

  • Author: Colleen Hoover
  • Publisher: Atria Books
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Maybe, Book 1.5
  • ISBN: 9781501125713

title: The Code Of The Extraordinary Mind
sheet_title: The Code Of The Extraordinary Mind Vishen Lakhiani
author: Vishen Lakhiani
description:
The Code of the Extraordinary Mind by Vishen Lakhiani, founder of Mindvalley, challenges the inherited rules that shape how most people live. Lakhiani coins the term 'Brules' for outdated beliefs passed down from one generation to the next, covering everything from education and work to love, spirituality and happiness.

Through ten unconventional laws, he offers a framework for questioning conditioning, rethinking beliefs and redefining success on your own terms. Energetic and personal, it suits readers interested in personal growth, mindset and living a more intentional life.

  • Author: Vishen Lakhiani
  • Publisher: Rodale Books
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593135822

title: I Will Teach You To Be Rich Sethi
sheet_title: I Will Teach You To Be Rich Sethi
author: Ramit Sethi
description:
I Will Teach You to Be Rich by personal finance expert Ramit Sethi is a practical six-week programme for taking control of your money. This revised second edition shows readers how to set up the right accounts, automate their finances and invest for the long term so their money grows with little ongoing effort.

Sethi's approach is refreshingly guilt-free: rather than cutting out every small pleasure, he encourages spending generously on the things you love while cutting back on what you don't. Covering debt, saving, investing and negotiating, it suits young professionals and anyone who wants a straightforward plan for building a rich life.

  • Author: Ramit Sethi
  • Publisher: Workman Publishing Company
  • Format: Paperback, 342 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781523505746

title: Riding the De(mon)
sheet_title: Riding The De Mon Murali Raghavan
author: Murali Raghavan
description:
Riding the De(mon) is a financial thriller by chartered accountant turned author Murali Raghavan, set against the backdrop of demonetisation in India. Vikram, a young IT professional at Bharat Bank, sits in a Chennai jail accused of defrauding the bank of more than ten crore rupees, and although he protests his innocence, the evidence against him is overwhelming.
