As the story unfolds, it draws in a spiritual leader facing a murder charge, a journalist chasing more than a headline and a scheme to use demonetisation to bring down a government. Fast-paced and grounded in the world of banking and money laundering, it will appeal to readers who enjoy financial crime and political intrigue.

  • Author: Murali Raghavan
  • Publisher: Inkstate
  • Format: Paperback, 248 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9789356104013

title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians: The Chalice of the Gods
sheet_title: Percy Jackson And The Olympians Rick Riordan
author: Rick Riordan
description:
The Chalice of the Gods is the sixth Percy Jackson and the Olympians adventure by Rick Riordan, reuniting Percy, Annabeth and Grover more than a decade after the original series. Percy simply wants a normal senior year, but to get into college he needs three letters of recommendation from the gods of Mount Olympus.

To earn the first, he must complete a quest for Ganymede, Zeus's cup-bearer, and recover a missing goblet before someone else gets hold of it. Packed with Riordan's trademark humour and playful take on Greek mythology, it can be read on its own and suits both longtime fans and newcomers.

  • Author: Rick Riordan
  • Publisher: Puffin Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 268 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Percy Jackson and the Olympians, Book 6
  • ISBN: 9780241647547

title: The Sun And Her Flowers
sheet_title: The Sun And Her Flowers Rupi Kaur
author: Rupi Kaur
description:
The Sun and Her Flowers is Rupi Kaur's second poetry collection, following Milk and Honey, and is illustrated by the author. It is a journey of growth and healing that touches on ancestry, migration, love, loss and finding a sense of home within yourself.

The book is arranged in five chapters named for the stages of a flower's life, from wilting and falling to rooting, rising and blooming. Honest, tender and direct, it celebrates love in many forms and suits readers who enjoy accessible modern poetry with emotional depth.

  • Author: Rupi Kaur
  • Publisher: Andrews McMeel Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781449486792

title: Why Has Nobody Told Me This Before?
sheet_title: Why Has Nobody Told Me This Before? Julie Smith
author: Julie Smith
description:
Why Has Nobody Told Me This Before? is a practical mental health handbook by clinical psychologist Dr Julie Smith. Drawing on her years of therapy work, she shares the tools and techniques she uses with clients to help people cope with life's ups and downs.

Written in short, bite-sized sections, the book lets readers turn straight to what they need, whether that is managing anxiety, dealing with low mood, building self-confidence, coping with grief or handling stress. Clear, warm and evidence-based, it is an accessible guide for anyone wanting to look after their emotional wellbeing.

  • Author: Julie Smith
  • Publisher: Michael Joseph
  • Format: Hardcover, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241529713

title: Kingdom of the Feared
author: Kerri Maniscalco
description:
Kingdom of the Feared is the third and final book in Kerri Maniscalco's Kingdom of the Wicked series, a dark romantic fantasy. Emilia is still reeling after learning that Vittoria, her twin, is alive, while longing to claim Wrath, the enigmatic demon prince who has become her king.

When a prominent figure from House Greed is killed and the evidence points to Vittoria, Emilia and Wrath are drawn into a rival demon court to uncover the truth about her sister. Steamy, atmospheric and full of intrigue, it brings the trilogy to a dramatic close for fans of romantasy.

  • Author: Kerri Maniscalco
  • Publisher: Hodder & Stoughton
  • Format: Paperback, 401 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Kingdom of the Wicked, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781399703222

title: Meeting Muhammad
author: Omar Suleiman
description:
Meeting Muhammad by Omar Suleiman is an inspiring introduction to the life and character of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. Across thirty detailed chapters built on narrations from his companions, it invites readers to move beyond simply knowing about the Prophet to truly knowing and loving him.

Suleiman helps readers imagine what it was like to sit in the Prophet's company, drawing lessons for faith and daily life along the way. Warm and accessible, it suits Muslims seeking a closer connection to the Prophet and anyone wishing to learn about his life and example.

  • Author: Omar Suleiman
  • Publisher: Kube Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 260 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847741776

title: The Exchange: After The Firm
sheet_title: The Exchange: After The Firm John Grisham
author: John Grisham
description:
The Exchange: After The Firm is John Grisham's sequel to The Firm, bringing back Mitch McDeere fifteen years after he and his wife, Abby, brought down Bendini, Lambert & Locke, the corrupt Memphis firm. Now living in Manhattan, Mitch has become a partner in the world's biggest law firm.

When an old mentor based in Rome requests a favour, Mitch is drawn into a dangerous international plot that puts everything he has built at risk. Fast-moving and full of legal intrigue, it suits longtime Grisham readers and newcomers who enjoy high-stakes thrillers.

  • Author: John Grisham
  • Publisher: Doubleday
  • Format: Hardcover, 338 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Firm, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780385548953

title: The Chimp Paradox
author: Steve Peters
description:
The Chimp Paradox by consultant psychiatrist Steve Peters presents a mind-management model for understanding and controlling impulsive thoughts and emotions. Peters divides the mind into three parts, the logical Human, the emotional Chimp and the Computer that stores habits and beliefs, and explains how they compete for control.

His programme has been used with elite athletes and business leaders to help them manage fear and self-doubt and act with greater focus and confidence. Practical and easy to follow, it suits anyone who wants to understand their reactions, improve their relationships and perform better at work and in life.

  • Author: Steve Peters
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 346 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780091935580

title: The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read
sheet_title: The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read Philippa Perry
author: Philippa Perry
description:
The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read (and Your Children Will Be Glad That You Did) is a warm and insightful parenting book by psychotherapist Philippa Perry. Rather than offering a rigid plan, Perry starts with parents themselves, showing how our own upbringing and emotional history shape the way we raise our children.

She explores what really matters for a child's emotional wellbeing, including validating feelings, repairing ruptures and building strong, lasting connection, and highlights the patterns worth avoiding. Wise and reassuring, it suits parents of children of any age, as well as anyone who wants to understand how childhood experiences echo through adult life.

  • Author: Philippa Perry
  • Publisher: Penguin Life
  • Format: Hardcover, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781984879554

title: Letting Go
author: David R. Hawkins
description:
Letting Go: The Pathway of Surrender by psychiatrist David R. Hawkins describes a simple technique for releasing negative feelings and the inner obstacles that stand in the way of peace and growth. Developed over decades of clinical practice, the method centres on surrendering emotions rather than suppressing or resisting them.

Hawkins applies the approach to areas such as stress, health, relationships and spiritual development, showing how letting go can bring greater freedom and calm. Thoughtful and practical, it suits readers interested in emotional wellbeing, spirituality and personal transformation.

  • Author: David R. Hawkins
  • Publisher: Hay House
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781401945015

title: Wrong Place Wrong Time
sheet_title: Wrong Place Wrong Time Gillian Mcallister
author: Gillian McAllister
description:
Wrong Place Wrong Time by Gillian McAllister is a gripping, inventive thriller built around a single question: can you prevent a murder that has already happened? Just after midnight as Halloween begins, Jen watches from her window as her eighteen-year-old son, Todd, stabs a stranger.

After Todd is arrested, Jen falls asleep in despair, only to wake on the previous day, before the crime has taken place. Each morning she finds herself further back in time, piecing together the hidden history that led to the attack. Clever, emotional and twisty, it suits readers who enjoy domestic suspense with an original premise.

  • Author: Gillian McAllister
  • Publisher: William Morrow Paperbacks
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063252356

title: How To Wean Your Baby
sheet_title: How To Wean Your Baby Charlotte Stirling Reed
author: Charlotte Stirling-Reed
description:
How to Wean Your Baby by nutritionist Charlotte Stirling-Reed is a practical, step-by-step plan for introducing solid foods, with a savoury-first approach designed to help babies enjoy vegetables from the very beginning. By starting with bitter and savoury tastes, she aims to encourage healthy eating habits and reduce fussiness later on.

This full-colour book combines evidence-based advice with simple, tasty recipes, and includes a day-by-day plan for the first 30 days of weaning, the stage when many parents feel most anxious. Friendly and practical, it suits first-time parents looking for clear guidance on getting started.

  • Author: Charlotte Stirling-Reed
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Hardcover, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781785043246

title: Measure What Matters: OKRs - The Simple Idea that Drives 10x Growth
sheet_title: Measure What Matters Okrs The Simple Idea That Drives 10X Gr
author: John Doerr
description:
Measure What Matters by venture capitalist John Doerr introduces Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), the goal-setting system he learned from Andy Grove at Intel and later brought to Google. Doerr explains how clear objectives and measurable results can help organisations of any size focus, align and achieve ambitious goals.

The book combines Doerr's own account with stories from leaders at organisations including Google, Intel and the Gates Foundation, showing OKRs at work in practice. With a foreword by Google co-founder Larry Page, it is a practical resource for founders, managers and teams who want to execute better.

  • Author: John Doerr
  • Foreword: Larry Page
  • Publisher: Portfolio Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 306 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241348482

title: The Montessori Toddler
author: Simone Davies
description:
The Montessori Toddler by Montessori teacher Simone Davies shows parents how to bring the principles of the Montessori classroom into the family home. Reframing the so-called terrible twos, it presents toddlerhood as a time of curiosity and growing independence to be supported rather than battled.

Davies explains how to set up child-friendly spaces, encourage practical skills such as dressing and pouring water, and handle tantrums without bribes, threats or punishment, while staying calm and present as a parent. With illustrations by Hiyoko Imai, it is a clear, practical guide for parents and carers of toddlers.

  • Author: Simone Davies
  • Illustrator: Hiyoko Imai
  • Publisher: Workman Publishing Company
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Parents' Guide to Montessori, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781523506897

title: The 80/20 Principle: Expanded and Updated
sheet_title: The 80 20 Principle Expanded And Updated Richard Koch
author: Richard Koch
description:
The 80/20 Principle is Richard Koch's business and self-help book built around a simple observation: a small share of our effort tends to produce the bulk of our results. Koch shows how this imbalance appears in sales, customers, time and relationships, and why spotting it changes how we decide what matters.

Rather than urging readers to work harder, the book argues for doing less of what barely counts and more of the few things that drive real progress. Practical and clearly argued, it suits managers, entrepreneurs and anyone trying to get more out of limited time, energy and resources at work and in everyday life.

  • Author: Richard Koch
  • Publisher: Crown Currency
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780385491747

title: The Body Keeps the Score
author: Bessel van der Kolk
description:
The Body Keeps the Score is psychiatrist Bessel van der Kolk's landmark study of trauma and how people recover from it. Drawing on more than thirty years of clinical work and research, he explains how overwhelming experiences reshape the brain and body, affecting memory, trust, self-control and the ability to feel safe and engaged.

Written for general readers as well as professionals, the book moves between neuroscience and real patient stories and surveys a wide range of treatments, including neurofeedback, meditation, yoga, theatre and sport. It is a compassionate, illuminating read for survivors, their families, therapists and anyone curious about the deep links between mind and body.

  • Author: Bessel van der Kolk
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 445 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780143127741

title: The Half Of It
sheet_title: The Half Of It Madison Beer
author: Madison Beer
description:
The Half of It is the memoir of singer-songwriter Madison Beer, who was discovered at the age of twelve and grew up with much of her life playing out online. She looks back on a decade in the public eye, from early fame through her teenage years to adulthood in her twenties.

Beer writes candidly about online harassment, a painful invasion of her privacy and her struggles with mental health, including the dark period surrounding her debut album Life Support and the recovery that followed. Honest and personal, it will speak to her fans and to younger readers interested in self-worth, resilience and life behind the social media image.

  • Author: Madison Beer
  • Publisher: Harper
  • Format: Hardcover, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063237698

title: The Guardians
author: John Christopher
description:
The Guardians is John Christopher's classic dystopian novel for young readers, set in a future England split between the crowded, regimented Conurbs and the old-fashioned country estates of the County. When orphaned Rob Randall slips across the border, he begins to see how carefully controlled his whole society really is.

At its heart the story is about freedom: how easily it can be traded for comfort, and why the young must fight to gain it and then hold on to it. This edition belongs to a fiction series published for schools, and the novel won the Guardian children's fiction prize, making it a strong choice for classrooms and for readers who enjoy classic science fiction.

  • Author: John Christopher
  • Publisher: Heinemann Educational Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 156 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780435121761

title: The Emotion Code Dr
sheet_title: The Emotion Code Dr Bradley Nelson
author: Bradley Nelson
description:
The Emotion Code is holistic physician Dr Bradley Nelson's guide to what he calls trapped emotions: the lingering emotional energy he believes difficult past experiences leave behind in the body. This revised and expanded edition sets out his approach to the subconscious mind and how unresolved feelings may affect wellbeing.

Nelson describes how these emotional burdens can, in his view, contribute to pain, illness and patterns in the way we think and relate to others, and he explains his method for identifying and releasing them. Written in an accessible style, it will appeal to readers exploring energy healing, holistic health and self-directed approaches to emotional wellbeing.

  • Author: Dr Bradley Nelson
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781785042874

title: Very Good Lives
sheet_title: Very Good Lives J K Rowling
author: J.K. Rowling
description:
Very Good Lives presents the commencement address J.K. Rowling gave at Harvard University in 2008, published in book form with illustrations by Joel Holland. In it, the author reflects on two themes that shaped her own path: the unexpected benefits of failure and the importance of imagination.

Drawing on her years after graduation, when life looked far from the success that followed, Rowling considers how setbacks can clarify what matters and how imagination allows us to understand and help others. Short, warm and thoughtful, it makes an ideal gift for graduates and for anyone standing at a crossroads in life.

  • Author: J.K. Rowling
  • Illustrator: Joel Holland
  • Publisher: Little, Brown and Company
  • Format: Hardcover, 74 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780316369152

title: The French Dispatch
author: Wes Anderson
description:
The French Dispatch is the book of Wes Anderson's film of the same name, published by Faber & Faber. The film presents a set of stories drawn from the last edition of a US magazine based in an invented twentieth-century French town, told in Anderson's distinctive, meticulously composed style.

The ensemble cast of the film includes Bill Murray, Tilda Swinton, Frances McDormand, Benicio del Toro, Adrien Brody, Timothée Chalamet, Léa Seydoux, Jeffrey Wright and Owen Wilson. A handsome hardback for film lovers, collectors of Anderson's work and anyone interested in screenwriting and the craft behind modern film-making.

  • Author: Wes Anderson
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571360475

title: THE 5 AM CLUB OWN YOUR MORNING ELEVATE YOUR LIFE
sheet_title: THE 5 AM CLUB OWN YOUR MORNING ELEVATE YOUR LIFE
author: Robin Sharma
description:
The 5 AM Club is Robin Sharma's guide to the power of an early-morning routine, a concept the leadership and performance coach has taught to clients for more than two decades. He argues that the first hours of the day, used well, can lift productivity, health, focus and calm.

Rather than a straight manual, the book unfolds as a story in which a pair of strangers, each going through a hard time, fall under the wing of an unconventional billionaire who shows them his morning method. Along the way Sharma shares habits drawn from high achievers, making this an approachable, motivating read for anyone hoping to reshape their days.

  • Author: Robin Sharma
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008312831

title: Ivy and Bean's Treasure Box
sheet_title: Ivy And Bean S Treasure Box Annie Barrows
author: Annie Barrows
description:
Ivy and Bean's Treasure Box collects the first three books in Annie Barrows' chapter-book series, illustrated by Sophie Blackall. It introduces two second graders who are sure they could never be friends: noisy, wild and goofy Bean, and quiet, thoughtful Ivy, who is busy learning to be a witch.

Of course, the two soon discover that being opposites makes them a perfect team, and their schemes and adventures follow from there. The set includes Ivy and Bean, Ivy and Bean and the Ghost That Had to Go and Ivy and Bean Break the Fossil Record, making it a lovely starting point for newly independent readers.

  • Author: Annie Barrows
  • Illustrator: Sophie Blackall
  • Publisher: Chronicle Books
  • Format: Paperback boxed set, 376 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Ivy & Bean, Books 1-3
  • ISBN: 9780811864954

title: Pachinko National Book Award Finalist
sheet_title: Pachinko National Book Award Finalist Min Jin Lee
author: Min Jin Lee
description:
Pachinko is Min Jin Lee's sweeping historical novel following one Korean family across four generations. It opens in the early twentieth century with Sunja, a fisherman's daughter who becomes pregnant by a wealthy, married stranger and chooses instead to marry a kind young minister bound for Japan.

That decision shapes the lives of her children and grandchildren as they face prejudice, poverty and hard choices as Koreans in Japan, from crowded markets and elite universities to the pachinko parlours on the edges of respectability. A richly told story of family, sacrifice, identity and belonging, it is a rewarding choice for book clubs and lovers of literary fiction.

  • Author: Min Jin Lee
  • Publisher: Grand Central Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 484 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781455563920

title: How To Read A Book
sheet_title: How To Read A Book Mortimer J. Adler
author: Mortimer J. Adler, Charles Van Doren
description:
How to Read a Book is Mortimer J. Adler and Charles Van Doren's classic guide to reading well. First published in 1940 and later thoroughly revised, it explains the different levels of reading, from basic comprehension and quick inspectional skimming to the slow, analytical reading that lets you truly grasp and judge a book.

The authors show how to classify a book, map out its structure, identify the author's argument and respond to it critically, then adapt those skills to practical works, fiction, plays, poetry, history, mathematics, philosophy and the social sciences. A suggested reading list and self-tests round it out, making it a lasting companion for students and lifelong learners.

  • Author: Mortimer J. Adler and Charles Van Doren
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Paperback, 424 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780671212094

title: Make Your Bed Little Things That Can Change Your Life
sheet_title: Make Your Bed Little Things That Can Change Your Life
author: William H. McRaven
description:
Make Your Bed is Admiral William H. McRaven's short, inspiring book based on the commencement speech he gave at the University of Texas. A former US Navy SEAL, he begins with the simplest daily habit of all, arguing that finishing one small task each morning builds momentum for everything that follows.

From there he shares ten lessons drawn from his SEAL training and military career, each tied to a personal story about discipline, resilience, teamwork and hope. Brief and direct, it makes a thoughtful gift for graduates, young leaders and anyone looking for practical encouragement to face life's challenges.

  • Author: William H. McRaven
  • Publisher: Grand Central Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781455570249

title: The Speed of Trust
sheet_title: Speed Of Trust Stephen M R Covey
author: Stephen M.R. Covey, Rebecca R. Merrill
description:
The Speed of Trust is Stephen M.R. Covey's business and leadership book on why trust is the factor that most affects how people and organisations perform. Written with Rebecca R. Merrill, it argues that when trust rises, work moves faster and costs fall, and when it drops, everything slows down and grows more expensive.

Covey breaks trust down into behaviours that can be learned, measured and improved, and shows how it operates across personal credibility, relationships, teams, organisations and markets. Practical and example-driven, it suits managers, team leaders, entrepreneurs and professionals who want to build stronger working relationships and lead with integrity.

  • Author: Stephen M.R. Covey with Rebecca R. Merrill
  • Publisher: Free Press
  • Format: Paperback, 354 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781416549000

title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
author: John Green
description:
The Anthropocene Reviewed is John Green's first work of nonfiction, a collection of personal essays expanded from his podcast of the same name. The Anthropocene is the current geological age, defined by humanity's impact on the planet, and Green reviews its many facets one by one, awarding each a rating out of five stars.

His subjects range widely, from the QWERTY keyboard and Halley's Comet to sunsets, scratch-and-sniff stickers and the Penguins of Madagascar. Funny, tender and often moving, the essays blend observation with memoir, reflecting on wonder, grief and what it means to be human. It is a fine pick for Green's longtime readers and fans of thoughtful essay collections.

  • Author: John Green
  • Publisher: Dutton
  • Format: Paperback, 294 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780525555230

title: The Gifts Of Imperfection Brene Brown
sheet_title: The Gifts Of Imperfection Brene Brown
author: Brené Brown
description:
The Gifts of Imperfection is social scientist Brené Brown's guide to wholehearted living, the book where much of her work on courage, vulnerability and self-worth began. It is built around ten guideposts that help readers loosen the grip of perfectionism and accept themselves as they are.

Brown turns her research into everyday practices, from cultivating self-compassion, gratitude and creativity to making room for rest, play and meaningful work. Warm, honest and down to earth, she also tackles the unrealistic expectations that so often hold us back. It is a gentle, encouraging read for anyone seeking more authenticity, connection and joy in daily life.

  • Author: Brené Brown
  • Publisher: Hazelden Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781616499600

title: One Up On Wall Street
sheet_title: One Up On Wall Street Peter Lynch
author: Peter Lynch
description:
One Up On Wall Street is Peter Lynch's classic guide to stock market investing for ordinary people. Lynch, who ran Fidelity's Magellan Fund, argues that individual investors have real advantages over professionals, because they often notice promising companies in daily life long before analysts do.

He explains how to research a business, judge its prospects and spot the shares he dubbed tenbaggers, stocks that grow to ten times their purchase price, while avoiding common traps. Clear, practical and full of plain-spoken advice, it remains a valuable read for beginners and experienced investors who want to make informed decisions with their own money.

  • Author: Peter Lynch
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780743200400

title: What Mummy Makes: Cook Just Once
sheet_title: What Mummy Makes: Cook Just Once Rebecca Wilson
author: Rebecca Wilson
description:
What Mummy Makes is Rebecca Wilson's family cookbook for parents who are weaning a baby and want to stop making separate meals. Its idea is simple: cook one dish that suits everyone at the table, with more than 130 recipes suitable for babies from six months old.

The recipes are designed to be quick, ready in under half an hour, and easy to adapt for different ages and dietary needs. Eating together also lets little ones learn by watching the rest of the family. It is a practical, time-saving choice for busy parents starting solids who want relaxed, shared mealtimes.

  • Author: Rebecca Wilson
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241455159

title: The 7 Habits Of Highly Effective Teens Covey
sheet_title: The 7 Habits Of Highly Effective Teens Covey
author: Sean Covey
description:
The 7 Habits of Highly Effective Teens is Sean Covey's adaptation of his father Stephen R. Covey's famous framework, written specifically for teenagers. This updated edition takes the seven habits into the digital age and applies them to the real pressures young people face at school, at home and online.

Using cartoons, quotes, true stories and practical exercises, Covey helps readers build self-esteem, make good friends, stand up to peer pressure, set goals and get along with parents. Upbeat and easy to dip into, it is a helpful choice for teens, parents, teachers and anyone guiding young people through big decisions.

  • Author: Sean Covey
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781476764665

title: The 4-Hour Work Week
author: Timothy Ferriss
description:
The 4-Hour Work Week is Timothy Ferriss's guide to designing a life that is not built entirely around work. This expanded and updated edition challenges the idea of saving freedom for retirement, arguing that travel, time and income can be enjoyed now through smarter choices about how you work.

Ferriss shares tactics for eliminating busywork, automating income, outsourcing tasks to virtual assistants and negotiating remote working arrangements, along with the principles behind his idea of lifestyle design. Bold and provocative, it appeals to entrepreneurs, employees who want more flexibility and anyone curious about escaping the traditional nine-to-five.

  • Author: Timothy Ferriss
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 396 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780091929114

title: The Course Of Love
sheet_title: The Course Of Love Alain De Botton
author: Alain de Botton
description:
The Course of Love is a novel by Alain de Botton that follows a romantic partnership well beyond the point where most love stories end. In Edinburgh, Rabih and Kirsten meet, fall in love, marry and have children, and the book traces what happens to their ideals as ordinary life sets in.

Interwoven with the story are de Botton's own reflections on attachment, sex, parenthood, arguments and forgiveness, offering wry, perceptive commentary on why long-term love is so demanding and so worthwhile. Wise and often funny, it suits readers who enjoy fiction with a philosophical edge and anyone curious about what it takes to make love last.

  • Author: Alain de Botton
  • Publisher: Scribner
  • Format: Paperback, 222 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781501134517

title: The Whole-Brain Child: 12 Revolutionary Strategies to Nurture Your Child's Developing Mind
sheet_title: The Whole-Brain Child 12 Revolutionary Strategies to Nuture
author: Daniel J. Siegel, Tina Payne Bryson
description:
The Whole-Brain Child is a practical parenting guide by neuropsychiatrist Daniel J. Siegel and parenting expert Tina Payne Bryson. It explains, in clear everyday language, how a child's brain is wired and how it develops, and why those changes shape children's emotions, behaviour and reactions.

The authors offer twelve strategies for turning daily struggles and meltdowns into chances to help children grow, including ways to connect the logical and emotional sides of the brain and calm big feelings. Illustrated with real-life examples and simple tools to share with kids, it is a helpful, encouraging read for parents, carers and educators.

  • Author: Daniel J. Siegel and Tina Payne Bryson
  • Publisher: Random House Publishing Group
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780553386691

title: WHAT TO EXPECT THE FIRST YEAR
sheet_title: WHAT TO EXPECT THE FIRST YEAR
author: Heidi Murkoff
description:
What to Expect the First Year is Heidi Murkoff's comprehensive guide to caring for a new baby, part of the long-running What to Expect series. This fully revised third edition keeps the familiar month-by-month format, walking parents through each stage of the first twelve months one step at a time.

It covers feeding, sleep, growth and development, everyday care, health concerns and the many questions that come up along the way, in a reassuring and easy-to-navigate style. Updated for modern families, it is an invaluable reference for new parents to keep close at hand from the first days at home onwards.

  • Author: Heidi Murkoff
  • Publisher: Workman Publishing Company
  • Format: Paperback, 704 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: What to Expect
  • ISBN: 9780761181507

title: Will
author: Will Smith, Mark Manson
description:
Will is the memoir of Will Smith, written with Mark Manson, tracing his journey from growing up afraid in a volatile West Philadelphia home to success as a rap star and later as one of Hollywood's biggest film actors. Along the way he describes the music and movie careers that made him a household name.

Yet the book is as much about inner life as outer achievement. Smith reflects candidly on fear, family, relationships and the search for happiness and real connection, sharing lessons learned through hard experience. Open and energetic, it will appeal to fans of his work and to readers who enjoy honest celebrity memoirs about personal growth.

  • Author: Will Smith with Mark Manson
  • Publisher: Penguin Press
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781984879868

title: Think Like A Monk
author: Jay Shetty
description:
Think Like a Monk is Jay Shetty's guide to bringing the wisdom of monastic life into everyday routines. After graduating from business school in London, Shetty chose to spend three years living as a monk in India before returning to share what he learned about peace of mind, focus and purpose.

Combining ancient teachings with modern research and personal stories, he offers practical exercises for overcoming negative thinking, managing fear and stress, building healthier habits and relationships, and finding meaning in work. Accessible and encouraging, it suits readers looking for a calmer, more intentional way of living.

  • Author: Jay Shetty
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Publishers UK
  • Format: Paperback, 402 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008355562

title: The Comfort Crisis
author: Michael Easter
description:
The Comfort Crisis is journalist Michael Easter's investigation into how modern comfort may be harming us. He asks whether our climate-controlled, well-fed and rarely challenged lives lie behind many of today's physical and mental health problems, and argues that regular, deliberate discomfort could be part of the answer.

To find out, Easter seeks out researchers, unconventional thinkers and specialists in physical and mental conditioning, and tests the ideas himself through challenging experiences in the wild. Lively and thought-provoking, it blends science, evolution and adventure, and suits readers interested in health, resilience and stepping beyond their comfort zone.

  • Author: Michael Easter
  • Publisher: Rodale Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593138762

title: Winter Turning: Wings of Fire Graphic Novel #7
sheet_title: Winter Turning: Wings Of Fire7 Tui T. Sutherland
author: Tui T. Sutherland
description:
Winter Turning is volume 7 of the Wings of Fire graphic novel series, adapting Tui T. Sutherland's fantasy novel with full-colour artwork by Mike Holmes. It follows Winter, a young IceWing prince who has always felt like a disappointment to his royal family, as he sets out to find his runaway sister, Icicle.

Icicle has fled Jade Mountain Academy after committing terrible crimes, and his clawmates Qibli, Moon and Kinkajou insist on joining his dangerous search, even when it leads them into the clutches of the cruel Queen Scarlet. A gripping story of loyalty, pride and second chances, it is ideal for young fans of the dragon saga and newcomers to graphic novels.

  • Author: Tui T. Sutherland
  • Illustrator: Mike Holmes
  • Publisher: Graphix
  • Format: Hardcover, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Wings of Fire Graphic Novel, Book 7
  • ISBN: 9781338730937

title: Collected Poems and Selected Translations
sheet_title: Norman Cameron: Collected Poems And Selected Norman Cameron
author: Norman Cameron
description:
Collected Poems and Selected Translations brings together the complete poetry of the British poet Norman Cameron (1905–1953) in a single paperback from Anvil Press Poetry. Alongside his own poems, it offers a selection of his translations, notably his versions of the French poet François Villon.

The volume is edited by Warren Hope and Jonathan Barker, with an introduction by Barker and a biographical study of Cameron by Hope, giving readers useful context on the poet's life and work. It is a valuable edition for poetry lovers and students of twentieth-century British verse.

  • Author: Norman Cameron
  • Editors: Warren Hope and Jonathan Barker
  • Publisher: Anvil Press Poetry
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780856464249

title: My Hygge Home: How To Make Home Your Happy Place
sheet_title: My Hygge Home: How To Make Home Your Happy Place Meik Wiking
author: Meik Wiking
description:
My Hygge Home is Meik Wiking's guide to turning your home into a place of comfort, calm and happiness, inspired by Danish design and traditions. Drawing on new research from the Happiness Research Institute in Copenhagen, which he leads, Wiking looks at what makes people feel truly content where they live.

He offers simple, budget-friendly ideas for using light, colour and space to create a cosy sanctuary, whatever the size of your home, along with ways to make room for rest and shared memories. Warm and full of inspiration, it makes a lovely gift for homemakers, new homeowners and fans of the Danish art of hygge.

  • Author: Meik Wiking
  • Publisher: Penguin Life
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241517970

title: The Life-Changing Magic of Not Giving a F**k
sheet_title: THE LIFECHANGING MAGIC OF NOT GIVING A F**K
author: Sarah Knight
description:
The Life-Changing Magic of Not Giving a F**k is Sarah Knight's irreverent self-help book about caring less in order to live more. A playful parody of Marie Kondo's famous decluttering guide, it applies the same tidy-up logic to the obligations, guilt and people-pleasing that clutter up our minds.

Knight introduces her two-step NotSorry Method for deciding what truly deserves your energy, time and money, and for letting go of the rest without feeling bad about it, from family drama and work politics to other people's opinions. Funny, frank and genuinely practical, it is ideal for anyone overcommitted and ready to reclaim their own priorities. The book contains strong language.

  • Author: Sarah Knight
  • Publisher: Quercus
  • Format: Hardcover, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784298463

title: Lifespan: Why We Age and Why We Don't Have To
sheet_title: Lifespan: Why We Age And Why We Don T Have To David Sinclair
author: David A. Sinclair
description:
Lifespan is Harvard geneticist David A. Sinclair's provocative look at why we grow old and whether we have to. Challenging the assumption that ageing is simply inevitable, he puts forward a bold theory that treats ageing itself as a condition that could one day be slowed, treated or even reversed.

Sinclair takes readers inside the latest longevity research, much of it from his own laboratory, explaining the ancient survival circuitry in our genes and the vitality genes scientists hope to switch on. He also discusses the lifestyle factors he believes matter and the ethical questions raised by much longer lives. It is a fascinating read for anyone interested in health, biology and the future of medicine.

  • Author: David A. Sinclair
  • Publisher: Thorsons
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008292348

title: How to Win: The Argument, the Pitch, the Job, the Race
sheet_title: How To Win: The Argument The Pitch The Job Rob Yeung
author: Rob Yeung
description:
How to Win is psychologist Dr Rob Yeung's practical guide to coming out on top when it counts, whether in a debate, a sales pitch, a job search or a competitive challenge. The first part of the book looks at the winning mindset, what success means and the general techniques anyone can learn to improve their chances.

The second part turns to specific scenarios, covering influence and persuasion, presenting ideas convincingly, job hunting, CVs and interviews, and time management and personal effectiveness. Clear and results-focused, it suits ambitious professionals, job seekers and anyone wanting to build confidence and perform better under pressure.

  • Author: Dr Rob Yeung
  • Publisher: Capstone
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780857084293

title: Willy And The Wobbly House
sheet_title: Willy And The Wobbly House Margot Sunderland
author: Margot Sunderland
description:
Willy and the Wobbly House is an illustrated therapeutic story by child psychotherapist Margot Sunderland, with pictures by Nicky Armstrong, written for children who are anxious or obsessional. Willy is a worried boy who feels that the world is unsteady and that something awful could happen at any moment.

His neighbour Joe has the opposite problem, so tidy and controlled that he can never truly relax and enjoy himself. With help from the Puddle People, the two boys find ways to loosen their rigid habits and live more freely. Part of a series designed to help children with their feelings, it is a useful resource for parents, teachers and therapists.

  • Author: Margot Sunderland
  • Illustrator: Nicky Armstrong
  • Publisher: Routledge
  • Format: Paperback, 28 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780863884986

title: The Last Devil To Die: Thursday Murder Club 4
sheet_title: The Last Devil To Die: Thursday Murder Club 4 Richard Osman
author: Richard Osman
description:
The Last Devil to Die is the fourth Thursday Murder Club mystery from Richard Osman. When an old friend of the group who dealt in antiques is murdered, and a dangerous package he was keeping safe disappears, the four retirement-village sleuths find themselves drawn into a tangled new case.

Their investigation brings them up against art forgers, online scammers and drug dealers, while heartbreak closer to home tests the friends in new ways. Warm, witty and moving as well as cleverly plotted, it is a treat for fans of the series and for readers who love a cosy crime story with plenty of heart.

  • Author: Richard Osman
  • Publisher: Viking
  • Format: Hardcover, 421 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Thursday Murder Club, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9780241512449

title: Principles For Success
author: Ray Dalio
description:
Principles for Success is an illustrated, condensed adaptation of Ray Dalio's longer book Principles: Life and Work. Dalio, the founder of the investment firm Bridgewater Associates, distils his unconventional approach to life and decision-making into a short, accessible format that readers of any age can enjoy.

Through engaging illustrations, it covers his core ideas on setting goals, learning from mistakes, facing reality and working with others to achieve exceptional results. Whether you already know Principles or are discovering Dalio's thinking for the first time, it is a quick, memorable introduction and a good gift for students and graduates.

  • Author: Ray Dalio
  • Publisher: Avid Reader Press / Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781982147211

title: Kingdom Of The Wicked
sheet_title: Kingdom Of The Wicked Kerri Maniscalco
author: Kerri Maniscalco
description:
Kingdom of the Wicked is the first book in Kerri Maniscalco's dark fantasy romance series. Emilia and her twin sister Vittoria are witches hiding their powers from the humans around them in Sicily, where they work in their family's well-known restaurant, until the night Emilia finds her twin brutally murdered.

Determined to find the killer, Emilia turns to forbidden dark magic and summons Wrath, one of the Wicked princes of Hell she was warned about as a child. Their uneasy alliance crackles with tension and attraction. Atmospheric and romantic, it suits readers who enjoy enemies-to-lovers stories, witches and mythology-rich fantasy.

  • Author: Kerri Maniscalco
  • Publisher: Jimmy Patterson Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 372 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Kingdom of the Wicked, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780316428460

title: Tokyo Revengers Omnibus Vol. 7-8
sheet_title: Tokyo Revengers Omnibus Vol. 7 8 Ken Wakui
author: Ken Wakui
description:
Tokyo Revengers Omnibus Vol. 7-8 collects volumes 7 and 8 of Ken Wakui's time-travel delinquent manga in one 2-in-1 edition, the fourth omnibus in the English release from Seven Seas. Takemichi has failed to bring Baji back to the Tokyo Manji Gang, and back in his own time, he finds that things have only grown worse.

He recalls pieces of the looming battle between Toman and Valhalla, in which Baji dies at Kazutora's hands and Mikey retaliates with brutal vengeance, and he must find a way to change that outcome. Packed with gang rivalry, loyalty and tough choices, this omnibus will grip fans of action-driven shonen manga.

  • Author: Ken Wakui
  • Publisher: Seven Seas
  • Format: Paperback, 414 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Tokyo Revengers 2-in-1 Omnibus, Book 4 (Vols. 7-8)
  • ISBN: 9781638587347

title: The Christmas Pig
author: J.K. Rowling
vendor: Little, Brown Books for Young Readers
description:
The Christmas Pig is J.K. Rowling's festive adventure for young readers, illustrated by Jim Field. Jack adores his old toy, Dur Pig, who has stood by him through happy times and hard ones, until one Christmas Eve DP goes missing.

But Christmas Eve is a night when lost things and toys can come alive, and Jack's brand-new Christmas Pig, the replacement he never wanted, comes up with a bold plan. Together they set off on a magical quest to bring back Jack's dearest companion. Heartfelt and full of adventure, it is a lovely story to share as a family at Christmas.

  • Author: J.K. Rowling
  • Illustrator: Jim Field
  • Publisher: Little, Brown Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Hardcover, 312 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781444964912

title: My Life In Full: Work Family And Our Future
sheet_title: My Life In Full: Work Family And Our Future Indra Nooyi
author: Indra Nooyi
description:
My Life in Full is the memoir of Indra Nooyi, who spent twelve years as chief executive of PepsiCo and became the first immigrant and woman of colour to head one of the Fortune 50. She traces her path from a childhood and schooling in 1960s India to the Yale School of Management and on to the top of corporate America.

Nooyi is candid about the sacrifices her career demanded and the tension between work and family that so many people face. Drawing on her experience, she makes a compelling case for better support for working families, including paid leave, flexible work and childcare. Thoughtful and practical, it suits leaders, professionals and anyone balancing ambition with home life.

  • Author: Indra Nooyi
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Hardcover, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780349426129

title: It Ends With Us: Special Hardback Edition
sheet_title: It Ends With Us: Special Hardback Edition Colleen Hoover
author: Colleen Hoover
description:
It Ends with Us is Colleen Hoover's emotional contemporary novel, presented here in a special hardback edition. Lily has worked hard to leave her small-town past behind, graduating from college, moving to Boston and opening her own business, when she falls for Ryle Kincaid, a confident and brilliant neurosurgeon.

Ryle appears almost perfect, yet his reluctance about relationships hints at deeper problems, and when Lily's first love, Atlas, reappears, she is forced to face difficult truths. Raw and powerful, the novel explores love, courage and breaking painful cycles. It is the first book in a duology, followed by It Starts with Us.

  • Author: Colleen Hoover
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Hardcover, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: It Ends with Us, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781398521551

title: The Architecture Book
author: DK
description:
The Architecture Book is part of DK's Big Ideas Simply Explained series, offering a clear, visual introduction to the thinking behind great buildings worldwide. It covers architecture from around the globe, explaining important movements, styles, architects and landmark structures in straightforward language.

Packed with timelines, diagrams, charts and striking illustrations, the book breaks complex topics into digestible entries, making it equally useful for curious newcomers and for those wanting to brush up on what they know. It suits students, design enthusiasts and anyone who wants to understand how buildings reflect the societies that made them.

  • Author: DK
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Big Ideas Simply Explained
  • ISBN: 9780241415030

title: The Secret
author: Rhonda Byrne
description:
The Secret is Rhonda Byrne's inspirational book about the law of attraction, the idea that our thoughts and feelings shape what we draw into our lives. It followed her 2006 documentary film of the same name and gathers ideas she traces through oral traditions, literature, religions and philosophies across the centuries.

Byrne explains how to apply these principles to money, health, relationships, happiness and personal goals, encouraging readers to focus on gratitude and positive intention. It suits readers interested in spirituality, mindset and personal development, and it later inspired the feature film The Secret: Dare to Dream.

  • Author: Rhonda Byrne
  • Publisher: Atria Books / Beyond Words
  • Format: Hardcover, 216 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781582701707

title: The Coming Wave
author: Mustafa Suleyman
description:
The Coming Wave is Mustafa Suleyman's urgent account of the technologies set to reshape the coming decade, written with Michael Bhaskar. As a co-founder of the AI company DeepMind, Suleyman has been at the heart of this revolution, and he argues that artificial intelligence and synthetic biology are spreading faster than we can control them.

He explores how these tools could bring extraordinary prosperity while also threatening the nation-state and the global order built on it, and why containing them may be the defining challenge of our time. Clear and thought-provoking, it suits readers interested in technology, politics and the future of society.

  • Author: Mustafa Suleyman with Michael Bhaskar
  • Publisher: The Bodley Head
  • Format: Hardcover, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847927484

title: None Of This Is True
sheet_title: None Of This Is True Lisa Jewell
author: Lisa Jewell
description:
None of This Is True is a psychological thriller from Lisa Jewell. On the evening she turns forty-five, podcaster Alix Summers gets talking to Josie Fair, a quiet, unremarkable woman in the same pub who, it turns out, was born on exactly the same day.

When the two cross paths again, Josie suggests she would make a fascinating subject for Alix's next podcast, hinting that big changes are coming in her life. Alix agrees despite her unease, only to discover that Josie is hiding very dark secrets. Twisty and unsettling, it is perfect for fans of dark, slow-burning suspense.

  • Author: Lisa Jewell
  • Publisher: Atria Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 390 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781982179007

title: Joyfull: Cook Effortlessly, Eat Freely, Live Radiantly
sheet_title: Joyfull: Cook Effortlessly Eat Freely Radhi Devlukia Shetty
author: Radhi Devlukia-Shetty
description:
Joyfull: Cook Effortlessly, Eat Freely, Live Radiantly is a cookbook by Radhi Devlukia-Shetty. It brings together plant-based recipes built around everyday cooking that is simple, nourishing and enjoyable.

Written for home cooks who want healthy food without fuss, it suits anyone exploring vegan meals or looking for fresh ideas to bring more balance and joy to the kitchen.

  • Author: Radhi Devlukia-Shetty
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008618735

title: Start With Why
author: Simon Sinek
description:
Start with Why is Simon Sinek's book on how great leaders and organisations inspire people to act. Sinek asks why some people and companies consistently achieve more and command deeper loyalty than their rivals, and finds the answer in a shared pattern: they begin by communicating their purpose before anything else.

Using examples such as the Wright brothers, Martin Luther King Jr. and Apple's Steve Jobs, he introduces the Golden Circle, a simple framework built on why, how and what. Clear and persuasive, it suits leaders, entrepreneurs, marketers and anyone who wants to build trust, motivate a team or find greater purpose in their work.

  • Author: Simon Sinek
  • Publisher: Portfolio
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781591842804

title: The Code Breaker
author: Walter Isaacson
description:
The Code Breaker is Walter Isaacson's biography of Jennifer Doudna, the Nobel Prize-winning biochemist who helped develop CRISPR, a simple and powerful tool for editing DNA. Isaacson follows her journey from a childhood fascination with science to a leading role in a scientific race that is transforming medicine.

The book explores how gene editing is already being used against deadly diseases and in the fight against the coronavirus, and asks the hard moral questions it raises, from treating illness to altering the genes of future generations. Vivid and accessible, it suits readers interested in science, innovation and the ethics of our genetic future.

  • Author: Walter Isaacson
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Hardcover, 560 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781398502314

title: House Of Flame And Shadow
sheet_title: House Of Flame And Shadow Sarah J. Maas
author: Sarah J. Maas
description:
House of Flame and Shadow is the third Crescent City novel by Sarah J. Maas, an adult fantasy romance series. Having glimpsed a world beyond Midgard, Bryce Quinlan is now cut off in an unfamiliar realm and desperate to return to the family, friends and mate she left behind.

Meanwhile Hunt Athalar is held captive once more by the Asteri, powerless and with no idea what has become of Bryce. Packed with intrigue, danger and romance, this instalment follows House of Earth and Blood and House of Sky and Breath and continues the story for readers of the series. This is the UK hardback edition.

  • Author: Sarah J. Maas
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury
  • Format: Hardcover, 816 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Crescent City, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781408884447

title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
sheet_title: Harry Potter And The Sorcerer S Stone J. K. Rowling
author: J.K. Rowling
description:
Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone is the first book in J.K. Rowling's Harry Potter series, in the American edition from Scholastic with illustrations by Mary GrandPré. Orphaned Harry lives a miserable life with his unkind aunt and uncle, sleeping in a cupboard under the stairs, until a letter reveals that he is a wizard.

Whisked off to Hogwarts, he discovers friendship, magic and the truth about his past as the only person ever to survive an attack by Lord Voldemort. A timeless story of courage, loyalty and belonging, it is the perfect start to the series for young readers. The book is published in the UK as Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone.

  • Author: J.K. Rowling
  • Illustrator: Mary GrandPré
  • Publisher: Scholastic
  • Format: Hardcover, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Harry Potter, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780590353403

title: The Light We Carry: Overcoming in Uncertain Times
sheet_title: The Light We Carry Overcoming In Uncertain Michelle Obama
author: Michelle Obama
description:
The Light We Carry is former First Lady Michelle Obama's follow-up to her memoir Becoming, sharing hard-won lessons on keeping hope and balance when the world feels unsettled. Drawing on her own experiences, she describes the habits, tools and relationships that help her navigate change, fear and self-doubt.

Candid and warm, she reflects on building honest, lasting friendships, finding strength in community and difference, parenting, partnership and facing adversity with grace. It is an encouraging, conversational read for anyone looking for perspective and resilience in challenging times.

  • Author: Michelle Obama
  • Publisher: Crown
  • Format: Hardcover, 319 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593237465

title: House Of Flame And Shadow
sheet_title: House Of Flame And Shadow Sarah J Maas
author: Sarah J. Maas
description:
House of Flame and Shadow is the third book in Sarah J. Maas's Crescent City series, the adult fantasy romance saga that began with House of Earth and Blood. Bryce Quinlan has seen a realm beyond Midgard, but now all she wants is to find her way back to the people she loves.

Lost in an unfamiliar world and unsure whom she can rely on, Bryce must depend on her wits, while Hunt Athalar is once more a prisoner of the Asteri and unable to help her. Full of high stakes, shifting alliances and romance, this hardback edition picks up after House of Sky and Breath for fans of the series.

  • Author: Sarah J. Maas
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 848 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Crescent City, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781635574104

title: Outlive: The Science And Art Of Longevity Peter Attia Md
sheet_title: Outlive: The Science And Art Of Longevity Peter Attia Md
author: Peter Attia, Bill Gifford
description:
Outlive is physician Peter Attia's guide to living longer and better, written with Bill Gifford. Attia argues that mainstream medicine has made too little headway against the chronic diseases of ageing, such as heart disease, cancer, Alzheimer's and diabetes, and calls for a proactive, preventive approach instead.

Drawing on the latest research, he sets out practical strategies for exercise, nutrition, sleep and emotional health, explaining how each can extend not just lifespan but the quality of the years ahead. Detailed yet readable, it suits anyone who wants to take a more active role in their long-term health.

  • Author: Peter Attia with Bill Gifford
  • Publisher: Harmony
  • Format: Hardcover, 496 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593236598

title: OMG Shakespeare Boxed Set
author: Courtney Carbone, Brett Wright
vendor: Random House Books for Young Readers
description:
OMG Shakespeare Boxed Set brings together three playful retellings of Shakespeare's best-known tragedies: YOLO Juliet, srsly Hamlet and Macbeth #killing it. Adapted by Courtney Carbone and Brett Wright, each story imagines the famous characters with smartphones, telling the plays through texts, emojis, photos and status updates.

Juliet and her Romeo, Hamlet and Ophelia, and the scheming Macbeths check in, post and message their way through love, revenge and ambition. Each book includes a cast list and glossary to help readers follow along. Light-hearted and accessible, it makes a fun introduction to Shakespeare for teens and a witty gift for readers who know the originals.

  • Publisher: Random House Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Hardcover boxed set

title: Spare By
author: Prince Harry
description:
Spare is the memoir of Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex. It begins with the moment that two boys followed the coffin of Diana, Princess of Wales, through London as millions looked on, and goes on to tell Harry's own story of what followed that day.

Harry writes with striking openness about grief, family, military service in Afghanistan, his mental health, his marriage and his decision to step back from royal life. Personal and revealing, it offers his perspective on the events that shaped him and on how love can outlast loss.

  • Author: Prince Harry
  • Publisher: Bantam
  • Format: Hardcover, 410 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780857504791

title: The Meaning Of Thought
sheet_title: The Meaning Of Thought Markus Gabriel
author: Markus Gabriel
description:
The Meaning of Thought is German philosopher Markus Gabriel's exploration of what makes human thinking distinctive, translated by Alex Englander. Writing at a time when knowledge is dismissed as fake news and artificial intelligence seems to rival the human mind, he steps back to ask what thought actually is.

Gabriel proposes that thinking is a kind of sixth sense, closely bound to our biological nature, rather than mere data processing. Thought, he argues, links images and ideas across our senses and reaches far beyond the present moment. Clear and challenging, it suits readers interested in philosophy of mind, technology and what it means to be human.

  • Author: Markus Gabriel
  • Translator: Alex Englander
  • Publisher: Polity
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781509538362

title: The Complete Works Of
sheet_title: The Complete Works Of William Shakespeare
author: William Shakespeare
description:
The Complete Works of William Shakespeare is a paperback edition published by Wentworth Press, crediting William Shakespeare together with the Shakespeare scholar Sidney Lee.

Shakespeare's plays and poems remain among the most widely read and performed works in English literature, and this edition suits students, theatre lovers and readers who want his writing on their own shelves.

  • With: Sidney Lee

  • Format: Paperback, 290 pages

title: Wings of Fire Box Set: The Dragonet Prophecy (Books 1-5)
sheet_title: Wings Of Fire: Dragonet Prophecy Box Set Tui T. Sutherland
author: Tui T. Sutherland
description:
This Wings of Fire box set gathers the first five books of Tui T. Sutherland's dragon fantasy series for young readers in paperback. In the land of Pyrrhia the dragon tribes have been at war for years, and a prophecy foretells that five dragonets will bring the bloodshed to an end and decide who will be the next queen.

But Clay, Sunny, Glory, Tsunami and Starflight are not sure they want that destiny, especially once they uncover the truth about their secret upbringing. The set contains Book 1, The Dragonet Prophecy; Book 2, The Lost Heir; Book 3, The Hidden Kingdom; Book 4, The Dark Secret; and Book 5, The Brightest Night.

  • Publisher: Scholastic
  • Format: Paperback boxed set, 1680 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Wings of Fire, Books 1-5

title: November 9
author: Colleen Hoover
description:
November 9 is a contemporary romance by Colleen Hoover, presented here in a large print edition. On the eve of her move to the other side of the country, Fallon crosses paths with Ben, a would-be writer, and the two spend her final hours in LA side by side.

Ben finds in Fallon's eventful life the spark for the book he has long wanted to write, and they promise to reunite each year on that very date. As time passes and their separate lives move on, Fallon begins to wonder whether Ben's story is the truth or a carefully crafted plot twist. Emotional and full of surprises, it suits readers who love heartfelt, twisty romance.

  • Author: Colleen Hoover
  • Publisher: Thorndike Press Large Print
  • Format: Paperback, large print, 463 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781432897291

title: Hat Box: The Collected Lyrics
sheet_title: Hat Box: The Collected Lyrics Stephen Sondheim
author: Stephen Sondheim
description:
Hat Box is a boxed set presenting Stephen Sondheim's complete collected lyrics, combining his two acclaimed volumes Finishing the Hat and Look, I Made a Hat. Together they cover the songs from his celebrated shows, including Sweeney Todd, Into the Woods, Company and West Side Story.

Sondheim annotates the lyrics with anecdotes, sharp observations and practical advice on the craft of songwriting, offering rare insight into how his work came together. Handsomely packaged, it is a treasured addition for musical theatre fans, aspiring lyricists and anyone who loves the art of the stage.

  • Author: Stephen Sondheim
  • Publisher: Knopf
  • Format: Hardcover box set
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780307957726

title: داليا
author: Sara Badawieh
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Dalia (داليا) is a novel in Arabic by Sara Badawieh. Its heroine, eighteen-year-old Dalia, is blamed for her mother's death after her reputation is ruined, and she flees her abusive father, who suffers from schizophrenia and wants to kill her in the name of family honour.

Growing up in a poor neighbourhood where women are expected to marry and raise children rather than study, Dalia dreams of university. Drawing strength from books and the power of words, she helps others in difficulty, works towards a doctorate and becomes an influential voice, yet she feels only one thing will make her whole: facing her father again.

  • Author: Sara Badawieh
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Farabi
  • Format: Paperback, 302 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144852323

title: Jasmine Tea
author: Sara Badawieh
description:
Jasmine Tea is a novel by Sara Badawieh about a marriage that begins under a cloud of secrets. On her first day as Ali's wife, Kenda learns that her new husband is a widower who does not love her, and that she is expected to care for a three-month-old baby who is not her own.

Ali, meanwhile, keeps silent about his father's murder and about the secrets he shared with his late wife, Niveen, before her suicide. Kenda longs to be accepted in a family after always feeling unwanted in her own, while Ali wishes she would simply disappear from his life. It is an emotional drama about grief, belonging and hidden truths.

  • Author: Sara Badawieh
  • Publisher: Independently published
  • Format: 291 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9798215927557

title: أماريتا
author: Amr Abdelhamid
description:
Amarita (أماريتا) is an Arabic fantasy novel by Amr Abdelhamid and the second book in his Land of Zicola series. It returns to Zicola, the proud land where intelligence itself is traded, as its people face their first real test and their festivities give way to fear.

Blame falls on Aseel, whose intelligence the people of Zicola once took from her entirely, as danger closes in on the city. Fast-paced and full of suspense, the novel continues the adventure begun in Land of Zicola and suits young adult and adult readers who enjoy imaginative Arabic fantasy.

  • Author: Amr Abdelhamid
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Format: Paperback, 327 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Land of Zicola, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9789776541054

title: أوبال
author: Hanan Lashin
description:
Opal (أوبال) is an Arabic fantasy novel by Hanan Lashin and the second book in her Kingdom of Eloquence series. It opens with a striking scene of horses racing in perfect rhythm through the rain to a green orchard, where the sounds that rise from them turn out to be human voices.

Continuing the adventure begun in Ikadoli, the series follows young warriors summoned to a misty kingdom to defend books, values and the purity of words. Richly descriptive and imaginative, it suits young adult readers and fans of Arabic fantasy with a literary flavour.

  • Author: Hanan Lashin
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Kingdom of Eloquence, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9789776541528

title: وادي الذئاب المنسية
author: Amr Abdelhamid
description:
The Valley of the Forgotten Wolves (وادي الذئاب المنسية) is an Arabic fantasy novel by Amr Abdelhamid, listed as the third book in his Land of Zicola series. In a land watched over by the Witness of the Sky, humans, wolves and the Maldiyun have lived in peace for thousands of years.

That peace is shaken when a fearsome wolf passes through one of six crossings and meets Musa, who is looking for any way out of his town.

  • Author: Amr Abdelhamid
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Land of Zicola, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9789779921914

title: أمواج أكما
author: Amr Abdelhamid
description:
Waves of Akma (أمواج أكما) is an Arabic fantasy novel by Amr Abdelhamid and the third book in his Rules of Jartin series. Its narrator learns that changing the rules of Jartin takes far more than strength.

The nobles of Jartin would sooner drown beneath the waves of Akma than grant others an equal right to acquire a soul. A natural next read for those following the series.

  • Author: Amr Abdelhamid
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The Rules of Jartin, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9789779920870

title: فتاة الياقة الزرقاء
author: Amr Abdelhamid
description:
The Blue Collar Girl (فتاة الياقة الزرقاء) is an Arabic novel by Amr Abdelhamid, published by Aseer Al-Kotob in 2021. Its narrator recalls the strange day her relatives crowded into the family home while her parents went to collect her newborn sister from a police station in the city.

In this world, village children are handed to their parents at the local station, but her sister Suzanne is different: she is one of the blue-collar ones, a child the family sees as arriving at exactly the right moment. Intriguing and unsettling, the novel suits readers who enjoy imaginative Arabic fiction with a mysterious premise.

  • Author: Amr Abdelhamid
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Format: 271 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789776902114

title: التأثير المركب
author: Darren Hardy
description:
The Compound Effect (التأثير المركب) is the Arabic edition of Darren Hardy's self-help book, translated by Ola Diob. Its central idea is that small, smart choices made consistently over time add up to dramatic results, in health, relationships, finances and career alike.

Hardy explains how daily habits, routines and momentum shape where we end up, and how to find the motivation to keep going, including the surprising energy that comes from having something to fight against. Practical and direct, it suits readers looking for a clear, step-by-step approach to lasting personal and professional success.

  • Author: Darren Hardy
  • Translator: Ola Diob
  • Publisher: I Carisma / Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Format: Paperback, 227 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789779922393

title: إيكادولي
author: Hanan Lashin
description:
Ikadoli (إيكادولي) is an Arabic fantasy novel by Hanan Lashin and the first book in her Kingdom of Eloquence series. It opens as its hero is seized by a giant bird and carried high above a deep valley, with an emerald river, rows of small huts and paths lined with yellow flowers far below.

A soft voice calls to him, repeating a strange word he cannot understand: Ikadoli. So begins a journey into a hidden kingdom where chosen warriors defend books, values and the beauty of language. Vividly written, it suits young adult readers and anyone who loves Arabic fantasy with a literary heart.

  • Author: Hanan Lashin
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Format: Paperback, 316 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Kingdom of Eloquence, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9789776541252

title: أمانوس
author: Hanan Lashin
description:
Amanos (أمانوس) is an Arabic fantasy novel by Hanan Lashin and the third book in her Kingdom of Eloquence series, which began with Ikadoli. The Kingdom of Eloquence is still calling on warriors to defend books, values and the purity of the written word.

As before, a chosen reader sees a mysterious symbol, watches books whirl through the air and finds their own face in a blank volume before a majestic, talking falcon carries them away to a cold, mist-wrapped kingdom. Imaginative and atmospheric, this instalment suits readers following the series and fans of Arabic fantasy.

  • Author: Hanan Lashin
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Format: Paperback, 360 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Kingdom of Eloquence, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9789776542495

title: على خطى إبراهيم
author: Kifah Abu Hnoud
description:
In the Footsteps of Abraham (على خطى إبراهيم) is a reflective Arabic book by Kifah Abu Hnoud on the life of the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham). It considers his three migrations, the many sacrifices of his life, his building of a House for God and his repeated moments of steadfast faith.

The author suggests that a life is measured by its depth rather than its length, and reflects on the honour granted to Ibrahim, including his place in the seventh heaven during the Prophet Muhammad's ascension. It is a short, contemplative read for those interested in Islamic spirituality and the stories of the prophets.

  • Author: Kifah Abu Hnoud
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Format: 103 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789776972346

title: الفيزياء بين البساطة والدهاء
author: Doha Saleh
description:
Physics Between Simplicity and Cunning (الفيزياء بين البساطة والدهاء) is an Arabic popular science book by Doha Saleh. It takes on the big questions that capture readers' imaginations, from whether we could travel through time to how black holes form and why scientists call them monsters of space.

Saleh also explores the theories behind ideas that sound like science fiction, such as other universes, being in two places at once, crossing continents in seconds or passing through a solid wall. Written in an approachable, curious style, it suits readers who want an accessible introduction to the stranger side of modern physics.

  • Author: Doha Saleh
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotob
  • Format: Paperback, 216 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789779921426

title: لماذا يسئ إبناؤنا التصرف وماذا نفعل حيال ذلك
sheet_title: لماذا يسئ إبناؤنا التصرف وماذا نفعل حيال ذلك
author: Kevin Leman
description:
This is the Arabic edition of a practical parenting guide by Dr Kevin Leman, Why Do Our Children Misbehave, and What Can We Do About It? (لماذا يسيء أبناؤنا التصرف؟ وماذا نفعل حيال ذلك؟), translated by Israa Gad. Leman argues that tantrums, answering back, slammed doors and meltdowns keep coming back because parents deal with the behaviour rather than its root causes.

He helps parents see situations through a child's eyes: why a child acts out, where that behaviour was learned and why it carries on. The book maps out the stages of misbehaviour, shows you how to tell which stage your child has reached, and offers workable strategies for turning poor conduct into good habits. A useful read for Arabic-speaking parents who want calmer days at home.

  • Author: Kevin Leman
  • Translator: Israa Gad
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotb
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789779922140

title: كويكول
author: Hanan Lashin
description:
This Arabic fantasy novel by Hanan Lashin, Kuyikul (كويكول), is the fourth book in her Kingdom of Eloquence (Mamlakat Al-Balagha) series. Its opening plunges the reader into a desperate chase: a young man races out of a forest towards a mountain ravine, hunted by the people of a cruel village, and must choose between turning to fight and leaping into the unknown.

Blending adventure, suspense and drama with a richly imagined world, the novel continues the saga for young adult and adult readers who enjoy Arabic fantasy fiction. Readers new to the series will get the most from it by starting with the earlier volumes.

  • Author: Hanan Lashin
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotb
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Kingdom of Eloquence (Mamlakat Al-Balagha), Book 4
  • ISBN: 9789779920887

title: الشيطان يحكي
author: Ahmed Khaled Mostafa

This Arabic novel by Ahmed Khaled Mostafa, The Devil Narrates (الشيطان يحكي), is a dark tale of suspense and the supernatural. It suits confident young readers as well as adults revisiting an American classic.

The War of the Worlds is H.G. Wells's pioneering tale of alien invasion, first published in 1898. When strange metal cylinders land near Woking, curious onlookers gather to stare, until Martians emerge and turn a deadly Heat-Ray on the crowd. Striding across southern England in towering fighting machines, the invaders leave ruin wherever they go.

Narrated by a man struggling to survive and find his way back to his wife, the novel captures panic, flight and the collapse of ordinary life, while raising unsettling questions about power and humanity's place in nature. It remains one of the founding works of science fiction and a gripping read for fans of classic adventure.

Heart of Darkness is Joseph Conrad's short, haunting novel of a journey into colonial Africa. Marlow, hired to captain a river steamer for an ivory-trading company, travels deep into the interior, where unsettling rumours surround Kurtz, a brilliant and mysterious agent who has slipped far beyond the company's control.

The Wizard of Oz is L. Frank Baum's classic children's fantasy, first published in 1900 as The Wonderful Wizard of Oz. When a tornado sweeps Dorothy and her little dog Toto out of Kansas, they land in the strange and magical Land of Oz and set off along the yellow brick road to ask the great Wizard to send them home.

Incredible Creatures by Margot Channing is part of the Inside Eye series, which uses detailed illustrations to show what is going on beneath the surface. She Persisted: Claudette Colvin is a chapter-book biography by Lesa Cline-Ransome, part of the She Persisted series inspired by Chelsea Clinton and Alexandra Boiger's picture book about women who stood up for what is right.
