  • Language: English
  • Series: Star Rewards - Life Skills for Kids
  • ISBN: 9781782704553

title: This Makes Me Happy: Dealing With Feelings
sheet_title: This Makes Me Happy: Dealing With Feelings
author: Courtney Carbone
description:
This Makes Me Happy by Courtney Carbone, illustrated by Hilli Kushnir, is a Step into Reading Step 2 title in the Dealing with Feelings series. A young girl's class trip to the fair is packed with excitement, from a roller coaster to a pie-eating contest and a petting zoo.

When her nut allergy stops her sharing a treat with her classmates, she learns that even a happy day can include some unhappy moments. Looking back on the trip helps her name her feelings and feel more confident. The series helps children put emotions into words as they learn to read, and stickers are included.

  • Author: Courtney Carbone
  • Illustrator: Hilli Kushnir
  • Publisher: Random House (Step into Reading)
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Step into Reading, Step 2
  • ISBN: 9780593434208

title: The Children's Book of Keeping Safe (Star Rewards)
sheet_title: THE CHILDRENS BOOK OF KEEPING SAFE (STAR REWARDS)
author: Sophie Giles
description:
The Children's Book of Keeping Safe by Sophie Giles, illustrated by Kate Davies, is part of Award Publications' Star Rewards series. It helps children learn how to play safely and stay safe, both at home and when they are out and about.

Reusable stickers add fun to every topic and encourage children to pay close attention to the pictures and think about how each lesson applies to their own lives. Gold stickers and a wipe-clean reward chart let parents praise good habits and record each success.

  • Author: Sophie Giles
  • Illustrator: Kate Davies
  • Publisher: Award Publications
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Star Rewards
  • ISBN: 9781841359090

title: Who Was Ben Franklin?
author: Dennis Brindell Fradin
description:
Who Was Ben Franklin? by Dennis Brindell Fradin, illustrated by John O'Brien, is part of the Who Was...? series of biographies for young readers. It introduces Benjamin Franklin, the scientist who flew a kite to show that lightning is electricity.

Franklin was also a printer, author, inventor and statesman who played a major part in the early history of the United States, and his talents were so varied that some people believed he had magical powers. Told honestly, with moments both sad and funny, his story is an engaging introduction to American history.

  • Author: Dennis Brindell Fradin
  • Illustrator: John O'Brien
  • Publisher: Grosset & Dunlap
  • Format: Paperback, 105 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Who Was...?
  • ISBN: 9780448424958

title: Who Was Leonardo Da Vinci?
author: Roberta Edwards
description:
Who Was Leonardo da Vinci? by Roberta Edwards, illustrated by True Kelley, is part of the Who Was...? biography series for young readers. It explores the life of a gifted painter, musician, scientist and inventor who imagined helicopters, submarines and flying machines centuries before they existed.

Readers also learn that Leonardo often struggled to finish what he started: just thirteen surviving paintings are credited to him, and his planned illustrated encyclopedia was left as thousands of loose notebook pages. Set in Renaissance Italy, it is a lively, approachable introduction to an extraordinary mind and the era he lived in.

  • Author: Roberta Edwards
  • Illustrator: True Kelley
  • Publisher: Penguin Workshop
  • Format: Paperback, 112 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Who Was...?
  • ISBN: 9780448443010

title: Maths Made Easy: Shapes & Patterns, Ages 3-5, Preschool
sheet_title: Maths Made Easy Shapes and Patterns Ages 3-5 Preschool
author: Carol Vorderman
description:
Maths Made Easy: Shapes & Patterns is a pre-school workbook for children aged 3 to 5 from Carol Vorderman's Maths Made Easy series. It invites young learners to explore shapes and patterns and to try simple measuring ideas such as tall, taller and tallest.

Each page offers short, focused practice, with parents' notes explaining what is being learned and how it links to the curriculum. A progress chart and gold stars help children see how far they have come, making early maths at home feel rewarding.

  • Author: Carol Vorderman
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Paperback, 40 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Maths Made Easy
  • ISBN: 9781409344889

title: The Halloween Tree
author: Ray Bradbury
description:
The Halloween Tree is Ray Bradbury's spooky adventure that unfolds on Halloween night. Eight costumed boys are hurrying to a haunted house outside town, where their friend Pipkin is due to join them, when they run into the tall, skeletal Mr Moundshroud, and Pipkin is snatched away by a mysterious dark presence.

To find him, Moundshroud carries the boys across centuries and continents by kite, from ancient Egypt to Mexico's Day of the Dead, as they uncover the true origins of Halloween. Rich, poetic and atmospheric, it is a perfect seasonal read for middle-grade readers and fans of classic fantasy.

  • Author: Ray Bradbury
  • Publisher: Yearling
  • Format: Paperback, 145 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780375803017

title: The Chalk Box Kid
author: Clyde Robert Bulla
vendor: Random House Books for Young Readers
description:
The Chalk Box Kid by Clyde Robert Bulla, illustrated by Thomas B. Allen, is a gentle early chapter book from Random House's Stepping Stone line. Nine-year-old Gregory has moved to a new neighbourhood and a new school, and his birthday turns out to be a lonely one.

Everything changes when he discovers a deserted old chalk factory just behind his home and makes it his secret place, where he can cover the dark brick walls with whatever he can imagine. A quietly uplifting story about creativity and resilience, it suits newly independent readers.

  • Author: Clyde Robert Bulla
  • Illustrator: Thomas B. Allen
  • Publisher: Random House Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Paperback, 64 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780394891026

title: أربطة
author: Domenico Starnone
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Domenico Starnone's novel Ties (أربطة), translated from the Italian by Amani Fawzi Habashi and published by Dar Al Karma. Like many long marriages, that of Vanda and Aldo has weathered hardship, slow wear and the weight of routine, and on the surface it seems to have survived intact.

Yet a fracture opened long ago, and over time the relationship has come to resemble a cracked vase that could shatter at the lightest touch, or may already have broken without anyone admitting it. A gripping, unsettling novel about love, family and the consequences of our choices, it was the first of Starnone's books to appear in Arabic.

  • Author: Domenico Starnone
  • Translator: Amani Fawzi Habashi
  • Publisher: Dar Al Karma
  • Format: Paperback, 202 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789776743052

title: أرى المعنى
author: Hisham Bustani
description:
I See the Meaning (أرى المعنى) is an Arabic collection by the Jordanian writer Hisham Bustani, published by Dar Al-Adab in 2012. Its subtitle describes the contents as narrative, music, or stories on the borders of poetry.

As that subtitle suggests, the pieces sit between short fiction and poetry, and the book will appeal to readers interested in experimental contemporary Arabic writing.

  • Author: Hisham Bustani
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Adab
  • Pages: 158
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953892276

title: علم اقتناء الثروة
author: Wallace D. Wattles
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Wallace D. Wattles's The Science of Getting Rich (علم اقتناء الثروة), the 1910 self-help classic, translated by Asmaa Arafa and published by Dar Dawen. Wattles argues that wealth comes from handling money and resources intelligently and from thinking in a deliberate, creative way.

The book invites readers to look at the resources around them with fresh eyes and to treat the pursuit of prosperity as a legitimate human ambition that can be approached with discipline rather than opportunism. It suits readers interested in personal finance, mindset and the roots of modern success literature.

  • Author: Wallace D. Wattles
  • Translator: Asmaa Arafa
  • Publisher: Dar Dawen
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778062656

title: ممر آمن للشيطان
author: Wesam Saeed
description:
A Safe Passage for the Devil (ممر آمن للشيطان) is an Arabic horror novel by Wesam Saeed, published by Dar Dawen. It centres on a narrow passageway said to bring a terrible curse on anyone who walks through it, testing their faith and forcing them to face their deepest fears.

Some who crossed it managed to resist the dark whispers that followed, while others gave in and let them rule their lives. When the family returns to uncover the passage's secret, the one person able to withstand its curse must confront it head on. It suits readers who enjoy psychological and supernatural horror.

  • Author: Wesam Saeed
  • Publisher: Dar Dawen
  • Format: Paperback, 159 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778061826

title: هناك حيث ينتهي النهر
author: Mariam Abdelaziz
description:
There, Where the River Ends (هناك حيث ينتهي النهر) is an Arabic novel by Mariam Abdelaziz, published by Al Kotob Khan. When Salma's father dies, men she has never met arrive claiming to be her uncles and take his body to be buried in the family's hometown of Rashid, where the Nile meets the Mediterranean.

Alone in Cairo, facing hostile neighbours and frustrated hopes in work and love, Salma travels to Rashid in search of her father's grave. Instead she uncovers a frightening world of loss, and of gangs who have turned the town into a launching point for migrant boats bound for Europe. A haunting novel of grief, family secrets and migration.

  • Author: Mariam Abdelaziz
  • Publisher: Al Kotob Khan
  • Format: Paperback, 191 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778031553

title: حياة في الإدارة
author: Ghazi A. Algosaibi
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
A Life in Administration (حياة في الإدارة) is the Arabic memoir of Ghazi A. Algosaibi, the Saudi poet, novelist, diplomat and minister, recounting his long career in public service.

Drawing on his years in university life, government ministries and diplomacy, he reflects on what leadership really requires, setting aside debates about whether management is a science or an art, or whether leaders are born or made, to focus on results. It is a valuable read for managers, students of administration and anyone interested in public leadership in the Arab world.

  • Author: Ghazi A. Algosaibi
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144860922

title: شمس اليوم الثامن
author: Ibrahim Nasrallah
description:
The Sun of the Eighth Day (شمس اليوم الثامن) is an Arabic novel by Ibrahim Nasrallah and part of his long Palestinian Comedy cycle. Set in Palestine, this short work draws richly on folk heritage, which Nasrallah treats as a source of identity and a vital part of both the people and the land that shapes them.

According to the author, the story grew from a tale about his grandfather and his camel that he heard from his mother many times as a child. Written to speak to readers of every age, it blends imagination, beauty and a search for meaning, and has a flavour quite different from his earlier novels.

  • Author: Ibrahim Nasrallah
  • Publisher: Arab Scientific Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 135 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The Palestinian Comedy, Book 13
  • ISBN: 9786140136007

title: الهجرة غرباً
author: Mohsin Hamid
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Mohsin Hamid's novel Exit West (الهجرة غرباً), translated by Nadine Nasrallah and published by Dar Al Tanweer. In an unnamed city sliding towards civil war, the independent, free-spirited Nadia meets the gentle, more reserved Saeed.

As violence engulfs their streets, they hear rumours of mysterious doors that can carry people to faraway places, at a price and at great risk. Leaving home behind, they step through one, and the novel follows them into an uncertain future as they struggle to keep their bond, and their sense of self, intact. A powerful, lyrical story of love and migration.

  • Author: Mohsin Hamid
  • Translator: Nadine Nasrallah
  • Publisher: Dar Al Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 205 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144720134

title: مفارقات السعادة
author: Luc Ferry
description:
This is the Arabic edition of French philosopher Luc Ferry's 7 façons d'être heureux, published in Arabic as The Paradoxes of Happiness (مفارقات السعادة) and translated by Ayman Abdel Hadi. Ferry observes that while the causes of unhappiness are easy to name, happiness itself is hard to define and harder still to secure.

Money, love, success and knowledge can all turn from sources of joy into sources of misery, and Ferry argues that our happiness depends far less on personal effort than on the state of the world and the fate of those we love. Rejecting ready-made recipes, he uses philosophy's honesty to clear away illusions while exploring seven ways of thinking about a happy life.

  • Author: Luc Ferry
  • Translator: Ayman Abdel Hadi
  • Publisher: Dar Al Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 207 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144720295

title: كيف تجد الحب (مدرسة الحياة)
author: The School of Life
description:
This is the Arabic edition of The School of Life's How to Find Love (كيف تجد الحب), edited by Alain de Botton and translated by Azdasheer Suleiman. It tackles a deceptively simple question: is love built on instinctive attraction, or on rational choice?

Choosing a partner is one of the hardest decisions we make, and repeated mistakes are costly. Drawing on psychology and lived experience, the book shows how our earliest experiences shape whom and how we love, and offers ideas for making wiser, braver and more effective choices in finding love and keeping it.

  • Author: The School of Life
  • Editor: Alain de Botton
  • Translator: Azdasheer Suleiman
  • Publisher: Dar Al Tanweer
  • Format: Hardcover, 109 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The School of Life
  • ISBN: 9786144722350

title: كيف تكسب الأصدقاء وتؤثر في الناس
sheet_title: كيف تكسب الأصدقاء وتؤثر في الناس
author: Dale Carnegie
description:
This is an Arabic edition of Dale Carnegie's How to Win Friends and Influence People (كيف تكسب الأصدقاء وتؤثر في الناس), published by Al-Ahliah. First published in 1936, it remains one of the best-known guides ever written on getting along with other people.

Carnegie sets out practical principles for making people like you, winning others round to your way of thinking and changing attitudes without causing resentment, illustrating each with everyday stories. His advice on listening, showing genuine interest and giving honest appreciation remains useful for professionals, students and anyone who wants to communicate more effectively.

  • Author: Dale Carnegie
  • Publisher: Al-Ahliah Publishing
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786589094319

title: كيف نتزوج (مدرسة الحياة)
author: The School of Life
description:
This is the Arabic edition of a School of Life book on weddings and marriage, How We Marry: The Wedding, Before and After (كيف نتزوج), edited by Alain de Botton and translated by Azdasheer Suleiman. It offers a bold rethink of one of humanity's most important rituals and of how we prepare for modern married life.

Many couples today feel uneasy with traditional wedding customs that no longer fit contemporary relationships. The School of Life responds by reimagining the ideal wedding day from scratch, looking at the planning beforehand, the celebration itself and the life together that follows. A thoughtful read for engaged couples and anyone interested in relationships.

  • Author: The School of Life
  • Editor: Alain de Botton
  • Translator: Azdasheer Suleiman
  • Publisher: Dar Al Tanweer
  • Format: Hardcover, 128 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The School of Life
  • ISBN: 9786144722404

title: ليلة واحدة تكفي
author: Qasem Tawfiq
description:
One Night Is Enough (ليلة واحدة تكفي) is an Arabic novel by Qasem Tawfiq, set on the night of the June 1967 defeat known as the Naksa. Its stage is an imagined café in Amman, where Wijdan, a nurse at a city hospital, takes shelter as war fills the sky with smoke.

Unable to risk the journey home, she spends the night there with Theeb, a young café worker who once left to live abroad before returning to Amman. Wijdan, from a family uprooted from Palestine in 1948, is still marked by the tragic loss of an earlier love. Over a few hours, the novel reveals both lives in depth and the feelings growing between them.

  • Author: Qasem Tawfiq
  • Publisher: Al-Aan Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 188 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789923135020

title: ميرا
author: Qasem Tawfiq
description:
Mira (ميرا) is an Arabic novel by Qasem Tawfiq, published by Al-Aan Publishers. It centres on Mira, a woman who has fallen into sin and no longer recognises the person she has become.

Written in intense, poetic prose rich with the imagery of the cross and Golgotha, the novel follows an inner cry that rises from the depths of her soul yet goes unheard by everyone around her. It suits readers of literary Arabic fiction drawn to stories of guilt, faith and inner struggle.

  • Author: Qasem Tawfiq
  • Publisher: Al-Aan Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 290 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789923130131

title: الفرار في عام ١٩٣٤
author: Su Tong
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Su Tong's novella The Escape of 1934 (الفرار في عام ١٩٣٤), translated from the Chinese by Yara Al-Masri and published by Masaa. In little more than a hundred pages, it tells a multi-generational family saga with remarkable compression.

Its narrator moves freely across time and place, recounting the lives of his ancestors as if he had witnessed them, starting even before his father was born. Su Tong himself summed it up as a tale of money and women, of birth and death. Born in Suzhou in 1963, he was hailed by critics as part of China's literary avant-garde.

  • Author: Su Tong
  • Translator: Yara Al-Masri
  • Publisher: Masaa Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 94 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9781988483313

title: الفن والخوف: ملاحظات حول مخاطر ومكافآت صنع الفن
sheet_title: الفن والخوف: ملاحظات حول مخاطر ومكافآت صنع الفن
author: David Bayles, Ted Orland
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Art & Fear: Observations on the Perils (and Rewards) of Artmaking (الفن والخوف) by David Bayles and Ted Orland, translated by Khaled Farouk and published by Dar Al Karma. It examines how art actually gets made, why it so often does not, and why so many artists give up along the way.

Both authors are working artists, and their observations come from daily experience of the practical problems of making art in the real world. Rather than a typical self-help title, it is a book by artists for artists, about what it feels like to sit at the easel or keyboard and try to do the work. It has become a classic among students and creators.

  • Author: David Bayles and Ted Orland
  • Translator: Khaled Farouk
  • Publisher: Dar Al Karma
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778638097

title: جسر بضفة وحيدة
attention: No photo found — photograph in store; Book not identified — description written from the title only
description:
A Bridge with a Single Bank (جسر بضفة وحيدة) is a book written in Arabic, with an evocative title.

  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789923133576

title: سولاريس
author: Stanisław Lem
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Stanisław Lem's Solaris (سولاريس), translated by Hatif Al-Janabi and published by Dar Al Karma. A philosophical classic of science fiction, it follows the scientist Kris Kelvin, who arrives at a research station near the planet Solaris to study the vast ocean covering its surface.

There he is confronted by a painful memory made flesh: a double of the woman he loved, who died long ago. The other scientists aboard suffer similar visitations, and suspicion grows that the ocean is a giant mind that brings memories to life, though its purpose stays a mystery. Translated into more than forty languages, it asks whether we can understand the universe without first understanding ourselves.

  • Author: Stanisław Lem
  • Translator: Hatif Al-Janabi
  • Publisher: Dar Al Karma
  • Format: Paperback, 267 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789776743540

title: الإلياذة
author: Homer
description:
This is an Arabic edition of Homer's The Iliad (الإلياذة), the most famous epic of the ancient world, in the Arabic rendering by Durayni Khashaba, published by Dar Al Tanweer. It tells of the Trojan War and the wrath of Achilles, from his bitter quarrel with Agamemnon to the death of Hector.

Khashaba's version made the Greek epic part of modern Arabic literary heritage, drawing on the eloquence of classical Arabic, the Arab tradition of poems of war, love and pride, and the popular folk epics. The result is a vivid, stately retelling for readers who love mythology, the classics and fine Arabic prose.

  • Author: Homer
  • Translator: Durayni Khashaba
  • Publisher: Dar Al Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 248 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778511543

title: الفوضى الرتيبة للوجود
author: Hisham Bustani
description:
The Monotonous Chaos of Existence (الفوضى الرتيبة للوجود) is an Arabic short story collection by the Jordanian writer Hisham Bustani, published by Dar Al-Farabi in 2010.

It is a collection of short fiction for readers exploring contemporary Arabic literature and new directions in the Arabic short story.

  • Author: Hisham Bustani
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Farabi
  • Pages: 190
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953715278

title: النمر الذي يدعي أنه بورخيس
author: Diaa Jubaili
description:
The Tiger Who Claims to Be Borges (النمر الذي يدعي أنه بورخس) is an Arabic short story collection by the Iraqi writer Diaa Jubaili, published by Dar Nabu.

Once again Jubaili refuses the ordinary, skilfully blending a realistic view of events with expansive fantasy. Each story suggests there is far more to life than what we see and grow used to, as lived experience and dreams merge, in the spirit of Borges's idea of writing as a guided dream. A surprising and absorbing read.

  • Author: Diaa Jubaili
  • Publisher: Dar Nabu
  • Format: Paperback, 206 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144721414

title: Horse and Pony Colouring Book
author: Jennifer Bell
description:
Horse and Pony Colouring Book features detailed line drawings by equestrian artist Jennifer Bell, showing a wide range of well-loved horse and pony breeds from around the world, all ready to be brought to life with colour.

Thirty full-colour stickers are included too, making it a lovely gift for young riders and pony fans aged 6 and up. It is published by Picthall & Gunzi, an imprint of Award Publications.

  • Author: Jennifer Bell
  • Publisher: Picthall & Gunzi (Award Publications)
  • Format: Paperback, 64 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781909763227

title: How to Change Your Parents into Superstars
sheet_title: How to Change Your Parents into Superstars
author: Pete Johnson
description:
How to Change Your Parents into Superstars is a comic story by Pete Johnson in the Louis the Laugh series, starring Louis, a schoolboy who dreams of becoming a stand-up comedian. Just when he needs them on his side, his parents seem more embarrassing than ever.

Will they ever back his hopes of becoming a star, why is everyone suddenly wearing glittery, ill-fitting outfits, and what is all that chanting about? Packed with misadventures and laugh-out-loud moments, it is also a gentle story about having the confidence to be yourself, ideal for young readers who love funny books.

  • Author: Pete Johnson
  • Illustrator: James Cottell
  • Publisher: Award Publications
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • Series: Louis the Laugh, Book 6
  • ISBN: 9781782703969

title: Loveless Love
author: Luigi Pirandello
description:
Loveless Love is a slim collection of short stories by Luigi Pirandello, the Italian modernist best known for Six Characters in Search of an Author. These tales were his very first published fiction, and each one turns on a romance that is unreturned, half-recognised or quietly mistaken.

A young man is drawn to a woman downstairs who is already promised to someone else; a lively girl is torn between her own wishes and her parents' plans for a sensible marriage; a celebrated beauty leaves a former admirer with lasting regret. Sharp and psychologically subtle, the stories anticipate the themes of his later work and suit readers who enjoy compact European classics.

  • Author: Luigi Pirandello
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 128 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Alma Classics 101 Pages
  • ISBN: 9781847498113

title: Mega Books: Minibeasts
author: Anna Award
description:
Mega Minibeasts is a large-format children's information book from Award Publications' Mega Books series, introducing young readers to some of the most remarkable insects and other small creatures.

Short, easy-to-read text sits alongside striking photographs, helping hesitant readers build confidence while they discover facts on their own. The publisher recommends it for ages 3 and up.

  • Author: Anna Award
  • Publisher: Award Publications
  • Format: Paperback, 34 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Mega Books
  • ISBN: 9781909763562

title: Mega Tractors Amazing Tractors and Other Tough Farm Machines
sheet_title: Mega Tractors Amazing Tractors and Other Tough Farm Machines
author: Louise Pritchard
description:
Mega Tractors is an oversized picture-information book by Louise Pritchard that takes young readers onto the farm to meet giant tractors, combine harvesters, balers, foragers and other heavy-duty machines, all shown in big, bold photographs.

Simple text is paired with questions to answer and things to spot on each page, keeping curious children involved, and a sheet of 30 colourful stickers adds extra fun. Developed with input from education specialists, it aims to build early reading, talking and comprehension skills. Suggested for ages 3 and up.

  • Author: Louise Pritchard
  • Editor: Paul Calver
  • Publisher: Parkwest Publications
  • Format: Paperback, 34 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Mega Books
  • ISBN: 9781909763210

title: Middle School: Hollywood 101
author: James Patterson
description:
Middle School: Hollywood 101 is a funny illustrated novel by James Patterson in the Middle School series starring Rafe Katchadorian, who tells the story in his own words. School has hit rock bottom for Rafe until an intriguing new girl turns up and, to his amazement, wants to be his friend.

Then a film production rolls into his hometown of Hills Village, things get strange in a hurry, and before he knows it Rafe has a foot in the movie business. Short chapters, lively drawings and plenty of comic chaos make it an easy pick for middle-grade readers, especially those who already know Rafe from earlier books.

  • Author: James Patterson
  • Publisher: Young Arrow
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Middle School
  • ISBN: 9781784756819

title: My Parents are Driving Me Crazy
sheet_title: My Parents are Driving Me Crazy
author: Pete Johnson
description:
My Parents Are Driving Me Crazy is a humorous children's novel by Pete Johnson about a young hero whose mum and dad are, just as the title says, driving him round the bend.

It belongs to Johnson's Louis the Laugh books and is followed by further comic family adventures, including How to Have Totally Awesome Parents. This edition is a paperback from Award Publications.

  • Author: Pete Johnson
  • Publisher: Award Publications
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Louis the Laugh, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781782701606

title: Mystery Ranch
author: Gertrude Chandler Warner
description:
Mystery Ranch is the fourth book in Gertrude Chandler Warner's classic Boxcar Children series, following Henry, Jessie, Violet and Benny Alden on another summer adventure. This time the four siblings go to stay on the ranch that belongs to their Aunt Jane, a beautiful place that has nevertheless caused a rift between her and their grandfather.

As the children explore the land, they stumble on a surprising find that might just help bring the family back together. Gentle suspense, close sibling bonds and a satisfying puzzle make it a good early chapter book for independent readers and for reading aloud.

  • Author: Gertrude Chandler Warner
  • Publisher: Albert Whitman & Company
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Boxcar Children, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9780807553916

title: Old Yeller
author: Fred Gipson
description:
Old Yeller is Fred Gipson's much-loved American classic about a frontier boy and the scruffy stray who turns into his fiercest protector. In the Texas Hill Country of the 1860s, Travis Coates, just fourteen, must look after the family farm while his father drives cattle north to Kansas.

No Country for Old Men is Cormac McCarthy's taut crime novel set along the Texas border in 1980. Out hunting, Llewelyn Moss stumbles on the bloody aftermath of a drug deal and a case holding more than two million dollars, and decides to keep it.

title: The Curse of the Mummy's Tomb
sheet_title: The Curse of the Mummy's Tomb
author: R.L. Stine
description:
The Curse of the Mummy's Tomb is an early Goosebumps adventure from R.L. Stine. On a trip to Egypt, young Gabe joins his archaeologist uncle Ben and his cousin Sari at the Great Pyramid, where a wrong turn leaves him lost deep inside the ancient tomb.

Strange noises, dark tunnels and the threat of a centuries-old curse turn the visit into a nightmare. Short chapters and plenty of shivers make it ideal for young readers who enjoy spooky, page-turning fun.

  • Author: R.L. Stine
  • Publisher: Scholastic Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Goosebumps, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9781407157498

title: الغباء البشري
author: Carlo M. Cipolla
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Human Stupidity (الغباء البشري) is the Arabic translation, by Imad Shiha, of the Italian economic historian Carlo M. Cipolla's famous essay on the basic laws of human stupidity. In a brief, witty argument, Cipolla sets out his laws and examines stupidity as one of the darkest forces holding back human welfare and happiness.

Both amusing and unsettling, the book suggests that foolish people may have far more influence on the world than we would like to think. It is a quick, thought-provoking read for anyone who has ever despaired at how widespread stupidity seems to be, and who would rather laugh at it than lose hope.

  • Author: Carlo M. Cipolla
  • Translator: Imad Shiha
  • Publisher: Dar Al Saqi
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786140322202

title: النباتية
author: Han Kang
description:
The Vegetarian (النباتية) is the Arabic edition of Han Kang's haunting novel, translated by Mahmoud Abdel Ghaffar. After a series of violent dreams, Yeong-hye, an outwardly ordinary woman in Seoul, abruptly refuses to eat meat, a quiet act of defiance that shocks her husband and family.

Told in three parts, through the eyes of her husband, her brother-in-law and her sister, the story follows the escalating consequences of her choice as she withdraws further from the world around her. Strange, sensual and disturbing, it is a powerful novel about control, desire, mental illness and the limits of the body.

  • Author: Han Kang
  • Translator: Mahmoud Abdel Ghaffar
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789938941104

title: رؤى
author: Nabil Farouk
description:
Visions (رؤى) is a science-fiction thriller in Arabic by the Egyptian author Nabil Farouk. Engineer Medhat is sent to fix a power cut at the Media Production City, but while he is working on the tower he is struck by lightning and falls into a coma that lasts nine years.

When he finally wakes, he is a different man, with seemingly limitless mental powers and disturbing visions. Soon he is drawn into fierce confrontations with mysterious forces that stretch back through the ages, building towards a decisive final battle. Fast-moving and hard to predict, it is a good choice for fans of Arabic adventure and speculative fiction.

  • Author: Nabil Farouk
  • Publisher: Dar Dawen
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778061345

title: سبيل الغارق: الطريق والبحر
author: Reem Bassiouney
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
The Path of the Drowning: The Road and the Sea (سبيل الغارق: الطريق والبحر) is a historical novel in Arabic by the Egyptian writer Reem Bassiouney. It follows Hassan, a man whose memory has been wiped away, as he is drawn into a story that reaches back through centuries of Egyptian history.

Moving through Alexandria, the novel touches on the British bombardment of the citadel built by the Mamluk sultan Qaitbay and on the long struggle over trade routes between East and West, from the Portuguese voyages around Africa to a Frenchman's dream of a shorter passage. Blending history, romance and a touch of the mystical, it suits readers of rich, sweeping historical fiction.

  • Author: Reem Bassiouney
  • Publisher: Nahdet Misr
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789771461630

title: شارون وحماتي
author: Suad Amiry
description:
Sharon and My Mother-in-Law: Ramallah Diaries (شارون وحماتي) is the Arabic edition of Palestinian architect and writer Suad Amiry's memoir, translated by Omar Saeed Al-Ayoubi. It records daily life in Ramallah during the Israeli incursion of 2002, when her ninety-two-year-old mother-in-law came to live with her.

Between curfews, checkpoints and permits, Amiry captures the gossip of neighbours, the impossibility of ordinary plans and the clash of personalities at home, finding dark humour in an absurd and exhausting situation. Warm, sharp and deeply human, it offers a vivid personal view of life under occupation.

  • Author: Suad Amiry
  • Translator: Omar Saeed Al-Ayoubi
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Adab
  • Format: Paperback, 280 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953892436

title: علاقات حرجة
author: Jamal Khashoggi
description:
Critical Relations: Saudi Arabia After 11 September (علاقات حرجة) is a book in Arabic by the Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi, published in 2002 by Riad El-Rayyes Books. It examines how the attacks of 11 September 2001 affected Saudi Arabia and its place in the world.

Drawing on the political debates of the time, Khashoggi looks at Saudi-American relations, the war on terrorism and Afghanistan, and the wider Arab-Israeli conflict, as well as the kingdom's internal politics. It is a useful read for anyone interested in Gulf politics and the Middle East in the early 2000s.

  • Author: Jamal Khashoggi
  • Publisher: Riad El-Rayyes Books
  • Format: Paperback, 334 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953211015

title: فستق عبيد
author: Samiha Khrais

description:
Slaves' Pistachios (فستق عبيد) is a novel in Arabic by the Jordanian writer Samiha Khrais. Following her earlier novel Babanoos, she returns to Sudan for another imaginative dig into history, this time ranging from Sudan to Algeria and, above all, Spain.

Spanning the late nineteenth century to the end of the Second World War, the book confronts slavery and the experience of Black Africans, and is built as a chorus of voices, with each character telling their own story in the first person. It suits readers of ambitious, many-voiced Arabic historical fiction.

  • Author: Samiha Khrais
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789923135822

title: لماذا يريد الرجل وترفض المرأة
author: Sherif Arafa
description:
Why Does the Man Want and the Woman Refuse? (لماذا يريد الرجل وترفض المرأة) is a book in Arabic by the Egyptian author Sherif Arafa, presented as a science-based guide to a healthy intimate life. Rather than preaching, it approaches marital intimacy through modern scientific research, with the aim of improving quality of life and happiness between spouses.

Arafa covers topics such as the differences in desire between men and women, overcoming a loss of interest within marriage, communication between partners and practical exercises for a more fulfilling relationship. Written for both men and women, it is aimed at adults who are married or preparing for marriage.

  • Author: Sherif Arafa
  • Publisher: Al-Dar Al-Masriah Al-Lubnaniah
  • Format: Paperback, 383 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789777952866

title: نظرية كل شيء : أصل ومصير الكون
sheet_title: نظرية كل شيء : أصل ومصير الكون
author: Stephen W. Hawking
description:
The Theory of Everything: The Origin and Fate of the Universe (نظرية كل شيء: أصل ومصير الكون) is the Arabic edition of Stephen Hawking's series of lectures on the history of the cosmos. Hawking moves from Aristotle's reasons for believing the Earth is round to Hubble's discovery that the universe is expanding, then tells the story of the Big Bang.

He goes on to his favourite subject, black holes, and closes with the search for a final theory that would unite physics. The translator has added explanatory notes to every chapter, including remarks on how physics has moved on since the lectures were given in the 1990s, making this an accessible introduction to cosmology.

  • Author: Stephen W. Hawking
  • Publisher: Natural Sciences Center
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789921001303

title: وتحكي الكيمياء
author: Munjed Saqr
description:
And Chemistry Speaks (وتحكي الكيمياء) is a book in Arabic by Munjed Saqr, published by Dar Al-Farabi. It is a creative work built around the science of chemistry, in which the author brings together an artistic sensibility and a scientific outlook.

The result is an unusual blend of art and science, aimed at readers who enjoy seeing scientific ideas explored with imagination.

  • Author: Munjed Saqr
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Farabi
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144325742

title: Jude The Obscure
author: Thomas Hardy
description:
Jude the Obscure is Thomas Hardy's final novel and one of his most powerful tragedies. Jude Fawley, a bright and sensitive young man from Wessex, dreams of studying at Christminster, Hardy's version of Oxford, and spends years teaching himself in the hope of winning a place there.

His ambitions are knocked off course by a hasty marriage to Arabella Donn, and later by his love for his free-thinking cousin Sue, with whom he lives unmarried as poverty and public disapproval close in. Passionate and searching, the novel takes aim at Victorian attitudes to marriage, class, education and religion. This annotated Alma Classics Evergreens edition suits students and lovers of the classics.

  • Author: Thomas Hardy
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 448 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Alma Classics Evergreens
  • ISBN: 9781847498076

title: Little Sticker Dolly Dressing Puppies
author: Fiona Watt
description:
Little Sticker Dolly Dressing: Puppies is an Usborne sticker activity book by Fiona Watt, illustrated by Lizzie Mackay, made for children who love dogs.

Children choose outfits for the dolls, then place their puppies and accessories into a series of scenes, including a woodland walk, a day at the beach, a trip to the vet and a training class, then decorate the pages with extra stickers. A fun, creative choice for quiet time and travel.

  • Author: Fiona Watt
  • Illustrator: Lizzie Mackay
  • Publisher: Usborne Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 24 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Little Sticker Dolly Dressing
  • ISBN: 9781474959995

title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and Other Stories
sheet_title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and Other Stories
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description:
Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and Other Stories brings together Robert Louis Stevenson's most famous novella with a selection of his shorter fiction. Set amid the fog and grime of Victorian London, the title story explores the unsettling link between the respected Dr Jekyll and the brutal Mr Hyde.

First published in 1886, this tale of murder, a divided self and dangerous science has been chilling readers ever since, and its final revelation remains one of the great twists in literature. This annotated Alma Classics edition includes illustrations and extra notes on the author's life, making it ideal for students and fans of Gothic fiction.

  • Author: Robert Louis Stevenson
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 250 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Alma Classics Evergreens
  • ISBN: 9781847493781

title: رسائل ستيفن زفايج
author: Stefan Zweig
description:
The Letters of Stefan Zweig and His Wife Lotte (رسائل ستيفن زفايج وزوجته لوت) is an Arabic translation by Maysara Salah El-Din of the correspondence the Austrian writer and his wife sent during their exile in Brazil, presented in Arabic for the first time.

Most of the letters were addressed to Lotte's family, especially her brother Manfred and his wife Hanna. They reveal the couple's frustration at wartime news and at censored, delayed post, the pain of losing a homeland, Lotte's struggle with asthma and Stefan's growing despair, offering an intimate portrait of their final years.

  • Author: Stefan Zweig
  • Translator: Maysara Salah El-Din
  • Publisher: Bayt Al-Yasmin
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778172140

author: Ahmed Mourad
description:
1919 (١٩١٩) is a historical novel in Arabic by the Egyptian author Ahmed Mourad, set in Cairo during the turbulent days of the 1919 revolution against British rule.

Against the backdrop of Saad Zaghloul's struggle with the British and the rise of the Wafd, the story moves through the city's cafes, including a secret group operating beneath the famous Cafe Riche, and into its hidden underworld. Rich in carefully researched historical detail and vivid dialogue, with characters readers will love and loathe, it is a gripping read for fans of historical fiction.

  • Author: Ahmed Mourad
  • Publisher: Dar El Shorouk
  • Format: Paperback, 534 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789770934265

title: الدحيحة: الأميرة ديانا
author: Taher El Moataz Bellah
description:
Al-Dahiha: Princess Diana (الدحيحة: الأميرة ديانا) is a popular biography in Arabic by Taher El Moataz Bellah, part of Kayan Publishing's Al-Dahiha series. It tells the life story of Diana, Princess of Wales, a woman who missed out on love in her own life yet gave it generously to those around her.

The book looks at how she lived and loved, her victories and defeats, the men drawn into her orbit and the questions that still surround her death, and explores how she became one of the most popular figures in the world, a fascination that has lasted decades beyond her death.

  • Author: Taher El Moataz Bellah
  • Publisher: Kayan Publishing
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Al-Dahiha, Season 3, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9789778201543

title: عمل تحبه
author: The School of Life
description:
A Job to Love (عمل تحبه) is the Arabic edition of The School of Life's practical guide to finding fulfilling work, edited by Alain de Botton and translated by Al-Harith Al-Nabhan.

Starting from the idea that, alongside a good relationship, meaningful work is central to a satisfying life, it helps readers understand themselves well enough to know where their energies truly belong. With warmth and practical insight, it guides readers to identify their real talents, make sense of mixed-up ambitions and find a career that suits them while there is still time.

  • Author: The School of Life
  • Editor: Alain de Botton
  • Translator: Al-Harith Al-Nabhan
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 207 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144722282

description:
Why Noble Character? (لماذا مكارم الأخلاق) is a book in Arabic whose title asks why good character and noble morals matter.

As the title suggests, it deals with ethics, values and virtuous conduct, making it a natural choice for readers interested in character, personal conduct and the place of good manners in everyday life.

  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789776578517

title: نساء روحي
author: Isabel Allende
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
The Soul of a Woman (نساء روحي) is the Arabic edition of Isabel Allende's memoir Mujeres del alma mía, translated by Mark Gamal. In it the Chilean novelist speaks candidly about her life, inviting readers along on an intimate journey that begins in childhood.

Allende reflects on love, ageing, her time in Lebanon and her travels, her path as a novelist and a feminist, and what it means to be a woman in a world run by men. She writes about her mother, her daughter Paula, who died young, and the women friends and pioneers who shaped her. Warm, frank and often funny, it suits fans of her novels and readers interested in women's lives.

  • Author: Isabel Allende
  • Translator: Mark Gamal
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953897455

title: How Flowers Grow
author: Emma Helbrough
description:
How Flowers Grow by Emma Helbrough is part of the Usborne Beginners series, colourful non-fiction books for children who are starting to read by themselves.

It explores the life of flowers, answering intriguing questions such as how plants survive in dry deserts, how animals help carry seeds to new places and which flower gives off a smell like rotting meat. Clear text and bright pictures make it ideal for young nature lovers at home or at school.

  • Author: Emma Helbrough
  • Publisher: Usborne Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Usborne Beginners
  • ISBN: 9780746074503

title: The Railway Children (Young Reading)
author: E. Nesbit (adapted by Mary Sebag-Montefiore)
description:
The Railway Children is an Usborne Young Reading Series Two retelling of E. Nesbit's classic novel, adapted by Mary Sebag-Montefiore and illustrated by Alan Marks.

When their father vanishes without explanation, Bobbie, Peter and Phyllis must leave their comfortable London home for a cottage in the countryside beside a railway line. Each day the children stand by the line and wave as the London train goes by, hoping their love will reach Father and that he will one day come home. This 64-page version is ideal for newly independent readers.

  • Author: E. Nesbit
  • Adapted by: Mary Sebag-Montefiore
  • Illustrator: Alan Marks
  • Publisher: Usborne Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 64 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Usborne Young Reading, Series 2
  • ISBN: 9780746079034

title: الجاسوس الانجليزي
author: Magdy El Shafee
description:
The English Spy (الجاسوس الإنجليزي) is a graphic novel in Arabic by the Egyptian artist Magdy El Shafee, founder of the Cairo Comix festival. The fruit of long research into Egypt at the end of the nineteenth century, it weaves archival documents into its artwork to tell stories of many traitors and a few brave souls.

The book revisits a murky chapter of Egyptian history, including the Urabi revolt and Khedive Tawfiq's betrayal of it, as well as the background to Khedive Ismail's decision to outlaw the slave trade in Egypt. It is a striking choice for readers of historical comics and anyone curious about Egypt's modern history.

  • Author: Magdy El Shafee
  • Publisher: Al-Mahrousa
  • Format: Paperback, 148 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The English Spy, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9789773139315

title: خزامى
author: Sinan Antoon
description:
Lavender (خزامى) is a novel in Arabic by the Iraqi writer and poet Sinan Antoon, published by Al-Kamel Verlag (Manshurat Al-Jamal).

The passage chosen to introduce the book is a bitter reflection on homeland and belonging, and on a state that treats its citizens' bodies as its own property, sending them to lost wars, starving them and punishing any dissent. It suits readers of contemporary Iraqi and Arabic literature.

  • Author: Sinan Antoon
  • Publisher: Al-Kamel Verlag (Manshurat Al-Jamal)
  • Format: Paperback, 251 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789922220710

title: عزاءات الفلسفة: كيف تساعدنا الفلسفة في الحياة
sheet_title: عزاءات الفلسفة: كيف تساعدنا الفلسفة في الحياة
author: Alain de Botton
description:
The Consolations of Philosophy: How Philosophy Helps Us in Life (عزاءات الفلسفة) is the Arabic edition of Alain de Botton's book, translated by Yazan Al-Hajj, which presents philosophy as a source of practical comfort.

De Botton turns to six great thinkers, Socrates, Epicurus, Seneca, Montaigne, Schopenhauer and Nietzsche, for help with everyday troubles such as unpopularity, lack of money, frustration, feelings of inadequacy, heartbreak and hardship. Witty, warm and clearly written, it treats philosophy as a practical aid to living, and suits anyone curious about big ideas.

  • Author: Alain de Botton
  • Translator: Yazan Al-Hajj
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 316 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789776483545

title: و يأتي الغد
author: Nabil Farouk
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
