description:
And Tomorrow Comes (ويأتي الغد) is a non-fiction book in Arabic by the Egyptian author Nabil Farouk. It gathers a wide range of scientific studies and recent research and uses them to sketch what the near future may look like.

Written in Farouk's lively, accessible style, it packs in a generous amount of information, making it a good choice for curious readers who enjoy popular science and speculation about tomorrow's world.

  • Author: Nabil Farouk
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778062328

title: The Son Of Neptune Heroes Of Olympus Book 2
sheet_title: The Son Of Neptune Heroes Of Olympus Book 2
author: Rick Riordan
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
The Son of Neptune is the second book in Rick Riordan's Heroes of Olympus series, the follow-up to the Percy Jackson adventures. Percy wakes with almost no memory of who he is and, after training with the wolf goddess Lupa, makes his way to Camp Jupiter, a camp for Roman demigods where nothing feels familiar.

There he teams up with Hazel, a girl who should be dead, and Frank, who is unsure of his own powers, on a perilous quest to Alaska to free Thanatos, the god of death. Fast, funny and full of Roman and Greek mythology, it is a great choice for middle-grade and teen readers who loved the original Percy Jackson books.

  • Author: Rick Riordan
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Heroes of Olympus, Book 2

title: Tuck Everlasting
author: Natalie Babbitt
description:
Tuck Everlasting is Natalie Babbitt's classic novel about the gift, and the burden, of living forever. After drinking from a hidden spring, the Tuck family stopped ageing, and they now move quietly through the world trying not to draw attention to themselves.

When young Winnie Foster, aged ten, discovers the truth, the Tucks carry her off to their home and try to help her understand why never growing older is not as wonderful as it sounds. Meanwhile, a mysterious stranger is on their trail, hoping to profit from the spring. Lyrical and thought-provoking, it is a timeless read for middle-grade readers and families.

  • Author: Natalie Babbitt
  • Publisher: Square Fish (Macmillan)
  • Format: Paperback, 148 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780312369811

title: مختارات الصدفة
author: Wael Ashry
description:
Chance Selections (مختارات الصدفة) is a collection of short prose pieces in Arabic by Wael Ashry. The texts turn their attention to chance meetings and passing everyday conversations, finding something strange and rich in the small details that people usually overlook.

Written in a light, conversational register, some passages even look at familiar human habits, such as taking photographs to hold on to a moment, from an outsider's puzzled point of view. At just over ninety pages it is a compact read for anyone who enjoys contemporary Arabic short fiction.

  • Author: Wael Ashry
  • Publisher: Waziz
  • Format: Paperback, 91 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789779445946

title: This Day Is Dark
author: R.H. Sin
description:
This Day Is Dark brings together poetry and prose by R.H. Sin. Drawing on the bleakest stretches of an eighteen-year period, it looks at what happens when warning signs in a relationship are taken for passion and love ends up with the wrong person.

Written in the direct, confessional voice his readers know well, the book traces how a love that was once celebrated can become unrecognisable, and how a promised forever can turn out to be temporary. It suits readers drawn to modern poetry about heartbreak and difficult relationships.

  • Author: R.H. Sin
  • Publisher: Andrews McMeel Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781524882211

title: أفاعي النار: حكاية العاشق علي بن محمود القصاد
sheet_title: افاعي النارحكاية العاشق علي بن محمود القصاد
author: Jalal Barjas
vendor: Arab Institute for Research and Publishing
description:
Fire Snakes: The Tale of the Lover Ali bin Mahmoud Al-Qassad (أفاعي النار: حكاية العاشق علي بن محمود القصاد) is a novel in Arabic by the Jordanian writer Jalal Barjas. It is built on a series of opposites, setting knowledge against ignorance, moderation against extremism, and reason and enlightenment against darkness of mind.

The story moves between dream and reality, and takes on the suppression of free thinking and the readiness of many to accept simplistic explanations of events, questions that remain pressing in the Arab world today. It is a strong choice for readers of serious contemporary Arabic fiction.

  • Author: Jalal Barjas
  • Publisher: Arab Institute for Research and Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 222 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144862490

title: القلب خلف الضلع تمامًا The Heart Behind The Rib
sheet_title: القلب خلف الضلع تمامًا The Heart Behind The Rib
author: Maria Dadouch
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
The Heart Behind the Rib (القلب خلف الضلع تمامًا) is a novel in Arabic for young adults by Maria Dadouch, which won the Khalifa Award for Education in 2020. When raiders overrun the city where Mustafa lives, he and his sister are seized and made slaves.

Mustafa manages to escape to Sfax, but his sister is left behind. Years later the raiders reach Sfax as well, and he must find a way to win back his sister and get free of them for good. It is a story of separation and courage for teenage readers in Arabic.

  • Author: Maria Dadouch
  • Publisher: Dar Al Yasmin
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789957682255

title: Hats Are Not For Cats
author: Jacqueline K. Rayner
description:
Hats Are Not for Cats! is a funny rhyming picture book by Jacqueline K. Rayner, presented here as a sturdy board book. A large, bossy dog in a plaid hat insists that hats belong to dogs alone, and that a little black cat wearing a red fez has no business putting one on.

The cat is not persuaded. She tries on one hat after another and calls in plenty of feline friends to join her, until everyone reaches a happy solution. With bouncy rhymes and lively pictures, it is a light-hearted way to talk with little ones about bossiness, standing your ground and sorting out disagreements.

  • Author: Jacqueline K. Rayner
  • Publisher: Clarion Books
  • Format: Board book, 30 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780358731085

title: Holes
author: Louis Sachar
description:
Holes is Louis Sachar's much-loved novel about Stanley Yelnats, a boy whose family has been dogged by bad luck for generations, all thanks to a curse traced back to his great-great-grandfather. Wrongly sent to Camp Green Lake, a detention centre for boys, Stanley spends every day digging holes in the baked earth of a lake that dried up long ago.

It soon becomes clear that the warden is searching for something buried there. Weaving past and present together with dark humour, the story is about friendship, justice and fate, and it rewards readers of all ages who like a clever puzzle. This is the first book in the Holes series.

  • Author: Louis Sachar
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Holes, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781408865231

title: How to Be a Hero
author: Cat Weldon
description:
How to Be a Hero, by Cat Weldon, is a funny fantasy adventure set among the gods and legends of Norse mythology, illustrated throughout by Katie Kear. Lotta is a hopeless trainee Valkyrie who mistakes Whetstone, a knocked-out Viking thief, for a fallen hero and proudly carries him off to Valhalla.

When a precious talking cup goes missing, the bickering pair set out to recover it and save their reputations, while the trickster god Loki schemes to use it to throw all nine worlds into chaos. Full of friendship, bravery and mischief, it suits middle-grade readers who enjoy humorous myth-based adventures.

  • Author: Cat Weldon
  • Illustrator: Katie Kear
  • Publisher: Macmillan Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: How to Be a Hero
  • ISBN: 9781529045031

title: Jacob's Room
author: Virginia Woolf
description:
Jacob's Room was the first novel Virginia Woolf wrote in her distinctive experimental style, and it stands as an important early work of modernism. It follows the life of Jacob Flanders, who is never shown directly but is pieced together from the impressions and memories of the people around him.

Elegiac in mood, the novel quietly mourns a generation of young men lost to the First World War, and Jacob remains a kind of absence at its heart. It is an essential read for anyone exploring Woolf's work or the beginnings of modernist fiction.

  • Author: Virginia Woolf
  • Publisher: Alma Books
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847498366

title: Paradise
author: Dante Alighieri
description:
Paradise is the last of the three parts of Dante Alighieri's The Divine Comedy, presented here in a dual-language edition with a verse translation by J.G. Nichols. Having passed through Hell and climbed Mount Purgatory, Dante now rises through the heavens, guided by his beloved Beatrice.

His vision of the cosmos is built from spheres that circle the Earth, from the Moon outwards to the Empyrean, and the journey becomes a search for wisdom, revelation and grace. With the Italian text alongside the English, this edition completes Nichols's translation of the whole poem and suits both students and lovers of classic poetry.

  • Author: Dante Alighieri
  • Translator: J.G. Nichols
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Divine Comedy, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781847496478

title: Pygmalion
author: George Bernard Shaw
description:
Pygmalion is George Bernard Shaw's celebrated comedy about language and class. The phonetics professor Henry Higgins bets Colonel Pickering that he can teach Eliza Doolittle, a Cockney flower seller, to speak like a duchess, only to find that she has a mind and ambitions entirely her own.

As the experiment goes on, the play takes sharp aim at social appearances, the class system and the place of women in society. This edition gives the definitive 1941 text, with footnotes marking where it differs from the 1916 edition. The play later inspired the musical My Fair Lady.

  • Author: George Bernard Shaw
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847498595

title: Talking To Strangers
author: Malcolm Gladwell
description:
Talking to Strangers is Malcolm Gladwell's investigation into why we so often misjudge people we do not know. Starting from cases such as a routine traffic stop that ended in tragedy, a spy who went undetected for years at the top of the Pentagon, and the wrongful conviction of Amanda Knox, he asks why lies are so hard to spot and faces so easy to misread.

Drawing on history, psychology and well-known legal cases, Gladwell builds a thought-provoking argument about the assumptions we bring to every encounter. Written in his trademark storytelling style, it suits readers of popular psychology and anyone curious about trust, deception and communication.

  • Author: Malcolm Gladwell
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141988504

title: The Adventures Of Tom Sawyer And Tom Sawyer Detective
sheet_title: The Adventures Of Tom Sawyer And Tom Sawyer Detective
author: Mark Twain
description:
This volume brings together The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, Mark Twain's classic story of a boy coming of age beside the Mississippi River, and its sequel Tom Sawyer, Detective. Bold, quick-witted Tom tries his Aunt Polly's patience, skips school whenever he can and, with his friend Huckleberry Finn, lands in all kinds of scrapes, including witnessing a murder.

Lively and funny, the novel celebrates youth and freedom while also looking at serious themes of its time, among them race, revenge and slavery. The companion story, first published in 1896, has fun with the conventions of detective fiction.

  • Author: Mark Twain
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 348 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847494900

title: The Last Battle
author: C.S. Lewis
description:
The Last Battle brings C.S. Lewis's beloved Chronicles of Narnia to an end as the seventh and concluding book. In Narnia's last days the land faces its greatest threat, which comes not from an invading army but from deceit and betrayal inside its own borders.

As lies take hold, the last king and a handful of loyal friends stand against the forces that would destroy everything they love. Featuring the original artwork by Pauline Baynes, it brings the series to a powerful close and can be read on its own, though it is most rewarding after the earlier adventures.

  • Author: C.S. Lewis
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Chronicles of Narnia, Book 7
  • ISBN: 9780007323142

title: The Last Diet
author: Shahroo Izadi
description:
The Last Diet by behavioural change specialist Shahroo Izadi offers a different approach to losing weight, one that sets no rules about which foods to eat or how. Instead it focuses on changing, for the long term, how you relate to food and to your own body.

Izadi draws on her professional work in addiction treatment and on her own experience of struggling with weight and body image, explaining how evidence-based tools she had used with clients helped her lose eight stone and manage unwanted habits. Her kindness-based method puts positive self-perception at the centre, making this a supportive read for anyone tired of restrictive diets.

  • Author: Shahroo Izadi
  • Publisher: Bluebird
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781509883387

title: The Legend Of Zelda Twilight Princess Vol. 4
sheet_title: The Legend Of Zelda Twilight Princess Vol. 4
author: Akira Himekawa
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Vol. 4 continues Akira Himekawa's manga adaptation of the much-loved Nintendo adventure. Link and Midna, the Twilight Realm's princess, travel to Death Mountain to drive back the darkness tormenting the Gorons and, if all goes well, claim another piece of the Shadow Crystal.

After this they will need only a single fragment more, but their quest is far from over, as shadows gather around Hyrule Castle and fierce enemies lie in wait. Packed with action and fantasy, this fourth volume suits fans of the game and readers who enjoy adventure manga.

  • Author: Akira Himekawa
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Volume 4
  • ISBN: 9781974702268

title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess Vol. 6
sheet_title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess Vol. 6
author: Akira Himekawa
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Vol. 6 is the sixth instalment of Akira Himekawa's manga version of the Nintendo classic. Link and Midna make for Snowpeak to hunt for the Mirror of Shadow's missing pieces, needed if they are ever to overcome Ganondorf.

Link has beaten many fearsome foes on his mission to protect both Hyrule and the Twilight Realm. Yet Midna begins to fear that everything he has witnessed, and his growing hunger for power, are changing him. A darker, more personal chapter in the series, it will appeal to fans of the game and of fantasy manga.

  • Author: Akira Himekawa
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Volume 6
  • ISBN: 9781974711635

title: The Magician's Elephant
author: Kate DiCamillo
description:
The Magician's Elephant is a magical tale by Kate DiCamillo set in the city of Baltese. When a fortune-teller sets up her tent in the market square, the orphan Peter Augustus Duchene goes to ask the question that matters most to him: is his sister still alive, and if she is, where can she be found?

The answer he receives, that an elephant will show him the way, triggers a series of extraordinary events. Gentle and hopeful, the story is about longing, belief and daring to ask 'what if', and it suits middle-grade readers and families reading aloud together.

  • Author: Kate DiCamillo
  • Publisher: Walker Books
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529516456

title: The Sense of an Ending
author: Julian Barnes
description:
Julian Barnes's The Sense of an Ending won the Man Booker Prize in 2011. At school, Tony Webster and his close circle of friends met Adrian Finn, a boy more serious and more intelligent than the rest, and they all promised to remain friends for life.

Decades later, Tony is middle-aged, with a career, one marriage and an amicable divorce behind him. Then a letter from a lawyer arrives and begins to unsettle his memories. A short, precise and quietly devastating novel about time, memory and how we come to terms with the past, it is ideal for book clubs and lovers of literary fiction.

  • Author: Julian Barnes
  • Publisher: Random House
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099570332

title: The Slippery Slope (A Series of Unfortunate Events)
sheet_title: The Slippery Slope (A Series of Unfortunate Events)
author: Lemony Snicket
description:
The Slippery Slope is the tenth book in Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events. Separated once again, the Baudelaire orphans face a desperate situation high in the Mortmain Mountains, where Violet and Klaus must climb a treacherous frozen slope to rescue their baby sister Sunny from the clutches of Count Olaf.

Along the way they make a surprising new ally and uncover more clues about the mysterious organisation known as V.F.D. Told with Snicket's darkly comic narration, wordplay and gloomy warnings, it suits confident middle-grade readers who like their adventures mysterious and full of twists.

  • Author: Lemony Snicket
  • Publisher: Egmont
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Series of Unfortunate Events, Book 10
  • ISBN: 9781405266154

title: Twinchantment (Twinchantment Series 1)
author: Elise Allen
description:
Twinchantment is the first book in Elise Allen's middle-grade fantasy series of the same name. In the kingdom of Kaloon, magic was banned generations ago, and with it twins, black cats and anything else thought to be magical. That leaves princesses Flissa and Sara with a dangerous secret: they are twins.

Since birth the sisters have posed as a single princess, Flissara, sharing royal duties from grand balls to fencing displays while hiding in plain sight. When magic strikes the kingdom for the first time in years, their secret and their close bond are put to the test. A fun, warm-hearted adventure for young fantasy fans.

  • Author: Elise Allen
  • Publisher: Disney-Hyperion
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Twinchantment, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781368012461

title: Who Moved My Cheese?
author: Spencer Johnson
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Who Moved My Cheese? by Spencer Johnson is a short parable about handling change at work and in life. It follows four characters living in a maze: two mice, Sniff and Scurry, and two tiny people, Hem and Haw, who all search for the cheese that keeps them content, a stand-in for whatever we most want, from a good job to peace of mind.

When their supply of cheese suddenly disappears, each character reacts differently, and their choices illustrate simple lessons about anticipating change, adapting quickly and letting go of old habits. Quick to read and easy to discuss, it is a popular choice for teams, managers and anyone facing a new chapter.

  • Author: Spencer Johnson
  • Foreword: Kenneth H. Blanchard
  • Language: English

title: Wild Fire - Shetland
author: Ann Cleeves
description:
Wild Fire brings Ann Cleeves's Shetland series, featuring Detective Inspector Jimmy Perez, to a close as its eighth and final novel. An English family has moved to the islands hoping for a better life for their autistic son, but when the body of a young nanny is found hanging in their barn, gossip about her affair with the husband spreads fast.

Perez is brought in to work the case alongside his boss and on-off partner Willow Reeves, who leads the case, and he soon faces one of the most unsettling cases of his career, along with news that will change his life. A gripping finale for fans of atmospheric island crime fiction.

  • Author: Ann Cleeves
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Shetland, Book 8
  • ISBN: 9781529050257

title: Happy Monsters
author: Summersdale Publishers
description:
Happy Monsters: A Child's Guide to Coping With Their Feelings is a 32-page children's book from Summersdale's Vie imprint. As its title suggests, it is designed to help young children recognise their emotions and find ways of coping with them.

It is a useful choice for parents, carers and teachers looking for a gentle starting point for conversations about feelings.

  • Author: Summersdale Publishers
  • Publisher: Vie (Summersdale)
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800074224

title: Jelly-Boy
author: Nicole Godwin
description:
Jelly-Boy is a picture book by Nicole Godwin, illustrated by Christopher Nielsen and published by Walker Books as a 32-page paperback. Its short, illustrated format makes it well suited to reading aloud with young children.

A good pick for families, classrooms and libraries building a shelf of contemporary picture books.

  • Author: Nicole Godwin
  • Illustrator: Christopher Nielsen
  • Publisher: Walker Books
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529502855

title: Lady Chatterley's Lover
author: D.H. Lawrence
description:
Lady Chatterley's Lover was D.H. Lawrence's final novel and remains one of the most talked-about works of twentieth-century fiction. It tells of Constance Chatterley, a young wife isolated in an empty marriage, and her growing passion for Oliver Mellors, the gamekeeper on her husband's estate.

Long regarded as Lawrence's most controversial book, and famously the subject of an obscenity trial in Britain, it is a lyrical and frank celebration of physical love as a source of renewal. Its psychological depth and sensual writing make it essential reading for students of modern literature and lovers of classic fiction.

  • Author: D.H. Lawrence
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847494085

title: Oliver Twist
author: Charles Dickens
description:
This edition of Oliver Twist is a Penguin Readers Level 6 adaptation of Charles Dickens's classic novel, retold by Kate Williams for learners of English. It follows Oliver, an orphan born in a workhouse, who escapes a miserable apprenticeship and heads to London.

There he falls in with the Artful Dodger and a gang of young pickpockets run by the old criminal Fagin. The story keeps Dickens's vivid picture of crime and of the harsh treatment of poor children in nineteenth-century London, while the simplified text makes it accessible for advanced learners and older students.

  • Author: Charles Dickens
  • Adapted by: Kate Williams
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 96 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Penguin Readers Level 6
  • ISBN: 9780241430958

title: Supercharged Green Juice & Smoothie Diet
author: Christine Bailey
description:
Supercharged Green Juice & Smoothie Diet by Christine Bailey is a recipe book of more than 100 green juices and smoothies designed to support weight loss, detox and energy. Built around green vegetables, every drink includes at least one 'supercharged' ingredient, from superfood powders such as acai and collagen to sea vegetables, seeds and bee products.

Bailey explains why green drinks can be a better choice than sugary alternatives, offering plenty of vitamins, minerals and phytonutrients along with steadier energy levels. It is a practical, colourful guide for anyone wanting to add more nourishing greens to their daily routine.

  • Author: Christine Bailey
  • Publisher: Nourish
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781848992931

title: The Boy in the Dress
author: David Walliams
description:
The Boy in the Dress is David Walliams's first children's novel, illustrated by Quentin Blake. Dennis leads a rather lonely life: his mum left two years ago, his lorry-driver dad is unhappy, his brother bullies him and hugs are banned at home. What he does have is football, where he is his team's top scorer, and a secret love of fashion.

When his friend Lisa finds his collection of Vogue magazines, she persuades him to go to school in a dress, with consequences that put his place in the big match at risk. Funny and touching, it is a story about being yourself and accepting others, ideal for middle-grade readers.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 233 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007279043

title: THE HUNDRED DRESSES
author: Eleanor Estes
description:
The Hundred Dresses is Eleanor Estes's Newbery Honor classic, illustrated by Caldecott Medal winner Louis Slobodkin. Wanda Petronski always turns up at school in the same faded blue dress, yet she tells her classmates that she has a hundred dresses at home, and they tease her mercilessly for it.

When Wanda's family moves away, her classmate Maddie is left ashamed of having stood by in silence, and resolves to act differently in future. A short, gentle and moving story about bullying, bystanders and the courage to speak up, it is a perfect read for children, classrooms and families.

  • Author: Eleanor Estes
  • Illustrator: Louis Slobodkin
  • Publisher: Clarion Books
  • Format: Paperback, 80 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780152052607

title: THE MISERABLE MILL
author: Lemony Snicket
description:
The Miserable Mill is the fourth book in Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events. Mr Poe brings Violet, Klaus and baby Sunny Baudelaire to their newest guardian, who runs the Lucky Smells Lumbermill in the town of Paltryville.

Rather than enjoying a new home, the children quickly learn that they are expected to work in the mill, and it is not long before Count Olaf's sinister schemes catch up with them again. Told with Snicket's gloomy wit and playful vocabulary, it suits middle-grade readers who enjoy darkly funny adventures.

  • Author: Lemony Snicket
  • Publisher: Egmont
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Series of Unfortunate Events, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9781405266093

title: The Tiger Rising
author: Kate DiCamillo
description:
The Tiger Rising is a moving middle-grade novel by Kate DiCamillo. Six months after his mother's death, Rob has moved to Florida with his father, who refuses to talk about her. Rob copes by locking every painful thought away in an imaginary suitcase, from the rash on his legs to the bullies at school.

Everything starts to shift when he discovers a caged tiger hidden in the woods, and on the same day meets Sistine Bailey, a fierce fellow outsider who insists the tiger must be set free. Tender and honest, it is a story about grief, friendship and finally letting feelings out.

  • Author: Kate DiCamillo
  • Publisher: Walker Books
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781406357639

title: The Time Machine
author: H.G. Wells
description:
The Time Machine, first published in 1895, is H.G. Wells's pioneering novel of time travel. A Victorian scientist builds a machine that carries him to the year 802,701, where he finds the Eloi, a gentle people whose lives seem free of hardship and full of harmony.

That first impression proves deceptive. Beneath the surface live the brutish Morlocks, and the truth about how the two races are bound together gives the Time Traveller a chilling vision of humanity's future and of its roots in his own era. This compact Vintage Classics edition is a fine introduction to a founding work of modern science fiction.

  • Author: H.G. Wells
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 96 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780525432357

title: THREE DAUGHTERS OF EVE
author: Elif Shafak
description:
Elif Shafak's Three Daughters of Eve moves between Istanbul and Oxford, spanning the decades from the 1980s until today. Peri, a wealthy Turkish wife and mother, is heading to a dinner party in Istanbul when a beggar grabs her handbag, and in the struggle an old photograph falls out.

The snapshot, of three students and their professor, carries Peri back to her time at Oxford, to her friends Shirin and Mona, a charismatic tutor's course on God, and a love she has tried hard to forget. A rich story of faith, friendship, tradition and modernity.

  • Author: Elif Shafak
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 367 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241979921

title: The Carnivorous Carnival (A Series of Unfortunate Events)
sheet_title: The Carnivorous Carnival (A Series of Unfortunate Events)
author: Lemony Snicket
description:
The Carnivorous Carnival is the ninth book in Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events. Still on the run, the Baudelaire orphans hide in the back of Count Olaf's car and end up at the shabby Caligari Carnival, where they disguise themselves as sideshow performers.

They hope that Madame Lulu, the carnival's fortune-teller, can tell them whether one of their parents might still be alive, but danger, hungry lions and Olaf's troupe are never far away. Darkly funny and full of Snicket's trademark asides, it suits middle-grade readers following the Baudelaires' increasingly perilous story.

  • Author: Lemony Snicket
  • Publisher: Egmont
  • Format: Paperback, 286 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Series of Unfortunate Events, Book 9
  • ISBN: 9781405266147

title: The Pearl
author: John Steinbeck
description:
The Pearl is John Steinbeck's short, powerful parable about wealth and what it can do to a person. Kino, a poor pearl diver, lives with his wife Juana and their baby son Coyotito, until the day he finds an enormous pearl that seems to promise a better future.

As news of the find spreads, greed and suspicion close in, and the pearl brings danger rather than freedom to the little family. Told with the simplicity of a folk tale, it is a moving study of how riches can darken even good hearts, and a favourite with students and readers new to Steinbeck.

  • Author: John Steinbeck
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 96 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241980361

title: Treehouse Tales: Too Silly To Be Told.. Until Now!
sheet_title: Treehouse Tales: Too Silly To Be Told.. Until Now!
author: Andy Griffiths
description:
Treehouse Tales: too SILLY to be told ... UNTIL NOW! is a children's book by Andy Griffiths from the world of his Treehouse series. As the title promises, it brings together tales that were once judged far too silly to share.

It is a natural next read for young fans of the Treehouse books who enjoy fast, ridiculous humour and illustrated stories.

  • Author: Andy Griffiths
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529088663

title: Sons And Lovers
author: D.H. Lawrence
description:
Sons and Lovers is D.H. Lawrence's closely autobiographical novel of family life in an English mining community. As the sensitive Gertrude Morel withdraws from her hard-drinking, violent husband, their marriage turns into a battleground, and she pours her hopes into her sons William and Paul, determined that they will escape life down the pit.

When William falls ill, Paul struggles to break free of his mother's overpowering love through a series of relationships with other women. Often seen as the first English novel rooted in genuine working-class experience, it is presented here in an annotated Alma Classics Evergreens edition with notes and photographs.

  • Author: D.H. Lawrence
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 480 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847497536

title: The Girl and the Ghost
author: Hanna Alkaf
description:
The Girl and the Ghost is Hanna Alkaf's middle-grade debut, a spooky story rooted in Malaysian folklore and a 2020 Kirkus Prize finalist. Suraya is thrilled when her witch grandmother passes on to her a pelesit, a spirit companion she names Pink, and the two soon become inseparable.

But Suraya does not know that a pelesit can turn dark, and as Pink's shadows grow, both of them risk being swallowed by the darkness. Chilling and emotionally rich, it explores friendship and growing up, and suits readers aged 8 to 12 who like their fantasy with a shiver.

  • Author: Hanna Alkaf
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780062940964

title: Adventuremice: Mermouse Mystery
author: Philip Reeve
description:
Adventuremice: Mermouse Mystery is the second book in the Adventuremice series by Philip Reeve and Sarah McIntyre. Pedro is settling into exciting life with the Adventuremice when a storm blows in and he comes across something he never expected to see: a real, live mermouse.

The little mermouse is lost, so Pedro and his friends must be brave and resourceful, diving deep beneath the waves to find the hidden Mermouse City and get him home safely. Packed with teamwork and friendship, it is a fun illustrated adventure for young readers moving on to chapter books.

  • Author: Philip Reeve
  • Co-author and illustrator: Sarah McIntyre
  • Publisher: David Fickling Books
  • Format: Paperback, 128 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Adventuremice, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781788452687

title: الأطفال لا يفهمون كلمة لا
author: Sara Al-Najjar
description:
Children Don't Understand the Word No (الأطفال لا يفهمون كلمة لا) is a parenting guide in Arabic by Sara Al-Najjar. It sets out 21 principles for raising a well-balanced, emotionally healthy child with a strong and confident personality.

Aimed at parents worn out by stubborn behaviour, endless questions or failed attempts at persuasion, it offers practical methods for guiding a child's behaviour without falling back on punishment, for understanding a child's nature so that they turn to you first, and for building a calmer, more harmonious home.

  • Author: Sara Al-Najjar
  • Publisher: Dar Dawen
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778062564

title: بلى يستقيم
author: Abdullah Fadaaq
vendor: Arwiqa for Studies, Translation and Publishing
attention: No photo found — photograph in store
description:
Indeed, It Stands Straight: Jurisprudence and Thought (بلى يستقيم: فقه وفكر) is a book in Arabic by Abdullah Fadaaq, published in 2020. It is a work of Islamic jurisprudence and religious thought.

Its subjects include Islamic law and its higher objectives (maqasid), the renewal of Islamic thought and the relationship between Islam and the state, together with the social side of these questions.

  • Author: Abdullah Fadaaq
  • Publisher: Arwiqa for Studies, Translation and Publishing
  • Format: 154 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789777972871

title: النقلة انقل حياتك من الطموح إلى المعنى
sheet_title: النقلة انقل حياتك من الطموح إلى المعنى
author: Wayne W. Dyer
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
The Shift: Taking Your Life from Ambition to Meaning (النقلة: انقل حياتك من الطموح إلى المعنى) is the Arabic edition of Wayne W. Dyer's book. It invites readers to move away from a life without direction towards one filled with meaning and purpose.

Dyer describes a series of shifts: from spirit into physical existence, then into ambition, where the false self or ego takes charge, and finally towards meaning, when that false self is set aside and life is guided by a new set of principles. It suits readers interested in spirituality and personal growth.

  • Author: Wayne W. Dyer
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953978048

title: ابق حيا
author: Ibrahim Ahmed Essa
description:
Stay Alive (ابق حيًا) is a historical novel in Arabic by Ibrahim Ahmed Essa, set during the great famine that struck Egypt under the Fatimid caliph Al-Mustansir Billah. With the Nile run dry and hunger everywhere, people are driven to eat whatever they can find, and society loses its humanity in the struggle to survive.

The story follows Hassan, a young man from Damascus who arrives in Fustat to pursue his studies and is caught up in a series of surprises involving friendship, revenge, love and betrayal. A gripping, atmospheric read for anyone who enjoys historical fiction rooted in Egypt's past.

  • Author: Ibrahim Ahmed Essa
  • Publisher: Dar Al Karma
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778625561

title: إحدى عشرة دقيقة
author: Paulo Coelho
description:
Eleven Minutes (إحدى عشرة دقيقة) is the Arabic edition of the novel by Paulo Coelho. It follows Maria, a young Brazilian woman who leaves home in search of a new life and ends up working as a prostitute in Geneva, treating it as a job with its own rules and feeling no shame.

For her, sex remains as mysterious as love, and the question at the heart of the book is what happens when someone in her position falls in love. Frank and reflective, it explores desire, intimacy and the search for meaning in Coelho's familiar philosophical style.

  • Author: Paulo Coelho
  • Publisher: All Prints Distributors & Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 271 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953882567

title: أنا قادم أيها الضوء
author: Mohamed Abu Al-Gheit
description:
I Am Coming, O Light (أنا قادم أيها الضوء) is a memoir in Arabic by the Egyptian journalist Mohamed Abu Al-Gheit, written during his fight against cancer. Rather than a simple patient's diary, it gathers the experiences, feelings and lessons of that time into a personal record of his own life and of his generation.

Moving freely from the private to the public, the book shifts between clear scientific explanation, political news, the debunking of myths about so-called alternative medicine, and reflections on life and death. Humane and determined in spirit, it is an inspiring read for anyone who values honest, thoughtful life writing.

  • Author: Mohamed Abu Al-Gheit
  • Publisher: Dar El Shorouk
  • Format: Paperback, 315 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789770937990

title: جسر عبدون

Abdoun Bridge (جسر عبدون) is a novel in Arabic by the Jordanian writer Qasem Tawfiq. Ranging between Amman and Al-Daffa, a city imagined by the author, this panoramic story follows writers, scientists, parents and children through their desires, discoveries and adventures.   • Publisher: Alaan Publishers and Distributors
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789923133637

title: حرب الكلب الثانية
author: Ibrahim Nasrallah
description:
The Second War of the Dog (حرب الكلب الثانية) is a novel in Arabic by Ibrahim Nasrallah, winner of the International Prize for Arabic Fiction in 2018. It imagines an unsettling society in which quarrels no longer end in injuries but in killing, and where people have begun to rid themselves even of those who resemble them.

Blending dark satire with dystopian fiction, Nasrallah examines violence, greed and the loss of humanity in a world that has already pushed out everyone who was different. Part of his Balconies series, it is a bold, thought-provoking read for lovers of contemporary Arabic literature.

title: ذات الشعر الاحمر
author: Orhan Pamuk
description:
The Red-Haired Woman (ذات الشعر الأحمر) is the Arabic edition of the novel by Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk, translated by Jalal Fattah Rifaat. Set in a small town some 30 miles from Istanbul in the turbulent 1980s, a time of coups and political upheaval, it centres on a well-digger and his young apprentice.

Searching for a substitute for the father who vanished from his life, the young hero grows close to the master well-digger, until an accident and an encounter with a mysterious red-haired woman change everything. The novel explores the tense bonds between fathers and sons, set against a society full of father figures, from the state to the mafia boss.

title: أريد أن أنام
author: Harriet Griffey
description:
I Want to Sleep (أريد أن أنام) is the Arabic edition of Harriet Griffey's practical guide to getting a better night's rest. It starts from the simple question of what is keeping you awake, and explains how understanding the way sleep works opens up many ways to improve it.

The book looks at the whole 24 hours of the day and how what we do while awake shapes the quality of our sleep at night. With easy, practical solutions for both occasional and long-term sleep problems, it is a helpful companion for anyone who struggles to rest well.

  • Author: Harriet Griffey
  • Publisher: Dar Al Saqi
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786140321144

author: Amir Atef
description:
Gresha Island (جزيرة جريشة) is a crime thriller in Arabic by Amir Atef. A remote island, the year 1798 and a hidden archaeological treasure known to very few lie at the heart of the story, and chance brings Karim to the island, followed by his old rival Omar, reigniting a feud that was once about money but now has far higher stakes.

A mysterious murder leads to a long-buried secret, and as the search goes on the victims and losses mount, forcing the characters into open confrontation, especially when a new rival appears from nowhere. The novel asks how far human greed can drive people once it takes hold.

  • Author: Amir Atef
  • Publisher: Dar Dawen
  • Format: Paperback, 316 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778062915

title: حامل الصحف القديمة
author: Ibrahim Abdel Meguid
description:
The Carrier of Old Newspapers (حامل الصحف القديمة) is a novel in Arabic by the Egyptian writer Ibrahim Abdel Meguid. After the Covid pandemic has kept him shut away at home, the narrator returns to his café in downtown Cairo and finds the man he knows as the newspaper carrier still holding his bundle of old papers.

As the story goes on, more and more people take to carrying old newspapers too, as if to escape what surrounds them. Written in an inventive form, the novel moves between laughter, needless loss and pain, capturing a reality stranger than fiction.

  • Author: Ibrahim Abdel Meguid
  • Publisher: Dar El Shorouk
  • Format: Paperback, 294 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789770938102

title: حقيقة الخديعة
author: Dan Brown
description:
Deception Point (حقيقة الخديعة) is the Arabic edition of Dan Brown's techno-thriller. When a new NASA satellite detects a rare object buried deep in the Arctic ice, the struggling space agency announces a much-needed triumph, with major consequences for American space policy and an approaching presidential election.

The President sends White House intelligence analyst Rachel Sexton, along with a team of experts including the charming scientist Michael Tolland, to verify the find. Rachel uncovers evidence of a daring scientific fraud, and before she can warn the President, she and Michael are attacked by a deadly team of assassins.

  • Author: Dan Brown
  • Publisher: Arab Scientific Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 471 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953299075

title: رواء مكة
author: Hassan Aourid
description:
The Quenching of Mecca (رواء مكة) is a work in Arabic by the Moroccan writer and thinker Hassan Aourid, drawn from his pilgrimage to Mecca. For him the Hajj, which could have been a ritual and nothing more, became an encounter with his own self.

Circling the Kaaba and drinking Zamzam water as the pilgrims hurried around him, he felt something welling up inside him like water rising from the depths, a renewed understanding of life as an answer to God's call. Reflective and personal, it suits readers interested in spiritual journeys and Muslim autobiography.

  • Author: Hassan Aourid
  • Publisher: Arab Cultural Centre
  • Format: 223 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953689234

title: كما يليق بأب يحاول
author: Moustafa Mounir
description:
As Befits a Father Who Tries (كما يليق بأب يحاول) is a novel in Arabic by Moustafa Mounir, a wildly imaginative story that is at once a chase, a family novel and a book about Egypt's most famous Nobel-winning writer. In a Cairo full of everyday dangers, an ordinary Egyptian man suddenly finds himself the main suspect in an espionage case.

Determined to take revenge on the strange zealots who killed his young son, and helped by his psychiatrist in the search for his wife, who vanished in bizarre circumstances, he stumbles on a mysterious novel, the hidden side of an important cultural institution and a peculiar secret organisation, and keeps asking how it all became so tangled.

  • Author: Moustafa Mounir
  • Publisher: Dar Al Karma
  • Format: 320 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778648003

Behind the Sun: Diaries of an Ahwazi Writer in Iran's Secret Prisons (وراء الشمس: يوميات كاتب أحوازي في زنازين إيران السرية) is a book in Arabic by Yousef Azizi. As its full title indicates, it is a first-hand account, written as diaries, of the author's time held in secret prison cells in Iran.

  • Author: Yousef Azizi
  • Publisher: Al-Mutawassit / Dar Al-Suwaidi
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9788899687755

title: الفتوحات الإسلامية
author: Saleh Ahmad Al-Ali
description:
The Islamic Conquests (الفتوحات الإسلامية) is a historical study in Arabic by the Iraqi historian Saleh Ahmad Al-Ali on the first Islamic conquests, events of great importance in the history of the Arabs and of the wider world. Where earlier accounts mostly traced the routes of armies and the order of battles, this study takes a different approach.

It outlines the major campaigns briefly, then examines the conquests front by front, concentrating on how the Arab forces and their opponents were organised, armed and deployed, and on the role of the community and its fighters. It is a valuable resource for students and readers of early Islamic history.

  • Author: Saleh Ahmad Al-Ali
  • Publisher: All Prints Distributors & Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 362 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953884271

description:
The White Zift (الزفت الأبيض) is a novel in Arabic for young adults by Maria Dadouch. Seventeen-year-old Kinan enjoys a close friendship with his father and with his friend Qais, a fast-growing following on his Facebook channel and a rising reputation in the school football league.

Cooking fish stew and sharing it with his father and Qais around their small kitchen table, he feels life could hardly be better, until the day a boy named Ghali puts a strange cigarette between his lips. It is a timely story for teenage readers about friendship, family and choices that can change a young life.

  • Author: Maria Dadouch
  • Publisher: Dar Al Yasmin
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789957682590

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
description:
Charles Darwin's landmark work On the Origin of Species sets out the theory of evolution by natural selection. When Darwin set out on HMS Beagle in late 1831, he had only a vague idea that all living things, past and present, were more closely related than the accepted creation story allowed.

Over a five-year voyage and many years of later study at his home in Kent, he gathered evidence from across the globe, from the Galapagos to Scotland, building a case that transformed how we understand the natural world. This annotated Evergreens edition from Alma Classics is ideal for students and curious readers.

  • Author: Charles Darwin
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847497840

title: THE 130-STOREY TREEHOUSE
author: Andy Griffiths
description:
The 130-Storey Treehouse is the tenth book in the Treehouse series by Andy Griffiths, illustrated by Terry Denton. Andy and Terry's treehouse keeps on growing, and the pair are busy building thirteen brand-new levels to take it to 130 storeys.

The new floors are still under construction and top secret, which sets the scene for another round of the pair's slapstick humour and outrageous adventures. Told through a lively mix of text and cartoons, it is perfect for young readers who love silly, fast-paced illustrated chapter books.

  • Author: Andy Griffiths
  • Illustrator: Terry Denton
  • Publisher: Macmillan Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Treehouse, Book 10

title: The 143-Storey Treehouse
author: Andy Griffiths

The 143-Storey Treehouse is the eleventh book in Andy Griffiths and Terry Denton's Treehouse series. Thirteen more levels have been added to the ever-growing treehouse, including a word-o-matic, a recycling centre, a wrecking ball, a dragon's cave, a complaining room and a graveyard where it is always midnight.

Andy has been feeling stressed, and Terry is determined to help him unwind, but nothing in this treehouse ever goes quite as expected. Packed with jokes and cartoons, it suits young readers who enjoy laugh-out-loud illustrated adventures.

  • Author: Andy Griffiths
  • Illustrator: Terry Denton
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Treehouse, Book 11
  • ISBN: 9781529047882

title: Hoot
author: Carl Hiaasen
description:
Hoot is Carl Hiaasen's funny, eco-minded mystery for young readers. New to Florida, Roy Eberhardt gets off to a bad start when the school bully Dana Matherson pins his face to the bus window, but that is how Roy spots a strange boy running away from the bus with no books and no shoes.

Curious, Roy follows the trail, which leads him to burrowing owls threatened by a building project, a mysterious eco-warrior, toilet-trained alligators and some very poisonous snakes. Sharp, warm and full of Hiaasen's trademark humour, it suits middle-grade readers who care about animals and the environment.

  • Author: Carl Hiaasen
  • Publisher: Yearling
  • Format: Paperback, 292 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780440419396

title: مصائر: كونشرتو الهولوكوست والنكبة
author: Rabai Al-Madhoun
vendor: Arab Institute for Research and Publishing
description:
Destinies: Concerto of the Holocaust and the Nakba (مصائر: كونشرتو الهولوكوست والنكبة) is a novel in Arabic by the Palestinian writer Rabai Al-Madhoun, winner of the International Prize for Arabic Fiction in 2016. It opens with Ivana, a Palestinian-Armenian woman who fell in love with a British doctor during the Mandate, had a daughter, Julie, and fled with her to London on the eve of the 1948 Nakba.

Before she dies, Ivana asks for half of her ashes to be scattered over the Thames and half returned to her birthplace, the old city of Acre. Julie and her husband Walid Dahman travel to Palestine to carry out her wish, and find themselves falling in love with the land.

  • Author: Rabai Al-Madhoun
  • Publisher: Arab Institute for Research and Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 267 pages

  • ISBN: 9786144195765

title: Code Name Bananas

description:
Code Name Bananas is a funny, action-packed children's novel by David Walliams set in London in 1940, during the Second World War. Eleven-year-old Eric spends every spare moment at London Zoo, where his favourite animal is Gertrude the gorilla.

When bombs start falling on the city, Eric decides he must save Gertrude, and together with his Uncle Sid, a zookeeper, they go on the run. Hiding out by the seaside, the unlikely trio stumble on a top-secret Nazi plot. Mixing wartime adventure with Walliams's trademark humour and a big-hearted friendship, it suits young readers who enjoy laugh-out-loud stories.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Language: English

title: Happening
author: Annie Ernaux
description:
Happening is Annie Ernaux's account of the abortion she sought as a young woman in 1963, when it was still illegal in France. At twenty-three and unmarried, she discovered she was pregnant and knew she could not keep the child, fearing the shame it would bring on her and her family.

Writing some forty years later and drawing on her memories and the diary she kept at the time, Ernaux recounts her desperate search for help and the danger she faced, in prose that is spare, precise and unflinching. A short but powerful work by the Nobel Prize-winning French author.

  • Author: Annie Ernaux
  • Publisher: Fitzcarraldo Editions
  • Format: Paperback, 76 pages
  • Language: English

title: Love is a Revolution
author: Renée Watson
description:
Love Is a Revolution is a young adult novel by Renée Watson about first love and learning to love yourself. When her cousin-sister-friend Imani insists on celebrating her birthday at an open mic night, Nala Robertson reluctantly tags along and falls head over heels for Tye Brown, the event's host.

Tye is a committed activist who spends his summer organising community events, while Nala would rather watch films and sample new ice-cream flavours. To win him over, she tells a few small lies, and keeping them going becomes harder as their relationship grows. Warm and funny, it is a story about honesty and self-acceptance.

  • Author: Renée Watson
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury YA
  • Format: Paperback, 295 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781526616821

title: Orlando
author: Virginia Woolf
description:
Orlando is Virginia Woolf's playful mock biography of a young nobleman who begins life as a favourite at the court of Queen Elizabeth I. After heartbreak he turns from romance to literature, and while serving as an ambassador in Constantinople he sleeps for days on end and wakes to find that he has become a woman.

Gifted with eternal youth, Orlando travels across Europe and through the centuries, discovering what it means to live as a woman. Inspired by Woolf's friend, the writer Vita Sackville-West, it is a witty, inventive classic about gender, identity and time.

  • Author: Virginia Woolf
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 258 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847493705

title: Ruin And Rising
author: Leigh Bardugo
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)

description:
Ruin and Rising is the final book in Leigh Bardugo's Shadow and Bone trilogy, part of the Grishaverse. Ravka's capital is lost and the Darkling now sits on its throne, so the country's last hope lies with an exhausted Sun Summoner, a tracker in disgrace and what is left of a once-mighty Grisha army.

Sheltering in caverns far underground, guarded by fanatical followers who believe she is a saint, Alina plans her next move: tracking down the firebird, the final amplifier she needs. As she uncovers the Darkling's secrets, she must decide what she is willing to sacrifice. A tense, emotional conclusion for fans of the series and the Netflix adaptation.

  • Author: Leigh Bardugo
  • Language: English
  • Series: Shadow and Bone Trilogy, Book 3 (Grishaverse)

title: She Said
author: Dominique Enright
description:
She Said: Witty Words from Wise Women is a collection of quotations compiled by Dominique Enright. It brings together the sharpest lines from politicians, writers, actors, artists, musicians and fashion figures, all united by quick minds and cutting wit.

Ranging from Sappho to Beyoncé and from Dorothy Parker to Carrie Fisher, and spanning almost three thousand years from around 700 BC to today, it includes cheeky comebacks, thoughtful reflections and righteous outrage. A fun gift book for anyone who enjoys a well-turned phrase.

  • Author: Dominique Enright
  • Publisher: Michael O'Mara Books
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages

title: The Crown (The Selection Book 5)
author: Kiera Cass
description:
The Crown is the fifth and final book in Kiera Cass's The Selection series. Two decades on from the romance of America Singer and Prince Maxon, their daughter Eadlyn is the first princess ever to run a Selection for herself.

Eadlyn never expected to find a true partner among her thirty-five suitors, let alone real love. But as the competition reaches its end, her heart surprises her, and she faces a choice that is harder, and matters more, than she ever imagined. A romantic, satisfying conclusion for fans of the series.

  • Author: Kiera Cass
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 279 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Selection, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9780007580248

title: The Heir (The Selection Book 4)
author: Kiera Cass
description:
The Heir is the fourth book in Kiera Cass's The Selection series, opening a new chapter in the kingdom of Illéa. Eighteen years after America Singer won Prince Maxon's heart through the Selection, it is their daughter Princess Eadlyn's turn to hold one.

Eadlyn has no intention of repeating her parents' fairy-tale romance, but as the competition gets under way she may find that her own happy ending is closer than she thought. Full of royal drama, rivalry and romance, it introduces a new generation of characters for fans of the original trilogy.

  • Author: Kiera Cass
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 342 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Selection, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9780007580224

title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess Vol. 7

description:
The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Vol. 7 continues Akira Himekawa's manga retelling of the Nintendo adventure. Wounded and drained after his fight with his own dark double, Link is left without Midna and cannot yet harness the Master Sword's power.

With his quest looking hopeless, he is haunted by dreams of a battle-scarred warrior, and the question of who this figure is and what he can teach Link drives the story forward. An exciting volume for fans of the game and readers who enjoy fantasy adventure in manga form.

  • Author: Akira Himekawa
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 168 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Volume 7
  • ISBN: 9781974715336

title: The Marvellers
author: Dhonielle Clayton
description:
The Marvellers is Dhonielle Clayton's first middle-grade novel and the opening book of the Conjureverse series. Eleven-year-old Ella Durand becomes the first Conjuror to be admitted to the Arcanum Training Institute, a magic school in the sky where Marvellers from around the world come to practise their cultural arts.

From brewing Indian spice elixirs to Caribbean steel-drum hypnosis and bargaining with fussy Irish faeries, the magic is dazzling, but Ella soon learns that being first is hard when some people see Conjure magic as dangerous and wrong. A vibrant fantasy about belonging, friendship and courage.

  • Author: Dhonielle Clayton
  • Publisher: Piccadilly Press
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Conjureverse, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781800785472

title: The Trumpet Of The Swan
author: E.B. White
description:
The Trumpet of the Swan is E.B. White's classic novel about Louis, a young trumpeter swan born without a voice. Unable to make the call that every swan needs, Louis is determined to find another way to be heard, and with the help of his friend Sam Beaver he learns to read and write.

When his devoted father steals a real trumpet for him, Louis sets out to master it and to pay off the debt, a journey that takes him far from home and towards the swan he loves. Gentle, funny and wise, it is a timeless story for young readers and for reading aloud.

  • Author: E.B. White
  • Publisher: Puffin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141354842

title: The Wolf Wilder
author: Katherine Rundell
description:
The Wolf Wilder is a historical adventure for young readers by Katherine Rundell, set deep in the snowbound forests of Russia. Feo lives with her mother, a wolf wilder: rather than taming animals, she takes wolves that have been kept by people and teaches them to survive on their own again, to hunt, to run and to stay wary of humans.

When the cruelty of the Russian Army reaches their isolated home, Feo is forced to flee through the snow with her wolves, and her journey becomes tangled up with the beginnings of a revolution. Lyrical and fierce, it is a story of courage, loyalty and standing up for what you love, ideal for confident middle-grade readers and animal lovers.

  • Author: Katherine Rundell
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781526605511

title: An Emotion Of Great Delight
author: Tahereh Mafi
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
An Emotion of Great Delight is a young adult novel by Tahereh Mafi set in 2003, a few months after the United States went to war with Iraq. Shadi, a Muslim teenager who wears hijab, faces rising suspicion and hostility towards her community while trying to keep her head down at school.

At home her life is falling apart: her family is grieving, her father is seriously ill, her mother is struggling and her friendships are fracturing. Quietly written and deeply felt, the novel explores grief, loneliness, dual identity and first love, and the right to find joy even in the darkest times. A moving read for teens and adults alike.

  • Author: Tahereh Mafi
  • Language: English

title: Meditations For Every Day
author: Summersdale
description:
Meditations for Every Day is a pocket-sized hardback from Summersdale offering a gentle route into meditation. As its subtitle suggests, it pairs simple practical tips with calming quotations from well-known champions of the practice, helping readers find moments of stillness in even the busiest of days.

Written for complete beginners as well as those hoping to refresh an existing routine, it encourages readers to pause, breathe and return to the present moment with comfort and confidence. Easy to dip into, it makes a thoughtful gift and a calm companion for building a lasting, nourishing daily habit.

  • Publisher: Summersdale
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800076761

title: Fairy Tail 4
author: Hiro Mashima
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Fairy Tail, Volume 4, continues Hiro Mashima's long-running fantasy manga about the rowdy wizards of the Fairy Tail guild. Hot-headed fire wizard Natsu, newcomer Lucy and Happy the flying cat have helped themselves to an S-Class quest, the most dangerous kind of job, which only the guild's top wizards are allowed to take.

The quest leads them to the mysterious Demon Island, where one wrong move could be fatal, and the guild sends help after them before they get in over their heads. Packed with magical battles, slapstick humour and loyal friendships, this volume opens one of the series' early story arcs and suits readers who enjoy energetic shonen adventure.

  • Author: Hiro Mashima
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • Series: Fairy Tail, Volume 4

title: Hilda And The Troll Graphic Novel
sheet_title: Hilda And The Troll Graphic Novel
author: Luke Pearson
description:
Hilda and the Troll is the first of Luke Pearson's Hilda graphic novels, originally published as Hildafolk. It introduces Hilda, an endlessly curious girl who can never stay still for long, and whose outings bring her face to face with sea spirits, giants and all kinds of strange creatures. When she comes across a mysterious rock shaped like a troll, her day takes a very unexpected turn.

Pearson's distinctive artwork and gentle humour make this a charming entry point to the world that went on to inspire the Netflix animated series. It suits young readers who love adventure and folklore, and works well as a shared read for families discovering graphic novels together.

  • Author: Luke Pearson
  • Publisher: Flying Eye Books
  • Format: Paperback, 40 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Hilda, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781909263789

title: Ima Koi: Now I'm in Love, Vol. 2
author: Ayuko Hatta
description:
Ima Koi: Now I'm in Love, Vol. 2 continues Ayuko Hatta's sweet shojo romance manga. Shy high school student Satomi once let love slip away because she could never bring herself to confess, so when she fell for someone new she blurted out her feelings at once, to the dazzlingly good-looking Yagyu, who to her astonishment agreed to go out with her.

In this volume the new couple head into summer, with a trip to the seaside, a nerve-racking date and a first sleepover testing Satomi's heart to its limits. Light, funny and full of fluttering first-romance moments, it suits readers who enjoy gentle, character-driven shojo stories.

  • Author: Ayuko Hatta
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 184 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Ima Koi: Now I'm in Love, Volume 2
  • ISBN: 9781974729739

title: Ima Koi: Now I'm in Love, Vol. 3
author: Ayuko Hatta
description:
Ima Koi: Now I'm in Love, Vol. 3 is the third volume of Ayuko Hatta's shojo romance manga. Satomi, a timid high school girl who finally found the nerve to declare her feelings, is now dating Yagyu, the strikingly handsome classmate who surprised her by saying yes.

This time the pair sign up for a couples' event at the school's cultural festival, and when an attractive older student appears on the scene, Yagyu finds himself feeling a little jealous. Warm, funny and full of the small thrills of a first relationship, it is a sweet read for fans of school-life romance.

  • Author: Ayuko Hatta
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 184 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Ima Koi: Now I'm in Love, Volume 3
  • ISBN: 9781974729746

title: Into The Dark Forest
author: Liz Flanagan
description:
Into the Dark Forest opens Liz Flanagan's Wildsmith series, an illustrated fantasy adventure with artwork by Joe Todd-Stanton. With war approaching her home city, Rowan and her mother escape to the Dark Forest, where Rowan meets her grandfather for the first time, along with his white wolf, Arto.

Missing her father but making new friends, including three powerful witches, Rowan saves a dragon hatchling from poachers and learns a secret about who she really is: she is a Wildsmith. Soon she is looking after a whole brood of young dragons, until danger forces the forest community to pull together. Full of magic, animals and warmth, it suits young readers who love dragons.

  • Author: Liz Flanagan
  • Illustrator: Joe Todd-Stanton
  • Publisher: UCLan Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Wildsmith, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781915235046

title: Introducing Chaos : A Graphic Guide
author: Ziauddin Sardar
description:
Introducing Chaos: A Graphic Guide is an illustrated introduction to chaos theory from Icon Books' long-running Introducing series, written by Ziauddin Sardar with illustrations by Iwona Abrams. It shows how chaotic behaviour turns up in surprising places, from the rise and fall of animal populations to the swings of the stock market.

The book traces these ideas back to their roots in modern mathematics and physics, then looks at how chaos connects with complexity, the idea that intricate systems can grow out of a handful of simple rules. Combining clear text with lively drawings, it suits curious general readers and students meeting the subject for the first time.

  • Author: Ziauddin Sardar
  • Illustrator: Iwona Abrams
  • Publisher: Icon Books
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Introducing Graphic Guides
  • ISBN: 9781848310131

title: The Invention of Solitude
author: Paul Auster
description:
The Invention of Solitude is Paul Auster's first prose book, a memoir in two parts. In the first, written after the sudden death of his father, Auster tries to piece together the life of a distant, elusive man he felt he had never truly known, uncovering a startling family secret along the way.

The second part is a looser, more meditative sequence of reflections on memory, chance, fatherhood and the act of writing, shaped in part by his relationship with his own young son. Intimate and searching, it lays the groundwork for themes that run through his later fiction and will appeal to readers of literary memoir.

  • Author: Paul Auster
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 185 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571284207

title: KICKING SICK
author: Amy Kurtz
description:
Kicking Sick: Your Go-To Guide for Thriving with Chronic Health Conditions is a practical, encouraging book by Amy Kurtz, with a foreword by Dr Mark Hyman. Kurtz lived with serious illness from her mid-teens into her twenties and writes from experience about the shame, fear, loneliness and frustration that long-term conditions can bring.

Drawing on how she transformed her own health, she shows readers how to move past despair, listen to their bodies, take charge of their care and build a strong support team of doctors, friends and family. Advice from the specialists who helped her adds expert perspective. It suits anyone living with a chronic condition, and those supporting them.

  • Author: Amy Kurtz
  • Foreword: Mark Hyman
  • Publisher: Sounds True
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781622036653

title: Megamonster
author: David Walliams
description:
Megamonster is a funny, fast-paced children's adventure by David Walliams, illustrated by Tony Ross. On a volcanic island ringed by shark-filled seas stands The Cruel School, where the lessons are absurd, the dinners revolting and the teachers frightening. When Larker is sent there, she quickly notices that something very strange is going on.

Her suspicions centre on the creepy science teacher, Doctor Doktur, a hidden cave and a mysterious Monsterfication Machine, and she sets out to uncover what he is plotting. Packed with gross-out humour and gloriously silly villainy, it is a great pick for young readers who love Walliams's mischievous style.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008499761

Naruto refuses to give up, but turning the battle around will take more than determination, and everything may depend on whether he and Sasuke can finally fight side by side and turn the tide of the war. Fast-paced and dramatic, this volume is for readers deep into the series who want to follow the war to its conclusion.

title: New From Here
author: Kelly Yang
description:
New From Here is a middle-grade novel by Kelly Yang set at the start of the COVID-19 pandemic. When the virus reaches Hong Kong, ten-year-old Knox Wei-Evans's mother decides almost overnight to move him and his siblings to California, leaving his father behind because of work.

At his new school Knox is treated as an outsider and blamed by classmates for the virus because he came from Asia, while at home his mother loses her job and nobody knows when the family will be together again. Honest and hopeful, it explores racism, family and finding your voice, and suits middle-grade readers and families talking about fairness and belonging.

  • Author: Kelly Yang
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster Children's UK
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages

description:
Percy Jackson's Greek Gods is Rick Riordan's retelling of the classic Greek myths, narrated by Percy Jackson himself. Asked by a publisher to write down what he knows about the gods, the son of Poseidon reluctantly agrees, starting with the creation of the world and moving through a who's who of the Olympians, from Apollo to Zeus.

Percy adds his own sarcastic commentary to every tale, which is full of feuds, trickery, monsters and divine misbehaviour, making ancient stories feel fresh and funny. With illustrations by John Rocco, it works as an entertaining introduction to Greek mythology and a treat for fans of the Percy Jackson books.

  • Illustrator: John Rocco
  • Language: English

title: Spy x Family, Vol. 8
author: Tatsuya Endo
description:
Spy x Family, Vol. 8 continues Tatsuya Endo's action comedy manga about a family built on secrets. Master spy Twilight has been ordered to assemble a fake family to complete his mission, unaware that his adopted daughter Anya can read minds and that his new wife Yor is secretly an assassin.

In this volume, the shadowy organisation Garden assigns Yor to guard a mafia family aboard a cruise ship, but Loid and Anya have won a holiday on the very same voyage. As the job grows more complicated, Yor begins to question her hidden life. Funny, warm and full of action, it is essential reading for fans of the series.

  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 216 pages

title: Superfood Sandwiches
author: Katy Chudy
description:
Superfood Sandwiches is a cookbook by chef Katy Chudy that turns the humble sandwich into a nourishing meal. Built around recognised superfoods, fresh vegetables and fruit, natural meats and cheeses and good bread, its recipes show how a sandwich can be wholesome, satisfying and suitable for any meal of the day.

Alongside the fillings there are recipes for breads, sauces, pestos and spreads, from buttermilk wholewheat loaves to tomatillo yoghurt sauce. Chudy offers shortcuts for cooks in a hurry as well as more ambitious options and ideas for using up leftovers, making it handy for budget lunches and special occasions alike.

  • Author: Katy Chudy
  • Publisher: Fair Winds Press
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781592336630

title: The 365 Bullet Guide
author: Zennor Compton
description:
The 365 Bullet Guide is an introduction to bullet journalling by Zennor Compton, illustrated by Marcia Mihotich. It explains how the bullet method works, beginning with a simple, reliable to-do list and building up to a creative system for organising the present, recording the past and planning the future.

For every day of the year there is a short exercise designed to take around six minutes or less, so readers can adopt the method as gradually as they like. Ideas range from habit trackers and sleep logs to handwriting practice. It suits anyone who wants to be more organised while having fun with pen and paper.

  • Author: Zennor Compton
  • Illustrator: Marcia Mihotich
  • Publisher: Boxtree
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English

title: The Elite (The Selection Book 2)
author: Kiera Cass
description:
The Elite is the second book in Kiera Cass's Selection series, a young adult romance set in a future kingdom where a group of girls compete to marry the crown prince. Only six contestants are left, and America Singer is closer than ever to winning Prince Maxon's heart and a life of glamour at the palace.

Yet the rivalry is growing fierce, rebel attacks outside the palace are pushing the kingdom towards war, and America is torn between her deepening feelings for Maxon and her first love, Aspen, who is never far away. Mixing romance, rivalry and royal intrigue, it continues the story begun in The Selection.

  • Author: Kiera Cass
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 326 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Selection, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780007466702

title: The Good Thieves
author: Katherine Rundell
description:
The Good Thieves is a historical heist adventure by Katherine Rundell. When Vita's beloved grandfather writes in anguish about losing his family home and the precious jewels hidden inside it, she and her mother cross the ocean to New York, and Vita resolves to win back what a ruthless swindler took from him.

Breaking into Hudson Hall will take careful planning and trustworthy allies, and she finds them in an unlikely crew of pickpockets, circus performers and animal handlers. Full of daring, friendship and Rundell's vivid storytelling, it is a thrilling read for middle-grade readers who enjoy adventure with plenty of heart.

  • Author: Katherine Rundell
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury
  • Format: Paperback, 323 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781408882658

title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess Vol. 9

author: Akira Himekawa
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Vol. 9 continues Akira Himekawa's manga adaptation of the Nintendo adventure game. Link and Midna, the Twilight Realm's princess, are racing to recover the pieces of the Shadow Crystal before an evil power can use them to take control of both worlds.

In this volume Midna tells Link about her past: how the sorcerer Zant transformed her and how bitterness drove her to use others in her quest for revenge. Link's forgiveness may give her the strength to keep going as they prepare to enter the Twilight Realm itself, where greater dangers await. A must for Zelda fans and readers of fantasy manga.

  • Author: Akira Himekawa
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 200 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Volume 9
  • ISBN: 9781974723386

title: The Next Together
author: Lauren James
description:
The Next Together is Lauren James's debut novel, a young adult romance that spans centuries. Katherine and Matthew are reborn again and again throughout history, and in every life they find each other, fall deeply in love and are torn apart, often while changing the course of events for the better.

Their stories unfold in very different eras, from the Crimean War and the siege of Carlisle to the years 2019 and 2039, as they try to discover why they keep coming back. The book is pieced together from narrative chapters alongside letters, diaries, news stories, online articles and historical records, blending fate, time travel and first love in an inventive format.

  • Publisher: Walker Books
  • Format: Paperback, 356 pages
  • Language: English

One True King is the sixth book in Soman Chainani's School for Good and Evil series and the closing part of its Camelot Years arc. The fairy tale of best friends Sophie and Agatha reaches its climax as the battle for Camelot's throne decides who will rule the Endless Woods.

With loyalties tested and the fate of Good and Evil at stake, the story builds towards the long-awaited ending of Sophie and Agatha's journey. Full of magic, twists and fierce friendship, it is essential reading for fans who have followed Sophie, Agatha and Tedros since their first days at the School.

  • Format: Paperback, 624 pages

The Tyrant's Tomb is the fourth book in Rick Riordan's The Trials of Apollo series. Stripped of his powers and living as a mortal teenager called Lester Papadopoulos, the god Apollo continues his mission to restore the ancient oracles, and this time his journey takes him to Camp Jupiter, the Roman demigod camp near San Francisco.

The Romans are bracing for a final battle against the Triumvirate, three wicked emperors of ancient Rome, and familiar faces such as Hazel, Reyna and Frank need Apollo's help to survive. Funny and moving in equal measure, the novel explores loss and what it really means to be a hero, and is a must for fans of the Camp Half-Blood books.
