The World's Worst Children is a collection of ten darkly comic cautionary tales by David Walliams, illustrated throughout by Tony Ross. It introduces five beastly boys and five ghastly girls, each one a hilarious warning about very bad behaviour.

Among them are Sofia Sofa, a television fan so glued to the settee that she starts to become part of it, and Blubbering Bertha, a big sister who simply cannot stop telling tales. Gleefully naughty and full of slapstick humour, it is perfect for reading aloud or for young readers who enjoy funny stories in short, satisfying chunks.

Fairy Tail, Volume 5, is the next instalment of Hiro Mashima's fantasy manga about a guild of wizards for hire. On the island quest, ice wizard Gray comes face to face with Lyon, his former training partner, who is trying to awaken a destructive demon and in doing so threatens to undo the sacrifice their teacher once made.

This volume reveals much more about Gray's past and what drives him, adding emotional depth to the series alongside its trademark humour and spectacular magical fights. It is a key chapter for anyone following the early adventures of Natsu, Lucy, Gray and Happy, and an easy pick for fans of action-packed shonen manga.

Chapters cover hearty breakfasts, soups, stews and curries, pot roasts and even puddings, and Wilson shares tips on cooking cheaply, cutting food waste and keeping meals free of added sugar. It suits busy households who want wholesome food that largely cooks itself while they get on with the day.

Influence is a young adult thriller by Sara Shepard, creator of Pretty Little Liars, and Lilia Buckingham. It follows Delilah Rollins, who arrives in Los Angeles after one of her videos goes viral and finds herself on the edge of a glittering world of online fame alongside established influencers.

Every girl she meets is hiding something, from former child star Jasmine to the seemingly carefree Fiona and the picture-perfect Scarlet Leigh, and when a secret threatens to surface, the pressure to protect their images turns dangerous. Sharp and suspenseful, it explores fame, friendship and the gap between online personas and real life.

Jayben and the Star Glass is the second adventure in Thomas Leeds's fantasy series following Jayben, a boy who remembers nothing of his past yet may be the only one able to save a magical world. He now knows he is the Ninth Dreamer, the one person with the power to stop Null, the villain who has been making the people of the Elf World forget.

With the Golden Torch stolen, Jayben must find another way to harness his power, and a magical Star Glass gem may hold the answer. His quest leads towards the scorching desert of Fellooz, where Null is already heading. Full of wonder and peril, it suits middle-grade readers who love epic magical adventures.

  • Author: Thomas Leeds
  • Publisher: Hodder Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages

When Number 6 targets Pop in hospital, Koichi's allies face a desperate fight. Packed with action, it is one for fans of the wider My Hero Academia universe.

Help comes from an unexpected direction when Kankuro, Temari and Gaara of the Sand Village arrive to fight alongside the Leaf, raising the question of whether they have another motive beyond renewing an old alliance. title: Black Coffee
author: Agatha Christie
description:
Black Coffee is a Hercule Poirot mystery adapted as a novel by Charles Osborne from Agatha Christie's original stage play. The inventor Sir Claud Amory discovers that the formula for his powerful new explosive has been stolen by someone in his own household, and he offers the thief a chance to return it unseen by plunging the room into darkness.

When the lights come back on, someone is dead, and Poirot must untangle family feuds, past romances and a houseful of suspicious guests to find the killer before disaster strikes. Classic country-house detection in Christie's familiar style, it will please fans of Golden Age crime.

The 156-Storey Treehouse is the twelfth book in the illustrated Treehouse series by Andy Griffiths, with pictures by Terry Denton. Andy and Terry are celebrating Christmas in their ever-growing treehouse, which now boasts 13 brand-new storeys to explore.

The latest additions include a wishing well, an aquarium wonderland, a record-breaking level, a TV quiz show run by a quizbot, a lost sausage office, an extremely smelly floor and a mind-reading machine that makes your perfect sandwich. Bursting with jokes and cartoons, it is a festive treat for young readers who love silly, fast-paced stories.

  • Illustrator: Terry Denton
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan

author: Eoin Colfer

The Fowl Twins launches Eoin Colfer's spin-off series set in the world of Artemis Fowl, starring Artemis's younger brothers. Myles and Beckett are twins but complete opposites: Myles is a fastidious genius with an IQ of 170 who prints himself a new suit every day, while Beckett is scruffy, carefree and would rather not wear clothes at all.

Left for one night in the care of the house's security system, the eleven-year-olds befriend a troll on the run and soon find themselves pursued by a scheming aristocrat and a nun with a talent for interrogation, both determined to get hold of the creature. Fast, funny and packed with gadgets and mayhem, it suits readers who love comic fantasy.

  • Author: Eoin Colfer
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 496 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Fowl Twins, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780008324858

title: The Giver
author: Lois Lowry
description:
The Giver is Lois Lowry's classic dystopian novel and the first book of The Giver Quartet. Jonas lives in a community that appears perfect: there is no conflict, poverty or pain, families and jobs are assigned, and everyone follows the rules without question. Yet in removing suffering, Sameness has also removed choice.

At the Ceremony of Twelve, Jonas is singled out for a special role and begins training with an old man known as the Giver, who holds the memories of the past. As he discovers what his society has given up, Jonas faces a difficult decision. Thought-provoking and moving, it is a powerful read for teenagers and adults alike.

  • Author: Lois Lowry
  • Publisher: Clarion Books
  • Format: Paperback, 225 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Giver Quartet, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780544336261

title: The Great Cardio Myth
author: Craig Ballantyne
description:
The Great Cardio Myth is a fitness book by Craig Ballantyne arguing that long cardio sessions are an inefficient route to weight loss and good health. Drawing on research, he explains why hours of endurance exercise may not make people slimmer or stronger, and how it can put excessive strain on the heart, joints and muscles.

In its place he sets out a high-intensity strength training programme designed to deliver the same or better results in a fraction of the time of a typical cardio workout. Practical and direct, it suits busy readers who want to rethink their exercise habits and build fitness with shorter, more focused sessions.

  • Author: Craig Ballantyne
  • Publisher: Fair Winds Press
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781592337392

The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Vol. 10 continues Akira Himekawa's manga adaptation of the Nintendo game. Believing that total victory and the ruin of Hyrule are finally within reach, Ganondorf sends out his armies, and the struggle for both the land of light and the Twilight Realm reaches a decisive moment.

Link and Midna fight side by side with the many friends they have made on their journey, and even an old enemy joins their cause as Link pushes into the heart of Ganondorf's fortress for a showdown. Action-packed and emotional, it is a key volume for fans of the series and of the Zelda games.

  • Publisher: VIZ Media

The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Vol. 8 continues Akira Himekawa's manga version of the Nintendo adventure. Link and Midna, the Twilight Realm's princess, are on a quest to gather the scattered pieces of the Shadow Crystal before a dark force can use them to seize power over both worlds.

Link has the courage to face the trials ahead, but his swordsmanship needs sharpening, so he trains under a mysterious skeletal warrior who wanders through space and time. Midna, meanwhile, is more determined than ever to mend the Mirror of Shadow. Full of adventure and fantasy, it is ideal for Zelda fans and manga readers alike.

  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 200 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Volume 8
  • ISBN: 9781974719822

title: TURTLES ALL THE WAY DOWN
author: John Green
description:
Turtles All the Way Down is a young adult novel by John Green about friendship, love and living with mental illness. Sixteen-year-old Aza Holmes is doing her best as a daughter, friend and student while coping with spiralling, intrusive thoughts that she cannot switch off.

When fugitive billionaire Russell Pickett disappears and a large reward is offered for information, Aza and her fearless best friend Daisy decide to investigate, a hunt that brings Aza back into contact with Pickett's son, Davis. Tender, funny and honest about anxiety and OCD, it suits teenage and adult readers who enjoy thoughtful contemporary fiction.

  • Author: John Green
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 286 pages
  • Language: English

title: The Wolf Who Fell Out of a Book
sheet_title: Wolf Who Fell Out Of A Bo
author: Thierry Robberecht
description:
The Wolf Who Fell Out of a Book is a playful picture book by Thierry Robberecht, illustrated by Grégoire Mabire and first published in French. When a storybook drops to the floor, a wolf tumbles out of its pages and must find his way back into a story before a hungry cat catches him.

Leaping from one book to the next, he discovers that his pointed teeth and dark fur do not fit in everywhere, until he arrives in a tale where a girl in a red hood needs exactly his kind of character. With colourful artwork and an open ending that invites children to imagine what happens next, it is a delightful read-aloud.

  • Author: Thierry Robberecht
  • Illustrator: Grégoire Mabire
  • Publisher: Gibbs Smith
  • Format: Hardcover, 24 pages
  • Language: English

author: K.A. Holt
description:
House Arrest is a middle-grade novel in verse by K.A. Holt. Timothy made one serious mistake, and now he is serving a year of house arrest, checking in every week with a probation officer and a therapist and keeping the journal that forms this story.

Life at home is hard, and when Timothy feels he has to take drastic action to help his struggling family, staying out of trouble becomes far more complicated than he expected. Moving, funny and heartfelt, it is a story about responsibility, family and earning redemption, told in accessible verse that draws readers in.

  • Author: K.A. Holt
  • Publisher: Chronicle Books
  • Format: Paperback, 312 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: House Arrest, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781452156484

title: Love in the Palm of Your Hand
sheet_title: Love In The Palm Of Your
author: Ghanshyam Singh Birla
description:
Love in the Palm of Your Hand: How to Use Palmistry for Successful Relationships is an illustrated guide by Ghanshyam Singh Birla that applies the art of palm reading to love and compatibility. It draws on the ancient Indian tradition of hand analysis, which treats the palm as a living record of a person's character, thoughts and emotions.

Hundreds of illustrations help readers compare their own hands with those of partners, friends and family and match them to personality types, while an included palm-print kit lets readers take prints for closer study. Presented as a tool for understanding personality rather than fortune-telling, it suits anyone curious about palmistry and relationships.

  • Author: Ghanshyam Singh Birla
  • Publisher: Destiny Books
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780892817184

title: Siege And Storm
author: Leigh Bardugo
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)

description:
Siege and Storm is the second book in Leigh Bardugo's Shadow and Bone trilogy, set in the Grishaverse. On the run across the sea and troubled by what happened on the Fold, Alina and Mal try to start again in a foreign land, keeping secret the fact that she is the Sun Summoner.

But the Darkling is back, stronger and more dangerous than before, and with a daring privateer on her side Alina returns to Ravka to oppose him. As her power grows, she is drawn deeper into forbidden magic and must choose between her country, her ambitions and the people she loves. A gripping middle chapter for fans of romantic fantasy.

  • Author: Leigh Bardugo
  • Language: English
  • Series: Shadow and Bone Trilogy, Book 2 (Grishaverse)

title: Spy x Family Vol. 6
author: Tatsuya Endo
description:
Spy x Family, Vol. 6 continues Tatsuya Endo's comedy manga about a fake family hiding very real secrets. Elite spy Twilight must marry and raise a child to carry out his mission, never suspecting that his daughter Anya is a mind reader and his wife Yor works as an assassin.

In this volume Twilight teams up with fellow agent Nightfall to enter an underground tennis tournament, hoping to get hold of an intelligence document that could push the world towards war. The mission is complicated by Nightfall's secret feelings for Twilight. Packed with action, comedy and heart, it is a treat for fans of the series.

  • Author: Tatsuya Endo
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English

  • ISBN: 9781974725137

title: I Say Oh You Say No
sheet_title: I Say Oh You Say No
author: John Kane
description:
I Say Oh, You Say No is an interactive read-aloud picture book by John Kane, published by Templar. As its title suggests, it invites children to join in with the story by calling out their own responses as it is shared.

Designed to be read together, it suits parents, carers and teachers looking for a lively, participatory story time with young children.

  • Author: John Kane
  • Publisher: Templar Publishing
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800785120

title: Quests for Glory (The School for Good and Evil, Book 4)
sheet_title: Quest For Glory School For Good And Evil 4
author: Soman Chainani
description:
Quests for Glory is the fourth book in Soman Chainani's School for Good and Evil series and the first of The Camelot Years. With the wicked School Master defeated, Sophie, Agatha, Tedros and their classmates step beyond the school walls into a new era in the Endless Woods.

Every fourth-year student must now complete a quest, where success brings lasting fame and failure means being forgotten. Agatha and Tedros face the challenges awaiting them in Camelot, while Sophie takes on new responsibilities of her own. Full of magic, humour and unexpected dangers, it opens a fresh chapter for fans of the series.

  • Author: Soman Chainani
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 576 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The School for Good and Evil, Book 4 (The Camelot Years, Book 1)
  • ISBN: 9780008224479

title: Which Way To Anywhere
author: Cressida Cowell
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Which Way to Anywhere is the first book in a fantasy adventure series by Cressida Cowell, creator of How to Train Your Dragon. Twins K2 and Izzabird O'Hero have promised to keep their family's magical heritage a secret, even from their stepsiblings Theo and Mabel, who think K2 is utterly hopeless.

But K2 has a hidden talent: the maps he draws of extraordinary worlds turn out to be real. When their baby sister Annipeck is kidnapped, the feuding stepsiblings must work together and use his maps to cross into another world on a daring rescue mission. Inventive and funny, it suits young readers who love magical journeys.

  • Author: Cressida Cowell
  • Publisher: Hachette Children's Group
  • Language: English
  • Series: Which Way to Anywhere, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781444968217

title: The Escape
author: Ximo Abadía
description:
The Escape is a picture book written and illustrated by Ximo Abadía. Also published with the subtitle A Story of 103 Missing Monkeys, it centres on the disappearance of a whole troop of monkeys.

A visual story for sharing with young children, it suits families and teachers looking for a picture book with a playful premise.

  • Author: Ximo Abadía
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781787419308

title: The Little Book Of Breathwork
author: Jo Peters
description:
The Little Book of Breathwork by Jo Peters is a beginner's guide to using the breath to feel calmer, clearer and healthier. It explains the essentials of breathwork, which draws on meditation and mindfulness as well as ancient yoga and qigong traditions, and gives step-by-step instructions for exercises to try safely at home.

The practices are simple enough for anyone to start with and are aimed at easing stress and anxiety, sharpening focus and bringing a deeper sense of calm. Compact and easy to follow, it makes a useful first handbook for readers new to breathing techniques and a thoughtful gift.

  • Author: Jo Peters
  • Publisher: Summersdale
  • Format: Paperback, 128 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800077089

title: الحوار مع الأبناء علاج لكل داء
sheet_title: الحوار مع الأبناء علاج لكل داء
author: Ghada Hashad
description:
Written in Arabic, Dialogue with Children: A Cure for Every Ill (الحوار مع الأبناء علاج لكل داء) is a parenting book by Ghada Hashad about the power of open conversation between parents and children. It presents dialogue as a practical remedy for many of the difficulties families face as children grow.

The author blends insights from older and modern sciences with Quranic reflections and Islamic teachings, together with the experience of educators and practical lessons gathered across the Arab world and Europe. Covering the years from pregnancy to adulthood, it offers guidance for parents and carers who want a closer, healthier relationship with their children.

  • Author: Ghada Hashad
  • Publisher: Aseer Al Kotb
  • Format: Paperback, 200 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789779921617

title: الشغف
author: Barbara De Angelis
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Barbara De Angelis's Passion (الشغف), published by Dar Al Khayal. De Angelis is an American writer best known for her books on love, relationships and personal growth.

Listed under spirituality and personal growth, it suits Arabic readers interested in self-development and in her approach to living a more fulfilling, wholehearted life.

  • Author: Barbara De Angelis
  • Publisher: Dar Al Khayal
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953650937

title: النظام والكلام
author: Adonis
description:
Order and Speech (النظام والكلام) is an Arabic-language prose work by Adonis, the Syrian-born poet and critic regarded as one of the most influential figures in modern Arabic poetry and thought. It is published by Dar Al Adab in Beirut.

Adonis is known for his searching essays on Arab culture, tradition, religion and modernity, and this volume will interest readers who follow his thinking beyond his poetry, as well as students of contemporary Arab intellectual life.

  • Author: Adonis
  • Publisher: Dar Al Adab
  • Format: Paperback, 284 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953891309

title: عقل 24 قيراط
author: Kholoud Al-Ghafri
description:
Written in Arabic, A 24-Carat Mind (عقل 24 قيراط) is a self-development book by Kholoud Al-Ghafri addressed to women. Its central idea is that while many of us devote great effort to gold and possessions we will one day leave behind, the one treasure we truly carry with us, the mind, is too often neglected.

The author guides readers through seven "investments" designed to burn away the impurities that weigh down their thinking, refining the mind step by step until it returns to its purest state. Encouraging and reflective, it suits readers looking for a faith-aware approach to personal growth and inner clarity.

  • Author: Kholoud Al-Ghafri
  • Publisher: Aseer Al Kotb
  • Format: Paperback, 168 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789776902015

title: عمارة السعادة
author: Alain de Botton
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Alain de Botton's The Architecture of Happiness (عمارة السعادة), translated by Al-Harith Al-Nabhan. In it, de Botton explores the subtle but powerful links between the buildings we live in and our long-term sense of wellbeing.

He asks what makes a home truly beautiful, why so much new building feels unappealing, and why people argue so passionately about sofas and paintings. Ranging from medieval timber cottages to modern towers, and from cathedrals to office blocks and tea sets, he offers surprising philosophical insights. It is an engaging read for anyone interested in architecture, design and philosophy.

  • Author: Alain de Botton
  • Translator: Al-Harith Al-Nabhan
  • Publisher: Dar Al Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 317 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144721742

title: المسير الأطول في التاريخ
author: George Meegan
description:
The Longest Walk in History (المسير الأطول في التاريخ) is the Arabic translation of British adventurer George Meegan's account of crossing the Americas entirely on foot. Translated by Ziad Tarek, with an introduction by Dr Huda Al-Qudah, it is published in Jordan by Alaan.

Meegan set out from Tierra del Fuego at the southern tip of the continent and walked north through country after country, including Argentina, Peru, Colombia, Central America, Mexico and the United States, all the way to Alaska, earning a place in Guinness World Records. It is a gripping read about ambition, endurance and the people and dangers met along the way.

  • Author: George Meegan
  • Translator: Ziad Tarek
  • Publisher: Alaan Publishers
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789923131589

title: سنوات الجرى فى المكان
author: Nora Nagi
description:
Years of Running in Place (سنوات الجري في المكان) is an Arabic-language novel by the Egyptian writer Nora Nagi. Set between a revolution and a pandemic, it follows five artists who try to move forward with their lives, only to find that time has stalled for them after one of their friends is lost in the square.

Struggling with grief, they cling to art, love and the small details that make up everyday life as a way of reclaiming their senses. Shaped by the aftermath of Egypt's January uprising, it is a moving contemporary novel for readers of modern Arabic fiction.

  • Author: Nora Nagi
  • Publisher: Dar El Shorouk
  • Format: Paperback, 265 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789770938010

The Peacock's Eye (عين الطاووس) is a novel in Arabic by the Lebanese writer Hanan Al-Shaykh, published by Dar Al-Adab in Beirut.

Al-Shaykh is one of the most widely read and translated Arab novelists, known for frank, vivid storytelling and for her portraits of women's lives and of Lebanese society. This edition will suit readers who enjoy contemporary Arabic literary fiction.

  • Author: Hanan Al-Shaykh
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Adab
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953897349

title: Where The Wild Things Are
author: Maurice Sendak
description:
Where the Wild Things Are is Maurice Sendak's classic picture book about imagination, mischief and coming home. After causing chaos in his wolf suit, Max is sent to bed without any supper, and in his bedroom a forest grows and an ocean appears, carrying him away to the land of the Wild Things.

Rather than eating him, the fearsome creatures crown Max their king and join him in a wild rumpus, until he begins to long for home and the people who love him. With its unforgettable illustrations and spare, rhythmic text, it remains a cherished read-aloud for young children and a treasured gift for families.

  • Author: Maurice Sendak
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 48 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780064431781

title: الرجل النمرة
author: Eka Kurniawan

description:
Man Tiger (الرجل النمرة) is the Arabic translation of Indonesian novelist Eka Kurniawan's Lelaki Harimau, translated by Ahmed Shafie. Set in a small coastal community, it reveals both a brutal killing and the young man responsible at the very start, then works its way back to explain how it came about.

Drawing on Indonesian myth, including the idea of a tiger spirit dwelling inside a man, Kurniawan blends magical realism with dark humour and sharp social observation. Compact and intense, it suits readers who enjoyed his novel Beauty Is a Wound and anyone drawn to bold, myth-infused fiction from Asia.

  • Author: Eka Kurniawan
  • Translator: Ahmed Shafie
  • Publisher: Al Kotob Khan
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778031041

title: الطريقة الأكثر فاعلية لإنجاز المهام
author: Damon Zahariades
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Damon Zahariades's productivity guide To-Do List Formula, published in Arabic as The Most Effective Way to Get Things Done (الطريقة الأكثر فاعلية لإنجاز المهام) and translated by Rasheda Ragab. It promises a stress-free method for writing task lists that actually work.

Zahariades looks at eight popular list-making approaches and explains why they fall short, highlights ten common mistakes people make when planning their tasks, and shows how to build a practical, achievable daily list. It suits professionals who struggle with deadlines, students organising their studies, and anyone juggling home and work commitments.

  • Author: Damon Zahariades
  • Translator: Rasheda Ragab
  • Publisher: Dar Dawen
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778062496

title: بحثاً عن كرة الصوف
author: Rosa Yassin Hassan
description:
In Search of the Ball of Wool (بحثًا عن كرة الصوف) is an Arabic-language novel by the Syrian writer Rosa Yassin Hassan. Its central image is the ball of wool that guides each exile through the labyrinth of life abroad: some have lost theirs and drift, some search for it obsessively, and a lucky few hold on to it calmly.

Set beneath the sky of Hamburg, the novel observes clashes between left and right, the city's homeless and its late-night bars, and the divide between wealthy districts and the neighbourhoods of migrants and refugees. It is a perceptive read on exile, identity and belonging in contemporary Europe.

  • Author: Rosa Yassin Hassan
  • Publisher: Riad El-Rayyes Books
  • Format: Paperback, 283 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953217499

title: Shusmo
author: Khaled ElAhmad
description:
Shusmo (شسمو) is an Arabic-language book by Khaled ElAhmad that tells the story of his own journey through the digital transformation. Its title is a colloquial Arabic expression meaning roughly "what's it called".

ElAhmad describes how he used social media to build a personal brand that helped him navigate life, sharing stories from Kuwait, Algeria, the United States and Jordan. He compares how each social platform differs and closes by examining the serious implications of big data and the economy of attention and emotion that drives social networks.

  • Author: Khaled ElAhmad
  • Publisher: Khaled ElAhmad
  • Format: Paperback, 128 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9781785820687

title: عم نتحدث حين نتحدث عن الصداقة
sheet_title: عم نتحدث حين نتحدث عن الصداقة
author: Bilal Alaa
description:
What We Talk About When We Talk About Friendship (عم نتحدث حين نتحدث عن الصداقة) is an Arabic-language novel by Bilal Alaa. Its narrator escapes his troubles by retreating into the homes of his friends and into his own memories.

Through this journey, the novel reflects on the presence and absence of friends, how friendships are formed, how they last or fall apart, and whether it is possible to truly connect with another person amid the tangles of reality, language and memory. It is a thoughtful, introspective read for lovers of contemporary Arabic fiction.

  • Author: Bilal Alaa
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789779445939

title: مقولات في فلسفة الدين على ضوء إلهيات المعرفة
sheet_title: مقولات في فلسفة الدين على ضوء إلهيات المعرفة
author: Shafiq Jaradi
description:
Propositions in the Philosophy of Religion in Light of the Theology of Knowledge (مقولات في فلسفة الدين على ضوء إلهيات المعرفة) is an Arabic-language work of philosophy by Shafiq Jaradi. It argues that the philosophy of religion has often claimed to speak for all civilisations while seeing the human being only partially, leaving aside deeper dimensions of human experience.

As an alternative, the author develops the project of a "theology of religious knowledge", re-examining the foundations of knowledge itself in order to restore what has been excluded and to understand the human being more fully. It is a demanding study for readers and students of philosophy, theology and religious thought.

  • Author: Shafiq Jaradi
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Maaref Al-Hikmiya
  • Format: Paperback, 435 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144400401

title: The Little Book Of Angels
author: Sophie Golding
description:
The Little Book of Angels by Sophie Golding is a compact introduction to the world of angels and the idea of spiritual guidance. Written for readers who have sensed a presence watching over them or experienced something they cannot explain, it explores angels in their many forms and how they are believed to communicate.

The book suggests ways to strengthen a connection with these messengers, interpret their signs and draw on their guidance to bring more peace, positivity and purpose to daily life. Pocket-sized and gentle in tone, it suits newcomers to angel lore and makes a thoughtful gift for spiritually curious friends.

  • Author: Sophie Golding
  • Publisher: Summersdale
  • Format: Paperback, 128 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800076945

title: الثقة
author: Barbara De Angelis
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Barbara De Angelis's Confidence: Finding It and Living It, published in Arabic as Confidence (الثقة). In this short book, De Angelis argues that most people misunderstand what confidence really means, and so never experience the deep, lasting kind they truly need.

She sets out a fresh way of thinking about self-trust and how to find it, presenting ideas that may differ from anything readers have heard before. Concise and encouraging, it suits anyone hoping to build inner confidence and carry it into every area of life.

  • Author: Barbara De Angelis
  • Publisher: Dar Al Khayal
  • Format: Paperback, 95 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953651569

title: THE SHINING
author: Stephen King
description:
The Shining is Stephen King's classic horror novel of isolation and haunting. Jack Torrance takes a job as winter caretaker of the remote Overlook Hotel in the Colorado mountains, moving in with his wife, Wendy, and their five-year-old son, Danny, who has a powerful psychic gift known as the shining.

As snowstorms cut the family off from the outside world, the hotel seems to come alive, its ghosts pressing in on Danny and slowly working on his father's fragile mind. Atmospheric, terrifying and deeply human, it is essential reading for horror fans, and its story continues in the sequel Doctor Sleep.

  • Author: Stephen King
  • Publisher: Hodder & Stoughton
  • Format: Paperback, 497 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Shining, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781444720723

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Brave New World is Aldous Huxley's classic dystopian novel, first published in 1932. It imagines a future World State where people are produced in laboratories, conditioned from birth to fit a rigid caste system and kept content with consumer pleasures and a drug called soma, so that stability is valued above everything, including freedom and individuality.

When an outsider raised beyond the borders of this society is brought into it, his reactions expose the emptiness beneath its comfort. Sharp, unsettling and still strikingly relevant, the novel raises lasting questions about technology, control and happiness, and is a cornerstone of science fiction for students and general readers alike.

  • Author: Aldous Huxley
  • Language: English

title: Hilda And The Bird Parade Graphic Novel
sheet_title: Hilda And The Bird Parade Graphic Novel
author: Luke Pearson
description:
Hilda and the Bird Parade is the third of Luke Pearson's Hilda graphic novels. Having moved with her mother from the wild countryside to the busy city of Trolberg, Hilda misses her magical friends and the wonders of her old home and is struggling to settle in.

On the day of the city's bird parade, though, she catches a glimpse of the magic she thought she had left behind, and an unexpected adventure begins. With Pearson's charming artwork and gentle humour, it is a lovely read for young fans of the Hilda books and the Netflix animated series they inspired.

  • Author: Luke Pearson
  • Publisher: Flying Eye Books
  • Format: Paperback, 48 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Hilda, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781911171027

title: Men Without Women
author: Ernest Hemingway
description:
Men Without Women is Ernest Hemingway's second collection of short stories, first published in 1927. Written in his famously spare style, the stories return to subjects that fascinated him, among them bullfighting and boxing, broken marriages, infidelity and death.

The collection includes some of his best-known short fiction, such as "The Killers", "Hills Like White Elephants" and "In Another Country", which helped establish his reputation as a master of the form. This Vintage Classics edition is a fine introduction to Hemingway for new readers and a rewarding collection for anyone who loves classic American literature.

  • Author: Ernest Hemingway
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593468845

title: Skill Sharpeners Grammar and Punctuation Grade 1
sheet_title: Skill Sharpeners Grammar and Punctuation Grade 1
author: Evan-Moor Educational Publishers
description:
Skill Sharpeners: Grammar and Punctuation, Grade 1 is a full-colour activity workbook from Evan-Moor Educational Publishers that helps young children build the language skills they need for reading and writing. It introduces core ideas such as nouns, verbs, sentence structure, subjects and predicates through clear examples.

Riddles, word games and real-world practice keep learning fun, while a language handbook offers a handy reference. Designed for extra practice at home or for homeschooling, it is a useful resource for parents and teachers who want to reinforce classroom learning in short, manageable sessions.

  • Publisher: Evan-Moor Educational Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Skill Sharpeners
  • ISBN: 9781629388694

title: Suddenly A Murder
author: Lauren Muñoz
description:
Suddenly a Murder is a young adult murder mystery by Lauren Muñoz with a glamorous 1920s twist. To celebrate the end of high school, Izzy Morales and her best friend Kassidy head off with a group of friends for a lavish, Roaring Twenties-themed weekend at the grand Ashwood Manor, complete with vintage gowns and diamonds.

The party ends abruptly when Kassidy's boyfriend is found dead, and with a storm trapping everyone on the island alongside two detectives, the guests become suspects. Everyone has secrets, and Izzy is the one who brought a knife. Twisty and atmospheric, it suits readers who love classic whodunits with a modern edge.

  • Author: Lauren Muñoz
  • Publisher: Hot Key Books
  • Format: Paperback, 308 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781471414237

title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time
sheet_title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time
author: Mark Haddon
description:
The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time is Mark Haddon's novel narrated by Christopher Boone, a fifteen-year-old with a remarkable gift for maths and very little understanding of other people. When he finds his neighbour's dog, Wellington, dead on the lawn one night, he resolves to find out who killed it, just like his hero Sherlock Holmes.

His investigation leads to unexpected discoveries about his own family and sends him on a daring journey far beyond his comfort zone. Funny, moving and told in a completely original voice, it is a modern classic enjoyed by teenagers and adults alike.

  • Author: Mark Haddon
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784707637

title: The Land of Stories: An Author's Odyssey
sheet_title: The Land Of Stories An Author'S Odyssey
author: Chris Colfer
vendor: Little, Brown Books for Young Readers
description:
The Land of Stories: An Author's Odyssey is the fifth book in Chris Colfer's fantasy adventure series about twins Alex and Conner Bailey and the fairy-tale world they discovered. The sinister Masked Man has raised an army of literary villains, and the twins must find a way to stop him.

Conner realises the only place to fight back is inside his own short stories, so the twins and their friends step into worlds born from his imagination, meeting allies no one could have predicted. Packed with humour, heart and inventive twists, it is a treat for fans as the series heads towards its finale.

  • Author: Chris Colfer
  • Publisher: Little, Brown Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Paperback, 438 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Land of Stories, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9780349132273

title: The Palestinian-Israeli Conflict A Very Short Introduction
sheet_title: The Palestinian-Israeli Conflict A Very Short Introduction
author: Martin Bunton
description:
The Palestinian-Israeli Conflict: A Very Short Introduction by historian Martin Bunton offers a concise, accessible account of one of the most bitter and closely watched disputes of modern times. Rather than telling the story as a single narrative, Bunton divides the history into twenty-year periods to show how the conflict has changed across successive generations.

Each chapter opens with the people and events that made particular years turning points, beginning with the 1897 Zionist Congress in Basel and the 1917 Balfour Declaration. Clear and compact, it is an ideal starting point for students and general readers seeking to understand the history behind the headlines.

  • Author: Martin Bunton
  • Publisher: Oxford University Press
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Very Short Introductions, No. 359
  • ISBN: 9780199603930

title: The Twits
author: Roald Dahl
description:
The Twits is Roald Dahl's gleefully revolting story about the nastiest married couple imaginable, illustrated by Quentin Blake. Mr and Mrs Twit are grubby, ugly and spiteful, and they spend their days playing horrible tricks on each other, trapping birds for their Bird Pie and making the monkeys they keep caged stand upside down.

Fed up with their cruel owners, the monkeys team up with the Roly-Poly Bird to plot a brilliant revenge. Short, funny and wonderfully disgusting, it is a perfect read-aloud and an ideal first Dahl book for young readers.

The book explains why the face you present at work should differ from your personal posts, with practical advice on polishing an online CV, taking part in industry groups and showcasing products and services on platforms such as Instagram. Easy to dip into during a commute or lunch break, it suits professionals who want to use social media confidently and appropriately.

Violeta is a sweeping historical novel by Isabel Allende that spans a century in the life of one remarkable woman. Violeta del Valle is born during a storm in 1920, the first daughter after five sons, just as the Spanish flu reaches her South American homeland in the aftermath of the First World War.

Her family survives the pandemic, only to lose everything in the Great Depression and retreat to a wild, remote part of the country where Violeta comes of age. Told as her own account of a life shaped by love, loss, political upheaval and resilience, it is a rich, absorbing read for lovers of literary and historical fiction.

  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages

This is the Arabic edition of Paulo Coelho's Maktub (مكتوب), translated by Rana Al-Saifi. Rather than a single narrative, the book gathers dozens of brief stories and scenes, some drawn from the author's own experience or things he heard, others from the folklore, legends and cultures of the world.

Each piece is told in just a few concentrated lines, offering a moment of reflection or a lesson for daily life. Easy to dip into, it suits readers who enjoy Coelho's spiritual, inspirational writing and those looking for short daily reflections.

Haaland is part of the Ultimate Football Heroes series by Matt Oldfield, a range of biographies written for young football fans. It tells the story of Norwegian striker Erling Haaland, following his journey from a football-mad child to one of the most feared goalscorers in Europe.

Written in a fast-paced, easy-to-follow style, the book shows how talent, hard work and determination helped him rise to the top of the game. It is a good choice for young readers who love football and want to know more about the players they watch, and a fun way to encourage reluctant readers.

Hedda Gabler and Other Plays gathers three major dramas by the Norwegian playwright Henrik Ibsen in a Penguin Classics edition introduced by Una Ellis-Fermor. Alongside Hedda Gabler it includes The Pillars of the Community and The Wild Duck, plays in which Ibsen examines private and public morality and the slippery nature of truth.

In one, a shipowner protects his standing by letting another man carry the blame for his own past; in another, an idealist's insistence on honesty wrecks a household; and in the title play, a restless woman trapped in a conventional marriage drives events towards tragedy. An ideal edition for students of theatre and for readers exploring the roots of modern drama.

Hilda and the Midnight Giant is the second of Luke Pearson's Hilda graphic novels, starring a fearless, blue-haired girl who happily befriends even the strangest visitors to her home. This time her house comes under siege from a crowd of tiny creatures who pelt it with stones and deliver notices telling her family to leave.

Then, once the sun goes down, a towering giant starts to appear at midnight, and Hilda seems to be the only person who can see him. With Pearson's distinctive artwork, gentle humour and a story rooted in folklore and friendship, it is a charming comic adventure for young readers and for anyone who enjoys imaginative graphic novels.

She Is a Haunting is a gothic young adult horror novel by Trang Thanh Tran. Jade Nguyen travels to Vietnam to spend five weeks with her estranged father, who is restoring an old French colonial house, and she intends to play the happy daughter just long enough to secure the money for college he has offered her.

The house, however, seems to want something from her family. Jade wakes unable to move, insects turn up where they do not belong, and the ghost of a bride whispers warnings to her at night. A layered, atmospheric story about identity, family secrets and colonial history, it will appeal to readers who like their horror unsettling and full of meaning.

Skill Sharpeners: STEAM, Grade 5 is a full-colour Evan-Moor workbook that asks fifth graders to apply science, technology, engineering, art and maths to challenges drawn from everyday life. Each unit pairs a reading passage with a hands-on project, such as designing an activity kit for days spent indoors, preparing a persuasive talk for a town council, or decorating fundraiser T-shirts. Beyond the Kingdoms is the fourth book in Chris Colfer's The Land of Stories series. The mysterious Masked Man is at large in the fairy-tale world, and twins Alex and Conner Bailey are the only ones who see the danger, especially now that Alex has been removed from the Fairy Council.

With help from Goldilocks, Jack, Red Riding Hood and Mother Goose, the twins learn that he holds a potion able to turn any book into a gateway, and that he is recruiting the most notorious villains in literature. The chase takes them through Oz, Neverland and Wonderland, making this a lively, imaginative adventure for middle-grade readers who love classic tales with a twist.

  • Format: Paperback, 448 pages

author: Yaa Gyasi
description:
Transcendent Kingdom is the second novel by Yaa Gyasi, author of Homegoing. Gifty grew up in Alabama hearing how her parents left Ghana in search of a better life, but her family shrinks to just her and her mother after her father leaves and her brother is lost to opioid addiction.

Now a neuroscience researcher, Gifty turns to science to understand addiction and depression, even as her grieving mother comes to stay with her. Moving between the lab, the church of her childhood and her family's past, the novel is a quiet, searching story about faith, science, grief and love, ideal for book clubs and readers of thoughtful literary fiction.

  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 248 pages
  • Language: English

title: Homegoing
author: Yaa Gyasi
description:
Homegoing is the debut novel by Yaa Gyasi, a sweeping work of historical fiction that begins with two half-sisters born in eighteenth-century Ghana. Effia is married to a British slaver and lives in comfort at Cape Coast Castle, while Esi is imprisoned in its dungeons and shipped across the Atlantic into slavery.

Each chapter follows a descendant of one of the two women, carrying the story through seven generations from the Gold Coast to the plantations of Mississippi, the coal mines of Alabama and the jazz clubs of Harlem. Wide in scope yet deeply personal, it traces how the legacy of slavery shapes families on both sides of the ocean, and makes a powerful choice for book groups.

  • Author: Yaa Gyasi
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241975237

title: If Tomorrow Doesn't Come
author: Jen St. Jude
description:
If Tomorrow Doesn't Come is a young adult love story by Jen St. Jude, set in the last days before the end of the world. On the very morning Avery Byrne has planned to take her own life, news breaks that an asteroid will strike Earth in nine days and nothing can be done to stop it.

As the countdown runs and long-held secrets surface, Avery fights to get home to the girl she has loved all her life, and to find a reason to hope for whatever time remains. A tender, emotional story about first love, mental health and courage, it suits readers who enjoy heartfelt queer romance.

  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English

title: Leave The World Behind
author: Rumaan Alam
description:
Leave the World Behind is a tense, unsettling novel by Rumaan Alam. Amanda and Clay rent a luxurious holiday home in a quiet corner of Long Island, hoping for a restful week with their two teenagers, until a knock late at night brings an older couple, Ruth and G. H., to the door, saying that the house belongs to them.

They report that a blackout has struck New York City, but with no phone signal, television or internet, nobody can confirm what is really happening. As the two families decide whether to trust each other, the novel builds a quiet dread while probing class, race, parenthood and the fragility of modern comforts. Ideal for readers who like literary fiction with a thriller's edge.

  • Author: Rumaan Alam
  • Publisher: Ecco
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English

author: Patrice Lawrence

Orangeboy is a gripping young adult thriller by Patrice Lawrence, set in London. Sixteen-year-old Marlon has promised his widowed mum that he will stay out of trouble and never turn out like his brother Andre, a gang leader, and he keeps his head down with his late dad's old records and his favourite science fiction.

Everything changes when his first date with Sonya ends in tragedy and Marlon finds himself hunted without knowing why. To uncover the truth and protect the people closest to him, he is pulled into the dangerous world his brother once ruled, with its weapons and drug deals. A fast, tense story about family, loyalty and growing up under pressure.

  • Publisher: Hodder Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English

Our Violent Ends by Chloe Gong is the second and final book in the duology that began with These Violent Delights, a reimagining of Romeo and Juliet set in 1920s Shanghai. Juliette Cai, heir to the Scarlet Gang, and Roma Montagov, heir to the rival White Flowers, are once again caught up in the feud between their families as fresh danger grips the city.

Blending a vivid historical setting, gang rivalry, a supernatural menace and a doomed romance, the novel brings the story of the two lovers to its conclusion. It is a dramatic choice for young adult readers who enjoy dark fantasy, retellings of classic stories and romance with very high stakes.

It suits parents looking for meaningful practice at home as well as teachers wanting ready-made enrichment, and it comes with access to a downloadable teaching guide.

title: The End Of The World Is A Cul De Sac

The End of the World is a Cul de Sac is the debut short story collection from Irish writer Louise Kennedy, whose stories show how private lives become entangled in wider political and national events. Among its characters are Sarah, left alone by her partner in a newly built house, and Orla, who must judge a contest at the local fete while coping with her husband's odd act of revenge.

Others include Peter, who brings up his daughter in remote rural isolation. Kennedy began writing at forty-seven, and her prose has a clarity and hard-won wisdom that make these stories of ordinary people under pressure quietly powerful. A fine choice for readers of literary short fiction and contemporary Irish writing.

  • Author: Louise Kennedy
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English

title: The Land of Stories: The Enchantress Returns : Book 2

The Enchantress Returns is the second book in Chris Colfer's The Land of Stories series. Twins Alex and Conner Bailey discover that the wicked Enchantress is back in the fairy-tale world, and she has kidnapped their mother in order to pressure their grandmother, the Fairy Godmother.

To rescue her, the twins must cross through a portal once more and hunt for a rare and powerful artefact, the Wand of Wonder, travelling to some of the most feared corners of the magical land. Packed with familiar fairy-tale characters, humour and peril, it is a page-turning adventure for middle-grade readers.

  • Publisher: Little, Brown Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Paperback, 519 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Land of Stories, Book 2

title: The Paris Apartment

The Paris Apartment is a twisty mystery thriller by Lucy Foley, set in a grand old apartment building on the rue des Amants, well away from the tourist sights of Paris. When Jess arrives to stay with her half-brother Ben, he is nowhere to be found, and she begins to suspect that his neighbours know more than they admit.

The residents, from the watchful concierge to a jilted lover, a nosy journalist, an innocent-seeming student and an unwelcome guest, all hide secrets of their own. Told from shifting points of view, the story moves at a brisk pace towards its reveals, making it a good pick for fans of closed-circle mysteries and psychological suspense.

  • Author: Lucy Foley
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008385071

title: The Valkyries
author: Paulo Coelho
description:
The Valkyries is Paulo Coelho's account of a journey he made with his wife, Cristina, through the Mojave Desert. It begins in Rio de Janeiro, where Coelho hands the only manuscript of The Alchemist to his enigmatic teacher, J., and admits that his dreams always seem to collapse just before they come true.

To lift this curse, J. sets him a daunting task: he must make contact with his guardian angel. The couple leave everything behind for forty days in the desert, where they encounter a band of women riders known as the Valkyries. Part adventure and part spiritual quest, it explores forgiveness, faith and trust in the future, for readers of Coelho's reflective, mystical writing.

  • Author: Paulo Coelho
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 245 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780722533949

title: Trespasses
author: Louise Kennedy

Trespasses is the first novel by Louise Kennedy, set in Northern Ireland during the Troubles. Cushla lives quietly with her mother in a small town outside Belfast, teaching at a Catholic primary school by day and working shifts in the family pub at night, where she meets Michael Agnew, an older, married Protestant barrister known for defending IRA members.

Against her better judgement, the two begin an affair. Then the father of one of her pupils is brutally attacked, setting off events that endanger everyone Cushla cares about. Tender and unflinching, it is a powerful story of love and divided loyalties in a place where background can count for more than character, ideal for book clubs.

  • Author: Louise Kennedy
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury
  • Format: Paperback, 311 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781526623362

author: Frances Hardinge

Unraveller is a dark young adult fantasy by Frances Hardinge, set in a land where any person may lay a curse capable of ruining someone else's life. Kellen is the only one known to be able to undo such curses, though his own gift remains something of a mystery to him.

He travels with Nettle, a girl he freed after she had been cursed into the shape of a bird and who has become his closest ally. But Kellen carries a curse of his own, and unless the pair can lift it, his power could start unravelling everything and everyone around him. Inventive and atmospheric, it suits readers who enjoy rich, unusual fantasy worlds.

  • Author: Frances Hardinge
  • Publisher: Macmillan Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 481 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529081411

Yoga of Light by Pauline Wills is a practical guide to working with the body's energy centres through yoga. It explains how energy lines running between the major and minor chakras form triangles of light, and how becoming aware of them during practice can energise the body and deepen a sense of inner light.

The book introduces ten major and twenty-one minor chakras and offers illustrated, step-by-step guidance on the postures, showing which triangles each pose activates and the health benefits it brings. Rooted in yoga's original teachings, it suits practitioners and teachers who want to bring an energetic and spiritual dimension to their asana practice.

  • Author: Pauline Wills
  • Publisher: Findhorn Press
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781620559444

title: How to Build a Better Pie

How to Build a Better Pie is a baking book by Millicent Souris, gathering sweet and savoury recipes along with advice on flaky pastry, toppings and fillings. It is written for home cooks who love the idea of pie but feel nervous about rolling out dough and getting fillings to behave.

Souris walks readers through the techniques behind a reliable crust, then moves on to fillings, from fruit pies that set properly to smooth custards and well-browned meringues, alongside savoury options. Clear and encouraging, it suits beginners and keen bakers who want to make pies with confidence.

  • Author: Millicent Souris
  • Publisher: Quarry Books
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781592537969

author: Derek Keilty

Ivy Newt and the Storm Witch is the first book in Derek Keilty's illustrated chapter book series for ages 5 to 7, with pictures by Magda Brol. Ivy is a determined young witch whose parents, the King and Queen of the Sand Witches, plan a spectacular birthday surprise for her: a magic act in which they vanish.

The trouble is that they really do disappear. To bring them back, Ivy and Tom, her loyal familiar, travel across the land of Miracula by broomstick and flying carpet, making new friends along the way as they set out to defeat Clawdelia Thorn, the wicked Queen of Grotland. A lively, funny adventure for newly confident readers.

description:
Mythos is Stephen Fry's lively retelling of the myths of ancient Greece and the first book in his Great Mythology series. Starting at the very beginning, with the emergence of the world from Chaos, it follows the rise of the Titans and the Olympian gods and the many stories of love, rivalry and mischief that surround them.

Fry respects the original tales while telling them in a warm, witty and modern voice, adding context about the words and ideas the myths have left behind. Accessible to newcomers and rewarding for readers who already know the stories, it is a great introduction to Greek mythology.

  • Author: Stephen Fry
  • Language: English
  • Series: Stephen Fry's Great Mythology, Book 1

title: Superfood Weeknight Meals
author: Kelly Pfeiffer

Superfood Weeknight Meals by Kelly Pfeiffer is a cookbook of healthy family dinners designed to reach the table in half an hour or less. It is built around ten everyday superfoods: quinoa, lentils, eggs, spinach, sweet potatoes, avocado, almonds, cauliflower, citrus fruit and olive oil.

Every recipe uses at least two of these ingredients, so busy cooks can serve something nourishing without hours in the kitchen, even when feeding fussy eaters. Simple yet creative, it is a helpful book for parents and for anyone who wants quick, wholesome food that the whole family will enjoy on a weeknight.

  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages

A Grimm Warning is the third book in Chris Colfer's The Land of Stories series. Conner Bailey believes his adventures in the fairy-tale world are behind him, until he comes across a message left two hundred years ago by the Brothers Grimm, warning that the Grande Armée plans to invade the Land of Stories.

With his twin sister Alex training as the next Fairy Godmother, Conner must work out what the warning means and gather help before it is too late. Mixing real history with classic fairy-tale characters, the book continues the series' blend of humour, magic and adventure for middle-grade readers.

  • Publisher: Hachette Children's Group
  • Format: Paperback, 470 pages
  • Language: English

You Made a Fool of Death With Your Beauty is a contemporary romance by Akwaeke Emezi. Feyi Adeola, a young artist who lost her husband five years ago, is slowly learning to live again when she is offered the chance to swap the heat of the city for an idyllic island holiday of poolside drinks, beach sunsets and lavish meals.

As she opens her heart again, Feyi finds herself drawn to the one man who is completely off limits. Sensual and emotional, the novel explores grief, desire, art and second chances, and is a good choice for readers who like romance with real depth and complicated choices.

  • Author: Akwaeke Emezi
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571372683

The Richest Man in Babylon is George S. Clason's classic guide to personal finance, told through a series of parables set in ancient Babylon. First published in the 1920s, the stories follow characters such as Arkad, a wealthy Babylonian who explains how he built his fortune, to illustrate simple, lasting rules for handling money.

Its lessons centre on thrift, paying yourself first by saving part of everything you earn, avoiding debt, investing wisely and protecting what you have. Written in plain, almost biblical language, it remains an approachable introduction to financial planning for young adults, first-time earners and anyone wanting to take control of their money.

title: Ivy Newt And The Time Thief
sheet_title: Ivy Newt And The Time Thief
author: Derek Keilty

Ivy Newt and the Time Thief is the second book in Derek Keilty's illustrated Ivy Newt series, set in the magical world of Miracula, with pictures by Magda Brol. Once a year, as the sun rises on Halloween, a spooky house materialises near Newt Castle, only to fade away when midnight strikes.

Ivy and Tom set out to discover why, and soon uncover a witch held captive, a mighty sorcerer and a curse that must be lifted before time runs out. Fast-paced and full of dramatic black-and-white illustrations, it is a spooky, fun adventure for children who are growing in confidence as readers.

  • Publisher: Scallywag Press
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English

author: Bahaa Taher

Love in Exile (الحب في المنفى) is a novel in Arabic by the Egyptian writer Bahaa Taher. Its narrator is a middle-aged Egyptian journalist, divorced and sidelined at home, who works as a correspondent in an unnamed European city, where he falls in love with Brigitte, a young Austrian woman.

Their relationship unfolds against the backdrop of the 1982 Israeli invasion of Lebanon and the Sabra and Shatila massacre, as the narrator confronts political disillusionment, the fading of his old ideals and the meaning of exile. Measured and deeply humane, it is a rewarding read for anyone interested in modern Egyptian and Arabic fiction.

  • Author: Bahaa Taher
  • Publisher: Dar El Shorouk
  • Format: Paperback, 314 pages
  • Language: Arabic
