description:
The Good Life (العيش الطيب) is a book in Arabic by Abdullah Al-Hashemi. Its title, which can also be rendered as Living Well, points to the idea of a good and wholesome way of living.

  • Author: Abdullah Al-Hashemi
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953651200

title: المشروع الوطني الفلسطيني: تطوره ومأزقه ومصائره
sheet_title: المشروع الوطني الفلسطيني: تطوره ومأزقه ومصائره
author: Maher Al-Sharif
description:
The Palestinian National Project: Its Development, Impasse and Fate (المشروع الوطني الفلسطيني: تطوره ومأزقه ومصائره) is a study in Arabic by historian Maher Al-Sharif, published by the Institute for Palestine Studies. It traces how the project took shape with the founding of Fatah in the late 1950s, after years of political uncertainty under the British Mandate.

The book follows its shift from liberation and return towards independence in a state in the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza, and then to a wager on a transitional period of self-rule whose failure led to today's deadlock. Treating ideas as products of their time, Al-Sharif asks why the national movement has not reached its goals.

  • Author: Maher Al-Sharif
  • Publisher: Institute for Palestine Studies
  • Format: 370 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144480939

title: آن فى المرتفعات الخضراء
author: L.M. Montgomery
description:
This is the Arabic edition of L.M. Montgomery's classic Anne of Green Gables (آن في المرتفعات الخضراء), translated by Inas Samir. Elderly siblings Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert decide to adopt a boy to help on their farm in Avonlea, on Prince Edward Island, but by mistake a talkative, red-haired orphan girl named Anne Shirley arrives instead.

Anne's warm heart, vivid imagination and talent for getting into scrapes gradually win over the Cuthberts and the whole community as she grows up, makes a lifelong friend in Diana Barry and finds her place in the world. A timeless coming-of-age story about belonging, friendship and imagination, ideal for young readers and families.

  • Author: L.M. Montgomery
  • Translator: Inas Samir
  • Publisher: Aseer Al Kotb
  • Format: Paperback, 452 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Anne of Green Gables, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9789778581058

title: تحكم في أصوات عقلك
author: Jon Acuff
description:
Control the Voices in Your Mind (تحكم في أصوات عقلك) is the Arabic edition of Jon Acuff's Soundtracks, his book on a surprising way to overcome overthinking, translated by Omar Fathi. It is aimed at anyone who spends their days replaying the past, worrying about the future or rehearsing problems before they arrive.

Acuff argues that overthinking is not a fixed trait but a habit of listening to unhelpful inner soundtracks, and shows how to quieten the discouraging voices that stall progress and replace them with more useful ones. Practical and upbeat, it suits readers who want to stop second-guessing themselves and put their thinking to better use.

  • Author: Jon Acuff
  • Translator: Omar Fathi
  • Publisher: Dar Dawen
  • Format: Paperback, 238 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778063271

title: صغر عقلك
author: Moataz Meshal
description:
Shrink Your Mind (صغر عقلك) is a self-development book in Arabic by Moataz Meshal. Starting from the idea that every person is born with an innate nature, or fitra, marked by curiosity, persistence, creativity and forgiveness, it asks why so many of us drift away from that nature as we grow older.

Drawing on real-life stories, the book invites readers to look at their lives again through the clear, unspoiled perception they had as children, to see how experience has changed them and how they can grow in a healthier direction. It suits readers looking for reflective, faith-informed personal development. The author's proceeds from the book go to charity.

  • Author: Moataz Meshal
  • Publisher: Dar Dawen
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778061253

title: قناع بلون السماء
author: Basem Khandaqji
description:
A Mask, the Colour of the Sky (قناع بلون السماء) is a novel in Arabic by the Palestinian writer Basem Khandaqji. Nur, an archaeologist living in a refugee camp in Ramallah, finds a blue Israeli identity card in the pocket of an old coat and decides to wear the mask of the occupier, hoping to understand the mindset on the other side.

Taking the name Ur, he joins an excavation team at a settlement, where Palestine's buried history surfaces from beneath the soil. Moving between the blue ID and the permit, and between a sidelined original story and a dominant invented one, the novel asks whether Nur can cast off the mask and find himself again. A layered read about identity and memory.

  • Author: Basem Khandaqji
  • Publisher: Dar Al Adab
  • Format: Paperback, 239 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953897387

title: السياسة والحيلة عند العرب
sheet_title: Seyasa Wa El Heela Aanda El Arab
author: René Khawam
description:
Politics and Cunning Among the Arabs (السياسة والحيلة عند العرب) is a book in Arabic published by Dar Al Saqi in London, edited by René Khawam with revision by Nazik Saba Yared. It presents a classical collection of tales of ruses and stratagems, catalogued under the title Raqa'iq al-Hilal fi Daqa'iq al-Hiyal.

The stories illustrate how trickery and clever schemes were used in politics and in daily life across the Arab world, offering a window onto older traditions of storytelling and statecraft. It will interest readers of classical Arabic prose, history and folklore.

  • Editor: René Khawam
  • Revised by: Nazik Saba Yared
  • Publisher: Dar Al Saqi
  • Format: Paperback, 232 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9781855160101

title: أربعون سؤالا عن الذات والمصير والصحة
sheet_title: اربعون سولاً عن المصير والروح والصحة
author: Sergei N. Lazarev
description:
Forty Questions on the Self, Destiny and Health (أربعون سؤالا عن الذات والمصير والصحة) is a book in Arabic by the Russian author Sergei N. Lazarev, in which he answers readers' questions about the self, fate and well-being.

Working through a series of commandments, Lazarev begins with love for the one God and acceptance of His will as a way to change behaviour and restrain the instincts, then turns to avoiding attachment to people and possessions, and to generosity, sacrifice, compassion, forgiveness and fasting. He also describes three levels of sin, linking spiritual life with health and destiny.

  • Author: Sergei N. Lazarev
  • Publisher: Dar Al Khayal
  • Format: 208 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953651118

title: القناع
author: Mustafa Hosny
description:
The Mask (القناع) is a book in Arabic by the Egyptian preacher Mustafa Hosny, part of his series on building a godly self. It explores the natural disposition, or fitra, with which God created people, and how fear can hide a person's true, God-given character behind a mask.

Hosny argues that people put on masks to protect themselves, worried that living with open-hearted mercy will leave them exposed, and shows how overcoming this manufactured fear lets a person live authentically. The book looks at several masks we commonly wear and how to remove them, making it a reflective guide for readers seeking harmony between faith, self and everyday life.

  • Author: Mustafa Hosny
  • Publisher: Nahdet Misr
  • Format: Paperback, 408 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789771461937

title: رغبات محققة اتقان فن التجلي
author: Wayne W. Dyer
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Wishes Fulfilled: Mastering the Art of Manifesting (رغبات محققة: إتقان فن التجلي) is the Arabic edition of Wayne W. Dyer's book on manifesting. Dyer encourages readers to feel in their bodies the very thing they wish to bring into being, and to recognise themselves as divine beings living in the physical world.

He gives the imagination a central role: once you picture who you want to become, you are urged to live from that end result as though it has already arrived. At the heart of the book is the idea of an inner divine spark, the I AM, which can work remarkable changes when nurtured. It suits readers of spiritual self-help.

  • Author: Wayne W. Dyer
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953978130

title: ساحر الكرملين
author: Giuliano da Empoli
description:
The Wizard of the Kremlin (ساحر الكرملين) is the Arabic edition of Giuliano da Empoli's novel Le Mage du Kremlin, translated by Abdelmajid Sebbata. Inspired by real events and people, it takes the reader inside the Russian state through the voice of Vadim Baranov, the fictional political adviser and strategist behind Vladimir Putin's rise.

From the war in Chechnya to the crisis in Ukraine and the Sochi Olympics, Baranov reveals how power works behind the scenes and what drives contemporary Russia during the Putin years. Sharp and absorbing, the novel suits readers interested in politics, power and modern Russian history.

  • Author: Giuliano da Empoli
  • Translator: Abdelmajid Sebbata
  • Publisher: Arab Cultural Centre
  • Format: Paperback, 285 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789920657471

title: لكُلٍّ ما لَهُ / حكايات المافيا
author: Leonardo Sciascia
description:
To Each His Own (لكل ما له) is the Arabic edition of Leonardo Sciascia's Sicilian classic A ciascuno il suo, translated by Erfan Rashid. Manno, a pharmacist in a small Sicilian town, receives an anonymous letter announcing that he will die, and the next day he and his hunting companion are both found dead.

When the police inquiry stalls, a modest schoolteacher with literary interests spots a clue and sets out to find the killer, slowly uncovering a web of desire, political scheming and complicity. More than a detective story, the novel is a sharp portrait of a society built on secrecy, silence and violence, and a fine introduction to Sciascia's writing about the Mafia.

  • Author: Leonardo Sciascia
  • Translator: Erfan Rashid
  • Publisher: Almutawassit
  • Format: Paperback, 200 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9791280738059

title: مقبرة قزحية للروح
author: Lina Meruane
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
An Iris Graveyard for the Soul (مقبرة قزحية للروح) is the Arabic edition of Chilean writer Lina Meruane's novel Sangre en el ojo, known in English as Seeing Red, translated by Mushira Moussa. It follows a Chilean writer living abroad who suffers a sudden haemorrhage in one eye and then the other, leaving her blind.

Moving between New York, where she undergoes surgery and an uncertain recovery, and Santiago, the story explores illness, dependence and the strange love affair that develops under such extreme pressure, asking how unconditional love really is. Intense and unsettling, it suits readers of bold contemporary Latin American fiction.

  • Author: Lina Meruane
  • Translator: Mushira Moussa
  • Publisher: Al Kotob Khan
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778031508

title: وقريبًا سيحل الظلام
author: Khaled Amin
description:
And Soon, Darkness Will Fall (وقريبًا سيحل الظلام) is a horror thriller in Arabic by Khaled Amin. A series of terrible murders spreads fear through Cairo, and a chilling killer known as Jado openly claims them, until the city's streets empty after dark.

A mysterious man decides to stand against him, gathering a special team of people with unusual abilities to hunt Jado down and expose who he is. Their chase leads to the secret of a frightening palace that haunts the killer's dreams and an abandoned town that appears on no map. Dark and suspenseful, it suits readers who enjoy Arabic horror and crime fiction.

  • Author: Khaled Amin
  • Publisher: Dar Dawen
  • Format: Paperback, 301 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778063219

title: الحالة الحرجة للمدعو ك
author: Aziz Mohammed
description:
The Critical Case of a Man Called K (الحالة الحرجة للمدعو ك) is a novel in Arabic by the Saudi writer Aziz Mohammed. Its narrator, a young man stuck in a dull office job at a large company, records his days with dry detachment until a serious illness forces him into a long course of chemotherapy.

Told in a cool, often darkly funny voice steeped in his reading of Kafka and other writers, the novel follows his treatment, his strained ties with family and colleagues, and his inner life as illness reshapes everything around him. A quiet, unflinching read for those who appreciate introspective contemporary Arabic fiction.

  • Author: Aziz Mohammed
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: 269 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953582399

title: الصبي الذي عرف الكثير
author: Cathy Byrd
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
The Boy Who Knew Too Much (الصبي الذي عرف الكثير) is the Arabic edition of Cathy Byrd's memoir about her son, Christian. At just two years old, Christian began describing vivid memories of being a tall baseball player in the 1920s and 1930s, sharing details about the life of the legendary Lou Gehrig that he could not have known.

Faced with her son's puzzling claims, Byrd set out to find answers, and the search challenged her beliefs and changed how she sees life and death. Told with openness and warmth, the book will interest readers drawn to true stories about past lives, spirituality and the mysteries of memory.

  • Author: Cathy Byrd
  • Publisher: Dar Al Khayal
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953650647

title: آفاق النظرية الأدبية من المحاكاة إلى التفكيكية
sheet_title: آفاق النظرية الأدبية من المحاكاة إلى التفكيكية
author: Saleh Zayyad
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Horizons of Literary Theory: From Mimesis to Deconstruction (آفاق النظرية الأدبية من المحاكاة إلى التفكيكية) is a work of literary criticism in Arabic by Saleh Zayyad, published by Dar Al-Tanweer.

As its title indicates, the book surveys the development of literary theory, from the classical idea of mimesis, or imitation, through to deconstruction. It suits students and readers of literature and criticism.

  • Author: Saleh Zayyad
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: 302 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789938886757

title: من أنــا؟
author: Mohammed Qasim Khudair
description:
Who Am I? (من أنا؟) is a popular science book in Arabic by Mohammed Qasim Khudair that explores what really makes up the self. Is it the body, the brain or something beyond them, and how much of the picture we hold of ourselves is real? The author approaches these questions through a futuristic fictional story woven with scientific facts about real people whose cases changed our understanding of identity.

The book then turns to sharpening thinking, analysis and critique: it sets out common fallacies, explains how experimental science works, and shows how people confuse genuine science with pseudoscience, especially so-called energy science. A clear, engaging read for curious minds who enjoy psychology and critical thinking.

  • Author: Mohammed Qasim Khudair
  • Publisher: Nova Plus
  • Format: Paperback, 238 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789996694875

title: الاسكندرية فى غيمة
author: Ibrahim Abdel Meguid
description:
Clouds over Alexandria (الإسكندرية في غيمة) is a novel in Arabic by the Egyptian writer Ibrahim Abdel Meguid and the third part of his Alexandria trilogy. Rather than following one set of heroes, the trilogy portrays the city itself at three turning points, after No One Sleeps in Alexandria, set during the Second World War, and Birds of Amber, set after the 1956 Suez war.

This volume turns to Alexandria in the 1970s, when a rising wave of religious extremism allied itself with the political establishment, the city's tolerance waned and the last traces of its cosmopolitan spirit began to fade. Each novel can be read on its own or in sequence, together forming a rich portrait of a changing city.

  • Author: Ibrahim Abdel Meguid
  • Publisher: Dar El Shorouk
  • Format: Paperback, 462 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Alexandria Trilogy, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9789770931790

title: أسلوب الرجل المتفوق
author: David Deida
description:
The Way of the Superior Man (أسلوب الرجل المتفوق) is the Arabic edition of David Deida's spiritual guide for men, translated by Omar Fathi. Since it first appeared, attitudes to sex and gender roles have changed a great deal, yet the book argues that men of every age still wrestle with relationships, purpose and desire.

Deida encourages men and women to engage openly and to offer the world their most valuable gifts, an honest heart and a deep presence. He calls for moving beyond both the macho, emotionless model of masculinity and the anxious, overly sensitive one, towards a more conscious and embodied way of being a man. This edition includes a new introduction.

  • Author: David Deida
  • Translator: Omar Fathi
  • Publisher: Dar Al Khayal
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953651026

title: ميّادة
author: Jean Sasson
description:
Mayada, Daughter of Iraq (ميادة ابنة العراق) is the Arabic edition of Jean Sasson's account of Mayada Al-Askari, an Iraqi writer and journalist from a prominent family: her grandfather Jafar Pasha Al-Askari founded the Iraqi army, and she was also a granddaughter of Sati Al-Husri, a founding figure of Arab nationalist thought.

Under Saddam Hussein's regime, Mayada was arrested and held in Cell 52 with seventeen other women, who shared how they were detained, the charges they faced and the brutal torture they endured. Sasson records their testimony with compassion, producing a harrowing but important portrait of life under the security services. Contains descriptions of torture and violence.

  • Author: Jean Sasson
  • Publisher: Al-Matbouat
  • Format: Paperback, 476 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953888163

title: ورد
author: Al-Jawhara Alremal
description:
Roses (ورد) is a book in Arabic by Al-Jawhara Alremal, listed as the third title in her series Me Before Everything (أنا قبل كل شيء).

Its narrator speaks of having found the best version of herself after shedding the memories and events that held her back, and urges the reader to let go of a painful past, disappointed hopes and old hurts in order to move forward. A short, reflective read for readers who enjoy emotional, motivational Arabic prose.

  • Author: Al-Jawhara Alremal
  • Publisher: Arab Literature Center
  • Format: 138 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Me Before Everything, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9786038346204

title: Book Of Night
author: Holly Black
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Book of Night is Holly Black's first novel for adults, a contemporary dark fantasy full of thieves, con artists and secret societies. In Charlie Hall's world, shadows can be altered and manipulated to change appearances, feelings and even memories, and to gain power, though every use of this magic comes at a cost.

Charlie is a small-time crook trying to leave her past behind by working as a bartender, but she is pulled back into a dangerous underworld of shadow magicians. Atmospheric and twisty, it suits fans of Black's young adult fantasy who want something darker, and readers who enjoy urban fantasy with a heist edge.

  • Author: Holly Black
  • Language: English
  • Series: Book of Night, Book 1

title: Cloud Cuckoo Land
author: Anthony Doerr
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Cloud Cuckoo Land is an ambitious novel by Anthony Doerr that links characters across centuries through a single ancient Greek story. In Constantinople in 1453, a young orphan who works as a seamstress and an animal-loving village boy find themselves on opposite sides of the walls during the great siege.

In Idaho in 2020, a troubled teenager plans an act of revenge while an elderly man rehearses a children's play, and in the distant future a girl named Konstance travels alone aboard an interstellar ship. Together their stories celebrate books, libraries and the power of storytelling to outlast catastrophe. A rich, absorbing read for literary fiction fans.

  • Author: Anthony Doerr
  • Language: English

title: I Went For Hajj!
author: Na'ima B. Robert
description:
I Went for Hajj is a rhyming picture book by Na'ima B. Robert that introduces young children to the Hajj pilgrimage through the eyes of a little boy who has just come home from Makkah as a Hajji.

Readers join him as he wraps himself in two simple white sheets, stands before the Kaaba and hears the call to prayer ring out, discovering the sights, sounds, smells and feelings of the most important journey in a Muslim's life. Written to be read aloud, it is a warm way to share the meaning of Hajj with children at home, in school or at the masjid.

  • Author: Na'ima B. Robert
  • Publisher: The Islamic Foundation
  • Format: Hardcover, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780860377528

title: Ignorance
author: Milan Kundera
description:
Ignorance is a novel by Milan Kundera, translated from the French by Linda Asher, about exile, memory and the longing to return home. Irena and Josef, who both left Czechoslovakia after the Soviet invasion and built lives abroad, meet by chance as they travel back to Prague twenty years later, after the fall of communism.

They once shared a brief romance, but their recollections of it no longer agree, and the novel uses their reunion to reflect on nostalgia, the unreliability of memory and the myth of the great return, echoing Homer's Odysseus. Wry, compact and philosophical, it is a rewarding read for admirers of Kundera and of thoughtful European fiction.

  • Author: Milan Kundera
  • Translator: Linda Asher
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 195 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571215515

title: Land Of The Lustrous 6
author: Haruko Ichikawa
description:
Land of the Lustrous, Vol. 6 is the sixth volume of Haruko Ichikawa's manga series, set in a far-future world of living gems who must fight off raids by the mysterious Lunarians. Phosphophyllite has been immobilised in battle, and only Ghost Quartz is nearby to help.

The two must hold out against a relentless Lunarian attack until reinforcements arrive, a tall order for such a new partnership, and Phos fears that Ghost could become one more casualty of the war. With its striking art and melancholy, philosophical tone, this volume continues a beautifully strange fantasy for older teen and adult manga readers.

  • Author: Haruko Ichikawa
  • Translators: Alethea Nibley and Athena Nibley
  • Publisher: Kodansha Comics
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Land of the Lustrous, Volume 6
  • ISBN: 9781632366368

title: Ragdoll
author: Daniel Cole
description:
Ragdoll is the first book in Daniel Cole's Fawkes and Baxter crime thriller series. Detective William Fawkes, nicknamed the Wolf, is back on duty after a suspension for assaulting a suspect, and he is eager for a big case when his former partner, Emily Baxter, calls him to a horrifying crime scene in London.

A single body has been stitched together from the parts of six different victims, and the killer soon sends a list of six more names, with the dates each will die, and the final target is Fawkes himself. Fast-paced, dark and laced with black humour, it is a gripping read for fans of serial-killer thrillers.

  • Author: Daniel Cole
  • Publisher: Orion
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Fawkes and Baxter, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781398704732

title: Raybearer
author: Jordan Ifueko
description:
Raybearer is the first book in Jordan Ifueko's young adult fantasy series. Tarisai has grown up lonely, raised in isolation by a mysterious woman called only The Lady, and longs above all to belong to a family. Then The Lady sends her to the capital of the empire of Aritsar to compete for a place on the Crown Prince's Council of Eleven.

Council members are bound to one another by the Ray, a connection deeper than blood, which is everything Tarisai has dreamed of. But her mother has laid a magical command on her: once she earns the prince's trust, she must kill him. Rich in West African-inspired world-building, it is a story about loyalty, identity and choosing your own path.

  • Author: Jordan Ifueko
  • Publisher: Hot Key Books
  • Format: Paperback, 496 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Raybearer, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781471409271

title: Rich Dad's Escape from the Rat Race
sheet_title: Rich Dads Escape from the Rat Race
author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
description:
Rich Dad's Escape from the Rat Race is a full-colour illustrated story by Robert T. Kiyosaki that introduces young readers to the money lessons behind Rich Dad Poor Dad. Aimed at children and teens, it questions the familiar advice to study hard, get good grades, find a secure job and leave the rest to a pension plan.

Through the adventures of Tim, Tina and Red as they try out their own business ideas, the book explains how to build assets and let money do the work, instead of spending a lifetime working for money. Short and accessible, it is a practical first step into financial literacy for children, teenagers and families.

  • Author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
  • Publisher: Plata Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 64 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781612680552

title: Rooster Fighter, Vol. 1
author: Shu Sakuratani
description:
Rooster Fighter, Vol. 1 opens Shu Sakuratani's action-comedy manga series, set in a world where colossal demons roam the land and terrorise ordinary people. Standing against them is a most unlikely hero: a rooster named Keiji, who is far more than a farmyard bird.

His enemies may tower ten storeys high, but nothing matches his courage, his fighting spirit or his fearsome battle cry. Gleefully absurd yet packed with dynamic fight scenes, this first volume is great fun for manga readers who enjoy monster battles with a strong streak of humour.

  • Author: Shu Sakuratani
  • Translator: Jonah Mayahara-Miller
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Rooster Fighter, Volume 1
  • ISBN: 9781974729845

title: Second First Impressions
author: Sally Thorne
description:
Second First Impressions is a warm romantic comedy by Sally Thorne, author of The Hating Game. Ruthie Midona is twenty-four but lives like someone far older, pouring herself into her job at a luxury retirement village and keeping so busy with its eccentric residents that she barely has a life of her own.

Then Teddy Prescott arrives as the newest employee: charming, handsome, a rich kid with no love of hard work, and Ruthie is unimpressed. She assigns him to two mischievous elderly residents, expecting them to drive him away, but things do not go to plan. Funny and tender, it suits fans of slow-burn, feel-good romance.

  • Author: Sally Thorne
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780349428932

title: Silver In The Bone
author: Alexandra Bracken
description:
Silver in the Bone is the first book in Alexandra Bracken's young adult fantasy series of the same name, drawing on the legends of King Arthur. Tamsin Lark is a Hollower, one of the people without magic who make their living by hunting down cursed and powerful relics.

When an ancient ring linked to the Lady of the Lake becomes the prize in a dangerous race, Tamsin is forced into an uneasy alliance with her infuriating rival, Emrys Dye, to find it first. Combining Arthurian myth, treasure-hunting adventure and a sharp-edged romance, it is a fast-paced read for fans of dark fantasy.

  • Author: Alexandra Bracken
  • Publisher: Quercus Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 496 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Silver in the Bone, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781786541703

title: Simply Climate Change
author: Clive Gifford, Daniel Hooke, Adam Levy, Frans Berkhout
description:
Simply Climate Change is part of DK's Simply series, a visual guide that explains the science, impact and politics of climate change in clear, bite-sized pages. Written by Clive Gifford, Daniel Hooke, Adam Levy and Frans Berkhout, it sets out why the climate is changing and what that means for people and the planet.

More than 100 key ideas are explained through concise text and simple graphics, from the causes of global warming to the technologies and practical steps that could help tackle it. It also outlines the political, social and economic debates surrounding the issue. A good starting point for students, curious readers and anyone wanting to understand the crisis without jargon.

  • Authors: Clive Gifford, Daniel Hooke, Adam Levy, Frans Berkhout
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: DK Simply
  • ISBN: 9780241516072

title: The Burning God
author: R.F. Kuang
description:
The Burning God is the final book in R.F. Kuang's Poppy War trilogy, an epic fantasy that draws on the history of twentieth-century China. Having saved the nation of Nikan from foreign invaders and waged a savage civil war against Empress Su Daji, Fang Runin, known as Rin, has been betrayed by her allies and left for dead.

Returning to her home province and the village of Tikany, Rin finds untrustworthy new allies in the Southern Coalition, and discovers that her true strength lies with ordinary people who worship her as a saviour. As her power grows, so does the danger of what she might become. A brutal, ambitious conclusion for readers of dark epic fantasy.

  • Author: R.F. Kuang
  • Publisher: HarperVoyager
  • Format: Paperback, 622 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Poppy War, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780008339180

title: The Definitive Book of Body Language
sheet_title: The Definitive Book of Body Language
author: Allan Pease, Barbara Pease
description:
The Definitive Book of Body Language by Allan and Barbara Pease is a practical guide to understanding nonverbal communication. It explains how gestures, posture and expressions reveal what people really think and feel, and how our own movements send signals to others, often without our realising it.

Drawing on decades of experience in the field, plus studies in psychology, evolutionary biology and neuroscience, the authors break body language down into its components, from handshakes and smiles to eye contact and seating positions. Useful for interviews, negotiations, dating and everyday conversations, it suits anyone who wants to read people better and make a stronger impression.

  • Authors: Allan Pease, Barbara Pease
  • Publisher: Orion
  • Format: Paperback, 392 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781409168508

title: The Fellowship of the Ring
sheet_title: THE FELLOWSHIP OF THE RING FELLOWSHIP OF THE RING VOL 1
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description:
The Fellowship of the Ring is the first volume of J.R.R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, continuing the story begun in The Hobbit. The Dark Lord Sauron has gathered the Rings of Power and seeks only the One Ring, which has passed from Bilbo Baggins to his young cousin Frodo in the quiet Shire.

Frodo must leave home and carry the Ring on a perilous journey across Middle-earth towards Mount Doom, the only place it can be destroyed, joined by a fellowship of hobbits, men, an elf, a dwarf and the wizard Gandalf. This HarperCollins paperback offers the definitive text, cover art adapted from a design by Tolkien himself and a map of Middle-earth.

  • Author: J.R.R. Tolkien
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 407 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Lord of the Rings, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780261103573

title: The Four Winds
author: Kristin Hannah
description:
The Four Winds is a historical novel by Kristin Hannah set during the Great Depression and the Dust Bowl. In Texas in 1934, Elsa Martinelli has at last found the family, home and farm she longed for on the Great Plains, but years of drought threaten everything she and her neighbours depend on.

When her husband abandons them, Elsa faces an agonising choice: hold on to the farm she cherishes, or head for California with Loreda and Ant, hoping for a fresh start. A moving story of motherhood, resilience, friendship between women and the American dream, it is a natural choice for book clubs.

  • Author: Kristin Hannah
  • Publisher: Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 454 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529054576

title: The Secret Commonwealth The Book of Dust Volume Two
sheet_title: The Secret Commonwealth The Book of Dust Volume Two
author: Philip Pullman
description:
The Secret Commonwealth is the second volume of Philip Pullman's The Book of Dust, set twenty years after La Belle Sauvage and seven years after the close of His Dark Materials. Lyra Silvertongue is now a twenty-year-old student in Oxford, and her bond with her daemon, Pantalaimon, has become strained in ways neither of them could have foreseen.

Lyra is drawn into hidden and dangerous factions, on a journey that takes her across Europe and towards Central Asia, while Malcolm Polstead, once a boy with a canoe and now a scholar, follows a path of his own. Darker and more grown-up than the earlier books, it is essential reading for longtime fans of Lyra's world.

  • Author: Philip Pullman
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 736 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Book of Dust, Volume 2
  • ISBN: 9780241373354

title: The Secret Lives Of Church Ladies
sheet_title: The Secret Lives Of Church Ladies
author: Deesha Philyaw
description:
The Secret Lives of Church Ladies is a short story collection by Deesha Philyaw about Black women and girls who, for a moment, choose to follow their own desires instead of always being good. Among them is fourteen-year-old Jael, who is infatuated with the preacher's wife, and a mother whose weekly peach cobbler is baked for her married pastor lover.

There are also two childhood friends, Eula and Caroletta, who find comfort in each other every New Year's Eve. Frank, funny and full of longing, these stories explore faith, sexuality, family and freedom, and will appeal to readers of bold, character-driven literary fiction.

  • Author: Deesha Philyaw
  • Publisher: Pushkin Press
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781911590712

title: The Silmarillion
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
The Silmarillion by J.R.R. Tolkien, edited and published after his death by his son Christopher Tolkien, tells the history of the Elder Days, the First Age of Middle-earth. It is the ancient background to The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, recounting events in which figures like Galadriel and Elrond were once involved.

At its heart is the struggle of the High Elves against Morgoth, the original Dark Lord, to win back the Silmarils, three jewels that hold the light of Valinor. Grand in scope and written like a mythology, it covers the creation of the world and the rise and fall of great kingdoms, and is essential reading for devoted Tolkien fans.

  • Author: J.R.R. Tolkien
  • Editor: Christopher Tolkien
  • Language: English

title: The Two Towers The Lord Of The Rings Part 2
sheet_title: The Two Towers The Lord Of The Rings Part 2
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description:
The Two Towers is the second volume of J.R.R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, following The Fellowship of the Ring. The Fellowship has broken apart, and while Frodo and Sam press on towards Mordor with a sly, creeping figure trailing them, their companions are scattered across Middle-earth.

Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli set out to rescue Merry and Pippin, who have been seized by orcs, and are drawn into the war against Saruman of Isengard and the defence of Rohan. Rich in landscape, legend and moral courage, this middle part of the epic leads directly into The Return of the King and is essential reading for fantasy lovers.

  • Author: J.R.R. Tolkien
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 329 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Lord of the Rings, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780261103580

title: The Years
author: Virginia Woolf
description:
The Years is Virginia Woolf's penultimate novel, following the Pargiter family from the 1880s into the 1930s against the busy backdrop of London's streets. Through the family's moments of closeness and distance, worry and success, it traces the passing of their Victorian world and the arrival of a very different modern one.

Etiquette moves from Victorian parlours to wartime air raids as the decades pass, yet Woolf's focus remains on how individuals endure through time, change, loss and renewal. This Penguin Classics edition comes with notes and an introduction by Jeri Johnson, making it ideal for students and lovers of modernist fiction.

  • Author: Virginia Woolf
  • Introduction: Jeri Johnson
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 448 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241372074

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
description:
The Catcher in the Rye is J.D. Salinger's classic novel of adolescence, narrated by the teenage Holden Caulfield. Expelled from yet another boarding school, Holden spends a few aimless days drifting around New York City before he can face his family, railing against the phoniness he sees in the adult world.

Told in Holden's restless, funny and often painfully honest voice, the novel captures the confusion, loneliness and longing that come with growing up. First published in 1951, it remains one of the most widely read coming-of-age stories in English and a natural choice for school reading lists, book clubs and anyone revisiting a modern classic.

  • Author: J.D. Salinger
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 230 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241950432

title: You Love Me
author: Caroline Kepnes
description:
You Love Me is the third novel in Caroline Kepnes's dark thriller series narrated by Joe Goldberg. Turning his back on city life, Joe settles on a quiet island off the Pacific Northwest coast, starts working in the town library and meets librarian Mary Kay DiMarco, determined this time to win her slowly and decently.

The catch is that Mary Kay already has a full life as a mother and a friend, and Joe's idea of patience has always had a sinister edge. Told in Joe's chilling, darkly funny voice, the book suits readers who enjoyed the earlier novels or the television adaptation and like their suspense from inside a disturbing mind.

  • Author: Caroline Kepnes
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster UK
  • Format: Paperback, 385 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: You, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781471191916

title: Hell's Paradise: Jigokuraku, Vol. 5
author: Yuji Kaku
description:
Hell's Paradise: Jigokuraku, Vol. 5 continues Yuji Kaku's dark action manga about Gabimaru, a ninja under sentence of death who can earn a pardon, and a reunion with the wife he loves, by bringing the shogun the elixir of life from a mysterious island.

In this volume, Gabimaru and his allies come face to face with the secrets of tao, the strange force that makes the island's rulers, the Lord Tensen, so dangerous, while Gabimaru's own behaviour begins to change in alarming ways. Mixing brutal battles, horror and an Edo-period setting, it suits older teen and adult manga readers following the series.

  • Author: Yuji Kaku
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 216 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Hell's Paradise: Jigokuraku, Vol. 5
  • ISBN: 9781974713240

title: How Will You Measure Your Life?
sheet_title: How Will You Measure Your Life?
author: Clayton M. Christensen, James Allworth and Karen Dillon
description:
How Will You Measure Your Life? is a reflective guide by Harvard Business School professor Clayton M. Christensen, written with James Allworth and Karen Dillon. It grew out of a talk Christensen gave to graduating students after surviving a series of serious illnesses, in which he asked how people can build lives that are genuinely fulfilling.

Christensen applies the business theories he developed over his career, including ideas about strategy, motivation and how we allocate our time and energy, to personal questions about careers, relationships, family and integrity. The result is a thoughtful, accessible book for graduates, professionals and anyone pausing to consider what success should really mean to them.

  • Authors: Clayton M. Christensen, James Allworth and Karen Dillon
  • Publisher: Thorsons
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008316426

title: King's Cage
author: Victoria Aveyard
description:
King's Cage is the third book in Victoria Aveyard's Red Queen series, a young adult fantasy set in a kingdom split between ordinary Reds and the superpowered Silver elite. Mare Barrow, the Lightning Girl, is now a prisoner of King Maven, held powerless by Silent Stone in his palace and haunted by her own mistakes.

While Mare endures captivity at the hands of the boy who betrayed her, the rebels and newbloods outside prepare for open war, and exiled prince Cal is determined to rescue her. Full of shifting loyalties, political scheming and tense romance, it raises the stakes for the series and leads into the final instalment, War Storm.

  • Author: Victoria Aveyard
  • Publisher: Orion
  • Format: Paperback, 512 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Red Queen, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781409150763

title: Kingdom Of The Cursed
author: Kerri Maniscalco
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Kingdom of the Cursed is the second book in Kerri Maniscalco's Kingdom of the Wicked fantasy romance series. Bound to the demon world after giving up her soul, the witch Emilia journeys with Wrath, the mysterious demon prince, to the Seven Circles, a seductive realm ruled by sin.

Still determined to avenge her murdered twin sister, Vittoria, Emilia is even willing to marry Pride, the demon prince who rules as king. In a court of scheming princes, lavish palaces and conflicting clues, she cannot be sure whom to trust, including Wrath himself. A dark, romantic page-turner for fans of enemies-to-lovers fantasy.

  • Author: Kerri Maniscalco
  • Language: English
  • Series: Kingdom of the Wicked, Book 2

title: Love In The Time Of Cholera
sheet_title: Love In The Time Of Cholera
author: Gabriel García Márquez
description:
Love in the Time of Cholera is Gabriel García Márquez's celebrated novel of a love that waits more than half a century. As young people, Florentino Ariza and Fermina Daza fall for each other, but she turns him away and marries the respected physician Dr Juvenal Urbino instead.

Florentino never stops loving her, and when Urbino dies in an accident decades later, he finally renews his declaration. Set in a Caribbean port city and written with the Nobel laureate's warmth, humour and lush detail, the novel explores devotion, ageing and the many forms love can take. It is a rewarding read for lovers of literary fiction and classic Latin American writing.

  • Author: Gabriel García Márquez
  • Translator: Edith Grossman
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 348 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241978924

title: Maps Of Our Spectacular Bodies
author: Maddie Mortimer
description:
Maps of Our Spectacular Bodies is the debut novel by Maddie Mortimer, a lyrical story of a woman facing serious illness. Lia lives with her husband Harry and their daughter Iris, who is finding her way through early adolescence, until a sudden diagnosis upends the family and long-buried secrets from Lia's past begin to surface.

Part of the story is narrated by the illness itself, a playful and menacing voice that roams through Lia's body and memories, from her devout mother to her first love. Inventive in form and moving in its treatment of family, mortality and the stories our bodies hold, it suits readers who enjoy experimental literary fiction and book club discussion.

  • Author: Maddie Mortimer
  • Publisher: Picador
  • Format: Paperback, 436 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529069389

title: Redemptor
author: Jordan Ifueko
description:
Redemptor is the second and final book in Jordan Ifueko's Raybearer duology, a young adult fantasy inspired by West African storytelling. Tarisai now sits on the throne of Aritsar as Empress Redemptor, and to satisfy the restless spirits of the dead she must form her own council and then descend into the Underworld as a sacrifice.

Haunted by child spirits demanding payment for the empire's past crimes, facing assassination attempts and unsure whom to trust, Tarisai has to decide whether she is meant to die for justice or live to build it. Rich in mythology, found family and moral questions about power, it brings the story begun in Raybearer to its conclusion.

  • Author: Jordan Ifueko
  • Publisher: Hot Key Books
  • Format: Paperback, 464 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Raybearer, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781471410130

title: Simply Maths
author: DK
description:
Simply Maths is part of DK's Simply series, a visual introduction to mathematics for readers who want clear answers without heavy jargon. It covers more than 90 key ideas, ranging across prime numbers, fractions, quadratic equations, probability and calculus, and gives each concept its own single page.

Entries are grouped by theme, including number, calculation, geometry, algebra, graphs, ratio, measurement, statistics and calculus, and pair short, plain explanations with bold graphics. It works well as a revision companion for school and college students, and as a refresher for adults who want to rebuild their confidence with numbers.

  • Author: DK
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: DK Simply
  • ISBN: 9780241515686

title: Song Of Solomon
author: Toni Morrison
description:
Song of Solomon is Toni Morrison's acclaimed novel about Macon 'Milkman' Dead, a young man born in a Michigan city just after a local eccentric leaps from a roof in the hope of flying. Restless and dissatisfied, Milkman eventually leaves the North to search for his family's roots in the South.

His journey becomes a search for identity, inheritance and the meaning of flight, populated by vivid characters such as his aunt Pilate and his friend Guitar. Blending realism with myth and folklore, it is one of Morrison's major works, and this Vintage Classics edition includes an introduction by Marlon James. It suits readers of American classics and literary fiction alike.

  • Author: Toni Morrison
  • Introduction: Marlon James
  • Publisher: Vintage Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 448 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784876456

title: The Daevabad Trilogy (2) — The Kingdom Of Copper
sheet_title: The Daevabad Trilogy (2) — The Kingdom Of Copper
author: S.A. Chakraborty
description:
The Kingdom of Copper is the second book in S.A. Chakraborty's Daevabad Trilogy and the follow-up to The City of Brass. Inspired by Middle Eastern and Islamic folklore, it returns to the magical city of Daevabad, where Nahri, a former con artist from Cairo, is learning to claim her healing heritage at the royal court.

Meanwhile Prince Ali, exiled by his father, struggles to survive in his ancestral homeland while new powers threaten to expose a dangerous family secret. As a great celebration draws djinn to the city, old rivalries and political tensions come to a head. Rich in mythology, intrigue and complex characters, it is a strong pick for fans of epic historical fantasy.

  • Author: S.A. Chakraborty
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 625 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Daevabad Trilogy, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780008239473

title: The Hospital : The Inside Story
author: Dr Christle Nwora
description:
The Hospital: The Inside Story is a nonfiction book for children by Dr Christle Nwora that takes young readers behind the scenes of a busy hospital. Following a single day, it introduces the many people who look after patients, from surgeons and nurses to ambulance crews and mental health therapists.

Along the way children follow several patients, including a couple welcoming a new baby, a boy having a cast fitted on a broken arm and a woman preparing for an operation, while simple explanations show how things such as X-rays work. It is a reassuring, informative read for curious children and for families preparing for a hospital visit.

  • Author: Dr Christle Nwora
  • Publisher: Priddy Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 64 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781838991524

title: The Spanish Love Deception
sheet_title: The Spanish Love Deception Tiktok Made Me Buy It!
author: Elena Armas
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
The Spanish Love Deception is a contemporary romance by Elena Armas and the first book in her Love Deception series. Catalina Martín needs a date for her sister's wedding in Spain, especially now that a fib about an American boyfriend has grown far beyond her control, and her ex and his new fiancée will be there too.

With only four weeks to find a willing stand-in, the last person she expects to volunteer is Aaron Blackford, her tall, infuriating and condescending colleague. As the fake relationship plays out in front of her lively family, the line between pretence and real feeling starts to blur. A slow-burn, enemies-to-lovers romance full of humour and warmth.

  • Author: Elena Armas
  • Language: English
  • Series: Love Deception, Book 1

title: Time of Contempt
sheet_title: Time of Contempt Witcher 2 - Now a major Netflix show
author: Andrzej Sapkowski
description:
Time of Contempt is Andrzej Sapkowski's second full-length Witcher novel, picking up after Blood of Elves, and one of the books behind the Netflix series. The Continent is sliding towards war as elves and other non-human races clash with humans, and kings fear both invasion from across the river and treachery from their neighbours.

At the heart of the story is Ciri, the young princess of prophecy, who is learning to master her magic while Geralt the witcher and the sorceress Yennefer try to keep her safe from everyone hunting her. Full of political intrigue, sharp dialogue and grey morality, it suits readers of epic fantasy and fans of the games and television adaptation.

  • Author: Andrzej Sapkowski
  • Translator: David French
  • Publisher: Gollancz
  • Format: Paperback, 331 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Witcher, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781473231092

title: TOWER OF DAWN
author: Sarah J. Maas
description:
Tower of Dawn is the sixth book in Sarah J. Maas's Throne of Glass series, and it turns the spotlight on Chaol Westfall. Badly injured after the fall of the glass castle and no longer Captain of the Guard, Chaol travels to the southern continent, where the Torre Cesme's famed healers in the city of Antica may be his only hope of recovery.

He and Nesryn Faliq are also there on a diplomatic mission, seeking the support of the powerful southern empire for the coming war, while Dorian and Aelin fight on at home. What they uncover will matter to the whole of Erilea. Set alongside the events of Empire of Storms, it adds new characters and lands before the series finale, Kingdom of Ash.

  • Author: Sarah J. Maas
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury
  • Format: Paperback, 660 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Throne of Glass, Book 6
  • ISBN: 9781408887974

title: Trainspotting
author: Irvine Welsh
description:
Trainspotting is Irvine Welsh's landmark novel about a group of young heroin users in Edinburgh, centred loosely on Mark Renton and his friends Sick Boy, Spud and the volatile Begbie. Told in a series of linked episodes and largely in Scots dialect, it follows their scams, highs and grim crashes.

Raw, darkly comic and unflinching, the novel captures addiction, poverty and friendship with an energy that still feels shocking, and it inspired Danny Boyle's well-known 1996 film. It is a strong choice for readers interested in modern Scottish fiction and contemporary classics, though its language and subject matter suit adult readers.

  • Author: Irvine Welsh
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 431 pages
  • Language: English (with Scots dialect)
  • ISBN: 9780099465898

title: Witch Hat Atelier 5
author: Kamome Shirahama
description:
Witch Hat Atelier, Vol. 5 continues Kamome Shirahama's richly drawn fantasy manga about Coco, a girl who discovers that magic is drawn in ink and becomes an apprentice to the witch Qifrey.

Deep inside the Serpentback Cave, the dark magic of a Brimmed Cap has turned Euini into a beast, Qifrey is gravely injured and the apprentices are surrounded by cursed Romonons. Coco, Tetia and their friends must rely on their wits and individual strengths to survive a ruthless new enemy. Detailed artwork and inventive world-building make it a rewarding read for fans of fantasy manga.

  • Author: Kamome Shirahama
  • Translator: Stephen Kohler
  • Publisher: Kodansha Comics
  • Format: Paperback, 188 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Witch Hat Atelier, Vol. 5
  • ISBN: 9781632369291

author: Roberto Bolaño
description:
2666 is Roberto Bolaño's vast final novel, completed in the last years of his life and published after his death. Its five connected parts circle around Santa Teresa, a fictional city on the Mexico–US border modelled on Ciudad Juárez, where academics, a reclusive author, a sportswriter and many others find their paths crossing.

Beneath these stories runs a horrifying series of murders of women in the city, which the novel examines in relentless detail as a sense of conspiracy builds. Ambitious, unsettling and vividly written, it suits patient readers of serious literary fiction, and this English edition is translated by Natasha Wimmer.

  • Author: Roberto Bolaño
  • Translator: Natasha Wimmer
  • Publisher: Picador
  • Format: Paperback, 898 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780330447430

title: Hell Bent
author: Leigh Bardugo
description:
Hell Bent is the second Alex Stern novel by Leigh Bardugo, following Ninth House. Galaxy 'Alex' Stern is determined to rescue her mentor Darlington from the underworld, even though Lethe, the society that keeps watch over Yale's secret magical houses, has forbidden any attempt.

With Dawes and a handful of unlikely allies, Alex digs through arcane texts and strange artefacts in search of a gateway to hell, breaking rule after rule. When members of the faculty start dying, it becomes clear something deadly is loose in New Haven. Dark, atmospheric and full of secret-society intrigue, it suits adult readers who enjoy dark academia and urban fantasy.

  • Author: Leigh Bardugo
  • Publisher: Gollancz
  • Format: Paperback, 478 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Alex Stern, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781473228030

title: Homesickness
author: Colin Barrett
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Homesickness is a collection of short stories by Irish writer Colin Barrett, his second book after the award-winning Young Skins. Its eight character-driven stories follow outsiders, misfits and the disaffected, mostly in County Mayo, with one journey reaching as far as Canada.

Among them, a quiet evening in a local pub is upended by a fugitive carrying a sword, restless ghosts linger at a funeral, a police officer reflects on her life after a shooting, and a would-be writer reacts badly to his father's illness. Wry, observant and darkly funny, it suits readers of contemporary Irish fiction and the short story form.

  • Author: Colin Barrett
  • Publisher: Penguin Random House
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529115703

title: Memory Palace Master
author: Dr Gareth Moore and Helena M. Gellersen
description:
Memory Palace Master is a puzzle book by Dr Gareth Moore and Helena M. Gellersen designed to sharpen observation and recall. Gellersen, who has worked with the University of Cambridge's Memory Laboratory, and puzzle author Moore pair proven memory techniques with more than 70 puzzles.

The exercises train visual, verbal and long-term recall, explaining why strategies such as visualising and repetition help information stick, and build towards the memory palace method, an ancient technique still used by memory athletes. It is a practical, enjoyable workout for anyone who wants a sharper, more reliable memory.

  • Authors: Dr Gareth Moore and Helena M. Gellersen
  • Publisher: Michael O'Mara
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781789293722

title: Navigating Panic Attacks
author: Dr Rita Santos
description:
Navigating Panic Attacks: How to Understand Your Fear and Reclaim Your Life is a self-help guide by Dr Rita Santos, part of Welbeck Balance's Navigating series. It treats panic attacks as a common feature of anxiety and shows that, whether they happen often or rarely, it is possible to change how you respond to them.

The book sets out practical, step-by-step strategies for coping, with an emphasis on understanding, self-awareness and tailored self-care that may reduce how often attacks happen. It suits anyone affected by panic attacks and those supporting them.

  • Author: Dr Rita Santos
  • Publisher: Welbeck Balance
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Navigating Series
  • ISBN: 9781789562552

title: The English Patient
author: Michael Ondaatje
description:
The English Patient is the Booker Prize-winning novel by Michael Ondaatje, set in a ruined villa in Italy as the Second World War draws to a close. There, four wounded lives come together: Hana, a worn-out young nurse; Caravaggio, a thief who has been maimed; Kip, a cautious Sikh sapper; and the patient himself, a badly burned man with no name.

As Hana cares for him, fragments of his memories emerge, revealing a story of desert exploration, passionate love and betrayal in North Africa before the war. Lyrical and richly layered, the novel later became an Oscar-winning film and remains a rewarding read for lovers of literary historical fiction.

  • Author: Michael Ondaatje
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781526605900

title: The Promise
author: Damon Galgut
description:
The Promise is a novel by South African author Damon Galgut, winner of the 2021 Booker Prize. It follows the Swarts, a white family on a farm near Pretoria, across several decades, with each section built around a family funeral, beginning with the death of Ma.

At its centre is a pledge made to Salome, who has spent her life working for the Swarts, that she will one day own her house and land, a pledge that is broken again and again as South Africa changes around them. With a roving, sharply observant narrative voice, it is a powerful choice for book clubs and readers of literary fiction.

  • Author: Damon Galgut
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529113877

title: What I'd Rather Not Think About
sheet_title: What ID Rather Not Think About
author: Jente Posthuma
description:
What I'd Rather Not Think About is a short novel by Dutch writer Jente Posthuma, translated by Sarah Timmer Harvey. Its narrator is a woman whose twin brother has taken his own life, and she looks back over their shared childhood and their adult years to try to understand him.

She recalls his search for happiness through relationships with men and a spell in the Bhagwan movement, and her own mix of love, resentment and longing. Written in brief, precise fragments with gentle humour amid the sadness, it is a tender exploration of grief, mental illness and the bond between twins, suited to readers of contemplative literary fiction.

When Marnie asks whether she likes him, Jane tells her first lie, and each untruth leads to another until resentment spills over into crime. The Bride (العروس) is a novel in Arabic by the Egyptian writer Hamdy El-Gazzar. It unfolds on a single New Year's Eve at Al-Arous, an upmarket restaurant on the first floor of a building in downtown Cairo, where the board gathers to present the annual accounts.

Grit: Why Passion and Resilience Are the Secrets to Success is a book by psychologist Angela Duckworth on what really drives outstanding achievement. Drawing on her research, she argues that natural talent matters less than we think, and that a combination of passion and long-term persistence, which she calls grit, is a better predictor of success.

Duckworth explains why some gifted people never reach their potential while others with fewer advantages go on to do remarkable things, and shows how grit can be developed through interest, practice, purpose and hope. title: How To Avoid A Climate Disaster

author: Bill Gates

How to Avoid a Climate Disaster is Bill Gates's practical, accessible plan for tackling climate change. He argues that the world must cut its greenhouse gas emissions all the way to zero, rather than simply reducing them, if it is to avoid catastrophe.

Gates explains where emissions come from across electricity, manufacturing, farming, transport and buildings, sets out which technologies already exist and which breakthroughs are still needed, and suggests what governments, businesses and individuals can do. Clear and solution-focused, it suits general readers who want to understand the challenge and what it will take to meet it.

In the Country of Men is the debut novel by Libyan-born author Hisham Matar, set in Tripoli in 1979 under Qaddafi's regime. Nine-year-old Suleiman spends his days playing in the heat with friends and visiting ancient ruins, while his nights are filled with his mother's troubling stories of old family grievances.

When he glimpses his father in the city, hidden behind dark glasses, at a time he was meant to be away on business, Suleiman's world begins to unravel as fear, surveillance and betrayal reach into his home. Told through a child's eyes, it is a moving, quietly devastating story of family, loyalty and life under dictatorship.

Jurgen Klopp is a biography of the charismatic German football manager by Elmar Neveling, updated to include Liverpool's Premier League title win in 2020. It traces how Klopp transformed Borussia Dortmund, leading them to consecutive Bundesliga titles and a Champions League final, before taking charge at Liverpool.

The Secret Life of Genes: Decoding the Blueprint of Life by Derek Harvey is an illustrated introduction to genetics and the ways genes make each of us unique. Readers also get a look at the Human Genome Project, a global effort that mapped all the genes in human DNA and opened up new fields of research. Clear text and illustrations make it a good choice for students and curious general readers interested in biology.

The Secret Life of the Brain: Unlocking the Mysteries of the Mind by Alfred David is an illustrated guide to how the human brain works. Neuroscience is still a young field with many open questions, and the book explores the advances made so far, from memory and intelligence to humour and dreams.

It also touches on why understanding the brain matters more than ever, with conditions such as Alzheimer's disease affecting an ageing population. Accessible and richly illustrated, it suits students and general readers who want to learn more about the organ that makes us who we are.

The God Delusion is Richard Dawkins's forceful case against religious belief, first published in 2006 and one of the most widely debated books of its time. The evolutionary biologist argues that belief in a supernatural creator is almost certainly mistaken and examines the harm he believes religion can do.

Dawkins takes on the classic arguments for God's existence, explores where religion and morality come from, and criticises the rise of fundamentalism and the challenge to science teaching posed by 'intelligent design'. Combative and provocative, it suits readers interested in science, philosophy and the debate between faith and reason, whatever their own views.

At its heart is Ailey Pearl Garfield, who carries the names of her great-grandmother Pearl and the dancer Alvin Ailey, and who grows up wrestling with what Du Bois called the problem of race and 'double consciousness'. Moving between Ailey's life in the city and the small Georgia town where her family's roots lie, the novel blends history, poetry and family secrets. Think and Grow Rich is Napoleon Hill's classic work of personal development, first published in 1937 and presented here in Vermilion's Life Essentials line. Although money features in the title, Hill argues that his philosophy applies to almost any goal, from building a career to transforming personal circumstances. Readers will find chapters on desire, faith, persistence, planning and the power of a focused mind, written in an energetic, motivational style. A foundational read for anyone interested in self-help, business thinking or the roots of modern success literature.

description:
Four Thousand Weeks: Time Management for Mortals is a book by Oliver Burkeman that takes a very different approach to productivity. It starts from a stark fact: if you live to eighty, you have only around four thousand weeks, and no system or life hack will ever let you fit everything in.

Rather than offering tips to cram more into each day, Burkeman argues that the endless pursuit of efficiency often makes us more anxious and less fulfilled. Drawing on philosophy and psychology, he encourages readers to accept their limits, make deliberate choices and focus on what matters most. A thoughtful, often funny read for anyone overwhelmed by their to-do list.

Surrounded by Vampires is Thomas Erikson's practical guide to spotting and handling the people who drain your time, energy and spirit, from the author of Surrounded by Idiots. Erikson sorts these so-called vampires into types, explaining how time suckers, energy suckers and soul suckers operate at work and in personal life.

Drawing on his background in human behaviour and communication, he offers strategies for setting boundaries, protecting your resources and dealing calmly with colleagues, friends or relatives who take more than they give. Readable and down to earth, it will appeal to fans of his earlier books and anyone who feels worn out by certain relationships.

attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Talking to Strangers is a book by Malcolm Gladwell, author of Outliers and The Tipping Point, about why our encounters with people we do not know so often go wrong. He asks how Fidel Castro deceived American intelligence for so long, and why Neville Chamberlain thought Hitler could be trusted.

Through a series of real cases, Gladwell examines the assumptions we make when judging strangers, such as defaulting to trust and believing that people's behaviour reveals what they feel, and shows how these habits can lead to misunderstanding and conflict. Engaging and thought-provoking, it suits readers interested in psychology, society and human behaviour.

  • Author: Malcolm Gladwell
  • Language: English

title: The Black Swan: The Impact of the Highly Improbable
sheet_title: The Black Swan The Impact Of The Highly Improbable
author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
description:
The Black Swan: The Impact of the Highly Improbable is Nassim Nicholas Taleb's influential study of rare, unpredictable events and the outsized role they play in history, markets and everyday life. A Black Swan, in Taleb's terms, is an occurrence that seems wildly unlikely, carries enormous consequences and is explained away only after it has happened.

Ranging across economics, philosophy and psychology, Taleb challenges our faith in forecasts and experts, and argues for building lives and institutions that can withstand shocks and profit from good surprises. Provocative and witty, it forms part of his Incerto series and is essential reading for anyone interested in risk, uncertainty and decision-making.

Things Have Gotten Worse Since We Last Spoke and Other Misfortunes collects three dark, unsettling horror stories by Eric LaRocca, including the title novella that became a viral sensation online.
