The other tales follow a grieving couple on a remote island who open their door to a stranger during a storm, and a man who confronts his neighbour after finding an odd object in his own garden. Intense and literary, it suits readers of extreme and psychological horror.

  • Author: Eric LaRocca
  • Publisher: Titan Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781803361499

title: Veggie Lean in 15
author: Joe Wicks
description:
Veggie Lean in 15 is the first vegetarian cookbook from Joe Wicks, the fitness coach known as The Body Coach. It brings the quick, healthy approach of his Lean in 15 books to meat-free cooking, with meals ready in about fifteen minutes.

Inside are 100 tasty meat-free recipes, a good number of them vegan as well, together with three of his HIIT workouts, a bonus abs workout and plenty of ideas for preparing meals ahead. Ideal for full-time vegetarians, part-time veggies and anyone hoping to eat less meat while staying fit.

  • Author: Joe Wicks
  • Publisher: Bluebird
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781509856152

title: Weyward
author: Emilia Hart
description:
Weyward is Emilia Hart's debut novel, weaving together the lives of three women from the same family across five centuries. In 2019, Kate flees London for a Cumbrian cottage left to her by her great-aunt; in 1942, Violet would rather climb trees and collect insects than become a proper young lady; and in 1619, Altha stands trial for witchcraft.

Linked by an uncanny bond with nature and a secret hidden in the cottage since the witch trials, each woman must find her own strength against those who would control her. Atmospheric and empowering, it is a compelling choice for readers of historical fiction with a touch of magic.

  • Author: Emilia Hart
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008499099

title: What Dogs Want
author: Mat Ward
description:
What Dogs Want: An Illustrated Guide for Happy Dog Care and Training is a friendly, illustrated guide from pet behaviourist Mat Ward to understanding what your dog is really trying to tell you. Every page features cartoons by Rupert Fawcett showing what is going on in a dog's head.

Readers learn to interpret body language and barking, and discover how dogs perceive and make sense of the world at every life stage. Ward champions modern, kind training based on love and encouragement, helping dogs feel secure and at home. Fun and practical, it suits new puppy owners and experienced dog lovers alike.

  • Author: Mat Ward
  • Illustrator: Rupert Fawcett
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781526639950

title: Winter Roses after Fall
author: R.H. Sin and Robert M. Drake
description:
Winter Roses after Fall is a collection of poetry and prose by R.H. Sin and Robert M. Drake, the authors of Empty Bottles Full of Stories and Falling Toward the Moon.

Framed by the image of a cold, melancholy season and a rose that blooms in spite of it, the pieces speak to anyone looking for warmth in hard times and hoping to grow through them. Emotional and direct, it suits readers of contemporary poetry who enjoy short, heartfelt writing.

  • Authors: R.H. Sin and Robert M. Drake
  • Publisher: Andrews McMeel Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781524867898

title: You Are Not So Smart
author: David McRaney
description:
You Are Not So Smart by David McRaney is an entertaining tour of the self-deceptions that shape the way we think, which grew out of his popular blog. It challenges the comfortable belief that our choices are guided by calm, rational logic.

In short chapters on subjects such as learned helplessness and the illusion of transparency, McRaney explains the stories we tell ourselves to account for our decisions, memories and feelings, and why those stories are so often untrue. Witty and eye-opening, it is ideal for readers who enjoy popular psychology and want a clearer view of their own blind spots.

  • Author: David McRaney
  • Publisher: Avery
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781592407361

title: The Last Ever After
author: Soman Chainani
description:
The Last Ever After is the third book in Soman Chainani's School for Good and Evil series and the epic conclusion of its original story arc. After A World Without Princes, Sophie and Agatha, once best friends, have parted ways, with Agatha returning to Gavaldon alongside Tedros while Sophie remains with the School Master.

But Evil has taken control, and villains from old fairy tales are returning to rewrite their stories and upset the balance between Good and Evil. Full of magic, twists and questions about friendship, love and identity, it is a satisfying finale for fans of the series.

  • Author: Soman Chainani
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 672 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The School for Good and Evil, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780007502868

title: The Upside of Irrationality
author: Dan Ariely
description:
The Upside of Irrationality: The Unexpected Benefits of Defying Logic is behavioural economist Dan Ariely's follow-up to Predictably Irrational. It examines the irrational forces behind our choices at work, in dating and in the temptation to cheat, and the surprising ways they can work in our favour.

Ariely asks why very large bonuses can make executives perform worse, why revenge matters so much to us, and why we value what we have built ourselves so highly. Drawing on lively experiments, it suits readers of popular psychology and economics who enjoy books such as Freakonomics.

  • Author: Dan Ariely
  • Publisher: Harper Perennial
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780061995040

title: Wotakoi: Love Is Hard for Otaku, Vol. 2
sheet_title: Wotakoi: Love Is Hard For Otaku 2
author: Fujita
description:
Wotakoi: Love Is Hard for Otaku, Vol. 2 continues Fujita's romantic comedy manga about geeky office workers trying to make love work. Frustrated by how slowly things are moving, Hirotaka invites Narumi out on a proper date, with one strict condition: neither of them may show their otaku side.

Without games, manga or anime to fall back on, can they find anything else in common? Meanwhile, Hanako and Taro look back on how their stormy romance began in high school, and Naoya appears to be making a new friend. Funny and sweet, Volume 2 suits fans of workplace romance and slice-of-life manga.

  • Author: Fujita
  • Publisher: Kodansha Comics
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Wotakoi: Love Is Hard for Otaku, Volume 2
  • ISBN: 9781632367051

title: The Yoga Plate
author: Tamal Dodge and Victoria Dodge
description:
The Yoga Plate by Tamal and Victoria Dodge brings yoga practice into the kitchen with 108 simple, nourishing vegan recipes. It is presented as the first modern cookbook to connect nutrition with ahimsa, the yogic principle of non-harming.

The authors argue that the way we eat is a central part of an effective practice, reflecting the way we care for ourselves, our families, animals and the planet. Combining plant-based cooking with yogic philosophy, it suits yoga practitioners, vegans and anyone looking for wholesome meat-free meals with a mindful approach.

  • Authors: Tamal Dodge and Victoria Dodge
  • Publisher: Sounds True
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781683643500

title: The Silva Mind Control Method
author: José Silva
description:
The Silva Mind Control Method is José Silva's guide to the programme he developed in the 1960s, which uses meditation and visualisation to help people change their lives. First published in 1978, it has long been a familiar title in the self-development field.

The book teaches techniques for easing stress, breaking bad habits, overcoming emotional insecurity, sharpening concentration and creativity, working with dreams and deepening relationships, illustrated with case studies. Accessible and practical, it suits readers interested in meditation, the power of the mind and personal growth.

  • Author: José Silva
  • Publisher: Gallery Books
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781982185602

title: The World's Worst Children
author: David Walliams
description:
The World's Worst Children is David Walliams' collection of ten wickedly funny cautionary tales about five beastly boys and five equally ghastly girls, illustrated in full colour by Tony Ross.

Meet Sofia Sofa, a television fan so stuck to her seat that she starts turning into one, Dribbling Drew, whose drool causes chaos on a school trip, and Blubbering Bertha, who sobs and spins dreadful fibs, while Raj, a favourite with fans, pops up too. Mischievous and gloriously silly, it makes a perfect gift for young readers and a great book for sharing aloud.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The World's Worst Children, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780008197049

title: The World's Worst Pets
author: David Walliams
description:
The World's Worst Pets is a collection of ten hilarious stories by David Walliams about the most outrageous animals imaginable, with colourful pictures throughout by Adam Stower. It follows his earlier collections about the world's worst children, teachers and parents.

Readers meet Houdini, the magician's rabbit, Zoom, the supersonic tortoise, Griselda, a grizzly hiding something big, and Furp, a truly monstrous goldfish. Packed with chaos and silliness, it is perfect for young readers who love funny stories and for anyone who has ever wondered what their pet gets up to.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Adam Stower
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 312 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008499778

title: What Happens While You Sleep
author: Anna Russelmann
description:
What Happens While You Sleep is a picture book by Anna Russelmann that explains, in a gentle and playful way, what goes on in the brain during sleep. When Malu goes to bed, two helpers called Hippo and Campus sort through everything she experienced that day, and even track down her missing teddy.

The story shows children why getting enough sleep is so important, while soft watercolour and chalk illustrations capture the dreamy mood of night-time. A lovely bedtime read that doubles as a clever introduction to how memory works.

  • Author: Anna Russelmann
  • Publisher: NorthSouth Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 48 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780735844469

title: Winter
author: Marissa Meyer
description:
Winter is the fourth and final novel in Marissa Meyer's Lunar Chronicles, the young adult series that reimagines classic fairy tales as science fiction. Princess Winter, stepdaughter of the cruel Lunar queen Levana, is loved by her people for her gentleness and grace, even though her face is scarred.

As the story reaches its climax, the series' fairy-tale heroines join forces with Winter to defeat Levana once and for all. Inspired by Snow White and full of romance, action and space-age intrigue, this hefty finale suits fans of the series and of inventive fairy-tale retellings. This edition features new cover art.

  • Author: Marissa Meyer
  • Publisher: Square Fish
  • Format: Paperback, 823 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Lunar Chronicles, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9781250768926

title: In a Nutshell: Cooking and Baking with Nuts and Seeds
author: Cara Tannenbaum and Andrea Tutunjian
description:
In a Nutshell: Cooking and Baking with Nuts and Seeds is a thorough handbook for cooking with nuts and seeds by Cara Tannenbaum and Andrea Tutunjian, who spent years on the teaching staff of the Institute of Culinary Education.

It offers more than 250 recipes, from pumpkin seed guacamole to a hazelnut roulade, along with the food history and cultural background of these versatile, nutritious ingredients. Chapters reflect the way people eat today, with sections such as Nibbles, Dip It and Noodles and Nuts, and there are dishes for omnivores, vegetarians and vegans alike. A rewarding book for keen home cooks and bakers.

  • Authors: Cara Tannenbaum and Andrea Tutunjian
  • Publisher: W. W. Norton & Company
  • Format: Hardcover, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780393065589

title: The World's Worst Parents
author: David Walliams
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
The World's Worst Parents is a collection of comic stories by David Walliams, illustrated in full colour by Tony Ross. Following The World's Worst Children and The World's Worst Teachers, it introduces ten parents who are far more than just embarrassing.

Each tale features a mum or dad whose behaviour is spectacularly, outrageously awful, told with Walliams's trademark mix of silliness and mischief. The short, self-contained stories and lively illustrations make it ideal for reading aloud or for young readers who want something quick and funny, and it is a natural next step for fans of his other collections.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Language: English

title: رسائل من مصر
author: Lucie Duff-Gordon
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Lucie Duff-Gordon's Letters from Egypt (رسائل من مصر), translated by the Egyptian novelist Ibrahim Abdel Meguid. The English writer and translator came to Egypt in 1862 hoping its dry climate would help her recover from tuberculosis, and she stayed until her death there in 1869.

Written to her husband, mother and daughter, the letters paint a vivid, affectionate picture of everyday Egyptian life, from religious tolerance and saints' festivals in Luxor to the hardships people endured under Khedive Ismail. A rich read for anyone interested in nineteenth-century Egypt, travel writing and history.

  • Author: Lucie Duff-Gordon
  • Translator: Ibrahim Abdel Meguid
  • Publisher: Bayt Al Yasmin
  • Pages: 517
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778171907

title: مثلجات القمر
author: Baek Heena
description:
Moon Sherbet (مثلجات القمر) is the Arabic edition of a children's picture book by the Korean author and illustrator Baek Heena. On a sweltering summer night the moon begins to melt, and a resourceful grandmother turns it into a cool, sweet treat.

A short and charming story, it makes a lovely bedtime read for children and families reading in Arabic.

  • Author: Baek Heena
  • Publisher: Dar Al Muna
  • Format: Hardcover
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789188863089

title: مسرى الغرانيق في مدن العقيق
author: Omaima Al-Khamis
description:
The Journey of the Cranes in the Cities of Agate (مسرى الغرانيق في مدن العقيق) is a historical novel in Arabic by the Saudi writer Omaima Al-Khamis, published in English as The Book Smuggler. It follows Mazid al-Hanafi, a young man from the heart of the Arabian Peninsula who suddenly finds himself entrusted with a dangerous mission.

Given seven commandments that he must forget once he has read them, Mazid travels from Baghdad to Jerusalem, Cairo, Kairouan and al-Andalus. His love of books, and his failure to obey every rule, bring his journey to an ending he never expected. A richly imagined voyage through the medieval Islamic world for lovers of literary historical fiction.

  • Author: Omaima Al-Khamis
  • Publisher: Dar Al Saqi
  • Format: Paperback, 559 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786140320659

title: من يرى ديم
attention: Identified from its cover photo (checked by eye); description is brief — add details from the copy
description:
Who Sees Deem? (من يرى ديم) is a book in Arabic. Its title asks who is able to see Deem, a name that points to the character at the centre of the book.

  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789189464346

title: اسمي أحمر
author: Orhan Pamuk
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Orhan Pamuk's My Name Is Red (اسمي أحمر), translated by Abdulkader Abdelli. Set in sixteenth-century Istanbul, the novel revolves around the murder of a miniaturist and the hunt for his killer among the Ottoman court's painters and illuminators.

Pamuk tells the story through many voices, among them the murdered man's corpse, a dog and even Satan, while immersing readers in the world of Islamic miniature painting, book illumination and the rivalries of the artists who practised it. A rich blend of mystery, history and philosophy from the Nobel Prize-winning Turkish author, ideal for lovers of literary fiction.

  • Author: Orhan Pamuk
  • Translator: Abdulkader Abdelli
  • Publisher: Dar El Shorouk
  • Format: Paperback, 538 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789770933671

title: الحراس
author: Alan Moore
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Watchmen (الحراس), the landmark graphic novel by writer Alan Moore and artist Dave Gibbons, translated by Ahmad Gamal Saad-Eddin. This Noir edition presents the artwork in black and white and collects the complete twelve-issue series in one volume.

It follows a group of former costumed heroes who have drifted back into ordinary lives, weighed down by a tangled history of alliances and rivalries, until a killer begins targeting them one by one. Regarded by many critics as the most important graphic novel ever made, it is essential reading for comics fans and readers of serious fiction.

  • Author: Alan Moore
  • Translator: Ahmad Gamal Saad-Eddin
  • Illustrator: Dave Gibbons
  • Publisher: Al Mahrousa Center for Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Watchmen, complete (issues 1-12)
  • ISBN: 9789773138882

title: الكتاب الذي لا يريد أن يكون مقروءا
sheet_title: الكتاب الذي لا يريد أن يكون مقروءا
author: David Sundin
description:
This is the Arabic edition of The Book That Did Not Want to Be Read (الكتاب الذي لا يريد أن يكون مقروءا), a playful picture book by the Swedish author David Sundin. From the very start, the book itself warns readers to stop, insisting it would much rather stay closed.

If they keep going, anything could happen: alligators may turn up and the book might even attempt to fly off. Interactive and full of humour, it is a delightful read-aloud that turns reading into a game, perfect for children and parents sharing stories in Arabic.

  • Author: David Sundin
  • Publisher: Dar Al Muna
  • Format: Hardcover
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789189464223

title: النار والعنقاء 2: صقر قريش
author: Walid Saif
description:
The Falcon of Quraysh (صقر قريش) is a historical novel in Arabic by the Palestinian-Jordanian writer and dramatist Walid Saif, and the second part of his Fire and the Phoenix series. It revisits the story of Abd al-Rahman I, the Umayyad prince known as the Falcon of Quraysh, who escaped the fall of his dynasty and went on to rule in al-Andalus.

Passages in the voice of Badr, the loyal companion who shared his long road, reflect on ambition, loyalty and what remains of a man once power has been won. Rich in history and character, it suits readers of Arabic historical fiction and anyone fascinated by the story of al-Andalus.

  • Author: Walid Saif
  • Publisher: Al-Ahlia Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 563 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The Fire and the Phoenix, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9789957393908

title: سلاحف إلى ما لا نهاية
sheet_title: سلاحف إلى ما لا نهاية شركة المطبوعات
author: John Green
description:
This is the Arabic edition of John Green's Turtles All the Way Down (سلاحف إلى ما لا نهاية), translated by Hajar Al-Musleh. Sixteen-year-old Aza never meant to chase the mystery of the vanished billionaire Russell Pickett, but a large reward is on offer and her bold best friend Daisy is keen to look into it.

Their search leads them to Pickett's son Davis, while Aza does her best as a daughter, friend and student as her obsessive thoughts keep pulling her inward. Tender and honest about living with anxiety, it is a moving young adult novel from the author of The Fault in Our Stars.

  • Author: John Green
  • Translator: Hajar Al-Musleh
  • Publisher: All Prints Distributors & Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 305 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953889948

title: كرينشو
author: Katherine Applegate
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Katherine Applegate's Crenshaw (كرينشو), translated by Sakina Ibrahim. Crenshaw is a very large cat, outspoken, bold and funny, and entirely imaginary, who has returned to young Jackson's life just when he needs help.

Jackson's family has lost almost everything, and the story asks whether an imaginary friend can be enough to see them through. Written with warmth and gentle humour, it shows that friends matter whether they are real or imagined, and it treats a difficult subject with real sensitivity. A touching read for children and families.

  • Author: Katherine Applegate
  • Translator: Sakina Ibrahim
  • Publisher: Dar Al Muna
  • Format: Hardcover, 227 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789188863553

attention: Identified from its cover photo (checked by eye); description is brief — add details from the copy
description:
The Wound (الجرح) is a book in Arabic. Its one-word title means a wound or injury.

  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789189464506

title: جمهورية الظلام
author: Fawwaz Haddad
description:
The Republic of Darkness (جمهورية الظلام) is a novel in Arabic by the Syrian writer Fawwaz Haddad. Its jacket excerpt describes a regime presented as a miracle, born of successive coups and kept alive by conspiracies, assassinations, executions, wars and prisons, which its loyalists believe is destined to last forever.

Against the backdrop of a war that serves to entrench that power, the novel examines dictatorship, inherited rule and the forces that sustain them. A bold political novel for readers of contemporary Arabic fiction.

  • Author: Fawwaz Haddad
  • Publisher: Riad El-Rayyes Books
  • Format: Paperback, 477 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953217574

title: ماذا تختار؟ موزة خضراء أم موزة صفراء
sheet_title: إخـياراً لصحة وحياة أفضل : ماذا تختار ؟
author: Ahmed Abdulmalik
description:
What Do You Choose? Green Banana or Yellow Banana (ماذا تختار؟ موزة خضراء أم موزة صفراء) is a practical health guide in Arabic by Ahmed Abdulmalik. It sets out a scientific way of making everyday decisions about food and health.

Across 50 common dilemmas, such as ketchup or mayonnaise, rice or bread, an orange or a vitamin C tablet, a vegetarian diet or meat, and laser surgery or contact lenses, it helps readers weigh up the options for themselves and their families. Clear and accessible, it suits anyone wanting to make healthier choices for a better life.

  • Author: Ahmed Abdulmalik
  • Publisher: Dhat Al Salasil Publications
  • Format: Paperback, 357 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789996680557

title: Trouble
author: Lex Croucher
description:
Trouble is a witty historical romance by Lex Croucher about a governess who is not what she seems. Emily Laurence has taken a post at Fairmont House under false pretences: the job was meant for her kind, clever sister Amy, while Emily is impolite, reckless, constantly angry and has no teaching experience whatsoever.

With Amy unwell, their father gone and their mother no help, Emily plans to stay undiscovered until she has collected some pay and pocketed a few valuables, as long as she stays out of the Edwards family's dramas. A lively, queer period romp for fans of irreverent historical romance.

  • Author: Lex Croucher
  • Publisher: Zaffre
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804180983

title: Soft Rattle & Teether: Woof Puppy
attention: Identified from its cover photo (checked by eye); description is brief — add details from the copy
description:
Soft Rattle & Teether: Woof Puppy is a soft baby item with a puppy theme which, as its name says, works as both a rattle and a teether.

Its friendly puppy character makes it a sweet small gift for a new arrival.

  • ISBN: 9789464543520

title: It's a Magical World
author: Bill Watterson
description:
It's a Magical World is the final collection of Bill Watterson's much-loved comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, gathering strips from the last stretch of its run, including full-colour Sunday pages. It follows imaginative six-year-old Calvin and his tiger Hobbes through more adventures and mischief.

Calvin's patient parents, his classmate Susie Derkins, his teacher Miss Wormwood and the babysitter Rosalyn all appear, along with his alter ego Spaceman Spiff battling aliens across the galaxy. Funny, clever and surprisingly profound, it is a treat for longtime fans and a fine introduction for new readers of all ages. Book 11 in the Calvin and Hobbes series.

  • Author: Bill Watterson
  • Publisher: Andrews McMeel Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Calvin and Hobbes, Book 11
  • ISBN: 9780836221367

title: Mad Honey
author: Jodi Picoult and Jennifer Finney Boylan
description:
Mad Honey is a moving novel by Jodi Picoult and Jennifer Finney Boylan about secrets, fresh starts and what we choose to carry from the past. After her seemingly perfect life in Boston fell apart when her husband showed a darker side, Olivia McAfee has returned to her small New Hampshire hometown, running the beekeeping business her father left while raising her son, Asher.

Lily Campanello and her mother have also moved to town, hoping for a new beginning before Lily's last year of high school. When Asher falls for Lily, their families' paths become entwined, until a tragedy changes everything. Gripping and thought-provoking, it is ideal for book clubs and fans of emotionally charged fiction.

  • Authors: Jodi Picoult and Jennifer Finney Boylan
  • Publisher: Hodder & Stoughton
  • Format: Paperback, 453 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781473692466

title: Ravensong
author: T.J. Klune
description:
Ravensong is the second book in T.J. Klune's Green Creek series, a paranormal fantasy romance of werewolves, witches and the bonds of a pack. Gordo Livingstone, embittered after being abandoned by his pack years ago, has tried to stay out of wolf business, keeping to his garage in a small mountain town.

Now, a year after the pack's victory over Richard Collins, Gordo is once again witch to the Bennett pack and struggling to ignore Mark Bennett and the bond between them. But a new threat is stirring, this time from within. Emotional and atmospheric, it suits fans of queer fantasy romance and found-family stories.

  • Author: T.J. Klune
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 576 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Green Creek, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781035002184

title: README.txt : A Memoir
author: Chelsea Manning
description:
README.txt is the memoir of Chelsea Manning, the former US Army intelligence analyst who, while posted to Iraq in 2010, passed hundreds of thousands of secret military and diplomatic files to the public. She recounts her arrest and trial, the long sentence that followed, and its commutation by President Obama in 2017.

Running alongside the story of the leaks is a deeply personal one: Manning's decision to live openly as a trans woman the day after her conviction, and her legal fight for medical care while in prison. It is a candid read on secrecy, accountability, identity and the cost of speaking out, for anyone interested in politics, technology and civil liberties.

  • Author: Chelsea Manning
  • Publisher: Bodley Head
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847925626

title: Speak! Overcoming the Fear and Horror of Public Speaking
sheet_title: Speak! Overcoming the Fear and Horror of Public Speaking
author: Dale Carnegie & Associates
description:
Speak! is a practical guide from Dale Carnegie & Associates, the training organisation that carries Dale Carnegie's name, written for anyone who dreads standing up in front of an audience. Its central idea is that nerves begin to fade once a speaker stops worrying about themselves and starts thinking about the people listening.

The book shows how to shape a message around what an audience needs, deliver it sincerely and let your own personality come through rather than hiding behind a script. It suits professionals, students and anyone preparing for presentations, meetings or speeches who wants to speak with more confidence and far less anxiety.

  • Author: Dale Carnegie & Associates
  • Publisher: G&D Media
  • Format: Paperback, 238 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781722505592

title: The Bookseller's Notebooks
author: Jalal Barjas
description:
The Bookseller's Notebooks is the English translation of Jordanian author Jalal Barjas's novel, which won the International Prize for Arabic Fiction in 2021. Its hero, Ibrahim al-Warraq, is a cultured bookseller and avid reader who, after losing his livelihood and his home, goes to live among the homeless and starts taking on the identities of characters from his favourite novels.

Spanning the years 1947 to 2019 and built from a series of interlinked notebooks, the novel draws together people who have lost their homes or never known their families. Translated by Paul G. Starkey, it explores loneliness, mental illness, justice and belonging, and suits readers of contemporary Arabic literature in translation.

  • Author: Jalal Barjas
  • Translator: Paul G. Starkey
  • Publisher: Interlink Books
  • Format: Paperback, 324 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781623718206

title: THE FOURTH MAN
author: Robert B. Baer
description:
The Fourth Man is a work of espionage nonfiction by Robert B. Baer, a former CIA officer. After the Cold War, American intelligence unmasked three high-profile spies working for Moscow, yet suspicions lingered that another mole had climbed to the very top of the CIA. Baer tells the story of the search for this hidden traitor, known as the Fourth Man.

At the heart of the account are three experienced women from counterintelligence who were given the job of finding him, and the troubling conclusion they reached. Drawing on insider knowledge, Baer connects that hunt to the rise of Putin's Russia, making this a compelling read for fans of true spy stories and Cold War history.

  • Author: Robert B. Baer
  • Publisher: Monoray
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800960503

title: The Passenger
author: Cormac McCarthy
description:
The Passenger is a novel by Cormac McCarthy, the first of his two linked final books. In 1980, salvage diver Bobby Western goes down to a jet that has sunk off the Mississippi coast and finds nine passengers still strapped in, while the pilot's flight bag, the black box and a tenth passenger have vanished.

Soon he is followed by men with badges and haunted by memories of his father, a physicist who helped create the atomic bomb, and of his brilliant sister Alicia. Moving from New Orleans bars to the Florida coast, the novel ranges over guilt, grief, science and morality, and is paired with its companion, Stella Maris.

  • Author: Cormac McCarthy
  • Publisher: Picador
  • Format: Paperback, 383 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Passenger, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780330535519

title: The Three Questions: How to Discover and Master the Power Within You
sheet_title: THE THREE QUESTIONS INTL HOW TO DISCOVER AND MASTER THE POWE
author: Don Miguel Ruiz
description:
The Three Questions is a spiritual guide by Don Miguel Ruiz, written with Barbara Emrys, that builds on his earlier book The Four Agreements. Rooted in the Toltec wisdom tradition of ancient Mexico, it centres on three simple but searching questions: who am I, what is truly real, and how we give expression to love.

Ruiz suggests that answering these honestly can free us from fear and false beliefs and help us use our personal power more wisely at every stage of life. Gentle and reflective in tone, it suits readers of The Four Agreements and anyone exploring spirituality, self-knowledge and personal growth.

  • Author: Don Miguel Ruiz
  • Co-author: Barbara Emrys
  • Publisher: HarperOne
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780062881564

title: The Wager
author: David Grann
description:
The Wager is David Grann's account of a real eighteenth-century naval disaster. In 1740 the British warship Wager sailed with a squadron on a secret mission to seize a Spanish treasure galleon, only to be wrecked off the coast of Patagonia. Months later, a battered boat carrying about thirty starving survivors reached Brazil, and its crew were welcomed as heroes.

Then three more castaways landed in Chile with a very different story, accusing the first group of mutiny. Grann pieces together the competing accounts, the brutal realities of life at sea and the court martial that followed, creating a gripping true story of shipwreck, survival, loyalty and how history gets told.

  • Author: David Grann
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster UK
  • Format: Paperback, 329 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781471183683

title: This Arab Life: A Generation's Journey into Silence
sheet_title: This Arab Life: A Generations Journey Into Silence
author: Amal Ghandour
description:
This Arab Life: A Generation's Journey into Silence is a memoir by Amal Ghandour, a writer born to Lebanese parents who grew up largely in Jordan. It traces how a generation of Arabs who came of age amid the region's turbulent politics gradually fell silent. The narrative opens in the Jordanian capital in mid-1973 and closes in Beirut at the end of 2021.

Blending personal memory with wider history, Ghandour turns a critical eye on her own privileged class and its part in the story rather than standing apart from it. Candid and reflective, it is a strong choice for readers interested in the modern Middle East, Jordan and Lebanon, and the personal side of political history.

  • Author: Amal Ghandour
  • Publisher: Bold Story Press
  • Format: Paperback, 178 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781954805262

title: When Things Don't Go Your Way
sheet_title: When Things Don T Go Your Way
author: Haemin Sunim
description:
When Things Don't Go Your Way: Zen Wisdom for Difficult Times is a book of gentle guidance from Korean Zen Buddhist teacher Haemin Sunim, translated by Charles La Shure. It starts from the idea that painful periods of loss, loneliness, rejection and uncertainty can also become chances to grow and to understand ourselves better.

In the style of his earlier books, Haemin Sunim combines short reflections, personal stories and calm, quotable sayings with soft illustrations, so it can be read in one sitting or dipped into when needed. It suits anyone going through a hard time or simply looking to care for their emotional wellbeing with more patience and kindness.

  • Author: Haemin Sunim
  • Translator: Charles La Shure
  • Publisher: Penguin Life
  • Format: Hardcover, 296 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241457290

title: How To Build A Boat
author: Elaine Feeney
description:
How to Build a Boat is a novel by Irish poet and novelist Elaine Feeney. Set in a small town in the west of Ireland, it follows thirteen-year-old Jamie O'Neill, a boy with a remarkable mind who longs to feel close to the mother he never knew, and two adults at his school who are drawn into his plans.

As the three of them work together on building a boat, their lives begin to change in ways none of them expected. Warm, funny and tender, the novel explores belonging, grief, friendship and what it means to be different, and is a fine pick for book clubs and readers of contemporary Irish fiction.

  • Author: Elaine Feeney
  • Publisher: Harvill Secker
  • Format: Paperback, 298 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781787303461

title: Lean in 15 - the Sustain Plan
author: Joe Wicks
description:
Lean in 15 - The Sustain Plan is a fitness cookbook from Joe Wicks, The Body Coach, designed to help readers hold on to their results and keep making progress. It pairs one hundred quick recipes, built around fifteen-minute cooking, with four workouts aimed at shedding fat and building lean muscle.

Fully illustrated and made for busy lives, the plan shows how to combine tasty, nourishing meals with a fresh training programme without long sessions at the stove or in the gym. It is a natural next step for readers of the earlier Lean in 15 books and anyone wanting a sustainable approach to healthy eating and exercise.

  • Author: Joe Wicks
  • Publisher: Bluebird
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781509820221

title: Me Vs Brain
author: Hayley Morris
description:
Me vs Brain: An Overthinker's Guide to Life is a funny, confessional book from comedian Hayley Morris, known for her online comedy sketches. Written in a chatty, self-deprecating voice, it sets out to reassure readers that the embarrassing thoughts and worries they keep to themselves are far more common than they think.

Morris covers everything from dating and bodies to mental health and periods, turning anxious late-night spirals into material for laughs. Frank, warm and relatable, it suits anyone who replays awkward moments in the middle of the night and would like some company in the overthinking.

  • Author: Hayley Morris
  • Publisher: Century
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529916782

title: Reason to Be Happy
author: Kaushik Basu
description:
Reason to Be Happy: Why Logical Thinking Is the Key to a Better Life is a book by economist Kaushik Basu, a former chief economist of the World Bank. Using puzzles and thought experiments, such as why friends tend to be better connected than we are, he shows how clear reasoning and game theory can improve everyday decisions.

Basu argues that acting sensibly often means imagining how a clever rival will respond, an idea he applies to situations ranging from the Cuban Missile Crisis to the challenge of letting go of anger. Engaging and accessible, it suits curious readers who enjoy popular economics and want to think more clearly in work and life.

  • Author: Kaushik Basu
  • Publisher: Torva
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781911709282

title: Sandman Volume 10: The Wake 30th Anniversary Edition
sheet_title: Sandman Volume 10: The Wake 30th Anniversary Edition
author: Neil Gaiman
description:
The Sandman Vol. 10: The Wake is the closing volume of Neil Gaiman's celebrated fantasy comic series, presented in the 30th anniversary edition with a new cover by Dave McKean. After the events of the previous book, the Endless, their allies and old enemies gather to mourn Dream, the Lord of Dreams, as a new Dream takes his place.

Collecting issues #70 to #75, with art by Michael Zulli, Jon J. Muth and Charles Vess, it offers a moving farewell to the saga, ending with the story of Shakespeare writing The Tempest. It is essential reading for anyone completing the series and is best enjoyed after the nine earlier volumes.

  • Author: Neil Gaiman
  • Illustrators: Michael Zulli, Jon J. Muth, Charles Vess
  • Publisher: DC Vertigo
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Sandman, Volume 10
  • ISBN: 9781401292034

title: The Aromatherapy Companion
author: Jade Shutes and Amy Galper
description:
The Aromatherapy Companion is a portable guide to essential oils by aromatherapy educator Jade Shutes and Amy Galper, a graduate of her training. A condensed version of their larger Ultimate Guide to Aromatherapy, it explains how essential oils work with our sense of smell, our brain and our skin.

Alongside more than 35 plant profiles, the book offers blends and recipes for health and beauty, with remedies covering areas such as digestion, immunity and women's health. Practical and compact, it suits beginners and home practitioners who want to make their own natural preparations for body, mind and spirit.

  • Author: Jade Shutes and Amy Galper
  • Publisher: Fair Winds Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780760377918

title: The Bullet That Missed
author: Richard Osman
description:
The Bullet That Missed is the third Thursday Murder Club mystery by Richard Osman, featuring the crime-solving pensioners of the Coopers Chase retirement village. A ten-year-old cold case leads Elizabeth, Joyce, Ron and Ibrahim to a much-loved local television presenter and a killing in which no body was ever found.

Meanwhile, Elizabeth receives a visit from a dangerous new adversary who gives her a stark choice: kill or be killed. Combining clever plotting with warmth and gentle humour, this cosy crime novel is perfect for fans of the series and readers who like their murder mysteries witty and character-driven.

  • Author: Richard Osman
  • Publisher: Viking
  • Format: Paperback, 413 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Thursday Murder Club, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780241512432

title: The Gift Of Intensity
author: Imi Lo
description:
The Gift of Intensity is a self-help book by Imi Lo for people who feel things deeply and often sense that they do not quite fit in. It sets out to show that being highly sensitive and emotionally intense is a strength to understand and use, not a flaw to be fixed.

Drawing on her clinical work and her own experience, Lo offers practical steps for handling low self-esteem, family tension, loneliness, workplace pressures and moments of emotional crisis, as well as for building healthier relationships in love and work. It suits sensitive readers and the people who care about them.

  • Author: Imi Lo
  • Publisher: John Murray One
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529341164

title: The Sandman Vol. 8: Worlds' End
sheet_title: The Sandman Volume 8: Worlds End 30th Anniversary Edition
author: Neil Gaiman
description:
The Sandman Vol. 8: Worlds' End is the eighth collected volume of Neil Gaiman's landmark comic series, in the 30th anniversary edition with a new Dave McKean cover. Caught in a freak summer snowstorm, two travellers take shelter at a strange inn where guests from many times and realities are waiting out a so-called reality storm.

To pass the time, the guests take turns telling stories, in a structure that echoes The Canterbury Tales: tales of sea monsters, cities that dream, ancient kings and an extraordinary funeral among them. Collecting issues #51 to #56, with Bryan Talbot among its artists, it is a rich anthology that shows the full range of the Sandman world.

  • Author: Neil Gaiman
  • Illustrator: Bryan Talbot
  • Publisher: DC Vertigo
  • Format: Paperback, 168 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Sandman, Volume 8
  • ISBN: 9781401289591

title: Harlem Shuffle
author: Colson Whitehead
description:
Harlem Shuffle is a crime novel by Colson Whitehead, whose books The Underground Railroad and The Nickel Boys each won the Pulitzer Prize. In early-1960s Harlem, Ray Carney sells affordable furniture on 125th Street and is working hard to build a respectable life for his growing family.

Yet Carney comes from a line of small-time crooks, money is tight, and his cousin Freddie keeps steering stolen goods his way, until a botched heist at the Hotel Theresa pulls him deep into the city's underworld. Stylish, funny and rich in period detail, it opens Whitehead's Harlem trilogy and suits fans of literary crime and historical fiction.

  • Author: Colson Whitehead
  • Publisher: Fleet
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Harlem Trilogy, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780708899465

title: How Not to F*ck Up Your Startup
sheet_title: How Not To FCk Up Your Startup : Lessons On Buil
author: Tom Fairey
description:
How Not to F*ck Up Your Startup is a no-nonsense guide by Tom Fairey for anyone hoping to turn a promising idea into a funded, growing business. It walks through the big questions founders face, from shaping a product and assembling a strong team to raising money and taking on the market.

Fairey pairs his own expertise with hard-won advice from founders with first-hand experience, flagging the common traps that sink new ventures before they find their feet. Direct and practical, it suits first-time entrepreneurs who sense they have a big opportunity but are unsure where to begin.

  • Author: Tom Fairey
  • Publisher: Robinson
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781472147523

title: Invasion: Inside Russia's War on Ukraine
sheet_title: Invasion Inside Russias War on Ukraine
author: Luke Harding
description:
Invasion: Inside Russia's War on Ukraine is an early account of the full-scale war by Luke Harding, a foreign correspondent for The Guardian who had long warned of Vladimir Putin's ambitions. Opening with the months of ominous signs that preceded the assault of February 2022, it shows how the Kremlin set out to swallow a neighbouring nation.

Reporting from the ground through the first months of the conflict, Harding gathers human stories of loss and courage while contrasting the two leaders at its centre, Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Vladimir Putin. Vivid and urgent, it is an important read for anyone seeking to understand the war and its global consequences.

  • Author: Luke Harding
  • Publisher: Guardian Books
  • Format: Paperback, 328 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781783352760

title: Our Missing Hearts
author: Celeste Ng
description:
Our Missing Hearts is a novel by Celeste Ng about a mother's love in a society ruled by fear. Bird Gardner, aged twelve, lives quietly with his father, a former linguist now shelving books at a university library, in an America where laws meant to protect 'American culture' let the authorities take children from dissident families, especially those of Asian descent.

His mother, Margaret, a poet of Chinese American heritage whose work has been pulled from libraries, left when he was nine. When a mysterious letter arrives, Bird sets out to find her and to learn the truth about her disappearance. Moving and timely, it suits readers of literary dystopian fiction and book clubs.

  • Author: Celeste Ng
  • Publisher: Abacus Books
  • Format: Paperback, 331 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781408716922

title: The Sandman Vol. 5: A Game of You
author: Neil Gaiman
description:
The Sandman Vol. 5: A Game of You collects a fan-favourite storyline from Neil Gaiman's acclaimed comic series, in the 30th anniversary edition with a new cover by Dave McKean. It brings back Barbie, first seen in The Doll's House, who learns that she is the princess of a vivid dream kingdom now menaced by a sinister figure called the Cuckoo.

Moving between Barbie's New York apartment building, home to an unforgettable group of neighbours, and the dreamland she must save, the story explores identity, friendship and the power of fantasy. Collecting issues #32 to #37, with art by Shawn McManus, Colleen Doran, Bryan Talbot and Stan Woch, it is a highlight for fans of the series.

  • Author: Neil Gaiman
  • Illustrators: Shawn McManus, Colleen Doran, Bryan Talbot, Stan Woch
  • Publisher: DC Vertigo
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Sandman, Volume 5
  • ISBN: 9781401288075

title: The Familiar
author: Leigh Bardugo
description:
The Familiar is a historical fantasy novel by Leigh Bardugo, set in Madrid during Spain's Golden Age. Luzia Cotado is a scullion who relies on tiny, secret miracles to survive her gruelling work in a shabby household, until her scheming mistress discovers the gift and decides to use it to climb the social ladder.

Luzia's talent soon catches the attention of the disgraced royal secretary Antonio Pérez, who sees in her a way back into royal favour after the defeat of the Armada. Drawn into a dangerous world of alchemists, mystics and tricksters, she must fight for her future in a story of ambition, faith, love and power.

  • Author: Leigh Bardugo
  • Publisher: Viking
  • Format: Paperback, 385 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241655313

title: The Power of Regret
author: Daniel H. Pink
description:
The Power of Regret: How Looking Backward Moves Us Forward is a book by Daniel H. Pink that challenges the popular ideal of living with no regrets. Drawing partly on the World Regret Survey he ran, which collected over 16,000 regrets from respondents across 105 countries, he combines research in social psychology with real-life stories.

Pink argues that regret, understood properly, is a valuable emotion that reveals what we care about and shows us how to act differently. Clear, warm and practical, it suits readers of popular psychology who want to make better decisions and live with more purpose at home and at work.

  • Author: Daniel H. Pink
  • Publisher: Canongate
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781838857035

title: The Sandman Vol. 3: Dream Country
author: Neil Gaiman
description:
The Sandman Vol. 3: Dream Country is the third collection of Neil Gaiman's influential comic series, presented in its 30th anniversary edition. Instead of one long arc, it gathers four standalone stories in which Dream plays only a small part, from a gathering of cats who dream of changing the world to a tale involving Calliope, the muse who bore him a son.

The volume also includes Gaiman's take on the first performance of Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, which won the World Fantasy Award for short fiction, a first for a comic. Collecting issues #17 to #20, with art by Kelley Jones, Charles Vess, Colleen Doran and Malcolm Jones III, it is an ideal sampler of the series' range.

  • Author: Neil Gaiman
  • Illustrators: Kelley Jones, Charles Vess, Colleen Doran, Malcolm Jones III
  • Publisher: DC Vertigo
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Sandman, Volume 3
  • ISBN: 9781401285487

title: The Song of the Cell
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
description:
The Song of the Cell: An Exploration of Medicine and the New Human is a sweeping history of cell biology by Siddhartha Mukherjee, the physician and Pulitzer Prize-winning author of The Emperor of All Maladies and The Gene. It tells how scientists came to see the cell as the basic unit of life, and how that insight transformed medicine.

Moving from the first microscopes to modern cell therapies, Mukherjee blends science and history with the stories of patients, doctors and researchers to explain how cells cooperate, defend, repair and sometimes fail. Looking ahead to a future in which cells can be engineered to heal the body, it suits curious general readers of popular science.

  • Author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
  • Publisher: Bodley Head
  • Format: Paperback, 496 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847925985

title: The Stoic Mindset
author: Mark Tuitert
description:
The Stoic Mindset: 10 Ancient Lessons for Modern Life is a practical introduction to Stoicism by Mark Tuitert, an Olympic gold medallist in speed skating who went on to become an entrepreneur. He explains how Stoic principles helped him overcome setbacks in both his sporting career and his private life.

Drawing on the teachings of Marcus Aurelius, Seneca and Epictetus, Tuitert distils the philosophy into ten clear lessons that anyone can apply to work, relationships and everyday challenges. Short and accessible, it is a good starting point for readers new to Stoicism who want to stay calm, focused and resilient.

  • Author: Mark Tuitert
  • Publisher: Penguin Life
  • Format: Hardcover, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241662786

title: Victory City
author: Salman Rushdie
description:
Victory City is a novel by Salman Rushdie, framed as the retelling of an ancient epic. In fourteenth-century southern India, after seeing her mother die, nine-year-old Pampa Kampana is touched by a goddess and given a mission: to help bring into being a great city called Bisnaga, whose name means victory city.

Over the following two and a half centuries, her life becomes bound up with the city's rise and fall as she strives to fulfil the goddess's command and win equality for women. Playful, mythic and full of invention, it is a rich read for fans of literary fiction, magical realism and Indian history.

  • Author: Salman Rushdie
  • Publisher: Jonathan Cape
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781787333451

title: Your Face Belongs To Us
author: Kashmir Hill
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Your Face Belongs to Us is an investigation by Kashmir Hill, a technology reporter for The New York Times, into Clearview AI, a little-known start-up that built a facial recognition app able to identify people from a single photo. Hill follows the company's story from a tip-off she first doubted to its use by police, the very rich and businesses.

Along the way she examines the history of facial recognition and the legal and ethical questions it raises, asking what becomes of privacy when anyone's face can be linked to their online life. It suits readers interested in technology, artificial intelligence and civil liberties.

  • Author: Kashmir Hill
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster UK
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781398509184

title: Unfortunately Yours
author: Tessa Bailey
description:
Unfortunately Yours is a contemporary romance by Tessa Bailey and the second book in her Vine Mess series, set in the wine country of California's Napa Valley. Having lost both her job and her fiancé, heiress Natalie Vos has come home and is ready to launch a new business, but her trust fund will only be released if she marries.

Her solution is to propose a marriage of convenience to August Cates, a former Navy SEAL running a struggling vineyard and the one man who drives her up the wall. Packed with banter and heat, this enemies-to-lovers story suits fans of steamy, funny romantic comedies.

  • Author: Tessa Bailey
  • Publisher: Avon
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Vine Mess, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780063239036

title: Kingdom Of The Feared
author: Kerri Maniscalco
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Kingdom of the Feared is the third and final book in Kerri Maniscalco's Kingdom of the Wicked series. Emilia has just learned that Vittoria, the twin she thought was dead, is alive, but before confronting her past she wants Wrath, her demon king, to be hers completely, body, heart and soul.

Then a powerful figure from House Greed is murdered, pulling Emilia and Wrath into another demon court, and the clues point to Vittoria, who is soon branded a traitor to the whole realm. Determined to uncover the truth about her sister, Emilia faces danger, desire and betrayal in a steamy, dramatic conclusion to the trilogy.

  • Author: Kerri Maniscalco
  • Language: English
  • Series: Kingdom of the Wicked, Book 3

title: The Histories
author: Herodotus
description:
The Histories by Herodotus, completed in the fifth century BC, is widely seen as the starting point of history writing in the West. At its heart is the story of the Persian Empire's invasions of Greece, told with a storyteller's flair and a boundless curiosity about the customs, legends and wonders of the peoples Herodotus encountered.

This Penguin Classics edition presents a lively modern translation by the historian Tom Holland, author of Persian Fire, with contributions from the classicist Paul Cartledge. Readable and absorbing, it opens up one of the founding texts of the ancient world for students and general readers alike.

  • Author: Herodotus
  • Translator: Tom Holland
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 880 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780140455397

title: The Origin Of Species
author: Charles Darwin
description:
The Origin of Species, first published by Charles Darwin in 1859, set out the theory of evolution by natural selection and changed the way we understand life on Earth. Darwin argued that species are not fixed creations but change over time through a ceaseless competition to survive, in which those best suited to their surroundings endure.

Aimed at a general audience, the book also reveals the intricate connections between animals, plants, climate and landscape. This Vintage Classics paperback makes one of the founding texts of modern science accessible to anyone curious about biology, nature and the history of ideas.

  • Author: Charles Darwin
  • Publisher: Vintage Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 512 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784873622

title: اوركسترا المغلوبين
author: Chigozie Obioma
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Orchestra of the Defeated (اوركسترا المغلوبين) is the Arabic edition of Nigerian author Chigozie Obioma's novel An Orchestra of Minorities, translated by Khulud Amr. It follows Chinonso, a lonely poultry farmer grieving his father and the sister who ran away, who falls for Ndali, a woman whose family rejects him because he is poor and has no degree.

To win her, he sells everything to study in Cyprus, only to be swindled and left stranded. The story is told by his chi, the guardian spirit that Igbo belief says stays with a person from conception to death, giving the novel a mythic, spiritual voice. It suits readers of African literature and literary fiction in Arabic.

  • Author: Chigozie Obioma
  • Translator: Khulud Amr
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 576 pages
  • Language: Arabic

title: التفاصيل
author: Ia Genberg
description:
The Details (التفاصيل) is the Arabic edition of Swedish author Ia Genberg's novel Detaljerna, translated by Sakina Ibrahim; the original won Sweden's August Prize in 2022. The novel is built around four people from the narrator's past, each portrait pieced together from small, carefully observed moments.

As these fragments accumulate, they form a larger picture that leaves the reader with lingering questions about memory, friendship, love and how other people shape who we become. Compact and intimate, it suits readers of contemporary literary fiction and Scandinavian writing in Arabic translation.

  • Author: Ia Genberg
  • Translator: Sakina Ibrahim
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Hardcover, 153 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789189464612

title: جزيرة الأشجار المفقودة
author: Elif Shafak
description:
The Island of Missing Trees (جزيرة الأشجار المفقودة) is the Arabic edition of Elif Shafak's novel, translated by Ahmed Hassan Al-Maeeni. In Cyprus in 1974, Kostas, a Greek Cypriot, and Defne, a Turkish Cypriot, meet in secret at a tavern where a fig tree grows through the roof, as war tears their island apart.

Decades later in London, their teenage daughter Ada begins to uncover the family history her parents never shared. Partly narrated by the fig tree itself, the novel weaves together love, loss, memory, migration and the natural world, and suits readers of literary and historical fiction in Arabic.

  • Author: Elif Shafak
  • Translator: Ahmed Hassan Al-Maeeni
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Adab
  • Format: Paperback, 486 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953897301

title: فوضى
attention: No photo found — photograph in store; Book not identified — description written from the title only
description:
Chaos (فوضى) is a book with a one-word Arabic title meaning chaos or disorder.

  • ISBN: 9782902064380

title: دفاتر الوراق
author: Jalal Barjas
vendor: Arab Institute for Research and Publishing
description:
The Bookseller's Notebooks (دفاتر الوراق) is the original Arabic edition of the novel by Jordanian writer Jalal Barjas, which won the International Prize for Arabic Fiction in 2021. Its hero, Ibrahim al-Warraq, is a well-read bookseller who, after losing his work and his home, drifts into the lives of the homeless and begins assuming the identities of characters from novels he loves.

Moving between 1947 and 2019 through a series of notebooks, the novel traces people cut off from home and family, exploring loneliness, belonging, mental illness and justice. It is an acclaimed work of contemporary Jordanian fiction for readers of literary novels in Arabic.

  • Author: Jalal Barjas
  • Publisher: Arab Institute for Research and Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 366 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786144861400

title: Threads That Bind
author: Kika Hatzopoulou
description:
Threads That Bind is the first book in Kika Hatzopoulou's young adult fantasy series of the same name, inspired by Greek mythology. Those descended from the Fates arrive in sets of three, gifted to weave, see or cut the threads that tie people to life and to what they love. Io, the youngest of the Ora sisters, uses her power as a private investigator in Alante, a city half lost beneath the water.

When a case reveals that someone is kidnapping women, damaging their life-threads and unleashing deadly wraiths on the streets, Io must team up with Edei Rhuna, enforcer for the city's notorious Mob Queen and the boy fate has bound to her as a soulmate. Mystery, romance and myth combine in a gripping series opener.

title: Survive Office Politics
author: Bloomsbury Publishing

Survive Office Politics: How to Overcome Problems, Dramas and Conflicts at Work is a concise, practical handbook from Bloomsbury Business for anyone dealing with tricky workplace dynamics, whether in the office or working remotely. It helps readers figure out the motives and alliances around them, spot warning signs early and stay calm under pressure.

Laid out in short, step-by-step sections, it includes quick tips, common mistakes to avoid, summaries of key points and suggestions for further reading. It suits early-career professionals, managers and anyone who wants to handle difficult colleagues and situations with confidence while getting on with the job.

title: The Sandman Vol. 4: Season of Mists
author: Neil Gaiman
description:
The Sandman Vol. 4: Season of Mists is the fourth collected volume of Neil Gaiman's acclaimed comic series, in its 30th anniversary edition. Ten millennia ago, Dream condemned his lover Nada to Hell. Persuaded by his family, the Endless, that this was unjust, he resolves to descend into Hell and free her, even though Lucifer has sworn to destroy him.

What follows is one of the saga's great turning points, as Lucifer hands Dream an unexpected and unwanted prize, the key to Hell itself, which gods and powers from many pantheons then try to claim. Collecting issues #21 to #28, with art by Kelley Jones among others, it is a key volume for fans of mythic fantasy.

title: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
sheet_title: The Invisible Life of Addie Larue
author: V.E. Schwab
description:
The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue is a fantasy novel by V.E. Schwab. In France in 1714, a desperate young woman strikes a deal with a dark power to live forever, but the price is that everyone she meets forgets her as soon as she is out of sight.

Across three centuries and many countries, Addie learns to survive, finding ways to leave her mark on art and history without ever being remembered. Then, in a hidden bookshop in New York, she meets a young man who remembers her name. Lyrical and romantic, it is a story about memory, freedom and what makes a life matter.

  • Publisher: Titan Books
  • Format: Paperback, 545 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781789095593

title: The Marriage Portrait
author: Maggie O'Farrell
description:
The Marriage Portrait is a historical novel by Maggie O'Farrell, inspired by the real life of Lucrezia de' Medici. In 1561, the sixteen-year-old Duchess of Ferrara is taken by her husband Alfonso to a remote country villa, and over dinner she becomes convinced that he means to kill her.

Moving between that night and Lucrezia's sheltered upbringing in the grandest palazzo in Florence, the novel portrays a spirited young woman trapped by the ambitions of powerful men. Rich in detail, it captures both the beauty and the cruelty of Renaissance Italy, and suits readers of literary historical fiction and fans of Hamnet.

  • Publisher: Tinder Press
  • Format: Paperback, 438 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781472223852

title: Same As Ever: A Guide To What Never Changes
sheet_title: Same As Ever: A Guide To What Never Changes
author: Morgan Housel
description:
Same as Ever is a book by Morgan Housel, who wrote The Psychology of Money, about the parts of human behaviour that never change. He argues that we are poor at forecasting because we fixate on what will be different in the future and overlook the habits and instincts that stay constant across the centuries.

Through short, story-driven chapters, Housel shows how greed, fear, risk, envy and overconfidence have shaped people's choices throughout history, and what that means for decisions about money, business and life today. Clear and thought-provoking, it suits readers of popular psychology, investing and business.

  • Author: Morgan Housel
  • Publisher: Harriman House
  • Format: Paperback, 250 pages
  • Language: English

title: The Last Devil To Die: The Thursday Murder Club 4

author: Richard Osman
description:
The Last Devil to Die is the fourth Thursday Murder Club mystery by Richard Osman. When an old friend of the group who deals in antiques is murdered and a perilous package in his care goes missing, Elizabeth, Joyce, Ron and Ibrahim set out to discover who is responsible.

Their investigation brings them up against art forgers, online scammers and drug dealers, while the friends also face sorrow much closer to home. Funny, poignant and cleverly plotted, it is a must for followers of the series and anyone who enjoys warm-hearted crime fiction.

author: Sarah Penner

The Lost Apothecary is a historical mystery and the debut novel of Sarah Penner. In 1791, hidden down a dark London alley, Nella runs a secret apothecary shop where she now sells carefully disguised poisons to women desperate to escape the men who have harmed them.

When her newest customer turns out to be twelve-year-old Eliza Fanning, an unlikely friendship sets events in motion that threaten everything. In present-day London, an aspiring historian stumbles on a clue that leads her into Nella's story. Moving between centuries, it explores friendship, secrets and justice, and suits book clubs and lovers of historical fiction.

Intermittent Fasting Made Easy is a practical, science-based guide by nutrition and fitness expert Thomas DeLauer, known for his popular YouTube channel. Cutting through the hype that surrounds this diet trend, he focuses on what you should actually do to get the best results from fasting in everyday life.

DeLauer breaks the process into its key stages, from the hours of fasting to the first meal that ends them and the eating period that follows, with checklists to keep you on track and tips aimed at fat loss, energy and muscle building. It suits busy people balancing work and family who want a realistic, well-explained approach.

The Sandman Vol. 6: Fables & Reflections gathers some of the most varied stories in Neil Gaiman's acclaimed comic series, presented in the 30th anniversary edition with a new cover by Dave McKean. Collecting issues #29 to #31, #38 to #40 and #50, along with Sandman Special #1, with art by Bryan Talbot, P. Craig Russell, Jill Thompson and others, it is a fine showcase of the series' breadth.

author: Neil Gaiman

The Sandman Vol. 7: Brief Lives is the seventh collected volume of Neil Gaiman's acclaimed comic series, in the 30th anniversary edition with a new Dave McKean cover. Their search through the waking world brings them into contact with long-lived humans and old gods, and leads Dream to a painful reckoning with his son, Orpheus. Immortal Longings is the first book in Chloe Gong's adult fantasy series Flesh and False Gods, loosely inspired by Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra. Every year crowds flood the twin capital cities of San-Er in the kingdom of Talin for a set of deadly games, in which contestants able to leap between bodies fight to the death for unimaginable wealth.

Princess Calla Tuoleimi has been in hiding since she killed her parents in a palace massacre five years ago, and now plans to win the games to get close enough to her uncle, the king, to finish what she started. Dark, violent and romantic, it suits readers who like their fantasy full of intrigue, danger and morally grey heroes.

So Much Talk (زحمة حكي) is a book in Arabic and the first book by media personality Ali Najm. It gathers life experiences and the emotions people meet along the way, from early feelings of admiration, love and fear to the feelings that mature with each new difficulty.

A Jar of Gold (جرة ذهب) is a novel in Arabic by Fawzi Abdu, subtitled The Caravan of Gold and Death. It tells the story of an enormous caravan of gold whose journey left treasure and bodies hidden in caves and mountains along its route.

How to Leave Your Psychopath: The Essential Handbook for Escaping Toxic Relationships is a candid guide by comedian Maddy Anholt, who spent years in controlling relationships before she recognised what was happening. Written in a warm, funny and accessible style, the book unpacks common manipulation tactics such as gaslighting, breadcrumbing and negging, and shows how to spot warning signs and controlling traits early. It suits anyone who wants to understand unhealthy relationships, leave one behind or support a friend going through it.

The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck Journal is an interactive companion by Mark Manson to his books The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck and Everything Is F*cked. Rather than a strict daily routine, it is designed to be picked up whenever you like, with prompts and pointed questions written in Manson's blunt, irreverent voice.

Love Marriage is a novel by Monica Ali about two very different families brought together by an engagement in London. Yasmin Ghorami, a young doctor with a loving family, is engaged to Joe Sangster, also a doctor, and as their wedding nears, her parents meet Joe's outspoken feminist mother and long-buried secrets begin to surface.

As lies and betrayals come to light, Yasmin is forced to question what she really wants from love and what a 'love marriage' truly means. Beginning as a sharp social comedy and deepening into something more moving, it explores culture, class, family and desire, and suits book clubs and fans of contemporary fiction.

Make Time: How to Focus on What Matters Every Day is a practical productivity book by Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky, the pair behind the design sprint process developed at Google Ventures. They argue that constant busyness and distraction have become our default settings, and that it does not have to be that way.

Rather than chasing efficiency, the book offers a flexible daily framework and dozens of small tactics for choosing a priority, staying focused and recharging your energy. Shaped by their experience designing technology products, it suits anyone who feels pulled in every direction by emails, meetings and screens and wants more time for what matters.

Memories is an illustrated poetry collection by Lang Leav, gathering favourite pieces from her collections Lullabies and Love & Misadventure together with thirty-five new poems not previously published in her books.

Short, heartfelt and easy to return to, the poems explore love, loss and longing, and are accompanied by the author's own colour illustrations. Presented as a hardback gift edition with a cloth spine and ribbon marker, it suits Lang Leav's readers and anyone looking for a thoughtful present for a poetry lover.

  • Publisher: Andrews McMeel Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages

  • ISBN: 9781449472399

title: Nine Lies About Work
author: Marcus Buckingham and Ashley Goodall

Nine Lies About Work: A Freethinking Leader's Guide to the Real World is a business book by Marcus Buckingham and Ashley Goodall that takes aim at widely accepted ideas about how organisations should run. They question beliefs such as the notion that culture drives success, that detailed strategic plans are essential, and that people crave feedback and need their weaknesses fixed.

Arguing that these assumptions breed frustration and a sense of unreality at work, the authors show how the best leaders focus instead on what is real: individual strengths, good information and the teams people actually work in. It suits managers, team leaders and HR professionals looking for a fresh view of work.

  • Publisher: Harvard Business Review Press
  • Format: Paperback

Passion for Seafood is a cookbook by Michelin-starred chef Gordon Ramsay devoted to the ingredients that excite him most: fish and shellfish. Written with home cooks in mind, particularly those who are new to preparing seafood, it opens with advice on picking the freshest fish.

Ramsay then covers essential techniques such as filleting, skinning, trimming, marinating and freezing, before sharing 100 recipes that range from simple fishcakes and fish pie to more ambitious dishes such as crab ravioli with a lemongrass dressing. It suits keen cooks who want to build confidence with fish at home.

  • Publisher: Bounty Books

The Complete Primary Dictionary is a children's dictionary from Schofield & Sims by Michael Janes, designed to help primary school pupils build their vocabulary and strengthen their reading, writing and spelling.

Written to support the dictionary skills set out in the National Curriculum, it encourages children to look words up on their own and to grow curious about language and meaning. At more than 600 pages, it is a thorough reference for home and the classroom.

The Daily Dad: 366 Meditations on Parenting, Love and Raising Great Kids is a book of daily reflections for fathers by Ryan Holiday, himself a father of two. Instead of a one-off parenting manual, it offers a short lesson for every day of the year, treating fatherhood as something practised day in, day out.

Each entry pairs a quotation from history, literature, philosophy or psychology, drawing on voices as varied as Socrates and Martin Luther King Jr., with Holiday's thoughts on setting the example a child needs. Warm and practical, it suits new and experienced dads alike and makes a thoughtful gift.

  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 432 pages
  • Language: English

title: The Wisdom of Sundays

The Wisdom of Sundays brings together highlights from Oprah Winfrey's conversations on her Emmy-winning television series Super Soul Sunday with some of today's leading thinkers and spiritual teachers. Contributors include Tony Robbins, Arianna Huffington, Shonda Rhimes, Eckhart Tolle, Elizabeth Gilbert and Cheryl Strayed, among many others.

The book is arranged in ten chapters, each marking a stage of her spiritual path and introduced by a personal essay, and covers themes such as purpose, ego, love, forgiveness and letting go. It is a lovely book to dip into for reflection and makes a meaningful gift.

  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Hardcover, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781509874118

Home Body is the third poetry collection by Rupi Kaur, author of milk and honey and the sun and her flowers. Written in her spare, direct style and illustrated with her own line drawings, it is an intimate journey through the past, present and potential of the self.

The poems explore love, acceptance, community, family, mental health and change, encouraging readers to make peace with themselves and their bodies. Honest and accessible, it suits Rupi Kaur's longtime readers and anyone new to contemporary poetry looking for words of comfort and self-acceptance.

  • Format: Hardcover, 208 pages

Megathreats: Ten Dangerous Trends That Imperil Our Future, and How to Survive Them is a book by economist Nouriel Roubini, nicknamed Dr Doom before his warnings about the 2008 financial crisis proved right. Here he argues that the world faces ten interlocking threats that could trigger a severe economic and political crisis.

Among them are record levels of debt, reckless money creation, the retreat from globalisation, the rivalry between the United States and China, and the impact of climate change. Hard-hitting and wide-ranging, it suits readers of economics, finance and world affairs who want to understand the risks ahead.

  • Author: Nouriel Roubini
  • Publisher: Hodder & Stoughton
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529373783

title: Silverview
author: John le Carré
description:
Silverview is the last novel John le Carré completed, published after his death. Julian Lawndsley has left a high-flying career in the City to run a bookshop in a quiet seaside town, but his new life is soon disturbed by Edward, a Polish émigré from the big house called Silverview, who seems to know a great deal about Julian's family.

Meanwhile, a letter warning of a dangerous leak reaches a senior intelligence officer in London, and the investigation leads to the same small town. A subtle, elegant spy story, it weighs public duty against private conscience and suits longtime le Carré readers and fans of literary espionage.

  • Author: John le Carré
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241550076

title: The Comfort Book
author: Matt Haig
description:
The Comfort Book is Matt Haig's gathering of short reflections, consolations and personal stories written for anxious, uncertain times. Blending philosophy, memoir and gentle self-examination, it draws on voices from across history, including Marcus Aurelius, Emily Dickinson, James Baldwin and Nellie Bly.

Arranged in brief pieces that are easy to dip into, the book reads like a conversation with a wise friend on a difficult day. It suits anyone facing stress, low mood or simply a need for perspective, and works equally well read cover to cover or opened at random when a little hope is needed.

  • Publisher: Canongate
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781838853938

title: Working Backwards
author: Colin Bryar and Bill Carr
description:
Working Backwards takes readers inside Amazon's management culture through the eyes of Colin Bryar and Bill Carr, two senior executives who joined the company in its early years. Together they set out the principles and working habits that shaped how Amazon builds products, makes decisions and hires its people.

Drawing on decades of combined experience, including the era that produced Kindle, Prime and Amazon Web Services, the authors explain practices such as starting new ideas with an imagined press release and using written narratives in place of slide decks. It is a practical read for founders, managers and anyone curious about how a large company keeps innovating.

  • Author: Colin Bryar and Bill Carr
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529033830

Think Like a Monk: Train Your Mind for Peace and Purpose Every Day is a self-help book by Jay Shetty, host of the podcast On Purpose. Before building a career in media, Shetty spent time living as a monk, and here he translates the wisdom he gained there into everyday practices for modern life.

Warm and accessible, with exercises and meditations throughout, it suits readers looking for a calmer, more meaningful everyday life.
