You Will Get Through This Night is a practical mental health guide from writer and entertainer Daniel Howell, created together with a qualified psychologist. The book is organised around three stages: getting through your hardest moments tonight, taking small steps tomorrow to shift thoughts and habits, and building longer-term foundations for the days that follow. Frank, personal and free of jargon, it suits readers looking for an honest, approachable companion on anxiety, low mood and everyday wellbeing.

You Have a Friend in 10A is the first short story collection from Maggie Shipstead, author of Great Circle. Its stories roam widely, taking in an Olympic village, a Pacific atoll, a Paris deathbed and the open ranchland of Montana.

Shipstead brings wit, sympathy and sharp observation to a varied cast, including a novelist brooding over the woman who inspired his debut and a love triangle that plays out across decades. Romantic Comedy is a witty novel by Curtis Sittenfeld, author of Rodham and American Wife. Sally Milz writes sketches for a famous late-night comedy show and has long since given up on love, even mocking the way ordinary-looking men win glamorous women while the reverse never seems to happen.

Then she meets Noah, a pop star known for dating models, and her carefully held assumptions begin to wobble. Funny, sharp and tender by turns, the novel plays with the conventions of the romcom while asking real questions about gender, fame and vulnerability, making it an ideal pick for book clubs and fans of smart contemporary romance.

  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages

  • ISBN: 9780857527509

title: قطار الجليد
author: Jacques Lob
description:
The Ice Train (قطار الجليد) is the Arabic edition of Le Transperceneige, the classic French graphic novel by Jacques Lob, known in English as Snowpiercer. The world has frozen over in an endless winter, and the last survivors of humanity ride a vast train of a thousand and one carriages that circles the planet without ever stopping.

This collected edition gathers the first three parts of the series in a single volume, translated into Arabic by Mohammed Ait Hanna. A bleak, gripping work of dystopian science fiction, it suits readers of graphic novels and anyone who knows the story from its film and television adaptations.

  • Author: Jacques Lob
  • Translator: Mohammed Ait Hanna
  • Publisher: Aseer Al-Kotb
  • Format: Paperback, 248 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Le Transperceneige, Books 1–3
  • ISBN: 9789776902022

title: I Am Enough
author: Sheridan Stewart
description:
I Am Enough follows broadcaster and author Sheridan Stewart through a 90-day challenge she created after years of struggling with burnout. What began as a plan to cut her spending gradually became a broader inquiry into how much is truly enough, whether in possessions, effort or self-worth.

Written with warmth and humour, the book pushes back against the constant pressure to achieve, buy and do more, and against the guilt that so often comes with it. It will appeal to readers seeking contentment, a slower pace and a kinder relationship with themselves.

  • Author: Sheridan Stewart
  • Publisher: Aurum
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780711278578

title: What Happened to You?: Conversations on Trauma, Resilience, and Healing
sheet_title: What Happened To You? Conversations On Trauma Resilience
author: Oprah Winfrey and Bruce D. Perry
description:
What Happened to You? brings together Oprah Winfrey and the psychiatrist and brain development expert Dr Bruce Perry in an extended conversation about trauma. Their central idea is a change of question: instead of asking what is wrong with someone, we should ask what has happened to them.

Mixing personal stories with accessible neuroscience, the authors show how early childhood experiences, good and bad, shape the adults we become, and how understanding that history can open the way to healing, stronger relationships and greater resilience. It is a compassionate read for parents, educators, carers and anyone working through their own past.

  • Author: Oprah Winfrey and Bruce D. Perry
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529068504

title: ساريك
author: Ulf Kvensler
description:
Sarek (ساريك) is the Arabic edition of Swedish author Ulf Kvensler's psychological thriller. Three old friends keep up a yearly tradition of hiking in the remote mountains of far northern Sweden, but this year Milena wants to bring along her new boyfriend, Jacob, and Anna and Henrik find it hard to say no.

Anna soon becomes convinced she has seen Jacob somewhere before, yet cannot place him, and the trip slowly turns into a nightmare with lasting consequences for all of them. Tense and atmospheric, with the wild landscape as a menacing backdrop, it suits readers of Scandinavian crime and suspense.

  • Author: Ulf Kvensler
  • Translator: Alaa Al-Din Abu Zeina
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Hardcover, 451 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789189464605

title: Pinch of Nom Quick & Easy
author: Kate Allinson and Kay Featherstone
description:
Pinch of Nom Quick & Easy is a collection of over 100 speedy, slimming dishes created by Kate Allinson and Kay Featherstone, the cooks behind the original Pinch of Nom cookbook. The focus is on minimal fuss and generous flavour, using ingredients that are easy to find in any supermarket.

Expect family favourites, all-in-one dinners, batch-cooking staples and lighter sweet treats, with dishes such as veggie satay noodles and creamy Cajun chicken pasta. It is a practical choice for busy households and anyone trying to eat more healthily without feeling they are missing out.

  • Author: Kate Allinson and Kay Featherstone
  • Publisher: Bluebird
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529034981

title: The Sushi Lover's Cookbook
author: Yumi Umemura
description:
The Sushi Lover's Cookbook by Japanese cooking expert Yumi Umemura shows home cooks how to make sushi for every occasion. Built around properly seasoned sushi rice, its 85 recipes range from classic thick and thin rolls to inventive modern creations.

Alongside traditional fillings, Umemura experiments with ingredients such as smoked salmon, roast beef, sun-dried tomatoes and even ratatouille, and includes playful ideas like pizza sushi. Clear and approachable, the book suits beginners as well as keen cooks who want to bring a fresh, international twist to Japanese home cooking.

  • Author: Yumi Umemura
  • Publisher: Tuttle Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9784805317327

title: The Lost Metal: A Mistborn Novel
sheet_title: The Lost Metal: A Mistborn Novel
author: Brandon Sanderson
description:
The Lost Metal is the final novel in Brandon Sanderson's second Mistborn era, the Wax and Wayne series set on the world of Scadrial. Lawman turned senator Waxillium Ladrian has spent years pursuing the Set, a shadowy organisation that counts members of his own family among its leaders.

When Marasi Colms and Wayne uncover a weapons stockpile bound for the city of Bilming, the trail leads to a dangerous new explosive and a conspiracy reaching into the halls of government. Blending fantasy, detective adventure and a steampunk-flavoured industrial setting, this action-packed conclusion will reward Mistborn readers and Cosmere fans alike.

  • Author: Brandon Sanderson
  • Publisher: Gollancz
  • Format: Paperback, 507 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Mistborn Saga, Book 7 (Wax and Wayne, Book 4)
  • ISBN: 9781473215276

title: LEGO Star Wars: Small Scenes From a Big Galaxy
sheet_title: LEGO (R) Star Wars (Tm) Small Scenes From a Big Galaxy
author: Vesa Lehtimäki
description:
LEGO Star Wars: Small Scenes From a Big Galaxy is a photography book by Finnish photographer Vesa Lehtimäki, who used his son's LEGO sets and minifigures to stage scenes from the Star Wars universe. The results range from dramatic to wonderfully comic, giving familiar characters and moments a fresh, playful twist.

Along the way, Lehtimäki shares notes on how the shots were made, offering ideas for budding photographers and LEGO builders. Beautifully presented, it makes a great gift for Star Wars fans, collectors and anyone who enjoys creative toy photography.

  • Author: Vesa Lehtimäki
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241206676

title: How To Prevent The Next Pandemic
sheet_title: How To Prevent The Next Pandemic
author: Bill Gates
description:
How to Prevent the Next Pandemic is Bill Gates's plan for making sure that a disease outbreak never again causes the kind of loss seen during COVID-19. Drawing on leading experts and his foundation's long experience fighting infectious disease, he first explains the science of how such outbreaks spread.

Gates then lays out the practical steps that governments, scientists and the private sector can take together, from better disease surveillance to faster vaccines and stronger health systems. Clear and optimistic, it is an accessible read for anyone interested in global health, science policy and preparing for future crises.

  • Author: Bill Gates
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781802060522

title: Soft Animals to Mix & Match: Baby Animals
sheet_title: Soft Animals Mix Match Baby Animals
description:
Baby Animals is part of the Soft Animals to Mix & Match series, a mix-and-match book for little ones built around a cast of baby animals.

As the series name suggests, it is designed around mixing and matching different animals, making it a playful choice for sharing with young children. A companion title, Farm Animals, is available in the same series.

  • Language: English
  • Series: Soft Animals to Mix & Match
  • ISBN: 9789464548587

title: The Little Liar
author: Mitch Albom
description:
The Little Liar is a novel by Mitch Albom set in Greece during the Nazi occupation of Salonika. Young Nico, just eleven, is told he can protect his family if he convinces the Jewish people of his city to climb aboard eastbound trains, which they are assured lead to jobs and security.

By the time Nico discovers the truth about those journeys, nothing can be undone. The novel also follows Nico's brother Sebastian, a girl named Fanni from their school and the German officer whose actions upended all their lives, tracing what becomes of them over many decades. A moving story about deceit, endurance and the redeeming power of love, it suits readers of Second World War historical fiction.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Hardcover
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751584578

title: المهاجرون
author: Vilhelm Moberg
description:
The Emigrants (المهاجرون) is the Arabic edition of Swedish author Vilhelm Moberg's classic novel Utvandrarna, the first book in his Emigrants series. It follows the first families who chose to leave rural Sweden for North America in the mid-nineteenth century, at the start of one of the largest migrations in Swedish history.

Moberg traces with great sensitivity the mix of hope and homesickness that drives his characters, and the hardships, many of them economic, that push people towards exile. An epic of historical fiction and a landmark of Scandinavian literature, it suits readers who enjoy sweeping, character-rich family stories.

  • Author: Vilhelm Moberg
  • Translator: Alaa Al-Din Abu Zeina
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Hardcover, 432 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The Emigrants, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9789187333040

title: The Museum of Odd Body Leftovers
sheet_title: The Mueseum Of Odd Body Leftovers
author: Rachel Poliquin
description:
The Museum of Odd Body Leftovers by Rachel Poliquin, illustrated by Clayton Hanmer, is a funny, fact-packed tour of the parts of our bodies that evolution has left behind. Written for readers aged 7 to 11, it treats the human body as a museum full of surprising exhibits.

Guided by Wisdom Tooth and Disappearing Kidney, young readers visit rooms devoted to goosebumps, hiccups, the appendix and other vestigial features that once mattered to our ancestors. Lively illustrations and a playful tone make evolution easy to grasp, and the book is a great fit for curious children, classrooms and STEM learning at home.

  • Author: Rachel Poliquin
  • Illustrator: Clayton Hanmer
  • Publisher: Greystone Kids
  • Format: Hardcover, 88 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781771647458

title: المغامرات العرضية الاضافية للمئوي هبط من النافذة واختفي 2
sheet_title: المغامرات العرضية الاضافية للمئوي هبط من النافذة واختفي 2
author: Jonas Jonasson
description:
The Accidental Further Adventures of the Hundred-Year-Old Man (المغامرات العرضية الإضافية للمئوي الذي هبط من النافذة واختفى) is the Arabic edition of Jonas Jonasson's comic sequel. Allan Karlsson, now a hundred and one, sets off on another unlikely journey with his irrepressible friend Julius Jonsson.

Older but no less curious, Allan stumbles through a string of absurd escapades that have plenty to say about the world we live in today. Witty, warm and satirical, it suits readers who enjoyed the first book and anyone who likes gentle Scandinavian humour.

  • Author: Jonas Jonasson
  • Translator: Alaa Al-Din Abu Zeina
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Hardcover, 400 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The Hundred-Year-Old Man, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9789188863799

title: المئوي الذي هبط من النافذه واختفى
sheet_title: المئوي الذي هبط من النافذه واختفى
author: Jonas Jonasson
description:
The Hundred-Year-Old Man Who Climbed Out of the Window and Disappeared (المئوي الذي هبط من النافذة واختفى) is the Arabic edition of Jonas Jonasson's comic novel. On the day of his hundredth birthday party, Allan Karlsson climbs out of his care-home window in his slippers and simply walks away.

His escape draws him into a chaotic chase involving a suitcase full of cash, a band of criminals and some less-than-brilliant police officers, while flashbacks reveal how Allan quietly played a part in many of the twentieth century's major events. Funny and big-hearted, it suits readers who enjoy offbeat adventure and gentle satire.

  • Author: Jonas Jonasson
  • Translator: Alaa Al-Din Abu Zeina
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Paperback, 381 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The Hundred-Year-Old Man, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9789187333187

title: تراتيل ثعابين البحر
author: Patrik Svensson
description:
Hymns of the Eels (تراتيل ثعابين البحر) is the Arabic edition of Swedish journalist Patrik Svensson's The Book of Eels, an exploration of one of nature's most enigmatic creatures. Despite centuries of study, nobody has ever watched European eels mate or give birth, and much about their long migrations remains unexplained.

Svensson weaves together marine biology, history and literature, from Aristotle to Sigmund Freud, with memories of fishing for eels alongside his father. The result is part natural history and part memoir, a thoughtful read for anyone drawn to nature writing and science told through personal stories.

  • Author: Patrik Svensson
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Hardcover, 278 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789188863331

title: الباريسي
author: Isabella Hammad
description:
The Parisian (الباريسي) is the Arabic edition of Isabella Hammad's debut novel. It follows a young Palestinian man from his studies in France during the First World War to his return home, as Palestine stands on the eve of its struggle for independence.

Set against the political upheavals that continue to shape the Middle East, the novel explores identity, power and enduring love, and the strange hold the past keeps on the present. Richly imagined and immersive, it suits readers of literary and historical fiction.

  • Author: Isabella Hammad
  • Translator: Al-Harith Al-Nabhan
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 542 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778280739

title: Israeli Apartheid: A Beginner's Guide
author: Ben White
description:
Israeli Apartheid: A Beginner's Guide by Ben White is a concise introduction to the Palestine/Israel conflict, written for students, activists and readers coming to the subject for the first time. It condenses scholarly research and expert analysis into clear, readable chapters.

This updated and expanded edition covers the blockade and military assaults on Gaza since 2008, newer policies affecting Israel's Palestinian citizens, and the rise of the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement. Grounded in the author's own time in Palestine and including first-hand Palestinian testimony, it combines hard facts with a strong human dimension.

  • Author: Ben White
  • Publisher: Pluto Press
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780745334639

title: Life Force
author: Tony Robbins, Peter H. Diamandis and Robert Hariri
description:
Life Force is Tony Robbins's wide-ranging guide to the latest advances in health technology and regenerative medicine, written with Peter H. Diamandis and Dr Robert Hariri. It sets out how emerging science can help readers feel more energetic and stronger, ward off illness and lengthen the healthy years of their lives.

Drawing on interviews with leading doctors and scientists, the book explores new diagnostic tools, therapies and lifestyle strategies, some already available and others on the horizon. Ambitious in scope and optimistic in tone, it suits readers interested in longevity, peak performance and taking a more active role in their own health.

  • Author: Tony Robbins, Peter H. Diamandis and Robert Hariri
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Paperback, 720 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781471188374

title: Make Brilliant Work
author: Rod Judkins
description:
Make Brilliant Work is a creativity guide by Rod Judkins, whose earlier book was The Art of Creative Thinking. Its starting point is that you do not need to be naturally gifted to produce outstanding work, and it backs that up with stories of people who struggled at school, lacked obvious talent or were repeatedly fired.

Drawing on figures such as Picasso, Steve Jobs, Roald Dahl, Steven Spielberg and Zaha Hadid, Judkins distils their working methods into lessons anyone can apply. It suits creative professionals, business teams and individuals who want to move their work from ordinary to exceptional.

  • Author: Rod Judkins
  • Publisher: Macmillan
  • Format: Hardcover, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529060133

title: Rationality: What It Is, Why It Seems Scarce, Why It Matters
sheet_title: Rationality : What It Is Why It Seems Scarce
author: Steven Pinker
description:
Rationality is Steven Pinker's lively defence of human reason, written against the popular idea that people are hopelessly irrational creatures ruled by bias. He argues that our species has shown remarkable powers of reasoning, yet we often fail to use the tools of good thinking developed over centuries.

Pinker explains those tools clearly and with humour, covering formal logic, probability and statistics, cause and effect, game theory and how to make sound choices when outcomes are uncertain. He then shows why rationality matters, both for better personal choices and for social and moral progress, making this an engaging read for anyone interested in psychology, philosophy and clear thinking.

  • Author: Steven Pinker
  • Publisher: Allen Lane
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241380284

title: The Playbook
author: Jennifer Jacquet
description:
The Playbook by Jennifer Jacquet is a sharp satire that exposes how corporations deny inconvenient science and spread doubt to protect their profits. It is written as if it were an instruction manual for executives in industries such as tobacco, oil and pharmaceuticals.

Step by step, it lays out the tactics of delay, distraction and misinformation used around climate change, public health and worker safety, from recruiting willing experts to muddying the evidence. Darkly comic but with a serious purpose, it is an eye-opening read for anyone interested in science, politics and corporate accountability.

  • Author: Jennifer Jacquet
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141982342

title: Why Be Happy?
author: Scott Haas
description:
Why Be Happy? by Scott Haas explores the Japanese way of acceptance, as its subtitle puts it, offering a different perspective on contentment from the familiar pursuit of happiness.

It will interest readers drawn to Japanese culture, philosophy and gentler, more practical approaches to wellbeing.

  • Author: Scott Haas
  • Publisher: John Murray One
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529338799

title: Jane Foster's Baby's First Stories: 0-3 Months
sheet_title: Jane Fosters Babys First Stories: 0 To 3 Months
author: Lily Murray
description:
Jane Foster's Baby's First Stories: 0-3 Months is a board book of simple stories written by Lily Murray and illustrated by Jane Foster, made for sharing with newborns.

Created for the very first months of life, it is designed for parents and carers to look and listen together with their baby, making it a gentle first addition to a child's bookshelf.

  • Author: Lily Murray
  • Illustrator: Jane Foster
  • Format: Board book
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800785137

title: The Ink Black Heart
author: Robert Galbraith
description:
The Ink Black Heart is the sixth Cormoran Strike mystery by Robert Galbraith. When a distraught Edie Ledwell turns up at the agency, she asks Robin Ellacott for help unmasking Anomie, an anonymous online figure who has been tormenting her over the popular cartoon she co-created.

Robin turns her away, only to learn days later that Edie has been murdered in Highgate Cemetery, the setting of her cartoon. Drawn into the hunt for Anomie's identity, Strike and Robin must navigate a tangled world of online fandom and digital aliases. Intricate and absorbing, it is a gripping read for fans of the series and of character-driven British crime fiction.

  • Author: Robert Galbraith
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 1024 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Cormoran Strike, Book 6
  • ISBN: 9780751584189

title: The Breakup Monologues
author: Rosie Wilby
description:
The Breakup Monologues is comedian and podcaster Rosie Wilby's funny, candid look at the end of relationships. After being dumped by email in 2011, she became fascinated by heartbreak and set out to understand why breakups hurt so much and what they can teach us.

Mixing personal stories and anecdotes from friends with insights from therapists, scientists and other experts, Wilby turns her romantic history into a celebration of what each ending has given her. Warm and reassuring, it is a good companion for anyone recovering from a breakup or curious about the psychology of love.

  • Author: Rosie Wilby
  • Publisher: Green Tree
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781472982285

title: The Cottage Fairy Companion
author: Paola Merrill
description:
The Cottage Fairy Companion is Paola Merrill's gentle guide to cottagecore and mindful, slow living. Merrill, who runs the YouTube channel The Cottage Fairy, swapped a hectic urban life for a home in the mountains, hoping to feel more connected to nature and to herself.

She shares the practices that shape her days, from creating a cosy, inspiring home and living in tune with the seasons to gardening and making tea, all accompanied by original illustrations. It suits readers seeking calm, comfort and a little more enchantment in everyday life.

  • Author: Paola Merrill
  • Publisher: Yellow Pear Press
  • Format: Paperback, 180 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781642509793

title: Optimal
author: Daniel Goleman and Cary Cherniss
description:
Optimal is a fresh look at emotional intelligence from Daniel Goleman, author of Emotional Intelligence, written with Cary Cherniss. It focuses on what it takes to reach and sustain peak performance, both for individuals and for the teams and organisations they work in.

The authors examine why so many people feel burnt out or stretched thin, and offer proven approaches for staying focused, resilient and effective. Practical and research-based, it suits managers, leaders and anyone who wants to make more of their working days.

  • Author: Daniel Goleman and Cary Cherniss
  • Publisher: Penguin Business
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241609033

title: Power For All
author: Julie Battilana and Tiziana Casciaro
description:
Power, for All by Julie Battilana and Tiziana Casciaro challenges common misconceptions about power. Rather than something fixed by personality or wealth, or inherently corrupt, they define it simply as the ability to influence the behaviour of others.

That influence, they show, comes from controlling access to resources other people value, which means anyone can gain it, whatever their income or status. Drawing on research and real-world examples, the book explains how power is acquired, how it slips away and how to wield it responsibly, making it a thought-provoking read for leaders, activists and curious readers alike.

  • Author: Julie Battilana and Tiziana Casciaro
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781982181109

title: Live Life In Crescendo
author: Stephen R. Covey with Cynthia Covey Haller
description:
Live Life in Crescendo is the final book from Stephen R. Covey, the leadership thinker behind The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People. It asks how to keep growing and contributing at every stage of life, especially as we move through midlife and beyond.

Covey's Crescendo Mentality encourages readers to believe that their most important work still lies ahead, using their time, talents and influence to keep learning and serving others, whether raising children, caring for parents, leading teams or planning what comes after a career. Inspiring and practical, it suits readers of all ages.

  • Author: Stephen R. Covey with Cynthia Covey Haller
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781398514157

title: Sekirei, Vol. 1 (Omnibus)
author: Sakurako Gokurakuin
description:
Sekirei, Vol. 1 is the first omnibus volume of Sakurako Gokurakuin's action-comedy manga series Sekirei. Minato Sahashi has failed his university entrance exams two years in a row and is close to giving up, until a girl named Musubi quite literally drops into his life.

Musubi is a Sekirei, one of a group of mysterious beings locked in a contest that only one of them can win, and she needs a destined partner to fight alongside her. Swept into the Sekirei Project, Minato finds his quiet life turned upside down. Mixing action, comedy and science fiction, it opens the series for manga fans.

  • Author: Sakurako Gokurakuin
  • Publisher: Yen Press
  • Format: Paperback, 450 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Sekirei Omnibus, Vol. 1
  • ISBN: 9780316441018

title: Wonder: Illustrated Edition
author: R.J. Palacio
description:
This full-colour illustrated edition of Wonder brings R.J. Palacio's novel to life with more than 25 original artworks and a newly written afterword by Palacio herself. August Pullman has a facial difference that has kept him out of mainstream school, but now he is starting fifth grade at Beecher Prep.

Auggie just wants to be treated like any other kid, but his new classmates struggle to see past his face. Told first from his point of view and then through the eyes of his sister, friends and others, the story becomes a moving portrait of kindness, empathy and acceptance. It makes a beautiful gift edition for middle-grade readers and families.

  • Author: R.J. Palacio
  • Publisher: Knopf Books for Young Readers
  • Format: Hardcover, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Wonder, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780593378175

title: Bored Of Lunch: The Healthy Air Fryer Book
sheet_title: Bored Of Lunch: The Healthy Air Fryer Book
author: Nathan Anthony
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Bored of Lunch: The Healthy Air Fryer Book is a cookbook by Nathan Anthony, creator of the popular healthy eating platform Bored of Lunch. It brings together 80 quick, easy and budget-friendly recipes designed specifically for the air fryer.

Whether you are new to air frying or already a fan, the recipes show how to make tasty, everyday meals with less oil, less fuss and lower energy use than a conventional oven. Practical and approachable, it is a great choice for busy households, beginners and anyone looking to eat more healthily without spending hours in the kitchen.

  • Author: Nathan Anthony
  • Language: English

title: THE BUSINESS BOOK
author: Sam Atkinson
description:
The Business Book is part of DK's Big Ideas Simply Explained series, offering a clear, visual introduction to the key concepts that have shaped business and commerce. It tackles questions such as how to build a strong brand, what marks out a great leader and why some companies thrive while others collapse.

Written in plain English, it pairs concise explanations with step-by-step diagrams and witty illustrations that make complex theories easy to follow. Whether you are launching a start-up, running a company or simply curious about how business works, it makes an engaging reference to dip into.

  • Author: Sam Atkinson
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Big Ideas Simply Explained
  • ISBN: 9781409341260

title: Your One Wild and Precious Life
sheet_title: Your One Wild and Precious Life
author: Maureen Gaffney
description:
Your One Wild and Precious Life is psychologist Maureen Gaffney's guide to making the most of time at every stage of adulthood. It begins at that point, often a few decades in, when people look back at how they got here and ahead to what they want to do next.

Drawing on recent research, Gaffney walks through each phase of life, from early childhood to later years, showing how each shapes us and how we can keep adapting with purpose. Insightful and encouraging, it suits readers at a crossroads who want practical tools for living well, whatever their age.

  • Author: Maureen Gaffney
  • Publisher: Penguin Life
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241437728

title: ابقي معي
author: Ayọ̀bámi Adébáyọ̀
description:
Stay With Me (ابقي معي) is the Arabic edition of Nigerian author Ayọ̀bámi Adébáyọ̀'s debut novel. Set against the political turmoil of Nigeria, it follows Yejide and Akin, whose marriage is tested by their struggle to have children and by family pressure for Akin to take a second wife.

Written with clarity and quiet wisdom, the novel explores love, loss, grief and the possibility of redemption as a family comes apart. It suits readers of contemporary African literature and moving, character-driven fiction.

  • Author: Ayọ̀bámi Adébáyọ̀
  • Translator: Sakina Ibrahim
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Hardcover, 315 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789187333927

title: الوصية
author: Nina Wähä
description:
The Testament (الوصية) is the Arabic edition of Swedish author Nina Wähä's novel Testamente, published in English as Testament. It tells the story of the Toimi family, parents Siri and Pentti and their many children, living in a harsh rural community in the far north of Sweden.

Wähä portrays the turmoil inside each family member at every stage of life, yet finds love, strength and light amid the darkness. Lively, multi-voiced and laced with black humour, the novel suits readers of Scandinavian literary fiction and family sagas.

  • Author: Nina Wähä
  • Translator: Madani Qasri
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Hardcover, 476 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789189464407

title: أكستاسي 65 يوم
author: Abdulhadi Al-Amshan
description:
Ecstasy: 65 Days (أكستاسي 65 يوم) is an Arabic book by Abdulhadi Al-Amshan that looks at life from the viewpoint of a person who has lived with darkness since the beginning. Each of its days reflects a phase that most of us pass through at least once.

Combining text with the author's own illustrations and artwork, it is aimed at readers who enjoy letting their imagination roam, including those who do not usually pick up a book.

  • Author: Abdulhadi Al-Amshan
  • Publisher: Self-published
  • Format: Hardcover, 276 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786030272259

title: عرين الأسد
author: Osamah M. Al Muslim
description:
The Lion's Den (عرين الأسد) is an Arabic fantasy novel by Osamah M. Al Muslim and the sixth book in his series Basatin Arabistan (The Gardens of Arabistan).

Running to some 650 pages, this instalment continues a saga that blends fantasy with darker, horror-tinged elements, and its short jacket line hints at a story of defending one's land against those who violate it. It is best read after the earlier books in the series.

  • Author: Osamah M. Al Muslim
  • Publisher: Arabic Literature Center
  • Format: Paperback, 650 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Basatin Arabistan, Book 6
  • ISBN: 9786038372067

title: On Giving Up
author: Adam Phillips
description:
On Giving Up is a short, searching meditation by the psychoanalyst and essayist Adam Phillips on the many things we choose, or are forced, to give up. He considers why dropping a bad habit can seem admirable, while losing the will to live is profoundly disturbing.

Phillips shows that the line between good and bad sacrifices is rarely clear in advance, and that letting something go is often our way of trying to shape a new future. Elegant and thought-provoking, it suits readers of psychology, philosophy and the essay form who enjoy questions more than easy answers.

  • Author: Adam Phillips
  • Publisher: Hamish Hamilton
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241656594

title: The Feminism Book
author: DK
description:
The Feminism Book is DK's illustrated guide to over a hundred landmark thinkers, campaigns and ideas in the history of women's rights. Part of the Big Ideas Simply Explained series, it traces feminism from its beginnings through the suffrage campaigns to recent movements such as #MeToo.

It introduces influential figures including Simone de Beauvoir and Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, and explains terms such as intersectionality and post-feminism in clear, accessible language, supported by diagrams and illustrations. With a foreword by Lucy Mangan, it is an ideal introduction for students and curious readers alike.

  • Author: DK
  • Foreword: Lucy Mangan
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Big Ideas Simply Explained
  • ISBN: 9780241350379

title: كوكو شانيل الأسطورة والحياة
author: Justine Picardie
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Coco Chanel: The Legend and the Life (كوكو شانيل الأسطورة والحياة) is the Arabic edition of Justine Picardie's biography of Gabrielle 'Coco' Chanel, the French designer who became one of the defining figures of twentieth-century fashion.

Picardie follows the trail of a woman who scattered, reshaped and concealed parts of her own story, visiting places tied to her life, from the Rue Cambon apartment and studio in Paris, where Karl Lagerfeld later presided, to members of her family in the French countryside. The result separates myth from reality and suits anyone interested in fashion history and remarkable lives.

  • Author: Justine Picardie
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Khayal
  • Format: Paperback, 363 pages
  • Language: Arabic

title: Soft Animals to Mix & Match: Farm Animals
sheet_title: Soft Animals Mix Match Farm Animals
description:
Farm Animals is part of the Soft Animals to Mix & Match series, a mix-and-match book for little ones built around familiar farmyard animals.

As the series name suggests, it is designed around mixing and matching different animals, making it a playful choice for sharing with young children. A companion title, Baby Animals, is available in the same series.

  • Language: English
  • Series: Soft Animals to Mix & Match
  • ISBN: 9789464548594

title: Permacrisis
author: Gordon Brown, Mohamed El-Erian and Michael Spence
description:
Permacrisis brings together former UK prime minister Gordon Brown and economists Mohamed El-Erian and Michael Spence to examine a world lurching from one emergency to the next. The three friends began their conversations online early in the pandemic, alarmed by unexpected shocks, weak policy responses and faltering international cooperation.

Pooling their long experience in government, finance and economic policy, they argue that today's gloomy path is not inevitable, and set out achievable ways to repair a fractured world through better growth, management and global coordination. It suits readers interested in economics, politics and the big challenges of our time.

  • Author: Gordon Brown, Mohamed El-Erian and Michael Spence
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781398525627

title: اعرف نفسك
attention: No photo found — photograph in store; Book not identified — description written from the title only
description:
Know Yourself (اعرف نفسك) is an Arabic-language book whose title points to the theme of self-knowledge and understanding one's own character.

It will interest Arabic readers drawn to personal development, psychology and reflection on the self, and to the timeless idea that understanding begins from within.

  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789953650296

title: Marvel Black Widow: Secrets of a Super-Spy
sheet_title: MARVEL BLACK WIDOW SECRETS OF A SUPER-SPY
author: DK
description:
Marvel Black Widow: Secrets of a Super-Spy is DK's richly illustrated guide to Natasha Romanoff, one of Marvel Comics' most enigmatic heroes. Spy, Avenger and agent of S.H.I.E.L.D., she has a past wrapped in secrecy and misinformation, and this book sets out to separate fact from fiction.

It follows her remarkable journey from Soviet-trained assassin to Super Hero, with detailed profiles, comic art and a striking cover by Jen Bartel. Full of spycraft and comic-book history, it makes an essential companion for Black Widow fans and Marvel collectors.

  • Author: DK
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 200 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241428016

title: The Complete Persepolis
author: Marjane Satrapi
description:
The Complete Persepolis gathers Marjane Satrapi's acclaimed graphic memoir in a single volume. Told in striking black-and-white comic strips, it recounts her childhood in Tehran within a large, loving family during the Islamic Revolution and the war that followed.

The story continues through her teenage years in Vienna, far from home, her return to Iran and her eventual decision to leave for good. Candid, funny and often heartbreaking, it captures both the upheaval of a nation and the universal experience of growing up, and is essential reading for fans of graphic novels and memoir.

  • Author: Marjane Satrapi
  • Publisher: Pantheon Books
  • Format: Paperback, 341 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Persepolis, Books 1–4
  • ISBN: 9780375714832

title: The Vegetable Gardening Book
author: Joe Lamp'l
description:
The Vegetable Gardening Book is television and podcast host Joe Lamp'l's comprehensive handbook for raising an organic vegetable plot, from sowing seeds to gathering the crop. Drawing on years of interviews with expert growers for his shows, plus his own hands-on experience, he shares practical advice for gardeners at every level.

Topics range from starting seeds and choosing varieties to building sturdy tomato cages and much more besides. Clear and encouraging, it suits beginners planning their first beds as well as experienced gardeners looking for fresh ideas to grow more productive, resilient crops.

  • Author: Joe Lamp'l
  • Publisher: Cool Springs Press
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780760375716

title: Waxing On: The Karate Kid and Me
sheet_title: Waxing On : The Karate Kid and Me
author: Ralph Macchio
description:
Waxing On: The Karate Kid and Me is Ralph Macchio's memoir of the 1984 film that made him a star and has followed him ever since. Now back as Daniel LaRusso in the Netflix series Cobra Kai, he looks back on the movie's enduring place in popular culture and in his own life.

Macchio offers an insider's account of how the role came about, from auditions and early innocence to life on set, and shares the stories behind some of the film's most famous moments. Nostalgic and warm, it is a treat for fans of the film, the franchise and 1980s cinema.

  • Author: Ralph Macchio
  • Publisher: Dutton
  • Format: Hardcover, 241 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593185834

title: Njuta
author: Niki Brantmark
description:
Njuta introduces the Swedish practice of savouring each moment, from Niki Brantmark, founder of the blog My Scandinavian Home. Meaning 'enjoy' or 'delight in', njuta is a philosophy of slow, intentional living that finds happiness in the smallest of pleasures.

Brantmark applies the idea to daily rituals, a comfortable home, time outdoors, mealtimes and fika, the changing seasons and celebrations with loved ones, with easy how-tos and practical lists throughout. It is a gentle, uplifting read for anyone hoping to live more mindfully and with greater gratitude.

  • Author: Niki Brantmark
  • Publisher: Harvest
  • Format: Hardcover, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063284081

title: The Ecology Book: Big Ideas Simply Explained
sheet_title: The Ecology Book Big Ideas Simply Explained
author: DK
description:
The Ecology Book is part of DK's Big Ideas Simply Explained series, exploring over 90 major ideas about how living things interact with one another and with their environment. It ranges across geography, geology, biology and the environmental movement, from classical thinkers to modern discoveries such as DNA and the Gaia hypothesis.

Short explanations, step-by-step diagrams and witty illustrations make complex science easy to follow, while feature boxes highlight green issues such as pesticides, endangered species and renewable energy. It is an accessible reference for students, nature lovers and anyone concerned about the health of the planet.

  • Author: DK
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Big Ideas Simply Explained
  • ISBN: 9780241350386

title: What To Expect Before You're Expecting
sheet_title: What To Expect Before You're Expecting
author: Heidi Murkoff
description:
What to Expect Before You're Expecting by Heidi Murkoff is a complete guide to getting pregnant from the What to Expect series. It helps would-be parents get ready for as healthy a pregnancy as possible, with down-to-earth tips, reassuring guidance and clever strategies for conceiving sooner.

It covers getting your body ready, foods that support fertility, which habits to drop or adopt, timing and the practicalities of trying to conceive, and when to seek fertility help, including the latest tests and treatments. Advice for would-be dads, women going it alone and same-sex couples is included too, making it a reassuring companion for anyone planning a family.

  • Author: Heidi Murkoff
  • Publisher: Workman Publishing Company
  • Format: Hardcover, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: What to Expect
  • ISBN: 9781523501519

title: صدام الملوك 1/2
author: George R.R. Martin
description:
A Clash of Kings (صدام الملوك) is the Arabic edition of the second novel in George R.R. Martin's epic fantasy series A Song of Ice and Fire, the saga behind Game of Thrones. Picking up straight after the first book, it finds the Seven Kingdoms torn apart as five kings fight for the Iron Throne while a blood-red comet crosses the sky.

As intrigue, betrayal and dark magic spread, a threat stirs in the far north and an exiled queen across the sea works to reclaim her father's throne. Vast, violent and richly plotted, it suits readers who want the full depth of the story behind the television series.

  • Author: George R.R. Martin
  • Translator: Hisham Fahmy
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 1072 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: A Song of Ice and Fire, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9789776483927

title: The Attention Fix
author: Anders Hansen
description:
The Attention Fix is Swedish psychiatrist Anders Hansen's guide to regaining focus in a world built to distract us. He explains how constant notifications, emails and endless scrolling are affecting our brains, and why so many of us now feel restless, unmotivated and unable to concentrate.

Drawing on the latest brain research, Hansen links digital overload to poor sleep, anxiety, low mood and burnout, then offers practical steps to break compulsive phone habits and build deep, single-task focus. Clear and science-based, it suits anyone who wants a healthier relationship with technology.

  • Author: Anders Hansen
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781785044342

title: Infectious Generosity
author: Chris Anderson
description:
Infectious Generosity is a hopeful book from Chris Anderson, the head of TED, about one of humanity's most powerful but underrated instincts. After years in which the internet often seemed to divide rather than unite us, he argues that generosity offers a route from outrage back to optimism.

Drawing on lessons from how TED grew by sharing ideas freely online, Anderson shows how the same connected technology can make acts of kindness spread further and faster than ever before. Inspiring and practical, it suits readers interested in social change, philanthropy and building a better future together.

  • Author: Chris Anderson
  • Publisher: WH Allen
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780753560501

title: The Iron Wall: Israel and the Arab World
sheet_title: The Iron Wall: Israel and the Arab World
author: Avi Shlaim
description:
The Iron Wall: Israel and the Arab World is historian Avi Shlaim's detailed account of Israel's relations with the Palestinians and the wider Arab world. It begins with the early Zionist movement under Theodor Herzl, which pursued a homeland in Palestine while largely disregarding the Arab population already living there.

Shlaim then traces how Israeli policy evolved across the decades, shaped by the strategy of the iron wall and by reliance on great-power support, first from Britain and later from the United States. Rigorous and highly readable, it is an essential work for students and readers of Middle East history and politics.

  • Author: Avi Shlaim
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 704 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141033228

title: The Storyteller: Tales of Life and Music
author: Dave Grohl
description:
The Storyteller: Tales of Life and Music is the memoir of Dave Grohl, drummer with Nirvana and founder of Foo Fighters. Written in his own hand rather than with a ghostwriter, it gathers stories from his life as a kid from Springfield, Virginia, who went on to live out his wildest musical dreams.

Grohl recalls life on the road, the bands and heroes who shaped him, and the joys and losses along the way, with the same energy he brings to the stage. Funny, heartfelt and full of rock and roll anecdotes, it is a natural pick for music fans and anyone who loves a great memoir.

  • Author: Dave Grohl
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Hardcover, 376 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781398503700

title: Joe's Family Food
author: Joe Wicks
description:
Joe's Family Food is a collection of 100 healthy, simple recipes from Joe Wicks, The Body Coach, designed to feed the whole family. As a busy dad of two, Wicks focuses on meals that are quick to prepare, leaving more room for family time.

Recipes cover quick midweek dinners, special occasions and plenty more, including dishes such as Mexican-style chicken burgers, all created to please adults and children alike. It is a practical, cheerful cookbook for parents who want nutritious food that makes mealtimes a fun, shared activity.

  • Author: Joe Wicks
  • Publisher: Bluebird
  • Format: Hardcover, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529016314

title: The Breathing Cure
author: Patrick McKeown
description:
The Breathing Cure by breathing specialist Patrick McKeown is a detailed guide to how the way we breathe affects almost every part of our health, from sleep and digestion to movement, mental wellbeing and sporting performance. It comes with a foreword by big-wave surfer Laird Hamilton.

McKeown shares techniques used by elite athletes and military personnel to clear a blocked nose, manage stress, calm the nervous system and improve lung function. Practical and wide-ranging, it suits fitness enthusiasts and health-conscious readers, as well as coaches, therapists, yoga and Pilates teachers and other professionals.

  • Author: Patrick McKeown
  • Foreword: Laird Hamilton
  • Publisher: Humanix Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 434 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781630061975

title: The Ramadan Family Cookbook
author: Anisa Karolia
description:
The Ramadan Family Cookbook by Anisa Karolia is a collection of 80 recipes created for sharing with loved ones during the holy month.

With dishes intended to gather family and friends around the table, it makes a thoughtful choice for anyone planning suhoor and iftar meals at home or looking for fresh ideas for festive cooking.

  • Author: Anisa Karolia
  • Publisher: Ebury Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529928631

title: The Cambridge Code
author: Emma Loveridge and Curly Moloney
description:
The Cambridge Code by Emma Loveridge and Curly Moloney is a psychology guide designed to reveal the unconscious patterns that shape how you think, act and react. Created with input from Cambridge University researchers and clinicians, it aims to help readers understand their innate preferences and traits.

The book comes with a half-hour quiz that generates a personal profile, then explains in plain language what your results mean for your work, relationships and wellbeing. It suits anyone curious about their own psychology and looking for practical self-understanding.

  • Author: Emma Loveridge and Curly Moloney
  • Publisher: Bluebird
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529039771

title: Healing Is The New High
author: Vex King
description:
Healing Is the New High is Vex King's guide to overcoming emotional pain and finding inner freedom. Drawing on the techniques that helped him move beyond a troubled past, he shows readers how to let go of trauma and become their own healers.

Combining yogic principles with simple, accessible exercises, King moves step by step from the body's energy and personal vibration to relationships, limiting beliefs and rediscovering your true self. Warm and encouraging, it suits readers of spiritual self-help and anyone beginning a healing journey.

  • Author: Vex King
  • Publisher: Hay House
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781788174770

title: Middle-earth Envisioned: The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings
sheet_title: Middle Earth Envisioned : The Hobbit & The Lord Of The Rings
author: Brian J. Robb and Paul Simpson
description:
Middle-earth Envisioned by Brian J. Robb and Paul Simpson explores the artistic legacy of J.R.R. Tolkien's world as reimagined in film, theatre and other media. It looks at how The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings have inspired generations of artists, performers and filmmakers.

Paintings, illustrations, theatre productions, radio serials and films are all discussed, shedding new light on the richly detailed world Tolkien created, from its languages and creatures to its wars. It is a rewarding read for Tolkien enthusiasts and fans of fantasy art and film.

  • Author: Brian J. Robb and Paul Simpson
  • Publisher: Race Point Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781937994273

title: Stanley Donwood: There Will Be No Quiet: The Artwork of Radiohead
sheet_title: Stanley Donwood There Will Be No Quiet
author: Stanley Donwood
description:
There Will Be No Quiet is Stanley Donwood's own account of the artwork he has created for Radiohead over more than two decades. Donwood, the artist behind the band's distinctive and ever-changing visual identity, opens up his notebooks, sketches, photographs and abandoned ideas.

Arranged chronologically, each chapter focuses on a major project, from album artwork and promotional pieces to personal work, and walks through it as a step-by-step case study. With commentary from Thom Yorke and previously unseen archive material, it is a treasure for Radiohead fans, designers and anyone interested in the creative process.

  • Author: Stanley Donwood
  • Commentary: Thom Yorke
  • Publisher: Abrams Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781419737244

title: Zionism and Its Discontents: A Century of Radical Dissent in Israel/Palestine
author: Ran Greenstein
description:
Zionism and Its Discontents by Ran Greenstein looks beyond the dominant nationalist narratives of Israel/Palestine to recover a century of radical dissent. It focuses on four distinct but connected movements that resisted Zionist rule and settlement in the decades either side of 1948.

Greenstein examines the Palestinian Communist Party, the bi-nationalist movement, Palestinian efforts to resist marginalisation after 1948 and the radical anti-Zionist group Matzpen. He also explores key ideas such as colonialism, settlement, ethnicity and class, making this a valuable study for readers of Middle East history and politics.

  • Author: Ran Greenstein
  • Publisher: Pluto Press
  • Format: Paperback, 241 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780745334677

title: How To Be Perfect
author: Michael Schur
description:
How to Be Perfect is Michael Schur's light-hearted introduction to moral philosophy, from the creator of the television comedy The Good Place. He takes the big questions of ethics, such as what it means to act well and why it matters, and tests them against the awkward dilemmas of everyday life.

Schur walks through some 2,500 years of ethical thinking, from Aristotle's virtue ethics to Kant and the utilitarians, explaining each school in plain language and poking gentle fun at its blind spots. Questions range from the trivial to the serious, including whether we can still enjoy art made by people who behaved badly. It suits curious readers who want philosophy that is funny, practical and free of jargon.

  • Author: Michael Schur
  • Publisher: Quercus Books
  • Format: Paperback, 289 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529421330

title: Showa 1944 1953
author: Shigeru Mizuki
description:
Showa 1944–1953: A History of Japan is the third of four volumes in Shigeru Mizuki's manga history of the Showa era, translated into English by Zack Davisson. It covers the final, catastrophic phase of the Pacific War, from island battles such as Guadalcanal and Okinawa to the atomic bombings and Japan's surrender, followed by the hard years of occupation and rebuilding.

Mizuki weaves the national story together with his own. A soldier who lost an arm on Rabaul, he weighs staying among the Tolai people who befriended him against returning to a ruined Japan and a career in art. The result is a powerful anti-war work from one of Japan's best-loved cartoonists, ideal for readers of graphic memoir and twentieth-century history.

  • Author: Shigeru Mizuki
  • Translator: Zack Davisson
  • Publisher: Drawn & Quarterly
  • Format: Paperback, 536 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Showa: A History of Japan, Volume 3 of 4
  • ISBN: 9781770466272

title: Nature Therapy
author: Remy Dambron
description:
Nature Therapy by Remy Dambron is a gentle, illustrated guide to ecotherapy, the practice of improving wellbeing by spending time with the natural world. It treats nature as something to be found almost anywhere, from a cliff path or a quiet wood to a back garden or a single houseplant on the windowsill.

The book offers ideas for discovering your own connection with the outdoors, with activities such as gardening, crafts, walking and wild swimming, plus simple ways to bring more nature into ordinary days. It suits anyone hoping to ease stress, feel healthier or find more meaning and calm, and makes a thoughtful gift for nature lovers.

  • Author: Remy Dambron
  • Publisher: Summersdale
  • Format: Hardcover, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781837991488

title: Quantum Body
author: Deepak Chopra
description:
Quantum Body is Deepak Chopra's exploration of how we age and what it takes to live longer and better, written with physicist Jack Tuszynski and endocrinologist Dr Brian Fertig. It sets out to link ideas from quantum physics and biology with everyday health concerns such as inflammation, stress and the ageing process.

Rather than offering quick fixes or costly anti-ageing packages, the authors argue that a deeper understanding of the connection between body and mind is the route to lasting wellbeing. Written for general readers, it suits anyone interested in longevity, holistic health and the meeting point of science and spirituality.

  • Author: Deepak Chopra
  • Publisher: Rider
  • Format: Paperback, 323 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846047701

title: The Art Of Disagreeing Well
author: Bo Seo
description:
The Art of Disagreeing Well is Bo Seo's account of what competitive debating taught him about listening, arguing and being heard. Seo moved from Korea to Australia as a boy with no English, found his voice through school debate and went on to win two world championships and coach the Harvard team.

Blending memoir with practical lessons, he unpacks the core skills of debate, including research, clear structure, finding the truth of a matter and persuasion, and shows how they can make conversations with friends, family and colleagues more productive. It suits anyone who dreads conflict or wants to argue more fairly and effectively.

  • Author: Bo Seo
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008498665

title: There's Still No Such Thing As 'Naughty'
sheet_title: Theres Still No Such Thing As Naughty Primary School Years
author: Kate Silverton
description:
There's Still No Such Thing As 'Naughty' is Kate Silverton's parenting guide to the primary school years, written for families with children aged 5 to 12. A child therapist, she explains that while children grow more independent at this stage, they still rely heavily on their parents for emotional support.

Drawing on neuroscience and her clinical work, Silverton offers compassionate, practical steps for helping children calm anxiety, manage big emotions and build resilience and empathy. Topics include healthy brain development, worries about school, screen time, the value of play and looking after your own mental health as a parent. It follows on from her earlier book on the early years.

  • Author: Kate Silverton
  • Publisher: Lagom
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781788706759

title: Thriving in the Eye of the Hurricane
sheet_title: Thriving in the Eye of the Hurricane
author: Joseph Bailey
description:
Thriving in the Eye of the Hurricane is a guide to resilience by Joseph Bailey, a licensed clinical psychologist with more than 40 years of practice, with a foreword by Michael Neill. It is built on the Three Principles approach to psychology, which Bailey helped to pioneer, and on what he calls the Transformation Principle.

The central idea is that our experience of life is shaped by our thinking, and that seeing this clearly can bring calm and inner strength even in chaotic times. Bailey draws on programmes he has led in medical schools, addiction treatment centres and healthcare settings, and shares practical tips for preventing burnout. It suits professionals under pressure and anyone seeking steadier footing.

  • Author: Joseph Bailey
  • Foreword: Michael Neill
  • Publisher: Mango Media
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781642506600

title: The Bezos Blueprint
author: Carmine Gallo
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
The Bezos Blueprint by Carmine Gallo, author of Talk Like TED, examines the communication habits Jeff Bezos relied on to turn Amazon from a garage start-up in Seattle into one of the world's biggest employers. Its subtitle casts Bezos as the world's greatest salesman.

Gallo breaks down how Bezos shaped the way Amazon staff write, pitch, present and collaborate, and how former colleagues have since adopted the same tools to launch companies of their own. Practical and full of examples, it suits leaders, entrepreneurs and anyone who wants to communicate ideas with more clarity and persuasive force.

  • Author: Carmine Gallo
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035004102

title: The Life-Changing Science of Detecting Bullshit
sheet_title: The LifeChanging Science Of Detecting Bullshit
author: John V. Petrocelli
description:
The Life-Changing Science of Detecting Bullshit is a guide to critical thinking by John V. Petrocelli, a psychology professor and social scientist whose TEDx talk on the subject inspired the book. He argues that everyone is vulnerable to misleading claims, however clever they think they are, and that most of us spread a little of it ourselves.

Using examples from Bernie Madoff's Ponzi scheme to the disastrous policies of Mao's Great Leap Forward, Petrocelli shows how unchallenged falsehoods shape memories, beliefs and decisions. He then sets out habits of healthy scepticism and scientific reasoning for sorting fact from fiction. It suits anyone tired of spin and misinformation who wants sharper judgement.

  • Author: John V. Petrocelli
  • Publisher: Griffin
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781250763587

title: الحرب والسلم 1/3
author: Leo Tolstoy
description:
This is the first volume of the Arabic edition of Leo Tolstoy's War and Peace (الحرب والسلم), published by Dar Al-Rafidain. Set in Russia during the Napoleonic Wars, the novel follows aristocratic families such as the Rostovs and the Bolkonskys, along with the searching Pierre Bezukhov, from the salons of St Petersburg to the battlefield of Borodino.

Tolstoy moves between private lives and great historical events, exploring love, ambition, faith, war and the question of what really drives history. Widely counted among the greatest novels ever written, it is a rewarding long read for lovers of classic and historical fiction who prefer to read in Arabic.

  • Author: Leo Tolstoy
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Rafidain
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: War and Peace (Arabic edition), Volume 1
  • ISBN: 9781988295152

title: The Fall of Númenor
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description:
The Fall of Númenor gathers into a single volume, for the first time, J.R.R. Tolkien's accounts of Middle-earth's Second Age, edited by Brian Sibley and illustrated with new watercolour and pencil artwork by Alan Lee. It draws on material first published by Christopher Tolkien in The Silmarillion, Unfinished Tales and The History of Middle-earth.

The story centres on Númenor, the island kingdom raised from the sea as a gift to the Men who fought against Morgoth, and traces its growth in wealth and power, how the Rings of Power were made, Sauron's return and the kingdom's catastrophic downfall, ending with the alliance of Elves and Men against Sauron. It is a handsome companion for anyone who loves The Lord of the Rings.

  • Author: J.R.R. Tolkien
  • Editor: Brian Sibley
  • Illustrator: Alan Lee
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Hardcover, 352 pages
  • Language: English

title: The Woman In Me
author: Britney Spears
description:
The Woman in Me is the memoir of pop star Britney Spears, published two years after she spoke out in court in June 2021 about the conservatorship that had controlled her life. In her own words, she tells the story of her career, her family and her fight to regain her freedom.

Candid and frequently funny, the book reflects on fame, faith, motherhood and resilience, and on what music and love have meant to her through it all. It is a moving read for fans and for anyone interested in celebrity culture and in a woman finally reclaiming control of her own narrative.

  • Author: Britney Spears
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Hardcover, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781398522527

title: The Blue Zones Secrets For Living Longer
sheet_title: The Blue Zones Secrets For Living Longer
author: Dan Buettner
description:
The Blue Zones Secrets for Living Longer is Dan Buettner's illustrated guide to the places where people live the longest, healthiest lives. A National Geographic explorer who has studied longevity for two decades, Buettner revisits Sardinia, Ikaria, Okinawa, Loma Linda in California and the Nicoya Peninsula of Costa Rica, and introduces a new blue zone.

He distils the habits these communities share, among them a sense of purpose, faith, strong social ties, time to rest, natural movement and a largely plant-based diet, along with foods linked to long life. Images by National Geographic photographers bring each region to life. It suits readers interested in health, nutrition and practical ways to add healthy years.

  • Author: Dan Buettner
  • Publisher: National Geographic
  • Format: Hardcover, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781426223471

title: فتاة البرتقال
author: Jostein Gaarder
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Norwegian author Jostein Gaarder's novel The Orange Girl (فتاة البرتقال), translated by Madani Qasri and published by Dar Al-Muna. Fifteen-year-old Georg barely remembers his father, who died when he was four. Eleven years later, a long letter his father wrote for him surfaces, addressed to the grown-up Georg.

The letter tells the story of the father's love for a mysterious young woman carrying a bag of oranges, and as Georg reads, it leads him to big questions about the meaning of life and death. Tender and thought-provoking, the novel celebrates life, love and courage, and suits teenagers and adults who enjoyed Sophie's World.

  • Author: Jostein Gaarder
  • Translator: Madani Qasri
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Paperback, 201 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789188356932

title: The Whole Vegetable
author: Sophie Gordon
description:
The Whole Vegetable is a sustainable cookbook by Sophie Gordon that shows how to cook with every part of a vegetable, cut food waste, make the most of leftovers and eat with the seasons. Its more than 130 recipes make vegetables the star of the plate rather than a side dish.

Gordon finds uses for the bits that usually end up in the bin, from leaves, stalks and tops to flowers, seeds and peelings. Dishes range from cauliflower carbonara and pumpkin tacos to a cherry breakfast crumble and Danish buns filled with apple and walnut. It suits home cooks who want delicious, eco-conscious food all year round.

  • Author: Sophie Gordon
  • Publisher: Michael Joseph
  • Format: Hardcover, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241465134

title: عاصفة السيوف 1/2
author: George R.R. Martin
description:
This is the Arabic edition of George R.R. Martin's A Storm of Swords (عاصفة السيوف), the third book in the epic fantasy series A Song of Ice and Fire, translated by Hisham Fahmy and published by Dar Al-Tanweer. The War of the Five Kings still rages across the Seven Kingdoms while the boy king Joffrey sits on the Iron Throne.

As the Lannisters move to secure their hold on power against Stannis Baratheon and Robb Stark, Daenerys Targaryen marches through distant lands with the world's only living dragons, and a vast wildling army gathers beyond the Wall. Darker still, an ancient threat stirs in the far north. Full of battles, betrayals and shocks, it is essential reading for fans of the saga and of Game of Thrones.

  • Translator: Hisham Fahmy
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer

  • Language: Arabic

title: Heart Bones
author: Colleen Hoover
description:
Heart Bones is a summer romance by Colleen Hoover. After a hard childhood marked by neglect, Beyah Grim has finally earned a full scholarship to study at Penn State and a way out of Kentucky. Then, two months before she is due to leave, an unexpected loss leaves her with nowhere to live.

She has to see out the summer in Texas, living with a father she barely knows, and has little patience for Samson, the wealthy, brooding boy next door. Yet the pull between them is hard to ignore, and with their futures heading to opposite ends of the country, they agree to keep things light. It suits readers who like emotional, character-driven love stories.

  • Author: Colleen Hoover
  • Publisher: Simon & Schuster
  • Format: Hardcover, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781398525030

title: Purposeful Curiosity
author: Dr Costas Andriopoulos
description:
Purposeful Curiosity by Dr Costas Andriopoulos explores how asking the right questions can lead to success and a more fulfilling life. Over five years he interviewed some of today's most inquisitive people, from explorers to entrepreneurs, to understand how they turned curiosity into achievement.

Combining insights from those interviews with the latest thinking in psychology, management and neuroscience, the book distils nine key lessons for putting your own curiosity to work, whatever your goals. Practical tips and takeaways run throughout. It suits professionals, leaders and anyone who wants to think more creatively and approach life and work with fresh questions.

  • Author: Dr Costas Andriopoulos
  • Publisher: Yellow Kite
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529356236

title: How Not to Fit In: An Unapologetic Guide to Navigating Autism and ADHD
sheet_title: How Not To Fit In: Unapologetic Approach To Navigating Autis
author: Jess Joy and Charlotte Mia
description:
How Not to Fit In is an unapologetic guide to life with autism and ADHD by Jess Joy and Charlotte Mia, two neurodivergent women who were diagnosed late and who founded the online community I Am Paying Attention. Part handbook and part rallying cry, it centres on real experiences of discovering and accepting a neurodivergent brain.

The authors look at why diagnosis can be so difficult and so shaped by gender, and how to navigate relationships, friendships, work and money in a world built around neurotypical minds. With up-to-date research, input from many experts and stories from people with lived experience, it suits anyone who suspects, or knows, that their brain works differently, and the people who love them.

  • Author: Jess Joy and Charlotte Mia
  • Publisher: Thorsons
  • Format: Hardcover, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008589226

title: Just Work
author: Kim Malone Scott
description:
Just Work is Kim Malone Scott's practical guide to tackling bias, prejudice and bullying at work, from the author of Radical Candor. She argues that organisations routinely overlook and underuse large numbers of people while promoting others beyond their competence, and that this is not only unfair but bad for business.

Scott offers a framework for recognising and addressing workplace injustice, respecting each person's individuality and collaborating more effectively. Written for leaders and employees alike, it shows how to build fairer teams and a genuinely inclusive culture. The book has since been republished under the title Radical Respect.

  • Author: Kim Malone Scott
  • Publisher: Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529063608

title: Undoctored
author: Adam Kay
description:
Undoctored is Adam Kay's follow-up to This Is Going to Hurt, the diary of his years as a junior doctor that became a BBC television series. This time he reflects on life after leaving medicine and on how deeply his years on the NHS frontline continue to shape him.

Subtitled The Story of a Medic Who Ran Out of Patients, it is his most personal book so far: by turns hilarious and heartbreaking, honest about the toll of the job and about wounds that never quite healed. It suits readers who loved his first book and anyone who enjoys sharp, funny and moving memoirs.

  • Author: Adam Kay
  • Publisher: Trapeze
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781398700383

title: MI COCINA
author: Rick Martínez
description:
Mi Cocina is Rick Martínez's personal cookbook of Mexican food, born from a journey that took him from Mexico City through all 32 states, 156 cities and some 20,000 miles. The recipes recreate dishes he tasted along the way, shaped by his own memories of flavour and the people he met.

Showing the regional variety and depth of Mexican cooking, the book includes Oaxacan meatballs in smoky chipotle sauce, northern-style grilled carne asada tucked into quesadillas and sweet corn tamales with shrimp from Sinaloa. Personal and cultural essays sit alongside the recipes, making it a rich read for home cooks and anyone who loves Mexican cuisine.

  • Author: Rick Martínez
  • Publisher: Clarkson Potter
  • Format: Hardcover, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593138700

title: Shubeik Lubeik
author: Deena Mohamed
description:
Shubeik Lubeik is Egyptian artist Deena Mohamed's debut graphic novel, set in a Cairo where wishes are real and openly sold, with the most powerful ones costing the most. The title is a fairytale phrase meaning 'your wish is my command' in Arabic, and Mohamed wrote, illustrated and translated the book herself.

Told in three parts, it follows Aziza, Nour and Shokry, each holding a powerful first-class wish and struggling with what it means to make a deepest desire come true, amid bureaucracy and familiar prejudices. Blending calligraphy with contemporary comic styles, it is a literary, feminist and political story that suits readers of graphic novels and magical realism.

  • Author: Deena Mohamed
  • Publisher: Pantheon
  • Format: Hardcover, 528 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781524748418

title: Women Resisting Sexual Violence And The Egyptian Revolution
sheet_title: Women Resisting Sexual Violence And The Egyptian Revolution
author: Manal Hamzeh
description:
Women Resisting Sexual Violence and the Egyptian Revolution: Arab Feminist Testimonies is a study by Manal Hamzeh of women's experiences during the 2011 uprising in Egypt. Women stood at the front of the protests, but activists faced a fierce backlash, including sexual violence and intimidation from the regime and even from fellow protesters.

The book is built around first-hand accounts from four women who played significant roles in the revolution, and the ways of resisting that they developed in response. Hamzeh examines how state violence and violence against women are connected, and contends that this resistance is transforming relations between women and men in Egypt and across the Arab world. It suits readers of feminist, Middle Eastern and political studies.

  • Author: Manal Hamzeh
  • Publisher: I.B. Tauris
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781350333321

title: The Art Of The Bible
author: Scot McKendrick and Kathleen Doyle
description:
The Art of the Bible by Scot McKendrick and Kathleen Doyle is a richly illustrated survey of 45 illuminated Bibles, chosen to trace 1,000 years of history across the Christian world. The authors, both leading manuscript experts, show how these books provide some of the richest evidence of early Christian painting and its interpretations of scripture.

The journey runs chronologically from Constantinople, Lindisfarne and Carolingian Tours to Winchester, Mozarabic Spain, Crusader Jerusalem, northern Iraq, Paris, Naples, Persia and beyond, ending in Gondar in imperial Ethiopia. Every manuscript is remarkable on its own, and together they make a sumptuous book for lovers of art history, medieval culture and religious heritage.

  • Author: Scot McKendrick and Kathleen Doyle
  • Publisher: Thames & Hudson
  • Format: Hardcover, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780500026168

title: The Rise of the Dragon
author: George R.R. Martin, Elio M. García Jr. and Linda Antonsson
description:
The Rise of the Dragon is an illustrated history of House Targaryen by George R.R. Martin, Elio M. García Jr. and Linda Antonsson, and the first volume in a lavish account of the dynasty at the heart of HBO's House of the Dragon. It features more than 180 new illustrations.

Drawing on the history first told in Martin's Fire & Blood, it follows the Targaryens from Aegon's conquest of Westeros to the Dance of the Dragons, the civil war that almost ended their rule. Full of political scheming, alliances and betrayals, it makes a striking reference for longtime fans of Westeros and for viewers new to the family's story.

  • Author: George R.R. Martin, Elio M. García Jr. and Linda Antonsson
  • Publisher: Voyager
  • Format: Hardcover, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Targaryen History, Volume 1
  • ISBN: 9780008557102

Ultimate Guide to Social Media Marketing is a practical handbook from Entrepreneur Press by Eric Butow, Jenn Herman, Stephanie Liu, Amanda Robinson and Mike Allton. It gives businesses an all-round view of social media marketing, moving from strategy to tactics, organic to paid campaigns, and B2B to B2C audiences.

Chapters explain why businesses need social media, how today's major networks and emerging platforms work, and how to build a strategy using current formats. Readers learn to use images and video, chatbots, paid ads and influencer partnerships, build a social media team and measure results over time. It suits small business owners, marketers and entrepreneurs.

  • Publisher: Entrepreneur Press
  • Format: Paperback, 376 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781599186740

Things I Have Learned in My Life So Far is designer Stefan Sagmeister's book of personal maxims turned into typographic art, presented here in an updated edition. The sayings began as a running list in his diary and became artworks shown on billboards, on magazine pages and in public places across the world.

This edition keeps every aphorism from the original 2006 book and adds 48 pages of new work, including material from his exhibitions in New York and Philadelphia and from his project The Happy Film. True to its playful design, it comes as 18 unbound booklets gathered in a laser-cut slipcase. It suits designers, artists and anyone curious about creativity and happiness.

  • Publisher: Abrams
  • Format: Paperback, 296 pages
  • Language: English
