Nike: Better is Temporary by Sam Grawe is Phaidon's large visual history of Nike's design culture, charting how the company grew from a rebellious upstart into a worldwide brand. Its title reflects the idea that being the best is always a journey rather than a destination.

Opening with Breaking2, Nike's 2017 bid to run a marathon in under two hours, the book examines five themes, namely performance, sustainability, collaboration, brand expression and inclusive design, setting famous products beside unpublished designs, prototypes and insider stories. The book is a designed object in its own right, with a silkscreened cover in Volt yellow and Hyperpunch pink. It suits designers, sneaker fans and lovers of sport.

  • Publisher: Phaidon
  • Format: Hardcover, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781838660512

Generous margins leave room for handwritten notes, prayers and reflections, making it well suited to personal study and journaling.

An extensive cross-reference system helps readers follow themes and passages across scripture. This edition is bound in black genuine leather, with the words of Christ printed in red and Thomas Nelson's Comfort Print typeface. Filled over time with a reader's own notes, it can become a treasured keepsake, and it makes a thoughtful gift.

From oranges and embroidery to dabke dancing and olive groves, the book celebrates the richness and resilience of Palestinian heritage. This paperback edition includes a revised appendix giving the Arabic names in Arabic script alongside simple guides to pronunciation. It makes an empowering read-aloud for families and classrooms.

  • Author: Golbarg Bashi
  • Illustrator: Golrokh Nafisi
  • Publisher: Dr. Bashi
  • Format: Paperback, 66 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780999002018

title: This Makes Me Angry
author: Courtney Carbone
description:
This Makes Me Angry by Courtney Carbone, illustrated by Hilli Kushnir, is a Step into Reading Step 2 early reader from the Dealing with Feelings series. It follows a little boy whose day keeps going wrong, first at home and later at school, until his frustration finally bursts out at lunch and he shouts at his friends.

With support from a kind school principal, he begins to recognise his feelings and let his anger go. Short, simple sentences, rhyme and repetition, and picture clues help children recognise familiar words and sound out new ones while learning to name their emotions. It suits children who are starting to read with some help.

  • Author: Courtney Carbone
  • Illustrator: Hilli Kushnir
  • Publisher: Step into Reading (Random House)
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Dealing with Feelings, Step into Reading Step 2
  • ISBN: 9780593564875

title: Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me: Miniature Edition - Hardcover
sheet_title: Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me: Miniature Edition - Hardcover
author: Eric Carle
description:
Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me is Eric Carle's classic picture book about Monica, who longs to play with the moon, and her father, who sets off with a very long ladder to fetch it for her. This listing is the miniature hardcover edition.

When Papa finally reaches the moon, he finds it is far too big to carry home, and the way the problem resolves itself gently introduces the moon's changing phases. Carle's bright collage illustrations include fold-out pages that open sideways and upwards, making it a joyful, interactive bedtime story for young children.

  • Author: Eric Carle
  • Publisher: Picture Book Studio
  • Format: Hardcover, 40 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780887081774

title: The Werewolf of Fever Swamp (Goosebumps) - Softcover
sheet_title: The Werewolf of Fever Swamp (Goosebumps) - Softcover
author: R.L. Stine
description:
The Werewolf of Fever Swamp is book 14 in R.L. Stine's classic Goosebumps series of spooky stories for young readers. Grady Tucker and his family have moved to a new home in Florida on the edge of the eerie Fever Swamp, where strange howls echo through the night.

When Grady adopts a big stray dog that looks a lot like a wolf, and local animals are attacked, the neighbours begin to point the finger. Grady is sure his pet is innocent, but something is prowling the swamp under the full moon. Fast-paced and full of chills, it suits middle-grade readers who like a good scare.

  • Author: R.L. Stine
  • Publisher: Scholastic
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • Series: Goosebumps, Book 14
  • ISBN: 9781407157528

title: Stay Out of the Basement (Goosebumps) - Softcover
sheet_title: Stay Out of the Basement (Goosebumps) - Softcover
author: R.L. Stine
description:
Stay Out of the Basement is the second book in R.L. Stine's Goosebumps series. Dr Brewer has been running plant experiments down in his basement, and he insists they are perfectly harmless. His children, Margaret and Casey, are not so sure, especially once they catch a glimpse of what he is growing.

Even more worrying, their father seems to be changing, picking up some decidedly plant-like habits. Is it all just part of a harmless experiment, or has something gone terribly wrong below the house? Creepy and darkly funny, it is a classic pick for middle-grade readers who enjoy spine-tingling stories.

  • Author: R.L. Stine
  • Publisher: Scholastic
  • Format: Paperback, 122 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Goosebumps, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781407157481

title: حكاية أمريكية
author: Philip Roth
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Philip Roth's American Pastoral, published as An American Tale (حكاية أمريكية) by Dar Al-Tanweer. The novel, which won the 1998 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, follows Seymour 'Swede' Levov, a legendary high-school athlete in Newark who seems to live the post-war American dream.

He marries a former Miss New Jersey, takes over his father's glove factory and settles in an old stone house in rural Old Rimrock. Then, in 1968, his adored daughter Merry, once bright and loving, commits a shocking act of political violence, and his world collapses. A powerful elegy for the promise of the American century, it suits readers of serious literary fiction.

  • Author: Philip Roth
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 527 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The American Trilogy, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9789778280340

title: خراب – كتاب عن الأمل
author: Mark Manson
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Mark Manson's Everything Is F*cked: A Book About Hope, published as Ruin: A Book About Hope (خراب – كتاب عن الأمل) by Dar Al-Tanweer. It is the follow-up to his earlier book The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck.

Manson asks why so many people feel anxious and hopeless at a time of unprecedented safety and prosperity, and examines how hope, values and emotion shape the way we live. Blunt, funny and provocative in his usual style, he argues for a more honest relationship with pain and uncertainty. It suits readers of popular psychology and self-help who prefer to read in Arabic.

  • Author: Mark Manson
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778280326

title: رقصة مع التنانين (جزئين)
author: George R.R. Martin
description:
This is the Arabic edition of George R.R. Martin's A Dance with Dragons (رقصة مع التنانين), the fifth book in A Song of Ice and Fire, translated by Hisham Fahmy and published by Dar Al-Tanweer in two parts. It brings back the characters who were missing from A Feast for Crows and picks up their tangled stories.

In the east, Queen Daenerys Targaryen struggles to end slavery and prove she can rule a city surrounded by enemies before she turns west to reclaim her father's throne. Tyrion Lannister flees across the sea with a price on his head, and in the north Jon Snow, new commander of the Night's Watch, tries to unite people against the threat coming with winter.

  • Author: George R.R. Martin
  • Translator: Hisham Fahmy
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 2 volumes, 1160 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: A Song of Ice and Fire, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9789778280425

title: بريد الذكريات
author: Emma Reyes
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Colombian artist Emma Reyes's memoir The Book of Emma Reyes, published as Memories by Post (بريد الذكريات) and translated by Mark Gamal. Written as a series of letters and published in Colombia in 2012, a decade after her death, it was quickly hailed as a classic. Gabriel García Márquez had encouraged her to write it.

Reyes recalls an extraordinary childhood in Bogotá: born out of wedlock, raised in a windowless room, then abandoned with her sister and sent to a convent where the girls scrubbed, ironed and sewed in fear of the devil. She escaped at nineteen and became an artist, later befriending figures such as Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera. It is a vivid, unsentimental memoir of resilience.

  • Author: Emma Reyes
  • Translator: Mark Gamal
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778280449

title: ليس لدى الكولونيل من يكاتبه
author: Gabriel García Márquez
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Gabriel García Márquez's No One Writes to the Colonel (ليس لدى الكولونيل من يكاتبه), translated by Saleh Almani and published by Dar Al-Tanweer together with other stories. Márquez wrote this short novel in the mid-1950s while living in Paris, where he had gone as a newspaper correspondent.

An elderly retired colonel goes down to the port every Friday to wait for the official letter that will grant the pension he was promised for serving his country, but it never arrives. Spare and precise in style, it is a quiet story of poverty, injustice, dignity and hope. It suits readers who love Latin American literature and Márquez in Arabic translation.

  • Author: Gabriel García Márquez
  • Translator: Saleh Almani
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778280548

title: جنتلمان في موسكو
author: Amor Towles
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Amor Towles's novel A Gentleman in Moscow (جنتلمان في موسكو), translated by Ehab Abdelhamid and published by Dar Al-Tanweer. In 1922, Count Alexander Ilyich Rostov is judged an unrepentant aristocrat by a Bolshevik tribunal and sentenced to house arrest in Moscow's grand Metropol Hotel.

Moved out of his elegant suite into a small attic room, the Count must make a life within the hotel's walls while Russia passes through decades of upheaval outside. Witty, warm and richly observed, the novel asks whether a life confined to a single building can still be full and meaningful. It suits readers of historical and literary fiction who prefer to read in Arabic.

  • Author: Amor Towles
  • Translator: Ehab Abdelhamid
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Tanweer
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778280319

title: Wayward Son
author: Rainbow Rowell
description:
Wayward Son is Rainbow Rowell's sequel to Carry On and the second book in the Simon Snow series. Simon has done everything a Chosen One is meant to do: he beat the Humdrum, ended the war and found love along the way. So why can he barely bring himself to get off the sofa?

His best friend Penny decides he needs a change of scene, so Simon, Penny and Baz set off in a vintage convertible on a road trip across the American West, where they run into dragons, vampires and plenty of trouble, and get thoroughly lost. Funny and heartfelt, it explores what comes after the hero's journey ends, and suits fans of queer young adult fantasy and romance.

  • Author: Rainbow Rowell
  • Publisher: Macmillan Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Simon Snow, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781509896905

title: I Wish You All the Best
sheet_title: I Wish You All the Best
author: Mason Deaver
description:
I Wish You All the Best is Mason Deaver's young adult novel about Ben De Backer, who comes out to their parents as nonbinary and is thrown out of the house as a result. Ben has to move in with Hannah, the older sister they have not seen in years, and start again at a new school.

Ben just wants to keep their head down, but Nathan Allan, a funny and outgoing classmate, has other ideas and decides to befriend them. As the friendship deepens into something more, a terrible turn of events starts to look like the beginning of a happier life. Tender and honest, it is a moving story of identity, family and first love.

  • Author: Mason Deaver
  • Publisher: Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • Series: I Wish You All the Best, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781035026227

title: أسباب وجيهة للمشاعر السيئة
author: Randolph M. Nesse
attention: No photo found — photograph in store; Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
This is the Arabic edition of psychiatrist Randolph M. Nesse's Good Reasons for Bad Feelings (أسباب وجيهة للمشاعر السيئة), which looks at mental illness through the lens of evolutionary biology. Drawing on cases from his clinical work, Nesse asks why natural selection has left the human mind so vulnerable to distress.

He shows how negative emotions such as anxiety and low mood can be useful in particular situations, yet may grow out of proportion and become disabling. Exploring why genes linked to depression, fear or schizophrenia persist, he offers a fresh way to understand why suffering is so common, along with new ideas for easing it. It suits readers interested in psychology and mental health.

  • Author: Randolph M. Nesse
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778280692

title: The Years
author: Annie Ernaux
attention: No photo found — photograph in store
description:
The Years is Annie Ernaux's acclaimed memoir of the period from 1941 to 2006, translated from French by Alison L. Strayer. Ernaux, who received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2022, builds the book from memories and impressions, photographs, songs, films, advertising, headlines and notes from decades of diaries.

Rather than writing 'I', she writes as 'we' and 'she', so that one woman's life merges with the story of her generation and of post-war France. The result is an unusual kind of autobiography, at once intimate and collective, in which time itself seems to tell the story. It suits readers of literary memoir, French literature and social history.

  • Author: Annie Ernaux
  • Translator: Alison L. Strayer
  • Publisher: Fitzcarraldo Editions
  • Format: Paperback, 232 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781913097066

title: لستُ بخير؟
author: Claire Chamberlain
description:
This is the Arabic edition of a self-help guide by Claire Chamberlain, published as Not Okay? (لستُ بخير؟) by Dar Al Saqi and translated by Reem Tawil. Its message is simple and reassuring: nobody feels fine all of the time, and struggling now and then is part of being human.

Written for anyone who is feeling low, overwhelmed or out of sorts for whatever reason, the book offers easy steps, practical advice and encouraging ideas for caring for mind, body and spirit, and for turning setbacks into something more positive. Short and accessible, it makes a gentle companion or a thoughtful gift.

  • Author: Claire Chamberlain
  • Translator: Reem Tawil
  • Publisher: Dar Al Saqi
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9786140322035

title: Hot Date!
author: Rawaan Alkhatib
description:
Hot Date! by Rawaan Alkhatib is a vibrant cookbook devoted entirely to the date, the ancient fruit treasured across many cultures. Its 99 recipes mix traditional favourites with inventive new dishes, ranging from party food to everyday feasts and from sweet to savoury.

Alkhatib draws on her roots in Middle Eastern and Indian cooking and a life spent travelling the world, exploring both the cultural significance of dates and how adaptable they are in the kitchen. Packed with colour and art, with photography by Linda Xiao, the recipes are full of flavour without being fussy. It suits adventurous home cooks and anyone who loves dates.

  • Author: Rawaan Alkhatib
  • Photographer: Linda Xiao
  • Publisher: Chronicle Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781797226446

title: 150 Libraries You Need to Visit Before You Die
sheet_title: 150 Libraries You Need to Visit Before You Die
author: Lea Teuscher
description:
150 Libraries You Need to Visit Before You Die by Lea Teuscher is a richly illustrated tour of 150 remarkable libraries across every continent. Part travel guide and part celebration of reading spaces, it steps inside buildings that hold precious collections and showcase architectural wonders.

The selection runs from lavish Baroque monastery libraries to sleek modern cultural centres, and each entry shares the story behind the place. It suits book lovers, architecture enthusiasts and travellers looking for quiet but endlessly fascinating places to visit, and makes a handsome gift.

  • Author: Lea Teuscher
  • Publisher: Lannoo Publishers
  • Format: Hardcover, 258 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9789020931037

title: Disaster Survival 101: The Essential Guide to Preparing for--And Surviving--Any Emergency Scenario
sheet_title: Disaster Survival 101: The Essential Guide to Preparing for--And Surviving--Any Emergency Scenario
author: Creek Stewart
description:
Disaster Survival 101 is survival expert Creek Stewart's step-by-step guide to preparing for, and getting through, emergencies of every kind, from natural disasters and power-grid failures to attacks and other hazards. It aims to replace panic with a calm, prepared mindset that supports good decisions under pressure.

Detailed chapters cover storing food, sourcing water, heating, generating power, first aid and the basics of self-sufficient living for sheltering at home, while the evacuation sections explain what to bring, choosing a destination and travelling there safely. It suits families and individuals who want practical peace of mind before disaster strikes.

  • Author: Creek Stewart
  • Publisher: Adams Media
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781507223079

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description:
The Great Gatsby is F. Scott Fitzgerald's celebrated novel of the Jazz Age, presented here by Alma Classics. Nick Carraway, a young man newly settled in a cottage on Long Island, is drawn to the glittering parties next door and to his mysterious neighbour, Jay Gatsby, a self-made millionaire with a murky history.

As the two become friends, Gatsby's longing for Daisy Buchanan, the married woman he has loved for years, comes to light, and a summer of excess slides towards tragedy. Widely seen as one of the great American novels, it is a sharp portrait of wealth and decadence and a lasting reckoning with the American dream.

  • Author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 210 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847496140

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
description:
Emma is Jane Austen's sparkling comedy of manners, presented here by Alma Classics. Handsome, clever and rich, Emma Woodhouse is confident she understands the hearts of everyone in the village of Highbury, and she takes great pleasure in arranging matches for her friends while having no intention of marrying herself.

Her well-meant schemes lead to a string of misunderstandings, and only her old friend Mr Knightley is willing to question her judgement. Witty and warm, the novel also reveals how narrow women's choices were in Regency England. Many readers count it among Austen's finest work, and it remains a delight for lovers of classic romance.

  • Author: Jane Austen
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 404 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847494139

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description:
Pride and Prejudice is Jane Austen's best-loved novel, presented here by Alma Classics. When the wealthy and aloof Mr Darcy arrives in the neighbourhood, quick-witted Elizabeth Bennet takes an instant dislike to him, and his pride and her prejudice set the scene for one of the most famous courtships in English literature.

Around them, the Bennet sisters chase their own hopes of love and security, while their parents' mismatched marriage shows just how much is at stake in choosing a partner. Full of sharp social observation and comedy, the novel has inspired countless adaptations and remains an essential read for lovers of classic romance.

  • Author: Jane Austen
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 311 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847493699

title: Sense and Sensibility
author: Jane Austen
description:
Sense and Sensibility was Jane Austen's first published novel, presented here by Alma Classics in a revised edition with notes, appendices, a chronology and a bibliography. It follows two very different sisters: sensible, self-controlled Elinor Dashwood and her passionate, impulsive younger sister, Marianne.

With little money and few connections after their father's death, both sisters see their chances of marrying for love slipping away. Through their contrasting experiences of love, heartbreak and hope, Austen offers a sharp portrait of how money and convention shaped women's lives, balanced with warmth and wit.

  • Author: Jane Austen
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847494849

title: The Prophet
author: Kahlil Gibran
description:
The Prophet is Lebanese-American poet Kahlil Gibran's best-known work, first published in 1923 and presented here by Alma Books. The prophet Almustafa has spent twelve years in Orphalese and is about to board the ship that will carry him home when the townspeople beg him to speak to them before he goes.

In a series of 26 poetic prose essays, he speaks on love, marriage, children, work, joy and sorrow, freedom, friendship, death and much more. Translated into more than 100 languages, the book remains a much-loved spiritual classic and a meaningful gift for anyone reflecting on life's big questions.

  • Author: Kahlil Gibran
  • Publisher: Alma Books
  • Format: Paperback, 128 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847498274

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
description:
The Prince is Niccolò Machiavelli's famous treatise on power and statecraft, presented here by Alma Classics in a new annotated translation by J.G. Nichols. Written by the Florentine diplomat at the end of a long political career in war-torn Italy, it is a frank handbook for any ruler who wants to gain and keep power.

Controversial from the start, the work turned Machiavelli's name into a byword for cunning and manipulation, and it influenced rulers including Frederick the Great and Napoleon. This edition includes notes, a translation of Hegel's essay on Machiavelli and Italy, plus the book's opening in the original Italian. It remains essential reading in political philosophy.

  • Author: Niccolò Machiavelli
  • Translator: J.G. Nichols
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 113 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847493231

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
description:
The Picture of Dorian Gray is Oscar Wilde's only novel, presented here by Alma Classics in an annotated edition with pictures and an account of the author's life and work. The artist Basil Hallward is painting a portrait of the beautiful young Dorian Gray when Lord Henry Wotton arrives and dazzles him with talk of youth and pleasure.

Dorian wishes that the painting could age in his place, and the wish comes true: while he stays young and lovely, the portrait records every sign of time and every sin. A witty, gothic reworking of the Faust legend, the novel explores beauty, art, morality and conscience, and remains a favourite with readers of classic fiction.

  • Author: Oscar Wilde
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 232 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847493729

title: A Room of One's Own
author: Virginia Woolf
description:
A Room of One's Own is Virginia Woolf's landmark extended essay, presented here by Alma Classics. First published in 1929, it grew out of lectures on women and fiction that Woolf gave at Newnham and Girton, the two women's colleges at Cambridge, in October 1928.

Using a fictional narrator, Woolf explores women both as writers and as characters in fiction, and makes her famous case that a woman needs money and a room of her own if she is to write. A founding text of feminist criticism, it argues for space, literal and figurative, for women within a literary tradition shaped by men, and remains witty, sharp and relevant.

  • Author: Virginia Woolf
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 180 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847497888

title: To the Lighthouse
author: Virginia Woolf
description:
To the Lighthouse is Virginia Woolf's modernist masterpiece, presented here by Alma Classics. At the Ramsays' holiday home on Skye, Mrs Ramsay promises her young son that they may visit the lighthouse across the bay the next day, but bad weather and her husband's doubts stand in the way.

The trip is finally made ten years later, after war, grief and loss have changed the family for ever. Moving between the thoughts of its characters, the novel reflects on memory, time, art and human relationships. Daring in style and rich in symbolism, it is one of the landmark works of early twentieth-century fiction.

  • Author: Virginia Woolf
  • Publisher: Alma Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 226 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847496577

title: There's an Alien in My Lunchbox!
sheet_title: There's an Alien in My Lunchbox!
author: Tessa Gearing
description:
There's an Alien in My Lunchbox! is a picture book by Tessa Gearing, illustrated by Chris Jevons and published by Andersen Press. As the title promises, it is a funny story about finding an alien where a packed lunch should be.

With 32 illustrated pages, it is a lively read-aloud for young children who enjoy silly surprises and space creatures.

  • Author: Tessa Gearing
  • Illustrator: Chris Jevons
  • Publisher: Andersen Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781839131684

title: Moon Garden
author: Melody Godfred
description:
Moon Garden: Poetry for Manifestation is a collection by Melody Godfred, author of Self Love Poetry for Thinkers & Feelers, in which the phases of the moon become a guide to setting intentions. Set in an imagined garden lit by moonlight, it combines personal poems with reflective, meditative prose.

Rather than urging readers to push harder, the book encourages them to slow down, heal gently and reconnect with their intuition and the rhythms of nature. It treats growth as something that unfolds in seasons of planting, tending, harvest and rest, and suits readers of spiritual poetry, journaling and mindful self-care.

  • Author: Melody Godfred
  • Publisher: Andrews McMeel Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9798881600044

title: Soon it Will be Sunday
author: Lang Leav
description:
Soon It Will Be Sunday is a collection from novelist and poet Lang Leav that blends poems, short essays and quiet ruminations on what it means to build a meaningful, fulfilled life as a woman.

Leav considers the bonds women form at different points in their lives, the mixed messages society sends them and the decisions that end up defining who they become, including the sense that options narrow as the years go by. Intimate and candid, it holds up a mirror to whichever season of womanhood a reader is living through, and suits fans of contemporary poetry and personal essays.

  • Author: Lang Leav
  • Publisher: Andrews McMeel Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9798881600112

title: A Midnight Moon
author: R.H. Sin
description:
A Midnight Moon is a poetry collection by R.H. Sin that explores loneliness, farewells and the search for comfort in the small hours of the night.

Written in the direct, unguarded voice that readers of Sin's earlier books will recognise, the poems move through heartbreak, hurt that is hard to forgive and the quiet solace found under a night sky. It is a fitting choice for anyone who turns to poetry while working through the end of a relationship, or who simply enjoys short, emotionally open verse.

  • Author: R.H. Sin
  • Publisher: Andrews McMeel Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781524889241

title: The Art of Archie: The Covers
sheet_title: Art Of Archie, The: The Covers
author: Victor Gorelick, Craig Yoe
description:
The Art of Archie: The Covers is an oversized hardcover celebrating more than seventy years of Archie comic book covers, edited by Craig Yoe and Victor Gorelick. It showcases Archie, Betty, Veronica and the rest of the Riverdale gang in full colour.

The book gathers work by much-loved Archie artists including Bob Montana, Dan DeCarlo, Dan Parent and Harry Lucey, with commentary on how the covers were conceived and drawn and the place they hold in American pop culture. It makes a handsome gift for comics collectors, fans of classic cartooning and anyone with a soft spot for Americana. The same editors also produced The Art of Betty and Veronica.

  • Editors: Victor Gorelick and Craig Yoe
  • Publisher: Archie Comics
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781936975792

title: 91 Cool Maths Tricks to Make You Gasp!
sheet_title: 91 Cool Maths Tricks to Make You Ga
author: Anna Claybourne
description:
91 Cool Maths Tricks to Make You Gasp! by Anna Claybourne is a lively activity book that shows children how surprising and entertaining numbers can be, with illustrations by Josephine Wolff.

Young readers learn to build codes that are hard to crack, spot strange number patterns and perform mind-reading tricks powered by maths, while topics like geometry, measurement and statistics are seen from a fresh angle. A glossary explains the key terms. Packed with tricks to try on friends and family, it is aimed at readers aged 8 and up and makes a good companion to classroom learning.

  • Author: Anna Claybourne
  • Illustrator: Josephine Wolff
  • Publisher: Arcturus Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 128 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781789505306

title: 77 Awesome Chemistry Facts Every Kid Should Know!
author: Anne Rooney
description:
77 Awesome Chemistry Facts Every Kid Should Know! is an illustrated introduction to chemistry for children by science writer Anne Rooney.

Each topic opens with a startling fact, such as diamonds falling as rain on some planets or steel being springier than a rubber band, and then explains the science behind it with bright diagrams and fact boxes. Along the way children meet atoms, chemical reactions and the periodic table, and find out what makes fireworks sparkle. It is a fun way to support STEM learning at home or at school.

  • Author: Anne Rooney
  • Publisher: Arcturus Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 128 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781398821934

title: 81 Mind-Blowing Biology Facts Every Kid Should Know!

description:
The New Silk Roads: The Present and Future of the World is Peter Frankopan's follow-up to The Silk Roads, bringing his sweeping reassessment of world history up to the present day.

Tracing the old trade routes eastwards from Europe through Russia and the Middle East to China, Frankopan shows how deeply connected the world remains, and how sharply the rising ambitions of the East contrast with the mood of isolation and fragmentation in the West during the years of Brexit and Trump. It suits readers of global history, politics and economics who want to understand where power is shifting.

  • Author: Peter Frankopan
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 356 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781526608246

title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
sheet_title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
author: Samantha Shannon
description:
The Priory of the Orange Tree is an epic fantasy by Samantha Shannon and the first book in The Roots of Chaos series. Inys has been governed by the House of Berethnet for a millennium, and the unmarried Queen Sabran the Ninth must produce an heir to keep the queendom safe as assassins draw ever closer.

Ead Duryan, an outsider at court and secretly a mage, guards Sabran with forbidden magic, while far across the sea Tané has trained her whole life to ride dragons. As the divided East and West stay locked in mistrust and an ancient enemy stirs, their stories converge in a sweeping tale of queens, dragons and loyalty. It suits readers who love richly built worlds and female-led high fantasy.

  • Author: Samantha Shannon
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury
  • Format: Paperback, 830 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Roots of Chaos, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781408883358

title: A Court of Frost and Starlight
sheet_title: A Court of Frost and Starlight
author: Sarah J. Maas
description:
A Court of Frost and Starlight is a shorter companion story in Sarah J. Maas's A Court of Thorns and Roses series, set in the aftermath of A Court of Wings and Ruin. Feyre, Rhysand and their friends are busy rebuilding the Night Court and a world changed by war.

As the Winter Solstice approaches, bringing a welcome pause, Feyre faces her first celebration as High Lady and discovers that those closest to her carry deeper wounds than she realised, scars that will shape the court's future. Warm, festive and character-focused, it bridges the first three books and the stories that follow, and is a treat for readers who love the series' found family.

  • Author: Sarah J. Maas
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 229 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Court of Thorns and Roses, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9781526617187

title: A Court of Silver Flames
author: Sarah J. Maas
description:
A Court of Silver Flames is the fifth book in Sarah J. Maas's A Court of Thorns and Roses series, turning the spotlight onto Feyre's fierce and prickly sister, Nesta Archeron.

Turned into one of the High Fae without her consent and haunted by the horrors of the war, Nesta is quick to anger and struggles to find her place in the Night Court. Cassian, the battle-hardened winged warrior who provokes her like no one else, is always nearby, and when the two are made to train together the tension between them catches fire. As a new threat looms, Nesta must face her past. It is a steamy, emotional romantasy for adult readers of the series.

  • Author: Sarah J. Maas
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 751 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Court of Thorns and Roses, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9781526635365

title: A Court of Wings and Ruin
sheet_title: A Court of Wings and Ruin
author: Sarah J. Maas
description:
A Court of Wings and Ruin is the third book in Sarah J. Maas's A Court of Thorns and Roses series. Feyre has returned to the Spring Court and her former lover Tamlin, playing a dangerous double game while her heart remains with Rhysand and the Night Court.

Determined to uncover Tamlin's dealings with her enemies, Feyre must keep up her deception as armies gather and war approaches. As secrets, lies and betrayals come to light, she finds that others are hiding things too, and the fight for the truth could cost her and everyone she loves dearly. Epic in scale, it brings the original trilogy to a dramatic close.

  • Author: Sarah J. Maas
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 699 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Court of Thorns and Roses, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781526617170

title: Heir of Fire
author: Sarah J. Maas
description:
Heir of Fire is the third book in Sarah J. Maas's Throne of Glass series. Having survived deadly contests and crushing heartbreak, the assassin Celaena Sardothien journeys across the sea to Wendlyn to face the truth about her heritage.

There she must confront her own past and her inner demons, while a brutal power prepares to conquer her world. The series broadens here, with new characters, new magic and higher stakes, and it suits readers following Celaena's journey through this sweeping young adult fantasy.

  • Author: Sarah J. Maas
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 576 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Throne of Glass, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781526635228

title: Throne of Glass
author: Sarah J. Maas
description:
Throne of Glass is the first book in Sarah J. Maas's fantasy series of the same name. In a kingdom where magic has vanished, the young assassin Celaena Sardothien is brought from prison to the royal castle to fight for her liberty.

If she defeats twenty-three killers, thieves and warriors in a deadly contest, she will win her release and become the King's Champion, sworn to the tyrant who rules from his glass throne. Along the way the Crown Prince tests her, a foreign princess becomes her friend and the Captain of the Guard watches over her, but something sinister lurks within the castle walls. It is a gripping start for fans of young adult fantasy.

  • Author: Sarah J. Maas
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 403 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Throne of Glass, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781526635297

title: Pocket Potters: Hermione Granger
author: J.K. Rowling
description:
Pocket Potters: Hermione Granger is a small illustrated hardback guide to Hermione from the Harry Potter books by J.K. Rowling, illustrated by Laura Proietti, and the third title in the Pocket Potters range.

Young fans discover her favourite subject, how she became friends with Harry and Ron and what a mountain troll smells like, spend a school day by her side and meet her cat, Crookshanks. Packed with spells, charms, potions and plenty of Gryffindor house points, it is a joyful, collectable mini guide for children who love the wizarding world.

  • Author: J.K. Rowling
  • Illustrator: Laura Proietti
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Pocket Potters, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781526674029

title: Pocket Potters: Harry Potter
author: J.K. Rowling
description:
Pocket Potters: Harry Potter is a small illustrated hardback guide to the boy wizard from J.K. Rowling's stories, illustrated by Natalie Smillie, and the first title in the Pocket Potters range.

Children can find out how old Harry was when he started at Hogwarts, who gave him the Marauder's Map and how big a Golden Snitch is, along with Quidditch thrills, Diagon Alley, secret passwords and his closest friends. Bright and collectable, it is an ideal first guide for young fans of the wizarding world.

  • Author: J.K. Rowling
  • Illustrator: Natalie Smillie
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Pocket Potters, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781526672605

title: Pocket Potters: Ron Weasley
author: J.K. Rowling
description:
Pocket Potters: Ron Weasley is a small illustrated hardback guide to Harry's loyal best friend from J.K. Rowling's stories, illustrated by Olia Muza, and the second title in the Pocket Potters range.

Young readers can explore Weasley family fun, wizarding sports, Hogwarts feasts and a household full of memorable pets, learning plenty about Ron along the way. Collectable and colourful, it makes a lovely little gift for children who enjoy the Harry Potter stories.

  • Author: J.K. Rowling
  • Illustrator: Olia Muza
  • Publisher: Bloomsbury Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Pocket Potters, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781526674012

title: Things No One Taught Us about Love: How to Build Healthy Relationships with Yourself and Others
sheet_title: Things No One Taught Us about Love: How to Build Healthy Relationships with Yourself and Others
author: Vex King
description:
Things No One Taught Us About Love by Vex King is a compact guide to building healthier relationships, starting with the one we have with ourselves. It condenses the ideas of his hardback Closer to Love into a shorter paperback.

Written in the warm, accessible voice of Good Vibes, Good Life, it looks at why so many of us expect romance to fix our problems and prove our worth, and how that pressure strains modern relationships. King encourages readers to understand themselves, recognise what love really is and form stronger, deeper connections. It suits anyone working on self-love, dating or their current relationship.

  • Author: Vex King
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035044412

title: The New Censorship
author: Ayala Panievsky
description:
The New Censorship: How the War on the Media Is Taking Us Down by Ayala Panievsky, a scholar and one-time journalist, examines how attacks on the press are weakening democracies around the world.

Panievsky looks at the unexpected ways in which today's media have helped amplify anti-democratic movements, from the rise of what she calls strategic bias to the use of liberal values as a weapon against the democracies built on them. She shows how the populist right has found subtler, more socially acceptable ways to pressure journalists, and argues that courageous reporting matters more than ever in an age of disinformation. It suits readers interested in politics and the media.

  • Author: Ayala Panievsky
  • Publisher: Footnote Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804441114

title: Fawning
author: Ingrid Clayton
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Fawning by clinical psychologist Ingrid Clayton, a specialist in recovery from complex trauma, explores a little-understood fourth response to trauma that sits alongside fight, flight and freeze.

Often mistaken for codependency or people-pleasing, fawning is the urge to stay close to someone, or something, that is causing us pain instead of stepping back: apologising to those who have hurt us, excusing poor behaviour or reshaping ourselves to win approval. Clayton explains why it happens and offers practical guidance for rebuilding a sense of self and finding our voice again. It suits readers working through trauma, people-pleasing or difficult relationships.

  • Author: Ingrid Clayton
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781785123030

title: Letter from Japan
author: Marie Kondo, Marie Iida
description:
Letter from Japan is a personal book from Marie Kondo, the tidying expert behind The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up and the Netflix series Tidying Up with Marie Kondo, co-authored with Marie Iida.

Going beyond tidying and sparking joy, Kondo explores the Japanese traditions, crafts, customs and sensibilities that have shaped her philosophy, and shares the principles she lives by each day. Reflective and gentle, it suits readers interested in Japanese culture, mindful living and bringing more calm and meaning to everyday life.

  • Authors: Marie Kondo and Marie Iida
  • Publisher: Leap
  • Format: Hardcover, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781785125140

title: Days at the Torunka Café
author: Satoshi Yagisawa
description:
Days at the Torunka Café is a warm Japanese novel by Satoshi Yagisawa, author of the Morisaki Bookshop books, translated by Eric Ozawa. It is set in a small café hidden down a narrow Tokyo side street, where local cats wander in as often as visitors.

Its regulars include Chinatsu Yukimura, an enigmatic young woman whose calling card is a paper napkin shaped like a ballerina; Hiroyuki Numata, a man in middle age hoping to recover the contentment he walked away from years ago; and Shizuku, the owner's teenage daughter, who is grieving the loss of her sister. Gentle and quietly moving, it suits readers who enjoy cosy, slice-of-life Japanese fiction about connection and small everyday miracles.

  • Author: Satoshi Yagisawa
  • Translator: Eric Ozawa
  • Publisher: Manilla Press
  • Format: Paperback, 229 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Days at the Torunka Café, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781786585226

title: Enchantra
author: Kaylie Smith
description:
Enchantra is the second book in Kaylie Smith's Wicked Games series, a dark and steamy fantasy romance of enemies turned lovers in which a trip to Italy becomes a deadly trap.

Genevieve Grimm has felt lost since her sister took charge of the family, so when an enigmatic friend of her mother's invites her to his grand Italian palace she accepts, hoping for magic, luxury and perhaps a midnight ball. Instead, his rude and handsome son, Rowen Silver, shuts her out the moment she arrives, and she soon finds herself caught in the family's cursed game. It suits readers of gothic, steamy romantasy.

  • Author: Kaylie Smith
  • Publisher: Second Sky
  • Format: Paperback, 425 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Wicked Games, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781836182559

title: Phantasma
author: Kaylie Smith
description:
Phantasma is the first book in Kaylie Smith's Wicked Games series, a dark gothic fantasy romance set inside a deadly contest held in a haunted mansion.

When her sister vanishes, Ophelia's only hope of saving her is to enter Phantasma and win its prize, a single wish. The game has two rules, survive and do not fall in love, and she must face nine trials that grow more perilous at every stage, among demons, temptations and rivals willing to do anything to win. As her fears threaten to overwhelm her, an enigmatic stranger proposes a deal. It suits fans of spooky, steamy romantasy.

  • Author: Kaylie Smith
  • Publisher: Second Sky
  • Format: Paperback, 493 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Wicked Games, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781836182160

title: My Very First Britannica Encyclopedia
author: Sally Symes, Hanako Clulow
description:
My Very First Britannica Encyclopedia is a hardback encyclopedia for young children from Britannica, by Sally Symes and Hanako Clulow.

As its title suggests, it is designed as a child's first reference book, giving early readers a friendly introduction to the wide world of knowledge for which Britannica is known.

  • Authors: Sally Symes and Hanako Clulow
  • Format: Hardcover
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804661314

title: The Penelopiad
author: Margaret Atwood
description:
The Penelopiad is Margaret Atwood's retelling of Homer's Odyssey from the point of view of Penelope, the wife Odysseus leaves behind when he sails off to the Trojan War.

Speaking from the underworld, Penelope recalls the challenge of ruling a kingdom alone, raising her headstrong son Telemachus, enduring gossip and fending off more than a hundred greedy suitors, all while resenting her cousin Helen, whose beauty started the war. A chorus of her twelve hanged maids adds a darker counterpoint. Witty and pointed, it suits readers who enjoy myth retellings and feminist fiction.

  • Author: Margaret Atwood
  • Publisher: Canongate Canons
  • Format: Paperback, 199 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781786892485

title: The Humans
author: Matt Haig
description:
The Humans is a darkly comic novel by Matt Haig. When Cambridge professor Andrew Martin solves the greatest mathematical puzzle in the world, an alien is sent to take his place, and soon finds himself appalled by the human race.

Found walking naked along a motorway and baffled by everyday life, the visitor at first finds Andrew's wife and teenage son repellent and feels warmth only for Newton, the family dog. Gradually, through music, poetry and small domestic pleasures, he begins to see what makes people worth saving. Funny and tender, it is a story about love, family and what it means to be human.

  • Author: Matt Haig
  • Publisher: Canongate Books
  • Format: Paperback, 291 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781805300175

title: Barcelona
author: Mary Costello
description:
Barcelona is a collection of short stories by Irish writer Mary Costello, peopled by characters whose calm surfaces hide turbulent inner lives.

In one story a young wife, unable to shake the memory of an earlier love, watches her marriage unravel in a hotel room in Spain; in another a father visits his scientist son in Paris and glimpses who he really is; in a third a woman listening to a celebrated writer read sees her own marriage in a painful new light. Precise and searching, the stories capture the quiet unease of modern life and suit readers of literary short fiction.

  • Author: Mary Costello
  • Publisher: Canongate Books
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781837260362

title: How to Stop Time
author: Matt Haig
description:
How to Stop Time is a novel by Matt Haig about Tom Hazard, a man who looks about forty but, because of a rare condition, has been alive for centuries. Now back in London, he has taken a job teaching history at a secondary school and longs for an ordinary life.

Tom has met Shakespeare, sailed with Captain Cook and shared drinks with Fitzgerald, but the secretive Albatross Society that protects people like him has one firm rule: never fall in love. When he falls for a charming French teacher at the school, painful memories and the dangers of his past begin to catch up with him. Moving and thoughtful, it explores time, memory and what makes a life worth living.

  • Author: Matt Haig
  • Publisher: Canongate Books
  • Format: Paperback, 345 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781838858476

title: The Comfort Book
author: Matt Haig
description:
The Comfort Book by Matt Haig is a gathering of short consolations, reflections and stories about hope, survival and the strange wonder of being alive.

Blending philosophy, memoir and personal reflection, Haig draws on thinkers and survivors from across history, from Marcus Aurelius and Nellie Bly to Emily Dickinson and James Baldwin. Made to be dipped into rather than read straight through, it offers the kind of reassurance you might seek from a good friend on a hard day, and suits anyone who found solace in Reasons to Stay Alive.

  • Author: Matt Haig
  • Publisher: Canongate Books
  • Format: Paperback, 260 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781786898326

title: The Life Impossible
author: Matt Haig
description:
The Life Impossible is a novel by Matt Haig about Grace Winters, a retired maths teacher who inherits a dilapidated house on Ibiza from a friend she lost touch with long ago.

With no return ticket and no plan, she travels to the island and sets out among its hills and beaches to learn how her friend lived and died, uncovering something far stranger than she ever imagined. To embrace it, Grace must first make peace with her own past. Full of wonder and adventure, it is a hopeful story about second chances and the power of starting again.

  • Author: Matt Haig
  • Publisher: Canongate Books
  • Format: Paperback, 324 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781838855581

title: Reasons To Stay Alive
author: Matt Haig
description:
Reasons to Stay Alive is Matt Haig's memoir of the breakdown he experienced at twenty-four, when depression and anxiety brought him to the edge of a cliff, and of the slow road back to health.

Part memoir and part guide, it mixes personal recollection with lists, reflections and practical observations, and is warm and often funny despite its subject. Haig writes about making the most of life, loving and reading more fully and feeling everything more deeply. It offers hope and understanding to anyone affected by mental illness, whether directly or through someone they love.

  • Author: Matt Haig
  • Publisher: Canongate Books
  • Format: Paperback, 259 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781782116820

title: Reasons To Stay Alive
author: Matt Haig
description:
Reasons to Stay Alive is Matt Haig's candid account of the depression and anxiety that overwhelmed him at the age of twenty-four, when he came close to ending his life, and of the long journey towards recovery.

Combining memoir with lists, short reflections and hard-won insight, Haig writes about the fear his illness brought, the ways it also shaped who he is, and his hunger to feel life as fully as possible. Honest, hopeful and sometimes funny, it reaches out to anyone living with mental illness or supporting someone who is, and shows that it is possible to come through dark times.

  • Author: Matt Haig
  • Publisher: Canongate Books
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781837264629

title: Right Kind of Wrong: How the Best Teams Use Failure to Succeed
sheet_title: Right Kind of Wrong: How the Best Teams Use Failure to Succeed
author: Amy C. Edmondson
description:
Right Kind of Wrong: How the Best Teams Use Failure to Succeed is a book by Amy C. Edmondson, the Harvard Business School professor known for her research on psychological safety, about learning to fail well.

Edmondson distinguishes between basic failures, complex failures and the intelligent failures that drive discovery, and shows how individuals, teams and organisations can prevent the avoidable kind while embracing the useful kind. Drawing on examples from medicine, business, science and everyday life, she explains how awareness of oneself, of situations and of systems helps people learn from mistakes. It suits leaders, managers and anyone keen to turn setbacks into progress.

  • Author: Amy C. Edmondson
  • Publisher: Penguin (Cornerstone)
  • Format: Paperback, 350 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847943781

title: The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do, and How to Change
sheet_title: The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do, and How to Change
author: Charles Duhigg
description:
The Power of Habit is Charles Duhigg's investigation into how habits form, why they stick and how they can be reshaped. A reporter by background, Duhigg moves between neuroscience labs, corporate boardrooms and personal stories to explain the loop of cue, routine and reward that sits behind so much of what we do each day.

The book looks at habits on three levels, in individuals, in organisations and in whole communities, and introduces the idea of keystone habits that can trigger wider change. Clear and story-driven, it suits anyone hoping to break an unwanted pattern, build a better routine or understand the psychology of behaviour at work and at home.

  • Author: Charles Duhigg
  • Publisher: Random House
  • Format: Paperback, 371 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847946249

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description:
To Kill a Mockingbird is Harper Lee's classic novel of childhood, conscience and injustice in the American South. Set in the small Alabama town of Maycomb during the Depression of the 1930s, it is narrated by young Scout Finch, whose lawyer father Atticus agrees to defend a Black man falsely accused of raping a white woman.

Seen through the eyes of Scout and her brother Jem, the story weighs prejudice, class and courage against the innocence of growing up, while their mysterious neighbour Boo Radley adds a thread of suspense. Warm, funny and deeply moving, it remains a staple of school reading lists and a rewarding novel for adults returning to it.

  • Author: Harper Lee
  • Publisher: Arrow Books
  • Format: Mass Market Paperback, 309 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099549482

title: The Four-Way Path
author: Héctor García, Francesc Miralles
description:
The Four-Way Path is a guide to finding purpose from Héctor García and Francesc Miralles, the authors of Ikigai. This time they turn to Hindu philosophy and its four aims of human life, virtue, prosperity, love and freedom, and explore how keeping these in balance can lead to a calmer, more meaningful existence.

Drawing on some of the oldest spiritual traditions of India, the authors offer gentle, practical reflections on easing anxiety and fear and living with greater intention. Comforting and accessible, it will appeal to readers who enjoyed Ikigai and to anyone looking for a fresh framework for thinking about happiness, fulfilment and what really matters.

  • Author: Héctor García, Francesc Miralles
  • Publisher: Cornerstone Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529908206

title: Innamorata
author: Ava Reid
description:
Innamorata is a gothic fantasy by Ava Reid and the opening book in The House of Teeth series. On an island where the dead once walked and noble houses wielded necromancy, a conqueror has burned the libraries and broken the old magic. The House of Teeth now survives through two cousins: the beautiful heiress Marozia and the silent, uncanny Lady Agnes.

Agnes carries her family's secrets and a mission of vengeance: arrange Marozia's betrothal to Liuprand, heir of the conqueror, and use the match to gain entry to the forbidden library inside his castle. Rich with dark romance, death magic and courtly intrigue, it suits readers of gothic romantasy and fans of Reid's lush, unsettling storytelling.

  • Author: Ava Reid
  • Publisher: Random House
  • Format: Paperback, 560 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The House of Teeth, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9798217300761

title: Explore the Solar System
author: DK
description:
Explore the Solar System is a children's non-fiction title from DK that introduces the Sun, the planets and our wider neighbourhood in space. It is presented as a lift-the-flap concertina book, so young readers can unfold it section by section and peek under the flaps as they go.

A hands-on first look at space for curious children, suited to sharing at home or in the classroom.

  • Author: DK
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 22 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241758083

title: Explore: Science
author: DK
description:
Explore: Science is an illustrated reference book from DK for young readers. As its subtitle suggests, it uses maps and diagrams to show how the world works, taking DK's familiar visual approach to make scientific ideas clear and easy to follow.

A browsable book for curious children and families who enjoy learning through pictures as much as words.

  • Author: DK
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241734865

title: Offline Humans
author: Natalie Alzate
description:
Offline Humans: How to Stop Scrolling and Reconnect with the Real World is a practical guide by writer and creator Natalie Alzate. It invites readers to step back from social media and constant notifications and rediscover the pleasures of life away from screens.

Rather than demanding a sudden digital detox, Alzate sets out a gradual, day-by-day plan for cutting down screen time, supported by journaling prompts, reflective exercises and creative ideas for offline activities. It suits anyone who feels drained by doom-scrolling and wants to protect their attention, spark creativity and look after their mental well-being.

  • Author: Natalie Alzate
  • Publisher: DK
  • Format: Hardcover, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593847008

title: Make Epic Money
author: Ankur Warikoo
description:
Make Epic Money is the third book from entrepreneur and content creator Ankur Warikoo, and his most focused yet on personal finance. Drawing on his own financial highs and lows, he sets out the lessons about money he would have liked to learn far earlier in life.

The book cuts through jargon to offer plain, practical guidance on earning, spending, saving and investing, and on making your money work as hard as you do. It suits young professionals and anyone starting to take their finances seriously who wants a straightforward, no-nonsense blueprint.

  • Author: Ankur Warikoo
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529146868

title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
sheet_title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
description:
How to Win Friends and Influence People is Dale Carnegie's enduring guide to getting along with others, first published in 1936. Built around simple principles and real-life anecdotes, it shows how to make people feel valued, handle disagreements gracefully and bring others round to your point of view without resentment.

Its advice covers making friends with ease, becoming a better conversationalist, leading without giving offence and winning over clients and customers. Conversational and practical, it remains a go-to read for professionals, managers, salespeople and anyone who wants warmer, more effective relationships in work and life.

  • Author: Dale Carnegie
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780091906351

title: The Magic of Thinking Big
author: David J. Schwartz
description:
The Magic of Thinking Big is David J. Schwartz's classic self-help book, originally released in 1959, on how the size of your thinking shapes the size of your success. Schwartz argues that ambition, confidence and positive habits of mind can be learned, and that anyone can train themselves to aim higher.

In practical, encouraging chapters he shows how to overcome self-doubt, turn negative thoughts into constructive ones, plan concrete goals and unlock creative thinking to get more done. Updated for modern readers, it suits anyone at a crossroads in work or life who wants a straightforward, motivating programme for change.

  • Author: David J. Schwartz
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781785040474

title: If You Live To 100, You Might As Well Be Happy: Lessons for a Long and Joyful Life: The Korean Bestseller
sheet_title: If You Live To 100, You Might As Well Be Happy: Lessons for a Long and Joyful Life: The Korean Bestseller
author: Rhee Kun Hoo
description:
If You Live To 100, You Might As Well Be Happy: Lessons for a Long and Joyful Life is a book of reflections by Rhee Kun Hoo, a retired Korean psychiatrist who began writing in his seventies. In his youth he was imprisoned for opposing an authoritarian government, and he later helped to reform mental health care in South Korea.

Now in later life, he shares gentle wisdom on ageing well: learning to forgive, knowing when to persevere and when to let go, facing insecurities and noticing the small pleasures each day brings. Warm and reassuring, it suits readers of all ages looking for comfort and perspective on living a good life.

  • Author: Rhee Kun Hoo
  • Publisher: Rider
  • Format: Hardcover, 197 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846047794

title: Surrounded by Setbacks
author: Thomas Erikson
description:
Surrounded by Setbacks: Or, How to Succeed When Everything's Gone Bad is Thomas Erikson's guide to coping when life, work or other people refuse to go to plan. It builds on the colour-coded behaviour model he introduced in Surrounded by Idiots, applying it to adversity rather than everyday communication.

Starting from the idea that there is little point trying to control everything around you, Erikson shows how to understand your own reactions, deal with difficult people and turn setbacks into progress. Practical and approachable, it suits readers of his earlier books and anyone facing a rough patch at home or at work.

  • Author: Thomas Erikson
  • Publisher: Vermilion
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Surrounded by Idiots
  • ISBN: 9781785043666

title: Embracing Hope: On Freedom, Responsibility & the Meaning of Life
sheet_title: Embracing Hope: On Freedom, Responsibility & the Meaning of Life
author: Viktor E. Frankl
description:
Embracing Hope: On Freedom, Responsibility and the Meaning of Life brings together four works by Viktor E. Frankl that had never been published before. Frankl was the psychiatrist and Holocaust survivor best known for Man's Search for Meaning, and these pieces extend his lifelong themes of purpose and meaning, with particular attention to personal and collective responsibility.

The book is divided into four parts. One draws on a 1955 article about the sense of emptiness Frankl saw spreading through Western society after the Second World War, which he described as a collective neurosis. Thoughtful and humane, it suits readers who found strength in Frankl's earlier writing and anyone reflecting on freedom and how to live well.

  • Author: Viktor E. Frankl
  • Publisher: Rider
  • Format: Hardcover, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846047879

title: Ignite Me
author: Tahereh Mafi
description:
Ignite Me is the third book in Tahereh Mafi's Shatter Me series, a young adult dystopian romance. With Omega Point destroyed, Juliette has no idea whether the rebels, her friends or Adam have survived, but she is more determined than ever to bring down The Reestablishment.

To do it she must turn to Warner, the person she never believed she could rely on, who offers to help her master her powers. Fast-paced and intensely romantic, it brings the original trilogy to a dramatic close and suits readers who love superpowered heroines, slow-burning tension and enemies-to-lovers stories.

  • Author: Tahereh Mafi
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Shatter Me, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781405291774

title: Unite Me
author: Tahereh Mafi
description:
Unite Me collects the first two Shatter Me novellas by Tahereh Mafi, Destroy Me and Fracture Me, in a single volume. Set alongside the main young adult dystopian series, the stories step outside Juliette's point of view to give readers fresh insight into the two young men at the heart of her story.

Destroy Me is told by Warner and Fracture Me by Adam, revealing their thoughts, loyalties and feelings for Juliette at key moments in the series. A must for fans who want more from the Shatter Me world, it is best enjoyed after reading the first two novels.

  • Author: Tahereh Mafi
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Shatter Me, Books 1.5 and 2.5
  • ISBN: 9781405296243

title: The Woman Dies
author: Aoko Matsuda
description:
The Woman Dies brings together fifty-two pieces of short and flash fiction by Aoko Matsuda, author of Where the Wild Ladies Are, translated from the Japanese by Polly Barton. Its starting point is the many forms of discrimination embedded in Japanese society, above all the deep and persistent roots of sexism.

Matsuda tackles serious subjects, from the way violence against women is normalised on screen to the aesthetics of technology, with inventive wordplay, objects that speak for themselves and a dry, deadpan wit. Surreal, playful and sharply critical, it suits readers of contemporary Japanese fiction and feminist writing who enjoy stories that are both funny and unsettling.

  • Author: Aoko Matsuda
  • Translator: Polly Barton
  • Publisher: Europa Editions
  • Format: Paperback, 200 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781787705876

title: Vulture
author: Phoebe Greenwood
description:
Vulture is the debut novel by Phoebe Greenwood, a sharp satire of the war news business and its ethical blind spots. Sara, an ambitious young journalist, is posted to Gaza's Beach Hotel to cover a war. The four-star hotel is a hub for the global media, where staff look after the world's press even as their own homes and families are in danger.

Desperate to make her name, Sara turns from her cautious fixer, Nasser, to Fadi, the youngest of an influential militant clan, in pursuit of a front-page story, with consequences for everyone around her. Tense and darkly comic, it suits readers of literary fiction about journalism, ethics and the Middle East.

  • Author: Phoebe Greenwood
  • Publisher: Europa Editions
  • Format: Hardcover, 300 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781787705791

title: Who Will Tell My Story?
author: Anonymous
description:
Who Will Tell My Story?: A Gaza Diary is the anonymous diary of a person living through the opening months of the bombardment of Gaza that followed the events of 7 October 2023. First published in The Guardian, it records an ordinary life suddenly overturned by fear and loss.

Writing in the moment, the author charts what siege does to the body, the mind and the rhythm of daily life, and wonders whether they will survive to tell the story at all. Intimate and unflinching, it is a first-hand record for readers who want to understand the human cost of the war.

  • Author: Anonymous
  • Publisher: Guardian Faber Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781783353279

title: Dead-End Memories
author: Banana Yoshimoto
description:
Dead-End Memories is a collection of short stories by Banana Yoshimoto, the Japanese author of Kitchen, translated into English by Asa Yoneda. This English edition is published by Faber.

A good choice for readers who enjoy Yoshimoto's quiet, tender style and contemporary Japanese fiction in translation.

  • Author: Banana Yoshimoto
  • Translator: Asa Yoneda
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571382347

title: Chris Mould's War of the Worlds
sheet_title: Chris Mould's War of the Worlds
author: H.G. Wells
description:
Chris Mould's War of the Worlds is an illustrated edition of H.G. Wells's classic science fiction novel, brought to life by artist Chris Mould. Wells's story follows a narrator caught up in a Martian invasion of England, as huge fighting machines stride across the countryside towards London.

Mould's illustrations bring fresh energy to one of the earliest and most influential alien-invasion stories, making it an inviting way for younger readers to discover the classic. It also suits collectors of illustrated editions and long-time fans of Wells.

  • Author: H.G. Wells
  • Illustrator: Chris Mould
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber Children's
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571377404

title: Murder Mindfully
author: Karsten Dusse
description:
Murder Mindfully is a darkly comic crime novel by German author Karsten Dusse, translated by Florian Duijsens. Björn, a lawyer, is told by his wife Katharina to sort out his work-life balance or she will leave and take their daughter with her. Reluctantly, he signs up for a mindfulness course and, to his surprise, it changes everything.

So when his brutal client, crime boss Dragan Sergowicz, gets in the way of the family time he now treasures, Björn applies his new calm, present-moment techniques in a deadly way. Witty, wry and surprisingly thoughtful, it suits readers who like their thrillers with a strong dose of black humour and a sideways look at self-help culture.

  • Author: Karsten Dusse
  • Translator: Florian Duijsens
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 408 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Murder Mindfully, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780571384044

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
description:
Nineteen Eighty-Four is George Orwell's landmark dystopian novel, presented here in an illustrated hardback edition from Faber. In the superstate of Oceania, the Party controls every aspect of life, Big Brother watches through ever-present telescreens and history is constantly rewritten to suit those in power.

Winston Smith, a low-ranking Party member, begins a secret diary and an illicit love affair with Julia, setting himself against a regime that seeks to control even thought itself. With illustrations accompanying Orwell's text, this edition suits both first-time readers and admirers of the classic looking for a special copy.

  • Author: George Orwell
  • Illustrator: Murugiah
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571394388

title: The Iron Man
author: Ted Hughes
description:
The Iron Man is Ted Hughes's classic children's story about a mysterious giant made of metal who appears on a clifftop and begins devouring farm machinery. The local people, alarmed by the damage, set out to trap him, but the Iron Man cannot be kept down for long.

When a vast creature from outer space lands and threatens the whole planet, the Iron Man, helped by a young boy named Hogarth, comes up with a plan to rescue the Earth. Written by a former Poet Laureate, it is a short, gripping tale that works wonderfully read aloud and remains a favourite in schools.

  • Author: Ted Hughes
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 63 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571226122

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description:
Never Let Me Go is Kazuo Ishiguro's haunting novel about friendship, memory and what it means to be human. Narrated by Kathy, it looks back on her years at Hailsham, an apparently idyllic English boarding school where pupils are carefully looked after and encouraged in art and literature but told little about the world beyond.

As Kathy, Ruth and Tommy grow up and eventually leave, they come to understand the truth of what Hailsham is and the future it has prepared them for. Quietly devastating and beautifully restrained, it is a modern classic from the author of The Remains of the Day and a superb choice for book clubs.

  • Author: Kazuo Ishiguro
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 282 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571258093

title: When We Were Orphans: A Novel
sheet_title: When We Were Orphans: A Novel
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description:
When We Were Orphans is a novel by Kazuo Ishiguro set in 1930s England and Shanghai. Christopher Banks has become one of the most celebrated detectives in London, admired throughout society for his cases, yet he remains haunted by the one mystery he has never solved: the disappearance of his parents in Shanghai during his childhood.

Returning to Shanghai as the city is engulfed by war, Banks sets out to uncover the truth at last. Blending detective story with Ishiguro's trademark unreliable memory and emotional restraint, it is a subtle, absorbing novel about the past we carry, suited to readers of literary fiction and fans of his other work.

  • Author: Kazuo Ishiguro
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 313 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571283880

title: How to Disagree
author: Ian Leslie
description:
How to Disagree: Lessons on Productive Conflict at Work and Home is Ian Leslie's exploration of why we argue and how to do it better. Rather than avoiding conflict, he argues, facing our differences openly is the way to make the most of them, whether in the office, in families or in public life.

Leslie draws on lessons from experts in handling disagreement and pairs them with examples of fruitful clashes in the arts, science and technology. Engaging and practical, it suits managers, teams and anyone who wants to turn heated arguments into better decisions at a time when society feels increasingly divided.

  • Author: Ian Leslie
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 286 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571374663

title: Ignite
author: Neeltje van Horen
description:
Ignite is a personal guide to living with more balance and contentment by Neeltje van Horen, a professor of financial economics. Despite a high-flying career, she found herself held back by constant self-doubt and stress, and turned to neuroscience and psychology for a way out.

She explains how gradually rewiring her thinking through small daily habits changed her life, and shares what she discovered along the way. Combining relatable stories, current research and practical strategies, the book suits busy professionals and anyone who feels stuck and wants to work with their own mind rather than against it.

  • Author: Neeltje van Horen
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781835010761

title: The Bell Jar
author: Sylvia Plath
description:
The Bell Jar is Sylvia Plath's only novel, a classic of twentieth-century American literature. Esther Greenwood, a gifted young woman spending a summer working at a magazine in New York, seems to have a bright future ahead of her, yet she feels increasingly disconnected from the world around her.

As the city's parties, dinners and romantic misadventures give way to a gradual descent into breakdown, Plath captures Esther's experience with sharp wit and piercing honesty. A landmark novel about mental illness, ambition and the pressures placed on women in 1950s America, it continues to resonate with readers today.

  • Author: Sylvia Plath
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 234 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571226160

title: Klara and the Sun
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description:
Klara and the Sun is a tender novel by Kazuo Ishiguro, narrated by an Artificial Friend called Klara who has a remarkable gift for observation. From her place in a store, she studies the customers who come in and the passers-by in the street outside, hoping that someone will soon choose her.

When her circumstances seem set to change, Klara is warned not to put too much faith in human promises. Through her unique perspective, Ishiguro looks at a rapidly changing world and asks what it truly means to love. Quiet, moving and thought-provoking, it suits readers of literary fiction and gentle, character-led science fiction.

  • Author: Kazuo Ishiguro
  • Publisher: Faber & Faber
  • Format: Paperback, 340 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780571364909

title: Rub-a-Dub Dinos Stickable Foam Bath Shapes
sheet_title: Rub-a-Dub Dinos Stickable Foam Bath Shapes
author: Mudpuppy
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Rub-a-Dub Dinos Stickable Foam Bath Shapes is a bath-time set from Mudpuppy featuring dinosaur-themed foam shapes. As the name suggests, the pieces are designed to stick to the side of the bath when wet, so little ones can arrange and rearrange them while they play.

A playful addition to bath time for young children who love dinosaurs.

  • Author: Mudpuppy
  • Illustrator: Teresa Bellón
  • Publisher: Mudpuppy Press
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780735375086

title: Wild Rainbow Color Magic Bath Book
sheet_title: Wild Rainbow Color Magic Bath Book
author: Mudpuppy
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Wild Rainbow Color Magic Bath Book is a six-page bath book from Mudpuppy, part of its Color Magic line. Designed for bath time, it gives little ones a book they can enjoy in the water, with a colourful rainbow theme suggested by its title.

A cheerful way to bring early book play into the bath, and a thoughtful gift for new families.

  • Author: Mudpuppy
  • Publisher: Galison
  • Format: Bath book, 6 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780735370395

title: Art of the Bookstore : The Bookstore Paintings of Gibbs M. Smith
sheet_title: Art of the Bookstore : The Bookstore Paintings of Gibbs M. Smith
author: Gibbs Smith
description:
The Art of the Bookstore: The Bookstore Paintings of Gibbs M. Smith is a celebration of bookshops and the people who run them. Gibbs Smith, founder of the publishing house that bears his name, pairs forty of his paintings of bookstores with words from independent booksellers around the world.

The result is an affectionate tribute to the atmosphere, character and community of independent bookselling, and to the love of books that sustains it. Presented as a giftable hardback, it suits book lovers, booksellers and anyone who enjoys browsing the shelves of a good bookshop.

  • Author: Gibbs Smith
  • Publisher: Gibbs Smith
  • Format: Hardcover, 152 pages
