  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781423606437

title: If an Egyptian Cannot Speak English
sheet_title: If an Egyptian Cannot Speak English
author: Noor Naga
description:
If an Egyptian Cannot Speak English is a novel by Noor Naga set in Cairo in the years after the Arab Spring. There, a young woman raised in America by Egyptian parents, 'returning' to a country she has never visited, meets a man who grew up in the village of Shobrakheit. Once a photographer of the revolution, he is now out of work, addicted to cocaine and living in a shack on a rooftop.

Love follows, and soon he is living in her bright apartment, but their longing for each other and for who they hope to become takes a violent turn. A dark romance that probes power, desire and the blind spots of American identity politics abroad, it suits readers of bold literary fiction.

  • Author: Noor Naga
  • Publisher: Graywolf Press
  • Format: Paperback, 194 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781644450819

title: The Burnout Doctor: Your 6-Step Recovery Plan
sheet_title: The Burnout Doctor: Your 6-Step Recovery Plan
author: Dr Claire Ashley
description:
The Burnout Doctor: Your 6-Step Recovery Plan is a compassionate guide to recognising, recovering from and preventing burnout by Dr Claire Ashley. A GP who burned out early in her own medical career, she combines her lived experience with a professional background in medicine and neuroscience.

Her six-step plan helps readers understand what burnout is, rebuild their energy and find sustainable ways of working, so they can do well at work without sacrificing their mental health. Non-judgemental and practical, it suits anyone feeling exhausted by work, as well as managers and colleagues who want to support others.

  • Author: Dr Claire Ashley
  • Publisher: Green Tree
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781399412803

title: King of Scars
author: Leigh Bardugo
description:
King of Scars is the first book in Leigh Bardugo's King of Scars duology, set in the Grishaverse of Shadow and Bone and Six of Crows. Nikolai Lantsov, the charming young king of Ravka, has rebuilt his war-torn country, but he hides a dangerous secret: a dark power growing inside him that threatens everything he has fought for.

With Zoya Nazyalensky, the formidable commander of the Grisha army, he sets out to find a cure before his enemies discover the truth, while across the border the spy Nina Zenik undertakes a perilous mission in Fjerda. Full of magic, political intrigue and banter, it suits fans of the Grisha books and lovers of epic young adult fantasy.

  • Author: Leigh Bardugo
  • Publisher: Hachette
  • Format: Paperback, 518 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: King of Scars, Book 1 (Grishaverse)
  • ISBN: 9781510104464

title: Worlds Collide
author: Chris Colfer
description:
Worlds Collide is the sixth and final book in Chris Colfer's The Land of Stories series. This time the fairy-tale heroes and villains are no longer confined to their own world, and they have spilled out into New York City, causing chaos in the Big Apple.

Twins Alex and Conner Bailey must face their toughest fight so far as they try to bring order back between the human world and the fairy-tale realm. Packed with action, humour and heart, it brings the series to a satisfying close and suits middle-grade readers who have followed the twins from the very beginning.

  • Author: Chris Colfer
  • Publisher: Hachette Children's Group
  • Format: Paperback, 448 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Land of Stories, Book 6
  • ISBN: 9781510201361

title: Raised by Wolves
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description:
Raised by Wolves is the first book in a young adult paranormal series by Jennifer Lynn Barnes, author of The Inheritance Games. As a four-year-old, Bryn saw a rogue werewolf kill her parents. Taken in by Callum, the alpha of a werewolf pack, she has grown up as a human among Weres, mostly obeying pack law.

Now fifteen, she discovers that the pack has been hiding a secret: Chase, a newly turned teenage werewolf kept in a cage. His arrival stirs terrifying memories of her parents' death, and in her search for answers Bryn is ready to defy the pack itself. Tense and romantic, it suits fans of paranormal fantasy and found-family stories.

  • Author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
  • Publisher: Quercus Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Raised by Wolves, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781786542380

title: Bethlehem: A Celebration of Palestinian Food
sheet_title: Bethlehem: A Celebration of Palestinian Food
author: Fadi Kattan
description:
Bethlehem: A Celebration of Palestinian Food is a cookbook by chef Fadi Kattan that doubles as a portrait of his home city. Kattan takes readers through Bethlehem's markets and spice shops and introduces the farmers and artisans who supply the ingredients at the heart of his cooking.

Alongside recipes rooted in Palestinian tradition and his own love of experimentation, the book shares the stories of local food producers, many of them older women, whom Kattan met while recording a podcast during the Covid pandemic. Warm and evocative, it suits home cooks, lovers of Middle Eastern food and anyone curious about Palestinian culture.

  • Author: Fadi Kattan
  • Publisher: Hardie Grant Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781958417287

title: How Do You Choose?
author: Erin Claire Jones
description:
How Do You Choose?: A Human Design Guide to What's Best for You at Work, in Love, and in Life is a practical introduction to Human Design by Erin Claire Jones, who coaches and teaches the system. Human Design is a personality system that blends astrology, Eastern philosophy and other elements to describe how each person makes decisions and thrives.

Jones shows how to use the system as an everyday tool, drawing on episodes from her own life and examples from her client work, to help readers make choices about careers, relationships and wellbeing that suit their individual design. Accessible and encouraging, it suits newcomers to Human Design and anyone seeking a fresh lens on decision-making.

  • Author: Erin Claire Jones
  • Publisher: HarperOne
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063412774

title: Trust Your Mind
author: Jenara Nerenberg
description:
Trust Your Mind: Embracing Nuance in a World of Self-Silencing is an examination of groupthink and self-censorship by Jenara Nerenberg, who wrote Divergent Mind and founded The Neurodiversity Project. She looks at how the pressure to hold the right opinions is narrowing debate and making people afraid to speak.

Exploring campuses, workplaces, the media and life online, Nerenberg offers tools for understanding how our minds work under social pressure and for turning fear into empathy. Thoughtful and timely, it suits readers who feel uneasy in a polarised culture and want to think independently while staying open to others.

  • Author: Jenara Nerenberg
  • Publisher: HarperOne
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063317093

title: How To Win
author: Kate Hays
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
How to Win is a guide to sustainable success by Dr Kate Hays, the sport psychologist who has worked with Sarina Wiegman's England women's team, the Lionesses. Over two decades in elite sport she has developed a framework called 'The Building Blocks of Success' for creating a winning mindset in individuals and teams alike.

Hays shares the lessons behind that approach to help readers find purpose, reach their potential and thrive, whether they are athletes, leaders or simply trying to do their best at work and at home. Clear and encouraging, it suits sports fans, managers and anyone interested in the psychology of high performance.

  • Author: Kate Hays
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008698294

title: A Dark Forgetting
author: Kristen Ciccarelli
description:
A Dark Forgetting is a romantic fantasy by Kristen Ciccarelli, author of The Crimson Moth, first published as Edgewood. However far she runs, Emeline Lark cannot escape the forest, which haunts her with strange disappearances and stories of fae magic. So when her grandfather vanishes, she has no choice but to head into the woods to find him.

There she meets Hawthorne Fell, a brooding tithe collector who does all he can to turn her back, and is drawn into a deadly curse tied to the past she left behind. Lush, atmospheric and romantic, it suits readers who enjoy fae folklore, dark forests and slow-burning love stories.

  • Author: Kristen Ciccarelli
  • Publisher: Magpie
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008783921

title: Every Spiral of Fate
author: Tahereh Mafi
description:
Every Spiral of Fate is the fourth book in Tahereh Mafi's This Woven Kingdom series, a sweeping young adult romantic fantasy. The wedding day has finally come: the Jinn queen Alizeh is to marry Cyrus, the mysterious ruler of Tulan, in an enchanted ceremony. But Cyrus, bound to his bride by a blood oath, finds little to celebrate.

He has lost his heart to the very person sworn to kill him, while Alizeh can free her people only by ending his life herself, and Prince Kamran waits to take his place. With danger gathering around the wedding, it is a tense, romantic instalment for readers following Alizeh's story.

  • Author: Tahereh Mafi
  • Publisher: Electric Monkey
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • Series: This Woven Kingdom, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9780008629212

title: Release Me
author: Tahereh Mafi
description:
Release Me is the second book in Tahereh Mafi's new series set in the Shatter Me world, a decade after The Reestablishment fell. Rosabelle Wolff's carefully laid plan has given way to a thirst for revenge. To rescue her sister, she has to return home and bring down the system that shaped her.

Numbing her mind and body has always kept her alive in Ark Island's surveillance state, but lately her defences are slipping, and James Anderson is the reason. Tense and romantic, it suits fans of Shatter Me and of enemies-to-lovers dystopian romance.

  • Author: Tahereh Mafi
  • Format: Hardcover
  • Language: English
  • Series: Shatter Me: The New Republic, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780008718176

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
description:
Brave New World is Aldous Huxley's classic dystopian novel, first published in 1932. It imagines a technologically advanced World State in which people are bred in laboratories, conditioned from birth to accept their place in a rigid caste system, and kept content with the drug soma and endless distraction.

When Bernard Marx, a discontented member of the elite, brings John, raised on a 'Savage Reservation', into this orderly society, the cost of its stability comes sharply into focus. A searching novel about freedom, happiness and control, it remains essential reading for students and anyone interested in where science and society may be heading.

  • Author: Aldous Huxley
  • Publisher: Harper Perennial
  • Format: Mass Market Paperback, 278 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063482708

title: Lebanon
author: Anissa Helou
description:
Lebanon: Cooking the Foods of My Homeland is a cookbook by food writer Anissa Helou celebrating the cuisine of the country where she grew up and where her late mother's family came from. Her ninth book, it shows the remarkable range of Lebanese cooking, from familiar classics such as hommos and kibbeh to lesser-known regional specialities.

Alongside the recipes, Helou explores the culinary history and culture behind each region's food, offering both a practical kitchen companion and a rich portrait of the country. It suits home cooks, lovers of Middle Eastern food and readers in the region who want to explore the depth of Lebanese tradition.

  • Author: Anissa Helou
  • Publisher: Ecco
  • Format: Hardcover, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063334922

title: A Study in Drowning
author: Ava Reid
description:
A Study in Drowning is Ava Reid's first young adult novel, a dark academic fantasy. Effy Sayre has believed in fairy tales all her life, because the Fairy King has appeared to her in visions since she was a child. Her battered copy of Emrys Myrddin's epic Angharad, the tale of a mortal girl who loves and then destroys the Fairy King, is what keeps her going.

When the late author's family invites entries to rebuild his estate, Effy is convinced she is meant to win, but crumbling Hiraeth Manor and its unwelcoming residents, including a rival scholar, hold dark secrets. Atmospheric and romantic, it suits fans of gothic fantasy, folklore and stories about the power of books.

  • Author: Ava Reid
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Study in Drowning, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780063211513

title: Red as Royal Blood
author: Elizabeth Hart
description:
Red as Royal Blood is a young adult murder mystery by Elizabeth Hart, set at a royal court full of secrets. Ruby has never met a puzzle she could not solve, and although she is destined to spend her life in service to the royal family, she longs for a real challenge. Nothing prepares her for the king's decision to name her his heir.

Thrust into a poisonous court, Ruby must steady a kingdom in crisis while facing the late king's furious widow and three arrogant princes who make no secret of their scorn. Then she finds a note from the king claiming he was murdered and warning that she could be next. Twisty and romantic, it suits fans of royal intrigue and whodunnits.

  • Author: Elizabeth Hart
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063441118

title: The Land of Sweet Forever
author: Harper Lee
description:
The Land of Sweet Forever: Stories and Essays is a posthumous collection of writing by Harper Lee, author of To Kill a Mockingbird. It brings together newly discovered short stories with essays and magazine pieces published during her lifetime, and is introduced by Casey Cep.

The early stories reveal Lee as a determined young writer honing her craft in the hope of magazine publication, long before Scout, Jem and Atticus made her name. A valuable companion to her two novels, it offers readers and admirers of American literature a fresh view of one of its most celebrated voices.

  • Author: Harper Lee
  • Introduction: Casey Cep
  • Publisher: Harper
  • Format: Hardcover, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063460515

title: The Second Chance Convenience Store
author: Ho-yeon Kim
description:
The Second Chance Convenience Store is a heartwarming novel by Korean author Ho-yeon Kim, translated by Janet Hong. Dok-go lives in Seoul Station, cannot recall anything of his past and could badly do with a drink. After he comes across a lost wallet and returns it to its owner, Mrs Yeom, a former history teacher who runs a neighbourhood corner shop, his life takes an unexpected turn.

Mrs Yeom offers him a job on the night shift, and his quiet kindness gradually touches the lives of staff and customers alike. Gentle, funny and full of warmth, this story of community and redemption suits readers who enjoy cosy, uplifting fiction in translation.

  • Author: Ho-yeon Kim
  • Translator: Janet Hong
  • Publisher: Harper Perennial
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063354777

title: Spellcaster
author: Jaymin Eve
description:
Spellcaster is the first book in Jaymin Eve's Weatherstone College series, a romantic fantasy set at the world's most prestigious college for witches. When a young woman's magic finally blooms at twenty-two, she is stunned to win a place there, even though her powers are still wildly unpredictable.

Determined to live up to her family's legacy, she is almost derailed on her first day by Logan Kingston, a powerful spellcaster and the son of her father's enemy, whom she has been warned to avoid. Full of ancient magic, rivalry and romance, it suits fans of enemies-to-lovers romantasy.

  • Author: Jaymin Eve
  • Publisher: MIRA
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Weatherstone College, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781335472007

title: Only God Can Judge Me
author: Jeff Pearlman
description:
Only God Can Judge Me: The Many Lives of Tupac Shakur is a biography of the rapper, actor and cultural icon by journalist Jeff Pearlman. Tracing Tupac's life from his childhood with an activist mother, through his rise to fame in the 1990s, to his murder in Las Vegas at the age of twenty-five, it pieces together a complex and contradictory figure.

Built on extensive reporting, the book explores Tupac's music, his films, his legal troubles and the East Coast and West Coast rivalry, while asking why his influence endures decades later. It suits hip-hop fans, music lovers and readers of in-depth biography.

  • Author: Jeff Pearlman
  • Publisher: Mariner Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 464 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063304574

title: Good to Great and the Social Sectors: A Monograph to Accompany Good to Great
sheet_title: Good to Great and the Social Sectors: A Monograph to Accompany Good to Great
author: Jim Collins
description:
Good to Great and the Social Sectors is a short monograph by Jim Collins written as a companion to his management classic Good to Great. It responds to the questions most often raised by readers working outside business, in areas such as education, healthcare, non-profits and government.

Drawing on conversations with more than a hundred social sector leaders, Collins shows how his principles, including Level 5 Leadership, can be adapted to organisations that measure success by mission rather than profit. Concise and practical, it suits non-profit managers, school and hospital leaders and anyone applying the ideas of Good to Great beyond the corporate world.

  • Author: Jim Collins
  • Publisher: Jim Collins
  • Format: Paperback, 35 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780977326402

title: Thorn Season
author: Kiera Azar
description:
Thorn Season is the first book in Kiera Azar's debut young adult romantasy trilogy. In Daradon, those known as Wielders are feared and persecuted for their Spectre, a shimmering magical thread that can reach beyond the body to caress, pick a lock or even kill, and they have always been hunted for it.

Alissa Paine, heiress to a family of Hunters, is herself a secret Wielder who has survived only through rigid self-control and her father's protection. When she is called to court for the debutante season, keeping her secret becomes harder than ever. Sharp and romantic, it suits fans of court intrigue and forbidden magic.

  • Author: Kiera Azar
  • Publisher: Storytide
  • Format: Paperback, 464 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Thorn Season, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780063463127

title: The Secret Book Society
author: Madeline Martin
description:
The Secret Book Society is a historical novel by Madeline Martin, set in London in 1895 during the Victorian era. Three women, each constrained by a stifling marriage or by society's expectations, are mysteriously invited to take tea with the reclusive Lady Duxbury, only to discover that the gathering hides a forbidden book club.

Among them are Eleanor Clarke, a loving mother trapped by a tyrannical husband, and Rose Wharton, an American heiress married into English society. Through books they discover friendship, independence and the nerve to take charge of their own lives. Warm and absorbing, it suits book club readers and lovers of stories about the power of reading.

  • Author: Madeline Martin
  • Publisher: Hanover Square Press
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781335016287

title: The Cortisol Reset Plan
author: Marina Wright
description:
The Cortisol Reset Plan is a complete guide to balancing hormones by health coach and nutritionist Marina Wright, who specialises in hormonal health. It explains how chronic stress and an imbalance in the stress hormone cortisol can lie behind unexplained weight gain, exhaustion, poor sleep and inflammation, symptoms that often go unrecognised, particularly in women.

Wright sets out what triggers these confusing symptoms, how long-term stress affects the body and which everyday habits help to restore balance, with the aim of reversing weight gain and supporting nervous system health. Practical and accessible, it suits anyone who feels run down and wants to understand the role hormones play in their wellbeing.

  • Author: Marina Wright
  • Publisher: HarperOne
  • Format: Hardcover, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063436275

title: I Am Cleopatra
author: Natasha Solomons
description:
I Am Cleopatra is a historical novel by Natasha Solomons, author of Fair Rosaline, that retells the life of one of history's most misunderstood women. As a favoured daughter of the Pharaoh, the young Cleopatra spends her childhood among the scrolls of Alexandria's great library, dreaming of one day telling her own story.

On her father's death the throne passes jointly to Cleopatra and her scheming younger brother Ptolemy, and while the young queen travels along the Nile to meet her people, Ptolemy plots to rule alone. Vivid and empowering, it reclaims Cleopatra's voice for readers who love historical retellings of remarkable women.

  • Author: Natasha Solomons
  • Publisher: Harper Perennial
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063449756

title: The Origin of Politics
author: Nicholas Wade
description:
The Origin of Politics is a provocative work of science and history by Nicholas Wade, author of Before the Dawn. Wade argues that human nature, shaped by evolution, is too often ignored by those who set out to reshape society, and that this is a serious error.

Surveying biological and political history, he challenges both the progressive belief that human nature can be moulded at will and the conservative view that it can never change for the better, and examines how ideologies that overlook our evolved instincts affect social cohesion, birth rates and the fortunes of nations. It suits readers interested in politics, evolution and debate.

  • Author: Nicholas Wade
  • Publisher: Harper
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063379787

title: Open to Work
author: Ryan Roslansky, Aneesh Raman
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Open to Work: How to Get Ahead in the Age of AI is a practical career guide by Ryan Roslansky and Aneesh Raman, LinkedIn's chief executive and its Chief Economic Opportunity Officer. Starting from the view that work is changing for everyone, they argue that old career advice about fixed skills and steady promotion no longer holds.

Drawing on LinkedIn data from more than a billion professionals, the authors explain which skills matter now and how to adapt as AI reshapes jobs, illustrated with stories of people who used AI to improve at their job, land a new role or start a business. It suits professionals at every stage who want to stay ahead.

  • Author: Ryan Roslansky, Aneesh Raman
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008770662

title: The Rose Bargain
author: Sasha Peyton Smith
description:
The Rose Bargain is a Victorian-inspired young adult romantasy by Sasha Peyton Smith, the first book in a series. In an alternate London of 1848, England has been ruled for four centuries by an undying fae monarch who seized the crown through trickery, and who grants each subject a single chance to strike a deal for whatever they most desire.

As Ivy Benton prepares for her debut, she sets out to win the hand of one of the queen's sons, only to find herself falling for his brother. Romantic, atmospheric and full of fae intrigue, it suits fans of Regency-style society drama and courtly fantasy.

  • Author: Sasha Peyton Smith
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Rose Bargain, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780063372535

title: Big Trust
author: Shadé Zahrai
description:
Big Trust: Rewire Self-Doubt, Find Your Confidence, and Fuel Success is a guide to overcoming insecurity by Dr Shadé Zahrai. She argues that what holds most people back is not a lack of skills, productivity or contacts but self-doubt: the inner voice that says others are further ahead, that you are an impostor or that you are not good enough.

Whether it shows up as perfectionism, overthinking or people-pleasing, Zahrai treats it as a single problem and offers ways to rewire these patterns, build lasting confidence and stop measuring yourself against others in a world designed to make you feel behind. It suits professionals and anyone whose self-doubt is getting in the way of success.

  • Author: Shadé Zahrai
  • Publisher: HarperOne
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063490109

title: The Lucky Ride
author: Yasushi Kitagawa
description:
The Lucky Ride is an uplifting Japanese novel by Yasushi Kitagawa, translated by Takami Nieda, about a man offered an unexpected chance at happiness. After losing several contracts, Shuichi must repay his company a large sum, forcing him and his wife to cancel the Paris trip they had spent a year planning.

The trip had been their best chance of reconnecting with their teenage daughter, who no longer attends school and rarely leaves her bedroom, and Shuichi is convinced he is the unluckiest man in Japan. Then a magical ride changes everything. Gentle and thought-provoking, it suits readers who enjoy life-affirming fiction in translation.

  • Author: Yasushi Kitagawa
  • Translator: Takami Nieda
  • Publisher: HarperOne
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063376243

title: Watch Me
author: Tahereh Mafi
description:
Watch Me is the first book in Tahereh Mafi's new series set in the Shatter Me world, a decade after Juliette Ferrars and Aaron Warner led the rebellion that toppled The Reestablishment and founded the New Republic. The peace they won is fragile, and The Reestablishment is regrouping, stronger and cleverer than before.

James Anderson, Warner's younger brother, makes it onto the Ark, the last stronghold of The Reestablishment, even if it lands him in a cell. There he meets Rosabelle Wolff, the perfect agent for The Reestablishment's mission, a young woman who always has a plan. Tense and romantic, it opens a new chapter for Shatter Me fans.

  • Author: Tahereh Mafi
  • Publisher: Electric Monkey
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Shatter Me: The New Republic, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780008722746

title: Tech-Powered Sales: Achieve Superhuman Sales Skills
sheet_title: Tech-Powered Sales: Achieve Superhuman Sales Skills
author: Justin Michael, Tony Hughes
description:
Tech-Powered Sales: Achieve Superhuman Sales Skills is a practical guide by sales experts Justin Michael and Tony Hughes to modern, technology-enabled selling. They argue that traditional sales methods are becoming outdated, and that tougher markets and remote working make it harder than ever to build a strong pipeline the old way.

The authors explain how to develop technical quotient, or TQ, and how to assemble an effective sales tech stack that boosts reach and results. Packed with actionable guidance, it suits sales professionals, team leaders and business owners who want to combine human skills with the latest tools.

  • Author: Justin Michael, Tony Hughes
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Leadership
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781400226528

title: Death on the Nile
author: Agatha Christie
description:
Death on the Nile is one of Agatha Christie's most celebrated Hercule Poirot mysteries. Aboard a luxurious steamer cruising the Nile, far from the rest of the world, Poirot finds himself among a group of travellers whose holiday is simmering with jealousy, resentment and passion.

When the wealthy young heiress Linnet Doyle is found shot dead, it seems that nearly everyone on board had a reason to want her gone, and Poirot must set aside the wonders of ancient Egypt to unravel a far deadlier puzzle. Atmospheric and ingeniously plotted, it is a perfect introduction to Christie for new readers.

  • Author: Agatha Christie
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 373 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Hercule Poirot, Book 18
  • ISBN: 9780007527557

title: The Mysterious Affair at Styles
author: Agatha Christie
description:
The Mysterious Affair at Styles is Agatha Christie's first published novel and the debut of her famous Belgian detective, Hercule Poirot. In the aftermath of the First World War, Captain Hastings is staying at Styles Court in Essex when its wealthy mistress, Emily Inglethorp, dies from strychnine poisoning.

Poirot, a refugee living nearby, is called in to investigate, and soon finds suspects throughout the household, from the victim's much younger husband to her stepsons. Full of clues, red herrings and Poirot's meticulous reasoning, it is the perfect place to start for readers new to Christie's detective fiction.

  • Author: Agatha Christie
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 258 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Hercule Poirot, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780007527496

title: Awful Auntie
author: David Walliams
description:
Awful Auntie is a funny and spooky children's adventure by David Walliams, illustrated by Tony Ross. Stella Saxby is the rightful heir to Saxby Hall, the grand family home, but her wicked Aunt Alberta is determined to take it from her, aided by her enormous and terrifying owl.

Trapped and outwitted at every turn, Stella has one secret weapon: a rather spooky new friend who helps her fight back. Full of slapstick humour, twists and heart, it suits young readers who love comic adventures and laugh-out-loud stories.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007453627

title: Boogie Bear
author: David Walliams
description:
Boogie Bear is a picture book by David Walliams, illustrated by Tony Ross. At the North Pole, a large, fluffy polar bear spends her days swimming, fishing and eating, until she drifts off to sleep and wakes to find herself a very long way from home.

Things look bad, and then they get worse, but her adventure becomes a funny and heartwarming story about celebrating difference. Lively and full of humour, it is a lovely read-aloud for young children and families.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 40 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008172787

title: Demon Dentist
author: David Walliams
description:
Demon Dentist is a darkly funny children's novel by David Walliams, illustrated by Tony Ross. Alfie hates going to the dentist, but when a new dentist, Miss Root, arrives in his town, strange things start to happen: instead of coins from the tooth fairy, children wake to find horrible surprises under their pillows.

Together with his friend Gabz, Alfie sets out to uncover the truth behind the sinister goings-on before it is too late. Spooky, silly and surprisingly moving, it suits young readers who like their adventures with plenty of laughs and a shiver or two.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 448 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007453580

title: Mr Stink
author: David Walliams
description:
Mr Stink is David Walliams's funny and touching children's novel, illustrated by Quentin Blake. Twelve-year-old Chloe feels lonely and unpopular, overshadowed by her seemingly perfect younger sister, until she befriends Mr Stink, the town tramp, and his loyal dog, the Duchess.

When Chloe's mother sets out to clear tramps from the town, Chloe hides Mr Stink in the family's garden shed, and secrets on both sides begin to unravel. Warm and full of humour, it is a story about kindness, family and looking beyond appearances, perfect for young readers and families.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 269 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007279067

title: The Beast of Buckingham Palace
author: David Walliams
description:
The Beast of Buckingham Palace is a sweeping children's adventure from David Walliams, illustrated by Tony Ross. Set in a strange and fiery future, it draws on myth and legend to tell the story of a small boy who discovers that the fate of the whole world rests on his shoulders.

Walliams pairs high-stakes fantasy with his trademark silliness, pitting good against evil in a tale full of danger, daring and laugh-out-loud moments. Tony Ross's lively drawings appear throughout, making this chunky novel an inviting read for confident middle-grade readers and a fun shared read-aloud for families.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 464 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008438708

title: The Ice Monster
author: David Walliams
description:
The Ice Monster is a big-hearted adventure from David Walliams, with illustrations by Tony Ross. It follows Elsie, a ten-year-old orphan living rough in Victorian London, who becomes fascinated by news of a woolly mammoth discovered frozen at the North Pole.

When Elsie finally meets the ancient creature in person, she is swept into a journey that stretches from London all the way to the Arctic. Funny, warm and full of peril, it celebrates unlikely friendship and the idea that heroes can be any shape or size, making it a great pick for middle-grade readers.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 496 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008164706

title: The World's Worst Children 2
author: David Walliams
description:
The World's Worst Children 2 is David Walliams' second collection of gleefully nasty tales about badly behaved boys and girls, illustrated throughout by Tony Ross. Ten new stories introduce a fresh gallery of horrors, from Humbert, a baby so hungry he devours everything his parents own, to Gruesome Griselda and her creepy-crawly pranks.

Each story is short, silly and wickedly funny, making the book ideal for dipping into at bedtime or for reluctant readers who like their humour on the gross side. Fans of the first volume will find plenty more cautionary chaos here.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The World's Worst Children, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780008621889

title: The World's Worst Children 3
author: David Walliams
description:
The World's Worst Children 3 brings together another ten hilariously horrible tales from David Walliams, illustrated throughout by Tony Ross. This time readers meet more ghoulish girls and naughty boys, including Boastful Barnabas, whose ego is so inflated he could burst, and Tandy, famous for tantrums of epic proportions.

The stories are quick to read and packed with outrageous situations, comic comeuppances and Ross's expressive illustrations. It is a natural next step for anyone who enjoyed the earlier collections, and works well for reading aloud or for independent readers who love a laugh.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The World's Worst Children, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780008621896

title: The World's Worst Monsters
author: David Walliams
description:
The World's Worst Monsters is a collection in David Walliams' World's Worst series, this time turning from naughty children, parents, teachers and pets to the creatures that lurk in the shadows. Ten tales feature a monstrous line-up that includes vampires, werewolves, mummies, ghosts and zombies.

The scares are mostly for laughs, with plenty of gross-out humour and surprising twists, and Adam Stower's full-colour illustrations bring each monster vividly to life. A fun pick for young readers who like their stories a little spooky and a lot silly.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Adam Stower
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008581633

title: THE DAY THE CRAYONS QUIT
author: Drew Daywalt
description:
The Day the Crayons Quit is a witty picture book written by Drew Daywalt and illustrated by Oliver Jeffers. When young Duncan opens his crayon box, he finds no crayons ready to colour, just a pile of letters from each one explaining why it has had enough.

Beige feels overlooked next to Brown, Blue is worn out from colouring water, and Orange and Yellow have fallen out over which of them truly represents the sun. Told through the crayons' funny, indignant notes, the story rewards creative thinking and makes a playful read-aloud for young children.

  • Author: Drew Daywalt
  • Illustrator: Oliver Jeffers
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 40 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Crayons
  • ISBN: 9780007513765

title: Green Eggs and Ham
author: Dr. Seuss
description:
Green Eggs and Ham is Dr. Seuss's classic rhyming picture book about persistence and trying new things. Sam-I-am is determined to get his grumpy friend to taste a plate of green eggs and ham, and he refuses to accept no for an answer, offering the dish in one unlikely place after another.

Built from a small vocabulary of simple, repeated words, the bouncy verse is ideal for children who are starting to read on their own, while the escalating silliness keeps it a favourite for reading aloud. It is a gentle, funny lesson in being open to something new.

  • Author: Dr. Seuss
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007355914

title: Oh, The Places You'll Go
author: Dr. Seuss
description:
Oh, the Places You'll Go! is Dr. Seuss's uplifting rhyming book about the journey of life, written as an encouraging send-off to a young reader setting out into the world. It celebrates the excitement of new beginnings while acknowledging that every path has its slumps, waiting places and moments of doubt.

With its bright illustrations and memorable verse, it is a popular gift for graduations, birthdays and other milestones, and speaks just as clearly to adults as to children. A warm reminder that perseverance and optimism can carry you a long way.

  • Author: Dr. Seuss
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 48 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007413577

title: Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus
sheet_title: Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus
author: John Gray
description:
Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus is John Gray's classic relationship guide, built on the idea that men and women often communicate, cope with stress and express their needs in very different ways. Using the memorable image of partners from two different planets, Gray explains common sources of misunderstanding between couples.

The book offers practical advice for improving communication, giving and receiving support, and resolving arguments before they escalate. It suits singles looking for insight, couples wanting to deepen their connection and anyone trying to understand why a relationship went off course.

  • Author: John Gray
  • Publisher: Thorsons
  • Format: Paperback, 307 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007152599

title: Looking for Alaska
author: John Green
description:
Looking for Alaska is John Green's debut novel, a coming-of-age story about friendship, first love and loss. Miles Halter, a teenager obsessed with famous last words, leaves his quiet, lonely life behind for Culver Creek boarding school, hoping to find the 'Great Perhaps' that the poet Rabelais spoke of.

There he meets the brilliant, funny and troubled Alaska Young, who pulls him into a world of pranks, late-night talks and big questions. Moving and thoughtful, it explores how one person can change another forever, and suits older teens and adult readers of contemporary fiction.

  • Author: John Green
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007523160

title: The One
author: Kiera Cass
description:
The One is the third book in Kiera Cass's Selection series, the romantic dystopian story of a televised competition for the heart of a prince. America Singer never expected to get anywhere near the crown, or to fall for Prince Maxon, yet as the contest draws to its close she is among the final contenders.

With rebel attacks growing more dangerous beyond the palace, America must decide what she truly wants and how hard she is willing to fight for it. Blending romance, royal intrigue and high stakes, it suits young adult readers who enjoy love triangles and fairy-tale settings with an edge.

  • Author: Kiera Cass
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 323 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Selection, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780007466719

title: Big Nate Flips Out
author: Lincoln Peirce
description:
Big Nate Flips Out is the fifth Big Nate novel by cartoonist Lincoln Peirce, mixing text and comic strips to follow sixth-grader Nate Wright, self-declared genius and detention regular. Nate has never been known for tidiness, and this time his messy habits land his best friend Francis in real trouble.

Can Nate finally get organised, or will the pressure send him over the edge? Packed with doodles, cartoons and classroom chaos, it is a great choice for reluctant readers and fans of illustrated school comedies.

  • Author: Lincoln Peirce
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 216 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Big Nate, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9780007478279

title: Big Nate Goes for Broke
author: Lincoln Peirce
description:
Big Nate Goes for Broke is the fourth novel in Lincoln Peirce's Big Nate series, starring Nate Wright, the sixth-grade cartoonist with a big personality and an even bigger talent for trouble. Like the other books in the series, it combines a fast-moving story with Peirce's own comic strips and doodles throughout.

The blend of prose and cartoons makes it an easy, entertaining read for children who might otherwise avoid long blocks of text, and a natural fit for fans of illustrated school stories.

  • Author: Lincoln Peirce
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 215 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Big Nate, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9780007462704

title: Big Nate on a Roll (Big Nate, Book 3)
sheet_title: Big Nate on a Roll (Big Nate, Book 3)
author: Lincoln Peirce
description:
Big Nate on a Roll is the third Big Nate novel from cartoonist Lincoln Peirce. Nate Wright has always been a star of his scout troop, until Artur, the boy everyone thinks is perfect, signs up and pushes Nate into second place.

With a big prize at stake, the rivalry heats up and Nate is determined to come out on top. Told through a lively mix of text and comic strips, it is funny, quick to read and ideal for middle-grade readers who love school-day mischief and cartoons.

  • Author: Lincoln Peirce
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 216 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Big Nate, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780007355181

title: The Boy with the Biggest Head in the World (Big Nate, Book 1)
sheet_title: The Boy with the Biggest Head in the World (Big Nate, Book 1)
author: Lincoln Peirce
description:
The Boy with the Biggest Head in the World is the first Big Nate novel by Lincoln Peirce, published in the US as Big Nate: In a Class by Himself. Nate Wright is convinced he is destined for greatness, but his school day gets off to a terrible start when he forgets his lunch and panics about a test he never studied for.

From an accidental collision with the head teacher to a run-in with Mrs Godfrey, the teacher he likes least, the disasters keep piling up. Mixing story and cartoons, it introduces a classic comic-strip hero to a new generation of readers.

  • Author: Lincoln Peirce
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 213 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Big Nate, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780007355167

title: Everything Is F*cked: A Book About Hope
sheet_title: Everything Is F*cked: A Book About Hope
author: Mark Manson
description:
Everything Is F*cked: A Book About Hope is Mark Manson's follow-up to The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck. He starts from a puzzle: by most material measures life has never been better, yet many people feel more anxious and hopeless than ever.

Drawing on psychology, philosophy and history, Manson examines where hope comes from, why it so often lets us down, and what a healthier relationship with it might look like. Blunt, funny and provocative, it suits readers who like their self-help with a strong dose of big ideas and irreverent humour.

  • Author: Mark Manson
  • Publisher: Harper
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063091054

title: Ex Libris: 100 Books for Everyone's Bookshelf
sheet_title: EX LIBRIS: 100 Books For Everyoneâ€™s Bookshelf
author: Michiko Kakutani
description:
Ex Libris is a collection of short, personal essays by Pulitzer Prize-winning critic Michiko Kakutani, each devoted to a book that has shaped her thinking and helps make sense of the world today. It ranges widely across fiction, memoir and nonfiction, old and new.

Readers will find contemporary novels, timeless classics and works of history and politics, all discussed in an accessible way and accompanied by illustrations throughout. It makes an inspiring reading list for book lovers and an elegant gift for anyone looking for their next great read.

  • Author: Michiko Kakutani
  • Publisher: William Collins
  • Format: Hardcover, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008421953

title: The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari
sheet_title: The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari
author: Robin Sharma
description:
The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari is Robin Sharma's inspirational fable about rediscovering purpose. Julian Mantle is a hard-driving, high-earning lawyer whose punishing lifestyle ends in a heart attack, prompting him to give up his possessions and travel to India in search of a more meaningful way to live.

Through the lessons he learns from Himalayan sages, the story shares simple principles on mindset, discipline, balance and personal fulfilment. Easy to read and gently motivating, it suits anyone feeling stuck in the rat race and looking for a fresh perspective on success.

  • Author: Robin Sharma
  • Format: Paperback, 231 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780007848423

title: Insurgent
author: Veronica Roth
description:
Insurgent is the second novel in Veronica Roth's Divergent trilogy, set in a dystopian Chicago where society is divided into factions. This anniversary edition, marking ten years since publication, includes bonus material from Roth and a reimagined cover by illustrator Victo Ngai.

As conflict spreads between the factions, Tris Prior fights to protect the people she loves while wrestling with grief, guilt, loyalty and identity. Old secrets surface, alliances shift, and Tris must accept everything that being Divergent means, whatever the cost. A gripping read for fans of action-packed young adult dystopian fiction.

  • Author: Veronica Roth
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 592 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Divergent, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780008468958

title: The World's Worst Teachers
author: David Walliams
description:
The World's Worst Teachers is a collection of ten darkly funny stories from David Walliams about the most dreadful grown-ups ever to stand at the front of a classroom, illustrated by Tony Ross. Meet Dr Dread, a science teacher who is part monster, the permanently furious Miss Seethe, and Pent, a teacher who is terrified of children.

Following on from the World's Worst Children books, it delivers the same mix of outrageous characters, gruesome twists and slapstick humour. Easy to dip into, it will appeal to anyone who has ever thought their own teacher was a nightmare.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008637545

title: Act Like a Lady, Think Like a Man: What Men Really Think About Love, Relationships, Intimacy, and Commitment
sheet_title: Act Like a Lady, Think Like a Man: What Men Really Think About Love, Relationships, Intimacy, and Commitment
author: Steve Harvey
description:
Act Like a Lady, Think Like a Man is comedian and broadcaster Steve Harvey's frank relationship guide for women, written to reveal how men really feel about love, intimacy and commitment. This is the expanded edition of the book.

Drawing on his experience as a radio host and stand-up comic, Harvey explains how men approach dating, what motivates them and how women can set their standards and recognise a partner worth keeping. Direct, humorous and practical, it suits women who want an insider's view of the male perspective.

  • Author: Steve Harvey
  • Publisher: Amistad
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780062351562

title: Death on the Nile
author: Agatha Christie
description:
Death on the Nile is one of Agatha Christie's best-known Hercule Poirot mysteries. A luxury cruise along the Nile should offer a peaceful escape, but beneath the calm of the Egyptian evenings simmer jealousy, greed and old grudges among the passengers.

When a young heiress is shot dead on board, Poirot must turn his attention from the wonders of ancient Egypt to a cunning murder with no shortage of suspects. Atmospheric and expertly plotted, it is a perfect introduction to Christie and essential reading for fans of classic crime.

  • Author: Agatha Christie
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 373 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Hercule Poirot, Book 18
  • ISBN: 9780008328948

title: Noise
author: Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony, Cass R. Sunstein
description:
Noise is a study of the hidden variability in human decision-making by Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony and Cass R. Sunstein. The authors show how professionals who should reach the same conclusion, such as doctors, judges or insurance underwriters, routinely arrive at strikingly different ones, and how even one person may judge differently depending on the time of day.

Alongside bias, they argue, this random scatter in judgement carries enormous and largely unnoticed costs across medicine, law, business and government. The book explains how to measure noise and offers practical techniques for reducing it, making it valuable reading for leaders, policymakers and anyone interested in better decisions.

  • Author: Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony, Cass R. Sunstein
  • Format: Paperback, 452 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008534448

title: Code Name Bananas
author: David Walliams
description:
Code Name Bananas is a wartime adventure from David Walliams, illustrated by Tony Ross. It is 1940 and Britain is fighting the Second World War, and eleven-year-old Eric is happiest at London Zoo, where his favourite resident is Gertrude the gorilla.

When bombs start falling on the city, Eric sets out to save Gertrude, and with the help of Uncle Sid, a zookeeper, the unlikely trio flee to the seaside, only to stumble on a top-secret enemy plot. Funny, exciting and full of heart, it suits middle-grade readers and families who enjoy history with plenty of laughs.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 480 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008471804

title: Geronimo
author: David Walliams
description:
Geronimo is a picture book from David Walliams and illustrator Tony Ross about a baby penguin with one big ambition: to fly. Everyone knows that penguins cannot take to the air, but Geronimo refuses to let that stop him from dreaming.

Supported by his father and friends, the determined little penguin sets out to prove the doubters wrong. Funny and touching, with comic illustrations on every page, it gently encourages children to chase even their wildest dreams and makes a lovely read-aloud for young children.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008279790

title: Slime
author: David Walliams
description:
Slime is a riotous children's novel from David Walliams, illustrated by Tony Ross. On the Isle of Mulch, the grown-ups seem to exist only to make children miserable, from the teacher to the ice-cream seller, and worst of all is the dreadful Greta Greed.

Then Ned, a boy who uses a wheelchair, makes an astonishing discovery: slime, a gooey substance with extraordinary powers. What exactly is it, and can it help the children get their own back on Mulch's meanest adults? Gross, gleeful and full of mischief, it is ideal for young readers who enjoy seeing horrible grown-ups get their comeuppance.

  • Author: David Walliams
  • Illustrator: Tony Ross
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008409555

title: Think Like a Monk
author: Jay Shetty
description:
Think Like a Monk is Jay Shetty's guide to applying monastic wisdom to everyday life. After spending three years as a monk in India before returning to the world of work, Shetty distils what he learned into practical lessons on calming the mind, finding purpose and building healthier habits.

The book tackles negativity, fear, comparison and stress, and offers exercises in meditation, gratitude and self-reflection that anyone can try. Accessible and encouraging, it suits readers looking for a more peaceful, focused and meaningful approach to modern life, whatever their beliefs.

  • Author: Jay Shetty
  • Publisher: Thorsons
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008746018

title: What You Do Is Who You Are
sheet_title: What You Do Is Who You Are
author: Ben Horowitz
description:
What You Do Is Who You Are is Ben Horowitz's exploration of how leaders build company culture, from the co-founder of the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz. He argues that culture is defined not by mission statements or values posters but by the everyday behaviour of people throughout an organisation.

To make his case, Horowitz draws on striking historical examples, including the Haitian revolutionary Toussaint Louverture, the samurai code of Bushido and Genghis Khan, alongside lessons from modern business. Practical and thought-provoking, it suits founders, managers and anyone trying to shape how a team actually behaves.

  • Author: Ben Horowitz
  • Publisher: William Collins
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008740696

title: Katabasis
author: R.F. Kuang
description:
Katabasis is a dark academia fantasy by R.F. Kuang in which two rival graduate students must travel into Hell itself. Alice Law has given up almost everything, her health, her pride and her peace of mind, to study Magick at Cambridge under Professor Jacob Grimes, the greatest magician of his age.

When Grimes is killed in a magical mishap for which she may be to blame, Alice resolves to bring back his soul, only to find Peter Murdoch, her academic rival, set on the same mission. Clever, haunting and darkly witty, it explores ambition, academia and the price of success, and suits adult readers of literary fantasy.

  • Author: R.F. Kuang
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Paperback, 550 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780008501877

title: Ruthless Vows
author: Rebecca Ross
description:
Ruthless Vows is the second book in Rebecca Ross's Letters of Enchantment duology, following Divine Rivals. Two weeks after Iris comes back from the front, battered and grieving, the war still rages, and Roman, stranded on the enemy's side, cannot remember who he is or what she meant to him.

Hoping to recover what he has lost, Roman starts writing again, now for the other side, and when a mysterious letter slips through his wardrobe door he begins corresponding with someone who feels strangely familiar. Romantic, magical and full of longing, it will delight readers of historical-flavoured romantasy.

  • Author: Rebecca Ross
  • Publisher: Magpie
  • Format: Paperback, 448 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Letters of Enchantment, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780008588267

title: The Signs
author: Tara Swart
description:
The Signs is neuroscientist and medical doctor Tara Swart's guide to reconnecting with intuition, from the author of The Source. She argues that in a busy, stressed and screen-dominated world we have lost touch with the instincts and senses humans once depended on, and with the signals they can offer.

Drawing on brain science, Swart explains how to tune back into these cues and use them for clearer decisions, greater resilience and progress towards personal goals. Combining research with accessible guidance, it suits readers interested in mindset, wellbeing and the science behind gut feelings.

  • Author: Tara Swart
  • Publisher: HarperOne
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780063485327

title: A War of Wyverns
author: S.F. Williamson
description:
A War of Wyverns is the second book in S.F. Williamson's A Language of Dragons series, an alternate-history fantasy in which dragons share Britannia with humans. Vivien Featherswallow now goes by many names: the wanted rebel known as The Swallow, a translator close to decoding a new language, and simply Viv, the girl who lost her love after turning spy.

As a conflict that started with bombs and teeth becomes one fought with words, Viv begins to suspect that everything she believed, even about herself, may be false. Tense and romantic, it suits young adult readers who enjoy dragons, intrigue and linguistic puzzles.

  • Author: S.F. Williamson
  • Publisher: HarperCollins
  • Format: Hardcover, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Language of Dragons, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780063353862

title: Own It
author: Iona Bain
description:
Own It! is a personal finance guide for young adults by Iona Bain, a UK money expert who specialises in millennial finances. Starting from the challenges facing her generation, from low wages and high house prices to poor returns on savings and the economic aftermath of Covid-19, she makes the case that investing is the key to a more secure future.

Bain explains pensions, savings and investment in plain language, covering everything from robo-advisers and auto-enrolment to green investing and the risks of forex schemes promoted on social media. Practical and upbeat, it is a helpful starting point for anyone who feels left behind financially.

  • Author: Iona Bain
  • Publisher: Harriman House
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780857198303

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
description:
The Psychology of Money is Morgan Housel's insightful look at why financial success has less to do with intelligence than with behaviour. Rather than treating money as a matter of formulas and spreadsheets, he shows how personal history, ego, pride and emotion shape the choices people make about saving, spending and investing.

Across 19 short, story-driven chapters, Housel explores luck and risk, the power of compounding, the meaning of enough and the value of patience. Clear and engaging, it suits newcomers and experienced investors alike, as well as anyone who wants a healthier relationship with wealth and happiness.

  • Author: Morgan Housel
  • Publisher: Harriman House
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780857197689

title: Stop Waiting, Start Investing
author: Ryan King
description:
Stop Waiting, Start Investing is Ryan King's beginner-friendly guide to building long-term wealth through the stock market with minimal effort. It is aimed at people who have never invested and do not know where to start, as well as those already investing who want reassurance that their approach is sound.

King champions a passive, simple and largely automated strategy that, as the subtitle promises, needs only around ten minutes of work. Clear and encouraging, it helps readers improve their financial education, overcome nerves about investing and take charge of their money.

  • Author: Ryan King
  • Publisher: Harriman House
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804090787

title: HBR Daily Leader: Everyday Wisdom for Exceptional Leadership
sheet_title: HBR Daily:Everyday Wisdom for Exceptional Leadership
author: Harvard Business Review
description:
HBR Daily Leader is a year-long companion for professional growth from Harvard Business Review, with an entry for each of the 365 days. Every day combines ideas to spark thinking, inspiring quotations and reflective questions, turning personal development into a manageable daily habit.

Topics range from communicating clearly and managing time to widening influence and building new skills, all distilled from HBR's best thinking on management. Easy to dip into, it suits new and experienced managers alike and makes a thoughtful gift for anyone stepping up into leadership.

  • Author: Harvard Business Review
  • Publisher: Harvard Business Review Press
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9798892791076

title: Don't Be Yourself
author: Tomas Chamorro-Premuzic
description:
Don't Be Yourself is a provocative challenge to one of today's most popular pieces of advice from psychologist Tomas Chamorro-Premuzic, author of Why Do So Many Incompetent Men Become Leaders? Drawing on decades of research, he argues that the cult of authenticity, at work and in life, often does more harm than good.

Examining everything from Silicon Valley's celebration of the true self to diversity initiatives that fail to deliver, he shows how an obsession with self-expression can undermine empathy, teamwork and leadership, and explains what to do instead. Sharp and research-driven, it suits managers, leaders and anyone curious about the psychology of success.

  • Author: Tomas Chamorro-Premuzic
  • Publisher: Harvard Business Review Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781647829834

title: The Power of Creative Destruction
author: Philippe Aghion, Céline Antonin, Simon Bunel
vendor: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
description:
The Power of Creative Destruction is an ambitious account of how economies grow, by economists Philippe Aghion, Céline Antonin and Simon Bunel, translated from the French by Jodie Cohen-Tanugi. Building on Joseph Schumpeter's idea that innovation constantly replaces old firms and technologies with new ones, the authors explain what drives prosperity and why it can stall.

Against a backdrop of rising inequality, sluggish growth and environmental crisis, they argue that the solution is not to abandon capitalism but to reform it, using evidence to show how smart policy can encourage innovation while protecting people. Rigorous yet readable, it suits students of economics, policymakers and curious general readers.

  • Author: Philippe Aghion, Céline Antonin, Simon Bunel
  • Translator: Jodie Cohen-Tanugi
  • Publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780674292093

title: Good Vibes, Good Life
author: Vex King
description:
Good Vibes, Good Life is Vex King's uplifting guide to self-love and positive living. Having overcome hardship himself, King draws on his personal experiences and intuitive wisdom, which made him a source of hope for many young people on Instagram.

The book explores how to genuinely love yourself, turn negative emotions into positive ones and seek lasting happiness. It encourages readers to practise self-care, step away from toxic energy, build habits such as mindfulness and meditation, and shift limiting beliefs to invite opportunity in. Beautifully designed with inspiring quotes throughout, it suits anyone ready for a more positive outlook.

  • Author: Vex King
  • Publisher: Hay House UK
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781788171823

title: Perfect Victims
author: Mohammed El-Kurd
description:
Perfect Victims is a collection of essays by Palestinian writer and poet Mohammed El-Kurd, author of Rifqa. It affirms the Palestinian spirit of resistance and refusal, and questions why Palestinians are constantly asked to prove their humanity to the rest of the world.

Rather than performing the role of the flawless, sympathetic victim, El-Kurd turns the gaze back on the reader, refusing both deference and condemnation. Fierce, lyrical and uncompromising, it argues that the way we look at Palestine reflects how we look at one another, and suits readers of political essays and Middle East affairs.

  • Author: Mohammed El-Kurd
  • Publisher: Haymarket Books
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9798888903155

title: Rifqa
author: Mohammed El-Kurd
description:
Rifqa is the debut poetry collection of Palestinian writer Mohammed El-Kurd, following in the footsteps of Ghassan Kanafani's Palestinian resistance literature. The title honours El-Kurd's grandmother, who was driven out of Haifa in 1948, and the poems draw on what his family has lost in Sheikh Jarrah, the Jerusalem neighbourhood whose refugee residents live under constant threat of eviction.

Through vivid, defiant verse, El-Kurd argues that the ongoing seizure and destruction of Palestinian homes is not a reminder of the Nakba but a continuation of it. Personal and political in equal measure, it suits readers of contemporary poetry and anyone seeking Palestinian voices on displacement and memory.

  • Author: Mohammed El-Kurd
  • Publisher: Haymarket Books
  • Format: Paperback, 100 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781642595864

title: Laozi's Dao De Jing: A New Interpretation for a Transformative Time
sheet_title: Laozi's Dao de Jing: A New Interpretation for a Transformative Time by Laozi
author: Ken Liu
description:
Laozi's Dao De Jing is a new English translation of the ancient Chinese classic by novelist and translator Ken Liu. Composed around 400 BC in an age of conflict and ambition, Laozi's text speaks up for humility, simplicity and everyday wisdom over clever elites and the certainty of ideologues.

Alongside the translation, Liu offers a series of commentaries on his own struggle to capture the meaning of the verses and how the work changed him. Beautifully designed, earthy and playful, it suits newcomers to Daoism as well as readers who already know the text in other versions.

  • Author: Laozi
  • Translator: Ken Liu
  • Publisher: Apollo
  • Format: Hardcover, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035917624

title: Click Here
author: Alex Schultz
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Click Here is a practical guide to growing a business online by Alex Schultz, Meta's chief marketing officer. Drawing on his long experience at the company, he explains how to choose between the many channels, platforms and tools available to modern marketers and how to get the most from a marketing budget.

Covering the key principles of digital marketing and advertising, the book is relevant whether you work for a global corporation or are launching your own start-up. Clear and grounded in real-world practice, it suits marketers, founders and business owners who want to understand what drives growth in the digital age.

  • Author: Alex Schultz
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035434107

title: The Wrath of the Fallen
author: Amber V. Nicole
description:
The Wrath of the Fallen is the fourth book in Amber V. Nicole's Gods & Monsters series, an epic and spicy romantasy. Samkiel, heir to the throne, has returned, and as the realms divide into those who back him and those who side with Nismera, open war grows ever closer.

Stripped of the Ring of Oblivion, Samkiel struggles to contain the dark force inside him, while Dianna is haunted by dreams of vengeance sent by an ancient power. Determined to protect her, Samkiel embarks on a perilous journey to the Otherworld, the one place he most fears to go. Fans of dark, high-stakes fantasy romance will find plenty to devour.

  • Author: Amber V. Nicole
  • Publisher: Headline
  • Pages: 528
  • Language: English
  • Series: Gods & Monsters, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9781035437030

title: Kiku: The Japanese Art of Good Listening
author: Haru Yamada
description:
Kiku: The Japanese Art of Good Listening is a book by Haru Yamada about kiku, the Japanese word for listening, and the idea that truly hearing other people is a skill worth cultivating. It approaches listening as an art rooted in Japanese culture.

It suits readers interested in communication, relationships and Japanese ways of thinking, and anyone hoping to become a more attentive listener at home or at work.

  • Author: Haru Yamada
  • Publisher: Headline
  • Format: Hardcover, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035411818

title: Keep Sharp
author: Sanjay Gupta
description:
Keep Sharp is a science-based guide to keeping your brain healthy as you age by Dr Sanjay Gupta, the neurosurgeon who serves as CNN's chief medical correspondent. Bringing together insights from leading researchers around the world, he sets out what really helps protect memory, focus and cognitive function, and what is merely myth.

Gupta looks at diet, exercise, sleep, social connection and mental challenges, considers whether brain-training games are worth the effort, and learns from people who stay mentally sharp well into old age. Practical and reassuring, it suits anyone who wants to look after their mind for the long term.

  • Author: Sanjay Gupta
  • Publisher: Headline Home
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781472274236

title: Mensa Train Your Brain: Memory
author: Gareth Moore
description:
Mensa Train Your Brain: Memory is a puzzle book by Gareth Moore, produced with Mensa, containing 200 puzzles designed to exercise and strengthen your memory.

The puzzles offer an enjoyable way to challenge your recall and keep your mind active, making the book a good choice for puzzle fans and anyone who wants to give their brain a regular workout.

  • Author: Gareth Moore
  • In association with: Mensa
  • Publisher: Welbeck
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781802791907

title: Ariadne
author: Jennifer Saint
description:
Ariadne is Jennifer Saint's debut novel, a feminist retelling of Greek myth from the point of view of the Cretan princess. Raised alongside her sister Phaedra by their feared father, King Minos, Ariadne lives within earshot of the Minotaur, the half-brother hidden in the Labyrinth below the palace, who demands a blood sacrifice every year.

When the Athenian prince Theseus is sent to Crete as the beast's next victim, Ariadne falls for him, but helping him means betraying her family and her homeland. Lyrical and absorbing, it gives voice to the overlooked women of a famous legend and suits fans of mythological retellings.

  • Author: Jennifer Saint
  • Publisher: Wildfire
  • Format: Paperback, 388 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781472273901

title: Rice, Miso Soup, Pickles
author: Yoshiharu Doi
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Rice, Miso Soup, Pickles is a reflective book on Japanese food and culture by Yoshiharu Doi, one of Japan's most respected food writers, now translated into English for the first time. Rather than a conventional cookbook, it explores the philosophy behind traditional Japanese home cooking and what it reveals about Japan itself.

Doi celebrates a way of eating rooted in seasonality and simplicity, one that supports health and longevity and finds calm in preparing the same modest meal day after day. It suits lovers of Japanese culture, home cooks seeking a gentler approach to food and anyone drawn to mindful living.

  • Author: Yoshiharu Doi
  • Publisher: Hodder & Stoughton
  • Pages: 288
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781399741033

title: Blood & Roses Volume 1
author: Callie Hart
description:
Blood & Roses Volume 1 brings together the first three books of Callie Hart's dark romance series. Zeth Mayfair is one of the most feared men in Seattle, someone who carries out whatever dirty work he is sent to do, until his employer moves into the trade in kidnapped women.

Trauma doctor Sloane Romera is desperate to find her missing sister, but every route into the world of human trafficking is closed to her, until help arrives in the dangerous, unexpected form of Zeth. Intense and explicit, this omnibus is intended for adult readers who enjoy dark, morally grey romance.

  • Author: Callie Hart
  • Publisher: Hodder & Stoughton
  • Format: Paperback, 388 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Blood & Roses, Books 1-3
  • ISBN: 9781399754781

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
description:
The Power of Now is Eckhart Tolle's influential guide to spiritual enlightenment, built on the idea that freedom from suffering lies in living fully in the present moment. Tolle explains how identifying with the restless, thinking mind keeps people trapped in regrets about the past and anxieties about the future.

Through a series of questions and answers, he offers practical ways to quieten mental chatter, observe thoughts without being ruled by them and reach a deeper sense of peace. Clear and thought-provoking, it suits anyone exploring mindfulness, spirituality or a calmer way of living.

  • Author: Eckhart Tolle
  • Publisher: Yellow Kite
  • Format: Hardcover, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781399743303

title: A Man Called Ove
author: Fredrik Backman
description:
A Man Called Ove is Fredrik Backman's first novel, translated from the Swedish by Henning Koch. Ove is, at first glance, the grumpiest man you could hope to avoid: a stickler for rules who patrols his neighbourhood daily and has no patience for anyone who cannot reverse a trailer properly.

When a lively young family moves in next door and accidentally flattens his mailbox, Ove's carefully ordered life begins to change. Touching and very funny, it is a story about grief, friendship and community that shows how much a gruff exterior can hide, and suits book clubs and lovers of warm-hearted fiction.

  • Author: Fredrik Backman
  • Translator: Henning Koch
  • Publisher: Sceptre
  • Format: Paperback, 295 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781444775815

title: Throne of Nightmares
author: Kerri Maniscalco
description:
Throne of Nightmares is the third book in Kerri Maniscalco's Prince of Sin series, a standalone fantasy romance built around a hunt for a dangerous magical book. Prince Sloth prefers the comfort of his enchanted library, yet when a long-forgotten god endangers the Underworld, he has to track down the Book of Nightmares, a relic of ancient, world-breaking power, before it frees the Goddess of Night.

Marked by betrayal and running out of time, he crosses paths with a sunny librarian who carries the Phoenix Tear, a rare stone that can open portals. Packed with magic, peril and romance, it suits adult readers of steamy romantasy.

  • Author: Kerri Maniscalco
  • Publisher: Hodderscape
  • Format: Paperback, 469 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Prince of Sin, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781399715751

title: Mile High
author: Liz Tomforde
description:
Mile High is the first book in Liz Tomforde's Windy City series, an enemies-to-lovers sports romance set in the world of professional hockey. Evan Zanders is Chicago's most notorious defenceman, a player fans love to hate, who spends as much time in the penalty box as on the ice and rarely leaves the arena alone.

Stevie Shay, a seasoned flight attendant, lands a job on the team's private plane and finds herself serving the most arrogant star in the league. Told with Gladwell's trademark curiosity and storytelling flair, it suits readers who enjoy big ideas about psychology, society and human behaviour.

  • Author: Malcolm Gladwell
  • Publisher: Abacus
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780349147192

title: Heir
author: Sabaa Tahir
description:
Heir is the first book in Sabaa Tahir's Heir Duology, a young adult fantasy set in the world of the Martial Empire. Three very different young people find their fates bound together: Aiz, a fierce girl from the Kegari slums driven by old grief and love for her people; Sirsha, an exiled tracker who uses magic to find her targets; and Quil, a crown prince.

As a murderer who preys on children across the empire stays one step ahead, their paths collide in a story of vengeance, loyalty and unexpected attraction. Fast-paced and emotionally charged, it suits fans of Tahir's An Ember in the Ashes and readers who enjoy layered, multi-voice fantasy.

  • Author: Sabaa Tahir
  • Publisher: Atom
  • Format: Paperback, 484 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Heir Duology, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780349125589

title: Iron Flame
author: Rebecca Yarros
description:
Iron Flame is the second novel in Rebecca Yarros's Empyrean series, following Fourth Wing. Violet Sorrengail has survived a first year at Basgiath War College against all expectations, but the training ahead is even more punishing, built to push dragon riders far past their limits.

A ruthless new vice commandant is determined to prove how powerless Violet is, unless she turns against Xaden, the man she loves, while the truth about the war beyond the college walls grows harder to ignore. Packed with dragons, danger, romance and shocking turns, it is essential reading for anyone who devoured the first book.

  • Author: Rebecca Yarros
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Paperback, 786 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Empyrean, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780349437057

title: Counting Miracles
author: Nicholas Sparks
description:
Counting Miracles is a novel by Nicholas Sparks about family, belonging and second chances. Tanner has spent his life on the move, never settling anywhere, until his dying grandmother tells him the name and whereabouts of the father he has never met.

He heads to the small town of Asheboro, North Carolina, intending to make peace with the past and then move on, as he always has. What he finds there may change his plans. Warm and emotional, it is a fine choice for readers who love Sparks's heartfelt, small-town storytelling.

  • Author: Nicholas Sparks
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751585575

title: Love and Other Words
author: Christina Lauren
description:
Love and Other Words is a contemporary romance by Christina Lauren. Macy, a new paediatrics resident, has built a careful, tidy life, complete with a wedding planned to an older, steady fiancé, until a chance encounter brings her face to face with Elliot, her first and only real love.
