Told across two timelines, the novel moves between their teenage years, when a bookish friendship slowly became something more after Macy lost her mother, and the present, where old wounds must finally be faced. Tender and nostalgic, it is ideal for fans of friends-to-lovers and second-chance love stories.

  • Author: Christina Lauren
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Paperback, 420 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780349417561

title: Flawless
author: Elsie Silver
description:
Flawless is the first book in Elsie Silver's Chestnut Springs series, a contemporary cowboy romance. Rhett Eaton is the golden boy of professional bull riding, but after a scandal threatens his image, his agent assigns his own sharp-tongued daughter, Summer, to keep him in line until the season ends.

The rules are simple: stay out of trouble and keep his hands to himself. Yet with long days on the road and close quarters, the attraction between them proves hard to ignore. Funny, steamy and full of heart, it suits readers who love sparky banter and small-town Western settings.

  • Author: Elsie Silver
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Chestnut Springs, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780349437675

title: The Thief
author: J.R. Ward
description:
The Thief is the sixteenth novel in J.R. Ward's Black Dagger Brotherhood, the paranormal romance series about a band of vampire warriors. Now that the Band of Bastards are their allies, the Brothers are close to wiping out the Lessening Society, yet the war is far from finished.

Throe, once Xcor's second in command, has turned to an ancient book to raise a new army driven by a power even darker than the Omega, leaving the Brotherhood facing threats on the battlefield and under its own roof. A must for longtime fans of the series and its blend of romance, danger and dark fantasy.

  • Author: J.R. Ward
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Hardcover, 454 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Black Dagger Brotherhood, Book 16
  • ISBN: 9780349409214

title: The Gardens of Light
author: Amin Maalouf
description:
The Gardens of Light is a historical novel by Amin Maalouf, translated from the French Les Jardins de lumière. It tells the story of Mani, the third-century painter, physician and philosopher whose name survives in the words Manichaean and Manichaeism, even though the man himself is little remembered.

Maalouf follows Mani's life and his attempt to reconcile the faiths of his time through a tolerant, humane vision, a mission that brought him persecution and suffering. Rich in history and ideas, it suits readers who enjoy literary historical fiction set in the ancient Middle East and stories about faith and tolerance.

  • Author: Amin Maalouf
  • Publisher: Time Warner Books UK
  • Format: Paperback, 254 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780349108711

title: For One More Day
author: Mitch Albom
description:
For One More Day is a novel by Mitch Albom about a mother, a son and the chance to set things right. Charley Benetto has lost almost everything to drink and regret, and when he learns he will not be invited to his daughter's wedding, he sets off on what he intends to be his final journey.

Arriving in the small town where he grew up, he walks into his old house to find his mother, gone for eight years, waiting for him as though nothing had changed. What follows is one ordinary, extraordinary day together, full of family secrets, forgiveness and reconciliation. A short, moving read about the bond between parents and children.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 197 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751537505

title: Have A Little Faith
author: Mitch Albom
description:
Have a Little Faith is a true story by Mitch Albom, the first he had written since Tuesdays with Morrie. It began when the elderly rabbi of his childhood congregation asked Albom to deliver his eulogy, a request that drew him back towards a faith he had drifted away from.

At the same time, Albom came to know a Detroit pastor, a former drug dealer and prisoner, who ministered to homeless people from a crumbling church whose roof had a hole in it. Moving between these two men and their very different worlds, the book reflects on belief, community and what it means to live a good life. Warm and thoughtful, it speaks to readers of any faith or none.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 262 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751537512

title: The First Phone Call From Heaven
sheet_title: The First Phone Call From Heaven
author: Mitch Albom
description:
The First Phone Call from Heaven is a novel by Mitch Albom set in a small town on the shores of Lake Michigan, where several residents begin to receive phone calls from loved ones who have died.

As word spreads and the town is engulfed by attention, people argue over whether the calls are a miracle or an elaborate hoax. Sully Harding, a grieving single father, sets out to discover the truth. Part mystery and part meditation on belief, it is a touching, compelling story about faith, loss and hope.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 308 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751541199

title: The Five People You Meet In Heaven
sheet_title: The Five People You Meet In Heaven
author: Mitch Albom
description:
The Five People You Meet in Heaven is Mitch Albom's much-loved fable about the meaning of a single life. Eddie, a war veteran and amusement-park maintenance man, dies on his eighty-third birthday in an accident while trying to save a young girl.

He wakes in an afterlife that is no garden paradise but a place where five people from his life, some close and some strangers, each explain how their paths crossed his and what it meant. Gentle and profound, it is a short novel about connection, sacrifice and purpose, ideal for book clubs and reflective readers.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Time Warner Paperbacks
  • Format: Paperback, 231 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Five People You Meet in Heaven, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780751536829

title: The Magic Strings of Frankie Presto
sheet_title: The Magic Strings of Frankie Presto
author: Mitch Albom
description:
The Magic Strings of Frankie Presto, a sweeping novel by Mitch Albom, is narrated by Music itself. Frankie, orphaned by war in Spain and brought up by a music teacher who cannot see, is sent to America at nine years old with nothing but a guitar and six magical strings.

His extraordinary talent carries him through a century of changing sounds, from classical and jazz to rock and roll, crossing paths with legends such as Django Reinhardt, Elvis Presley and Hank Williams. Yet his gift weighs on him, because his strings can alter other people's futures. A bittersweet tale of love, music and fate.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 526 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751541212

title: The Next Person You Meet in Heaven
sheet_title: The Next Person You Meet in Heaven
author: Mitch Albom
description:
The Next Person You Meet in Heaven is Mitch Albom's sequel to The Five People You Meet in Heaven, telling the story of Annie, the little girl Eddie died saving at the amusement park.

The accident left Annie badly hurt and with no memory of its cause, and its shadow followed her into adulthood. Years later, her own journey leads her to heaven and a reunion with Eddie, as she discovers how her life was woven together with the lives of others. A touching companion to the original about love, loss and the ways our lives connect.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 210 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Five People You Meet in Heaven, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780751571905

title: The Time Keeper
author: Mitch Albom
description:
The Time Keeper is a fable by Mitch Albom about the man who invented the world's first clock. Punished for centuries for daring to measure time, he is finally released and given a chance at redemption: he must teach two people what time truly means.

Back on earth, he crosses paths with a teenage girl on the brink of giving up and a wealthy, elderly businessman desperate to live forever, and he can only save himself by saving them both. A short, thoughtful novel about how we spend our days and why every moment matters.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 238 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751541175

title: Tuesdays With Morrie
author: Mitch Albom
description:
Tuesdays with Morrie: An Old Man, a Young Man, and Life's Greatest Lesson is Mitch Albom's memoir of his final conversations with Morrie Schwartz, the college professor who had mentored him some twenty years before.

After learning that Morrie was dying of ALS, also known as motor neurone disease, Albom began visiting him every Tuesday, just as he had in his student days. Their talks became a last class on the things that matter most, among them love, work, family, ageing, forgiveness and death. Wise, tender and often funny, it is a timeless book for anyone thinking about how to live well.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Paperback, 203 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751569575

title: The Soulmate Equation
sheet_title: The Soulmate Equation the New York Times Bestselling rom com
author: Christina Lauren
description:
The Soulmate Equation is a romantic comedy by Christina Lauren. Jess is a whizz with numbers and a busy single mother who has all but given up on finding love, until she hears about a new matchmaking company that pairs people using their DNA.

Her results show an almost unheard-of match with Dr River Peña, the company's founder, a man she already knows and cannot stand. Persuaded to give the match a chance, she begins to wonder whether the science might be right after all. Witty and warm, it suits fans of opposites-attract romance.

  • Author: Christina Lauren
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Paperback, 355 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: DNA Duo, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780349426891

title: The Unhoneymooners
author: Christina Lauren
description:
The Unhoneymooners is a romantic comedy by Christina Lauren. Olive has always been unlucky, while her identical twin, Amy, seems to win at everything, even managing to pay for her entire wedding by entering online competitions.

When food poisoning sweeps through the wedding party, sparing only Olive and the groom's brother Ethan, her sworn enemy, the pair end up taking the free Hawaiian honeymoon together while pretending to be newlyweds. Sparky, funny and full of banter, it is a feel-good pick for fans of enemies-to-lovers and fake-relationship stories.

  • Author: Christina Lauren
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780349417592

title: Terms and Conditions
author: Lauren Asher
description:
Lauren Asher continues her Dreamland Billionaires series with Terms and Conditions, the follow-up to The Fine Print. Declan Kane is in line to run his family's media empire, but his grandfather's will requires him to marry and have an heir first, so his assistant, Iris, offers to become his wife.

Their arrangement comes with clear rules: move in, hold a wedding, have a baby and keep feelings out of it. Yet the more they play the loving couple in public, the harder it becomes to tell what is real. A grumpy-sunshine romance built on a marriage of convenience.

  • Author: Lauren Asher
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Paperback, 477 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Dreamland Billionaires, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780349433455

title: The Fine Print
author: Lauren Asher
description:
The Fine Print launches Lauren Asher's Dreamland Billionaires series. Rowan Kane, heir to a family empire of theme parks, studios and hotels, stands to inherit it all if he can successfully renovate the Dreamland park.

When Zahra sends in a tipsy proposal criticising the park's priciest ride, she expects to be fired; instead, Rowan offers her a dream job under the toughest boss she has ever had. Complicating things further, he has been messaging her under a false name. A grumpy-sunshine workplace romance with plenty of sparks.

  • Author: Lauren Asher
  • Publisher: Piatkus
  • Format: Paperback, 434 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Dreamland Billionaires, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780349433448

title: The Stranger in the Lifeboat
author: Mitch Albom
description:
The Stranger in the Lifeboat is a novel by Mitch Albom. After an explosion sinks their ship, ten survivors drift on a raft with dwindling food, water and hope, until on the third day they pull a man from the waves who quietly claims to be the Lord.

From there the story wonders what we would really do if God answered our cries for help in person. Suspenseful and thought-provoking, it is a compelling read for anyone who enjoys fiction that explores faith, doubt and the unexpected ways prayers may be answered.

  • Author: Mitch Albom
  • Publisher: Sphere
  • Format: Hardcover, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780751584530

title: Breaking Dawn
author: Stephenie Meyer
description:
Breaking Dawn is the fourth and final novel in Stephenie Meyer's Twilight Saga. Bella Swan has made her choice, and her marriage to the vampire Edward Cullen sets in motion consequences no one could have foreseen.

Told partly from Jacob Black's perspective, the story follows an unexpected pregnancy, a dramatic transformation and a looming confrontation with the powerful Volturi that threatens everyone Bella loves. The epic conclusion to the saga, it brings the love story of Bella, Edward and Jacob to a close.

  • Author: Stephenie Meyer
  • Publisher: Atom
  • Format: Paperback, 702 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Twilight Saga, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9781907410352

title: Eclipse
author: Stephenie Meyer
description:
Eclipse is the third novel in Stephenie Meyer's Twilight Saga. As a series of mysterious killings shakes Seattle and the vengeful vampire Victoria continues to hunt her, Bella Swan finds herself in danger once more.

At the same time, she must choose between her love for Edward Cullen and her deep friendship with the werewolf Jacob Black, knowing that her decision could reignite the old feud between vampires and wolves. Romantic and suspenseful, it raises the stakes as the saga heads towards its finale.

  • Author: Stephenie Meyer
  • Publisher: Atom
  • Format: Paperback, 628 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Twilight Saga, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781904233916

title: Remain
author: Nicholas Sparks and M. Night Shyamalan
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Remain is a novel co-written by Nicholas Sparks and filmmaker M. Night Shyamalan, blending a love story with supernatural mystery. Tate Donovan, a New York architect grieving the death of his sister, travels to Cape Cod to design a summer house for his best friend.

Before she died, his sister told him she could see spirits still bound to the living, a gift she said ran in their family, and Tate, who trusts only logic, struggles to accept it. Then, while staying at an old bed-and-breakfast on the Cape, he meets a young woman named Wren who unsettles everything he believes. A haunting mix of romance, grief and the unexplained.

  • Authors: Nicholas Sparks and M. Night Shyamalan
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781408724859

title: The 169-Storey Treehouse
author: Andy Griffiths and Terry Denton
description:
The 169-Storey Treehouse is the thirteenth book in the Treehouse series from Andy Griffiths and Terry Denton, the illustrated comic adventures of Andy and Terry, who live in an ever-growing treehouse.

This time the friends have added thirteen new levels, though they are still under construction. Packed with cartoons, silly jokes and over-the-top adventure, it is a fun pick for young readers who enjoy funny, highly illustrated stories, and a natural next step after The 156-Storey Treehouse.

  • Authors: Andy Griffiths and Terry Denton
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • Series: Treehouse, Book 13
  • ISBN: 9781529097160

title: Conform
author: Ariel Sullivan
description:
Conform is the opening novel in Ariel Sullivan's dystopian romance trilogy. Hundreds of years after a devastating world war, humanity survives in a single city ruled by the Illum, a secretive and technologically advanced elite who keep their citizens under constant watch.

Twenty-seven-year-old Emeline spends her days sorting ancient art for destruction while waiting to be chosen as a Mate in a procreation contract, hiding how little she fits in a society that values people for their genes and health. Soon she finds her heart divided between two men, and her loyalty tested by a rebellion stirring beneath the surface.

  • Author: Ariel Sullivan
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 480 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Conform, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781035072262

title: The Fallen and the Kiss of Dusk
sheet_title: The Fallen and the Kiss of Dusk
author: Carissa Broadbent
description:
The Fallen and the Kiss of Dusk is the fourth book in Carissa Broadbent's Crowns of Nyaxia series and the second half of the duet that began with The Songbird and the Heart of Stone. Mische's great sacrifice saved the people she loves but cast the world into endless night, and Asar, held captive by the gods, wants only vengeance and to find her.

Offered one last chance at redemption by a goddess, the two set out to take the death god's power so that Asar can become truly divine. Their quest spans mortal and immortal realms as the underworld nears collapse and war among the gods looms. An epic, emotional romantasy finale.

  • Author: Carissa Broadbent
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 576 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Crowns of Nyaxia, Book 4 (The Shadowborn Duet, Book 2)
  • ISBN: 9781035051656

title: The Songbird & the Heart of Stone
sheet_title: The Songbird & the Heart of Stone
author: Carissa Broadbent
description:
The Songbird and the Heart of Stone is the third book in Carissa Broadbent's Crowns of Nyaxia series and opens a two-book story. Mische was once devoted to the sun god, but being forcibly Turned into a vampire cost her her home, her mortal life and the sun god's love.

Now condemned to die for slaying the prince who made her a vampire, she is offered an unexpected path that leads down into the underworld, where she must choose between redemption and a forbidden love that sets her against the gods. Dark, lush and romantic, it suits fans of epic fantasy romance with mythic stakes.

  • Author: Carissa Broadbent
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 517 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Crowns of Nyaxia, Book 3 (The Shadowborn Duet, Book 1)
  • ISBN: 9781035050734

title: A Steeping of Blood
author: Hafsah Faizal
description:
A Steeping of Blood is the second and concluding book in Hafsah Faizal's Blood and Tea duology, following A Tempest of Tea. In the city of White Roaring, vampires are under threat, the press has been wiped out and the public is demanding justice.

There is no time for Arthie Casimir to grieve, or to dwell on newfound feelings, as she pulls her scattered crew back together for one last fight. To win it, she must return to where her story began, in Ceylan, and confront the ghosts of her past. A twisty, atmospheric finale full of vampires, schemes and secrets.

  • Author: Hafsah Faizal
  • Publisher: First Ink
  • Format: Paperback, 448 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Blood and Tea, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781529098921

title: A Tempest of Tea
author: Hafsah Faizal
description:
A Tempest of Tea is the first book in Hafsah Faizal's Blood and Tea duology, a young adult fantasy full of vampires, secrets and romance. Arthie Casimir, a criminal mastermind of White Roaring, deals in secrets and runs an elegant tearoom by day.

After dark, her establishment becomes an illicit bloodhouse serving the city's feared vampires. When it comes under threat, Arthie must strike an unlikely bargain with an alluring stranger and gather a crew of misfits for a daring heist. A great match for readers who loved Six of Crows and found-family adventures.

  • Author: Hafsah Faizal
  • Publisher: First Ink
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Blood and Tea, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781529098938

title: The Sleepless
author: Jen Williams
description:
The Sleepless is a gods-and-monsters romantic fantasy by Jen Williams, the opening book of a duology. Elver guards a wild and deadly monster forest; saved from death by a god, she now carries a poison in her skin that harms anyone she touches.

Then she meets Artair, the one person her touch cannot hurt, because he is one of the Sleepless, doomed to host a malevolent spirit in his own body. That spirit, Lucian, takes over whenever Artair sleeps and has plans of his own for Elver. Dark, romantic and inventive, it suits readers who enjoy monster-filled worlds and dangerous attraction.

  • Author: Jen Williams
  • Publisher: First Ink
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Sleepless Duology, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781035058037

title: Sisters in Yellow
author: Mieko Kawakami
description:
Sisters in Yellow is a novel by Mieko Kawakami, translated from the Japanese by Laurel Taylor and Hitomi Yoshio. Hana, who grew up without a father and is tired of being pitied, is drawn to Kimiko, an older woman with a youthful, glamorous energy who chats freely about boys, school and dreams of a better life.

Joined by two other young women who have had their own share of hardship, they set out to rebuild their futures by opening a bar called Lemon, battling loan sharks, organised crime and plain bad luck along the way. A gripping portrait of female friendship, money and survival on the margins of Tokyo nightlife.

  • Author: Mieko Kawakami
  • Translators: Laurel Taylor and Hitomi Yoshio
  • Publisher: Picador
  • Format: Paperback, 430 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035024148

title: The Art of Spending Money
author: Morgan Housel
description:
The Art of Spending Money: Simple Choices for a Richer Life is the third book from Morgan Housel, the writer behind The Psychology of Money and Same as Ever. This time he turns from saving and investing to the other side of the coin: how to use money in ways that genuinely make life better.

Rather than offering one-size-fits-all rules, Housel explores the psychology behind our spending, why some purchases bring lasting satisfaction while others fall flat, and how to align money with what we truly value. Clear, thoughtful and full of stories, it suits anyone who wants a healthier, happier relationship with their finances.

  • Author: Morgan Housel
  • Publisher: Harriman House
  • Format: Paperback, 254 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804091890

title: The Eyes of Gaza
author: Plestia Alaqad
description:
The Eyes of Gaza: A Diary of Resilience is a first-hand account by Palestinian journalist Plestia Alaqad, who was 22 when she recorded the opening 45 days of the war on Gaza that began in 2023.

Written as a series of diary entries, echoing her own journal and the social media posts that reached audiences around the world, the book records the horror of life under bombardment alongside the courage, warmth and humanity of the people around her. A powerful, personal testimony for readers seeking to understand Gaza through the voices of those who lived it.

  • Author: Plestia Alaqad
  • Publisher: Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 170 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035070268

title: This is For Everyone
author: Tim Berners-Lee
description:
This Is for Everyone: The Unfinished Story of the World Wide Web is the memoir of Sir Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the web, who chose to give his creation to the world without seeking commercial reward.

He describes how the web came to be and how it opened up new forms of creativity and collaboration, before a commercial race reshaped it in ways that now strain democracy and polarise public debate. Optimistic, technically insightful and wryly funny, it is a timely read for anyone curious about the technology that shapes daily life and where it should go next.

  • Author: Tim Berners-Lee
  • Publisher: Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035023684

title: The Psychology of Wealth
author: Napoleon Hill
description:
The Psychology of Wealth brings together core teachings of Napoleon Hill, author of Think and Grow Rich and one of the pioneers of personal success writing. The volume combines two of his works, The Master Key to Riches and The Magic Ladder to Success, with three further essays.

Together they form a practical guide to building wealth and achieving lasting success, centred on Hill's belief in the power of mindset, purpose and personal initiative. A useful one-volume introduction for readers interested in classic self-improvement thinking and the habits behind prosperity.

  • Author: Napoleon Hill
  • Publisher: Macmillan Business
  • Format: Paperback, 512 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035059744

title: The (True!) History Of Art
author: Sylvain Coissard
description:
The (True!) History of Art by Sylvain Coissard, illustrated by Alexis Lemoine, is a playful, tongue-in-cheek look at the hidden stories behind some of the world's best-known paintings, from Monet and Rembrandt to Munch, Van Gogh and Cézanne.

Through a series of comic parodies, it offers outrageous answers to questions art lovers never thought to ask, such as what made Munch's figure scream or why Van Gogh's bedroom looks so neat. A witty, compact hardback gift for anyone who enjoys art history with a sense of humour.

  • Author: Sylvain Coissard
  • Illustrator: Alexis Lemoine
  • Publisher: SelfMadeHero
  • Format: Hardcover, 48 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781906838713

title: The Secret Language of Work
author: Erin McGoff
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
The Secret Language of Work: Hyper-Helpful Scripts for Every Situation is a practical career guide by Erin McGoff, the creator of AdviceWithErin. It focuses on the words that make a difference at work, offering ready-to-adapt scripts for the moments that so often leave people tongue-tied.

McGoff covers job interviews, salary negotiations, setting boundaries with colleagues, speaking up for yourself and handling awkward office situations, helping readers decode the unwritten rules of professional communication. Clear and confidence-building, it is especially useful for early-career professionals and anyone who wants to say the right thing at work.

  • Author: Erin McGoff
  • Publisher: Penguin Random House
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241802557

title: Memory Games For Clever Kids
author: Gareth Moore
description:
Memory Games for Clever Kids by Gareth Moore, illustrated by Chris Dickason, is an activity book packed with more than 70 puzzles designed to give young memories a workout. It belongs to the Clever Kids range of brain-training books from Buster Books.

Inside are pairs to match, differences to spot, number codes to crack and picture puzzles to solve, keeping children busy while sharpening concentration and recall. A fun choice for car journeys, quiet afternoons or any child who loves puzzles.

  • Author: Gareth Moore
  • Illustrator: Chris Dickason
  • Publisher: Buster Books
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781780558721

title: 10-Minute Brain Games For Clever Kids
author: Gareth Moore
description:
10-Minute Brain Games for Clever Kids by Gareth Moore is a puzzle book of 90 quick, timed challenges, each designed to be completed in around ten minutes.

The mix includes memory tests using words, shapes and numbers, simple sums, word squares, jumbled sentences, verbal reasoning, Sudoku and Kakuro, working on language, attention, memory and reasoning. Tackling one puzzle a day makes it easy to build a regular brain-training habit, and it is a great pick for curious young puzzlers.

  • Author: Gareth Moore
  • Publisher: Buster Books
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781780555935

title: Baron Wenckheim’s Homecoming
author: László Krasznahorkai
description:
Baron Wenckheim's Homecoming is a novel by László Krasznahorkai, the 2025 Nobel laureate in Literature, in an English translation by Ottilie Mulzet. The book completes a four-part cycle of novels and took the US National Book Award in the translated literature category in 2019.

Baron Béla Wenckheim, a gentle, Prince Myshkin-like figure fleeing gambling debts in Buenos Aires, comes back, near the end of his life, to his small Hungarian hometown, hoping to find Marika, the girl he loved in his school days. His arrival unleashes a whirl of gossip, swindlers and local politics, rendered in Krasznahorkai's famously long, hypnotic sentences. Darkly comic and apocalyptic, it is a major work of contemporary European fiction.

  • Author: László Krasznahorkai
  • Translator: Ottilie Mulzet
  • Publisher: New Directions
  • Format: Paperback, 576 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780811239707

title: I Found Myself - Last Dreams
author: Naguib Mahfouz
description:
I Found Myself: Last Dreams gathers the final dream pieces written by the Egyptian Nobel laureate Naguib Mahfouz in his last years, now available in English in a translation by the novelist Hisham Matar.

These brief, poetic vignettes blend the strangeness of night-time dreams with the storytelling craft that defined Mahfouz's long career, often returning to familiar places and faces from his past. They are accompanied by atmospheric, dreamlike photographs by Diana Matar. A beautiful, contemplative book for admirers of Mahfouz and of short, luminous prose.

  • Author: Naguib Mahfouz
  • Translator: Hisham Matar
  • Photographs: Diana Matar
  • Publisher: New Directions
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780811231022

title: Herscht 07769
author: László Krasznahorkai
description:
Herscht 07769 is a novel by László Krasznahorkai, translated from the Hungarian by Ottilie Mulzet. Florian Herscht, a gentle giant living in a small town in Thuringia, eastern Germany, becomes convinced after attending adult-education physics classes that the destruction of all matter is close at hand.

He writes letter after letter to Chancellor Angela Merkel to warn her, while working as a graffiti cleaner for the Boss, a Bach-obsessed neo-Nazi leader hunting whoever keeps defacing the region's Bach monuments with wolf symbols. Told in one long, rolling sentence, it is a dark, absurd and urgent portrait of contemporary Germany.

  • Author: László Krasznahorkai
  • Translator: Ottilie Mulzet
  • Publisher: New Directions
  • Format: Paperback, 406 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780811231534

title: Satantango
author: László Krasznahorkai
description:
Satantango is the debut novel of László Krasznahorkai, the Hungarian winner of the 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature, in an English translation by George Szirtes. It is also well known as the basis for Béla Tarr's acclaimed film adaptation.

Over a few days of relentless rain, the dozen remaining residents of an isolated, decaying settlement scheme betray one another and dream of escape, until the return of a charismatic figure they believed dead upends everything. Bleak, mesmerising and darkly funny, it is a landmark of modern European fiction.

  • Author: László Krasznahorkai
  • Translator: George Szirtes
  • Publisher: New Directions
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780811220897

title: The Melancholy of Resistance
author: László Krasznahorkai
description:
The Melancholy of Resistance is a novel by László Krasznahorkai, translated from the Hungarian by George Szirtes. In the depths of winter, a strange circus arrives in a small Hungarian town, advertising a giant stuffed whale as its main attraction.

Rumours spread that the circus has sinister intentions, and as fear grips the town its inhabitants grasp at any promise of order. At the centre is Valuska, a dreamy, gentle young man, alongside the scheming Mrs Eszter and her withdrawn husband. Surreal and unsettling, it was later adapted by Béla Tarr as the film Werckmeister Harmonies.

  • Author: László Krasznahorkai
  • Translator: George Szirtes
  • Publisher: New Directions
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780811215046

title: The Untethered Soul
author: Michael A. Singer
description:
The Untethered Soul: The Journey Beyond Yourself by Michael A. Singer is an accessible guide to consciousness and inner freedom. Singer invites readers to notice the constant voice in their heads and to recognise that they are the awareness observing their thoughts and emotions, not the thoughts themselves.

Drawing on meditation and contemplative traditions, he explains how to let go of habitual tension, fear and painful patterns so that energy and openness can flow freely. Clear and practical, it suits anyone seeking more peace, presence and freedom in everyday life, whatever their spiritual background.

  • Author: Michael A. Singer
  • Publisher: New Harbinger Publications
  • Format: Paperback, 200 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781572245372

title: British Museum: Talk Like an Egyptian
sheet_title: British Museum: Talk Like an Egyptian
author: Tegen Evans
description:
Talk Like an Egyptian is an illustrated children's book published by Nosy Crow in association with the British Museum, written by Tegen Evans with illustrations by Nina Chakrabarti.

As its title suggests, the book takes young readers back to ancient Egypt, making it a natural pick for children curious about the ancient world and the British Museum's collections.

  • Author: Tegen Evans
  • Illustrator: Nina Chakrabarti
  • Publisher: Nosy Crow
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781805130093

title: The World Atlas of Coffee 3rd edition
sheet_title: The World Atlas of Coffee 3rd edition
author: James Hoffmann
description:
The World Atlas of Coffee, now in its third edition, is James Hoffmann's illustrated guide to coffee from bean to cup. Hoffmann, who won the World Barista Championship and co-founded London's Square Mile Coffee Roasters, explains how coffee is grown, harvested, processed and roasted before it reaches your brewer.

A country-by-country tour of the world's coffee-producing regions explores how origin shapes flavour, while practical sections cover brewing methods and tasting. Richly photographed and clearly written, it suits curious home brewers, coffee professionals and anyone who wants to understand what is in their cup.

  • Author: James Hoffmann
  • Publisher: Mitchell Beazley
  • Format: Hardcover, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781784729868

title: Persiana Easy
author: Sabrina Ghayour
description:
Persiana Easy is a cookbook by Sabrina Ghayour, offering a fresh collection of Middle Eastern-inspired recipes designed to be as simple as possible to make at home.

Ghayour pairs bold, fragrant flavours with straightforward methods, covering everything from weeknight dinners and one-tray bakes to pastries and desserts. Ideal for busy home cooks who want vibrant, crowd-pleasing food for family and friends without fuss, and a natural next step for fans of her earlier Persiana books.

  • Author: Sabrina Ghayour
  • Publisher: Mitchell Beazley
  • Format: Hardcover, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781783256129

title: Matcha: A Cookbook
author: Hamlyn
description:
Matcha: A Cookbook from Hamlyn is a compact hardback devoted to the powdered Japanese green tea that has travelled from centuries-old tea ceremonies into kitchens and cafés around the world. It explains where matcha comes from, why it is prized for its antioxidants and nutritional value, and how to bring its vivid colour and grassy flavour into everyday cooking.

Forty recipes are arranged across breakfasts; soups, sides and snacks; main dishes; and sweets and drinks, running from a classic latte to tea loaves, smoothie bowls, ice cream and even an infused salt, with a few homemade beauty ideas too. It suits curious home cooks, wellness fans and anyone looking for a giftable little kitchen book.

  • Publisher: Hamlyn
  • Format: Hardcover, 80 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780600640103

title: Turmeric: A Cookbook
author: Hamlyn
description:
Turmeric: A Cookbook is a small Hamlyn hardback celebrating the golden spice that has long been valued in traditional Chinese and Indian medicine and is now widely regarded as a natural anti-inflammatory. It introduces the health benefits linked to turmeric and explains why cooking it, or pairing it with ginger and black pepper, helps it work harder.

The 40 recipes span breakfast, lunch, dinner and the moments in between, using both the fresh root and the ground powder. Expect ideas for juices, smoothies and infusions alongside soups, curries, roasted vegetables, hummus and marinades. A handy pick for health-minded cooks who want to use this superfood more often.

  • Publisher: Hamlyn
  • Format: Hardcover, 80 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780600640080

title: Joyspan
author: Kerry Burnight
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Joyspan: The Art and Science of Thriving in Life's Second Half is a practical guide to growing older well from gerontologist Dr Kerry Burnight, whose large online following calls her simply 'Dr Kerry'. Pushing back against fearful, anti-ageing messages, she argues that a good long life should be measured by its quality rather than by its length alone.

Drawing on her professional experience and on lessons from her 95-year-old mother, Betty, Burnight shares the ideas and tools she uses to help people swap worry about later life for calm confidence. It will suit readers planning their own second half as well as those supporting ageing parents.

  • Author: Kerry Burnight
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781783256341

title: Calm for Every Day
author: Summersdale
description:
Calm for Every Day: Simple Tips and Inspiring Quotes to Help You Find Peace is a pocket-sized hardback from Summersdale designed to help you handle stress and anxiety with a little more ease. Rather than promising a life free of worry, it treats those feelings as a normal part of being human and focuses on how you respond to them.

Short, practical tips sit alongside a collection of soothing quotations. Topics include noticing how stress shows up in the body, simple mindfulness exercises, ways to steady yourself when anxiety strikes and gentle self-care ideas. It makes an easy dip-in companion for busy days and a thoughtful small gift.

  • Publisher: Summersdale
  • Format: Hardcover, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800071827

title: Little Box of Mindful Meditations
attention: Identified from its cover photo (checked by eye); description is brief — add details from the copy
description:
Little Box of Mindful Meditations is, as its title suggests, a small boxed collection of meditations centred on mindfulness.

Its compact format makes it easy to keep close at hand at home or at work, and it would suit anyone beginning a mindfulness practice as well as those looking for a gentle, thoughtful gift.

  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800074064

title: Little Box of Self-Care
author: Summersdale
attention: No photo found — photograph in store
description:
Little Box of Self-Care is a boxed deck of 52 cards from Summersdale, put together to help you look after your mind, body and soul.

Designed to be kept within easy reach, the cards can be drawn one at a time whenever you need a moment of encouragement, and the box makes a thoughtful gift for a friend who could use some gentle looking after.

  • Publisher: Summersdale
  • Format: Boxed card set, 52 cards
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800071797

title: You Are So Awesome: 52 Amazing Cards of Uplifting Quotes and Inspiring Affirmations
sheet_title: You Are So Awesome 52 Cards Of Uplifting Quotes A
author: Summersdale
description:
You Are So Awesome: 52 Amazing Cards of Uplifting Quotes and Inspiring Affirmations is a boxed card set from Summersdale filled with encouraging words. Each of the 52 cards carries either an uplifting quotation or a positive affirmation intended to lift your mood and boost your self-belief.

Pick one each morning, keep a favourite on your desk or pass them on to someone who needs reminding how wonderful they are. A cheerful, simple gift for friends, colleagues and anyone going through a tough patch.

  • Publisher: Summersdale
  • Format: Boxed card set, 52 cards
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781800071643

title: Murder in the Name of Honor
sheet_title: Murder in the Name of Honor
author: Rana Husseini
description:
Murder in the Name of Honor is Jordanian journalist Rana Husseini's searching investigation into so-called honour crimes, in which a woman is killed or maimed by a relative who believes she has shamed the family. The book shows that these acts occur in many traditional societies and also among immigrant families in Europe and the US.

Husseini has spent years reporting on these killings and campaigning to break the silence that surrounds them, and her account looks both at the victims themselves and at the attitudes and legal leniency that allow such crimes to continue. Powerful and often difficult reading, it suits anyone interested in human rights, women's rights and the Middle East.

  • Author: Rana Husseini
  • Publisher: Oneworld Publications
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781851685240

title: Gaza in My Phone
author: Mazen Kerbaj
description:
Gaza in My Phone collects the drawings that Lebanese comics artist Mazen Kerbaj began making just two days after 7 October 2023, as images of the war on Gaza poured onto his phone screen. Working from Berlin, he drew to bear witness, to raise awareness and simply to keep his footing amid the horror.

The art is stark, high-contrast black and white, paired with sharp captions and slogans, and much of it has travelled widely online as an expression of solidarity with Palestine. The book also asks what it means to look, and to keep looking, when those in power would rather we did not. A vital record for readers of political comics and graphic journalism.

  • Author: Mazen Kerbaj
  • Publisher: OR Books
  • Format: Paperback, 144 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781682196434

title: The Hypocrite
author: Jo Hamya
description:
The Hypocrite is a sharp literary novel by Jo Hamya about a daughter, her father and the stories each tells about the other. In the summer of 2020, a 61-year-old novelist takes his seat in a packed London theatre to watch his daughter Sophia's first play, only to discover that it is about the holiday they shared in Sicily ten years earlier.

Moving between that tense evening and the hot Aeolian summer of 2010, when Sophia experienced her first love while typing up the novel her father dictated to her, the book examines generational resentment, gender and the question of who gets to judge whom. A compact, provocative choice for book clubs and fans of contemporary literary fiction.

  • Author: Jo Hamya
  • Publisher: Orion Publishing Group
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781399613248

title: The Convenience Store by the Sea (Winter Cover)
sheet_title: The Convenience Store by the Sea (Winter Cover)
author: Sonoko Machida
description:
The Convenience Store by the Sea is a warm, gently quirky Japanese novel by Sonoko Machida, translated into English by Bruno Navasky, offered here in its special winter-cover edition. The story is set in Mojiko, a seaside corner of Kitakyushu, where a round-the-clock convenience store called Tenderness has quietly become the heart of the neighbourhood.

Its handsome manager has a devoted fan club, the regulars are a delightfully eccentric bunch, and the shelves offer everything from hot coffee and parfaits to egg sandos and fried chicken. Told through linked stories, it celebrates kindness, connection and community, and will appeal to readers who love cosy, comforting Japanese fiction.

  • Author: Sonoko Machida
  • Translator: Bruno Navasky
  • Publisher: Orion Publishing Group
  • Pages: 288
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Convenience Store by the Sea, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781398728417

title: Finding My Way
author: Malala Yousafzai
description:
Finding My Way is Malala Yousafzai's candid memoir about the years after the attack that made her famous. Shot by the Taliban at fifteen and suddenly cast as a global symbol of courage, she found that life away from the cameras was far harder to navigate than anyone imagined.

Here she writes with humour and tenderness about friendship, first love, anxiety and working out who she really is, tracing her journey from lonely schoolgirl to reckless university student to a young adult who has made peace with her history. Expect nearly failed exams, being ghosted and meeting her husband, all told with refreshing honesty. A warm, relatable read for anyone who has struggled with other people's expectations.

  • Author: Malala Yousafzai
  • Publisher: Hachette Australia
  • Format: Paperback, 305 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781399619356

title: Alchemy of Secrets
author: Stephanie Garber
description:
Alchemy of Secrets is a romantic fantasy by Stephanie Garber, author of Caraval, set in the hidden magical underbelly of modern Los Angeles. Holland St. James has always believed that magic is real, and a folklore class held in an old cinema, taught by a mysterious woman known only as the Professor, seems to prove her right.

When Holland tracks down the Watch Man, a local legend said to know the hour of your death, he predicts she will die at midnight the following night unless she can locate an ancient artefact called the Alchemical Heart. Racing the clock beside an alluring stranger who claims her sister sent him, she discovers that everyone around her is hiding something. Twisty and atmospheric, it opens a new series.

  • Author: Stephanie Garber
  • Publisher: Gollancz
  • Format: Trade Paperback, 324 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Alchemy of Secrets, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781399631334

title: Oathbringer Part One
author: Brandon Sanderson
description:
Oathbringer Part One is the first half of the third book in Brandon Sanderson's epic fantasy series The Stormlight Archive, published as two volumes in this UK paperback edition. On the storm-battered world of Roshar, humanity faces a new Desolation as the Voidbringers return and the destructive Everstorm sweeps across the land.

Dalinar Kholin's armies have paid dearly for their victory, Kaladin races to warn his family while wrestling with the justice of the parshmen's anger, and Shallan explores the ancient tower city of Urithiru, once home to the Knights Radiant. Vast in scope and rich in worldbuilding, it continues directly into Oathbringer Part Two and is best read after Words of Radiance.

  • Author: Brandon Sanderson
  • Publisher: Gollancz
  • Format: Paperback, 635 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Stormlight Archive, Book 3 (Part 1)
  • ISBN: 9780575093362

title: Oathbringer Part Two
author: Brandon Sanderson
description:
Oathbringer Part Two completes the third instalment of Brandon Sanderson's The Stormlight Archive, picking up directly from Oathbringer Part One in this two-volume UK paperback edition. The Everstorm has woken the parshmen to the injustice of their long enslavement, and the Voidbringers are gathering strength across Roshar.

As Dalinar strives to unite the nations against the coming Desolation, Kaladin and Shallan confront hard truths about loyalty, identity and the hidden history of the Knights Radiant. Packed with large-scale battles, intricate magic and character-driven drama, it brings the book to a powerful close and sets the stage for Rhythm of War.

  • Author: Brandon Sanderson
  • Publisher: Gollancz
  • Format: Paperback, 756 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Stormlight Archive, Book 3 (Part 2)
  • ISBN: 9780575093379

title: The Way of Kings Part One
sheet_title: The Way of Kings Part One
author: Brandon Sanderson
description:
The Way of Kings Part One is the first half of the opening novel in Brandon Sanderson's The Stormlight Archive, presented as a separate volume in this UK paperback edition. It introduces Roshar, a world of rock and relentless highstorms so powerful that plants, animals and whole cities have adapted simply to survive them.

Centuries after the fall of the Knights Radiant, their Shardblades and Shardplate still turn ordinary fighters into near-unstoppable warriors, and kingdoms are traded to possess them. Against this backdrop, the lives of a soldier, a highprince and a young scholar begin to intertwine. Ambitious and immersive, it is an ideal starting point for fans of epic fantasy.

  • Author: Brandon Sanderson
  • Publisher: Gollancz
  • Format: Paperback, 594 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Stormlight Archive, Book 1 (Part 1)
  • ISBN: 9780575097360

title: Glass Sword
author: Victoria Aveyard
description:
Glass Sword is the second book in Victoria Aveyard's young adult fantasy series Red Queen. Mare Barrow's blood is Red, the colour of the common people, yet she wields a Silver ability, control over lightning, that makes her a weapon both sides want to command.

Hunted by the vengeful Silver king, Mare goes searching for other Red-and-Silver newbloods to recruit to the rebellion. But every victory costs lives, and she fears she is turning into the very kind of monster she has sworn to destroy. A tense, twisty instalment full of betrayal, divided loyalties and slow-burning romance.

  • Author: Victoria Aveyard
  • Publisher: Orion Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 444 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Red Queen, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781409150749

title: Red Queen
author: Victoria Aveyard
description:
Red Queen is the opening novel in Victoria Aveyard's young adult fantasy series of the same name, set in a world split by the colour of its people's blood. Red-blooded commoners serve a Silver elite who possess extraordinary, almost godlike powers.

Seventeen-year-old Mare Barrow, a Red from the impoverished Stilts, finds work in the Silver Palace and, to everyone's shock, reveals a lethal ability of her own. To hide the anomaly, the Silvers pass her off as a lost Silver princess betrothed to a prince, while Mare secretly aids the rebel Red Guard. Full of palace intrigue, betrayal and a dangerous love triangle.

  • Author: Victoria Aveyard
  • Publisher: Orion
  • Format: Paperback, 383 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Red Queen, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781409150725

title: War Storm
author: Victoria Aveyard
description:
War Storm is the fourth and final novel in Victoria Aveyard's Red Queen series. Still bruised by Cal's betrayal, Mare Barrow is determined to guard her heart and win freedom for Reds and newbloods alike by bringing down the kingdom of Norta and its young king, Maven.

To defeat the boy who nearly broke her, Mare must ally with the one who did break her heart, joining Cal's Silver allies with the Scarlet Guard. Yet Maven's obsession with her drives him to destroy anything in his way. An epic conclusion full of battles, shifting alliances and hard choices about power and love.

  • Author: Victoria Aveyard
  • Publisher: Orion Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 662 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Red Queen, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9781409175995

title: Hivemind: The New Science of Tribalism in Our Divided World
sheet_title: Hivemind: The New Science of Tribalism in Our Divided World
author: Sarah Rose Cavanagh
description:
Hivemind: The New Science of Tribalism in Our Divided World is psychologist Sarah Rose Cavanagh's exploration of how groups come to think, feel and believe as one. She looks at the hive mind, the shared consciousness that forms when communities align around common ideas, and asks how it is shaping today's polarised politics and culture.

People have always defined themselves through their tribes, whether built on faith, heritage or simple shared tastes. Cavanagh examines what happens when those groups only echo our own views back to us, and what it might take to reconnect across the divides. Thought-provoking reading for anyone curious about psychology, society and polarisation.

  • Author: Sarah Rose Cavanagh
  • Publisher: Orion Publishing Group
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781409194323

title: Rule of Wolves
author: Leigh Bardugo
description:
Rule of Wolves is the second and concluding book in Leigh Bardugo's King of Scars duology, set in the Grishaverse. As Fjerda's vast army readies itself to invade Ravka, the young king Nikolai Lantsov must draw on all his wit and charm, and on the demon that lives inside him, to save his country.

Meanwhile, General Zoya Nazyalensky must embrace her full power as a Stormwitch, and spy Nina Zenik risks everything working undercover in Fjerda. Told from multiple viewpoints, it brims with war, politics, magic and romance, and is best enjoyed after King of Scars and the Shadow and Bone and Six of Crows books.

  • Author: Leigh Bardugo
  • Publisher: Orion Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 592 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: King of Scars, Book 2 (Grishaverse)
  • ISBN: 9781510109186

title: Finale
author: Stephanie Garber
description:
Finale is the concluding instalment of Stephanie Garber's Caraval trilogy, a lush young adult fantasy of magic, games and romance. Two months after the last Caraval, the Fates have escaped their enchanted cards, Legend has claimed the empire's throne, and Tella is set on stopping his coronation.

Tella is convinced that her mother, who remains under a spell of enchanted sleep, should rightfully rule, while Scarlett launches a game of her own, challenging Julian and Count Nicolas d'Arcy, the man she was once engaged to, to compete for her hand. With both sisters fighting to protect the people they love, the trilogy reaches a dramatic, emotional ending. Read after Caraval and Legendary.

  • Author: Stephanie Garber
  • Publisher: Hachette
  • Format: Paperback, 480 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Caraval, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9781399633833

title: The Philosophy of Dumbness
author: Joseph Choma
description:
The Philosophy of Dumbness, by Joseph Choma, is a playful yet rigorous book about contemporary architecture that approaches big ideas through the unexpected lens of dumbness. It asks what we really mean by technology and how we ought to define intelligence in design.

Examples from the history of science, art and architecture show how seemingly simple approaches can point the way to smarter practice. More than fifty contributors, including Jürgen Mayer H., Carl Lostritto and Catie Newell, each respond to one question: what is the dumbest, yet smartest, thing they have done. The result is a lively snapshot of architectural culture for designers, students and curious readers.

  • Author: Joseph Choma
  • Publisher: ORO Editions
  • Format: Paperback, 140 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781951541378

title: The 13-Storey Treehouse
author: Andy Griffiths, Terry Denton
description:
The 13-Storey Treehouse is the first book in the hilarious Treehouse series by Andy Griffiths, illustrated by Terry Denton. Andy and Terry live in an amazing treehouse boasting a huge catapult, a hidden lab underground, a shark tank full of man-eaters plus a marshmallow machine that trails after you, shooting snacks into your mouth.

The pair are supposed to be writing a book, but sea monkeys, a mutant mermaid sea monster and a bubble of burp gas keep getting in the way. Told through a lively mix of text and cartoon illustrations on almost every page, it is perfect for reluctant and newly confident readers who love silly, anything-goes humour.

  • Author: Andy Griffiths
  • Illustrator: Terry Denton
  • Publisher: Macmillan Children's Books
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Treehouse, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781447279785

title: Blue Ocean Shift
author: W. Chan Kim, Renée Mauborgne
description:
Blue Ocean Shift: Beyond Competing is the follow-up to Blue Ocean Strategy by INSEAD professors W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne. Building on more than ten years of further research and practice, it shows organisations how to leave crowded, cut-throat markets behind and create new, uncontested market space.

The authors pair lessons from human psychology with hands-on tools for creating markets, guiding readers step by step through the process and showing how to build the confidence teams need to act. They also make the case that non-disruptive creation matters as much as disruption. Ideal for leaders, entrepreneurs and managers looking for fresh routes to growth.

  • Authors: W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne
  • Publisher: Pan Books
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781509832217

title: Anti-Stress Dot-to-Dot
author: Emily Wallis
description:
Anti-Stress Dot-to-Dot: Beautiful, Calming Pictures to Complete Yourself by Emily Wallis is an activity book for grown-ups who want a relaxing, screen-free way to unwind. Its pages are filled with intricate dot-to-dot puzzles that gradually reveal detailed drawings as you join each point in turn.

Subjects include majestic wildlife, graceful buildings and lovely natural scenes, and each puzzle offers a few quiet, absorbing minutes of focus. A thoughtful gift for anyone who enjoys mindful hobbies such as colouring, or who simply needs a calming break from a busy day.

  • Author: Emily Wallis
  • Publisher: Boxtree
  • Format: Paperback, 96 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780752265865

title: American Classics Collection
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald, Edith Wharton, Nathaniel Hawthorne, Mark Twain
description:
American Classics Collection is a 2019 Pan Macmillan set bringing together works by four great American writers: F. Scott Fitzgerald, Edith Wharton, Nathaniel Hawthorne and Mark Twain. Running to more than 1,600 pages in total, it spans American fiction from the nineteenth century into the early twentieth.

Gathered in one place, these authors offer a broad view of American life, from Hawthorne's New England and Twain's Mississippi to Wharton's New York society and Fitzgerald's Jazz Age, making the set an appealing gift for lovers of classic literature.

  • Authors: F. Scott Fitzgerald, Edith Wharton, Nathaniel Hawthorne, Mark Twain
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Pages: 1,624
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529004984

title: Money in One Lesson
author: Gavin Jackson
description:
Money in One Lesson by economics writer Gavin Jackson is an accessible guide to what money actually is and why it so rarely behaves the way we expect. Vital to the economy and to everyday life, money has no value in itself; it works only because we collectively agree to believe in it.

Jackson tackles the questions behind the headlines, from cryptocurrencies and high inflation to the extraordinary measures taken by central banks and the West's grip on the global banking system. Using colourful historical examples, he shows how money has shaped the fortunes of empires and ordinary people alike. Clear, lively reading for anyone wanting to understand modern economics.

  • Author: Gavin Jackson
  • Publisher: Pan
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529051858

title: We Free the Stars
author: Hafsah Faizal
description:
We Free the Stars is the second and concluding novel in Hafsah Faizal's Sands of Arawiya duology, a young adult fantasy whose world draws on ancient Arabia. One battle has ended, yet the real war has only just begun, and Zafira and Nasir, short of allies and resources, are determined to bring magic back to their kingdom.

An ancient evil is rising again, Nasir struggles to master the power in his blood, and Zafira faces a darkness of a very different kind. Even so, the two find themselves falling deeper in love, knowing that saving their world may demand painful sacrifices. A lush, emotional finale for readers who enjoy enemies-to-lovers romance and richly drawn fantasy settings.

  • Author: Hafsah Faizal
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 624 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Sands of Arawiya, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781035058761

title: We Hunt the Flame
author: Hafsah Faizal
description:
We Hunt the Flame is the first book in Hafsah Faizal's Sands of Arawiya duology, a young adult fantasy set in a vividly imagined world inspired by ancient Arabia. Zafira is the Hunter, who disguises herself as a man and risks her life to feed her people. Nasir, the feared Prince of Death, is an assassin bound to obey his father, the sultan.

Neither wanted the legend that has grown around them. When Zafira sets out on a perilous quest to bring magic back to their ailing land, Nasir is dispatched on a mission of his own, and as their paths cross an ancient evil begins to wake. A striking debut about courage, identity and conquering fear, with a slow-burn, enemies-to-lovers romance.

  • Author: Hafsah Faizal
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 528 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Sands of Arawiya, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781035058754

title: Kaizen
author: Sarah Harvey
description:
Kaizen: The Japanese Method for Transforming Habits, One Small Step at a Time by Sarah Harvey introduces the Japanese philosophy of continuous improvement through tiny, manageable changes. Big lifestyle goals can feel overwhelming and invite self-doubt, but kaizen breaks them down into steps so small they are easy to begin.

Harvey explains how the approach first made its name in business, famously at Toyota, and then shows how to apply it to everyday life. Even the most ambitious aim, such as running a marathon, can start with something as simple as looking up a local running club. A practical, encouraging guide for anyone wanting lasting change without burning out.

  • Author: Sarah Harvey
  • Publisher: Bluebird
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529005356

title: Success Habits: Proven Principles for Greater Wealth, Health, and Happiness
sheet_title: Success Habits: Proven Principles for Greater Wealth, Health, and Happiness
author: Napoleon Hill
description:
Success Habits: Proven Principles for Greater Wealth, Health, and Happiness brings together core ideas from Napoleon Hill, the pioneering personal-achievement writer best known for Think and Grow Rich. It sets out the habits and attitudes that Hill believed lie behind lasting success in work, money and life.

Written in Hill's direct, motivational style, the book is aimed at readers who want a practical framework for building wealth while also looking after their health and happiness. A useful starting point for newcomers to Hill's philosophy and a handy refresher for long-time fans of classic self-help.

  • Author: Napoleon Hill
  • Publisher: Pan Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529006476

title: Masters of Death
author: Olivie Blake
description:
Masters of Death is a witty paranormal fantasy by Olivie Blake, author of The Atlas Six. Viola Marek is a struggling estate agent who also happens to be a vampire, and her latest listing has a serious problem: it is haunted by a murdered ghost who refuses to leave until he learns how he died.

Her unlikely solution is Fox D'Mora, a medium who is mostly a fraud but also, as it happens, the godson of Death himself. With help from a mischievous poltergeist, a demon who works as a personal trainer, an acid-tongued angel and a reaper in love, the pair are pulled into a quest neither of them wanted. Darkly funny, romantic and inventive.

  • Author: Olivie Blake
  • Publisher: Tor
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035011537

title: The Inner Game of Tennis
author: W. Timothy Gallwey
description:
The Inner Game of Tennis by W. Timothy Gallwey is the influential guide to the mental side of peak performance, first published in 1972. Rather than focusing on technique, Gallwey argues that every match has two parts: the outer game against your opponent and the inner game against your own doubts, nerves and lapses of focus.

Drawing on Zen ideas and humanistic psychology, his approach teaches you to quieten the critical mind, trust your body and build concentration, willpower and confidence. This edition includes an introduction by sports psychologist Geoff Beattie. Players of every level will benefit, and its lessons apply just as well to work, study and life beyond the court.

  • Author: W. Timothy Gallwey
  • Publisher: Macmillan
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035047925

title: Before We Forget Kindness
author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
description:
Before We Forget Kindness is the fifth book in Toshikazu Kawaguchi's Before the Coffee Gets Cold series, in an English translation by Geoffrey Trousselot. Once again the little café that lets customers travel through time welcomes four new visitors, each hoping to revisit a moment that still weighs on them.

A father who could not bring himself to let his daughter marry, a woman who never handed over her Valentine's chocolates, a boy longing to smile for his divorced parents and a wife holding a baby without a name must all obey the café's strict rules and return before their coffee goes cold. Tender and quietly moving, it is a story about closure and moving forward.

  • Author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
  • Translator: Geoffrey Trousselot
  • Publisher: Picador
  • Format: Paperback, 203 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Before the Coffee Gets Cold, Book 5
  • ISBN: 9781035046256

title: Before We Say Goodbye
author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
description:
Before We Say Goodbye is the fourth book in Toshikazu Kawaguchi's Before the Coffee Gets Cold series, in an English translation by Geoffrey Trousselot. The regulars of Cafe Funiculi Funicula know all about its legend: a special seat that can carry a customer back in time.

Over the years, visitors have used it to reunite with lost loves, make peace with estranged relatives and see departed family once more. But the journey has its risks and firm rules: travellers must have been to the café before, and they must come back before their coffee cools. This gentle, bittersweet instalment brings new stories of regret, love and farewells.

  • Author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
  • Translator: Geoffrey Trousselot
  • Publisher: Picador
  • Format: Paperback, 175 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Before the Coffee Gets Cold, Book 4
  • ISBN: 9781035044528

title: Tales from the Cafe
author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
description:
Tales from the Cafe is the second book in Toshikazu Kawaguchi's Before the Coffee Gets Cold series, in an English translation by Geoffrey Trousselot. Tucked down a quiet Tokyo back street, a café that has served carefully brewed coffee for over a century offers its customers something extraordinary: the opportunity to journey into the past.

Four new customers arrive at Cafe Funiculi Funicula, each hoping to see someone again, perhaps for the very last time, while abiding by the café's peculiar rules. Exploring love, regret and what we would say if given one more chance, it is a gentle, heartwarming read for fans of the first book and of uplifting Japanese fiction.

  • Author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
  • Translator: Geoffrey Trousselot
  • Publisher: Picador
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Before the Coffee Gets Cold, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781529050868

title: There are Rivers in the Sky
sheet_title: There are Rivers in the Sky
author: Elif Shafak
description:
There Are Rivers in the Sky is a sweeping novel by Elif Shafak that links three lives across centuries through two great rivers and one ancient poem. In Nineveh, beside the Tigris, the learned but merciless Assyrian king Ashurbanipal builds a vast library, and from its ruins the Epic of Gilgamesh survives to shape all that follows.

Born in London in 1840 beside the foul-smelling Thames, Arthur has only his remarkable memory to lift him out of poverty. The novel also follows Narin, a young Yazidi girl in Turkey in 2014, and Zaleekhah, a hydrologist in London in 2018, as water, memory and story connect them. Rich and moving, it suits lovers of literary historical fiction.

  • Author: Elif Shafak
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 483 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241988749

title: The Fall
author: Albert Camus
description:
The Fall is Albert Camus's short, piercing novel, presented here in Robin Buss's English translation. In a bar in Amsterdam, Jean-Baptiste Clamence, a handsome former Paris lawyer once admired for his virtue, spends several drunken evenings telling his life story to a stranger he has just met.

What begins as charming conversation turns into a dark confession of vanity, seduction, excess and self-loathing, revealing a man stripped of innocence who has stared into life's emptiness. Written by the Nobel Prize-winning author of The Outsider, it is a brilliant, unsettling study of guilt and judgement.

  • Author: Albert Camus
  • Translator: Robin Buss
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 92 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141187945

title: The First Man
author: Albert Camus
description:
The First Man is Albert Camus's final, unfinished novel, whose manuscript was recovered from the wreckage of the 1960 car crash that killed him. It was not published until more than three decades later, in 1994, and is widely regarded as the most autobiographical of his novels.

Jacques Cormery grows up poor in Algiers, sustained by devotion to his quiet mother, who cannot read, and by a schoolteacher who changes how he sees the world. Tender and deeply personal, it offers rich insight into Camus's life, his Algerian roots and the themes that run through his greatest books.

  • Author: Albert Camus
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141185231

title: The Outsider
author: Albert Camus
description:
The Outsider is Albert Camus's landmark novel, here in a fresh translation by Sandra Smith. When his mother dies, Meursault refuses to perform the grief others expect of him, and when he later kills a man on a blazing Algerian beach, his apparent indifference condemns him as much as the crime itself.

Camus's study of a man face to face with life's absurdity became a defining work of existentialist literature, yet it also brims with quiet delight in the physical world. Smith based her translation partly on recordings of Camus reading the text aloud, capturing its subtle, dreamlike atmosphere. Essential reading for students and lovers of modern classics.

  • Author: Albert Camus
  • Translator: Sandra Smith
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 111 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141198064

title: Lion of Jordan: The Life of King Hussein in War and Peace
sheet_title: Lion of Jordan: The Life of King Hussein in War and Peace
author: Avi Shlaim
description:
Lion of Jordan: The Life of King Hussein in War and Peace is historian Avi Shlaim's major biography of the Hashemite king who ruled Jordan for more than four decades. Shlaim portrays Hussein as a statesman, peacemaker and shrewd political realist who became one of the most enduring figures in the modern Middle East.

The book follows Hussein through regional wars, attempts on his life and constant diplomacy between the Arab world and Israel, as he worked to keep his country stable and his dynasty secure while pursuing peace. Drawing on extensive research, it is essential reading for anyone interested in Jordan's history and Middle Eastern politics.

  • Author: Avi Shlaim
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 698 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141017280

title: Girl, Woman, Other
author: Bernardine Evaristo
description:
Girl, Woman, Other is Bernardine Evaristo's exuberant novel and joint winner of the 2019 Booker Prize. Moving from Newcastle to Cornwall and across more than a century of British life, it follows twelve characters, most of them Black British women, whose stories gradually interconnect.

Each is searching for something, whether that is a common history, a surprising future, somewhere to belong, a lover or a missing parent, and Evaristo moves between them in a fluid, poetic style that is funny, sharp and warm. A rich portrait of identity, family, feminism and belonging, it is a superb choice for book clubs and readers of contemporary literary fiction.

  • Author: Bernardine Evaristo
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 453 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241984994

title: A New Earth
author: Eckhart Tolle
description:
A New Earth is Eckhart Tolle's follow-up to The Power of Now, a spiritual guide to awakening to a deeper level of consciousness and inner peace. Tolle explains how the ego, with its constant hunger for identity, status and entitlement, drives much of the suffering in our personal lives and in the wider world.

By recognising the ego for what it is and living more fully in the present moment, he suggests, readers can move beyond fear and find lasting contentment, while helping to create a more awakened, compassionate world. Written in a calm, accessible style, it has become a cornerstone of modern spiritual self-help for seekers of every background.

  • Author: Eckhart Tolle
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141039411

title: Honour
author: Elif Shafak
description:
Honour is a powerful family novel by Elif Shafak, set between Turkey and London. Pembe and Adem Toprak leave their homeland to build a new life in Britain, but the traditions and beliefs they carry with them go on to shape the futures of their son and daughter, Iskender and Esma.

Bound by mistakes from the past, the Topraks are shattered by a brutal crime committed in the name of honour. Spanning decades, the novel explores loss, loyalty and betrayal, the collision between tradition and modern life, and how love and heartbreak can pull a family apart. Gripping and compassionate, it suits readers of literary and family fiction.

  • Author: Elif Shafak
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 342 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241972946

title: The Architect's Apprentice
author: Elif Shafak
description:
The Architect's Apprentice is an intricate historical novel by Elif Shafak set in sixteenth-century Istanbul. A young stowaway named Jahan arrives in the city with nothing to his name but a rare white elephant, Chota, intended as a gift for the Sultan's menagerie.

From these humble beginnings, Jahan rises through the Ottoman court and becomes an apprentice to Sinan, the great royal architect, helping to build some of the empire's most magnificent mosques and bridges. Along the way he encounters scheming courtiers, false friends, Roma travellers and animal tamers. Rich in colour and storytelling, it is a treat for lovers of historical fiction.

  • Author: Elif Shafak
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 464 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241970942

title: The Bastard of Istanbul
author: Elif Shafak
description:
The Bastard of Istanbul is a vibrant family saga by Elif Shafak, longlisted for the 2008 Orange Prize. On a rainy afternoon, nineteen-year-old Zeliha, unmarried and pregnant, visits a doctor's clinic in Istanbul, and what happens there shapes the next two decades.

Twenty years on, her daughter Asya lives in a household of colourful women, since a family curse means the Kazanci men die young. When a young Armenian-American woman with ties to the family arrives in search of her roots, long-buried secrets surface, linking both families to the painful history of Turks and Armenians. Warm, funny and bold, it suits readers who love literary family drama.

  • Author: Elif Shafak
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 363 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241972908

title: Metamorphosis and Other Stories
author: Franz Kafka
description:
Metamorphosis and Other Stories gathers the short fiction Franz Kafka chose to publish during his lifetime, in Michael Hofmann's English translation. At its heart is the famous novella in which travelling salesman Gregor Samsa wakes one morning to find he has been transformed into a monstrous insect.

Alongside it are prose poems, sketches, allegories and longer stories, including the tale of an ape who addresses a scientific academy. Darkly funny, unsettling and strikingly original, these pieces capture the loneliness, anxiety and absurdity of modern life that made Kafka one of the most influential writers of the twentieth century. An essential collection for lovers of classic literature.

  • Author: Franz Kafka
  • Translator: Michael Hofmann
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 299 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780143105244

title: My Friends
author: Hisham Matar
description:
My Friends is a moving novel about friendship, exile and home by Hisham Matar. Khaled and Mustafa meet as eighteen-year-old students at university in Edinburgh, both expecting to go back to Libya once their studies are done.

A reckless trip to London to join a protest outside the Libyan embassy changes everything when officials open fire on the crowd and both young men are wounded. In the decades afterwards, Khaled and Mustafa, together with their writer friend Hosam, remain tied by that shared past, until revolution at home makes each decide whether to keep the London lives they have made or return to the country they left. A quiet, profound book for lovers of literary fiction.

  • Author: Hisham Matar
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 464 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241987032

title: By Any Other Name
author: Jodi Picoult
description:
By Any Other Name is a dual-timeline novel by Jodi Picoult about two women, centuries apart, who must each conceal their work behind another name. In the present day, young playwright Melina Green has written a play inspired by Emilia Bassano, an ancestor from Elizabethan England, but in a theatre world stacked against women she doubts it will ever be staged.

When her best friend enters it into a festival using a man's name, Melina's story begins to echo Emilia's. In 1581, Emilia is a gifted, well-educated young ward of English aristocrats, and the novel imagines her as the true author of Shakespeare's plays. A thought-provoking blend of history, drama and feminism for book clubs.

  • Author: Jodi Picoult
  • Publisher: Michael Joseph
  • Format: Paperback, 544 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241676059

title: Someone Else's Shoes: The Delightful No 1 Sunday Times Bestseller 2023
sheet_title: Someone Else's Shoes: The Delightful No 1 Sunday Times Bestseller 2023
author: Jojo Moyes
description:
Someone Else's Shoes is a warm, funny novel by Jojo Moyes, author of Me Before You, about two very different women whose lives collide after a simple mix-up.
