Sam, overwhelmed by the pressures of everyday life, accidentally picks up the wrong bag at the gym and finds it holds a designer Chanel jacket and a pair of glamorous high heels.

Trying them on, she feels like another woman entirely. The bag belongs to Nisha, a wealthy woman whose comfortable life is suddenly falling apart, and as their paths cross, both discover what it really means to walk in someone else's shoes. An uplifting story of friendship, resilience and second chances for readers of contemporary women's fiction.

  • Author: Jojo Moyes
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 418 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781405943505

title: The Personal MBA: A World-Class Business Education in a Single Volume
sheet_title: The Personal MBA: A World-Class Business Education in a Single Volume
author: Josh Kaufman
description:
The Personal MBA: A World-Class Business Education in a Single Volume is Josh Kaufman's self-teaching alternative to an expensive business degree, presented here in a revised and expanded edition. Kaufman argues that the core principles of business can be learned without the cost, time and debt of a formal MBA.

The book distils key subjects, from creating value and marketing to sales, finance, systems and human behaviour, into clear mental models you can apply straight away. Whether you are starting a company, developing your career or simply want to understand how businesses really work, it makes a practical, wide-ranging reference to keep on your desk.

  • Author: Josh Kaufman
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 446 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780670919536

title: Lolita
author: Vladimir Nabokov
description:
Lolita is Vladimir Nabokov's notorious and dazzling novel, narrated by the cultured, self-justifying Humbert Humbert, whose obsession with twelve-year-old Dolores Haze, the girl he calls Lolita, drives him to possess her and to try to fix her forever in art.

Nabokov's prose is witty, playful and elaborate, drawing the reader into the voice of an unreliable narrator while exposing the cruelty behind his charm. Adapted for the screen by Stanley Kubrick (1962) and Adrian Lyne (1997), it remains one of the most debated and influential works of twentieth-century fiction and a landmark of modern literature.

  • Author: Vladimir Nabokov
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 331 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141182537

title: On Palestine
author: Noam Chomsky, Ilan Pappé
description:
On Palestine brings together two of the most prominent voices on the Israeli–Palestinian conflict, Noam Chomsky and Ilan Pappé, in a short, urgent book written in the aftermath of Operation Protective Edge, Israel's 2014 assault on Gaza, which left thousands of Palestinians dead.

Through essays and conversation, they examine the history of the occupation, the future facing Palestinians and the ways outside pressure might bring Israel's human rights violations to an end. A sequel to their earlier book Gaza in Crisis, it is essential reading for anyone seeking to understand Palestine today.

  • Authors: Noam Chomsky and Ilan Pappé
  • Editor: Frank Barat
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 215 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241973523

title: Whatever You Think, Think the Opposite
sheet_title: Whatever You Think, Think the Opposite
author: Paul Arden
description:
Whatever You Think, Think the Opposite is a short, provocative book from Paul Arden, the former advertising creative director and author of It's Not How Good You Are, It's How Good You Want to Be. Arden turns conventional wisdom upside down, encouraging readers to be bolder with risk and get far more enjoyment from their work.

He makes the case that caution can be the most dangerous choice of all, and that bad decisions, unreasonable behaviour and risky ideas can lead to unexpected success. Packed with bold, punchy pages, striking images and memorable examples, it is a quick, inspiring read for creatives, entrepreneurs and anyone stuck in a rut.

  • Author: Paul Arden
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 143 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141025711

title: Electra and Other Plays
author: Sophocles
description:
Electra and Other Plays collects four tragedies by Sophocles in David Raeburn's translation, with an introduction by Pat Easterling. Sophocles turned familiar Greek myths into gripping dramas driven by complex human characters and searching moral questions.

In Electra, a young woman mourns her father Agamemnon, murdered by her mother's lover, and longs for revenge. Ajax traces the downfall of a great warrior, Women of Trachis follows Deianeira's tragic attempt to win back Heracles, and Philoctetes weighs brute force against moral integrity. An essential volume for students of classical drama and lovers of Greek tragedy.

  • Author: Sophocles
  • Translator: David Raeburn
  • Introduction: Pat Easterling
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780140449785

title: Bluey: Barky Boats
author: Bluey
description:
Bluey: Barky Boats is a picture book from Ladybird based on the much-loved animated series Bluey. Bluey and her friend Mackenzie have a whole day with their buddies ahead of them, and they are excited about playing Barky Boats and making a fairy garden.

But Mia and Captain, their buddies, appear to have other things on their minds, and Bluey and Mackenzie start to wonder whether there will still be time to play. A gentle story about friendship, big adventures and growing up, ideal for sharing with young Bluey fans at bedtime or story time.

  • Publisher: Ladybird
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Bluey
  • ISBN: 9780241574171

title: The Island Of Missing Trees: The Top 10 Sunday Times Bestseller
sheet_title: The Island Of Missing Trees: The Top 10 Sunday Times Bestseller
author: Elif Shafak
description:
The Island of Missing Trees is a lyrical, magical novel by Elif Shafak about love, loss and belonging. In 1974, on divided Cyprus, a Greek Christian boy, Kostas, and a Turkish Muslim girl, Defne, meet secretly in a tavern in the city they share.

Growing through the tavern's roof is a fig tree that witnesses their love, and decades later the story moves to London, where their sixteen-year-old daughter, Ada, tries to understand the family history she has never been told. Tender and richly imagined, it explores memory, migration and the scars of conflict.

  • Author: Elif Shafak
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 356 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241988725

title: Ikigai
author: Héctor García, Francesc Miralles
description:
Ikigai by Héctor García and Francesc Miralles explores the Japanese concept of ikigai, often translated as a reason to live or a reason to get up in the morning. It describes ikigai as the point where your needs, ambitions, talents and sense of fulfilment meet, creating a life of balance and purpose.

Drawing on the habits of some of Japan's longest-lived communities, the authors offer gentle guidance on finding and nurturing your own passion, staying active and approaching each day with meaning and joy. A short, calming read that suits anyone looking to slow down and rethink what matters most.

  • Authors: Héctor García and Francesc Miralles
  • Publisher: Cornerstone
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529902402

title: Anxious People: A Novel
author: Fredrik Backman
description:
Anxious People is a warm, funny and surprising novel from Fredrik Backman, whose earlier books include A Man Called Ove. On New Year's Eve, a bungling bank robber, fleeing a failed hold-up, bursts into an apartment viewing and takes everyone there hostage.

The hostages turn out to be a mismatched group of strangers, and as a father-and-son pair of police officers try to piece together what happened, the captives' secrets, regrets and insecurities slowly spill out. Full of humour and heart, it is a compassionate story about friendship, forgiveness and the worries we all carry, perfect for book clubs.

  • Author: Fredrik Backman
  • Translator: Neil Smith
  • Publisher: Penguin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 397 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781405930253

title: Diary of an Awesome Friendly Kid
sheet_title: Diary of an Awesome Friendly Kid
author: Jeff Kinney
description:
Diary of an Awesome Friendly Kid: Rowley Jefferson's Journal is a spin-off from the Diary of a Wimpy Kid series by Jeff Kinney, told this time by Greg Heffley's cheerful best friend, Rowley. After watching Greg fill journal after journal, Rowley finally gets to share his own side of the story.

He has also promised to write Greg's biography along the way, since Greg is convinced that fame and fortune await him, but Rowley's sweet, innocent take on events is not quite what Greg had in mind. Packed with Kinney's trademark cartoons and jokes, it is a fun, easy read for Wimpy Kid fans.

  • Author: Jeff Kinney
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Diary of an Awesome Friendly Kid, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9780241405703

title: Rowley Jefferson's Awesome Friendly Adventure
author: Jeff Kinney
description:
Rowley Jefferson's Awesome Friendly Adventure is a fantasy quest from the Diary of a Wimpy Kid world by Jeff Kinney, imagined and written by Greg Heffley's best friend, Rowley. Roland and his loyal companion, Garg the Barbarian, leave their safe little village to rescue Roland's mum from the evil White Warlock.

Their journey is full of danger and plenty of mishaps, all told with Rowley's trademark sweetness and drawn in Kinney's familiar cartoon style. It follows Diary of an Awesome Friendly Kid and is perfect for young readers who enjoy laugh-out-loud adventures with a big heart.

  • Author: Jeff Kinney
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Diary of an Awesome Friendly Kid, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9780241458839

title: Matilda
author: Roald Dahl
description:
Matilda is Roald Dahl's classic story of a brilliant little girl with an extraordinary mind, illustrated by Quentin Blake. Matilda's parents think she is nothing but a nuisance who reads too much, and the headmistress at her school, the fearsome Miss Trunchbull, believes all children are horrible pests.

With the help of her kind teacher, Miss Honey, and a surprising power of her own, Matilda sets out to change her story. This special edition includes writing tips and activities to help readers create their own stories, plus pull-out illustrations imagining Matilda as a grown-up. A wonderful gift for young readers and Dahl fans.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241558317

title: Major Works of the Stoics (Boxed Set): Meditations, Letters from a Stoic, Discourses and Selected Writings
sheet_title: Major Works of the Stoics (Boxed Set): Meditations, Letters from a Stoic, Discourses and Selected Writings
author: Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, Epictetus
description:
Major Works of the Stoics is a boxed set of three Penguin Classics hardbacks bringing together the essential writings of the great Stoic philosophers, in mini clothbound editions designed by Coralie Bickford-Smith. It contains Marcus Aurelius's Meditations, Seneca's Letters from a Stoic and Epictetus's Discourses and Selected Writings.

Composed by a Roman emperor as private notes to himself, the Meditations has guided readers for almost two millennia. Seneca's letters champion self-possession, friendship and courage in the face of misfortune, while Epictetus teaches that contentment comes from distinguishing what we can control from what we cannot. A beautiful gift and an ideal introduction to Stoicism.

  • Authors: Marcus Aurelius, Seneca and Epictetus
  • Translators: Martin Hammond, Robin Campbell and Robert Dobbin
  • Cover design: Coralie Bickford-Smith
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Hardcover boxed set, 3 volumes, 1,184 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241765791

title: Macbeth
author: William Shakespeare
description:
Macbeth is William Shakespeare's darkest and most compact tragedy, a story of ambition, guilt and the supernatural. Promised the crown of Scotland by three witches and urged on by his wife, the soldier Macbeth kills King Duncan, only to find that one murder leads inexorably to more.

Haunted by visions and by the ghosts of those he has destroyed, Macbeth descends into tyranny and paranoia, while Lady Macbeth is consumed by guilt. This Penguin edition, which has George Hunter as editor and an introduction from Carol Rutter, is a reliable choice for students as well as anyone discovering the play for the first time.

  • Author: William Shakespeare
  • Editor: George Hunter
  • Introduction: Carol Rutter
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141396316

title: When Stars Are Scattered
author: Victoria Jamieson, Omar Mohamed
description:
When Stars Are Scattered is a graphic novel memoir created by Victoria Jamieson and Omar Mohamed, based on Omar's childhood as a Somali refugee. Omar and his little brother Hassan have grown up in Dadaab, a Kenyan refugee camp, where food is scarce, the days are long and there is no proper medical care for Hassan, who does not speak.

When Omar is offered the chance to go to school, he sees a possible route to a better future, but it means leaving his brother, his only remaining family, every day. Honest, hopeful and gently humorous, it is a powerful book about resilience, family and home for young readers and adults alike.

  • Authors: Victoria Jamieson and Omar Mohamed
  • Publisher: Dial Books
  • Format: Paperback, 264 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780525553908

title: Fight Club
author: Chuck Palahniuk
description:
Fight Club is Chuck Palahniuk's explosive debut novel and a cult classic of modern American fiction. Its unnamed narrator, an insomniac stuck in a numbing office job, finds release first in support groups and then in the underground fight club he founds with the anarchic, charismatic Tyler Durden.

Every weekend, men with respectable white-collar jobs gather in basements and car parks to fight bare-handed, returning to work bruised but strangely empowered. But Tyler's ambitions grow far beyond the fights into something much more dangerous. Savage, darkly funny and famously twisty, the novel inspired David Fincher's 1999 film and remains a sharp satire of consumerism and masculinity.

  • Author: Chuck Palahniuk
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 218 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099765219

title: Footnotes in Gaza
author: Joe Sacco
description:
Footnotes in Gaza is Joe Sacco's landmark work of comics journalism, investigating a largely forgotten episode in the history of the Gaza Strip. In 1956, in the southern town of Rafah on the Egyptian border, Israeli soldiers shot dead 111 Palestinian refugees, an event that barely made the historical record.

Sacco travels to Gaza, immerses himself in daily life and interviews survivors and witnesses, weaving their memories together with present-day scenes to ask whether the killings were a cold-blooded massacre or a terrible mistake. Meticulously drawn and deeply humane, it shows how past violence shapes the present, and is essential reading on Palestine.

  • Author: Joe Sacco
  • Publisher: Jonathan Cape
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781787332010

title: Bluey: Bad Mood
author: Bluey
description:
Bluey: Bad Mood is a picture book from Ladybird based on the much-loved Australian animated series Bluey, about a lively Blue Heeler puppy and her family. As the title suggests, this story centres on a bad mood, something many families with young children will recognise.

Short and colourful at 32 pages, it is ideal for reading aloud with young fans of the show.

  • Publisher: Ladybird
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Bluey
  • ISBN: 9780241604885

title: The Very Busy Spider
author: Eric Carle
description:
The Very Busy Spider is Eric Carle's classic picture book about a little spider who spends the day spinning a web on a farmyard fence. One farm animal after another invites her to play, but she is far too busy to stop.

Its multi-sensory pages let children feel the raised lines of the web taking shape, from one thread to a beautiful finished creation, alongside Carle's bright collage illustrations and simple, rhythmic text. Sturdy and interactive in this board book format, it is perfect for reading aloud and sharing with young children.

  • Author: Eric Carle
  • Publisher: Hamish Hamilton
  • Format: Board Book, 26 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241135907

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar's 123
author: Eric Carle
description:
The Very Hungry Caterpillar's 123 is a counting board book from Eric Carle, built around his famous caterpillar and a parade of animal friends. Children count upwards from a single giraffe all the way to ten creatures, with the caterpillar himself joining in along the way.

Carle's bright collage artwork and the simple one-to-ten structure make this a gentle first introduction to numbers for babies and toddlers. The sturdy board pages are made for small hands, and it sits happily alongside other titles in The World of Eric Carle.

  • Author: Eric Carle
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Board book, 22 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141367941

title: The Wimpy Kid Movie Diary How Greg Heffley Went Hollywood
sheet_title: The Wimpy Kid Movie Diary How Greg Heffley Went Hollywood
author: Jeff Kinney
description:
The Wimpy Kid Movie Diary: How Greg Heffley Went Hollywood is Jeff Kinney's behind-the-scenes account of how his Diary of a Wimpy Kid books were turned into live-action films by 20th Century Fox. This updated edition covers all three movies, including Dog Days.

Kinney, who admits he knew little about filmmaking at the start, walks readers through the whole process in a book packed with on-set photos, pages from the script, storyboards, costume sketches and new cartoons. It is a fun, visual companion for fans of the series who want to see how Greg's world made the jump from page to screen.

  • Author: Jeff Kinney
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Diary of a Wimpy Kid (companion)
  • ISBN: 9780141345154

title: The Wimpy Kid Movie Diary: The Next Chapter (The Making of The Long Haul)
sheet_title: The Wimpy Kid Movie Diary: The Next Chapter (The Making of The Long Haul)
author: Jeff Kinney
description:
The Wimpy Kid Movie Diary: The Next Chapter takes readers behind the scenes of Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Long Haul, the 20th Century Fox film adapted from Jeff Kinney's story of the Heffley family's road trip.

Kinney compares making a movie to a family road trip full of detours and surprises, and he shows how the crew pulled off scenes such as a flock of seagulls attacking a minivan, along with a robotic pig and an animatronic toddler. Set photographs, storyboards and new cartoons by Kinney make it a lively read for young fans curious about how films are made.

  • Author: Jeff Kinney
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Hardcover, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Diary of a Wimpy Kid (companion)
  • ISBN: 9780141388199

title: Glorious Rivals
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description:
Glorious Rivals is the second book in Jennifer Lynn Barnes's The Grandest Game series, a young adult mystery set in the world of her Inheritance Games novels. The seven players who came to Hawthorne Island are still competing, each carrying private secrets and personal reasons for wanting to win.

With huge sums of money at stake and romance and danger tightening around the contestants, the competition grows ever more intricate as the players race to solve puzzles and stay alive. Fans of clever riddles, high stakes and the Hawthorne family will find plenty to enjoy, though readers should start with The Grandest Game.

  • Author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Grandest Game #2
  • ISBN: 9780241683668

title: The Grandest Game
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description:
The Grandest Game opens Jennifer Lynn Barnes's spin-off series from The Inheritance Games. Each year, heiress Avery Grambs, together with the four Hawthorne brothers, hosts a competition on a private island, and this time just seven golden tickets grant entry to a game worth millions.

The players arrive with very different motives, from money to power to reasons they keep hidden, and Grayson Hawthorne has an important part to play behind the scenes. Expect elaborate puzzles, shifting alliances and a touch of romance in a fast-moving young adult mystery for fans of puzzle-driven thrillers.

  • Author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 372 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Grandest Game #1
  • ISBN: 9780241672044

title: Peppa Pig: Bedtime Little Library
author: Neville Astley and Mark Baker
description:
Peppa Pig: Bedtime Little Library is a set of small board books that follows Peppa and her little brother George as they wind down for the night, based on the animated series created by Neville Astley and Mark Baker.

The stories move through the evening routine, from bath and story time to bedtime and dreams, helping young children settle down for sleep. Chunky pages suit the smallest hands, and the back covers combine to make a simple jigsaw picture.

  • Author: Neville Astley and Mark Baker
  • Publisher: Penguin Random House
  • Format: Board book, 48 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241294055

title: Peppa Pig: George's Train Ride
author: Neville Astley and Mark Baker
description:
Peppa Pig: George's Train Ride is a novelty board book from Ladybird, based on the animated series created by Neville Astley and Mark Baker. George heads off by train on a long trip with Peppa, Mummy Pig and Daddy Pig, and young readers ride along with him.

The book itself is shaped like a train and rolls on six real wheels, so it doubles as a toy for playtime once the story is finished. Sturdy board pages make it a good fit for little train fans.

  • Author: Neville Astley and Mark Baker
  • Publisher: Ladybird
  • Format: Board book, 12 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241375891

title: Peppa Pig: Peppa's Talent Show
author: Neville Astley and Mark Baker
description:
Peppa Pig: Peppa's Talent Show is a noisy sound book from Ladybird in which Peppa, George and their friends put on a talent show, and everyone wonders what Peppa's own talent will turn out to be. It is based on the animated series created by Neville Astley and Mark Baker.

The story is full of music, magic tricks and bubbles, and 18 different sounds let children join in with the performances on every page. It is an interactive read-aloud for young Peppa fans who like to press, listen and play along.

  • Author: Neville Astley and Mark Baker
  • Publisher: Ladybird
  • Format: Hardcover sound book, 24 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241487129

title: Peppa Pig: The Wheels on the Bus
sheet_title: Peppa Pig: The Wheels on the Bus
author: Neville Astley and Mark Baker
description:
Peppa Pig: The Wheels on the Bus sets the classic nursery rhyme alongside Peppa and her friends in a sturdy board book from Ladybird, based on the animated series created by Neville Astley and Mark Baker.

Children can sing along as the bus makes its journey, and the book comes with real wheels, so it can be pushed along the floor once the song is over. It is a playful choice for toddlers who love Peppa and familiar rhymes.

  • Author: Neville Astley and Mark Baker
  • Adapted by: Claire Sipi
  • Publisher: Ladybird
  • Format: Board book, 12 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241294598

title: Percy Jackson and the Greek Heroes
sheet_title: Percy Jackson and the Greek Heroes
author: Rick Riordan
description:
Percy Jackson and the Greek Heroes sees Rick Riordan's demigod narrator, Percy Jackson, son of Poseidon, retell the stories of the great heroes of Greek mythology. It follows on from Percy's earlier guide to the gods and has also been published as Percy Jackson's Greek Heroes.

Percy reaches back thousands of years for tales of beheaded monsters, offended gods, trips to the Underworld and endings that are often tragic, all told in his trademark sarcastic, funny voice. It is an entertaining way into the classic legends for middle-grade readers and longtime fans of Camp Half-Blood.

  • Author: Rick Riordan
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 550 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Camp Half-Blood Chronicles
  • ISBN: 9780141362250

title: The Dark Prophecy
author: Rick Riordan
description:
The Dark Prophecy is the second book in Rick Riordan's The Trials of Apollo, set in the same world as Percy Jackson. The god Apollo, banished to Earth in the body of an awkward mortal teenager, must keep working through a series of dangerous trials to win back his place on Mount Olympus.

With his companions, Apollo hunts for the ancient oracles, and this time the trail leads to a haunted cave somewhere in the American Midwest, while the second member of a villainous Triumvirate stands in his way. Riordan blends myth, humour and fast action in a series well suited to middle-grade and young teen readers.

  • Author: Rick Riordan
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 414 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Trials of Apollo #2
  • ISBN: 9780141363967

title: The Hidden Oracle
author: Rick Riordan
description:
The Hidden Oracle launches Rick Riordan's The Trials of Apollo series. Having angered Zeus, his father, Apollo is thrown out of Olympus and wakes up in New York City in the body of an ordinary teenage boy, stripped of his divine powers.

Hunted by old enemies among gods, monsters and mortals, the ancient god has to work out how to survive as a human and turns to the one place that might shelter him: Camp Half-Blood. Packed with humour, mythology and familiar faces from the Percy Jackson books, it is a lively start for middle-grade and young teen readers.

  • Author: Rick Riordan
  • Publisher: Puffin
  • Format: Paperback, 374 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Trials of Apollo #1
  • ISBN: 9780141363929

title: Danny the Champion of the World
sheet_title: Danny the Champion of the World
author: Roald Dahl
description:
Danny the Champion of the World is Roald Dahl's warm-hearted story of a boy and his father, illustrated by Quentin Blake. Danny lives in a gypsy caravan with his dad, a wonderful storyteller who is also his best friend, and he is already a skilled young car mechanic.

Everything changes when Danny uncovers a secret his father has kept for years, and soon the two are plotting an ambitious scheme against Victor Hazell, a rich and unpleasant landowner. Funny, tender and full of mischief, it is a classic for confident young readers and a lovely book to share aloud.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: Puffin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 202 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780142410332

title: Fantastic Mr Fox
author: Roald Dahl
description:
Fantastic Mr Fox is Roald Dahl's much-loved story of a clever fox who outwits three greedy farmers, with illustrations by Quentin Blake. Boggis, Bunce and Bean are tired of Mr Fox raiding their farms, so the three of them team up to surround him and his family.

Trapped underground, Mr Fox refuses to give up and comes up with a daring plan to save everyone. Short chapters, comic villains and plenty of cunning make this an ideal early chapter book and a favourite read-aloud for families.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: Puffin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 81 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780142410349

title: The Magic Finger
author: Roald Dahl
description:
The Magic Finger is a short, funny story by Roald Dahl, illustrated by Quentin Blake. The Gregg family next door love to go hunting, and the young girl who narrates the tale cannot stand it, no matter how politely she asks them to stop.

When the Greggs push her too far, her temper sets off the Magic Finger, and suddenly the hunters find themselves turned into birds and living in a nest, while the ducks they hunted take their place. A quick, satisfying read with a clear message about kindness to animals, it suits newly independent readers.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: Puffin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 96 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780142413852

title: The Twits
author: Roald Dahl
description:
The Twits is Roald Dahl's gleefully revolting story about Mr and Mrs Twit, a filthy, spiteful couple who spend their days playing horrible tricks on each other, illustrated by Quentin Blake.

When they are not pranking one another, the Twits catch birds for their pies and make the Muggle-Wump monkeys spend the day upside down, until the animals decide it is time to get even. Short, outrageous and very funny, it is a perfect pick for young readers who enjoy a cheeky story with a satisfying comeuppance.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: Puffin Books
  • Format: Paperback, 87 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780142410394

title: The Witches
author: Roald Dahl
description:
The Witches is Roald Dahl's darkly funny tale about real witches, who look like ordinary women and live ordinary lives while secretly loathing children, illustrated by Quentin Blake.

The Grand High Witch, who rules over every witch, has a scheme to make every child vanish, and only a young boy and his wise grandmother stand in her way. Thrilling, a little scary and full of Dahl's wicked humour, it is a classic for confident young readers and a memorable family read-aloud.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 325 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241578179

title: Bluey: Road Trip
author: Bluey
description:
Bluey: Road Trip is a board book from Ladybird based on the animated children's series Bluey, following Bluey and her family as they set off on a road trip together.

Its sturdy pages and bright artwork from the show make it a good fit for toddlers and preschoolers who already love the Heeler family.

  • Author: Bluey
  • Publisher: Ladybird
  • Format: Board book, 24 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241605202

title: The Lovely And The Lost
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description:
The Lovely and the Lost is a young adult survival thriller by Jennifer Lynn Barnes, author of The Inheritance Games. It centres on a family that trains search-and-rescue dogs for a living and is called in when a child goes missing in a vast national park covering some 750,000 acres.

Combining wilderness danger, a race against time and the bond between handlers and their dogs, the novel offers the suspense and tight plotting that Barnes's readers enjoy. It was first announced under the working title Lost Causes.

  • Author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241763094

title: Voices of the Fallen Heroes
author: Yukio Mishima
description:
Voices of the Fallen Heroes and Other Stories is a new collection of short fiction by the Japanese novelist Yukio Mishima, edited by Stephen Dodd and published by Penguin Classics. The stories date from the 1960s, the last decade of Mishima's career, and appear in English versions by a team of translators, with an introduction by John Nathan.

The pieces range from autobiography to outright horror: a writer gripped by visions of the apocalypse, a marquis whose voyeurism ends in violence, beatniks dancing to jazz in a ruined church, and first love turning to obsession. The title story centres on a séance that summons the spirits of young officers of the Imperial Army. A haunting introduction to a major voice in twentieth-century Japanese literature.

  • Author: Yukio Mishima
  • Editor: Stephen Dodd
  • Introduction: John Nathan
  • Translators: Jeffrey Angles, Tomoko Aoyama, Sam Bett, Juliet Winters Carpenter, Stephen Dodd, Paul McCarthy, John Nathan, Hannah Osborne, Oliver White
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241723609

title: Fake
author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
description:
Fake is a personal finance book by Robert T. Kiyosaki, the author of Rich Dad Poor Dad. In it he takes aim at the ideas about money, investing and education that are widely accepted as fact, and asks readers to separate what is genuine from what is not.

Written in Kiyosaki's direct, contrarian style, the book argues that a solid grasp of real facts is the foundation for taking charge of your own finances. It suits readers of the Rich Dad series and anyone who wants to question conventional financial advice before deciding how to save and invest.

  • Author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
  • Publisher: Plata Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 560 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781612681092

title: The Oresteia
author: Aeschylus
description:
The Oresteia is Aeschylus's great trilogy of Greek tragedy, made up of Agamemnon, The Libation Bearers and The Eumenides, presented by Penguin Classics in Robert Fagles's translation with an introduction and notes by Fagles and W. B. Stanford.

The plays follow a cycle of murder and vengeance in the royal house of Argos: Agamemnon is killed by his wife Clytemnestra on his return from war, their son Orestes avenges him, and he is finally judged before a court established by Athena. Moving from blood feud to the rule of law, it remains one of the founding works of Western drama.

  • Author: Aeschylus
  • Translator: Robert Fagles
  • Introduction and notes: Robert Fagles and W. B. Stanford
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 336 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780140443332

title: Decolonising My Body
author: Afua Hirsch
description:
Decolonising My Body is a work of non-fiction by journalist and author Afua Hirsch about beauty, the body and the ideas that shape how we see ourselves. Getting her first tattoo at the age of forty set her on a path to free her own body from colonial ideas about purity, ageing and adornment.

Drawing on global research, personal stories and interviews with beauty experts, practitioners and clients, Hirsch traces the global history of rituals around skin, hair and body modification, and asks whose standards we are really trying to meet. A thoughtful read for anyone interested in race, gender and culture.

  • Author: Afua Hirsch
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529954197

title: We Are Not Numbers
author: Ahmed Alnaouq
description:
We Are Not Numbers: The Voices of Gaza's Youth, compiled by Ahmed Alnaouq, brings together stories by young people from Gaza who have lived their whole lives under occupation and blockade. In their own words, they describe ordinary hopes and fears lived out in extraordinary circumstances.

One teenager lies awake hoping her roof will not fall in; a student looks online at pictures of the world's great libraries he dreams of visiting; another young woman notes the buildings she longs to rebuild. The result is a moving collection of personal testimony that puts individual faces and voices to the headlines, for readers seeking to understand life in Gaza.

  • Author: Ahmed Alnaouq
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804955697

title: MetaMAUS
author: Art Spiegelman
description:
MetaMaus is Art Spiegelman's companion to Maus, his graphic memoir of his father's survival of the Holocaust. Originally subtitled as a look inside a modern classic, it explores how and why the landmark book was made.

Built around in-depth interviews, the book takes up the questions Spiegelman is most often asked, including why he chose to tell the story in comics and why he drew Jews as mice, and it is illustrated with sketches, drafts, family photographs and archival material. Essential reading for anyone who has read Maus and wants to understand its making.

  • Author: Art Spiegelman
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781405982962

title: Innamorata
author: Ava Reid
description:
Innamorata is the first book in Ava Reid's The House of Teeth series, a gothic fantasy set on an island where the dead once walked and seven noble houses held power through necromancy, until a conqueror burned their libraries and killed their lords.

Defying the new order, only the House of Teeth endures, through its two remaining members: the beautiful heiress Marozia and her strange cousin, Lady Agnes, who has been silent for seven years yet carries the true secrets of the family. Agnes is charged with recovering the lost art of death magic and restoring her house's honour, in a dark, lush tale of ambition, devotion and romance.

  • Author: Ava Reid
  • Publisher: Del Rey
  • Format: Paperback, 560 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The House of Teeth #1
  • ISBN: 9781529910674

title: A Theory of Dreaming
author: Ava Reid
description:
A Theory of Dreaming follows Ava Reid's A Study in Drowning as the second and final book in her dark academia fantasy duology. Having defeated the Fairy King and left her nightmares behind, Effy has worked with Preston on a thesis about Angharad, the country's beloved fairy tale, and become the first woman ever admitted to the literature college.

Yet her success brings new dangers: the whole university, and soon the whole nation, seems eager to watch her fail, and the consequences of their first discovery pull Effy and Preston into one last adventure. A dreamlike, romantic conclusion for readers who loved the first book.

  • Author: Ava Reid
  • Publisher: Random House Publishing Group
  • Format: Paperback, 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: A Study in Drowning #2
  • ISBN: 9781529948349

title: Fight Oligarchy
author: Bernie Sanders
description:
Fight Oligarchy is a political book by US Senator Bernie Sanders, who argues that a small group of the extremely wealthy now dominates America's economy, politics and media, leaving ordinary people with little say over their country's future.

Sanders examines the crises facing the United States during Donald Trump's presidency, including what he sees as repeated attacks on democracy, and sets out how citizens can organise and push back. Direct and urgent, it is a call to build a political movement that serves working people rather than billionaires, and will interest readers following American politics and economic inequality.

  • Author: Bernie Sanders
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 160 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781837312948

title: There Are Places in the World Where Rules Are Less Important Than Kindness
sheet_title: There Are Places in the World Where Rules Are Less Important Than Kindness
author: Carlo Rovelli
description:
There Are Places in the World Where Rules Are Less Important Than Kindness is a collection of short writings by the Italian physicist Carlo Rovelli, many of which first appeared in the Italian press. Following his curiosity wherever it leads, he moves freely between science, literature, philosophy and politics.

Topics include Newton's interest in alchemy, Einstein's errors, Nabokov's butterflies and Dante's view of the cosmos, alongside travels in Africa, the mind of the octopus, psychedelics and what atheism means. Clear, witty and wide-ranging, it suits readers who enjoyed Seven Brief Lessons on Physics or simply love thoughtful essays.

  • Author: Carlo Rovelli
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141993256

title: A Thousand Blues
author: Cheon Seon-ran
description:
A Thousand Blues is a Korean science fiction novel by Cheon Seon-ran, translated into English by Chi-Young Kim. In 2035, near a racecourse, a young woman discovers a robot named Coli lying on a scrapheap, gazing up at the sky, and decides to look after him.

Together they set out to save Today, a racehorse worn out by years of racing and destined for slaughter, with a gentle plan to let her run one more race at the slowest pace of her life. A tender, hopeful story about care, disability and learning to slow down, it will appeal to readers of uplifting translated fiction.

  • Author: Cheon Seon-ran
  • Translator: Chi-Young Kim
  • Publisher: Transworld
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804995327

title: The Extinction of Experience
author: Christine Rosen
description:
The Extinction of Experience is Christine Rosen's thoughtful inquiry into what we lose as more of daily life is filtered through screens and apps. From photo-editing tools and payment apps to memes and the Metaverse, she looks at how mediated technology has changed our sense of self and blurred the line between virtual and real.

In a reflective, humane style, Rosen identifies everyday human experiences that are fading away, such as face-to-face conversation and a sense of place, and invites readers to recover and cultivate them. A timely read for anyone uneasy about how technology shapes attention, relationships and identity.

  • Author: Christine Rosen
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529967036

title: A History of Modern Syria
author: Daniel Neep
description:
A History of Modern Syria by Daniel Neep is a substantial account of a country whose politics have rarely been settled. Carved from the Ottoman Empire after the First World War and then placed under a harsh French mandate, Syria was given new borders that split families, trading networks and political loyalties.

Neep follows the country's later efforts to come to terms with those borders, including its short-lived union with Egypt in the late 1950s, repeated defeats by Israel, and the civil war that began in 2011. A detailed, wide-ranging history for readers seeking to understand Syria and the wider Middle East.

  • Author: Daniel Neep
  • Format: Hardcover, 704 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241003299

title: 10 to 25
author: David Yeager
description:
10 to 25: The Science of Motivating Young People is a book by developmental psychologist David Yeager about how adults can bring out the best in those aged between ten and twenty-five. Drawing on research into adolescence and early adulthood, it explains what drives young people and how adults can motivate them more effectively.

Aimed at parents, educators, mentors and anyone who leads young people, the book turns scientific findings into practical guidance for being a positive, motivating influence. It is a thoughtful choice for readers who want to understand teenagers and young adults better.

  • Author: David Yeager
  • Publisher: Penguin (Cornerstone)
  • Format: Paperback, 464 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804953969

title: Awakening
author: Deepak Chopra
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Awakening is a guide to spiritual and personal transformation by Deepak Chopra, published in the US as Awakening: The Path to Freedom and Enlightenment. Building on decades of his teaching, Chopra explores how readers can connect with their true selves and shape a life that is no longer ruled by fear.

Through a series of illuminating sutras, he shows how to move beyond merely getting by towards an awakened way of living, and he offers a Wellbeing Index for tracking progress along the way. Readers interested in meditation, consciousness and personal growth will find a clear, accessible companion here.

  • Author: Deepak Chopra
  • Format: Hardcover
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846047329

title: Quantum Body
author: Deepak Chopra
description:
Quantum Body: The New Science of Living a Longer, Healthier, More Vital Life is a health and wellbeing book by Deepak Chopra, written in collaboration with physicist Jack Tuszynski and endocrinologist Brian Fertig. It applies ideas from quantum science to the way we think about ageing, illness and vitality.

The authors propose that beneath the physical body, which ages and decays, lies a quantum body operating at the sub-atomic level, influencing thoughts, feelings and biological responses. Understanding it, they argue, could change the way we age. A thought-provoking read for those interested in mind-body health and Chopra's work.

  • Author: Deepak Chopra
  • Publisher: Rider
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846047718

title: Charlotte's Web
author: E. B. White
description:
Charlotte's Web is E. B. White's classic children's novel about friendship on a farm, with illustrations by Garth Williams. Wilbur, a runt piglet saved by a girl named Fern, grows up in a barn and learns that he is destined for the dinner table.

Help comes from an unlikely friend: Charlotte, a wise and clever spider, who weaves words into her web to convince the farmer that Wilbur is no ordinary pig. Funny, gentle and deeply moving, it is a timeless story about loyalty, loss and the cycle of life, perfect for reading aloud or for independent young readers.

  • Author: E. B. White
  • Illustrator: Garth Williams
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241777503

title: Tell Me Everything
author: Elizabeth Strout
description:
Tell Me Everything is a novel by Elizabeth Strout that takes readers back to Crosby, Maine, and brings together some of her best-loved characters, including Lucy Barton, Olive Kitteridge and Bob Burgess. As autumn settles over the town, a shocking crime unsettles the community.

Around that mystery, Strout explores unlikely friendships, past loves and people who fall for each other yet choose to live apart, as her characters wonder what any single life really means. Quietly hopeful and full of compassion, it is a rewarding read for book clubs and for admirers of literary fiction about ordinary lives.

  • Author: Elizabeth Strout
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 329 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Amgash #5
  • ISBN: 9780241634363

title: Super Agers
author: Eric Topol
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Super Agers: An Evidence-Based Approach to Longevity is a guide to the science of healthy ageing by Eric Topol, a prominent medical researcher. He argues that medicine is at a turning point, with new treatments arriving faster than ever to tackle the chronic diseases that affect most older adults.

Topol explains the developments behind this shift, from drugs such as semaglutide to artificial intelligence, and shows how readers, their families and friends can benefit from them. Rigorous yet accessible, it suits anyone who wants an evidence-led view of how to stay healthier for longer.

  • Author: Eric Topol
  • Publisher: Cornerstone
  • Pages: 464
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529979992

title: Electra and Other Plays
author: Euripides
description:
Electra and Other Plays gathers five tragedies by Euripides in John Davie's translation for Penguin Classics, with an introduction by Richard Rutherford. Written while Athens and Sparta were locked in their long struggle for dominance, the plays are shadowed by war and especially by its toll on women.

In Electra, Agamemnon's children avenge their father by killing their mother; Suppliant Women follows mothers mourning sons lost in battle; and Andromache, Hecabe and Trojan Women portray the defeated survivors of Troy. An essential collection for students and readers of Greek drama.

  • Author: Euripides
  • Translator: John Davie
  • Introduction: Richard Rutherford
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 267 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780140446685

title: Age of Revolutions
author: Fareed Zakaria
description:
Age of Revolutions: Progress and Backlash from 1600 to the Present is Fareed Zakaria's sweeping account of the upheavals that have shaped the modern world. Two decades after he warned of the rise of illiberal democracy, he places today's polarised, populist politics within a long historical frame.

Drawing on years of research and interviews with global leaders, the book shows how classical liberalism emerged and the cycles of fury and counter-revolution that followed bursts of rapid change. Clear and thought-provoking, it will appeal to readers of history, politics and economics who want to make sense of the present.

  • Author: Fareed Zakaria
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781802065596

title: The Penguin Book of Puzzles
author: Gareth Moore
description:
The Penguin Book of Puzzles, compiled by Gareth Moore, is a collection of brain-teasers gathered from across history and from some of the greatest puzzle-setters of all time. It stretches from ancient riddles to modern challenges that still baffle sharp minds.

Inside are crosswords, maths problems, wordplay and logic teasers, along with curious puzzle types rescued from past centuries. Ranging from gentle to fiendish, the puzzles suit beginners and seasoned solvers alike, making this a satisfying book to dip into or give as a gift.

  • Author: Gareth Moore
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781405970495

title: A Hymn to Life
author: Gisèle Pelicot
description:
A Hymn to Life is the memoir of Gisèle Pelicot, translated from the French (Et la joie de vivre). Her life changed overnight when police revealed that the man she had been married to for fifty years had, for close to a decade, been secretly drugging her and bringing many unknown men to the house to assault her.

Four years later, her husband and fifty co-defendants went on trial, and her decision to give up her anonymity drew attention around the world, along with her insistence that the shame belonged to her abusers. Told with courage and dignity, this is a powerful account of survival, justice and the will to live fully again.

  • Author: Gisèle Pelicot
  • Publisher: The Bodley Head
  • Format: Paperback, 246 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847928979

title: We Do Not Part
author: Han Kang
description:
We Do Not Part is a novel by the South Korean author Han Kang that moves from present-day Korea into a painful chapter of the country's past. One December morning, Kyungha hears from her friend Inseon, who is in a Seoul hospital and needs her to come at once.

The two women have not seen each other for more than a year, and the request sets Kyungha on a journey that draws her into buried history. Written with a dreamlike, wintry intensity, it is a haunting work of literary fiction about memory, grief and friendship.

  • Author: Han Kang
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 375 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241997048

title: Thief of Night
author: Holly Black
description:
Thief of Night is Holly Black's sequel to Book of Night, her first novel for adults, and completes her duology of shadow magic and crime. Charlie Hall has always been crooked, a con artist who rarely meets a bad decision she does not commit to wholeheartedly.

She is skilled enough to take a shadow out of a locked tower, but this time the prize is far more personal, as she must find a way to win back a heart. Dark, sharp and full of twists, it is a gripping urban fantasy for readers who enjoyed the first book.

  • Author: Holly Black
  • Publisher: Del Rey
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Charlatan Duology #2
  • ISBN: 9781529150032

title: The Atomic Habits Workbook
author: James Clear
description:
The Atomic Habits Workbook is James Clear's official companion to Atomic Habits, designed to turn the ideas of the original book into everyday practice. It works as a hands-on guide for forming better habits and dropping unhelpful ones, one step at a time.

Guided journal prompts help readers examine their current habits and the influences behind them, while practical exercises and ready-made templates make it easy to track progress and apply Clear's system. It is a useful next step for anyone who has read Atomic Habits and wants a practical way to make lasting changes.

  • Author: James Clear
  • Publisher: Cornerstone
  • Format: Paperback, 320 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529981230

title: Worlds of Islam
author: James McDougall
description:
Worlds of Islam: A Global History is historian James McDougall's account of Islam as a faith constantly on the move, from its beginnings in seventh-century Arabia to the digital age. He follows its spread over a thousand years, as soldiers, traders and missionaries took it to the margins of Europe, maritime Southeast Asia and deep into China.

McDougall goes on to trace the remarkable diversity of the Muslim world in the modern era, from empires and Gulf monarchies to revolutionary nationalist movements from Algeria to Indonesia, as well as preachers, reformers and activists in Europe and North America. A wide-ranging history for general readers and students alike.

  • Author: James McDougall
  • Format: Hardcover
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241528488

title: Easy Air Fryer
author: Jamie Oliver
description:
Easy Air Fryer is Jamie Oliver's cookbook dedicated to getting the most from an air fryer, whether you have just bought one or already use it every day. Developed over months of testing, the recipes show how versatile the gadget can be, for cooking ahead or making meals on the spot.

Chapters cover quick fixes, new classics, vegetable-led dishes, salads, canapés, baking and puddings, all aimed at tasty, nutritious food without fuss. Packed with tips and fresh ideas, it is a practical choice for busy home cooks who want more from their machine.

  • Author: Jamie Oliver
  • Publisher: Penguin Michael Joseph
  • Format: Hardcover, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241733431

title: Legenda
author: Janina Ramirez
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
Legenda is a work of history by Janina Ramirez, author of Femina, examining how the stories of medieval women have been reshaped over the centuries to serve politics and the building of nations. Figures such as Isabella of Castile, Joan of Arc and Lady Godiva are widely remembered, yet their lives have often been distorted and used as weapons.

Ramirez looks past the myths to find the real women underneath, while also recovering pioneering women of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries whose roles in revolutionary Europe have been overlooked. A lively, revisionist read for anyone interested in medieval history, national identity and women's history.

  • Author: Janina Ramirez
  • Publisher: Ebury Publishing
  • Pages: 480
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780753560426

title: Killer Spirit
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description:
Killer Spirit is the second book in Jennifer Lynn Barnes's The Squad series, a funny young adult spy story. Toby Klein is an unlikely varsity cheerleader at Bayport High, because the squad is secretly a team of teenage government operatives, and she must juggle pep rallies and handsprings with hacking and protocol.

When something is brewing in Bayport, the Squad is sent to find out what, but the mission turns dangerous fast, while homecoming court nominations and team captain Brooke threaten Toby's sanity in other ways. Witty and action-packed, it is ideal for fans of clever, lighthearted teen thrillers.

  • Author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 368 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Squad #2
  • ISBN: 9780241802366

title: Lessons in Power
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description:
Lessons in Power is the second book in Jennifer Lynn Barnes's The Fixer series, a young adult political thriller originally released as The Long Game. Tess Kendrick, a student at Washington's exclusive Hardwicke School, comes from a family that makes problems vanish, but she also has ties to political dynasties and power.

When Tess agrees to manage a classmate's student council campaign, the contest between children of the capital's elite quickly turns into something far more dangerous. Full of secrets, betrayal and sharp twists, it is a gripping read for fans of The Inheritance Games.

  • Author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Fixer #2
  • ISBN: 9780241763124

title: Perfect Cover
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description:
Perfect Cover opens Jennifer Lynn Barnes's The Squad series, a witty young adult spy adventure. Toby Klein is a sophomore computer hacker with a karate black belt, no school spirit and, according to her guidance counsellor, an attitude problem, which makes her the last girl anyone would expect to join the cheerleading squad.

But at Bayport High, the varsity squad is a front for an elite team of teenage government agents, and they want Toby. Mixing high school politics with undercover missions, it is a fun, fast read for fans of smart, funny teen thrillers.

  • Author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 304 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Squad #1
  • ISBN: 9780241802465

title: The Ruling Class
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description:
The Ruling Class is the first book in Jennifer Lynn Barnes's The Fixer series, a young adult political thriller first published as The Fixer. When Tess Kendrick moves to Washington, D.C. to live with her older sister Ivy, she discovers that Ivy is the city's go-to fixer, making powerful people's scandals disappear.

Enrolled at the exclusive Hardwicke School, Tess soon becomes a fixer herself for the sons and daughters of Washington's elite. As both sisters lead double lives, a scandal at school reaches Capitol Hill, and Tess must uncover who is behind it before she becomes a target. Smart, fast-paced and twisty.

  • Author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Fixer #1
  • ISBN: 9780241763070

title: The Same Backward as Forward
author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
description:
The Same Backward as Forward is Jennifer Lynn Barnes's prequel to The Inheritance Games, a flip book that tells one love story from two sides: read hers, then turn the book over to see it through his eyes. Twenty-year-old Hannah Rooney keeps her head down in nursing school, staying clear of her notorious criminal family until she and her younger sister Kaylie can escape their hometown of Rockaway Watch.

Tobias Hawthorne II, sole heir to one of America's greatest fortunes, plays the part of the entitled heir to perfection. A must for fans who want the backstory of the Hawthorne family.

  • Author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Inheritance Games #0
  • ISBN: 9780241772225

title: When We Were Monsters
author: Jennifer Niven
description:
When We Were Monsters is a psychological thriller for young adults by Jennifer Niven, author of All the Bright Places. Eight students at a prestigious boarding school win places on an exclusive creative programme, but only one will win a life-changing opportunity, and when a teacher is found dead, the students all have reasons to wish her out of the way.

Effy is writing about the betrayal behind her mother's death, while Arlo dreams of getting his novel published and of winning back Effy after vanishing from her life three years earlier. Rivalry, romance and buried secrets twist together in a dark academia mystery.

  • Author: Jennifer Niven
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241772492

title: By Any Other Name
author: Jodi Picoult
description:
By Any Other Name is a dual-timeline novel by Jodi Picoult about two women, centuries apart, who are linked by a secret. Melina Green, a New York playwright, is still waiting to see one of her plays performed, and she comes to believe that only a deception will earn her the recognition she craves.

Centuries earlier, Emilia Bassano, a forebear of Melina's and the mistress of a powerful Elizabethan nobleman, faced the same silencing, and the bold deception she chose echoed down the generations. Exploring authorship, ambition and the price women pay to be heard, it is ideal for book clubs and lovers of historical fiction.

  • Author: Jodi Picoult
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 544 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781405961899

title: We All Live Here
author: Jojo Moyes
description:
We All Live Here is a contemporary novel by Jojo Moyes about a woman and her chaotic blended family. Lila Kennedy is juggling a failed marriage, two difficult daughters, a crumbling house, a stalled career and a complicated love life, and her elderly stepfather appears to have settled in without anyone quite agreeing to it.

Then her real father, who left for Hollywood thirty-five years ago and has barely been in touch since, turns up on her doorstep. Warm, funny and perceptive, it explores forgiveness and what family really means, and suits readers who enjoy heartfelt, character-driven fiction.

  • Author: Jojo Moyes
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 440 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241415528

title: The Amazing Generation
author: Jonathan Haidt
description:
The Amazing Generation is a guide for children and tweens by Jonathan Haidt, inspired by his book The Anxious Generation. It aims to help young readers build a happy, adventurous life that is not taken over by smartphones and social media, whether or not they already have them.

The book mixes surprising facts, a graphic novel section, interactive challenges and insights into how tech companies hold attention, along with stories from young adults who wish they had waited longer for a phone. Upbeat and practical, it encourages kids to grow into confident, independent people.

  • Author: Jonathan Haidt
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241806586

title: Scaffolding
author: Lauren Elkin
description:
Scaffolding is a novel by Lauren Elkin in which two couples occupy one Paris flat, in the city's north-east, almost half a century apart. In 2019, psychoanalyst Anna is coming to terms with a recent miscarriage; with her husband David working in London, she fixates on renovating the kitchen and befriends Clémentine, a young member of a radical feminist collective.

In 1972, Florence, a psychology student, and her husband Henry are also redoing their kitchen, and she hopes for a baby while he hesitates about fatherhood. Weaving the two stories together, Elkin explores marriage, fidelity and pregnancy in a richly layered literary novel.

  • Author: Lauren Elkin
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529932942

title: The Wolf King
author: Lauren Palphreyman
description:
The Wolf King is the first book in Lauren Palphreyman's romantasy series of the same name, set as war breaks out between humans and werewolves. On the night before her wedding, Princess Aurora spares a young werewolf during a cruel dog fight and draws the attention of Callum, a powerful alpha.

That same night Callum escapes and carries Aurora off to the wild country beyond the northern border, where the wolf clans are uniting, convinced she holds the key to defeating the humans. As forbidden attraction grows between them, danger closes in from both sides. An enemies-to-lovers fantasy romance full of tension and passion.

  • Author: Lauren Palphreyman
  • Publisher: Wayward TxF
  • Format: Paperback, 479 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Wolf King #1
  • ISBN: 9781911751069

title: The Economic Government of the World
sheet_title: The Economic Government of the World
author: Martin Daunton
description:
The Economic Government of the World: 1933–2023 is Martin Daunton's history of the bodies and individuals that have sought to steer the world economy. Beginning in 1933, when a World Monetary and Economic Conference met after the Great Depression, it runs to the G20's handling of the economic fallout of Covid-19.

Daunton examines how policymakers have balanced the competing pulls of democracy, national self-determination and globalisation, and the lasting influence of the organisations created at Bretton Woods, including the International Monetary Fund and what became the World Bank. A detailed, authoritative study for readers of economic history and international relations.

  • Author: Martin Daunton
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 1024 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141038674

title: What You Are Looking for Is in the Library: A Novel
sheet_title: What You Are Looking for Is in the Library: A Novel
author: Michiko Aoyama
description:
What You Are Looking For Is in the Library is a gentle Japanese novel by Michiko Aoyama, translated by Alison Watts, about the comfort and change that the right book can bring. In Tokyo, the enigmatic librarian Sayuri Komachi has an uncanny sense of what each visitor is really searching for in life.

She gives each of them a book recommendation that points the way. Five people at a crossroads come to her: a restless retail worker, a mother demoted after maternity leave, an accountant dreaming of an antiques shop, a young manga artist in a slump and a recently retired man. Warm, uplifting and ideal for book lovers.

  • Author: Michiko Aoyama
  • Translator: Alison Watts
  • Publisher: Random House UK
  • Format: Paperback, 266 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804994139

title: Decolonizing Language and Other Revolutionary Ideas
sheet_title: Decolonizing Language and Other Revolutionary Ideas
author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
description:
Decolonizing Language and Other Revolutionary Ideas is a collection of essays by Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o, the Kenyan novelist and postcolonial thinker behind modern classics such as Petals of Blood, A Grain of Wheat and Weep Not, Child. He emerged from the literary scene of the 1950s and 1960s, as colonial rule in Africa came to an end.

In the late 1970s Ngũgĩ famously abandoned English for his novels, choosing to write in Gĩkũyũ, his first language. These essays reflect on African literature, language, power and postcolonial criticism, and offer a stimulating introduction to his thinking for students and general readers alike.

  • Author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
  • Publisher: Allen Lane
  • Format: Hardcover, 214 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241780978

title: Meditations for Mortals
author: Oliver Burkeman
description:
Meditations for Mortals: Four Weeks to Embrace Your Limitations and Make Time for What Counts is Oliver Burkeman's guide to living well within the limits of a finite life. Structured as a four-week journey, it asks how we can accept constraints we cannot change and make sensible choices when the to-do list never ends.

Borrowing from psychology, literature, philosophy, religion and even self-help, Burkeman offers practical tools and fresh perspectives, suggesting that meaningful productivity is often about allowing things to happen rather than forcing them. Bracing, funny and reassuring, it suits readers who enjoyed Four Thousand Weeks.

  • Author: Oliver Burkeman
  • Publisher: The Bodley Head
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847927620

title: Digital Exhaustion
author: Paul Leonardi
description:
Digital Exhaustion: Simple Rules for Reclaiming Your Life is Paul Leonardi's examination of why our devices leave us so drained, and how to build a healthier relationship with them. He looks at the endless scrolling, constant notifications and the sense that no amount of replying or reading ever lets us catch up.

Rather than calling for a total digital detox, which is unrealistic for most people with jobs, friends and families, Leonardi sets out an achievable path to using technology with more energy and less fatigue. A practical read for anyone feeling worn down by screens.

  • Author: Paul Leonardi
  • Publisher: Ebury Edge
  • Format: Paperback, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529146844

title: Wake
author: Rebecca Hall
description:
Wake: The Hidden History of Women-Led Slave Revolts is a graphic history and memoir by historian Rebecca Hall, illustrated by Hugo Martínez. It tells the story of enslaved women who planned and led uprisings, both aboard slave ships crossing the Atlantic and across the Americas, and who were then erased from the history books.

Hall, the granddaughter of enslaved people, describes her own search through court records, ship captains' logs, old letters and archaeological evidence to recover these women's stories. Powerful and inventive, it suits readers of history, graphic non-fiction and Black women's history.

  • Author: Rebecca Hall
  • Illustrator: Hugo Martínez
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 208 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780141997735

title: Gone Before Goodbye
author: Reese Witherspoon and Harlan Coben
description:
Gone Before Goodbye is a thriller co-written by Reese Witherspoon and Harlan Coben. Maggie McCabe, a gifted former army combat surgeon, is struggling after a string of personal tragedies when a former colleague offers her work treating wealthy, anonymous clients who expect both the finest care and total discretion.

The job takes her across the world to an extremely secretive and powerful man in need of unusual medical help, but when her patient vanishes while still in her care, Maggie finds herself in serious danger. Fast-paced and twisty, it is perfect for fans of high-stakes suspense.

  • Author: Reese Witherspoon and Harlan Coben
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 448 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804955994

title: The Impossible Fortune
author: Richard Osman
description:
The Impossible Fortune is the fifth Thursday Murder Club mystery by Richard Osman. After a quiet year, the friends are busy with other things: Joyce is planning a wedding, Elizabeth is grieving, Ron has family worries and Ibrahim is still counselling his favourite criminal.

Then a guest at the wedding tells Elizabeth they fear for their life, and the gang are pulled into a new case involving a villain desperate to get hold of an uncrackable code. Warm, witty and cleverly plotted, it is a treat for fans of cosy crime and the series so far.

  • Author: Richard Osman
  • Publisher: Viking
  • Format: Paperback, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Thursday Murder Club #5
  • ISBN: 9780241743997

title: The Thursday Murder Club
author: Richard Osman
description:
The Thursday Murder Club is the first novel in Richard Osman's cosy crime series. In a quiet retirement village, four unlikely friends, Elizabeth, Joyce, Ibrahim and Ron, gather every Thursday to look into unsolved murders from old police files.

When a brutal killing happens right on their doorstep, the club suddenly has a live case to crack. They may be nearly eighty, but they have plenty of tricks left, and they are determined to catch the killer first. Funny, warm and full of twists, it is an ideal introduction to the series.

  • Author: Richard Osman
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Thursday Murder Club #1
  • ISBN: 9781405985840

title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians: The Lightning Thief
sheet_title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians: The Lightning Thief
author: Rick Riordan
description:
Percy Jackson and the Olympians: The Lightning Thief is the first book in Rick Riordan's much-loved series about a modern-day demigod. Percy is a good-hearted boy who struggles to concentrate in class and keep his temper, and life at boarding school takes a strange turn when a teacher appears to transform into a monster and attack him.

Soon Percy learns that he is the son of a Greek god and is sent on a quest across America to prevent a war among the gods of Olympus. Funny, fast-moving and full of mythology, it is a perfect start to the series for middle-grade readers.

  • Author: Rick Riordan
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Hardcover, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Percy Jackson and the Olympians #1
  • ISBN: 9780241777480

title: Matilda
author: Roald Dahl
description:
Matilda is Roald Dahl's beloved story of an extraordinary girl with a brilliant, magical mind, presented here as a clothbound hardback in the Puffin 85th Anniversary Clothbound Collection, with illustrations by Quentin Blake and a foreword by Robin Stevens.

Matilda's parents see her as a nuisance who reads too much, and her headmistress, the fearsome Miss Trunchbull, treats children as pests to be locked away. With the help of books and her own remarkable powers, Matilda finds a way to change her story and prove how extraordinary children can be. A timeless gift edition.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Illustrator: Quentin Blake
  • Foreword: Robin Stevens
  • Publisher: Puffin Classics
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Puffin 85th Anniversary Clothbound Collection
  • ISBN: 9780241777466

title: The Magic Finger
author: Roald Dahl
description:
The Magic Finger is Roald Dahl's short, mischievous tale about a young girl who cannot bear the hunting trips her neighbours take every weekend. The Gregg family set off each Saturday to shoot wildlife, and when her temper finally boils over she points her special finger at the whole family, with astonishing results.

Soon the Greggs find themselves sprouting wings while the ducks they hunted take over their home. Told with Dahl's trademark wit and a clear sense of fairness, it is a quick, funny read that also gets children thinking about how we treat animals, and it works well for newly confident readers and for reading aloud.

  • Author: Roald Dahl
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 80 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241568675

title: Lucky Loser
author: Russ Buettner, Susanne Craig
description:
Lucky Loser is an investigative history of Donald Trump's money by New York Times reporters Russ Buettner and Susanne Craig. Drawing on years of reporting into his finances, they trace how Trump received vast sums from his father, Fred, and argue that a long run of business failures was hidden behind a carefully crafted image of self-made success.

The book follows the money from the family's property empire through casinos, licensing deals and television fame, setting the public story against the financial record. Detailed yet readable, it is essential reading for anyone interested in American politics, business journalism and how a reputation can be built and sold.

  • Author: Russ Buettner, Susanne Craig
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 528 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529935806

title: A Quiet Place
author: Seichō Matsumoto
description:
A Quiet Place is a Japanese crime novel by Seichō Matsumoto, translated into English by Louise Heal Kawai. Tsuneo Asai, a softly spoken government official, is away on business in Kobe when he hears that Eiko, his wife, has suffered a fatal heart attack. Her weak heart makes the death unsurprising, yet the place where she died, a small shop in a seedy part of Tokyo, makes no sense for such a shy, retiring woman.

As Tsuneo quietly pieces together her final months, he finds a nearby house known as a meeting place for lovers and begins to suspect a secret life. Matsumoto, a leading figure in Japanese social crime fiction, builds tension through character and atmosphere, making this an absorbing choice for readers of slow-burning psychological mysteries.

  • Author: Seichō Matsumoto
  • Translator: Louise Heal Kawai
  • Publisher: Penguin Classics
  • Format: Paperback, 231 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241744208

title: Murder at Mount Fuji
author: Shizuko Natsuki
description:
Murder at Mt. Fuji is a classic Japanese mystery by Shizuko Natsuki, translated by Robert B. Rohmer. Jane Prescott, who has spent years studying Japanese culture, works as English tutor to Chiyo Wada, the gentle daughter of a powerful aristocratic family, and accepts an invitation to celebrate New Year at the Wadas' lavish villa.

Soon after Jane arrives, Chiyo is driven to kill in self-defence, and the family close ranks to shield her from the police, pulling Jane into their plan. As the investigation unfolds, she starts to sense that nothing is quite as it appears. Elegant and twisting, it suits fans of classic closed-circle detective fiction.

  • Author: Shizuko Natsuki
  • Translator: Robert B. Rohmer
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 295 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804959602

title: The Samurai Detectives: Volume 1
author: Shōtarō Ikenami
description:
The Samurai Detectives is the first volume of Shōtarō Ikenami's historical crime series, translated from Japanese by Yui Kajita. In Edo-era Japan, young swordsman Akiyama Daijiro has opened his own fencing school beside the river and is still waiting for his first pupil when a mysterious samurai arrives with a troubling offer: a large sum of gold to wound the daughter of one of the Shogun's most powerful advisers.

Refusing to let the matter rest, Daijiro joins forces with his father Kohei, a legendary swordsman, and the formidable fighter Mifuyu to uncover the conspiracy. Episodic, atmospheric and full of swordplay, it suits readers who enjoy historical adventure, Japanese fiction in translation and detective stories with a strong sense of place.

  • Author: Shōtarō Ikenami
  • Translator: Yui Kajita
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Samurai Detectives, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781405975766

title: The Tesla Files
author: Sönke Iwersen, Michael Verfürden
description:
The Tesla Files is an investigative account of Elon Musk's car company by journalists Sönke Iwersen and Michael Verfürden. It is built on a huge leak of confidential internal Tesla documents passed to the authors by a whistleblower, and examines what lies beneath the company's polished public image.

The authors look at reports of frequent accidents in Tesla's factories, serious concerns about its Autopilot software, a workplace culture driven by fear and a long trail of promises that were never kept. Carefully documented and clearly told, it is a timely read for anyone interested in technology, corporate power and the influence of one of the richest men on the planet.

  • Author: Sönke Iwersen, Michael Verfürden
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Hardcover, 352 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241797747

title: When Everyone Knows That Everyone Knows...
sheet_title: When Everyone Knows That Everyone Knows...
author: Steven Pinker
description:
When Everyone Knows That Everyone Knows... is Steven Pinker's exploration of common knowledge: the state in which people not only know something but know that others know it, and so on without end. The Harvard cognitive scientist shows how this layered awareness quietly shapes friendships, markets, politics and everyday social life.
