Pinker uses the idea to explain puzzles such as financial booms and busts, revolutions that seem to erupt from nowhere, the theatre of diplomacy, online shaming campaigns and an awkward first date, as well as the lengths people go to in order to keep things unsaid. Lively and wide-ranging, it suits readers of popular psychology, economics and social science.

  • Author: Steven Pinker
  • Publisher: Allen Lane
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241618837

title: We'll Prescribe You Another Cat
author: Syou Ishida
description:
We'll Prescribe You Another Cat is Syou Ishida's warm-hearted return to the Kokoro Clinic for the Soul, the sequel to We'll Prescribe You a Cat, translated from Japanese by E. Madison Shimoda. The clinic's address is uncertain and it can be hard to find, yet it always appears for those who need it most, and its treatment is as unusual as ever: a cat.

This time the patients meet a new set of feline healers, including Kotetsu, a boisterous four-month-old Bengal, small but fearless Shasha and the soft, sleepy Ms. Michiko. Characters drift from one chapter into the next, creating a gentle, quietly funny portrait of loneliness, healing and connection for readers who love cosy Japanese fiction.

  • Author: Syou Ishida
  • Translator: E. Madison Shimoda
  • Publisher: Doubleday
  • Format: Hardcover, 236 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: We'll Prescribe You a Cat, Book 2
  • ISBN: 9781529936735

title: Atmosphere
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description:
Atmosphere is a historical novel by Taylor Jenkins Reid set in the early years of NASA's space shuttle programme. Joan Goodwin, a reserved physics and astronomy professor at Rice University who has loved the stars all her life, applies when NASA begins recruiting women scientists, and in 1980 she is selected to train as an astronaut in Houston.

Among a close-knit group of fellow candidates, Joan finds friendship, rivalry and an unexpected love that changes how she sees herself. Blending the thrill and danger of spaceflight with an intimate romance, it is a moving, absorbing read for book clubs and fans of character-driven historical fiction.

  • Author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
  • Publisher: Hutchinson Heinemann
  • Format: Paperback, 332 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529152982

title: iWar
author: Tim Higgins
attention: Matched by title (edition/cover may differ)
description:
iWar is Wall Street Journal columnist Tim Higgins's account of the fight over Apple's control of the iPhone and its App Store. It tells how Apple built enormous power over apps, commerce and culture, and how a loose alliance of tech billionaires, each with their own motives, set out to break that grip.

The cast includes Spotify's Daniel Ek, Epic Games founder Tim Sweeney, whose Fortnite became central to the battle, and Elon Musk, with China's WeChat also part of the story. Briskly told and closely reported, it suits readers interested in technology, competition and who controls the digital economy.

  • Author: Tim Higgins
  • Publisher: Transworld
  • Format: 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781911709657

title: On Freedom
author: Timothy Snyder
description:
On Freedom is a work of political philosophy by Yale historian Timothy Snyder, author of On Tyranny. Snyder argues that many people now think of freedom simply as being left alone by the state, and that this narrow, negative idea has left democracies exposed and drifting toward crisis.

In its place he sets out a richer, more positive vision of freedom, grounded in the conditions that allow people to flourish and to act together. Thoughtful and urgent, it suits readers concerned about authoritarianism and anyone who wants to understand what a free society really requires.

  • Author: Timothy Snyder
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781529929287

title: Raise Your Soul
author: Yanis Varoufakis
description:
Raise Your Soul is Yanis Varoufakis's personal history of resistance, told through the lives of five women who shaped him: Eleni, Anna, Trisevgeni, Georgia and Danaë. Beginning in 1920s Egypt, it follows his family through a century of Greek upheaval, from Nazi occupation and civil war to military dictatorship and the recent economic crisis.

Moving between family memoir and political history, the economist and former Greek finance minister reflects on how courage and defiance at home formed his own convictions, and on the authoritarian forces that still threaten Europe. Intimate yet wide in scope, it will appeal to readers of memoir, modern European history and political thought.

  • Author: Yanis Varoufakis
  • Publisher: The Bodley Head
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781847929075

title: Autocracy, Inc.
author: Anne Applebaum
description:
Autocracy, Inc. is Anne Applebaum's sharp analysis of how modern dictatorships really work. She argues that today's autocracies are no longer lone strongmen ruling by fear alone, but members of loose networks that share money, surveillance tools and propaganda techniques to stay in power.

Applebaum shows how kleptocratic finance, information warfare and mutual support link very different regimes across the world, and sets out how democracies can organise to push back. Concise and clearly argued, it is an essential guide for readers following current affairs, international politics and the defence of liberal democracy.

  • Author: Anne Applebaum
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593471203

title: Immortal Consequences
author: I.V. Marie
description:
Immortal Consequences is the first book in I.V. Marie's dark academia fantasy series The Souls of Blackwood Academy. Blackwood is a legendary boarding school on the edge of the afterlife, and once students pass through its gates the only way out is to win the Decennial, a ruthless magical contest that ends with a single winner.

Six of Blackwood's top pupils are selected to compete this time, among them two bitter academic rivals bound by a strange connection, a fiercely ambitious girl, a student haunted by lost love and a charming playboy. Romantic, eerie and full of twists, it suits readers who love romantasy, rivals-to-lovers tension and deadly school games.

  • Author: I.V. Marie
  • Publisher: Delacorte Press
  • Format: Paperback, 512 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: The Souls of Blackwood Academy, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9798217116799

title: And the River Drags Her Down
sheet_title: And the River Drags Her Down
author: Jihyun Yun
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
And the River Drags Her Down is a haunting young adult horror novel by Jihyun Yun about sisterhood, grief and revenge. Soojin Han has always obeyed the rules of her family's ancestral magic, above all never to revive anything bigger than her palm, until her older sister Mirae is found drowned in the river beside their small seaside town.

Soojin breaks every rule to bring her back, and at first the reunited sisters are overjoyed. But Mirae grows restless and hungry for more than a hidden life, and the consequences spread. Slow-burning and eerie, steeped in family myth, it suits readers of atmospheric YA horror and dark fantasy.

  • Author: Jihyun Yun
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9798217122806

title: Empire of AI
author: Karen Hao
photo_source: Goodreads (matched by title; edition may differ)
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
Empire of AI is journalist Karen Hao's investigation into OpenAI and the race to build ever more powerful artificial intelligence. Hao began covering the company in 2019, when it presented itself as a safety-focused non-profit led by Sam Altman, and she follows its transformation into one of the most influential and contested businesses in technology.

Drawing on years of reporting and close access, she examines the enormous resources, data and human labour that modern AI demands, and the costs borne by workers and communities around the world. Rigorous and eye-opening, it is essential reading for anyone who wants to understand who is shaping AI and at what price.

  • Author: Karen Hao
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9798217060481

title: Distancing
author: L. David Marquet, Michael A. Gillespie
description:
Distancing is a practical guide to better decision-making from former US Navy captain L. David Marquet, who wrote Turn the Ship Around!, and psychology professor Michael A. Gillespie. They argue that being too immersed in our own point of view pushes us to defend past choices and protect our self-image, instead of seeing a situation clearly.

Their answer is psychological distancing, which they break into three techniques: stepping into another person's perspective, picturing ourselves from further away, and imagining how our future selves will judge today's choices. With clear examples for leaders and teams, it shows readers how to coach themselves toward calmer, wiser decisions.

  • Author: L. David Marquet, Michael A. Gillespie
  • Publisher: Portfolio
  • Format: Hardcover, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780593713105

title: The Men's Fashion Book
author: Phaidon Editors
description:
The Men's Fashion Book is Phaidon's A to Z celebration of 500 of the most important names in menswear, covering some two centuries of style. Entries span designers, brands, photographers, models, tailors, retailers, stylists and style icons from around the world, each brought to life with a striking image.

Created in partnership with Jacob Gallagher, who edits men's fashion for the Wall Street Journal's Off Duty, the book moves from classic tailoring to streetwear, placing established names like Paul Smith and Giorgio Armani beside newer talent. A handsome hardback, it makes an inspiring reference for fashion lovers, designers and anyone curious about how men dress.

  • Author: Phaidon Editors
  • Introduction: Jacob Gallagher
  • Publisher: Phaidon Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 528 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781838662479

title: The Arabesque Table: Contemporary Recipes from the Arab World
sheet_title: The Arabesque Table: Contemporary Recipes from the Arab World
author: Reem Kassis
description:
The Arabesque Table is a cookbook by Palestinian writer Reem Kassis that reimagines the food of the Arab world for today's home kitchen. Combining historical research with family and cultural knowledge, Kassis shows how this remarkably varied cuisine has evolved over centuries and offers her own modern takes on its classic dishes.

The book gathers 130 accessible recipes, arranged by main ingredient and illustrated with vivid photography, with stories that root each dish in its history and setting. It suits confident cooks and curious beginners alike, and anyone who wants to explore Arab cooking beyond the familiar favourites.

  • Author: Reem Kassis
  • Publisher: Phaidon Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 256 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781838662516

title: Exotic
author: Judy Sund
description:
Exotic: A Fetish for the Foreign is art historian Judy Sund's illustrated survey of the West's long fascination with faraway places and unfamiliar cultures. Through a wide range of images, the book traces how ideas of 'the foreign' have been absorbed into Western art, design, architecture and wider culture.

Sund shows how this attraction to the strange, the beautiful and the grotesque has repeatedly fed Western creativity, while also raising questions about how other cultures are seen and represented. Richly visual and thought-provoking, it suits readers interested in art history, design and cross-cultural exchange in an increasingly connected world.

  • Author: Judy Sund
  • Publisher: Phaidon Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780714876375

title: The City & The City
author: China Miéville
description:
The City & The City is China Miéville's genre-bending crime novel. When a woman's body turns up in Besźel, a decaying city on the edge of Europe, Extreme Crime Squad detective Inspector Tyador Borlú expects a routine case, but the clues lead him to Ul Qoma, a rival city that occupies the same physical space and is kept apart only by strict habit and law.

Partnered with Qussim Dhatt, a detective from Ul Qoma, Borlú is drawn into a conspiracy that tests the boundaries both cities depend on. Part police procedural, part weird fiction, it is a clever, unsettling novel about perception and borders, ideal for readers who enjoy literary crime and speculative fiction.

  • Author: China Miéville
  • Publisher: Picador
  • Format: Paperback, 384 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781035060245

title: Rich Family Smart Family
author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
description:
Rich Family Smart Family is a personal finance book by Robert T. Kiyosaki, author of Rich Dad Poor Dad. As its subtitle, Raise Your Family's Financial IQ and Take Control of Your Future, makes clear, it is about building financial knowledge across the whole family.

It suits parents and households who want to talk about money together and plan for the future with more confidence.

  • Author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
  • Publisher: Plata Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 176 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781612681337

title: Rich Dad Poor Dad
author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
description:
Rich Dad Poor Dad is Robert T. Kiyosaki's personal finance classic about growing up with two father figures: his own well-educated father, who struggled with money, and his best friend's father, an entrepreneur who became his 'rich dad'. Their contrasting attitudes shaped how Kiyosaki came to think about work, wealth and investing.

The book questions the belief that a high salary is the route to riches, and explains why it pays to have money working for you rather than simply working for a pay cheque, with a focus on financial literacy, assets and liabilities. Straightforward and motivating, it remains a popular first step for readers new to personal finance.

  • Author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
  • Publisher: Plata Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 348 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Rich Dad, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781612681139

title: A Moon Will Rise from the Darkness: Reports on Israel’s Genocide in Palestine
sheet_title: A Moon Will Rise from the Darkness: Reports on Israel’s Genocide in Palestine
author: Francesca Albanese
description:
A Moon Will Rise from the Darkness collects the reports of Francesca Albanese, the UN Special Rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories, on Israel's conduct since October 2023. Albanese first sets out her case that the violence of this period amounts to genocide, then places it within a longer history of settler colonialism.

The final reports turn to the international companies that profit from the killing and destruction. The volume also includes a new reflection by Albanese, accounts from the three previous rapporteurs, Michael Lynk, John Dugard and Richard Falk, plus a preface co-written by Mandy Turner and Lex Takkenberg. It is an important record for readers of human rights, international law and Middle East politics.

  • Author: Francesca Albanese
  • Forewords: Richard Falk, John Dugard, Michael Lynk
  • Preface: Lex Takkenberg, Mandy Turner
  • Publisher: Pluto Press
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780745352312

title: Yoga : the Secret of Life
author: Francesco Mastalia
description:
Yoga: The Secret of Life is a fine art photo-documentary by photographer Francesco Mastalia that portrays 108 leading yoga practitioners and their spiritual and physical journeys. Each portrait is paired with the subject's own reflections on how this ancient practice has reshaped their lives, inside and out.

Mastalia produced every image with the wet collodion process, hand-coating glass plates in a technique dating from the 1850s, which gives each ambrotype a timeless, one-of-a-kind quality. A beautiful hardback for yoga students, teachers and lovers of photography, it invites quiet reflection on who we are and how to live well.

  • Author: Francesco Mastalia
  • Publisher: powerHouse Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781576878569

title: Abundance
author: Ezra Klein, Derek Thompson
description:
Abundance is a book on politics and policy by journalists Ezra Klein and Derek Thompson. They argue that liberal democracy is endangered not only by autocrats but by progressive governments that fail to build and deliver, leaving people facing high costs and shortages of housing, clean energy and working public services.

Drawing on decades of reporting on politics, economics and culture, the authors examine why building has become so hard and set out an agenda focused on growth, supply and getting things done. Provocative and readable, it suits anyone interested in housing, infrastructure, technology and the future of progressive politics.

  • Author: Ezra Klein, Derek Thompson
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781805226055

title: Psycho-Cybernetics 365
author: Maxwell Maltz, Matt Furey
description:
Psycho-Cybernetics 365 is a book of daily inspiration drawn from the teachings of Dr Maxwell Maltz, whose 1960 classic Psycho-Cybernetics was a pioneering work on self-image and personal change. It condenses his ideas into a short reading for each day of the year.

Each entry offers a brief lesson on themes such as building a healthier self-image, using visualisation and mental rehearsal, and learning to relax, with commentary from Matt Furey, a Maltz scholar who heads the Psycho-Cybernetics Foundation. It suits readers who want a steady daily habit of reflection and goal-setting.

  • Author: Maxwell Maltz, with commentary by Matt Furey
  • Publisher: Souvenir Press
  • Format: 416 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781805225690

title: Going Home: A Walk Through Fifty Years of Occupation
sheet_title: Going Home: A Walk Through Fifty Years of Occupation
author: Raja Shehadeh
description:
Going Home: A Walk Through Fifty Years of Occupation is a memoir by Palestinian lawyer and writer Raja Shehadeh. On a walk through Ramallah, the city where he grew up, he revisits its streets, houses, shops and people, recording how the place and its community have changed over half a century.

Part elegy, part reflection on ageing and the setbacks of the resistance, the book notes green hills and olive groves giving way to concrete, the tightening grip of occupation and settlements on daily movement, and the traces of history that still shape the city. Quietly powerful, it suits readers of memoir, Palestinian life and Middle East history.

  • Author: Raja Shehadeh
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 224 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781788163071

title: Why Nations Fail
author: Daron Acemoglu, James A. Robinson
description:
Why Nations Fail by economists Daron Acemoglu and James A. Robinson asks why some countries grow rich while others stay poor. Their answer is that geography, climate and culture matter far less than institutions: the political and economic rules that decide who holds power and who shares in prosperity.

Ranging across history from ancient Rome and Tudor England to modern China, the authors contrast inclusive institutions, which let people invest and keep the rewards of their work, with extractive ones that serve narrow elites. Ambitious and accessible, it is a stimulating read for anyone interested in economics, politics and global development.

  • Author: Daron Acemoglu, James A. Robinson
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 529 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781846684302

title: Art of Seduction
author: Robert Greene
description:
The Art of Seduction is Robert Greene's study of seduction as a subtle, indirect form of power, from the author of The 48 Laws of Power. The first part describes the different types of seducer, from the Siren and the Rake to the Charismatic and the Star, along with the anti-seducer, so readers can recognise which type they most resemble.

The second part breaks the seductive process into twenty-four strategies, illustrated with stories drawn from history, literature and the lives of famous figures. Provocative and richly researched, it suits readers interested in psychology, persuasion and human behaviour, and fans of Greene's other books on power and strategy.

  • Author: Robert Greene
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 466 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781861977694

title: The Daily Laws
author: Robert Greene
description:
The Daily Laws: 366 Meditations distils more than two decades of Robert Greene's writing on power, seduction, strategy, mastery and human nature into a single page for each day of the year. Every entry offers a concise lesson drawn from one of his books, followed by a short daily commandment to put into practice.

Quick to read but rich in insight, it works both as an accessible introduction for newcomers to Greene and as a way for longtime readers to revisit and absorb his ideas. It suits anyone interested in self-improvement, psychology and building better habits of thought.

  • Author: Robert Greene
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 463 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781788168540

title: The Laws of Human Nature
author: Robert Greene
description:
The Laws of Human Nature is Robert Greene's in-depth guide to understanding why people behave as they do. Drawing on psychology and on the lives of historical figures, Greene sets out a series of laws covering traits such as irrationality, narcissism, envy, aggression and conformity, and shows how they shape our everyday dealings with others.

The aim is twofold: to help readers judge others more accurately and guard against manipulation, and to recognise the same forces in themselves so they can respond with greater calm and self-awareness. Substantial and absorbing, it suits fans of The 48 Laws of Power and anyone interested in psychology and personal development.

  • Author: Robert Greene
  • Publisher: Profile Books
  • Format: Paperback, 624 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781781259191

title: Old School
author: Jeff Kinney
description:
Old School is the tenth book in Jeff Kinney's Diary of a Wimpy Kid series. Greg Heffley's mum and dad think life was better in the past, before screens and modern comforts, but Greg is far from convinced that a world without gadgets, heating or proper plumbing sounds like much fun.

Much to his dismay, he is packed off on a school trip to Hardscrabble Farm for a week of chores and outdoor living, with predictably chaotic results. Told through Greg's diary entries and packed with cartoon drawings, it is a quick, funny read for reluctant and keen readers alike.

  • Author: Jeff Kinney
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Diary of a Wimpy Kid, Book 10
  • ISBN: 9780141377094

title: The Getaway
author: Jeff Kinney
description:
The Getaway is the twelfth book in Jeff Kinney's Diary of a Wimpy Kid series. With cold weather arriving and the stress of Christmas looming, the Heffley family trade winter at home for a holiday at a resort on a tropical island, hoping for a few relaxing days in the sun.

Paradise turns out to be far from perfect, as sunburn, upset stomachs and unwelcome creatures threaten to ruin the trip. Told through Greg's diary entries and cartoons, it is a funny, fast-paced holiday misadventure for young readers who enjoy humour and family chaos.

  • Author: Jeff Kinney
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 226 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Diary of a Wimpy Kid, Book 12
  • ISBN: 9780141385259

title: The Last Straw
author: Jeff Kinney
description:
The Last Straw is the third book in Jeff Kinney's Diary of a Wimpy Kid series. Greg Heffley's dad, Frank, is determined to toughen up his son, and lines up a string of sporty, outdoorsy activities designed to make him a little less wimpy.

Greg manages to wriggle out of most of them, until his father starts talking about military academy and Greg realises he will need his cleverest scheme yet. Packed with cartoons and Greg's deadpan diary entries, it is an easy, laugh-out-loud read for children aged 7 and up and anyone who enjoys school and family comedy.

  • Author: Jeff Kinney
  • Publisher: Penguin
  • Format: Paperback, 226 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Diary of a Wimpy Kid, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9780141324920

title: What Fury Brings
author: Tricia Levenseller

description:

The story starts with a company close to collapse in 1996 that decided to move its production offshore.

McGee traces how Apple sent thousands of its engineers to China, achieving extraordinary scale in the iPhone era while binding itself to an authoritarian government with ever-growing demands. A sharp blend of business history and geopolitics, it will appeal to readers interested in technology, supply chains and relations between the US and China.

How Countries Go Broke is Ray Dalio's analysis of what he calls the Big Debt Cycle, the long-term pattern by which government debts build up, become unmanageable and are eventually resolved. Writing from decades of experience as an investor, Dalio asks whether there are limits to national borrowing and whether a major reserve-currency nation such as the US could genuinely go broke.

Drawing on history and his own research, he explains the warning signs that matter, where he believes current debt trends are heading and what policymakers and investors might do about them. It is a timely read for anyone following economics, markets and public finance, and readers of his Principles books will recognise the approach.

title: Beauty and the Beast (Disney Animated Classics)
sheet_title: Beauty and the Beast (Disney Animated Classics)
author: Sally Morgan
description:
Beauty and the Beast forms part of the Disney Animated Classics series, offering Sally Morgan's retelling of the celebrated Disney film. The tale of Belle, the cursed Beast and his enchanted castle is accompanied by striking development art from Disney's original studio artists.

An introduction from one of Disney's filmmakers sheds light on the production, and the closing pages profile the artists involved. With a cloth binding, ribbon bookmark, foil detailing and decorated endpapers, it makes a memorable gift for fans of the film.

  • Author: Sally Morgan
  • Publisher: Studio Press
  • Format: Hardcover
  • Language: English
  • Series: Disney Animated Classics
  • ISBN: 9781787417366

title: Cinderella (Disney Animated Classics): A Deluxe Gift Book Of The Classic Film - Collect Them All!
sheet_title: Cinderella (Disney Animated Classics): A Deluxe Gift Book Of The Classic Film - Collect Them All!
author: Walt Disney Company
description:
Cinderella is part of the Disney Animated Classics collection, a deluxe gift book that retells the classic Disney film. Cinderella's journey from the cinders to the royal ball, complete with Fairy Godmother and glass slipper, is illustrated with paintings, story sketches and development art from Disney's original studio artists.

It includes a foreword from Mark Henn, who has worked at Walt Disney Animation Studios as both director and supervising animator, plus notes on the artists behind the film. Cloth-bound, with a ribbon bookmark, foil detailing and decorated endpapers, it is a charming keepsake for Disney lovers.

  • Author: Walt Disney Company
  • Publisher: Studio Press Books
  • Format: Hardcover, 68 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Disney Animated Classics
  • ISBN: 9781787415423

title: Disney Dot-to-Dot Princesses
author: Walt Disney Company
description:
Disney Dot-to-Dot Princesses is an activity book in which readers connect numbered dots to uncover 100 pictures from the world of the Disney Princesses. The images range from castles and loyal sidekicks to fairy-tale endings, and each puzzle is made up of hundreds of dots.

Once a picture is finished, readers can add colour with pencils to make each princess scene come alive. A relaxing, absorbing pastime for Disney fans who enjoy puzzles and colouring.

  • Author: Walt Disney Company
  • Publisher: Studio Press
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781787418387

title: Sleeping Beauty (Disney Animated Classics)
author: Lily Murray
description:
Sleeping Beauty is a title in the Disney Animated Classics series, with Lily Murray's retelling of the classic Disney film. Princess Aurora, Maleficent's curse and the three good fairies are brought to life through paintings, sketches and development art by Disney's original studio artists.

The book includes a foreword from Mike Gabriel, whose work at Walt Disney Animation Studios has spanned animation, story, visual development and directing, and a closing section on the artists behind the film. With cloth binding, a ribbon bookmark, gold foil detailing and decorated endpapers, it is a treasured gift for fans.

  • Author: Lily Murray
  • Publisher: Templar Publishing
  • Format: Hardcover, 64 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Disney Animated Classics
  • ISBN: 9781787414174

title: Arabic Folktales for Language Learners
author: Sarah Risha
description:
Arabic Folktales for Language Learners: Traditional Stories in Arabic and English by Sarah Risha is a bilingual reader from Tuttle Publishing. It presents traditional folktales in both Arabic and English, giving learners a way to build their language skills through storytelling.

Its title notes that free bilingual online audio accompanies the stories, making it a useful companion for students of Arabic who want to practise reading and listening.

  • Author: Sarah Risha
  • Publisher: Tuttle Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 256 pages
  • Language: Arabic and English
  • ISBN: 9780804857109

title: Where's Molly
author: H.D. Carlton
description:
Where's Molly is a dark romance by H.D. Carlton, set in the world of her Cat and Mouse duet. Molly Devereaux disappeared in the Oregon woods and the world is still asking what became of her; now living deep in the Montana mountains, she is learning to accept a new life while still feeling like a ghost.

The mountains are beautiful, but they also hide horrors that come out at night. The story should be read after Haunting Adeline and its sequel Hunting Adeline. It contains dark subject matter, and the author provides content warnings on her website.

  • Author: H.D. Carlton
  • Format: Paperback, 228 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Cat and Mouse, Book 2.5
  • ISBN: 9781638932482

title: Making Levantine Cuisine
author: Anny Gaul, Graham Auman Pitts, Vicki Valosik
description:
Making Levantine Cuisine: Modern Foodways of the Eastern Mediterranean, edited by Anny Gaul, Graham Auman Pitts and Vicki Valosik, is a scholarly collection exploring the food cultures of the Levant. It examines how the region's cooking blends rural and urban, local and global influences, and untangles the histories and migrations behind familiar dishes.

Contributors look at how sugar, pistachios and olive oil have been produced and traded, and investigate the social origins of shawarma, falafel, kibbe, shakshuka and Adana kebab, with family recipes scattered throughout. An engaging read for food lovers, historians and anyone interested in the Eastern Mediterranean.

  • Editors: Anny Gaul, Graham Auman Pitts, Vicki Valosik
  • Publisher: University of Texas Press
  • Format: Hardcover, 288 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781477324578

title: Magic Painting Bugs
author: Abigail Wheatley
description:
Bugs Magic Painting Book by Abigail Wheatley, illustrated by Andy Tudor, is part of Usborne's Magic Painting Books series. Children bring 16 creepy-crawlies to life, including dragonflies, scarab beetles and millipedes, using only water and the brush supplied with the book.

A laminated flap on the back cover stops water soaking through to the pages underneath. It is a simple way to keep young children busy indoors while they practise brush and pen control.

  • Author: Abigail Wheatley
  • Illustrator: Andy Tudor
  • Publisher: Usborne Publishing Ltd
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Usborne Magic Painting Books
  • ISBN: 9781474986229

title: Magic Painting The Snow Queen
author: Susanna Davidson
description:
Snow Queen Magic Painting Book by Susanna Davidson, illustrated by Barbara Bongini, retells the classic fairy tale of the Snow Queen as part of Usborne's Magic Painting Books series. Young readers follow brave Gerda as she sets out to rescue her dearest friend from the Snow Queen's frozen grip.

To reveal the pictures, children dip the brush in water and sweep it over the monochrome designs, watching 16 scenes fill with colour. A magical, absorbing activity that combines storytelling with creative play.

  • Author: Susanna Davidson
  • Illustrator: Barbara Bongini
  • Publisher: Usborne Publishing Ltd
  • Format: Paperback, 32 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Usborne Magic Painting Books
  • ISBN: 9781474933803

title: Fingerprint Activities Zoo
author: Fiona Watt
description:
Fingerprint Activities Zoo by Fiona Watt is a creative activity book from Usborne's Fingerprint Activities series that comes with seven colourful ink pads. Each page offers ideas for turning fingerprints into zoo animals, from a spotted cheetah and hippos in a lake to stripy-tailed lemurs and koalas up in the trees.

The spiral binding lets the book lie flat while children fill the pages with their own prints, making it easy to use at the table. A fun, hands-on way to get creative with colour.

  • Author: Fiona Watt
  • Publisher: Usborne
  • Format: Spiral-bound, 64 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Usborne Fingerprint Activities
  • ISBN: 9781803705095

title: That's not my bunny Book and Toy
sheet_title: That's not my bunny Book and Toy
author: Fiona Watt
description:
That's Not My Bunny Book and Toy is a gift set from Usborne that pairs a copy of Fiona Watt's touchy-feely board book That's Not My Bunny with a soft, cuddly bunny toy. Part of the long-running That's not my... series, the book invites babies and toddlers to explore textured patches on every page.

Little ones can also hunt for the small white mouse that appears throughout while playing with the matching bunny. A sweet first present that combines sensory play, simple repeated text and a comforting companion.

  • Author: Fiona Watt
  • Publisher: Usborne Books
  • Format: Board book and soft toy, 10 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: That's not my...
  • ISBN: 9781801319676

title: That's not my mermaid
author: Fiona Watt
description:
That's Not My Mermaid by Fiona Watt is a touchy-feely board book in Usborne's That's not my... series. On each page a different colourful mermaid appears, and babies and toddlers can feel smooth, bumpy and shiny textured patches as they search for the right one.

Spotting the little white mouse on every spread adds to the fun. Sturdy, bright and simple, it is a lovely first book for sharing and for encouraging early sensory and language awareness.

  • Author: Fiona Watt
  • Publisher: Usborne Publishing Ltd
  • Format: Board book, 10 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: That's not my...
  • ISBN: 9781474995283

title: That's not my polar bear Book and Toy
sheet_title: That's not my polar bear Book and Toy
author: Fiona Watt
attention: Partly matched — check details against the copy
description:
That's Not My Polar Bear Book and Toy is a gift set pairing Fiona Watt's touchy-feely board book That's Not My Polar Bear with a soft polar bear toy. The book belongs to Usborne's That's not my... series, which uses textured patches and simple text to engage the youngest readers.

It makes a cosy gift for little ones who enjoy touch-and-feel books and a cuddly companion to go with them.

  • Author: Fiona Watt
  • Publisher: Usborne
  • Format: Board book and soft toy
  • Language: English
  • Series: That's not my...
  • ISBN: 9781801310451

title: Baby's Very First Noisy Book Dinosaurs
sheet_title: Babys Very First Noisy Book Dinosaurs
author: Fiona Watt
description:
Baby's Very First Noisy Book Dinosaurs by Fiona Watt is a sturdy sound board book from Usborne's Baby's Very First range. Bright, friendly dinosaurs stomp across the pages, and little hands can press the buttons to hear them.

The sounds include a hungry diplodocus, squeaking baby dinosaurs and a roaring T. rex, among others. A playful introduction to dinosaurs and sounds for babies.

  • Author: Fiona Watt
  • Publisher: Usborne Publishing Ltd
  • Format: Board book, 10 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Baby's Very First Noisy Book
  • ISBN: 9781474999113

title: Dance with the Giraffes
author: Sam Taplin
description:
Dance with the Giraffes by Sam Taplin, illustrated by Ana Martín Larrañaga, is a lively Usborne novelty board book designed to get little children up and moving. Each spread features its own troupe of giraffes on the move, along with a catchy tune to dance to.

Simple text teaches one easy dance move for each tune, and at the end children combine all the moves to perform the complete giraffe dance. A joyful, interactive book that brings together music, movement and play.

  • Author: Sam Taplin
  • Illustrator: Ana Martín Larrañaga
  • Publisher: Usborne Books
  • Format: Board book, 10 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781803700953

title: Men in the Sun
author: Ghassan Kanafani
description:
Men in the Sun and Other Palestinian Stories collects short fiction by the celebrated Palestinian writer Ghassan Kanafani, translated from Arabic by Hilary Kilpatrick. Its title novella follows three Palestinian men who attempt a gruelling, dangerous crossing of the Iraqi desert in the hope of finding work and money in Kuwait.

Facing indifferent border officials and the merciless desert heat, their journey grows ever more desperate. Written in a deceptively plain, often lyrical style, the stories offer a powerful portrait of exile and displacement and remain a landmark of modern Arabic literature.

  • Author: Ghassan Kanafani
  • Translator: Hilary Kilpatrick
  • Publisher: Verso Books
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9781804298589

title: Bittersweet
author: Susan Cain
description:
Bittersweet: How Sorrow and Longing Make Us Whole is Susan Cain's exploration of loss, longing and the melancholy side of human experience, from the author of Quiet. Cain argues that impermanence runs through every life and is bound up with love, growth and creativity, yet we rarely give it the attention it deserves.

Blending memoir, reporting and social science, she shows how joy and sorrow exist side by side, how a wistful, melancholic nature may actually be a strength, and how accepting our losses can make us more fully human. A thoughtful, consoling read for anyone navigating grief or change.

  • Author: Susan Cain
  • Publisher: Viking
  • Format: Paperback
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780241300688

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description:
Dracula is Bram Stoker's landmark Gothic horror novel, presented here in a Vintage Collector's Classics hardback edition. Told through letters, diaries and newspaper cuttings, it follows young solicitor Jonathan Harker on a business trip to a remote castle in Transylvania, where his host, Count Dracula, proves far more sinister than he first appears.

As the Count makes his way to England, a small band led by Professor Van Helsing must confront an ancient evil that survives on the blood of the living. Atmospheric and unsettling, the novel that defined the modern vampire remains essential reading for lovers of classic and Gothic fiction.

  • Author: Bram Stoker
  • Publisher: Vintage Classics
  • Format: Hardcover, 432 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Vintage Collector's Classics
  • ISBN: 9781529954319

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
description:
Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's much-loved novel of four sisters growing up together in New England, presented in a deluxe Vintage Collector's Classics hardback. Responsible Meg, fiery and ambitious Jo, gentle Beth and artistic Amy navigate family life, friendship, first love and hardship as they come of age.

Warm, funny and honest, it remains one of the great classics of family life and girlhood. This gift edition is finished with a silk ribbon marker, sprayed page edges, foil-decorated covers and marbled endpapers, making it a beautiful keepsake for readers old and new.

  • Author: Louisa May Alcott
  • Publisher: Vintage Classics
  • Format: Hardcover, 272 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Vintage Collector's Classics
  • ISBN: 9781529954289

title: Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and Other Stories
sheet_title: Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and Other Stories
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description:
Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and Other Stories brings together Robert Louis Stevenson's famous novella of a divided self with a selection of his shorter fiction, in a Vintage Collector's Classics hardback. In the title story, the London lawyer Mr Utterson investigates the troubling link between his respected friend Dr Henry Jekyll and the brutal, repellent Edward Hyde.

A gripping exploration of the darker side of human nature and Victorian respectability, it remains one of the most influential tales in Gothic fiction. The accompanying shorter pieces offer further examples of Stevenson's storytelling.

  • Author: Robert Louis Stevenson
  • Publisher: Vintage Classics
  • Format: Hardcover, 240 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Vintage Collector's Classics
  • ISBN: 9781529954326

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
description:
Brave New World is Aldous Huxley's classic dystopian novel, in a Vintage edition introduced by Margaret Atwood. In the World State of the future, stability and contentment are engineered from birth: people are bred in hatcheries, conditioned for their roles and kept docile with the drug soma.

When Bernard Marx brings John, an outsider raised beyond the reach of this society, into its heart, the cost of a world built on pleasure and constant surveillance becomes clear. Unnerving and strikingly prescient about consumerism and technology, it remains essential reading.

  • Author: Aldous Huxley
  • Introduction: Margaret Atwood and David Bradshaw
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 229 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099518471

title: After Dark
author: Haruki Murakami
description:
After Dark is a short novel by Haruki Murakami, translated from Japanese by Jay Rubin, that unfolds over a single night in Tokyo. As midnight approaches, Mari is reading alone in an all-night diner when a young musician interrupts her; neither of them can get home until the trains start running again.

Before dawn she is drawn into the aftermath of a violent incident at a love hotel, while elsewhere her beautiful sister Eri lies in a strangely deep sleep that has lasted two months. Dreamlike and quietly unsettling, it is an atmospheric introduction to Murakami's fiction.

  • Author: Haruki Murakami
  • Translator: Jay Rubin
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 201 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099506249

title: South of the Border, West of the Sun
sheet_title: South of the Border, West of the Sun
author: Haruki Murakami
description:
South of the Border, West of the Sun is Haruki Murakami's spare, haunting novel of first love and longing, translated from Japanese by Philip Gabriel. Growing up as an only child in suburban post-war Japan, Hajime finds a kindred spirit in Shimamoto, also an only child, and the two spend hours together playing records from her father's collection.

Years later, now in his thirties, Hajime is happily married with two daughters and runs a successful jazz bar in Tokyo, when Shimamoto suddenly reappears, beautiful and mysterious. A quietly intense story about memory, desire and the pull of the past.

  • Author: Haruki Murakami
  • Translator: Philip Gabriel
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 190 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099448570

title: The Elephant Vanishes
author: Haruki Murakami
description:
The Elephant Vanishes is a collection of short stories by Haruki Murakami, in which ordinary lives are quietly knocked off balance by the strange and inexplicable. In the title story, a man's equilibrium is disturbed when an elephant disappears from his town; elsewhere, a hungry couple decide to rob a McDonald's in the middle of the night.

A woman finds herself the object of a small green monster's affection, and a sleepless wife slips into a strange, wakeful twilight. Playful, eerie and often funny, these stories make an ideal introduction to Murakami's singular imagination.

  • Author: Haruki Murakami
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 327 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099448754

title: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
author: Haruki Murakami
description:
The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle is one of Haruki Murakami's most ambitious novels, translated from Japanese by Jay Rubin. Toru Okada, an unemployed man living a quiet suburban life in Tokyo, sets out to find his missing cat, and soon afterwards his wife, Kumiko, disappears too.

Strange phone calls, a pair of psychic sisters, a dry well and a veteran's harrowing memories of wartime Manchuria draw him into a hidden world beneath everyday life. Mysterious, absorbing and deeply strange, it is a landmark of contemporary fiction for readers ready for an immersive journey.

  • Author: Haruki Murakami
  • Translator: Jay Rubin
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 609 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099448792

title: A History Of God
author: Karen Armstrong
description:
A History of God is Karen Armstrong's sweeping account of how the idea of one God has developed over some four thousand years in Judaism, Christianity and Islam. Tracing belief from its ancient roots through philosophy, mysticism and reform to the modern age, Armstrong shows how each era has reshaped its understanding of the divine.

She also confronts the tension between the goodness these faiths proclaim and the conflict and prejudice that organised religion has at times fuelled. Clear, learned and balanced, it is a rewarding read for anyone interested in religion, history and the search for meaning.

  • Author: Karen Armstrong
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 511 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099273677

title: Ripley
author: Patricia Highsmith
description:
The Talented Mr. Ripley is the first of Patricia Highsmith's novels about Tom Ripley, the charming, amoral young man who became one of crime fiction's most memorable antiheroes. In 1950s New York, Tom is scraping by when a wealthy shipbuilder asks him to travel to Italy and persuade his son, Dickie Greenleaf, to come home.

Seduced by Dickie's privileged life on the Italian coast and resentful of his friendship with Marge, Tom finds his fascination turning to obsession, and then to something far more dangerous. Tense, stylish and psychologically sharp, it is a classic of suspense for readers who enjoy literary crime.

  • Author: Patricia Highsmith
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 258 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Ripley, Book 1
  • ISBN: 9781529940886

title: The Housekeeper and the Professor
author: Yōko Ogawa
description:
The Housekeeper and the Professor is a gentle, luminous novel by Yōko Ogawa, translated from Japanese by Stephen Snyder. A brilliant mathematician, injured in an accident years earlier, can hold new memories for only eighty minutes, and a young single mother is hired as his housekeeper.

Each morning they must be introduced again, yet through his love of numbers, with puzzles built from her shoe size or birthday, a tender bond grows between the Professor, the Housekeeper and her young son, whom he nicknames Root. Quietly moving, it celebrates memory, family and the beauty of mathematics.

  • Author: Yōko Ogawa
  • Translator: Stephen Snyder
  • Publisher: Vintage
  • Format: Paperback, 180 pages
  • Language: English
  • ISBN: 9780099521341

title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5—Golden Wind, Vol. 4
author: Hirohiko Araki
description:
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5—Golden Wind, Vol. 4 continues Hirohiko Araki's Italian arc of the long-running manga saga in VIZ Media's deluxe hardcover format, complete with colour pages. Giorno Giovanna and Bruno Bucciarati's squad are aboard a high-speed express bound for Florence, guarding their charge while enemies close in and a brand-new hostile Stand attacks.

Even getting off the train offers no real escape, so the tension stays high from start to finish. Araki's flamboyant character designs, inventive Stand battles and offbeat humour are all on show, making this a strong addition for fans following the Joestar bloodline through its fifth part.

  • Author: Hirohiko Araki
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Hardcover, 378 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Part 5: Golden Wind, Vol. 4
  • ISBN: 9781974724123

title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5—Golden Wind, Vol. 5
author: Hirohiko Araki
description:
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5—Golden Wind, Vol. 5 is the fifth of ten deluxe hardcover volumes collecting Hirohiko Araki's Golden Wind arc, published by VIZ Media with colour pages. The story follows Giorno Giovanna, the young gangster who is secretly Dio Brando's son, as he works his way upward inside an Italian crime organisation alongside Bruno Bucciarati's team.

Their mission to keep Trish, the daughter of the gang's mysterious boss, out of the hands of rival Stand users drives the action across Italy. Expect Araki's trademark mix of strategic Stand duels, striking poses and dark humour, ideal for readers continuing the Joestar saga in a collectible format.

  • Author: Hirohiko Araki
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Hardcover, 378 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Part 5: Golden Wind, Vol. 5
  • ISBN: 9781974724130

title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5—Golden Wind, Vol. 6
author: Hirohiko Araki
description:
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5—Golden Wind, Vol. 6 continues Hirohiko Araki's Italian mafia arc in VIZ Media's deluxe hardcover edition with colour pages. Giorno Giovanna and his comrades have so far kept Trish alive, but only just, and every stage of their desperate mission puts their own lives on the line once more.

This volume shifts the balance in an intriguing way as Trish starts to reveal a hidden ability of her own, which may finally give the team the advantage. Inventive Stand battles, bold artwork and Araki's eccentric sense of humour make it a natural next step for fans collecting the deluxe series.

  • Author: Hirohiko Araki
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Hardcover, 378 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Part 5: Golden Wind, Vol. 6
  • ISBN: 9781974724147

title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 6—Stone Ocean, Vol. 2
author: Hirohiko Araki
description:
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 6—Stone Ocean, Vol. 2 continues the sixth part of Hirohiko Araki's manga saga in VIZ Media's deluxe hardcover format with colour pages. Jolyne Cujoh, daughter of Jotaro Kujo, is locked up in a Florida prison, and in this volume Jotaro arrives to break her out, only for father and daughter to walk straight into an enemy ambush.

Caught in a dreamworld as their physical bodies slowly dissolve, they battle for survival, and an unseen foe strips Jotaro of his Stand and his memories, leaving him barely alive. Ermes then uncovers a lead that offers hope. Strange, tense and inventive, it suits readers following the Joestar line into a new generation.

  • Author: Hirohiko Araki
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Hardcover, 400 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Part 6: Stone Ocean, Vol. 2
  • ISBN: 9781974742882

title: Jojo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5--Golden Wind, Vol. 1
sheet_title: Jojo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5--Golden Wind, Vol. 1
author: Hirohiko Araki
description:
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5—Golden Wind, Vol. 1 opens the fifth part of Hirohiko Araki's manga saga in a deluxe VIZ Media hardcover with colour pages. The action moves from Japan to Italy, where Koichi Hirose travels to Naples in search of Giorno Giovanna, an ambitious young gangster who is secretly the son of Dio Brando, the Joestar family's great enemy.

Mafia intrigue, family legacy and outlandish Stand powers collide as Giorno sets his sights on rising through the criminal underworld. This is the place to begin the Golden Wind arc, giving newcomers and long-time fans alike a handsome hardcover edition with plenty of Araki's bold, theatrical artwork.

  • Author: Hirohiko Araki
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Hardcover, 285 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Part 5: Golden Wind, Vol. 1
  • ISBN: 9781974723492

title: Jojo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5--Golden Wind, Vol. 2
sheet_title: Jojo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5--Golden Wind, Vol. 2
author: Hirohiko Araki
description:
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 5—Golden Wind, Vol. 2 continues Hirohiko Araki's Italian arc in VIZ Media's deluxe hardcover edition, which includes colour pages. Not long ago Giorno Giovanna was a small-time hustler, but now he wants far more: to become a genuine mafioso and eventually seize control of a dangerous Neapolitan gang.

Here Giorno joins the organisation, studies how it really operates and begins gathering the allies he will need, all while facing hostile Stand users at every turn. It suits readers who enjoy crime drama blended with supernatural battles and Araki's distinctive, theatrical style.

  • Author: Hirohiko Araki
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Hardcover, 379 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Part 5: Golden Wind, Vol. 2
  • ISBN: 9781974723997

title: Jujutsu Kaisen, Vol. 5
author: Gege Akutami
description:
Jujutsu Kaisen, Vol. 5 is the fifth volume of Gege Akutami's dark supernatural shonen manga, set in a world in which cursed spirits prey on people and the scattered remains of the feared demon Ryomen Sukuna could bring catastrophe. The sorcerers of Jujutsu High train to hold these curses back.

In this instalment everyone is stunned to learn that Yuji Itadori is still alive, but there is little time for a reunion as Jujutsu High faces its rival school from Kyoto in a fierce exchange event where fair play is far from guaranteed. Fast-paced fights and sharp humour make it a gripping read for fans of action manga.

  • Author: Gege Akutami
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Paperback, 192 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: Jujutsu Kaisen, Vol. 5
  • ISBN: 9781974714810

title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 2--Battle Tendency, Vol. 2
sheet_title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 2--Battle Tendency, Vol. 2
author: Hirohiko Araki
description:
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 2—Battle Tendency, Vol. 2 is a deluxe VIZ Media hardcover of Hirohiko Araki's second JoJo arc, starring Joseph Joestar, grandson of the original hero Jonathan. In this volume more of the ancient Pillar Men stir from their slumber, and Joseph must join forces with newcomer Caesar Zeppeli to foil their sinister scheme.

These beings possess unimaginable strength, so the two young fighters face a race to sharpen their Ripple techniques before it is too late. With larger-than-life heroes, outrageous villains and clever battles of wits, the volume captures the wild energy of the series.

  • Author: Hirohiko Araki
  • Publisher: VIZ Media
  • Format: Hardcover, 361 pages
  • Language: English
  • Series: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Part 2: Battle Tendency, Vol. 2
  • ISBN: 9781421578835

title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 2--Battle Tendency, Vol. 3
sheet_title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 2--Battle Tendency, Vol. 3
author: Hirohiko Araki
description:
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Part 2—Battle Tendency, Vol. 3 continues Hirohiko Araki's second arc in deluxe hardcover from VIZ Media. Bleach (3-in-1 Edition), Vol. 1 collects the first three volumes of Tite Kubo's supernatural action manga in a single book. Ichigo Kurosaki has been able to see ghosts for as long as he can remember, but his life is turned upside down when he meets Rukia Kuchiki, a Soul Reaper sent to fight Hollows, evil spirits that hunt people with strong spiritual energy.

When Rukia tries to lend Ichigo part of her power to save his family, he absorbs all of it and becomes a Soul Reaper himself, taking on her duties while she slowly recovers. Stylish art, sharp humour and memorable characters make this omnibus a convenient entry point for new readers.

Kafka Hibino, who clears up kaiju remains for a living, has long dreamed of joining the Defense Force, but an unexpected transformation turns him into a kaiju himself.

In this volume the Defense Force's final exam has ended, yet the trials keep coming when an enigmatic humanoid kaiju brings a defeated monster back to life and sets it on Kikoru Shinomiya. Kaiju No. 8, Vol. 3 is the third volume of Naoya Matsumoto's action manga about Kafka Hibino, a kaiju clean-up worker who finally gets his chance to join Japan's Defense Force, only to discover that he can turn into a monster himself.

Having driven off a humanoid kaiju to save Iharu and Reno, Kafka is spotted by officers before he can return to human form, and Vice-Captain Hoshina leads a unit sent to neutralise him. Tension, humour and huge set-piece battles make this a gripping instalment for readers following the series.

The attack on the Tachikawa base of the Defense Force rages on as officers struggle to hold back a swarm of smaller kaiju, while Vice-Captain Hoshina unleashes his full strength against the most powerful monster of the group. Packed with large-scale battles and big character moments, it suits fans of energetic shonen action.

Dr. STONE, Vol. 1 launches the science-adventure manga written by Riichiro Inagaki and illustrated by Boichi. In an instant all of humanity is petrified, including high-schooler Taiju just as he is about to confess his feelings to his crush. Thousands of years later he breaks free into a world reclaimed by nature.

Reunited with his brilliant, science-obsessed friend Senku, Taiju sets out to rebuild civilisation from scratch using nothing but knowledge and ingenuity. Mixing real scientific ideas with humour and adventure, the series suits curious readers who enjoy clever problem-solving alongside action.

Dr. STONE, Vol. 2 continues Riichiro Inagaki and Boichi's manga about a world in which all of humanity was mysteriously petrified. Senku, Taiju and Yuzuriha are close to producing gunpowder when they notice smoke rising far away, a possible sign that other people have revived.

Senku gambles on answering with a smoke signal, but the formidable Tsukasa is set on halting their progress, and his arrival threatens to end everything. Blending inventive science, survival drama and rivalry, it is a satisfying follow-up for readers who enjoyed the opening book.

Hunter x Hunter, Vol. 7 continues Yoshihiro Togashi's adventure manga about Hunters, licensed specialists who track down treasure, rare creatures and wanted people after passing a punishing qualification exam. Young Gon Freecss and his friend Killua are training at Heavens Arena under the guidance of their master, Wing.

As they study the mysterious power known as Nen, Gon completes his lessons and learns that he has also passed a secret final stage of the Hunter exam. Moon is a travelling salesman who earns his living crossing a chain of connected worlds on half-forgotten railway lines. Little Book of Louis Vuitton by Karen Homer is a compact, richly illustrated history of one of the world's great luxury houses. It begins with the young Louis arriving in Paris to make his way, and follows the house through the upheavals of two world wars and the Depression as well as the glamour of the 1920s and 1960s.

Later chapters cover its international growth in the 1980s, the formation of the LVMH group and the appointment of Marc Jacobs in 1997, tracing how a trunk-maker became a high-fashion label famous for its monogram. It is a stylish gift for fashion lovers and a handy primer on the brand.

Little Book of Dior by Karen Homer tells the story of the House of Dior, the label that changed the way women dressed and how they saw themselves. It starts with the revolutionary New Look of 1947 and moves through decades of couture, red-carpet gowns and statement pieces worn by stars such as Sophia Loren and Natalie Portman.

Illustrated with around 100 images, the book follows the house from Christian Dior's own vision through the designers who succeeded him, including Yves Saint Laurent and Maria Grazia Chiuri. Elegant and concise, it is a lovely coffee-table book for fashion enthusiasts and a thoughtful gift.

The book explores the label's hallmarks, from understated luxury and innovative technical fabrics to an aesthetic shaped by minimalism and contemporary art, with images of key garments and collections throughout. author: Herodotus
description:
Histories by Herodotus, the fifth-century BC Greek writer often called the father of history, is the earliest surviving major work of Western historical writing. This Wordsworth Editions volume presents George Rawlinson's translation, edited by Tom Griffith, of his sweeping account of the conflict between the Greeks and the Persian Empire.

Along the way Herodotus fills his narrative with digressions on customs, legends and curiosities from across the ancient world, including the story behind the run from Marathon, the Spartan stand at Thermopylae and the naval battle of Salamis. Lively and full of surprises, it remains essential reading for anyone interested in ancient history and the classics.

It combines the Collected Poems of 1928 and the unexpurgated Pansies and Nettles, in the arrangement Lawrence himself approved, with the poems from the two notebooks he was still filling when he died in 1930. Readers can trace how his poetry developed and see how original his voice was, making it a rewarding volume for students and poetry lovers.

The manifesto's stark analysis of capitalism, class struggle and industrial labour sits alongside Engels's vivid study of life among Manchester's workers and his account of how socialist theory developed. Their chase leads through Paris and beyond, uncovering codes hidden in Leonardo da Vinci's art, including Madonna of the Rocks, and a secret society guarding an explosive historical secret. As much as it tells the lives of its characters, the novel tells the story of a people: of the refugee camp where they live and of Palestine, the homeland that is absent. It is a narrative of exile, of the human capacity to hold oneself together, and of clinging to beauty in a besieged reality, suiting readers of Arabic literary fiction.

Loewenstein, an Australian Jewish journalist and author known for his opposition to racism, examines how advanced weaponry and pervasive surveillance are used to control millions of Palestinians.

He then shows how these tools and techniques are sold to governments worldwide, from European Union states and English-speaking democracies to brutal dictatorships. Stealing from the Saracens (السرقة من المسلمين) is the Arabic edition of Diana Darke's study of how Islamic architecture shaped Europe. Darke argues that Europe's cultural borrowing from the Islamic world, often overlooked today, survives in some of its most recognisable buildings, such as Notre-Dame and London's Houses of Parliament.

The book traces styles and ideas from Damascus, Baghdad and Cairo through Muslim Spain, Sicily and Venice into Europe, showing how crusaders, pilgrims and merchants carried them home, and how Christopher Wren drew on the so-called Saracen style of Gothic. Khaled, one of the last Andalusians driven out of Granada, recounts his unfinished tragedy in a lost booklet. When Iyad finds it, the two souls become entwined and revenge turns into a search for meaning and redemption, while a love story with Aisha, a woman of Andalusian descent, runs through the background. Returning after a brain tumour diagnosis, he builds a huge fence, only to find his neighbours wandering freely through his garden, and he must rein in his temper with their provocations and questions. He then applies these defining criteria to what has taken place in Gaza and compares it with earlier cases in which international civil and criminal courts confirmed that genocide had occurred. The study closes with proposals that could help deter or combat the crime, making it a useful reference for readers of international law and human rights.

This Arabic picture book, Who Hid the Eid Lamb? (من خبأ خروف العيد؟), is written by Taghreed Najjar and illustrated by Hassan Manasra. Grandmother Fattoum remembers the year she grew attached to the Eid lamb when she was seven, and tells her grandchildren Maher and Salma about the adventures that followed.

Her story carries her grandchildren, and the young reader, back to her childhood in the village, bringing to life the atmosphere of Eid and the bond between generations. It is a warm choice for sharing during the Eid season and for families who enjoy stories rooted in Arab heritage.

The three books are This Is How Fish Swim, Tasseh Tarantaseh and My Turtle's Name Is Nahla, and the CD lets families listen and sing along together. It is a lovely way to pass on Arab childhood rhymes and build early Arabic vocabulary with young children at home or in the classroom.

The rhymes are grouped by theme: counting rhymes in Us Three Together, rhymes about jobs in Mr. Policeman and silly rhymes in Saadeh the Monkey. Rhymes like these help children with counting, new words and memory while building their sense of humour and bringing parents and children closer. The CD makes it easy to sing along at home.

This is an Arabic-language book titled Me (أنا), published by Al Salwa Publishers. Its short, single-word title places the self at the centre.

Al Salwa is an Amman-based publisher of Arabic books, many of them for children and young readers, and this title is part of its Arabic list.

  • Publisher: Al Salwa Publishers
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789957043193

title: الطنطورية
author: Radwa Ashour
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Egyptian novelist Radwa Ashour's The Woman from Tantoura (الطنطورية). The novel takes its name from Tantoura, a Palestinian coastal village south of Haifa whose people suffered a massacre in 1948, and uses that event as the starting point for the story of a family uprooted from their home.

Following its heroine from girlhood to old age across roughly half a century, including years as a refugee in Lebanon, the book weaves documented history together with literary imagination. Moving and humane, it suits readers of historical fiction and anyone wishing to understand the Palestinian experience of displacement.

  • Author: Radwa Ashour
  • Publisher: Dar El Shorouk
  • Format: Paperback, 463 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789770928295

title: مصائد الرياح
author: Ibrahim Nasrallah
description:
This is an Arabic novel by Palestinian-Jordanian writer Ibrahim Nasrallah, Wind Traps (مصائد الرياح), part of his Palestinian Comedy cycle. Spanning the years from 1930 to 2021, it ties a long national story to an unexpected love affair, with events that move between Palestine, Britain and the wider Arab world.

Told by an all-knowing narrator across three periods, three places and three paths, the novel follows characters haunted by pasts they keep hidden alongside others determined to live openly, while horses that share the fate of the people resist cages and traps with an instinct for freedom. It suits readers of literary fiction and of Nasrallah's earlier novels.

  • Author: Ibrahim Nasrallah
  • Publisher: Arab Scientific Publishers
  • Format: Paperback, 311 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The Palestinian Comedy, Book 14
  • ISBN: 9786140137332

title: أزمة علم النفس المعاصر
author: Georges Politzer
description:
This is the Arabic edition of French philosopher Georges Politzer's Critique of the Foundations of Psychology, published in Arabic as The Crisis of Contemporary Psychology (أزمة علم النفس المعاصر) and translated by Lutfi Fatim. Politzer's work is a theoretical challenge to the assumptions on which modern psychology was built.

Grounded in dialectical materialist philosophy, the book argues for a psychology rooted in the concrete lives of real people. The Arabic edition presents it as a contribution that anyone working in psychology should know, noting how heavily psychology in the Arab world has relied on English and American sources. It suits students and readers of psychology, philosophy and the history of ideas.

  • Author: Georges Politzer
  • Translator: Lutfi Fatim
  • Publisher: Al-Mahrousa Center for Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 118 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789773138820

title: شبيك لبيك ج2
author: Deena Mohamed
description:
This is the second volume of Egyptian artist Deena Mohamed's Arabic graphic novel Shubeik Lubeik (شبيك لبيك), Part 2 of the three-part series. It is set in a Cairo where wishes are bottled, bought and sold like any other goods.

In this instalment we meet a new character, Nour, who buys a wish from Shokry's kiosk, only to discover that using it is far from simple. After all, how exactly do you wish for happiness? Blending fantasy with sharp social observation and striking artwork, the series suits readers of graphic novels, magical realism and contemporary Arabic storytelling.

  • Author: Deena Mohamed
  • Publisher: Al-Mahrousa Center for Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 178 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Shubeik Lubeik, Part 2
  • ISBN: 9789773137786

title: شبيك لبيك ج3
author: Deena Mohamed
description:
This is the third and final volume of Deena Mohamed's Arabic graphic novel Shubeik Lubeik (شبيك لبيك), concluding the series set in a Cairo where wishes are sold in bottles.

Only one wish remains at Shokry's kiosk, and circumstances may push the kiosk owner to use it himself. Caught between his conscience and his beliefs, he must decide what to do. Combining fantasy and social commentary with expressive artwork, this finale suits readers who have followed the first two parts and fans of graphic novels and magical realism.

  • Author: Deena Mohamed
  • Publisher: Al-Mahrousa Center for Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 210 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: Shubeik Lubeik, Part 3
  • ISBN: 9789773138424

title: عالم صوفي رواية حول تاريخ الفلسفة
sheet_title: عالم صوفي رواية حول تاريخ الفلسفة
author: Jostein Gaarder
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Norwegian author Jostein Gaarder's Sophie's World: A Novel About the History of Philosophy (عالم صوفي). It begins when teenager Sophie Amundsen finds two mysterious notes waiting for her, one asking 'Who are you?' and the other 'Where does the world come from?'

Those questions draw her into a correspondence course with an unknown philosopher, and through it into a lively tour of Western thought from the ancient Greeks to the modern age, while the story itself takes increasingly strange turns. Accessible and thought-provoking, it suits young adults and grown-ups alike who want an engaging introduction to philosophy.

  • Author: Jostein Gaarder
  • Publisher: Dar Al-Muna
  • Format: Hardcover, 552 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789188356116

title: السكرية
author: Naguib Mahfouz
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Sugar Street (السكرية), the third and final part of Naguib Mahfouz's celebrated Cairo Trilogy, which follows the family of Al-Sayyid Ahmad Abd Al-Jawad across the first half of the twentieth century.

The novel opens on a note of grief carried over from the end of Palace of Desire: Aisha loses her husband and two sons to typhoid, and the once-radiant daughter becomes a pale, withdrawn figure, left with only her teenage daughter Naima. As a new generation comes of age amid political upheaval, Mahfouz brings the family saga to its close. It suits readers of classic Arabic literature and family sagas.

  • Author: Naguib Mahfouz
  • Publisher: Dar Diwan
  • Format: Paperback, 400 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • Series: The Cairo Trilogy, Book 3
  • ISBN: 9789778616149

title: الكرنك
author: Naguib Mahfouz
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Naguib Mahfouz's short novel Karnak Café (الكرنك). Set between Egypt's 1967 defeat and the 1973 war, it takes its name from a Cairo coffee house run by Qurunfula, a retired dancer, whose tables become a meeting place for students and intellectuals.

Among the regulars are young people raised on the ideals of the revolution, including Hilmi, Ismail and Zaynab, who fall victim to the abuses of the intelligence services: arbitrary accusations, arrests and torture. A sharp political novel, it suits readers of Mahfouz and anyone interested in modern Egyptian history.

  • Author: Naguib Mahfouz
  • Publisher: Dar Diwan
  • Pages: 116
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778639759

title: أولاد حارتنا
author: Naguib Mahfouz
description:
This is the Arabic edition of Naguib Mahfouz's Children of the Alley (أولاد حارتنا), one of the Nobel laureate's most famous and debated novels. In a Cairo alley, the patriarch Gabalawi lives secluded in his great house behind high walls and gardens, while his descendants quarrel over the family estate and local strongmen hold the neighbourhood in their grip.

Generation after generation, a saviour figure rises to lead the people against injustice, yet greed and ignorance return them to where they began. Widely read as an allegory of humanity's spiritual history, the novel was serialised in Al-Ahram in 1959 and caused such controversy that its publication as a book was delayed for years. It suits readers of classic and allegorical fiction.

  • Author: Naguib Mahfouz
  • Publisher: Dar Diwan
  • Pages: 576
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789778616200

title: ابتسم فأنت ميت
author: Hassan Al-Jundi
description:
This is an Arabic novel by Egyptian writer Hassan Al-Jundi, Smile, You're Dead (ابتسم فأنت ميت). Its tagline sets a chilling tone, suggesting that the only person you can force to smile is one who is already dead.

Shelved by readers among horror and thriller fiction, it suits fans of dark, suspenseful Arabic storytelling.

  • Author: Hassan Al-Jundi
  • Publisher: Dark Publishing
  • Format: Paperback, 277 pages
  • Language: Arabic
  • ISBN: 9789776634312

It will appeal to readers interested in health, well-being and the connection between body and mind.
